Q: Which exams is Parts of Speech useful for?
A: Candidates preparing for APSC, Assam Police, DME will find Parts of Speech relevant, because the content is built around the way these papers frame their questions.
Q: What is a part of speech?
A: A part of speech is the class to which a word belongs according to the work it does in a sentence, such as noun, pronoun, adjective, verb, adverb, preposition, conjunction or interjection.
Q: Can one word be more than one part of speech?
A: Yes. A word's part of speech depends on its function, so "book" is a noun in "a book" and a verb in "to book a seat".
Q: How are articles and determiners related to parts of speech?
A: Articles (a, an, the) and determiners (this, some, any, each) are usually treated as a special kind of adjective because they come before a noun and limit it.
Q: Why is parts of speech important for competitive exams?
A: It is the base of grammar, so it directly helps in error spotting, fill in the blanks, voice, narration and subject-verb agreement questions in APSC, ADRE and Assam Police papers.
Q: How many parts of speech are there in English?
A: There are eight traditional parts of speech: noun, pronoun, adjective, verb, adverb, preposition, conjunction and interjection.
Q: Part of speech কাক বোলে?
A: বাক্যত এটা শব্দই কৰা কামৰ ভিত্তিত সেই শব্দক যি শ্ৰেণীত ধৰা হয়, তাক part of speech বোলে. যেনে noun, pronoun, adjective, verb, adverb, preposition, conjunction বা interjection।
Q: এটা শব্দয়ে একাধিক part of speech হ'ব পাৰেনে?
A: হয়। শব্দৰ কামেহে শ্ৰেণী ঠিক কৰে, গতিকে "book" শব্দটো "a book" ত noun আৰু "to book a seat" ত verb।
Q: Article আৰু determiner-ৰ সম্পৰ্ক কি?
A: Article (a, an, the) আৰু determiner (this, some, any, each) দুয়ো noun-ৰ আগত আহি তাৰ পৰিসৰ নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰে, সেয়ে ইহঁতক adjective-ৰ এক বিশেষ ৰূপ হিচাপে ধৰা হয়।
Q: প্ৰতিযোগিতামূলক পৰীক্ষাৰ বাবে parts of speech কিয় গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: ই ব্যাকৰণৰ ভিত্তি, গতিকে APSC, ADRE আৰু অসম আৰক্ষীৰ error spotting, fill in the blanks, voice, narration আৰু subject-verb agreement আদি প্ৰশ্নত পোনপটীয়াকৈ সহায় কৰে।
Q: ইংৰাজীত কিমানটা part of speech আছে?
A: পৰম্পৰাগতভাৱে আঠটা: noun, pronoun, adjective, verb, adverb, preposition, conjunction আৰু interjection।

### Clauses Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/english/sentence-structure/clauses/
Summary: Practice clauses questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: A group of words that contains a subject and a finite verb and forms part of a sentence is a ___.
A: Clause — A clause has its own subject and verb.
Q: A clause that can stand alone as a complete sentence is called the ___ clause.
A: Main — A main (independent) clause makes complete sense by itself.
Q: A clause that cannot stand alone and depends on the main clause is a ___ clause.
A: Subordinate — A subordinate clause depends on the main clause for its meaning.
Q: Identify the main clause: 'I know that he is honest.'
A: I know — 'I know' can stand alone and carries the main idea.
Q: Identify the subordinate clause: 'I know that he is honest.'
A: that he is honest — 'That he is honest' cannot stand alone; it is the object of 'know'.
Q: Identify the main clause: 'He returned home before it rained.'
A: He returned home — 'He returned home' makes complete sense by itself.
Q: Which of the following contains a noun clause?
A: I know that he is honest. — 'That he is honest' works as the object of 'know' (a noun clause).
Q: A clause that works as the subject or object of a verb is a ___ clause.
A: Noun — A noun clause does the work of a noun.
Q: 'That he is honest' in 'I know that he is honest' is a ___ clause.
A: Noun — It is the object of the verb 'know'.
Q: A clause that qualifies (describes) a noun or pronoun is an ___ clause.
A: Adjective — An adjective clause is also called a relative clause.
Q: Identify the adjective clause: 'The boy who stood first is my friend.'
A: who stood first — The clause qualifies the noun 'boy'.
Q: 'Who stood first' in the above sentence is a ___ clause.
A: Adjective (Relative) — It is introduced by the relative pronoun 'who'.
Q: A clause that modifies a verb, an adjective or another adverb is an ___ clause.
A: Adverb — An adverb clause does the work of an adverb.
Q: Identify the adverb clause: 'He works hard so that he may pass.'
A: so that he may pass — The clause shows the purpose of working hard.
Q: The clause 'so that he may pass' shows ___.
A: Purpose — 'So that' introduces an adverb clause of purpose.
Q: In 'As he was ill, he did not come', the clause 'as he was ill' is an adverb clause of ___.
A: Reason — 'As' (meaning because) shows the reason.
Q: Identify the adverb clause of time: 'When the rain stopped, we went out.'
A: When the rain stopped — 'When' shows the time of the action.
Q: Which sentence contains an adverb clause of place?
A: I will go where you go. — 'Where you go' shows the place of going.
Q: Identify the adverb clause of condition: 'If you work hard, you will succeed.'
A: If you work hard — 'If' introduces a condition.
Q: Identify the adverb clause of result: 'He is so weak that he cannot walk.'
A: that he cannot walk — 'So...that' expresses result/consequence.
Q: Which sentence contains an adverb clause of comparison?
A: She is not as clever as her sister. — 'As...as' shows comparison.
Q: Identify the adverb clause of concession: 'Although he is poor, he is honest.'
A: Although he is poor — 'Although' introduces a clause of concession (contrast).
Q: Fill in the blank: '___ he will come is doubtful.'
A: That — Here the noun clause is the subject: 'That he will come'.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'The news ___ he has passed is true.'
A: that — The noun clause is in apposition to 'the news'.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'I doubt ___ he will come.'
A: whether — After 'doubt' (in doubt), 'whether/if' is used.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'Tell me ___ you want.'
A: what — 'What you want' is the object of 'tell'.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'The man ___ helped me was my uncle.'
A: who — 'Who' is the subject of the adjective clause.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'The man ___ I met yesterday is a doctor.'
A: whom — 'Whom' is the object of 'met'.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'The boy ___ father died is poor.'
A: whose — 'Whose' shows possession.
Q: Combine using an adjective clause: 'I have a friend. He lives in Guwahati.'
A: I have a friend who lives in Guwahati. — The pronoun 'he' is replaced by the relative 'who'.
Q: Combine using a relative clause: 'This is the house. Rabindranath was born here.'
A: This is the house where Rabindranath was born. — The relative adverb 'where' joins the clauses.
Q: 'Where I was born' in 'This is the house where I was born' is a/an ___ clause.
A: Adjective — It qualifies the noun 'house'.
Q: 'That she was ill' in 'She said that she was ill' is a ___ clause.
A: Noun — It is the object of the verb 'said'.
Q: 'Where he lives' in 'I don't know where he lives' is a ___ clause.
A: Noun — It is the object of 'know' (indirect question).
Q: A sentence having one main clause and one or more subordinate clauses is a ___ sentence.
A: Complex — Complex sentences contain subordinate clauses.
Q: Two or more main clauses joined by 'and', 'but' or 'or' make a ___ sentence.
A: Compound — Coordinating conjunctions make compound sentences.
Q: Combine using 'though': 'He is poor. He is happy.'
A: Though he is poor, he is happy. — 'Though' joins them as an adverb clause of concession.
Q: Combine using 'because': 'He failed. He was careless.'
A: He failed because he was careless. — 'Because' shows the reason for his failure.
Q: Identify the kind of sentence: 'I called him but he did not come.'
A: Compound — Two main clauses are joined by 'but'.
Q: Name the clause: 'that he is honest' in 'The truth is that he is honest.'
A: Noun clause — A noun clause (it is the complement of the verb 'is').
Q: 'When he came' in 'I was sleeping when he came' is an adverb clause of ___.
A: Time — Time (it shows when the action happened).
Q: What is a clause?
A: A clause is a group of words that contains both a subject and a finite verb. It may be independent (able to stand alone) or dependent (needing a main clause).
Q: What are the three kinds of subordinate clauses?
A: They are the noun clause, which acts as a noun, the adjective clause, which describes a noun, and the adverb clause, which modifies a verb and answers when, where, why, how or under what condition.
Q: How do I tell a phrase from a clause?
A: A clause has a subject and a finite verb, while a phrase has neither together. If you cannot find a subject-verb pair, it is a phrase.
Q: When do I put a comma after a clause?
A: When an adverb clause comes at the beginning of a sentence, a comma follows it. A non-defining adjective clause is set off by commas on both sides, but a defining clause takes no comma.
Q: Can a dependent clause stand alone as a sentence?
A: No. A dependent clause must be attached to a main clause. If it stands alone, it becomes a sentence fragment and is treated as an error.
Q: Clause কি?
A: Clause হৈছে কৰ্তা আৰু finite ক্ৰিয়া দুয়ো থকা শব্দৰ গোট। ই independent (নিজে থিয় দিব পৰা) বা dependent (মূল clause প্ৰয়োজন হোৱা) হ'ব পাৰে।
Q: Subordinate clause ৰ তিনিটা প্ৰকাৰ কি কি?
A: Noun clause, যিয়ে নামৰ কাম কৰে; adjective clause, যিয়ে নামৰ বৰ্ণনা কৰে; আৰু adverb clause, যিয়ে ক্ৰিয়া যোগ্য কৰি কেতিয়া, ক'ত, কিয়, কেনেকৈ বা কি চৰ্তত কয়।
Q: Phrase আৰু clause ৰ পাৰ্থক্য কেনেকৈ চিনি পাম?
A: Clause ত কৰ্তা আৰু finite ক্ৰিয়া থাকে, phrase ত দুয়ো একেলগে নাথাকে। কৰ্তা-ক্ৰিয়া যোৰ নাপালে সেয়া phrase।
Q: Clause ৰ পিছত কেতিয়া comma দিব লাগে?
A: Adverb clause বাক্যৰ আৰম্ভণিত থাকিলে তাৰ পিছত comma পৰে। Non-defining adjective clause ৰ দুয়োফালে comma থাকে, কিন্তু defining clause ত comma নাই।
Q: Dependent clause নিজে বাক্য হিচাপে থিয় দিব পাৰে নেকি?
A: নোৱাৰে। Dependent clause ক মূল clause ৰ লগত যুক্ত কৰিব লাগে। অকলে থিয় হ'লে ই sentence fragment হৈ ভুল হিচাপে গণ্য হয়।

### Punctuation Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/english/sentence-structure/punctuation/
Summary: Practice punctuation questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'where are you going'
A: Where are you going? — A question begins with a capital letter and ends with a question mark.
Q: A statement (assertive) sentence ends with a ___.
A: Full stop (.) — A full stop (period) ends a statement.
Q: What mark is used at the end of an interrogative sentence?
A: Question mark (?) — Questions end with a question mark.
Q: Which mark is used to express a sudden strong feeling or emotion?
A: Exclamation mark (!) — An exclamation mark follows words showing strong feeling.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'what a lovely day'
A: What a lovely day! — An exclamatory sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with '!'
Q: Which punctuation mark is used to separate items in a list?
A: Comma (,) — A comma separates words in a list.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'I bought apples oranges and bananas'
A: I bought apples, oranges and bananas. — Commas separate the items of the list.
Q: Choose the correct possessive form: 'This is my ___ book.'
A: Rina's — The apostrophe + s ('s) shows possession for a singular owner.
Q: Choose the correct plural possessive form: 'The books belong to the boys.'
A: The boys' book — For plural nouns ending in 's', only an apostrophe is added after 's'.
Q: Choose the correct contraction: 'Do not go there.'
A: Don't go there. — In contractions, the apostrophe replaces the missing letters (Do not = Don't).
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'Yes I will come'
A: Yes, I will come. — A comma follows the introductory word 'Yes'.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'He said I am busy'
A: He said, "I am busy." — A comma comes after 'said' and the exact words are put in quotation marks.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence (indirect question):
A: She asked me where I was going. — An indirect question does not end with a question mark.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
A: He was tired; he went to bed. — A semicolon joins two closely related clauses without a conjunction.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
A: He bought three things: a pen, a book and a bag. — A colon is used before a list.
Q: Choose the correct way to end a formal letter:
A: Yours faithfully, — The subscription of a letter ends with a comma.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
A: Dr. Bora is a doctor. — A full stop is used after the abbreviation 'Dr.'.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'he lives in guwahati'
A: He lives in Guwahati. — The first word and proper nouns (Guwahati) begin with capital letters; the sentence ends with a full stop.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'my friend and i went to school'
A: My friend and I went to school. — The pronoun 'I' is always written as a capital letter.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
A: What is your name? My name is Rina. — A new sentence after a question mark begins with a capital letter.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence (avoiding wrong apostrophe):
A: The cats are sleeping. — Apostrophes are not used to form simple plurals.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence (question in quotation):
A: He asked, "Who are you?" — The question mark stays inside the quotation marks.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated expression:
A: Well done! — 'Well done' expresses praise, so it ends with an exclamation mark.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
A: She is twenty-one years old. — Compound numbers from twenty-one to ninety-nine take a hyphen.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
A: He is a well-known singer. — A compound adjective before a noun takes a hyphen.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'Although he was tired he kept working'
A: Although he was tired, he kept working. — A comma separates the subordinate clause from the main clause.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'oh what a pity'
A: Oh, what a pity! — An interjection like 'Oh' is followed by a comma.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'Rina come here'
A: Rina, come here. — A noun in direct address is separated by a comma.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'After the rain the ground was wet'
A: After the rain, the ground was wet. — An introductory phrase is followed by a comma.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'may i come in'
A: May I come in? — It is a polite question, so it ends with a question mark.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence (reporting statement):
A: She said that she was ill. — No quotation marks or comma are used in indirect speech.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
A: Raju — my best friend — is coming today. — Dashes set off an added explanation in the middle of a sentence.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated question tag:
A: You are tired, aren't you? — A comma separates the statement from the question tag.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
A: What's your name? — 'What's' is the contraction of 'What is'.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'its raining'
A: It's raining. — 'It's' = 'It is' (contraction with apostrophe).
Q: Fill in the blank with the correct form: 'The dog wagged ___ tail.'
A: its — 'Its' (no apostrophe) shows possession.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'she said i like tea'
A: She said, "I like tea." — The reporting verb is followed by a comma and the quote begins with a capital letter.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'how strange that he left'
A: How strange that he left! — It expresses wonder, so it ends with an exclamation mark.
Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'we visited delhi agra and jaipur'
A: We visited Delhi, Agra and Jaipur. — Proper nouns begin with capitals and list items are separated by commas.
Q: Which punctuation mark is used at the end of an interrogative sentence?
A: Question mark (?) — Question mark (?)
Q: The mark (') used to show possession or to form contractions is called the ___.
A: Apostrophe — Apostrophe
Q: Why is punctuation important in competitive exams?
A: Punctuation decides meaning and is tested inside error-spotting, sentence-improvement and direct-speech questions. A wrong comma or apostrophe changes the sense of a sentence and loses marks.
Q: When should I use a semicolon instead of a comma?
A: Use a semicolon to join two independent clauses that are closely related and have no conjunction, and to separate list items that already contain commas.
Q: What is a comma splice?
A: It is the error of joining two independent clauses with only a comma. Replace the comma with a semicolon or add a coordinating conjunction.
Q: Where does the punctuation go with quotation marks?
A: When the punctuation belongs to the quoted words, place it inside the closing quotation mark, as in "She said, 'I am ready.'".
Q: Do I need a comma after an introductory adverb clause?
A: Yes. When an adverb clause comes at the beginning of a sentence, a comma follows it, as in "When the bell rang, we left".
Q: প্ৰতিযোগিতামূলক পৰীক্ষাত যতিচিহ্ন কিয় গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: যতিচিহ্নই অৰ্থ নিৰ্ণয় কৰে আৰু error spotting, sentence improvement তথা প্ৰত্যক্ষ উক্তিৰ প্ৰশ্নত ইয়াক পৰীক্ষা কৰা হয়। ভুল comma বা apostrophe এ বাক্যৰ অৰ্থ সলনি কৰি নম্বৰ হেৰুৱায়।
Q: Comma ৰ পৰিৱৰ্তে কেতিয়া semicolon ব্যৱহাৰ কৰিম?
A: ঘনিষ্ঠভাৱে সম্পৰ্কিত আৰু conjunction নথকা দুটা independent clause যুক্ত কৰিবলৈ, আৰু আগতেই comma থকা তালিকাৰ পদ আতৰাবলৈ semicolon ব্যৱহাৰ কৰক।
Q: Comma splice কি?
A: কেৱল comma ৰে দুটা independent clause যুক্ত কৰাৰ ভুলক comma splice বোলে। Comma টো semicolon লৈ সলনি কৰক বা coordinating conjunction যোগ কৰক।
Q: Quotation mark ৰ লগত যতিচিহ্ন ক'ত পৰে?
A: যেতিয়া যতিচিহ্ন উদ্ধৃত শব্দৰ হয়, তেতিয়া ইয়াক উদ্ধৃতিৰ ভিতৰত ৰাখক, যেনে "She said, 'I am ready.'"।
Q: আৰম্ভণিৰ adverb clause ৰ পিছত comma লাগে নেকি?
A: লাগে। Adverb clause বাক্যৰ আৰম্ভণিত থাকিলে তাৰ পিছত comma পৰে, যেনে "When the bell rang, we left"।

### Types of Sentences Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/english/sentence-structure/types-of-sentences/
Summary: Practice types of sentences questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Which type of sentence is: 'The sun rises in the east.'
A: Declarative — It makes a statement or gives information.
Q: Which type of sentence is: 'Please close the door.'
A: Imperative — It expresses a request (a kind of imperative sentence).
Q: Which type of sentence is: 'What a beautiful picture it is!'
A: Exclamatory — It expresses a sudden feeling of wonder.
Q: Which type of sentence is: 'Where do you live?'
A: Interrogative — It asks a question.
Q: Which type of sentence is: 'May you live long!'
A: Optative — It expresses a wish or prayer.
Q: Which type of sentence is: 'Help me, please.'
A: Imperative — It is a request made in the imperative form.
Q: A sentence that asks a question is called an ___ sentence.
A: Interrogative — Interrogative sentences ask questions.
Q: An assertive sentence is also called a ___ sentence.
A: Declarative — Assertive and declarative sentences both state a fact.
Q: Which of the following is a declarative sentence?
A: The earth is round. — It states a plain fact.
Q: Which of the following is an imperative sentence?
A: Don't make a noise. — It gives a negative command (prohibition).
Q: Change into an exclamatory sentence: 'He is a very honest man.'
A: What an honest man he is! — Pattern: What + a/an + adjective + noun + subject + verb!
Q: Change into an assertive sentence: 'What a beautiful flower it is!'
A: It is a very beautiful flower. — 'Very' is used in place of 'what a/an' in the assertive form.
Q: Change into an interrogative sentence: 'No one can deny that he is honest.'
A: Can anyone deny that he is honest? — A negative assertive sentence turns into a positive interrogative one.
Q: Change into an assertive sentence: 'Am I a fool?'
A: I am not a fool. — This rhetorical question means a negative assertion.
Q: Change into an imperative sentence: 'You should not waste time.'
A: Do not waste time. — A prohibition is expressed with 'Do not + base verb'.
Q: Which of the following is an optative sentence?
A: May God bless you! — It expresses a blessing/prayer.
Q: Which of the following is an exclamatory sentence?
A: How fast he runs! — It shows a sudden feeling using 'How'.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'An imperative sentence expresses a ___, a request or advice.'
A: command — Imperative sentences express commands, requests or advice.
Q: 'Don't waste time.' is a ___ sentence.
A: negative imperative — It is a command in the negative form.
Q: A sentence which expresses a sudden strong feeling is called a/an ___ sentence.
A: Exclamatory — Sudden feelings (joy, sorrow, wonder) are expressed by exclamatory sentences.
Q: A sentence that has only one subject and one finite verb is called a ___ sentence.
A: Simple — A simple sentence has one main clause only.
Q: A sentence that has two or more main clauses joined by a conjunction is a ___ sentence.
A: Compound — A compound sentence joins main clauses with and/but/or.
Q: A sentence that has one main clause and one or more subordinate clauses is a ___ sentence.
A: Complex — A complex sentence contains a subordinate clause.
Q: Identify the kind of sentence: 'He came home and slept.'
A: Compound — Two main clauses are joined by 'and'.
Q: Identify the kind of sentence: 'He is so weak that he cannot walk.'
A: Complex — Main clause + subordinate clause ('that he cannot walk').
Q: Identify the kind of sentence: 'He is too weak to walk.'
A: Simple — The phrase 'too...to' has no finite verb, so it is a simple sentence.
Q: Identify the kind of sentence: 'I know that he is honest.'
A: Complex — It has a main clause and a noun clause ('that he is honest').
Q: Identify the kind of sentence: 'Work hard or you will fail.'
A: Compound — Two clauses are joined by 'or'.
Q: Identify the kind of sentence: 'The boy who stole the pen was punished.'
A: Complex — It contains an adjective clause ('who stole the pen').
Q: Which of the following is a simple sentence?
A: Being ill, he stayed at home. — Option B has only one subject and one finite verb ('being ill' is a phrase).
Q: Change into a simple sentence: 'As he was ill, he stayed at home.'
A: Being ill, he stayed at home. — The adverb clause becomes a participle phrase 'being ill'.
Q: Change into a compound sentence: 'He must work hard to pass.'
A: He must work hard or he will not pass. — The infinitive 'to pass' is converted into a second clause with 'or'.
Q: Change into a complex sentence: 'Work hard and you will pass.'
A: If you work hard, you will pass. — The first clause becomes an adverb clause of condition 'If...'.
Q: The part of the sentence about which something is said is called the ___.
A: Subject — The subject is the doer that the sentence is about.
Q: The part of the sentence that says something about the subject is the ___.
A: Predicate — The predicate begins with the verb.
Q: Identify the subject in: 'The old man walks slowly.'
A: The old man — 'The old man' is who the sentence talks about.
Q: A group of words without a finite verb is called a ___.
A: Phrase — A phrase has no subject-finite verb combination.
Q: A group of words that has a subject and a finite verb but forms only part of a sentence is a ___.
A: Clause — A clause is part of a sentence but has its own subject and verb.
Q: A group of words that makes complete sense is a ___.
A: Sentence — A sentence expresses a complete thought.
Q: Which of the following is a phrase?
A: on the table — The other options have their own subjects and verbs.
Q: Which of the following is a complete sentence?
A: The sun shines. — Only option B has a subject and a verb and makes complete sense.
Q: What kind of sentence is: 'How beautiful the sunset is!'
A: Exclamatory — An exclamatory sentence (expresses wonder).
Q: What are the four types of sentences by function?
A: They are declarative (a statement), interrogative (a question), imperative (a command or request) and exclamatory (a strong feeling). Many books add a fifth, the optative, which expresses a wish or prayer.
Q: What is the difference between a phrase and a clause?
A: A phrase is a group of related words without a subject and a verb, while a clause contains both a subject and a verb and may be independent or dependent.
Q: How do I identify a complete sentence?
A: Check for a subject and a finite verb that agree with each other and together express a complete thought. If either is missing, it is only a phrase or a fragment.
Q: What is a compound-complex sentence?
A: It contains at least two independent clauses and at least one dependent clause, combining the features of both the compound and the complex sentence.
Q: What is a comma splice?
A: It is the error of joining two independent clauses with only a comma. A coordinating conjunction or a semicolon should be used instead.
Q: কাৰ্য অনুসৰি বাক্যৰ চাৰিটা প্ৰকাৰ কি কি?
A: ঘোষণামূলক (বক্তব্য), প্ৰশ্নবোধক (প্ৰশ্ন), আদেশাত্মক (আদেশ বা অনুৰোধ) আৰু বিস্ময়সূচক (প্ৰবল ভাৱ)। বহু কিতাপে পঞ্চম আশীৰ্বাদসূচক প্ৰকাৰো যোগ কৰে, যিয়ে ইচ্ছা বা প্ৰাৰ্থনা প্ৰকাশ কৰে।
Q: Phrase আৰু clause ৰ পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: Phrase হৈছে কৰ্তা আৰু ক্ৰিয়া নথকা সম্পৰ্কিত শব্দৰ গোট, আনহাতে clause ত কৰ্তা আৰু ক্ৰিয়া দুয়ো থাকে আৰু ই স্বাধীন বা পৰাধীন হ'ব পাৰে।
Q: সম্পূৰ্ণ বাক্য কেনেকৈ চিনি পাম?
A: কৰ্তা আৰু তাৰ সৈতে মিলা finite ক্ৰিয়া আছে নে নাই চাওক, আৰু দুয়োৱে মিলি সম্পূৰ্ণ ভাৱ প্ৰকাশ কৰে নে নাই দেখক। যিকোনো এটা নাথাকিলে ই phrase বা fragment মাত্ৰ।
Q: Compound-complex বাক্য কি?
A: ইয়াত অন্ততঃ দুটা independent clause আৰু অন্ততঃ এটা dependent clause থাকে, অৰ্থাৎ compound আৰু complex ৰ লক্ষণ একত্ৰিত হয়।
Q: Comma splice কি?
A: কেৱল comma ৰে দুটা independent clause যুক্ত কৰাৰ ভুলক comma splice বোলে। তাৰ পৰিৱৰ্তে coordinating conjunction বা semicolon ব্যৱহাৰ কৰিব লাগে।

Q: What is error spotting?
A: Error spotting is a question type in which a sentence is divided into marked parts and you must identify the part that contains a grammatical, word-choice, spelling, punctuation or meaning error.
Q: Which grammar rules are most commonly tested?
A: Subject-verb agreement, tense sequence, prepositions, articles, comparison, parallelism and misplaced modifiers are the most frequently tested rules in these questions.
Q: Can the error be in meaning rather than grammar?
A: Yes. Sometimes every part is grammatical but one word reverses the meaning of the sentence or creates redundancy, such as "return back", so the sense must also be checked.
Q: How do I improve speed in error spotting?
A: Practise the core rules until they become habits, read the whole sentence once for sense, and then run a fixed checklist over agreement, tense, prepositions, articles, parallelism and modifiers.
Q: Does reading help in error spotting?
A: Yes. Reading English regularly trains the ear to notice wrong agreement and wrong prepositions quickly, and it also builds the vocabulary needed to detect meaning errors.
Q: Error spotting কি?
A: Error spotting হৈছে এনে প্ৰশ্নৰ ধৰণ য'ত বাক্যক চিহ্নিত অংশত ভাগ কৰি ব্যাকৰণ, শব্দ বাছনি, বানান, যতিচিহ্ন বা অৰ্থৰ ভুল থকা অংশ চিনাক্ত কৰিব লাগে।
Q: আটাইতকৈ বেছি কোন নিয়ম পৰীক্ষা হয়?
A: Subject-verb agreement, tense sequence, preposition, article, comparison, parallelism আৰু misplaced modifier এই প্ৰশ্নবোৰত আটাইতকৈ বেছি পৰীক্ষা কৰা নিয়ম।
Q: ভুলটো ব্যাকৰণৰ সলনি অৰ্থৰ হ'ব পাৰেনে?
A: পাৰে। কেতিয়াবা প্ৰতিটো অংশ ব্যাকৰণগতভাৱে শুদ্ধ কিন্তু এটা শব্দই অৰ্থ ওলোটা কৰে বা redundancy ৰচে, যেনে "return back", গতিকে অৰ্থও পৰীক্ষা কৰিব লাগে।
Q: Error spotting ত গতি কেনেকৈ বঢ়াম?
A: মূল নিয়মবোৰ অভ্যাস কৰি সেয়া স্বভাৱ কৰি লওক, গোটেই বাক্য এবাৰ পঢ়ি অৰ্থ লওক, তাৰ পিছত agreement, tense, preposition, article, parallelism আৰু modifier ৰ নিৰ্দিষ্ট checklist চলাওক।
Q: পঢ়া-শুনাই error spotting ত সহায় কৰেনে?
A: হয়। নিয়মীয়াকৈ ইংৰাজী পঢ়িলে কাণে ভুল agreement আৰু ভুল preposition দ্ৰুতভাৱে ধৰে, লগতে অৰ্থৰ ভুল ধৰিবলৈ প্ৰয়োজনীয় শব্দভাণ্ডাৰও গঢ়ে।

Q: What is an idiom?
A: An idiom is a fixed group of words whose meaning cannot be understood from the individual words, such as "break the ice", which means to start a conversation.
Q: Why can an idiom not be changed?
A: Because the meaning belongs to the whole expression, changing or reordering the words destroys it. "Let the cat out of the bag" cannot become "let the dog out of the bag".
Q: What is the difference between an idiom and a proverb?
A: An idiom names a situation or idea, while a proverb is a short saying that offers general advice or a truth, such as "Strike while the iron is hot".
Q: How are phrasal verbs related to idioms?
A: A phrasal verb behaves like an idiom because its meaning is not the sum of its parts. "Give up" means to quit, and "put off" means to postpone, so the particle must be learnt with the verb.
Q: How should I memorise idioms for the exam?
A: Learn each idiom with its meaning and one example sentence, picture its literal scene, and revise in small groups. Grouping phrasal verbs by their main verb also helps to avoid confusion.
Q: Idiom কি?
A: Idiom হৈছে শব্দৰ এটা নিৰ্দিষ্ট গোট যাৰ অৰ্থ শব্দবোৰৰ পৰা বুজিব নোৱাৰি, যেনে "break the ice" ৰ অৰ্থ কথা আৰম্ভ কৰা।
Q: Idiom কিয় সলনি কৰিব নোৱাৰি?
A: কাৰণ অৰ্থ সম্পূৰ্ণ প্ৰকাশৰ, শব্দ সলনি বা ক্ৰম ওলোটালে নষ্ট হয়। "let the cat out of the bag" ক "let the dog out of the bag" কৰিব নোৱাৰি।
Q: Idiom আৰু proverb ৰ পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: Idiom এ পৰিস্থিতি বা ভাবৰ নাম দিয়ে, আনহাতে proverb এ সাধাৰণ সত্য বা উপদেশ দিয়া চমু প্ৰচলিত কথা, যেনে "Strike while the iron is hot"।
Q: Phrasal verb আৰু idiom ৰ সম্পৰ্ক কি?
A: Phrasal verb এ idiom ৰ দৰে কাম কৰে কাৰণ তাৰ অৰ্থ অংশবোৰৰ যোগফল নহয়। "give up" ৰ অৰ্থ এৰি দিয়া, "put off" ৰ অৰ্থ পিছুৱাই দিয়া, গতিকে particle ক্ৰিয়াৰ লগত শিকিব লাগে।
Q: পৰীক্ষাৰ বাবে idiom কেনেকৈ মনত ৰাখিম?
A: প্ৰতিটো idiom অৰ্থ আৰু এটা উদাহৰণ বাক্যসহ শিকি আক্ষৰিক দৃশ্য কল্পনা কৰক আৰু সৰু গোটত পুনৰালোচনা কৰক। Phrasal verb মূল ক্ৰিয়া অনুসৰি গোটালে বিভ্ৰান্তি কম।

Q: What is one word substitution?
A: One word substitution means replacing a longer phrase or clause with a single exact word, such as using "atheist" for a person who does not believe in God.
Q: How can I remember so many words?
A: Learn the common roots and suffixes first, and group words into families of persons, places, studies and qualities. This lets you decode and recall words far faster than memorising a plain list.
Q: What is the difference between an apiary and an aviary?
A: An apiary is a place where bees are kept, while an aviary is a place where birds are kept. Such place words are often paired in exam options to test exact knowledge.
Q: Do all substitutions end in a suffix?
A: Most do, such as "-logy" for a study, "-phobia" for a fear and "-cide" for killing, but some are simple words. The suffix is a strong clue, not a rule.
Q: Which substitutions are most important for Assam exams?
A: Words for persons and studies built on Greek and Latin roots, such as bibliophile, xenophobia, misanthrope and philanthropy, are the most frequently asked and should be learnt first.
Q: One word substitution কি?
A: One word substitution মানে দীঘল পদ বা clause ৰ ঠাইত এটা সঠিক শব্দ ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা, যেনে ঈশ্বৰত অবিশ্বাসী ব্যক্তিৰ বাবে "atheist"।
Q: ইমান শব্দ কেনেকৈ মনত ৰাখিম?
A: আগতে সাধাৰণ root আৰু suffix শিকি ব্যক্তি, স্থান, বিদ্যা, গুণ পৰিয়ালত শব্দ গোটাওক। ইয়াৰ দ্বাৰা শব্দ ভাঙি মনত ৰখাটো সাধাৰণ তালিকাতকৈ বহু দ্ৰুত হয়।
Q: Apiary আৰু aviary ৰ পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: Apiary হৈছে মৌমাখি ৰখা ঠাই, আনহাতে aviary হৈছে চৰাই ৰখা ঠাই। এনে স্থানৰ শব্দ প্ৰায়ে সঠিক জ্ঞান পৰীক্ষা কৰিবলৈ যোৰ পাতি দিয়া হয়।
Q: সকলো substitution suffix ৰে শেষ হয়নে?
A: বেছিভাগ হয়, যেনে বিদ্যাৰ বাবে "-logy", ভয়ৰ বাবে "-phobia", বধৰ বাবে "-cide", কিন্তু কিছু সাধাৰণ শব্দ। Suffix শক্তিশালী সংকেত, নিয়ম নহয়।
Q: অসমৰ পৰীক্ষাৰ বাবে কোন substitution বেছি গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: Greek-Latin root ৰ ব্যক্তি আৰু বিদ্যাৰ শব্দ, যেনে bibliophile, xenophobia, misanthrope, philanthropy আটাইতকৈ বেছি সোধা হয় আৰু আগতে শিকা উচিত।

Q: What is sentence rearrangement?
A: Sentence rearrangement means arranging jumbled words, phrases or sentences in the correct order so that they form a meaningful, coherent whole.
Q: How do I find the first sentence?
A: The first sentence introduces the topic and needs no earlier reference. It usually contains no pronoun such as "he" or "this" and no connector such as "however" or "therefore".
Q: What role do connectors play?
A: Connectors carry the logic of the passage. Words like "however", "therefore", "first" and "finally" tell you whether the next sentence contrasts, results, adds or continues, and so fix the order.
Q: Why must a pronoun not come before its noun?
A: A pronoun stands for a noun that must already have appeared. If a sentence begins with "this problem", the problem must have been described earlier, so that sentence cannot come first.
Q: How can I improve accuracy quickly?
A: Practise short passages daily, scan for pronouns and connectors first, and always read the final order as one passage to check that it flows before marking the answer.
Q: Sentence rearrangement কি?
A: Sentence rearrangement মানে এলমেলি দিয়া শব্দ, পদ বা বাক্যবোৰ সঠিক ক্ৰমত সজাই অৰ্থপূৰ্ণ, সংহত গোট কৰা।
Q: প্ৰথম বাক্য কেনেকৈ বিচাৰিম?
A: প্ৰথম বাক্যই বিষয় আৰম্ভ কৰে আৰু আগৰ উল্লেখ নালাগে। ই সাধাৰণতে "he" বা "this" ৰ দৰে pronoun আৰু "however" বা "therefore" ৰ দৰে connector ৰে আৰম্ভ নহয়।
Q: Connector ৰ ভূমিকা কি?
A: Connector এ অনুচ্ছেদৰ যুক্তি বহন কৰে। "however", "therefore", "first", "finally" ৰ দৰে শব্দই পিছৰ বাক্যই বিপৰীত, ফলাফল, সংযোজন নে ক্ৰম CONTINUE কৰিছে কয় আৰু ক্ৰম নিৰ্ণয় কৰে।
Q: Pronoun নামৰ আগত কিয় থাকিব নোৱাৰে?
A: Pronoun এ এনে নামৰ ঠাই লয় যি আগতে আহি থাকিব লাগে। বাক্য "this problem" ৰে আৰম্ভ হ'লে সমস্যাটো আগতে বৰ্ণনা কৰা থাকিব লাগে, গতিকে সেই বাক্য প্ৰথম হ'ব নোৱাৰে।
Q: শুদ্ধতা দ্ৰুত কেনেকৈ বঢ়াম?
A: দৈনিক চুটি অনুচ্ছেদ অভ্যাস কৰক, প্ৰথমে pronoun আৰু connector বিচাৰক, আৰু উত্তৰ চিহ্নিত কৰাৰ আগতে শেষ ক্ৰমটো এটা অনুচ্ছেদ হিচাপে পঢ়ি বৈ যায় নে নাই পৰীক্ষা কৰক।

Q: What is the difference between a synonym and an antonym?
A: A synonym has the same or nearly the same meaning as the given word, while an antonym has the opposite meaning. A synonym question asks you to keep the sense; an antonym question asks you to reverse it.
Q: Do all synonyms fit in every sentence?
A: No. Two words may share a core meaning yet differ in intensity, connotation or grammatical use, so only one may fit the tone and part of speech of a particular sentence.
Q: How can I find the meaning of an unfamiliar word?
A: Use roots, prefixes and suffixes. "Bene-" means good, "mal-" means bad, "un-" reverses a meaning, and "-less" means without, so an unknown word can often be decoded from its parts.
Q: Why does context matter in these questions?
A: Many English words carry more than one meaning. The sentence decides whether "bank" means a river bank or a money bank, so the context must be read before an option is chosen.
Q: Which words are most frequently asked in Assam exams?
A: Everyday formal words such as abandon, benevolent, lucid, obsolete, frugal and ambiguous recur across papers, so these high-frequency words should be learnt with their synonyms and antonyms together.
Q: Synonym আৰু antonym ৰ পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: Synonym ৰ অৰ্থ দিয়া শব্দৰ লগত একে বা প্ৰায় একে, antonym ৰ অৰ্থ বিপৰীত। Synonym প্ৰশ্নই অৰ্থ ৰাখিবলৈ কয়, antonym প্ৰশ্নই ওলোটা কৰিবলৈ কয়।
Q: সকলো synonym প্ৰতিটো বাক্যত খাপ খায়নে?
A: নাখায়। দুটা শব্দৰ মূল অৰ্থ একে হ'লেও তীব্ৰতা, connotation বা ব্যাকৰণগত প্ৰয়োগ বেলেগ হ'ব পাৰে, গতিকে এটাহে কোনো বাক্যত খাপ খায়।
Q: অচিনাকি শব্দৰ অৰ্থ কেনেকৈ পাম?
A: Root, prefix আৰু suffix ব্যৱহাৰ কৰক। "bene-" ৰ অৰ্থ ভাল, "mal-" ৰ অৰ্থ বেয়া, "un-" এ অৰ্থ ওলোটা কৰে আৰু "-less" ৰ অৰ্থ অবিহনে, গতিকে শব্দৰ অংশৰ পৰা অৰ্থ উলিয়াব পাৰি।
Q: এই প্ৰশ্নত context ৰ গুৰুত্ব কিয়?
A: বহু ইংৰাজী শব্দৰ এটাতকৈ বেছি অৰ্থ থাকে। বাক্যয়ে "bank" নদীৰ পাৰ নে টকাৰ বেংক নিৰ্ণয় কৰে, গতিকে বিকল্প বাছনিৰ আগতে context পঢ়িব লাগে।
Q: অসমৰ পৰীক্ষাত আটাইতকৈ বেছি কোন শব্দ সোধা হয়?
A: abandon, benevolent, lucid, obsolete, frugal, ambiguous ৰ দৰে দৈনন্দিন আনুষ্ঠানিক শব্দ বছৰে বছৰে আহে, গতিকে এইবোৰ synonym আৰু antonymসহ শিকা উচিত।

### Ahom Dynasty Architecture — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/art-culture/assam-art-culture-sec/ahom-dynasty-architecture-assam/
Summary: Practice ahom dynasty architecture questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Which is the famous Ahom palace located at Garhgaon?
A: The Kareng Ghar (Gargaon Palace) is the famous Ahom palace at Garhgaon.
Q: Who built the Kareng Ghar at Gargaon?
A: The Kareng Ghar was originally built by Suklenmung (Garh Gayan) in 1540 and rebuilt by later kings.
Q: Which Ahom king shifted the capital from Gargaon to Rangpur?
A: Rudra Singha shifted the capital from Gargaon to Rangpur in the early 18th century.
Q: Which is the famous Ahom palace at Rangpur?
A: The Talatal Ghar at Rangpur is the famous Ahom palace built by Swargadeo Rudra Singha.
Q: Which is the largest and most impressive Ahom palace?
A: The Talatal Ghar is the largest and most impressive Ahom palace.
Q: What is the Talatal Ghar famous for architecturally?
A: The Talatal Ghar is famous for its underground tunnels and secret passages used for escape.
Q: Which is the famous Ahom amphitheatre at Rangpur?
A: The Rang Ghar is the famous two-storeyed Ahom amphitheatre at Rangpur.
Q: Who built the Rang Ghar?
A: The Rang Ghar was built by Swargadeo Pramatta Singha in 1746.
Q: What was the Rang Ghar used for?
A: The Rang Ghar was used as a royal pavilion for watching sports, elephant fights and cultural performances.
Q: Which is the emblem of the Assam government derived from Ahom architecture?
A: The Rang Ghar has been adopted as the emblem of the Government of Assam.
Q: Which Ahom king constructed the Kareng Ghar at Gargaon with bricks?
A: The brick construction of the Kareng Ghar was carried out by King Suklenmung.
Q: What is the name of the Ahom royal burial mounds?
A: The Ahom royal burial mounds are called 'Maidams'.
Q: Where are the royal maidams of the Ahom kings located?
A: The royal maidams are located at Charaideo, near Sivasagar.
Q: What was the Charaideo Maidam used for?
A: The Charaideo maidams were the royal burial grounds of the Ahom kings and queens.
Q: Which was the first capital of the Ahom kingdom in Assam?
A: Charaideo was the first capital of the Ahom kingdom established by Sukapha in 1253.
Q: Which style of construction is the Talatal Ghar?
A: The Talatal Ghar is an octagonal brick structure with a blend of Ahom and Mughal architectural styles.
Q: Which Ahom monument has underground storeys?
A: The Talatal Ghar has three underground storeys with secret tunnels.
Q: Which is the temple-like structure built by the Ahoms at Sivasagar?
A: The Shivdol, Joydol and Vishnudol temples at Sivasagar were built by the Ahom queen Ambika.
Q: Who built the Shivdol at Sivasagar?
A: The Shivdol was built by the Ahom queen Ambika, wife of Swargadeo Siva Singha, in 1734.
Q: Which is the tallest temple (Dol) in Assam?
A: The Shivdol at Sivasagar is the tallest temple in Assam.
Q: Which artificial tank was excavated by the Ahoms at Sivasagar?
A: The Sivasagar Tank (Borpukhuri) was excavated by the Ahom queen Ambika.
Q: Which Ahom king built the Tolatol Ghar?
A: The Tolatol Ghar is associated with the palace complex of Rangpur built by Rudra Singha.
Q: Which material was primarily used in the construction of Ahom monuments?
A: Bricks, stone and lime mortar were primarily used in Ahom construction.
Q: Which Ahom king built the Gargaon Palace with a 'multi-storeyed' design?
A: King Gadadhar Singha rebuilt the Gargaon Palace with a seven-storeyed (Kareng) design.
Q: What is the architectural style of the Rang Ghar?
A: The Rang Ghar is built in a unique style resembling a royal ship with a curved roof.
Q: Which Ahom capital was established by Sukapha?
A: Sukapha established the capital at Charaideo in 1253.
Q: What is the 'Sivasagar' also known as?
A: Sivasagar is also known as the 'City of Ahom' due to its rich Ahom monuments.
Q: Which Ahom monument resembles the shape of a 'Bengal tiger'?
A: The Rang Ghar is sometimes likened to a crouching tiger due to its shape.
Q: Which Ahom king built the 'Fakuwa Doul'?
A: The Fakuwa Doul at Sivasagar was built during the reign of the Ahom kings.
Q: Which is the main architectural legacy of the Ahoms in the Brahmaputra valley?
A: The palaces, maidams, tanks and temples at Gargaon, Rangpur and Sivasagar form the main legacy.
Q: Which Ahom monument is a World Heritage site (tentative)?
A: The Charaideo Maidams have been included in the UNESCO World Heritage tentative list and inscribed in 2024.
Q: What is the shape of the Kareng Ghar's central structure?
A: The Kareng Ghar has a rectangular, multi-tiered structure with arched doorways.
Q: Which Ahom king's reign saw the construction of many brick temples at Sivasagar?
A: The reign of Siva Singha and Queen Ambika saw the construction of many brick temples at Sivasagar.
Q: Which structure served as the royal pavilion for the Ahom kings during the Rongali Bihu?
A: The Rang Ghar served as the royal pavilion from which the Ahom kings watched games and celebrations.
Q: What is the construction material of the Talatal Ghar?
A: The Talatal Ghar is built of bricks and stone, with wooden beams in its interior.
Q: Which are the main Ahom monuments and where are they located?
A: The main Ahom monuments are the Kareng Ghar at Gargaon, the Talatal Ghar and the Rang Ghar at Rangpur near Sivasagar, the Sivadol, Joydol and Devidol at Sivasagar, and the Maidams at Charaideo. The Talatal Ghar is the largest Ahom palace and the Rang Ghar is the royal amphitheatre.
Q: Who built the Rang Ghar and what was it used for?
A: The Rang Ghar was built by King Pramatta Singha in the eighteenth century. It served as the royal pavilion from which the Ahom kings watched sports, elephant fights and cultural performances. It is regarded as one of the oldest surviving amphitheatres in Asia and is the emblem of the Government of Assam.
Q: What are the Charaideo Maidams and why are they important?
A: The Charaideo Maidams are the royal burial mounds of the Ahom kings and queens. Charaideo was the first Ahom capital, established by Sukapha in 1253. The Moidams were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2024, making them the first World Heritage cultural site in Assam.
Q: Who built the Sivasagar Sivadol and the Sivasagar tank?
A: The Sivasagar Sivadol, the tallest temple in Assam, was built by Queen Ambika, the wife of King Siva Singha, in 1734. The Sivasagar tank or Borpukhuri was also excavated by Queen Ambika in memory of her husband.
Q: Which materials and styles were used in Ahom architecture?
A: Ahom buildings mainly used bricks and lime mortar because good building stone was scarce in the Assam valley. Their architecture is a synthesis of the Tai tradition of the rulers, the local Assamese tradition and Mughal influences, and it features arches, domes, multi-storeyed structures and underground chambers.
Q: প্ৰধান আহোম স্মৃতিসৌধসমূহ কি কি আৰু ক'ত অৱস্থিত?
A: প্ৰধান আহোম স্মৃতিসৌধসমূহ হৈছে গড়গাঁৱৰ কৰেং ঘৰ, শিৱসাগৰৰ ওচৰত ৰংপুৰৰ তলাতল ঘৰ আৰু ৰং ঘৰ, শিৱসাগৰৰ শিৱদৌল, জয়দৌল তথা দেৱীদৌল, আৰু চৰাইদেউৰ মৈদাম। তলাতল ঘৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ আহোম প্ৰাসাদ আৰু ৰং ঘৰ ৰাজকীয় ৰংগশালা।
Q: ৰং ঘৰ কোনে নিৰ্মাণ কৰিছিল আৰু ইয়াৰ ব্যৱহাৰ কি আছিল?
A: ৰং ঘৰ অষ্টাদশ শতিকাত ৰজা প্ৰমত্ত সিংহে নিৰ্মাণ কৰিছিল। ই ৰাজকীয় মণ্ডপ হিচাপে কাম কৰিছিল, যাৰপৰা আহোম ৰজাসকলে খেল, হাতী যুঁজ তথা সাংস্কৃতিক পৰিৱেশন চাইছিল। ই এছিয়াৰ আটাইতকৈ প্ৰাচীন জীৱন্ত ৰংগশালাসমূহৰ এটা হিচাপে গণ্য কৰা হয় আৰু অসম চৰকাৰৰ প্ৰতীক।
Q: চৰাইদেউ মৈদাম কি আৰু কিয় গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: চৰাইদেউ মৈদাম হৈছে আহোম ৰজা তথা ৰাণীসকলৰ ৰাজকীয় সমাধি-ঢিপি। চৰাইদেউ প্ৰথম আহোম ৰাজধানী, যি চুকাফাই ১২৫৩ চনত স্থাপন কৰিছিল। মৈদামসমূহ ২০২৪ চনত ইউনেস্কো বিশ্ব ঐতিহ্য ক্ষেত্ৰ হিচাপে খোদিত হৈছিল, যাৰ ফলত এইবোৰ অসমৰ প্ৰথম বিশ্ব ঐতিহ্য সাংস্কৃতিক ক্ষেত্ৰ হৈ পৰিছে।
Q: শিৱসাগৰ শিৱদৌল আৰু শিৱসাগৰ টেংকী কোনে নিৰ্মাণ কৰিছিল?
A: শিৱসাগৰ শিৱদৌল, অসমৰ আটাইতকৈ ওখ মন্দিৰ, ৰজা শিৱ সিংহৰ পত্নী ৰাণী অম্বিকাই ১৭৩৪ চনত নিৰ্মাণ কৰিছিল। শিৱসাগৰ টেংকী বা বৰপুখুৰীও ৰাণী অম্বিকাই তেওঁৰ স্বামীৰ স্মৃতিত খন্দাইছিল।
Q: আহোম স্থাপত্যত কি সামগ্ৰী তথা শৈলী ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা হৈছিল?
A: অসম উপত্যকাত ভাল নিৰ্মাণ শিল দুৰ্লভ হোৱাৰ বাবে আহোম অট্টালিকাই মূলতঃ ইটা আৰু চূণৰ চূৰ্ণ ব্যৱহাৰ কৰিছিল। তেওঁলোকৰ স্থাপত্য শাসকসকলৰ তাই পৰম্পৰা, স্থানীয় অসমীয়া পৰম্পৰা আৰু মোগল প্ৰভাৱৰ সংমিশ্ৰণ, আৰু ইয়াত খিলান, গম্বুজ, বহুতলীয়া গঠন তথা মাটিৰ তলৰ কোঠা আছে।

### Assamese Literature & Historical Chronicles (Buranjis)
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/art-culture/assam-art-culture-sec/assamese-literature-buranjis-culture/
Summary: Practice assamese literature & historical chronicles (buranjis) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free.
Q: What is the earliest specimen of Assamese literature?
A: The Charyapada, a collection of Buddhist mystical songs, is the earliest specimen of Assamese literature.
Q: Who is known as the father of Assamese literature?
A: Srimanta Sankardeva is known as the father of Assamese literature.
Q: Which is the most famous work of Sankardeva?
A: The Kirtan Ghosa is the most famous work of Sankardeva.
Q: Who wrote the 'Namghosa'?
A: The Namghosa was written by Mahapurusha Madhavdeva.
Q: Which is the first Assamese translation of the Ramayana?
A: The Saptakanda Ramayana by Madhava Kandali is the first Assamese translation of the Ramayana.
Q: Who wrote the 'Saptakanda Ramayana'?
A: Madhava Kandali wrote the Saptakanda Ramayana in the 14th century.
Q: What is a Buranji?
A: A Buranji is a historical chronicle or record maintained by the Ahom administration.
Q: In which language were the earliest Buranjis written?
A: The earliest Buranjis were written in the Tai (Ahom) language.
Q: Which Buranji is the most important for the reign of Sukapha?
A: The 'Assam Buranji' and the 'Chutiya Buranji' are important, with the Ahom Buranji covering early reigns.
Q: Who compiled the first systematic history of Assam in English?
A: Edward Gait wrote 'A History of Assam' (1905), the first systematic history of Assam.
Q: Who is the author of the 'Buranji Vivek Ratna'?
A: The 'Buranji Vivek Ratna' was written by the Ahom scholar Kasinath Tamuli Phukan.
Q: Which is the first Assamese newspaper?
A: The Orunodoi, published in 1846 by the American Baptist Mission, is the first Assamese periodical.
Q: Who is known as the 'Pioneer of Assamese Prose'?
A: Anandaram Dhekial Phukan is known as the pioneer of Assamese prose.
Q: Who wrote the famous 'Assam Buranji' in the early 19th century?
A: The 'Assam Buranji' was written by Kashinath Tamuli Phukan.
Q: Who is the author of 'Buranji Vivak Ratna'?
A: The 'Buranji Vivak Ratna' was authored by Kasinath Tamuli Phukan.
Q: Which Assamese writer is known as the 'Sahityarathi'?
A: Lakshminath Bezbaroa is known as the 'Sahityarathi' (Charioteer of Literature).
Q: Who is the founder of the Assamese novel?
A: Lakshminath Bezbaroa is regarded as the founder of the Assamese novel.
Q: Which is the first Assamese novel?
A: 'Mirijiyori' by Rajanikanta Bordoloi is considered the first Assamese novel (1894).
Q: Who is called the 'Bard of Brahmaputra'?
A: Bishnu Prasad Rabha is affectionately called the 'Bard of Brahmaputra'.
Q: Who is the first Assamese woman novelist?
A: Indira Goswami (Mamoni Raisom Goswami) is one of the most celebrated Assamese novelists.
Q: Which Assamese writer won the Jnanpith Award?
A: Indira Goswami won the Jnanpith Award in 2000 for her contribution to Assamese literature.
Q: Who is known as the 'Xatraiya Kabya' poet?
A: The early Vaishnavite poets like Sankardeva and Madhavdeva are known for devotional poetry.
Q: Who wrote the first Assamese grammar in Assamese?
A: The first Assamese grammar was written in the form of the 'Katha Gosha' by Bhattadeva, and later grammars by missionaries.
Q: Who is the father of Assamese prose?
A: Bhattadeva (Bhatta Dev) is considered the father of Assamese prose.
Q: Which work is Bhattadeva famous for?
A: Bhattadeva is famous for the 'Katha Bhagavat' and 'Katha Gita', early works of Assamese prose.
Q: Who wrote the 'Burhanjis' in the Ahom era?
A: The official chroniclers called 'Phukans' and the royal scribes wrote the Buranjis.
Q: Which is the longest poem of Assamese literature?
A: The 'Kirtan Ghosa' is considered one of the longest and most important devotional works.
Q: Who is the author of 'Khargosh' satire?
A: Lakshminath Bezbaroa is famous for his satirical essays in the 'Burhi Aair Xadhu' and other works.
Q: Which is the famous collection of folk tales by Lakshminath Bezbaroa?
A: The 'Burhi Aair Xadhu' is the famous collection of folk tales by Lakshminath Bezbaroa.
Q: Who is the first Assamese poet to write in free verse?
A: Amulya Barua is considered the first Assamese poet to write in free verse.
Q: Which Buranji records the battle of Saraighat?
A: The 'Purani Asom Buranji' and the Ahom Buranjis record the events including the battle of Saraighat.
Q: Who wrote the 'Deodhai Buranji'?
A: The 'Deodhai Buranji' was written by the royal astrologers and priests of the Ahom court.
Q: Which is the first drama of Assamese literature?
A: The 'Chihna Yatra' of Sankardeva is the first drama of Assamese literature.
Q: Who is the author of 'Miri Jiyori'?
A: Rajanikanta Bordoloi wrote 'Miri Jiyori'.
Q: Which Assamese poet is known for the 'Xongkiar' or the bards of the Sattras?
A: The devotional poets of the Vaishnavite Sattras, beginning with Sankardeva, are known as the bardic poets.
Q: What is the earliest specimen of Assamese literature?
A: The Charyapada is the earliest specimen of Assamese literature. It is a collection of Buddhist mystical songs composed between the eighth and twelfth centuries and was discovered by Haraprasad Shastri in Nepal.
Q: Who wrote the first Assamese Ramayana and what is it called?
A: The first Assamese Ramayana, called the Saptakanda Ramayana, was written by Madhava Kandali in the fourteenth century. It is one of the earliest full Ramayanas in any modern Indian language.
Q: What is a Buranji?
A: A Buranji is a historical chronicle of the Ahom kingdom written by official chroniclers called Phukans and by royal scribes. The earliest Buranjis were written in Tai-Ahom and were later translated into Assamese.
Q: Who is the father of Assamese prose and what did he write?
A: Bhattadeva is regarded as the father of Assamese prose. He translated the Bhagavata Purana into prose in works such as the Katha Bhagavat and the Katha Gita.
Q: Who is the Sahityarathi of Assamese literature?
A: Lakshminath Bezbaroa is known as the Sahityarathi, or charioteer of Assamese literature. He is the founder of the Assamese novel and wrote the famous folk-tale collection Burhi Aair Xadhu.
Q: অসমীয়া সাহিত্যৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি নিদৰ্শন কি?
A: চৰ্যাপদ অসমীয়া সাহিত্যৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি নিদৰ্শন। ই অষ্টমৰপৰা দ্বাদশ শতিকাৰ ভিতৰত ৰচিত বৌদ্ধ ৰহস্যময় গীতৰ সংগ্ৰহ আৰু হৰপ্ৰসাদ শাস্ত্ৰীয়ে নেপালত আৱিষ্কাৰ কৰিছিল।
Q: প্ৰথম অসমীয়া ৰামায়ণ কোনে লিখিছিল আৰু ইয়াৰ নাম কি?
A: প্ৰথম অসমীয়া ৰামায়ণ, যাক সপ্তকাণ্ড ৰামায়ণ বোলা হয়, মাধৱ কন্দলীয়ে চতুৰ্দশ শতিকাত লিখিছিল। ই যিকোনো আধুনিক ভাৰতীয় ভাষাৰ আটাইতকৈ প্ৰাচীন পূৰ্ণ ৰামায়ণসমূহৰ এটা।
Q: বুৰঞ্জী কি?
A: বুৰঞ্জী হৈছে আহোম ৰাজ্যৰ ঐতিহাসিক বৰ্ণনা, যি ফুকন নামৰ চৰকাৰী ইতিহাসকাৰ তথা ৰাজকীয় লিপিকৰসকলে লিখিছিল। আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি বুৰঞ্জীসমূহ তাই-আহোমত লিখা হৈছিল আৰু পিছত অসমীয়ালৈ অনুবাদ কৰা হৈছিল।
Q: অসমীয়া গদ্যৰ পিতৃ কোন আৰু তেওঁ কি লিখিছিল?
A: ভট্টদেৱক অসমীয়া গদ্যৰ পিতৃ হিচাপে গণ্য কৰা হয়। তেওঁ কথাভাগৱত তথা কথাগীতাৰ দৰে কৰ্মত ভাগৱত পুৰাণক গদ্যলৈ অনুবাদ কৰিছিল।
Q: অসমীয়া সাহিত্যৰ সাহিত্যৰথী কোন?
A: লক্ষ্মীনাথ বেজবৰুৱাক সাহিত্যৰথী বোলা হয়। তেওঁ অসমীয়া উপন্যাসৰ প্ৰতিষ্ঠাপক তথা বিখ্যাত লোককথা সংগ্ৰহ বুঢ়ী আইৰ সাধুৰ লেখক।

### Bihu Festival Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/art-culture/assam-art-culture-sec/bihu-festival/
Summary: Bihu festival questions with answers for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Covers the three Bihus, Bihu dances, folk songs and the culture of the festival.
Q: How many Bihus are celebrated in Assam?
A: Assam celebrates three Bihus: Bohag or Rongali Bihu, Kati or Kongali Bihu, and Magh or Bhogali Bihu.
Q: Which Bihu marks the Assamese New Year?
A: Bohag Bihu, also called Rongali Bihu, is celebrated in mid-April and marks the Assamese New Year.
Q: Which instruments are used in Bihu dance?
A: The main instruments are the dhol, pepa, taal, gagana and toka, along with the Bihu songs sung by the dancers.

### Classical & Folk Dances Questions — Assam Art Culture
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/art-culture/assam-art-culture-sec/classical-folk-dances-assam/
Summary: Assam Art Culture practice: free classical & folk dances questions with answers for Assam competitive exams.
Q: Which classical dance form of India originated in Assam?
A: Sattriya dance, one of the eight classical dance forms of India, originated in Assam.
Q: Who is credited with the origin of Sattriya dance?
A: Srimanta Sankardeva is credited with the origin of Sattriya dance in the 15th-16th century.
Q: In which year was Sattriya dance recognised as a classical dance by the Sangeet Natak Akademi?
A: Sattriya dance was recognised as a classical dance by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000.
Q: What is the dance-drama form created by Sankardeva called?
A: The dance-drama form created by Sankardeva is called Ankiya Naat, performed in Bhaona.
Q: Which instrument is essential for Sattriya dance performances?
A: The Khol (drum) and cymbals (tal) are essential instruments for Sattriya dance.
Q: Which Assamese folk dance is associated with the Bihu festival?
A: The Bihu dance is the most popular folk dance associated with the Bihu festival.
Q: Who generally performs the Bihu dance in Assam?
A: Bihu dance is mainly performed by young men and women, with the youth dressed in traditional attire.
Q: Which is the folk dance of the Bodo community?
A: Bagurumba is the famous folk dance of the Bodo community of Assam.
Q: Which community performs the Jhumur dance?
A: The Jhumur dance is performed by the tea tribe (tea garden) communities of Assam.
Q: What is the Ojapali dance form associated with?
A: Ojapali is a traditional performing art combining music, dance and narration, associated with folk epics.
Q: Which dance form is performed during the Deodhani ritual?
A: The Deodhani dance is performed during rituals associated with the worship of Goddess Manasa.
Q: Which community of Assam performs the Deodhani dance?
A: The Deodhani dance is associated with the Maroi community and the Ojapali tradition.
Q: What is the traditional dance of the Mising community?
A: The Misings perform dances like the Ali-Ai-Ligang dance, a ritual dance of their festival.
Q: Which is the dance performed by the Karbi community?
A: The Karbi community performs dances like the Ajoi and Bairang dances.
Q: Which dance is associated with the Rabha community?
A: The Rabha community performs the Chorchori (Kham) dance during their festivals.
Q: What is the significance of the Gayan-Bayan in Sattriya performance?
A: Gayan-Bayan are the musicians and dancers who perform the preliminary 'Ghosa' before the main Sattriya item.
Q: Which costume is worn during the Sattriya dance?
A: Male dancers wear the 'Chhapa' dress with turbans while female performers wear silk mekhela-sador.
Q: Which festival of Assam prominently features the Jhumur dance?
A: The Jhumur dance is prominently performed during the tea garden community's 'Tusu' and Karam festivals.
Q: What is the name of the dance performed by the Sonowal Kachari community?
A: The Sonowal Kacharis perform the 'Boro' or 'Bathow' dance during their festivals.
Q: Which dance form is associated with the worship of Krishna in the Sattras?
A: The Sattriya Nritya and the Ankiya Naat are associated with the worship of Krishna.
Q: What is the dance form of the Tiwa community called?
A: The Tiwa community performs dances like the 'Nrikri' and 'Deori' dances during festivals.
Q: Which dance of the Dimasa community is performed during their festivals?
A: The Dimasa community performs the 'Baidi' dance during their festivals like Bushu.
Q: What is the dance of the Deuri community associated with?
A: The Deuri community's dances are associated with their animistic rituals and agricultural festivals.
Q: Which is the popular dance of the Goalpara region of Assam?
A: The Goalpariya dance, performed with local instruments, is popular in the Goalpara region.
Q: Which musical style is used in the Sattriya dance?
A: The Sattriya dance uses the Borgeet and Ankiya Nat music composed by Sankardeva and Madhavdeva.
Q: Which festival celebrates the classical heritage of Assam's dances?
A: The 'Sattriya Samaroh' and the Sankardeva Jayanti celebrations highlight Assam's classical dance heritage.
Q: What is the dance performed during the Magh Bihu called?
A: During Magh Bihu, the Bihu dance and the 'Sokotoni' dance are performed near the community bonfire (Meji).
Q: Which is the dance-drama form performed by the Oja with his palis?
A: Ojapali is the narrative dance-drama performed by the Oja (lead) with his palis (assistants).
Q: Which costume is associated with the Bihu dance of women?
A: Women wear the traditional Mekhela Sador with a Gamosa tied around the waist and headgear.
Q: Which dance is performed by the Garo community in Assam?
A: The Garo community performs the 'Porda' and 'Wangala' dances during their harvest festival.
Q: What is the role of the Sutradhar in an Ankiya Bhaona performance?
A: The Sutradhar is the narrator-conductor who introduces the story and directs the Bhaona performance.
Q: Which dance form of Assam uses masks extensively?
A: The 'Mukha Nritya' (mask dance) of the Sattras, especially from Samaguri Satra, uses masks extensively.
Q: Which community performs the 'Lakhar' or 'Fakira' dance?
A: The 'Lakhar' dance is performed by the followers of the Fakir sect, mainly in the lower Assam region.
Q: Which dance celebrates the agricultural cycle of paddy cultivation?
A: The Bihu dance celebrates the agricultural cycle, especially the harvesting and sowing seasons.
Q: What is the 'Husori' performance during Bohag Bihu?
A: Husori is the group song and dance performed by male troupes visiting homes during Bohag Bihu.
Q: Which is the classical dance of Assam and who introduced it?
A: Sattriya is the classical dance of Assam. It was introduced by the Vaishnava saint and reformer Srimanta Sankardeva in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries as a part of the Ankiya Naat performed in the Sattras. It received formal recognition as a classical dance in the year 2000.
Q: What are the two streams of Sattriya dance?
A: Sattriya is performed in two streams, the Gayan-Bayan and the Kharmanar. The Gayan-Bayan is performed by male dancers or bhokots, while the Kharmanar is performed by women and has softer, more graceful movements. Both use the Khol and the Taal.
Q: Which dance is associated with Rongali Bihu and what is Husori?
A: The Bihu dance is associated with Rongali or Bohag Bihu, the spring festival of Assam. The Husori is a related tradition in which a group of male performers visits households during Bihu and sings and dances in the courtyard. The Bihu dance set a Guinness World Record in Guwahati in 2023.
Q: Bagurumba belongs to which community and festival?
A: Bagurumba is the major folk dance of the Bodo community. It is performed during the Bwisagu or Baisagu festival, which marks the Bodo New Year. It is often called the butterfly dance because of the graceful, fluttering movements of the dancers.
Q: Where is the Deodhani dance performed and what does it represent?
A: The Deodhani dance is a ritual dance performed mainly at the Kamakhya temple during the Ambubachi Mela. The performer is believed to be possessed by the goddess Manasa, and the dance is characterised by vigorous, trance-like movement. It belongs to the Shakti tradition of Assam.
Q: অসমৰ শাস্ত্ৰীয় নৃত্য কোনটো আৰু ইয়াক কোনে আৰম্ভ কৰিছিল?
A: সত্ৰীয়া অসমৰ শাস্ত্ৰীয় নৃত্য। ইয়াক বৈষ্ণৱ সন্ত তথা সংস্কাৰক শ্ৰীমন্ত শংকৰদেৱে পঞ্চদশ-ষোড়শ শতিকাত সত্ৰত পৰিৱেশন কৰা অঙ্কীয়া নাটৰ অংশ হিচাপে আৰম্ভ কৰিছিল। ই ২০০০ চনত শাস্ত্ৰীয় নৃত্য হিচাপে আনুষ্ঠানিক স্বীকৃতি লাভ কৰিছিল।
Q: সত্ৰীয়া নৃত্যৰ দুটা ধাৰা কি কি?
A: সত্ৰীয়া দুটা ধাৰাত পৰিৱেশন কৰা হয়—গায়ন-বায়ন আৰু খৰমানাৰ। গায়ন-বায়ন পুৰুষ নৃত্যশিল্পী বা ভকতে পৰিৱেশন কৰে, আনহাতে খৰমানাৰ নাৰীয়ে পৰিৱেশন কৰে আৰু ইয়াৰ গতি অধিক কোমল। দুয়োটাত খোল আৰু তাল ব্যৱহাৰ হয়।
Q: ৰঙালী বিহুৰ সৈতে কোনটো নৃত্য জড়িত আৰু হুঁচৰি কি?
A: বিহু নৃত্য অসমৰ ৰঙালী বা ব’হাগ বিহুৰ সৈতে জড়িত। হুঁচৰি এক সম্পৰ্কিত পৰম্পৰা য’ত পুৰুষ শিল্পীৰ এটা দলে বিহুৰ সময়ত ঘৰে ঘৰে গৈ চোতালত গান গায় আৰু নাচে। বিহু নৃত্যই ২০২৩ চনত গুৱাহাটীত গিনিজ বিশ্ব অভিলেখ সৃষ্টি কৰিছিল।
Q: বাগৰুম্বা কোনটো জনগোষ্ঠী আৰু উৎসৱৰ?
A: বাগৰুম্বা বড়ো জনগোষ্ঠীৰ প্ৰধান লোকনৃত্য। ই বাইচাগু বা ব’হাগ বিহু উৎসৱত পৰিৱেশন কৰা হয়, যি বড়ো নতুন বছৰ চিহ্নিত কৰে। নৃত্যশিল্পীসকলৰ কোমল, পখিলা-সদৃশ গতিভংগীৰ বাবে ইয়াক প্ৰায়ে পখিলা নৃত্য বোলা হয়।
Q: দেওধনী নৃত্য ক’ত পৰিৱেশন কৰা হয় আৰু ই কি প্ৰতিনিধিত্ব কৰে?
A: দেওধনী নৃত্য মূলতঃ কামাখ্যা মন্দিৰত অম্বুবাচী মেলাৰ সময়ত পৰিৱেশন কৰা আচৰিত নৃত্য। শিল্পীগৰাকী মনসা দেৱীত আৱিষ্ট বুলি বিশ্বাস কৰা হয়, আৰু এই নৃত্য শক্তিশালী, সমাধি-সদৃশ গতিৰে বৈশিষ্ট্যপূৰ্ণ। ই অসমৰ শাক্ত পৰম্পৰাৰ অন্তৰ্গত।

### Traditional Crafts & Metalwork (Bell Metal, Brass

Q: Which place in Assam is famous for bell metal craft?

Q: What is the Sarai commonly used for in Assamese culture?

Q: Which traditional Assamese mat is woven from reeds?

Q: Which is the traditional Assamese fishing net craft?
