A: Koodiyattam, the Sanskrit theatre tradition of Kerala, is recognised by UNESCO as a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity. It is traditionally performed in temple theatres called Koothambalam. Vedic chanting was also among the early Indian traditions inscribed by UNESCO.
Q: What are the four types of puppetry in India?
A: The four types are string puppetry, shadow puppetry, glove puppetry and rod puppetry. Examples include Kathputli of Rajasthan and Kundhei of Odisha for string puppets, Tholu Bommalata of Andhra Pradesh and Togalu Gombeyaata of Karnataka for shadow puppets, Pavakoothu of Kerala for glove puppets, and Putul Nach of West Bengal for rod puppets.
Q: Which martial art belongs to Kerala and which to Tamil Nadu?
A: Kalaripayattu belongs to Kerala and is often called the mother of Indian martial arts, practised in a kalari or training hall. Silambam, the stick-fighting art using a long bamboo staff, belongs to Tamil Nadu. Other examples are Gatka of Punjab, Thang-Ta of Manipur, Mardani Khel of Maharashtra and Lathi Khela of Bengal.
Q: What are Ankia Naat and Bhaona?
A: Ankia Naat is the one-act devotional drama created by the Assamese saint Srimanta Sankardeva in the sixteenth century, and Bhaona is its performance. These forms present Krishna-centred devotion and are linked with the Vaishnava tradition of Assam. The term Raas refers to the circular devotional dance-drama associated with Krishna in Assam.
Q: নাট্যশাস্ত্ৰ কাৰে লিখিছিল আৰু ই কিয় গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: নাট্যশাস্ত্ৰ ঋষি ভৰত মুনিয়ে লিখিছিল আৰু ই প্ৰায় খ্ৰীষ্টপূৰ্ব ২০০ৰ পৰা খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দ ২০০ৰ ভিতৰত ৰচিত। ই ভাৰতীয় নাট্য, নৃত্য, সংগীত আৰু সৌন্দৰ্যতত্ত্বৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি বিদ্যমান গ্ৰন্থ, আৰু ই নৱৰস, অভিনয়, সূত্ৰধাৰ আৰু পূৰ্বৰঙ্গৰ দৰে ধাৰণা ব্যাখ্যা কৰে। ইয়াক পঞ্চম বেদ কোৱা হয় কাৰণ ই পৰিৱেশনৰ জৰিয়তে পৱিত্ৰ জ্ঞান সকলোৰে বাবে উপলব্ধ কৰিছিল।
Q: কোন ভাৰতীয় নাট্য পৰম্পৰা ইউনেস্কʼৰ দ্বাৰা অমূৰ্ত ঐতিহ্য হিচাপে স্বীকৃত?
A: কেৰালাৰ সংস্কৃত নাট্য পৰম্পৰা কূটিয়াট্টম ইউনেস্কʼৰ মানৱজাতিৰ মৌখিক আৰু অমূৰ্ত ঐতিহ্যৰ উৎকৃষ্ট নিদৰ্শন হিচাপে স্বীকৃত। ইয়াক পৰম্পৰাগতভাৱে কূট্টম্বলম নামৰ মন্দিৰ ৰঙ্গমঞ্চত পৰিৱেশন কৰা হয়। বৈদিক উচ্চাৰণো ইউনেস্কʼৰ দ্বাৰা তালিকাভুক্ত প্ৰথম ভাৰতীয় পৰম্পৰাসমূহৰ এটা আছিল।
Q: ভাৰতত পুতলা নাচৰ চাৰিটা প্ৰকাৰ কি কি?
A: চাৰিটা প্ৰকাৰ হৈছে তাঁত-পুতলা, ছাঁ-পুতলা, হাত-পুতলা আৰু লাঠি-পুতলা। উদাহৰণস্বৰূপে ৰাজস্থানৰ কথপুতলি আৰু ওড়িশাৰ কুণ্ডেই তাঁত-পুতলা, অন্ধ্ৰ প্ৰদেশৰ তোলু বোম্মালাটা আৰু কৰ্ণাটকৰ তোগালু গোম্বেয়াটা ছাঁ-পুতলা, কেৰালাৰ পাৱাকূথু হাত-পুতলা, আৰু পশ্চিম বাংলাৰ পুতুল নাচ লাঠি-পুতলা।
Q: কোন যুদ্ধ কলা কেৰালাৰ আৰু কোন তামিলনাডুৰ?
A: কালাৰিপায়াত্তু কেৰালাৰ আৰু ইয়াক প্ৰায়ে ভাৰতীয় যুদ্ধ কলাৰ মাতৃ বুলি কোৱা হয়, কালাৰি বা প্ৰশিক্ষণ ভৱনত অনুশীলন কৰা হয়। চিলাম্বাম, দীঘল বাঁহৰ লাঠি ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা লাঠি-যুঁজ কলা, তামিলনাডুৰ। আন উদাহৰণ হৈছে পঞ্জাৱৰ গাটকা, মণিপুৰৰ থাং-টা, মহাৰাষ্ট্ৰৰ মৰ্দানি খেল আৰু বাংলাৰ লাঠি খেলা।
Q: অঙ্কীয়া নাট আৰু ভাওনা কি?
A: অঙ্কীয়া নাট হৈছে ষোড়শ শতিকাত অসমৰ সন্ত শ্ৰীমন্ত শঙ্কৰদেৱে সৃষ্টি কৰা একাঙ্ক ভক্তিমূলক নাটক, আৰু ভাওনা ইয়াৰ পৰিৱেশন। এই ৰূপসমূহে কৃষ্ণ-কেন্দ্ৰিক ভক্তি প্ৰদৰ্শন কৰে আৰু অসমৰ বৈষ্ণৱ পৰম্পৰাৰ সৈতে জড়িত। ৰাস শব্দই অসমত কৃষ্ণৰ সৈতে জড়িত বৃত্তাকাৰ ভক্তিমূলক নৃত্য-নাটক বুজায়।

### Ancient Assam History — 300 Practice Questions | ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-history/ancient-assam-sec/ancient-assam/
Summary: 300 ancient Assam history questions with answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Covers Kamarupa, Varman and Salastambha dynasties.
Q: Which inscription first mentions the name Kamarupa?
A: The Allahabad Pillar inscription of Samudragupta, which names Kamarupa as a frontier kingdom, is usually taken as the first historical mention of the name.
Q: Who founded the Varman dynasty of Kamarupa?
A: Pushyavarman founded the Varman dynasty in the fourth century CE. Bhaskaravarman was its most powerful ruler.
Q: Why is ancient Assam important for Assam competitive exams?
A: It is the starting point of Assam history and appears regularly in the Assam History section of ADRE, APSC and Assam Police papers.

Q: The language of the ancient Assamese inscriptions is?

A: A cave (of the god Mahendra?)

Q: Which ancient inscription is found at the base of the Nilachal hill?

Q: Epigraphic evidence suggests that ancient Assam used which system of governance?

Q: What are the two main types of ancient Kamarupa inscriptions?
A: Copper-plate inscriptions and stone (or rock) inscriptions.
Q: Which is the most important copper plate of the Varman dynasty?
A: The Nidhanpur copper plate of Bhaskaravarman, a re-issue of a grant first made by Bhutivarman.
Q: Which rock inscription belongs to Mahendravarman?
A: The Umachal rock inscription of the 5th century, associated with a cave of the god Mahendra.
Q: Which copper plate records the reign of Vanamaladeva?
A: The Parbatiya copper plate, found near Tezpur on the bank of the Brahmaputra.
Q: In which language and script were these inscriptions written?
A: They were written in Sanskrit, in verse and prose, using the Brahmi script and its later regional forms.
Q: প্ৰাচীন কামৰূপৰ শিলালিপিৰ দুটা মূল প্ৰকাৰ কি?
A: তাম্ৰপত্ৰ শিলালিপি আৰু শিল (বা শিলা) শিলালিপি।
Q: বৰ্মন বংশৰ আটাইতকৈ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ তাম্ৰপত্ৰ কোনখন?
A: ভাস্কৰবৰ্মনৰ নিধানপুৰ তাম্ৰপত্ৰ, যি ভূতিবৰ্মনে প্ৰথমে কৰা দানৰ পুনৰ্জাৰি।
Q: মহেন্দ্ৰবৰ্মনৰ কোন শিলালিপি?
A: পঞ্চম শতিকাৰ উমাচল শিলালিপি, মহেন্দ্ৰ দেৱতাৰ গুহাৰ সৈতে জড়িত।
Q: ৱনমালাদেৱৰ ৰাজত্ব কোন তাম্ৰপত্ৰত লিপিবদ্ধ?
A: পাৰ্বতীয়া তাম্ৰপত্ৰ, ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰৰ পাৰত তেজপুৰৰ ওচৰত পোৱা গৈছে।
Q: এই শিলালিপিবোৰ কোন ভাষা আৰু লিপিত লিখা হৈছিল?
A: সংস্কৃতত, পদ্য আৰু গদ্যত, ব্ৰাহ্মী লিপি আৰু তাৰ পিছৰ আঞ্চলিক ৰূপত।

### Administration, Society & Religion — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-history/ancient-assam-sec/ancient-society-admin/
Summary: Practice administration, society & religion questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: The ancient Assamese kingdom was known as?
A: Kamarupa (or Pragjyotisha)
Q: The head of the administration in ancient Kamarupa was?
A: The king (Maharajadhiraja)
Q: The king of Kamarupa was assisted by which officials?
A: Ministers (Mahamatya), priests and other officers
Q: The council of ministers in ancient Kamarupa was called?
A: Mantriparishad
Q: The land was granted by the king to whom in ancient Assam?
A: Brahmans, temples and state officials
Q: The villages in ancient Kamarupa were administered by?
A: Local headmen (Gramani) and officials
Q: The society of ancient Kamarupa was divided according to?
A: The varna (caste) system of Brahmans, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras
Q: The dominant religion in ancient Kamarupa during the Varman period was?
A: Brahmanism (with Shaiva, Vaishnava and Shakta worship)
Q: Buddhism existed in Kamarupa mainly through?
A: Monasteries and pilgrims like Xuanzang's visits
Q: Which goddess was worshipped in ancient Kamarupa?
A: Goddess Kamakhya (Shakti)
Q: The cult of which deity had ancient roots in Assam?
A: The cult of the Mother Goddess (Kamakhya)
Q: Ancient Kamarupa was known for its development in which field?

A: China, Tibet and Southeast Asian regions

A: Land revenue and taxes
Q: Which deity was the family deity of the later Kamarupa kings?
A: The goddess Kamakhya
Q: The capital city of Pragjyotishpur corresponds to which modern city?
A: Guwahati (Gauhati) area
Q: The position of women in ancient Kamarupa was?
A: Comparatively respected but within a patriarchal society
Q: The ancient Kamarupa kingdom had which type of military force?
A: A standing army with elephants and cavalry
Q: The title 'Maharajadhiraja' in Kamarupa meant?
A: King of great kings (paramount sovereign)
Q: Which religion received patronage of both the Varman and later kings?
A: Brahmanical Hinduism

A: Copper and gold (for inscriptions and trade)

A: Sculpture and temple architecture

A: Indo-Aryan (Brahmanical) and indigenous traditions

Q: What was the ancient Assamese kingdom called?
A: It was known as Kamarupa, or Pragjyotisha, and was headed by a king titled Maharajadhiraja.
Q: What was the council of ministers called in ancient Kamarupa?
A: The Mantriparishad, comprising ministers (Mahamatya), priests and other officers.
Q: To whom did the king grant land?
A: Land was granted to Brahmins, temples and state officials through agrahara grants recorded on copper plates.
Q: What was the main religion of ancient Kamarupa?
A: Brahmanism, expressed through Shaiva, Vaishnava and Shakta worship, with Buddhism also present.
Q: Which goddess was central to the religion of Kamarupa?
A: The goddess Kamakhya (Shakti), who was regarded as the family deity of the later kings.
Q: প্ৰাচীন অসমীয়া ৰাজ্যক কি বোলা হৈছিল?
A: ই কামৰূপ বা প্ৰাগজ্যোতিষ নামেৰে জনা গৈছিল, আৰু ইয়াৰ মুৰব্বী আছিল মহাৰাজাধিৰাজ উপাধিৰ এজন ৰজা।
Q: প্ৰাচীন কামৰূপত মন্ত্ৰী পৰিষদক কি বোলা হৈছিল?
A: মন্ত্ৰীপৰিষদ, য'ত মন্ত্ৰী (মহামাত্য), পুৰোহিত আৰু আন বিষয়াসকল আছিল।
Q: ৰজাই কাক ভূমি দান দিছিল?
A: ব্ৰাহ্মণ, মন্দিৰ আৰু ৰাজ্যিক বিষয়াসকললৈ অগ্ৰহাৰ দানৰ জৰিয়তে তাম্ৰপত্ৰত লিপিবদ্ধ কৰি ভূমি দিয়া হৈছিল।
Q: প্ৰাচীন কামৰূপৰ প্ৰধান ধৰ্ম কি আছিল?
A: ব্ৰাহ্মণ্য ধৰ্ম, শৈৱ, বৈষ্ণৱ আৰু শাক্ত উপাসনাৰ জৰিয়তে প্ৰকাশিত, আৰু বৌদ্ধ ধৰ্মও উপস্থিত আছিল।
Q: কামৰূপৰ ধৰ্মত কোন দেৱী কেন্দ্ৰীয় আছিল?
A: কামাখ্যা (শক্তি) দেৱী, যাক পিছৰ ৰজাসকলৰ বংশীয় দেৱতা বুলি গণ্য কৰা হৈছিল।

Q: Which Purana gives a detailed account of the geography and mythology of ancient Kamarupa?

A: Samudragupta
Q: Which Tantra text is an important source for ancient Assamese religion?
A: The Yogini Tantra
Q: The Vishnu Purana mentions which famous dynasty of Kamarupa?
A: The Bhauma (Naraka) dynasty
Q: The Mahabharata mentions the name of which ancient capital of Assam?
A: Pragjyotisha
Q: Which king of Pragjyotisha is mentioned as fighting for the Kauravas in the Mahabharata war?
A: Bhagadatta
Q: The Nidhanpur copper plate is an important epigraphic source for which period?
A: The Varman dynasty period
Q: The Harshacharita describes the embassy of which Kamarupa king to Harshavardhana?
A: Bhaskaravarman
Q: Which later Assamese chronicles provide historical material for the medieval period, not the ancient?
A: The Buranjis
Q: The location of ancient Pragjyotisha is identified with which modern city?
A: Guwahati
Q: Which Chinese source mentions the state of 'Kamarupa' besides Xuanzang's account?
A: The writings of Wang-Hiuen-tse (Wang Hiuen Tse's account)
Q: The Yogini Tantra describes the extent of Kamarupa from the Karatoya river to which river?
A: The Dikkaravasini (Dikshu) river in the east
Q: The historical geography of Kamarupa is best described in which text?
A: The Kalika Purana and Yogini Tantra
Q: The account of Xuanzang about Kamarupa is found in which of his works?
A: Si-yu-ki (Records of the Western World)
Q: Which king of Kamarupa is described as contemporary of the Gupta ruler Samudragupta?
A: Pushyavarman
Q: The term 'Kamarupa' for Assam is derived from which tradition?
A: The legend of Kamadeva (Kamadeva's form being restored by Shiva)
Q: Which archaeological site in Guwahati has yielded early medieval sculptures?
A: Ambari
Q: Which Purana is the main literary source for ancient Kamarupa?
A: The Kalika Purana gives a detailed account of the geography and mythology of ancient Kamarupa and its early rulers.
Q: Which ruler of Kamarupa is named in the Allahabad pillar inscription?
A: Pushyavarman is named in the Allahabad pillar inscription of the Gupta emperor Samudragupta.
Q: Which Chinese traveller visited Kamarupa and in which year?
A: Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang) visited Kamarupa in 643 AD and recorded it in his Si-yu-ki.
Q: Which source records the embassy of Bhaskaravarman to Harshavardhana?
A: Banabhatta's Harshacharita describes the embassy of Bhaskaravarman to Harshavardhana.
Q: Which texts describe the extent of Kamarupa between the Karatoya and Dikkaravasini rivers?
A: The Kalika Purana and the Yogini Tantra together describe the geography and boundaries of Kamarupa.
Q: প্ৰাচীন কামৰূপৰ মূল সাহিত্যিক উৎস কোনখন পুৰাণ?
A: কালিকা পুৰাণে প্ৰাচীন কামৰূপৰ ভূগোল, পৌৰাণিক বিৱৰণ আৰু প্ৰাৰম্ভিক ৰজাসকলৰ বিষয়ে বিস্তাৰিতভাৱে কয়।
Q: এলাহাবাদ স্তম্ভ শিলালিপিত কামৰূপৰ কোন ৰজাৰ নাম আছে?
A: গুপ্ত সম্ৰাট সমুদ্ৰগুপ্তৰ এলাহাবাদ স্তম্ভ শিলালিপিত পুষ্যবৰ্মনৰ নাম আছে।
Q: কোন চীনা পৰিৱ্ৰাজকে কেতিয়া কামৰূপ ভ্ৰমণ কৰিছিল?
A: জুৱানজাঙে (হিউয়েন ছাঙ) ৬৪৩ খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দত কামৰূপ ভ্ৰমণ কৰি ছি-য়ু-কি গ্ৰন্থত লিপিবদ্ধ কৰিছিল।
Q: হৰ্ষবৰ্ধনলৈ ভাস্কৰবৰ্মনৰ দূতাবাস কোনে লিপিবদ্ধ কৰিছে?
A: বাণভট্টৰ হৰ্ষচৰিতে ভাস্কৰবৰ্মনৰ দূতাবাসৰ কথা বৰ্ণনা কৰিছে।
Q: কৰতোয়া আৰু দিক্কৰৱাসিনী নদীৰ মাজৰ কামৰূপৰ বিস্তৃতি কোনে বৰ্ণনা কৰিছে?
A: কালিকা পুৰাণ আৰু যোগিনী তন্ত্ৰই কামৰূপৰ ভূগোল আৰু সীমা বৰ্ণনা কৰিছে।

### Bhauma / Asura Dynasty (Narakasura) — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-history/ancient-assam-sec/bhauma-asura-dynasty/
Summary: Practice bhauma / asura dynasty (narakasura) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Who is regarded as the founder of the Bhauma (Asura) dynasty of Pragjyotisha?
A: Naraka (Narakasura)
Q: Why is the dynasty of Naraka called 'Bhauma'?
A: Because Naraka was the son of Bhumi (the Earth goddess)
Q: According to the Kalika Purana, Naraka was the son of?
A: Bhumi (Earth) and Vishnu (in his Varaha form)
Q: Narakasura established the kingdom of Pragjyotisha with its capital at?
A: Pragjyotishpur
Q: Naraka is credited with the introduction of which religious practice in Kamarupa?
A: The worship of Kamakhya at Nilachal
Q: Who was the son and successor of Narakasura?
A: Bhagadatta
Q: Bhagadatta fought on which side in the Mahabharata war?
A: The Kauravas
Q: Bhagadatta was a friend of which great king?
A: Duryodhana
Q: Who killed Bhagadatta in the Mahabharata war?
A: Arjuna
Q: The son of Bhagadatta who also fought in the Mahabharata war was?
A: Vajradatta
Q: According to tradition, the Bhauma dynasty ruled Pragjyotisha for how many generations?
A: Fourteen generations
Q: The last king of the Bhauma dynasty according to some accounts was?
A: Vajradatta (or the later Bhauma kings)
Q: Naraka is believed to have defeated which earlier Danava king?
A: Ghatakasura (Ghatak)
Q: Which goddess is said to have blessed Naraka with the kingdom?
A: Kamakhya (the goddess)
Q: The Bhauma dynasty is also referred to as?
A: The Asura or Naraka dynasty
Q: The gift of land (Sasan) given by the Bhauma kings to Brahmans is described in?
A: The Kalika Purana
Q: According to legend, Naraka's capital Pragjyotisha is near which sacred hill?
A: The Nilachal hill
Q: The Bhauma kings are described in the Puranas as followers of?
A: The demonical (asuric) cult of the goddess
Q: Bhagadatta is described in the Mahabharata as the king of which region?
A: Pragjyotisha
Q: Historically, the Bhauma dynasty is treated as?
A: A legendary dynasty with possible historical nucleus
Q: Who founded the Bhauma (Asura) dynasty of Pragjyotisha?
A: Naraka (Narakasura) is regarded as the founder of the Bhauma (Asura) dynasty.
Q: Why is Naraka's dynasty called Bhauma?
A: It is called Bhauma because Naraka was the son of Bhumi, the Earth goddess.
Q: Who was the son and successor of Narakasura?
A: Bhagadatta, who is described in the Mahabharata as the king of Pragjyotisha, succeeded Narakasura.
Q: On which side did Bhagadatta fight in the Mahabharata war?
A: Bhagadatta fought on the side of the Kauravas and was killed by Arjuna.
Q: For how many generations did the Bhauma dynasty rule according to tradition?
A: According to tradition the Bhauma dynasty ruled Pragjyotisha for fourteen generations.
Q: প্ৰাগজ্যোতিষৰ ভৌম (অসুৰ) বংশ কোনে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল?
A: নৰক (নৰকাসুৰ)ক ভৌম (অসুৰ) বংশৰ প্ৰতিষ্ঠাপক হিচাপে গণ্য কৰা হয়।
Q: নৰকৰ বংশক ভৌম কিয় বোলা হয়?
A: নৰক ভূমি (পৃথিৱী দেৱী)ৰ পুত্ৰ আছিল বাবে ইয়াক ভৌম বোলা হয়।
Q: নৰকাসুৰৰ পুত্ৰ আৰু উত্তৰাধিকাৰী কোন আছিল?
A: ভগদত্ত, যাক মহাভাৰতত প্ৰাগজ্যোতিষৰ ৰজা বুলি বৰ্ণনা কৰা হৈছে, নৰকাসুৰৰ উত্তৰাধিকাৰী হৈছিল।
Q: মহাভাৰত যুদ্ধত ভগদত্তই কোন পক্ষে যুঁজিছিল?
A: ভগদত্তই কৌৰৱৰ পক্ষে যুঁজিছিল আৰু অৰ্জুনে তেওঁক বধ কৰিছিল।
Q: পৰম্পৰা অনুসৰি ভৌম বংশই কিমান পুৰুষ ৰাজত্ব কৰিছিল?
A: পৰম্পৰা অনুসৰি ভৌম বংশই প্ৰাগজ্যোতিষত চৈধ্যজন পুৰুষ ৰাজত্ব কৰিছিল।

### Danava Dynasty Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-history/ancient-assam-sec/danava-dynasty/
Summary: Practice danava dynasty questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: According to the Kalika Purana, who was the first king of Pragjyotisha?
A: Mahiranga (a Danava)
Q: The first dynasty of ancient Kamarupa according to legend is called?
A: The Danava (Mahiranga) dynasty
Q: Mahiranga was a king of which community according to the Puranas?
A: The Danavas (demons)
Q: Who succeeded Mahiranga in the Danava dynasty?
A: Hataka
Q: The list of Danava kings according to the Kalika Purana is?
A: Mahiranga, Hataka, Sambar, Ratna and Ghatak
Q: Which Danava king was killed by the gods according to the legend?
A: Ghatakasura (Ghatak), the last of the Danava line
Q: The Danava dynasty of Kamarupa is described in which Purana?
A: The Kalika Purana
Q: The Danava dynasty is considered by historians as?
A: Mythological (legendary) rulers without historical evidence
Q: The capital of the Danava rulers was?
A: Pragjyotisha
Q: The last Danava king 'Ghatakasura' was succeeded by whom?
A: Naraka (of the Bhauma/Asura line)
Q: Which goddess is believed to have killed the Danava rulers?
A: The goddess Kamakhya
Q: The Danava kings are associated with which religious tradition?
A: Saktism (worship of the goddess)
Q: According to the Kalika Purana, the Danavas were defeated by?
A: The gods led by Naraka (or the goddess)
Q: The story of the Danava dynasty is part of which narrative tradition?
A: The Puranic narratives of Kamarupa
Q: Mahiranga is also known as?
A: Mahiranga Danava (the first demon king)
Q: The seat of the Danava kings near Pragjyotisha is identified with?
A: The area of Nilachal hill (Kamakhya region)
Q: Historically, the Danava dynasty is placed before which historical dynasty?
A: The Varman dynasty
Q: The legend of the Danavas connects the origin of Kamarupa to?
A: The worship of Kamakhya and the foundation of Pragjyotisha
Q: Who was the first king of the Danava dynasty?
A: Mahiranga, a Danava (demon), was the first king of Pragjyotisha according to the Kalika Purana.
Q: Which Purana describes the Danava dynasty of Kamarupa?
A: The Kalika Purana describes the Danava dynasty of Kamarupa.
Q: Who were the kings of the Danava line in order?
A: Mahiranga, Hataka, Sambar, Ratna and Ghatak, with Ghatakasura (Ghatak) as the last.
Q: Who succeeded the last Danava king Ghatakasura?
A: Ghatakasura was succeeded by Naraka, the founder of the Bhauma (Asura) line.
Q: Is the Danava dynasty historical?
A: No. Historians regard the Danava dynasty as legendary or mythological rulers without historical evidence, placed before the historical Varman dynasty.
Q: দানৱ বংশৰ প্ৰথম ৰজা কোন আছিল?
A: কালিকা পুৰাণ অনুসৰি মহিৰঙ্গ, এজন দানৱ (অসুৰ), প্ৰাগজ্যোতিষৰ প্ৰথম ৰজা আছিল।
Q: কামৰূপৰ দানৱ বংশ কোনখন পুৰাণত বৰ্ণনা কৰা হৈছে?
A: কালিকা পুৰাণত কামৰূপৰ দানৱ বংশ বৰ্ণনা কৰা হৈছে।
Q: দানৱ বংশৰ ৰজাসকল ক্ৰম অনুসৰি কোন কোন আছিল?
A: মহিৰঙ্গ, হাটক, সম্ভৰ, ৰত্ন আৰু ঘাটক; শেষৰজন ঘাটকাসুৰ (ঘাটক)।
Q: শেষ দানৱ ৰজা ঘাটকাসুৰৰ উত্তৰাধিকাৰী কোন হৈছিল?
A: ঘাটকাসুৰৰ উত্তৰাধিকাৰী আছিল নৰক, ভৌম (অসুৰ) বংশৰ প্ৰতিষ্ঠাপক।
Q: দানৱ বংশ ঐতিহাসিক নেকি?
A: নহয়। ঐতিহাসিকসকলে দানৱ বংশক ঐতিহাসিক প্ৰমাণবিহীন কিংবদন্তিমূলক শাসক হিচাপে গণ্য কৰে; ই ঐতিহাসিক বৰ্মণ বংশৰ আগত স্থাপিত।

### Fall of Kamarupa Kingdom Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-history/ancient-assam-sec/fall-of-kamarupa/
Summary: Practice fall of kamarupa kingdom questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: The ancient kingdom of Kamarupa came to an end around which century?
A: 12th century AD
Q: The final decline of Kamarupa was caused by?
A: External invasions and internal fragmentation
Q: After the fall of Kamarupa, the region was divided into?
A: Smaller kingdoms like Kamata and the eastern principalities
Q: The kingdom of Kamata emerged from which part of Kamarupa?
A: The western part of Kamarupa
Q: The decline of the Pala dynasty of Kamarupa was completed by?
A: Vaidyadeva and subsequent invasions from the west
Q: Which event is considered the final end of the unified Kamarupa kingdom?
A: The fragmentation after the 12th century (into Kamata and other states)
Q: The successors of Kamarupa in the east were known as?
A: The eastern independent kingdoms (like the Chutiya and Kachari states)
Q: The Kamata kingdom was later ruled by which dynasty?
A: The Khen dynasty (and later the Koch dynasty)
Q: The political fragmentation of Kamarupa led to the rise of?
A: Independent kingdoms like Kamata, Kachari, Chutiya and Barahi
Q: The invasions of which kings weakened Kamarupa in the 11th-12th centuries?
A: The Sena and other western kings
Q: After the fall of ancient Kamarupa, the Kamata kingdom's capital was?
A: Kamata (near present-day Gosanimari/Cooch Behar region)
Q: Which ruler of the Khen dynasty later revived the name Kamata?
A: Prithu (or the early Khen rulers)
Q: The end of the ancient Kamarupa tradition is linked with the rise of?
A: The medieval kingdoms (Koch, Ahom and Kachari)
Q: Historically, the fall of Kamarupa marked the beginning of?
A: The medieval period of Assam's history
Q: The name 'Kamata' later gave rise to which modern region?
A: Kamrup (Kamrup district of Assam)

Q: When did the ancient kingdom of Kamarupa come to an end?
A: Around the 12th century AD, when the unified kingdom fragmented.
Q: What caused the fall of Kamarupa?
A: A combination of external invasions and internal fragmentation, including weak central authority and powerful local landholders.
Q: Which kingdom emerged from the western part of Kamarupa?
A: The Kamata kingdom, later ruled by the Khen dynasty and then the Koch dynasty.
Q: Which eastern states succeeded ancient Kamarupa?
A: Independent eastern kingdoms such as the Chutiya, Kachari and Barahi states.

A: The end of ancient Kamarupa and the entry of the Ahoms in 1228 AD under Sukapha.
Q: প্ৰাচীন কামৰূপ ৰাজ্যৰ সমাপ্তি কেতিয়া ঘটিছিল?
A: প্ৰায় দ্বাদশ শতিকাত, যেতিয়া একত্ৰিত ৰাজ্য ভাঙি যায়।
Q: কামৰূপৰ পতনৰ কাৰণ কি আছিল?
A: বাহ্যিক আক্ৰমণ আৰু আভ্যন্তৰীণ বিভাজনৰ সংমিশ্ৰণ, যাৰ ভিতৰত দুৰ্বল কেন্দ্ৰীয় কৰ্তৃত্ব আৰু শক্তিশালী স্থানীয় ভূমিধাৰীও আছিল।
Q: কামৰূপৰ পশ্চিম অংশৰ পৰা কোন ৰাজ্য ওলাইছিল?
A: কামতা ৰাজ্য, যাক পিছত খেন বংশই আৰু তাৰ পিছত কোচ বংশই শাসন কৰিছিল।
Q: প্ৰাচীন কামৰূপৰ উত্তৰাধিকাৰী পূবৰ ৰাজ্যবোৰ কোন?
A: চুতীয়া, কছাৰী আৰু বৰাহীৰ দৰে স্বাধীন পূবৰ ৰাজ্য।
Q: অসমৰ ইতিহাসৰ মধ্যযুগ কোন ঘটনাৰ পৰা আৰম্ভ হয়?
A: প্ৰাচীন কামৰূপৰ সমাপ্তি আৰু ১২২৮ খ্ৰী.ত সু-কাফাৰ নেতৃত্বত আহোমৰ প্ৰৱেশৰ পৰা।

A: Usha was the daughter of Banasura; she married Aniruddha, a grandson of Krishna.

A: The Agnigarh hill near Tezpur is associated with the Usha-Aniruddha legend.

A: Bhismaka was a mythological king of the Kundil region; his daughter Rukmini married Krishna.

Q: বাণাসুৰ কোন আছিল আৰু তেওঁৰ ৰাজধানী ক'ত আছিল?
A: বাণাসুৰ শোণিতপুৰৰ এজন শক্তিশালী অসুৰ ৰজা আছিল; তেওঁৰ ৰাজধানী শোণিতপুৰ বৰ্তমান তেজপুৰৰ সৈতে চিনাক্ত কৰা হয়।
Q: ঊষা কাৰ জীয়ৰী আছিল আৰু কাক বিয়া কৰিছিল?
A: ঊষা বাণাসুৰৰ জীয়ৰী আছিল; তাই কৃষ্ণৰ নাতি অনিৰুদ্ধক বিয়া কৰিছিল।
Q: তেজপুৰৰ ওচৰৰ কোন পাহাৰ ঊষা-অনিৰুদ্ধ কিংবদন্তিৰ সৈতে জড়িত?
A: তেজপুৰৰ ওচৰৰ অগ্নিগড় পাহাৰ ঊষা-অনিৰুদ্ধ কিংবদন্তিৰ সৈতে জড়িত।
Q: ভীষ্মক কোন আছিল আৰু তেওঁৰ জীয়ৰী ৰুক্মিণীয়ে কাক বিয়া কৰিছিল?
A: ভীষ্মক কুণ্ডিল অঞ্চলৰ এজন কিংবদন্তিমূলক ৰজা আছিল; তেওঁৰ জীয়ৰী ৰুক্মিণীয়ে কৃষ্ণক বিয়া কৰিছিল।
Q: অসমীয়া পৰম্পৰাত কুণ্ডিল কোন অঞ্চলৰ সৈতে চিনাক্ত কৰা হয়?
A: অসমীয়া পৰম্পৰাত কুণ্ডিলক ঊজনী অসমৰ সাদিয়া অঞ্চলৰ সৈতে চিনাক্ত কৰা হয়।

### Origin of Names (Pragjyotisha & Kamarupa) — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-history/ancient-assam-sec/origin-names-assam/
Summary: Practice origin of names (pragjyotisha & kamarupa) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: The name 'Pragjyotisha' is derived from which two Sanskrit words?
A: Prag (east) and Jyotisha (astrology/stars)
Q: Pragjyotisha literally means?
A: The city of eastern astrology
Q: According to tradition, the name 'Kamarupa' comes from the story of?
A: Kamadeva (the god of love)
Q: The legend says Kamarupa is the place where Shiva restored the body of Kamadeva. Hence the name means?
A: The place where Kama got his form (Kama + Rupa)
Q: The name 'Kamarupa' appears first in which epigraphic source?
A: The Allahabad pillar inscription (4th century AD)
Q: The ancient name of Assam, 'Kamarupa', covered roughly which region?
A: The Brahmaputra valley and parts of north Bengal
Q: The name 'Assam' is generally derived from which word?
A: Asama, meaning unequalled or peerless
Q: Some scholars connect the origin of the name 'Assam' with?
A: The Ahoms (Shan invaders who settled in the region)
Q: The ancient capital of Kamarupa, 'Pragjyotishpur', is identified with which place?
A: Present-day Guwahati (ancient Pragjyotisha)
Q: In which Purana is the name 'Kamarupa' linked to the demon Naraka?
A: The Kalika Purana
Q: The eastern boundary of ancient Kamarupa according to the Kalika Purana is?
A: The Dikkaravasini (Dikshu) river
Q: The western boundary of ancient Kamarupa according to the Yogini Tantra is?
A: The Karatoya river
Q: The term 'Kamata' used for later Assam is derived from?
A: The Kamata kingdom (related to Kamadeva tradition)
Q: Pragjyotisha was also known by which name in ancient texts?
A: Pragjyotishpur
Q: The name 'Sounitapura' or 'Sonitpur' is connected with which mythological ruler?
A: Banasura (Bana)
Q: Modern Tezpur is identified with which ancient place?
A: Sonitpur (Sounitapura)
Q: The name 'Kundil' in tradition is associated with which mythological kingdom?
A: The kingdom of Bhismaka (father of Rukmini)
Q: The name 'Lohitya' used in ancient texts refers to which river?
A: The Brahmaputra
Q: The Brahmaputra is called 'Lohitya' or 'Luit' because?
A: Lauhit means red (the river's reddish waters)
Q: The ancient name of the region 'Pragjyotisha-Kamarupa' indicates?
A: Both the capital (Pragjyotisha) and the kingdom (Kamarupa)
Q: What does the name Pragjyotisha literally mean?
A: Pragjyotisha is derived from prag (east) and jyotisha (astrology/stars), literally meaning the city of eastern astrology.
Q: How did the name Kamarupa originate?
A: Kamarupa comes from the legend of Kamadeva; it means the place where Kama regained his form (Kama + Rupa).
Q: Where does the name Kamarupa appear first in an inscription?
A: The name Kamarupa appears first in the Allahabad pillar inscription of Samudragupta.
Q: Which rivers marked the boundaries of ancient Kamarupa?
A: The Karatoya river in the west (Yogini Tantra) and the Dikkaravasini/Dikshu river in the east (Kalika Purana).
Q: Which modern city is identified with ancient Pragjyotishpur?
A: Ancient Pragjyotishpur is identified with present-day Guwahati.
Q: প্ৰাগজ্যোতিষ নামৰ আক্ষৰিক অৰ্থ কি?
A: প্ৰাগজ্যোতিষ প্ৰাক্ (পূব) আৰু জ্যোতিষ শব্দৰপৰা আহিছে, যাৰ আক্ষৰিক অৰ্থ পূবৰ জ্যোতিৰ্বিজ্ঞানৰ নগৰ।
Q: কামৰূপ নামৰ উৎপত্তি কেনেকৈ হ'ল?
A: কামৰূপ কামদেৱৰ কিংবদন্তিৰপৰা আহিছে; ইয়াৰ অৰ্থ কামে ৰূপ লাভ কৰা স্থান (কাম + ৰূপ)।
Q: কামৰূপ নাম প্ৰথমে কোন শিলালিপিত দেখা যায়?
A: কামৰূপ নাম প্ৰথমে সমুদ্ৰগুপ্তৰ এলাহাবাদ স্তম্ভ শিলালিপিত দেখা যায়।
Q: প্ৰাচীন কামৰূপৰ সীমা কোন নদীয়ে গঠন কৰিছিল?
A: পশ্চিমত কৰতোয়া নদী (যোগিনী তন্ত্ৰ) আৰু পূবত দিক্কৰৱাসিনী/দিক্ষু নদী (কালিকা পুৰাণ)।
Q: প্ৰাচীন প্ৰাগজ্যোতিষপুৰ কোন আধুনিক নগৰৰ সৈতে চিনাক্ত কৰা হয়?
A: প্ৰাচীন প্ৰাগজ্যোতিষপুৰ বৰ্তমান গুৱাহাটীৰ সৈতে চিনাক্ত কৰা হয়।

Q: Who founded the Pala dynasty of Kamarupa and when?
A: Brahmapala founded the Pala dynasty of Kamarupa around c. 900 AD.
Q: Is the Pala dynasty of Kamarupa the same as the Pala dynasty of Bengal?
A: No. They are two different dynasties, which is why the Kamarupa line is sometimes called the Brahmapala dynasty.
Q: Which king of the dynasty was the most powerful?
A: Ratnapala, known from the Bargaon copper plate, who also fought against the Palas of Gauda.

Q: কামৰূপৰ পাল বংশ কোনে আৰু কেতিয়া প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল?
A: ব্ৰহ্মপালে প্ৰায় খ্ৰী. ৯০০ চনত কামৰূপৰ পাল বংশ প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল।
Q: কামৰূপৰ পাল বংশ বংগৰ পাল বংশৰ সৈতে একে নেকি?
A: নহয়। এইবোৰ দুটা পৃথক বংশ, সেয়ে কামৰূপৰ বংশক কেতিয়াবা ব্ৰহ্মপাল বংশ বুলি কোৱা হয়।
Q: বংশৰ কোন ৰজা আটাইতকৈ শক্তিশালী আছিল?
A: ৰত্নপাল, বৰগাঁও তাম্ৰপত্ৰৰ পৰা জনা, যি গৌড়ৰ পালসকলৰ বিৰুদ্ধেও যুঁজিছিল।
Q: বংশৰ শেষ ব্যক্তিৰ সৈতে কোন দান জড়িত?
A: কামৌলি তাম্ৰপত্ৰ বৈদ্যদেৱৰ সৈতে জড়িত, যি কামৰূপত ক্ষমতা দখল কৰা সেনাপতি আছিল।
Q: পালসকলৰ অধীনত কামৰূপৰ বিস্তৃতি কিমান আছিল?
A: পশ্চিমে কৰতোয়া নদীৰ পৰা পূবে ডিক্ৰং (ডিখৌ) লৈ।

### Pre & Proto-History Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC

Q: The Neolithic site Daojali Hading is located in which district of Assam?
A: Dima Hasao district
Q: Which Neolithic site in Assam is situated near Kamrup?
A: Sarutaru
Q: Stone tools of which age have been discovered in the Garo hills region?
A: Palaeolithic (Old Stone) Age
Q: The Rongram valley of the Garo hills has yielded tools of which period?
A: The Palaeolithic period
Q: Hand-axes and chopping tools of the Stone Age in Assam are classified under which culture?
A: The Soanian-Acheulian type (Lower Palaeolithic)
Q: The megalithic culture in Assam is associated with which communities?
A: The Khasis, Garos and other hill tribes
Q: The ancient site of Bhaitbari is located near which river?
A: The Krishnai river
Q: The Neolithic period in Assam is generally dated to?
A: c. 2000-1000 BC (approx. 3rd-2nd millennium BC)
Q: Which site in Kamrup district has yielded both Stone Age and early historic material?
A: Sarutaru
Q: The ancient site 'Ambari' in Guwahati shows evidence of habitation from which period?
A: The early historic period (c. 2nd century AD onwards)
Q: Which communities are believed to have been the earliest inhabitants of Assam?
A: Austro-Asiatic (like Khasis) and Tibeto-Burman peoples
Q: The presence of 'rubble' and red pottery at Ambari indicates contact with which culture?
A: The Gangetic (North Indian) cultures
Q: Which agricultural practice marks the beginning of the Neolithic stage in Assam?
A: Cultivation of paddy (rice) and use of polished stone tools
Q: The discovery of which objects at Daojali Hading shows early trade links?
A: Jadeite (beads) and pottery resembling Ban Chiang culture
Q: The early inhabitants of Assam are believed to have practised which type of agriculture?
A: Jhum (shifting) cultivation
Q: Which iron tools were introduced in Assam during the early historic phase?
A: Iron ploughshares and agricultural implements
Q: The 'Madan Kamdev' ruins near Baihata Chariali belong to which period?
A: The 9th-10th century AD (early medieval)
Q: Madan Kamdev is often called the?
A: The Khajuraho of Assam
Q: The archaeological site 'Dah Parbatiya' is located near which town?
A: Tezpur
Q: The ruins of the Dah Parbatiya temple are attributed to which dynasty?
A: The Salastambha (Mlechchha) dynasty period
Q: Which Neolithic tool is most commonly found at Assam's prehistoric sites?
A: Cord-impressed pottery and polished stone axes
Q: The prehistoric culture of Assam shows influence of which Southeast Asian culture?
A: The Ban Chiang culture of Thailand
Q: Which archaeological evidence from Ambari suggests trade with the Gangetic plains?
A: Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW) type pottery and beads
Q: The early historic urban centre of ancient Pragjyotisha developed around which area?
A: The area around present-day Guwahati
Q: Which crop is believed to have been first domesticated in the Assam region?
A: Rice (paddy)
Q: Where is the Neolithic site Daojali Hading located?
A: Daojali Hading is located in Dima Hasao district of Assam.
Q: Which Neolithic site lies in the Kamrup district?
A: Sarutaru, near Kamrup, has yielded both Stone Age and early historic material.
Q: Which culture influenced the prehistoric pottery of Assam?
A: The Ban Chiang culture of Thailand influenced the prehistoric pottery of Assam.
Q: Which crop was first domesticated in the Assam region?
A: Rice (paddy) is regarded as the crop first domesticated in the Assam region.
Q: Which site in Guwahati shows early historic habitation?
A: Ambari in Guwahati shows evidence of habitation from about the 2nd century AD onward.
Q: নিঅলিথিক স্থান দাওজালি হাডিং ক’ত অৱস্থিত?
A: দাওজালি হাডিং অসমৰ ডিমা হাছাও জিলাত অৱস্থিত।
Q: কামৰূপ জিলাত কোন নিঅলিথিক স্থান আছে?
A: কামৰূপৰ ওচৰৰ শৰুতৰুতে প্ৰস্তৰ যুগ আৰু প্ৰাৰম্ভিক ঐতিহাসিক দুয়োটা সমল পোৱা গৈছে।
Q: অসমৰ প্ৰাগৈতিহাসিক মাটিৰ পাত্ৰত কোন সংস্কৃতিৰ প্ৰভাৱ আছিল?
A: থাইলেণ্ডৰ বান চিয়াং সংস্কৃতিৰ প্ৰভাৱ অসমৰ প্ৰাগৈতিহাসিক মাটিৰ পাত্ৰত আছিল।
Q: অসম অঞ্চলত প্ৰথমে কোন শস্য পোহনীয়া কৰা হৈছিল?
A: ধানক অসম অঞ্চলত প্ৰথমে পোহনীয়া কৰা শস্য হিচাপে গণ্য কৰা হয়।
Q: গুৱাহাটীৰ কোন স্থানে প্ৰাৰম্ভিক ঐতিহাসিক বসতি দেখুৱায়?
A: গুৱাহাটীৰ আমবাৰীয়ে প্ৰায় খ্ৰীষ্টীয় দ্বিতীয় শতিকাৰপৰা বসতিৰ প্ৰমাণ দেখুৱায়।

### Salastambha (Mlechchha) Dynasty — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-history/ancient-assam-sec/salastambha-dynasty/

Q: Who founded the Salastambha (Mlechchha) dynasty of Kamarupa?
A: Salastambha
Q: The Salastambha dynasty ruled Kamarupa from approximately which period?
A: c. 655-900 AD
Q: The Mlechchha dynasty is also known as?
A: The Salastambha dynasty
Q: Salastambha, the founder, is described in inscriptions as?
A: The son of Bhaskaravarman (adopted), a descendant of the god Naraka
Q: The origin of the Salastambha dynasty is considered to be?
A: Non-Brahmanical (foreign or Mlechchha) origin
Q: Which king of the dynasty shifted the capital to a new city?
A: Harjaravarman (from Pragjyotishpur to Haruppeswara)
Q: The name Haruppeswara is identified with which modern site?
A: Tezpur (Dhenukapura)
Q: Which Salastambha king had the title 'Maharajadhiraja'?
A: Harjaravarman (and other later kings)
Q: The king who built the city of Haruppeswara was?
A: Harjaravarman
Q: Which Salastambha king was a devotee of the goddess Durga?
A: Harjaravarman
Q: The Hayunthal copper plate inscription belongs to which king?
A: Harjaravarman
Q: The Tezpur copper plate inscription of which king mentions the construction of a temple?
A: Vanamala (Vanamaladeva)
Q: The greatest king of the Salastambha dynasty was?
A: Vanamaladeva (Vanamala)
Q: Vanamaladeva is described in the Parbatiya copper plate as?
A: A great devotee of Mahadeva (Shiva)
Q: The Parbatiya copper plate inscription belongs to which king?
A: Vanamaladeva
Q: Which king of the dynasty fought against the Palas of Bengal?
A: Vanamaladeva (against Gopala)
Q: The Salastambha dynasty was overthrown by?
A: Brahmapala (founder of the Pala dynasty)
Q: The last ruler of the Salastambha dynasty was?
A: Tyagasimha
Q: During the Salastambha period, the western boundary of Kamarupa was?
A: The Karatoya river
Q: The Salastambha kings styled themselves as?
A: Kings of Kamarupa (Lords of Pragjyotisha)
Q: Which Salastambha king is known for his victory against the Gauda king?
A: Vanamaladeva
Q: The Salastambha kings followed which religion?
A: Brahmanical Hinduism (mainly Shaivism)
Q: The famous stone inscription of Tezpur is associated with?
A: Harjaravarman (his stone inscription)
Q: The Harjaravarman stone inscription at Tezpur records?
A: His religious devotions and genealogy
Q: The Salastambha dynasty had how many known rulers?
A: About 15 rulers
Q: During which king's reign did the Ahom-period city of Tezpur function as capital?
A: Harjaravarman (Haruppeswara)
Q: The Salastambha period is known for the development of?
A: Architecture and temple building
Q: The king who granted the Parbatiya copper plate was?
A: Vanamaladeva
Q: The Salastambha kings traced their descent from?
A: The god Naraka (Bhagadatta lineage)
Q: Vanamaladeva's rule witnessed conflict with which neighboring power?
A: The Pala dynasty of Bengal
Q: The economy of the Salastambha period was primarily based on?
A: Agriculture and land grants
Q: The Salastambha dynasty is sometimes called?
A: The Mlechchha dynasty (of foreign origin)
Q: Which Salastambha king was defeated by Dharmapala of Bengal?
A: Probably a king before Vanamaladeva (during Gopala's reign)
Q: The cultural significance of the Salastambha period lies in?
A: The blending of indigenous and Hindu traditions
Q: Which Salastambha king is known for the construction of a temple at Haruppeswara?
A: Harjaravarman

A: Yes — the content is fully bilingual. You can switch between Assamese and English at any point while working through Salastambha Mlechchha Dynasty of Kamarupa (Bilingual English & Assamese), which helps when a term is clearer in one language than the other.
Q: How many questions does Salastambha Mlechchha Dynasty of Kamarupa (Bilingual English & Assamese) include?
A: The Salastambha Mlechchha Dynasty of Kamarupa (Bilingual English & Assamese) set is expanded over time, so the number of questions keeps growing. At the moment you can work through about 35 questions here with full answers.
Q: Who founded the Salastambha (Mlechchha) dynasty and when?
A: Salastambha founded the dynasty, which ruled Kamarupa from about c. 655 AD to c. 900 AD.
Q: Why is the dynasty called Mlechchha?
A: The kings were regarded as being of non-Brahmanical, possibly tribal or foreign, descent, and so were called Mlechchha in the inscriptions.
Q: Which king moved the capital to Haruppeswara?
A: Harjaravarman shifted the capital from Pragjyotishpur to Haruppeswara, identified with present-day Tezpur.
Q: Who was the greatest king of the dynasty?
A: Vanamaladeva (Vanamala), praised in the Parbatiya copper plate as a great devotee of Shiva and credited with victories over Gauda and Gopala.
Q: How did the Salastambha dynasty end?
A: Brahmapala, the founder of the Pala dynasty of Kamarupa, overthrew it; its last ruler is named as Tyagasimha.
Q: শালস্তম্ভ (ম্লেছ্ছ) বংশ কোনে আৰু কেতিয়া প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল?
A: শালস্তম্ভে বংশটো প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল, যি প্ৰায় খ্ৰী. ৬৫৫ ৰ পৰা ৯০০ লৈকে কামৰূপ শাসন কৰিছিল।
Q: বংশটোক ম্লেছ্ছ কিয় বোলা হয়?
A: ৰজাসকলক অব্ৰাহ্মণ্য, সম্ভৱতঃ জনজাতীয় বা বিদেশী মূলৰ বুলি গণ্য কৰা হৈছিল, সেয়ে শিলালিপিত তেওঁলোকক ম্লেছ্ছ বোলা হৈছিল।
Q: কোন ৰজাই ৰাজধানী হৰুপ্পেশ্বৰলৈ স্থানান্তৰ কৰিছিল?
A: হৰ্জৰবৰ্মনে ৰাজধানী প্ৰাগজ্যোতিষপুৰৰ পৰা হৰুপ্পেশ্বৰলৈ স্থানান্তৰ কৰিছিল, যাক বৰ্তমানৰ তেজপুৰৰ লগত চিনাক্ত কৰা হয়।
Q: বংশৰ শ্ৰেষ্ঠ ৰজা কোন আছিল?
A: ৱনমালাদেৱ (ৱনমালা), পাৰ্বতীয়া তাম্ৰপত্ৰত শিৱৰ মহান ভক্ত বুলি প্ৰশংসিত আৰু গৌড় আৰু গোপালৰ বিৰুদ্ধে বিজয়ৰ কৃতিত্বপ্ৰাপ্ত।
Q: শালস্তম্ভ বংশৰ সমাপ্তি কেনেকৈ ঘটিছিল?
A: কামৰূপৰ পাল বংশৰ প্ৰতিষ্ঠাপক ব্ৰহ্মপালে ইয়াক উৎখাত কৰিছিল; ইয়াৰ শেষ শাসকৰ নাম ত্যাগসিংহ।

### Varman Dynasty & Bhaskarvarman — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-history/ancient-assam-sec/varman-dynasty/
Summary: Practice varman dynasty & bhaskarvarman questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Who was the founder of the Varman dynasty of Kamarupa?
A: Pushyavarman
Q: Pushyavarman founded the Varman dynasty in approximately which year?
A: c. 350 AD
Q: The Varman dynasty ruled Kamarupa for how many years approximately?
A: About 300 years (c. 350-650 AD)
Q: Pushyavarman emerged as a ruler during the decline of which empire?
A: The Gupta empire
Q: Which Gupta ruler is mentioned in connection with the early Varman kings?
A: Samudragupta
Q: The successor of Pushyavarman was?
A: Samudravarman
Q: The wife of Samudravarman, who is mentioned in inscriptions, was?
A: Dattadevi
Q: The first four Varman kings acknowledged the nominal supremacy of which empire?
A: The Gupta empire
Q: Which Varman king performed the horse sacrifice (asvamedha)?
A: Mahendravarman and Narayanavarman
Q: The capital of the Varman dynasty was?
A: Pragjyotishpur
Q: The greatest king of the Varman dynasty was?
A: Bhaskaravarman
Q: Bhaskaravarman ruled Kamarupa from approximately which period?
A: c. 600-650 AD
Q: Bhaskaravarman was a contemporary of which great North Indian king?
A: Harshavardhana (Harsha)
Q: Bhaskaravarman allied with Harshavardhana against which king?
A: Sasanka of Gauda
Q: Who was Sasanka?
A: The king of Gauda (Bengal) who killed Harsha's elder brother
Q: Bhaskaravarman sent an embassy to Harshavardhana led by whom?
A: His minister Hangsavega
Q: Which Chinese pilgrim was invited to Kamarupa by Bhaskaravarman?
A: Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang)
Q: Bhaskaravarman is known for his patronage of which religion?
A: Buddhism (besides Brahmanism)
Q: Which university did Bhaskaravarman have contacts with?
A: Nalanda

A: Bhaskaravarman (re-issue of an earlier grant)

A: Bhutivarman
Q: Which Varman king is mentioned as having the title 'Maharajadhiraja'?
A: Bhaskaravarman
Q: The Varman kings performed which Vedic sacrifice to strengthen their rule?
A: Asvamedha (horse sacrifice)
Q: The Dubi copper plate inscription belongs to which king?
A: Bhaskaravarman
Q: The Nagaon copper plate inscription is of which Varman king?
A: Bhaskaravarman
Q: Which Varman king was defeated by the Gauda king Mahasena?
A: Susthitavarman (Mriganka)
Q: The son of Susthitavarman who later became king was?
A: Supratisthitavarman and then Bhaskaravarman
Q: Bhaskaravarman was the son of?
A: Susthitavarman (Mriganka)
Q: The Harshacharita describes the wealth and power of which Kamarupa king?
A: Bhaskaravarman
Q: Which Varman king is described as a devotee of the goddess?
A: Narayanavarman
Q: The Varman dynasty came to an end with the death of?
A: Bhaskaravarman
Q: After Bhaskaravarman, the throne of Kamarupa was taken over by?
A: Salastambha (founder of the Mlechchha dynasty)
Q: The Varman kings were followers of which religion predominantly?
A: Brahmanism (Hinduism)
Q: Which Buddhist institution did Bhaskaravarman support?
A: The Nalanda monastery
Q: The Varman inscriptions record grants of land to which class?
A: Brahmans and religious establishments
Q: The period of the Varman dynasty is described as?
A: The golden age of ancient Kamarupa
Q: Pushyavarman performed which sacrifice according to the Dubi copper plate?
A: Asvamedha (horse sacrifice)
Q: The administrative system of the Varmans was based on?
A: The traditional Indian (Brahmanical) system with a strong monarchy
Q: Which river served as the western boundary of the Varman kingdom?
A: The Karatoya river
Q: The name of the last Varman king is?
A: Bhaskaravarman
Q: Bhaskaravarman is described by Xuanzang as a king of?
A: Kamarupa (Pragjyotisha)
Q: Which Varman king had the title 'Maharajadhiraja' (King of great kings)?
A: Bhaskaravarman
Q: The Varman kings maintained relations with which empire through marriage?
A: The Gupta empire
Q: The famous Chinese pilgrim stayed in Kamarupa during whose reign?
A: Bhaskaravarman
Q: The Varman period saw the growth of which religion in Kamarupa?
A: Both Brahmanism and Buddhism
Q: Which Varman king was a devotee of Vishnu?
A: Narayanavarman (and later kings)
Q: The title used by Pushyavarman in early inscriptions was?
A: Maharajadhiraja (or Maharaja)
Q: The Varman kingdom was also known as?
A: Kamarupa (or Pragjyotisha)
Q: The successors of the Varman dynasty are known as?
A: The Salastambha (Mlechchha) dynasty
Q: The Varman kings claimed descent from which mythical ancestor?
A: Naraka, the legendary founder of the Pragjyotisha lineage
Q: Who founded the Varman dynasty and when?
A: Pushyavarman founded the Varman dynasty around c. 350 AD.
Q: Who was the greatest king of the Varman dynasty?
A: Bhaskaravarman, who ruled c. 600-650 AD and held the title Maharajadhiraja.
Q: With which North Indian king was Bhaskaravarman allied?
A: Bhaskaravarman was a contemporary of and allied with Harshavardhana against Sasanka of Gauda.
Q: Which inscription belongs to Bhaskaravarman and re-issues an earlier grant?
A: The Nidhanpur copper plate, a re-issue of an earlier grant first issued by Bhutivarman.
Q: Which dynasty succeeded the Varmans?
A: After Bhaskaravarman, Salastambha founded the Mlechchha (Salastambha) dynasty.
Q: বৰ্মণ বংশ কোনে আৰু কেতিয়া প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল?
A: পুষ্যবৰ্মনে প্ৰায় খ্ৰী. ৩৫০ চনত বৰ্মণ বংশ প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল।
Q: বৰ্মণ বংশৰ শ্ৰেষ্ঠ ৰজা কোন আছিল?
A: ভাস্কৰবৰ্মন, যি খ্ৰী. ৬০০-৬৫০ চনত ৰাজত্ব কৰিছিল আৰু মহাৰাজাধিৰাজ উপাধি ধাৰণ কৰিছিল।
Q: ভাস্কৰবৰ্মন কোন উত্তৰ ভাৰতৰ ৰজাৰ সৈতে মিত্ৰ আছিল?
A: ভাস্কৰবৰ্মন হৰ্ষবৰ্ধনৰ সমসাময়িক আছিল আৰু গৌড়ৰ শশাংকৰ বিৰুদ্ধে তেওঁৰ সৈতে মিত্ৰ আছিল।
Q: ভাস্কৰবৰ্মনৰ কোন শিলালিপিয়ে আগৰ দান পুনৰ্জাৰি কৰিছে?
A: নিধানপুৰ তাম্ৰপত্ৰ, যি ভূতিবৰ্মনে প্ৰথমে জাৰি কৰা আগৰ দানৰ পুনৰ্জাৰি।
Q: বৰ্মণসকলৰ পিছত কোন বংশ আহিছিল?
A: ভাস্কৰবৰ্মনৰ পিছত শালস্তম্ভই ম্লেছ্ছ (শালস্তম্ভ) বংশ প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল।

### Xuanzang's Visit to Kamarupa — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-history/ancient-assam-sec/xuanzang-visit/
Summary: Practice xuanzang
Q: Who visited Kamarupa in 643 AD?
A: Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang)
Q: Xuanzang was a pilgrim from which country?
A: China
Q: Xuanzang visited Kamarupa during the reign of which king?
A: Bhaskaravarman
Q: Who invited Xuanzang to visit Kamarupa?
A: Bhaskaravarman
Q: The account of Xuanzang's visit to Kamarupa is recorded in?
A: His book Si-yu-ki
Q: According to Xuanzang, the circuit (extent) of Kamarupa was about?
A: About 1000 li
Q: According to Xuanzang, the people of Kamarupa were?
A: Of short stature, dark complexion and fierce in nature
Q: Xuanzang described the language of Kamarupa as?
A: Slightly different from mid-India
Q: According to Xuanzang, how many Buddhist monasteries existed in Kamarupa?
A: Only a few (about a hundred temples of devas, few Buddhist monasteries)
Q: Xuanzang noted that the ruler of Kamarupa was a patron of?
A: Learning (Buddhism and scholarship)
Q: Before visiting Kamarupa, Xuanzang was staying at which university?
A: Nalanda
Q: Xuanzang described the capital of Kamarupa as?
A: Pragjyotishpur (a prosperous city)
Q: According to Xuanzang, the climate and crops of Kamarupa were?
A: Fertile with abundant crops
Q: Xuanzang mentioned that Kamarupa was located east of which country?
A: Eastern India (towards the east of Pundravardhana)
Q: Xuanzang's journey to Kamarupa took him from?
A: Nalanda via Karnasuvarna (through Bengal)
Q: Bhaskaravarman held a grand assembly for Xuanzang at?
A: Pragjyotishpur (Kamarupa)
Q: How many days did the grand assembly held for Xuanzang in Kamarupa last?
A: Eighteen days
Q: According to Xuanzang, Kamarupa was about how many li in circuit?
A: About 1000 li
Q: Xuanzang found the people of Kamarupa to be?
A: Honest but fierce and prone to violence

A: Its geography, society, religion and economy
Q: Xuanzang described Kamarupa as rich in which resources?
A: Rice, fruits and other agricultural products
Q: Xuanzang noted that the king of Kamarupa was a friend of?
A: Harshavardhana
Q: According to Xuanzang, Kamarupa was ruled by a dynasty of?
A: Kshatriya origin (the Varmans)
Q: Xuanzang's account is considered a reliable source for which period?
A: The 7th century Kamarupa (Varman period)
Q: After leaving Kamarupa, Xuanzang proceeded towards?
A: Pundravardhana (Bengal)
Q: Who was Xuanzang and when did he visit Kamarupa?
A: Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang) was a Buddhist pilgrim from China who visited Kamarupa in 643 AD.
Q: In which book is Xuanzang's account of Kamarupa recorded?
A: His account is recorded in the Si-yu-ki (Records of the Western World).
Q: During whose reign did Xuanzang visit Kamarupa?
A: Xuanzang visited Kamarupa during the reign of Bhaskaravarman, who invited him.
Q: What did Xuanzang record about the extent of Kamarupa?
A: He recorded that the circuit of Kamarupa was about 1000 li.
Q: How long did the grand assembly held for Xuanzang last?
A: The grand assembly held for Xuanzang at Pragjyotishpur lasted eighteen days.
Q: জুৱানজাং কোন আছিল আৰু কেতিয়া কামৰূপ ভ্ৰমণ কৰিছিল?
A: জুৱানজাং (হিউয়েন ছাঙ) চীনৰ এজন বৌদ্ধ পৰিৱ্ৰাজক আছিল, যি ৬৪৩ খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দত কামৰূপ ভ্ৰমণ কৰিছিল।
Q: কামৰূপৰ বিষয়ে জুৱানজাঙৰ বৃত্তান্ত কোনখন গ্ৰন্থত আছে?
A: তেওঁৰ বৃত্তান্ত ছি-য়ু-কি (পশ্চিম জগতৰ ৰেকৰ্ড) গ্ৰন্থত আছে।
Q: জুৱানজাঙে কাৰ ৰাজত্বকালত কামৰূপ ভ্ৰমণ কৰিছিল?
A: জুৱানজাঙে ভাস্কৰবৰ্মনৰ ৰাজত্বকালত কামৰূপ ভ্ৰমণ কৰিছিল, যি তেওঁক আমন্ত্ৰণ কৰিছিল।
Q: কামৰূপৰ বিস্তৃতিৰ বিষয়ে জুৱানজাঙে কি লিপিবদ্ধ কৰিছিল?
A: তেওঁ লিপিবদ্ধ কৰিছিল যে কামৰূপৰ পৰিধি প্ৰায় ১০০০ লি।
Q: জুৱানজাঙৰ বাবে আয়োজিত মহাসভা কিমান দিন চলিছিল?
A: প্ৰাগজ্যোতিষপুৰত জুৱানজাঙৰ বাবে আয়োজিত মহাসভা আঠাইশ দিন চলিছিল।

### Ahom Administration (Paik, Khel, Posha) — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-history/medieval-assam-sec/ahom-administration/
Summary: Practice ahom administration (paik, khel, posha) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: What type of government did the Ahom state have?
A: Monarchy
Q: What title was given to the Ahom king?
A: Swargadeo
Q: What does the title 'Swargadeo' literally mean?
A: Lord of Heaven (Heavenly king)
Q: Who assisted the Ahom king in administration?
A: Ministers and the three great Gohains
Q: Who were the three great Gohains?
A: Burhagohain, Borgohain, Borpatrogohain
Q: During whose reign were the three great Gohain offices established or formalized?
A: Subinpha
Q: Around what period were the Gohain offices formalized under Subinpha?
A: c. 1281-1293
Q: Who was the commander-in-chief of the Ahom army?
A: Barbarua
Q: Who was the most important officer of the Ahom state after the king?
A: Barbarua
Q: What was the Ahom name of the office of the Barbarua?
A: Phu-Ke-Lung
Q: What was the Ahom name of the office of the Borgohain?
A: Thao-Ru
Q: What was the Ahom name of the office of the Borpatrogohain?
A: Thao-Mung
Q: What was the Ahom name of the office of the Phukan?
A: Thao-Lu
Q: What was the Ahom name of the office of the Baruah?
A: Phu-Kan
Q: In the Paik system, what was a 'Paik'?
A: An adult able-bodied male liable to render free service to the state
Q: What was the approximate age group of a Paik?
A: About 15 to 50 years
Q: Paiks rendered free service to the state in lieu of what?
A: Taxes
Q: What was the backbone of the Ahom state?
A: The Paik system
Q: What was a 'Got' in the Paik system?
A: A group of 3-4 paiks
Q: In the Got system, how did paiks serve by rotation?
A: One paik served while the others cultivated
Q: What was a 'Khel' in the Ahom paik organization?
A: A group of paiks allotted a specific duty or craft
Q: Every paik belonged to which unit?
A: A Khel
Q: What was the land allotted to a paik family called?
A: Gau
Q: Who reorganized the Paik system?
A: Momai Tamuli Barbarua
Q: During whose reign was the Paik system reorganized by Momai Tamuli Barbarua?
A: Pratap Singha
Q: What was the 'Posa' system?
A: Annual tribute paid by subjugated hill tribes to the Ahom state
Q: Who paid the Posa tribute to the Ahom state?
A: The subjugated hill tribes such as the Nagas
Q: Under whom was the Posa system formalized?
A: Suhungmung
Q: What was the first capital of the Ahom kingdom?
A: Charaideo
Q: Which city served as the Ahom capital before Rangpur?
A: Garhgaon
Q: Which of the following was an important Ahom capital in the 18th century?
A: Rangpur
Q: In which year did Jorhat become the capital of the Ahom kingdom?
A: 1794
Q: Who was the supreme judge in the Ahom state?
A: The king
Q: From whom was the Ahom army mainly raised?
A: The paiks
Q: A Phukan was the head of what?
A: A Phukan, a large administrative division or district
Q: A Rajkhowa was the head of what?
A: A Rajkhowa, a smaller administrative unit than a Phukan
Q: What did the rotation principle in the Got system ensure?
A: Continuous labour and cultivation for the state
Q: Why was a Got made up of 3-4 paiks?
A: So that while one served, the others could cultivate and service remained continuous
Q: Which of the following was a Khel duty or craft?
A: Blacksmiths, boatmen and weavers
Q: What did paiks do in times of peace?
A: Public works such as roads, forts, embankments and palaces
Q: What did the paiks form in times of war?
A: The military
Q: Khels organized the paiks on the basis of what?
A: Specific duty or craft, that is, division of labour
Q: On what basis did the state allot land to paik families?
A: Their service and grade in the hierarchy
Q: The Paik system was essentially what kind of system?
A: A labour service system in lieu of taxes
Q: In what form was the Posa usually paid?
A: In kind, that is, in goods
Q: By what other name is Suhungmung known?
A: Dihingia Raja
Q: What office did Momai Tamuli hold when he reorganized the Paik system?
A: Barbarua
Q: On which public projects did the paiks work?
A: Roads, forts, embankments and palaces
Q: In the administrative hierarchy, which officer commanded a larger area than a Rajkhowa?
A: A Phukan
Q: Traditionally, how many paiks was a Baruah in charge of?
A: About 20 paiks
Q: What kind of power did the Gohains hold?
A: Great power including land and subjects
Q: The Gohains were nobles drawn from which group?
A: The leading clans
Q: The Barbarua performed dual functions as what?
A: Commander-in-chief and chief administrator
Q: Which unit was larger, a Phukan or a Rajkhowa?
A: A Phukan
Q: Besides land revenue, from what did the Ahom state derive income?
A: Trade, elephants and other sources
Q: Who settled local disputes in the Ahom state?
A: Officials and village heads
Q: Paiks were graded hierarchically; land was allotted to them on the basis of what?
A: Service
Q: Under Suhungmung in the early 16th century, which system was formalized?
A: The Posa system
Q: Momai Tamuli Barbarua reorganized the Paik system in which period?
A: The early 17th century
Q: Which officer combined both civil and military functions in the Ahom state?
A: Barbarua
Q: From which organization were the officers of the Ahom army drawn?
A: The paik organization, with officers like Phukan and Rajkhowa
Q: In the Khel system, paiks were allotted duties such as what?
A: Makers of arms, boatmen and weavers
Q: The Ahom king was assisted by ministers and whom?
A: The three great Gohains
Q: Which of the following was NOT one of the three great Gohains?
A: Barbarua
Q: The payment of Posa signified what?
A: The subjugation or overlordship of the hill tribes
Q: The Paik system was the core of what?
A: Ahom administration
Q: Which capital was established by Sukapha?
A: Charaideo
Q: The last Ahom capital before the British annexation was which city?
A: Jorhat
Q: In war the paiks formed the army; in peace they did what?
A: Public works for the state
Q: Which statement about the Barbarua is correct?
A: He was the most important officer after the king
Q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
A: Borgohain - Thao-Ru
Q: The subjugated hill tribes paid Posa as what?
A: Annual tribute in kind
Q: 'Phu-Ke-Lung' was the Ahom name for which office?
A: Barbarua
Q: 'Thao-Mung' was the Ahom name for which office?
A: Borpatrogohain
Q: 'Thao-Ru' was the Ahom name for which office?
A: Borgohain
Q: 'Thao-Lu' was the Ahom name for which office?
A: Phukan
Q: 'Phu-Kan' was the Ahom name for which office?
A: Baruah
Q: Which of the following groups of matchings is correct?
A: Barbarua - Phu-Ke-Lung; Borgohain - Thao-Ru; Borpatrogohain - Thao-Mung; Phukan - Thao-Lu
Q: The rotation of service in a Got ensured that what happened?
A: Cultivation and state labour went on simultaneously
Q: Which statement about the paiks is correct?
A: They were adult males aged about 15 to 50 liable to free state service
Q: The Khel division of paiks was primarily based on what?
A: Occupation or craft specialization
Q: In the Ahom system, a paik family's land plot was called what?
A: Gau

A: It was paid by the Ahom king to the Mughals

A: Pratap Singha in the early 17th century
Q: Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the Ahom capitals?
A: Charaideo to Garhgaon to Rangpur to Jorhat
Q: The three great Gohains were nobles of what kind?
A: The leading clans, holding land and subjects
Q: Which pair is correctly matched?
A: Barbarua - commander-in-chief
Q: Which statement about the Gohain offices is correct?
A: They were established or formalized under Subinpha around c. 1281-1293
Q: In the Ahom judicial system, which statement is correct?
A: The king was the supreme judge
Q: Which statement about the paik-khel organization is FALSE?
A: A Khel was headed by a Gohain of the leading clan

Q: What title did the Ahom king hold and what does it mean?
A: The king held the title Swargadeo, which literally means Lord of Heaven (heavenly king).
Q: Who were the three great Gohains and when were their offices formalized?
A: The Burhagohain, Borgohain and Borpatrogohain; their offices were formalized under Subinpha, around c. 1281-1293.
Q: Who was the most important officer after the king and who commanded the army?
A: The Barbarua was the most important officer after the king and also served as commander-in-chief of the Ahom army.
Q: What was the Paik system and who reorganized it?
A: In the Paik system, adult able-bodied males aged about 15-50 rendered free service in lieu of taxes; it was reorganised by Momai Tamuli Barbarua during the reign of Pratap Singha.
Q: What were Got, Khel and Gau in the Ahom system?
A: A Got was a group of 3-4 paiks who served by rotation, a Khel was a group of paiks allotted a specific duty or craft, and a Gau was the land allotted to a paik family.
Q: আহোম ৰজাই কি উপাধি বহন কৰিছিল আৰু ইয়াৰ অৰ্থ কি?
A: ৰজাই স্বৰ্গদেউ উপাধি বহন কৰিছিল, যাৰ আক্ষৰিক অৰ্থ স্বৰ্গৰ প্ৰভু (স্বৰ্গীয় ৰজা)।

A: বুঢ়াগোহাঁই, বৰগোহাঁই আৰু বৰপাত্ৰগোহাঁই; তেওঁলোকৰ পদ সুবিনফাৰ অধীনত, প্ৰায় ১২৮১-১২৯৩ চনত সুনিৰ্দিষ্ট হৈছিল।
Q: ৰজাৰ পিছত আটাইতকৈ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ বিষয়া কোন আছিল আৰু সেনাৰ নেতৃত্ব কোনে দিছিল?
A: বৰবৰুৱা ৰজাৰ পিছত আটাইতকৈ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ বিষয়া আছিল আৰু আহোম সেনাবাহিনীৰ সেনাপতিও আছিল।

A: পাইক প্ৰথাত প্ৰায় ১৫-৫০ বছৰীয়া প্ৰাপ্তবয়স্ক সক্ষম পুৰুষে কৰৰ পৰিৱৰ্তে বিনামূলীয়া সেৱা আগবঢ়াইছিল; ইয়াক প্ৰতাপ সিংহৰ ৰাজত্বকালত মোমাই তামুলী বৰবৰুৱাই পুনৰ্গঠন কৰিছিল।

A: গোত আছিল ৩-৪ জন পাইকৰ দল যিসকলে ঘূৰ্ণনক্ৰমে সেৱা কৰিছিল, খেল আছিল এটা নিৰ্দিষ্ট কৰ্তব্য বা শিল্পৰ বাবে আবণ্টিত পাইকৰ দল, আৰু গাও আছিল এটা পাইক পৰিয়ালক আবণ্টিত মাটি।

Q: Who founded the Ahom kingdom and in which year did he enter Assam?
A: Sukapha, a Tai (Shan) prince of Mong Mao, founded the Ahom kingdom; he crossed the Patkai range and entered the Brahmaputra valley in 1228 AD.
Q: What was the first capital of the Ahom kingdom and when was it established?
A: Charaideo, established in 1253 AD in the eastern part of the Brahmaputra valley.
Q: What does the name Sukapha mean and what does 'kha' mean in Tai?
A: Sukapha means Tiger prince; in the Tai language 'kha' means tiger. His full title was Chaolung Sukapha, meaning great lord.
Q: Why is Charaideo important in Ahom history?
A: It was the first Ahom capital and later became the sacred burial ground of Ahom kings, famous for the royal Maidams (burial mounds).
Q: What was the early religion of the Ahoms?
A: The early Ahoms followed animism; they adopted Hinduism only in later times.

A: চৰাইদেউ, ১২৫৩ খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দত ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ উপত্যকাৰ পূব অংশত স্থাপিত।

A: সুকাফাৰ অৰ্থ বাঘ ৰাজকুমাৰ; টাই ভাষাত 'খা'ৰ অৰ্থ বাঘ। তেওঁৰ সম্পূৰ্ণ উপাধি চাওলুং সুকাফা, অৰ্থাৎ মহান প্ৰভু।

Q: আহোমসকলৰ প্ৰাৰম্ভিক ধৰ্ম কি আছিল?

Q: When and where was the first major Ahom-Mughal battle fought?
A: The Battle of Samdhara, in 1615, near present-day Guwahati, during the reign of Ahom king Pratap Singha.
Q: Who was Mir Jumla and when did he invade Assam?
A: Mir Jumla was the Mughal Subedar of Bengal under Aurangzeb; he invaded Assam in 1662, forcing Ahom king Jayadhwaj Singha to flee from Garhgaon.
Q: What were the key terms of the Treaty of Ghilajharighat (1663)?
A: The Ahoms agreed to pay an annual tribute that included elephants, and the Ahom princess Ramani Gabharu, daughter of Jayadhwaj Singha, was sent to the Mughal harem.
Q: Who won the Battle of Saraighat and who led each side?
A: The Ahoms won at Saraighat in 1671; Lachit Borphukan led the Ahom forces against the Mughal army led by Raja Ram Singh.
Q: What happened at the Battle of Itakhuli and where was the boundary fixed?
A: In 1682 the Ahom king Gadadhar Singha expelled the Mughals from Lower Assam, and the boundary was fixed at the Manas river.

A: সমধৰা যুদ্ধ, ১৬১৫ চনত, বৰ্তমান গুৱাহাটীৰ ওচৰত, আহোম ৰজা প্ৰতাপ সিংহৰ ৰাজত্বকালত।

A: মিৰ জুমলা আওৰংজেৱৰ অধীনত বংগৰ মোগল ছুবেদাৰ আছিল; তেওঁ ১৬৬২ চনত অসম আক্ৰমণ কৰিছিল, যাৰ ফলত আহোম ৰজা জয়ধ্বজ সিংহে গড়গাঁওৰ পৰা পলাব লগীয়া হৈছিল।

A: Maha Bandula – Burmese general who led the third invasion
Q: Which combination of regions did the Burmese advance toward, alarming the British East India Company?
A: Bengal, Cachar and Manipur
Q: Which of the following statements about the Burmese invasions is NOT true?
A: Maha Bandula led the first Burmese invasion
Q: Purnananda Burhagohain, the Ahom chief minister, died during the first Burmese invasion while doing what?
A: Fleeing from the advancing Burmese
Q: Which Burmese king was on the throne when the first invasion of Assam was ordered?
A: Bodawpaya
Q: What was the long-term consequence of Gaurinath Singha's appeal for Burmese help during his reign (1780-1795)?
A: The Burmese presence later became a burden and paved the way for the later invasions
Q: Which statement about Jogeswar Singha is correct?
A: He was a puppet king installed by the Burmese in 1821
Q: What was the immediate international consequence of the Burmese occupation of Assam?
A: It alarmed the British East India Company and led to the First Anglo-Burmese War
Q: Is Burmese Invasions - Maanor Akroman (Bilingual English & Assamese) free to use on axomexam?
A: Burmese Invasions - Maanor Akroman (Bilingual English & Assamese) is completely free. You can read all 55 questions and their explanations on axomexam.in with no registration or charge, which makes it easy to revise the same set more than once.
Q: Are the Burmese Invasions - Maanor Akroman (Bilingual English & Assamese) questions available in Assamese and English?
A: Yes. Burmese Invasions - Maanor Akroman (Bilingual English & Assamese) is bilingual: the question, every option and the full explanation are given in both Assamese and English, so you can read the problem in one language and the solution in the other.
Q: How many questions does Burmese Invasions - Maanor Akroman (Bilingual English & Assamese) include?
A: The Burmese Invasions - Maanor Akroman (Bilingual English & Assamese) set is expanded over time, so the number of questions keeps growing. At the moment you can work through about 55 questions here with full answers.
Q: What is meant by Maanor Akroman?
A: Maanor Akroman is the Assamese term for the Burmese invasions and the oppression and atrocities suffered in Assam between 1817 and 1826.
Q: Who invited the Burmese to invade Assam and why?
A: Badan Chandra Borphukan, after being exiled by chief minister Purnananda Burhagohain, went to Burma and persuaded the Burmese king Bodawpaya to invade Assam.
Q: Who was the last independent Ahom king?
A: Chandrakanta Singha (Tai name Sudingpha), who ruled with interruptions during 1811-1818 and 1819-1821 and was deposed by the Burmese.
Q: Which general led the third Burmese invasion and what did the Burmese do?
A: Maha Bandula led the third invasion in 1821-22; the Burmese sacked Jorhat and the royal capital and occupied Assam, installing Jogeswar Singha as a puppet king in 1821.
Q: How did the Burmese invasions end for Assam?
A: They led to the First Anglo-Burmese War (1824-1826), which ended with the Treaty of Yandabo on 24 February 1826, after which Assam passed to the British.
Q: মানৰ আক্ৰমণ বুলিলে কি বুজায়?
A: মানৰ আক্ৰমণ হৈছে ১৮১৭ৰ পৰা ১৮২৬ চনৰ ভিতৰত অসমত হোৱা মানসকলৰ আক্ৰমণ তথা অত্যাচাৰৰ অসমীয়া নাম।
Q: কোনে আৰু কিয় মানসকলক অসম আক্ৰমণ কৰিবলৈ মাতিছিল?
A: মুখ্যমন্ত্ৰী পূৰ্ণানন্দ বুঢ়াগোহাঁইয়ে নিৰ্বাসন দিয়াৰ পিছত বদন চন্দ্ৰ বৰফুকনে বাৰ্মালৈ গৈ মান ৰজা বদৌপায়াক অসম আক্ৰমণ কৰিবলৈ পতিয়ন নিয়াইছিল।
Q: শেষ স্বাধীন আহোম ৰজা কোন আছিল?
A: চন্দ্ৰকান্ত সিংহ (তাই নাম চুদিংফা), যি ১৮১১-১৮১৮ আৰু ১৮১৯-১৮২১ চনত বাধা-বিঘিনিৰ মাজেৰে শাসন কৰিছিল আৰু মানসকলে তেওঁক পদচ্যুত কৰিছিল।
Q: তৃতীয় মান আক্ৰমণৰ নেতৃত্ব কোনে দিছিল আৰু মানসকলে কি কৰিছিল?
A: মহা বান্দুলাই ১৮২১-২২ চনত তৃতীয় আক্ৰমণৰ নেতৃত্ব দিছিল; মানসকলে যোৰহাট আৰু ৰাজধানী লুটপাট কৰি অসম দখল কৰিছিল আৰু ১৮২১ চনত যোগেশ্বৰ সিংহক পুতলা ৰজা হিচাপে স্থাপন কৰিছিল।
Q: মানৰ আক্ৰমণে অসমৰ বাবে কি পৰিণতি আনিছিল?
A: ই প্ৰথম ইংৰাজ-মান যুদ্ধ (১৮২৪-১৮২৬)লৈ লৈ গৈছিল, যি ২৪ ফেব্ৰুৱাৰী ১৮২৬ চনত য়াণ্ডাবু সন্ধিৰ দ্বাৰা শেষ হৈছিল আৰু তাৰ পিছত অসম ব্ৰিটিছৰ অধীনলৈ গৈছিল।

Q: Where was the Chutiya kingdom located and what was its capital?
A: It lay in eastern/upper Assam and its capital was Sadiya, in present-day Tinsukia district.
Q: Who was the last king of the Chutiya kingdom?
A: Nitipal was the last king; he was killed after the Ahom conquest.

A: Ratnadhwajpal built the city of Ratnapur at Sadiya.

A: ই পূব/উজনি অসমত আছিল আৰু ৰাজধানী আছিল সাদিয়া, বৰ্তমান তিনিচুকীয়া জিলাত।
Q: চুতীয়া ৰাজ্যৰ শেষ ৰজা কোন আছিল?

Q: চুতীয়া ৰাজ্য কোনে আৰু কেতিয়া জয় কৰিছিল?
A: আহোম ৰজা সুহুংমুঙে (দিহিঙ্গিয়া ৰজা) ১৫২৩ চনত জয় কৰিছিল।
Q: সতী সাধনী কোন আছিল?
A: ৰাজ্য পতনৰ সময়ত অপমানতকৈ মৃত্যু বাছনি কৰাৰ বাবে স্মৰণীয় বীৰাঙ্গনা চুতীয়া ৰাণী-ৰাজকুমাৰী; তেওঁ চুতীয়া সাহসৰ প্ৰতীক।
Q: ৰত্নপুৰ নগৰ কোন শাসকে নিৰ্মাণ কৰিছিল?
A: ৰত্নধ্বজপালে সাদিয়াত ৰত্নপুৰ নগৰ নিৰ্মাণ কৰিছিল।

### Early Invasions (Bakhtiyar Khilji) — ADRE, APSC

Q: Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khalji was a ___ general of the Delhi Sultanate.

Q: Who was Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khalji?
A: A Turkish general of the Ghurid dynasty who served under Qutb-ud-din Aibak of the Delhi Sultanate.
Q: When did Bakhtiyar Khalji invade Assam and how was he defeated?
A: He invaded in 1205-06 AD and was defeated and driven out by king Prithu of Kamarupa with the help of allied neighbouring kings.

A: About 1000 cavalry - the claim that he brought 10,000 is the incorrect statement tested in questions.

Q: মুহম্মদ বিন বখতিয়াৰ খিলজি কোন আছিল?
A: ঘুৰি বংশৰ এজন তুৰ্কী সেনাপতি, যি দিল্লী চুলতানীৰ কুতুব-উদ-দ্বীন আইবকৰ অধীনত কাম কৰিছিল।
Q: বখতিয়াৰ খিলজিয়ে কেতিয়া অসম আক্ৰমণ কৰিছিল আৰু কেনেকৈ পৰাজিত হৈছিল?
A: তেওঁ ১২০৫-০৬ খ্ৰী.ত আক্ৰমণ কৰিছিল আৰু কামৰূপৰ ৰজা পৃথুৱে মিত্ৰপক্ষীয় চুবুৰীয়া ৰজাসকলৰ সহায়ত তেওঁক পৰাস্ত কৰি খেদি পঠিয়াইছিল।
Q: বখতিয়াৰ খিলজিৰ সৈতে কিমান অশ্বাৰোহী আছিল?
A: প্ৰায় ১০০০ অশ্বাৰোহী - তেওঁ ১০,০০০ লৈ আহিছিল বুলি কোৱাটোৱেই প্ৰশ্নত পৰীক্ষা কৰা অশুদ্ধ উক্তি।
Q: আক্ৰমণৰ কথা কোনখন ইতিহাস পুথিত আছে?
A: তবাকাত-ই-নাছিৰী, মিনহাজ-উদ-দ্বীন চিৰাজে লিখা।
Q: প্ৰথম আক্ৰমণৰ পিছত কি ঘটিছিল?
A: প্ৰায় ১২২৮ চনত নাছিৰুদ্দিন মাহমুদে (ইলতুৎমিছৰ পুত্ৰ) কামৰূপ আক্ৰমণ কৰি ৰজা সন্ধ্যাক ৰাজধানী সলাবলৈ বাধ্য কৰে, আৰু ১২৫৭ চনত বলবনৰ পুত্ৰই আন এক ব্যৰ্থ অভিযান চলায়।

A: It split into two branches - Koch Bihar in the west and Koch Hajo in the east.
Q: When did Koch Bihar merge with India?
A: Koch Bihar became a British princely state and merged with India in 1949.
Q: কোচ ৰাজ্য কোনে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল?
A: বিশ্ব সিংহই প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল; তেওঁ প্ৰায় ১৫১৫ৰ পৰা ১৫৪০ চনলৈ শাসন কৰিছিল আৰু হৰিয়া মণ্ডলৰ পুত্ৰ আছিল।
Q: কোচ ৰাজ্যৰ মহান শাসক কোন আছিল?
A: নাৰায়ণ, যি প্ৰায় ১৫৪০ৰ পৰা ১৫৮৭ চনলৈ শাসন কৰিছিল, মহান কোচ শাসক হিচাপে গণ্য কৰা হয়।
Q: চিলাৰাই কোন আছিল?
A: চিলাৰাই (সুক্লধ্বজ) নাৰায়ণৰ ভাতৃ আৰু বিখ্যাত কোচ সেনাপতি আছিল; তেওঁ ১৫৭১ চনত মৃত্যুবৰণ কৰে।
Q: নাৰায়ণৰ মৃত্যুৰ পিছত কোচ ৰাজ্যৰ কি হৈছিল?
A: ই দুটা শাখাত বিভক্ত হৈছিল - পশ্চিমত কোচ বিহাৰ আৰু পূৱত কোচ হাজো।
Q: কোচ বিহাৰ কেতিয়া ভাৰতৰ সৈতে একত্ৰিত হৈছিল?
A: কোচ বিহাৰ ব্ৰিটিছ দেশীয় ৰাজ্য হৈ পৰে আৰু ১৯৪৯ চনত ভাৰতৰ সৈতে একত্ৰিত হয়।

### Medieval Assam History — 300 Practice Questions | ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-history/medieval-assam-sec/medieval-assam/
Summary: 300 medieval Assam history questions with answers for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Covers the Ahom, Koch and Kachari kingdoms and the Battle of Saraighat.
Q: Who founded the Ahom kingdom in Assam?
A: Sukaphaa founded the Ahom kingdom in 1228 CE after entering the Brahmaputra valley through the Patkai range.
Q: Who won the Battle of Saraighat?
A: The Ahoms under Lachit Borphukan defeated the Mughals under Ram Singh in 1671 at Saraighat near Guwahati.
Q: What was the paik system?
A: The paik system was the Ahom labour and military organisation in which every adult male served the state as a soldier or worker for part of the year.

Q: When did the Moamoria Rebellion begin and under which king?
A: It began in 1769 during the reign of Ahom king Lakshmi Singha, also known by the Tai name Sunyeopha.
Q: Who founded the Moamara Satra and who were the Moamorias?
A: The Moamara Satra was founded by Aniruddhadeva, a disciple of Gopal Ata. The Moamorias were its Vaishnavite followers, mostly from the Moran and other common and lower-caste communities.
Q: What happened at Rangpur in 1769?
A: The rebels captured the Ahom capital Rangpur and took king Lakshmi Singha prisoner; he was later restored through the efforts of nobles, Brahmins and loyalists.
Q: What were the main causes of the Moamoria Rebellion?
A: Chiefly the Ahom court's support for orthodox Sakta Brahmins and its persecution of Vaishnavite Moamorias, along with caste discrimination, heavy taxation and oppressive administration.
Q: How did the Moamoria Rebellion affect the Ahom kingdom?
A: It greatly weakened the Ahom kingdom, forced Gaurinath Singha to flee in 1786, led him to invite the Burmese, and ultimately paved the way for the Burmese invasions and British intervention.
Q: মোৱামৰীয়া বিদ্ৰোহ কেতিয়া আৰু কোন ৰজাৰ অধীনত আৰম্ভ হৈছিল?
A: ই ১৭৬৯ চনত আহোম ৰজা লক্ষ্মী সিংহৰ ৰাজত্বকালত আৰম্ভ হৈছিল, যাক তাই নাম চুঙেউফা বুলিও জনা যায়।
Q: মোৱামৰা সত্ৰ কেৱে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল আৰু মোৱামৰীয়াসকল কোন আছিল?
A: মোৱামৰা সত্ৰ গোপাল আতাৰ শিষ্য অনিৰুদ্ধদেৱে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল। মোৱামৰীয়াসকল আছিল ইয়াৰ বৈষ্ণৱ অনুগামী, মূলতঃ মৰাণ আৰু অন্যান্য সাধাৰণ আৰু নিম্ন বৰ্ণৰ সম্প্ৰদায়ৰ লোক।
Q: ১৭৬৯ চনত ৰংপুৰত কি হৈছিল?
A: বিদ্ৰোহীসকলে আহোম ৰাজধানী ৰংপুৰ দখল কৰি ৰজা লক্ষ্মী সিংহক বন্দী কৰিছিল; পিছত সভাসদ, ব্ৰাহ্মণ আৰু অনুগতসকলৰ চেষ্টাত তেওঁ পুনৰ সিংহাসনত বহিছিল।
Q: মোৱামৰীয়া বিদ্ৰোহৰ মূল কাৰণসমূহ কি আছিল?
A: মূলতঃ আহোম ৰাজসভাৰ ৰক্ষণশীল শাক্ত ব্ৰাহ্মণসকলৰ প্ৰতি সমৰ্থন আৰু বৈষ্ণৱ মোৱামৰীয়াসকলৰ ওপৰত নিৰ্যাতন, লগতে বৰ্ণ বৈষম্য, অত্যধিক কৰ আৰু দমনমূলক শাসন।
Q: মোৱামৰীয়া বিদ্ৰোহই আহোম ৰাজ্যক কেনেকৈ প্ৰভাৱিত কৰিছিল?
A: ই আহোম ৰাজ্যক অতিশয় দুৰ্বল কৰি পেলাইছিল, ১৭৮৬ চনত গৌৰীনাথ সিংহক পলাবলৈ বাধ্য কৰিছিল, তেওঁক মানসকলক মাতিবলৈ বাধ্য কৰিছিল, আৰু শেষত মান আক্ৰমণ তথা ব্ৰিটিছ হস্তক্ষেপৰ বাট মুকলি কৰিছিল।

### Neo-Vaishnavite Movement (Sankardeva) — ADRE, APSC

Q: In which year was Srimanta Sankardeva born?
A: 1449 AD
Q: Where was Srimanta Sankardeva born?
A: Bordowa (Nagaon)
Q: What is the name of the religious movement founded by Sankardeva in Assam?
A: Eka Sharana Naam Dharma
Q: Who founded the Neo-Vaishnavite movement in Assam?
A: Sankardeva

A: Madhavdeva

A: 1489 AD

A: Letekupukhuri

A: Satyasandhya

A: Kusumber Bhuyan

A: His grandmother Khersuti

A: 1568 AD

A: 1596 AD

A: Sankardeva

A: Sangeet Natak Akademi

A: A prayer house (house of naam)

A: A Vaishnavite monastery / centre of worship

A: A one-act devotional drama

A: 32 years

A: Shakti worship (Shakta)

A: Koch kingdom

A: Four

A: Bheladanga

A: Bheladanga

A: Devotional songs

A: Gunamala

A: Sankardeva

A: Sankardeva

A: Naam Ghosha

A: Naam Ghosha

A: Satsang (congregation)

A: Image worship and animal sacrifice
Q: Where was the first Ankiya Naat (the Chihna-yatra) staged?
A: Bordowa

A: After Sankardeva's death in 1568

Q: Who founded the Neo-Vaishnavite movement in Assam and what was it called?
A: Srimanta Sankardeva founded the movement and called it Eka Sharana Naam Dharma, the religion of single refuge in the Name of God.
Q: Who was Madhavdeva and what is his great work?
A: Madhavdeva was the chief disciple of Sankardeva, born in 1489 and died in 1596. He became head of the movement after 1568 and composed the Naam Ghosha.
Q: What are the Satra, Namghar and Ankiya Naat?
A: A Satra is a Vaishnavite monastery and centre of worship, a Namghar is the prayer house, and an Ankiya Naat is a one-act devotional drama. The first such drama was the Chihna-yatra.
Q: What are the four Samhatis of the Vaishnavite Satras?
A: The four Samhatis are Brahma (associated with Damodardeva), Purusha (Gopal Ata), Nika (Mathuradasa) and Kala.
Q: Which classical dance of India developed from this movement?
A: Sattriya dance, which developed in the Satras and was recognised as a classical dance of India by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.
Q: অসমত নৱ-বৈষ্ণৱ আন্দোলন কেৱে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল আৰু ইয়াৰ নাম কি আছিল?
A: শ্ৰীমন্ত শংকৰদেৱে এই আন্দোলন প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল আৰু ইয়াৰ নাম দিছিল এক শৰণ নাম ধৰ্ম, অৰ্থাৎ ঈশ্বৰৰ নামত একক আশ্ৰয়ৰ ধৰ্ম।
Q: মাধৱদেৱ কোন আছিল আৰু তেওঁৰ মহান ৰচনা কি?
A: মাধৱদেৱ শংকৰদেৱৰ প্ৰধান শিষ্য আছিল, ১৪৮৯ চনত জন্ম আৰু ১৫৯৬ চনত মৃত্যু। ১৫৬৮ চনৰ পিছত তেওঁ আন্দোলনৰ মুৰব্বী হৈছিল আৰু নামঘোষা ৰচনা কৰিছিল।
Q: সত্ৰ, নামঘৰ আৰু অংকীয়া নাট কি?
A: সত্ৰ হৈছে বৈষ্ণৱ মঠ আৰু উপাসনাৰ কেন্দ্ৰ, নামঘৰ হৈছে প্ৰাৰ্থনাৰ ঘৰ, আৰু অংকীয়া নাট হৈছে একাঙ্কী ভক্তিমূলক নাটক। প্ৰথম এনে নাট আছিল চিহ্ন-যাত্ৰা।
Q: বৈষ্ণৱ সত্ৰসমূহৰ চাৰিটা সম্বতি কি কি?
A: চাৰিটা সম্বতি হৈছে ব্ৰহ্ম (দামোদৰদেৱৰ সৈতে সম্পৰ্কিত), পুৰুষ (গোপাল আতা), নিকা (মথুৰাদাস) আৰু কাল।
Q: এই আন্দোলনৰ পৰাই বিকশিত ভাৰতৰ শাস্ত্ৰীয় নৃত্য কোনটো?
A: সত্ৰীয়া নৃত্য, যি সত্ৰসমূহত বিকশিত হৈছিল আৰু সংগীত নাটক অকাডেমীয়ে ভাৰতৰ শাস্ত্ৰীয় নৃত্য হিচাপে স্বীকৃতি দিছিল।

Q: When and where was the Battle of Saraighat fought?
A: It was fought in 1671 near Guwahati at a narrow stretch of the Brahmaputra river during the reign of Ahom king Udayaditya Singha.
Q: Who led the two sides at the Battle of Saraighat?
A: Lachit Borphukan led the Ahom forces, and the Mughal army was led by Ram Singh, son of Raja Jai Singh I, sent by Emperor Aurangzeb.
Q: Why is the Battle of Saraighat famous?
A: It was a decisive naval victory in which the Ahoms used small swift boats to destroy the large Mughal fleet, saving Assam from Mughal occupation; it is regarded as the greatest naval victory in Assam's history.
Q: What happened at the Battle of Itakhuli in 1682?
A: Under Ahom king Gadadhar Singha, the Ahom commander Hussain Borphukan defeated the Mughal Faujdar Mansur Khan at Itakhuli hill, permanently driving the Mughals out of Guwahati and Lower Assam.
Q: Where was the Ahom-Mughal boundary fixed and when is Lachit Divas observed?
A: After Itakhuli the boundary was fixed at the Manas river. Lachit Divas is observed on 24 November, the birth anniversary of Lachit Borphukan.
Q: শৰাইঘাটৰ যুদ্ধ কেতিয়া আৰু ক'ত হৈছিল?
A: ই ১৬৭১ চনত গুৱাহাটীৰ ওচৰত ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ নদীৰ এটা সংকীৰ্ণ অংশত আহোম ৰজা উদয়াদিত্য সিংহৰ ৰাজত্বকালত হৈছিল।
Q: শৰাইঘাটৰ যুদ্ধত দুয়োপক্ষৰ নেতৃত্ব কোনে দিছিল?
A: লাচিত বৰফুকনে আহোম বাহিনীৰ নেতৃত্ব দিছিল, আৰু মোগল সেনাৰ নেতৃত্ব দিছিল সম্ৰাট ঔৰংজেৱৰ দ্বাৰা প্ৰেৰিত ৰাজা জয় সিংহ I ৰ পুত্ৰ ৰাম সিংহই।
Q: শৰাইঘাটৰ যুদ্ধ কিয় বিখ্যাত?
A: এইটো এটা চূড়ান্ত নৌ বিজয় আছিল, য'ত আহোমসকলে সৰু দ্ৰুতগামী নাৱেৰে বিশাল মোগল নৌবহৰ ধ্বংস কৰি অসমক মোগল দখলৰ পৰা ৰক্ষা কৰিছিল; ইয়াক অসমৰ ইতিহাসৰ মহান নৌ বিজয় বুলি গণ্য কৰা হয়।
Q: ১৬৮২ চনত ইটাখুলিৰ যুদ্ধত কি হৈছিল?
A: আহোম ৰজা গদাধৰ সিংহৰ অধীনত আহোম সেনাপতি হুছেইন বৰফুকনে ইটাখুলি পাহাৰত মোগল ফৌজদাৰ মনছুৰ খানক পৰাস্ত কৰি গুৱাহাটী আৰু নামনি অসমৰ পৰা মোগলক চিৰদিনৰ বাবে খেদি পঠিয়াইছিল।
Q: আহোম-মোগল সীমা ক'ত স্থিৰ হৈছিল আৰু লাচিত দিৱস কেতিয়া পালন কৰা হয়?
A: ইটাখুলিৰ পিছত সীমা মনাহ নদীত স্থিৰ হৈছিল। লাচিত দিৱস ২৪ নৱেম্বৰত, লাচিত বৰফুকনৰ জন্ম জয়ন্তীত পালন কৰা হয়।

Q: When and why was the Treaty of Yandabo signed?
A: It was signed on 24 February 1826 to end the First Anglo-Burmese War (1824-1826), after Burmese expansion into Assam, Manipur and Arakan threatened the British frontier.
Q: Which territories did Burma cede under the Treaty of Yandabo?
A: Burma ceded Assam, Manipur, Arakan (now Rakhine) and Tenasserim (now Tanintharyi), and gave up all claims over Assam, Cachar and Jaintia.
Q: What did Burma have to pay under the treaty?
A: Burma agreed to pay an indemnity of one crore rupees in installments and to receive a British resident at Ava.
Q: Who was the last Ahom king and how did the dynasty end?
A: Purandar Singha was the last Ahom king. The British restored him in 1833 as a tributary ruler of Upper Assam and deposed him in 1838 for failing to pay the annual tribute, ending the dynasty.
Q: What was the result of the Treaty of Yandabo for Assam?
A: Assam passed to the British East India Company in 1826, the Burmese threat ended, and British colonial rule began. Assam later became a separate province in 1874 with its capital at Shillong.
Q: য়াণ্ডাবু সন্ধি কেতিয়া আৰু কিয় স্বাক্ষৰিত হৈছিল?
A: ই ২৪ ফেব্ৰুৱাৰী ১৮২৬ চনত প্ৰথম ইংৰাজ-মান যুদ্ধ (১৮২৪-১৮২৬) শেষ কৰিবলৈ স্বাক্ষৰিত হৈছিল, যেতিয়া অসম, মণিপুৰ আৰু আৰাকানলৈ বাৰ্মাৰ সম্প্ৰসাৰণে ব্ৰিটিছ সীমাক ভাবুকি দিছিল।
Q: য়াণ্ডাবু সন্ধি অনুসৰি বাৰ্মাই কোনবোৰ অঞ্চল এৰি দিছিল?
A: বাৰ্মাই অসম, মণিপুৰ, আৰাকান (এতিয়া ৰাখাইন) আৰু টেনাছেৰিম (এতিয়া টেনিন্থাৰী) এৰি দিছিল, আৰু অসম, কাছাৰ তথা জয়ন্তীয়াৰ ওপৰত সকলো দাবী ত্যাগ কৰিছিল।
Q: সন্ধি অনুসৰি বাৰ্মাই কি দিবলগীয়া হৈছিল?
A: বাৰ্মাই কিস্তিত এক কোটি টকা ক্ষতিপূৰণ দিবলৈ আৰু আভাত এজন ব্ৰিটিছ ৰেচিডেণ্টক গ্ৰহণ কৰিবলৈ সন্মত হৈছিল।
Q: শেষ আহোম ৰজা কোন আছিল আৰু বংশৰ অন্ত কেনেকৈ হৈছিল?
A: পুৰন্দৰ সিংহ শেষ আহোম ৰজা আছিল। ব্ৰিটিছে তেওঁক ১৮৩৩ চনত উচ্চ অসমৰ ৰাজস্ব-দানকাৰী শাসক হিচাপে পুনঃস্থাপন কৰি ১৮৩৮ চনত বাৰ্ষিক ৰাজস্ব নিদিয়াৰ বাবে পদচ্যুত কৰিছিল, যাৰ ফলত বংশৰ অন্ত পৰিছিল।
Q: য়াণ্ডাবু সন্ধিৰ অসমৰ বাবে পৰিণতি কি হৈছিল?
A: ১৮২৬ চনত অসম ব্ৰিটিছ ইষ্ট ইণ্ডিয়া কোম্পানীৰ অধীনলৈ গৈছিল, মান ভাবুকিৰ অন্ত পৰিছিল আৰু ব্ৰিটিছ ঔপনিৱেশিক শাসন আৰম্ভ হৈছিল। পিছলৈ ১৮৭৪ চনত অসম সুকীয়া প্ৰদেশ হৈছিল আৰু ইয়াৰ ৰাজধানী আছিল শ্বিলং।

A: Purandar Singha was restored as the tributary king of Upper Assam in 1833, but he was deposed in 1838 for failing to pay the tribute; his deposition ended the Ahom dynasty.
Q: When did Assam become a separate province and who was its first Chief Commissioner?
A: Assam was made a separate Chief Commissioner's Province in 1874, with Shillong as its capital and Colonel R.H. Keatinge as its first Chief Commissioner.
Q: য়াণ্ডাবু সন্ধি কেতিয়া আৰু ক'ত স্বাক্ষৰিত হৈছিল?
A: ই ১৮২৬ চনৰ ২৪ ফেব্ৰুৱাৰী তাৰিখে য়াণ্ডাবু নামৰ গাঁৱত, আভাৰ ওচৰত ইৰাৱতী নদীৰ পাৰত স্বাক্ষৰিত হৈছিল, যিয়ে প্ৰথম ইংগ-বাৰ্মা যুদ্ধৰ অন্ত পেলাইছিল।
Q: য়াণ্ডাবু সন্ধি অনুসৰি বাৰ্মাই ব্ৰিটিছক কি অঞ্চল ছুটি দিছিল?
A: বাৰ্মাই অসম, মণিপুৰ, আৰাকান আৰু টেনাছেৰিম ব্ৰিটিছক ছুটি দিছিল, কাছাৰ আৰু জয়ন্তীয়াৰ ওপৰত দাবী পৰিত্যাগ কৰিছিল, আৰু আভাত ব্ৰিটিছ দূত গ্ৰহণ কৰিবলৈ মান্তি হৈছিল।
Q: অসমৰ প্ৰথম ব্ৰিটিছ এজেণ্ট কোন আছিল?
A: ডেভিড স্কটক ১৮২৬ চনত অসমৰ প্ৰথম ব্ৰিটিছ এজেণ্ট হিচাপে নিযুক্তি দিয়া হৈছিল; তেওঁৰ পদটোক পাছত কমিছনাৰ উপাধি দিয়া হয়।
Q: ব্ৰিটিছসকলে নামনি আৰু উজনি অসম কেতিয়া দখল কৰিছিল?
A: ব্ৰিটিছসকলে ১৮২৮ চনত নামনি অসমৰ প্ৰশাসন দখল কৰিছিল আৰু উজনি অসম পাছত, ১৮২৮ৰ পিছত দখল কৰিছিল।
Q: পুৰন্দৰ সিংহ কোন আছিল আৰু তেওঁৰ কি হৈছিল?
A: পুৰন্দৰ সিংহক ১৮৩৩ চনত উজনি অসমৰ খাজনাদায়ী ৰজা হিচাপে পুনৰ সিংহাসনত বহুওৱা হৈছিল, কিন্তু ১৮৩৮ চনত খাজনা দিবলৈ ব্যৰ্থ হোৱাৰ বাবে তেওঁক পদচ্যুত কৰা হয়; এই পদচ্যুতিয়ে আহোম ৰাজবংশৰ অৱসান ঘটায়।
Q: অসম কেতিয়া সুকীয়া প্ৰদেশ হ'ল আৰু প্ৰথম মুখ্য কমিছনাৰ কোন আছিল?
A: ১৮৭৪ চনত অসমক সুকীয়া মুখ্য কমিছনাৰৰ প্ৰদেশ কৰা হয়, ৰাজধানী শ্বিলং আৰু প্ৰথম মুখ্য কমিছনাৰ কৰ্নেল আৰ.এইচ. কিটিং।
