Q: When and how was the Civil Disobedience Movement launched?
A: Mahatma Gandhi launched the Civil Disobedience Movement on 12 March 1930 with the Dandi March, also called the Salt Satyagraha, whose objective was to break the salt law by making salt from seawater.
Q: Who led the Civil Disobedience Movement in Assam?
A: The Indian National Congress led the movement in Assam, and a prominent Congress leader who led it here was Gopinath Bordoloi; the Assam phase took place in 1930.
Q: What was the Cunningham Circular and who issued it?
A: The Cunningham Circular was a government order issued in Assam in 1930 during the Civil Disobedience Movement by the Director of Public Instruction (DPI) of Assam, whose name was Cunningham, not by the Governor.
Q: What did the Cunningham Circular forbid and what penalties did it threaten?
A: It forbade students and teachers from taking part in political activities and required them to remain loyal to the government, threatening withdrawal of scholarships and expulsion from institutions.
Q: How did the students of Assam react to the Cunningham Circular?
A: The students of Assam were the main protesters; students of Cotton College, Guwahati, boycotted classes and demonstrated, and the agitation was strong enough to force the government to withdraw the Circular.

A: Besides salt satyagraha, the Civil Disobedience Movement in Assam included the boycott of foreign cloth and British goods, and picketing.

A: অসমত আন্দোলন ভাৰতীয় জাতীয় কংগ্ৰেছে পৰিচালনা কৰিছিল, আৰু ইয়াত আগশাৰীৰ কংগ্ৰেছ নেতা আছিল গোপীনাথ বৰদলৈ; অসমৰ পৰ্যায়টো ১৯৩০ চনত হৈছিল।

Q: Why did the early anti-British revolts take place in Assam?
A: They took place because the British, contrary to expectations after the Treaty of Yandabo of 1826, stayed back in Assam and ruled it as a conquered territory, which created deep resentment among the Ahom nobility.
Q: Who led the anti-British uprising in Upper Assam in 1828?
A: Gomdhar Konwar, who belonged to the Ahom royal family, led the uprising in 1828, supported by the Burhagohain and other nobles; he was captured and exiled.
Q: What was the aim of Gomdhar Konwar's uprising?
A: The aim was to drive out the British and restore Ahom rule in Assam.
Q: Who was Piyoli Phukan and what did he do?
A: Piyoli Phukan was a former Barbarua who, in 1830, formed a conspiracy to overthrow the British and restore the Ahom kingdom.
Q: How was Piyoli Phukan punished?
A: His conspiracy was betrayed; he was arrested and hanged at Guwahati in 1830, and his associate Jiuram Dulia Barua was also punished.
Q: Who is regarded as one of the first martyrs of the freedom movement in Assam?
A: Piyoli Phukan is regarded as one of the first martyrs of the freedom movement in Assam.
Q: অসমত প্ৰাৰম্ভিক ব্ৰিটিছ বিৰোধী বিদ্ৰোহ কিয় হৈছিল?
A: ১৮২৬ চনৰ য়াণ্ডাবু সন্ধিৰ পিছত ব্ৰিটিছে আশা কৰাৰ বিপৰীতে অসমত থাকি গৈ জয় কৰা অঞ্চল হিচাপে শাসন কৰাৰ বাবে এই বিদ্ৰোহ হৈছিল, যিয়ে আহোম অভিজাতসকলৰ গভীৰ ক্ষোভৰ সৃষ্টি কৰিছিল।
Q: ১৮২৮ চনত উজনি অসমত ব্ৰিটিছ বিৰোধী বিদ্ৰোহৰ নেতৃত্ব কোনে দিছিল?
A: আহোম ৰাজবংশৰ গোমধৰ কোঁৱৰে ১৮২৮ চনত বিদ্ৰোহৰ নেতৃত্ব দিছিল, বুঢ়াগোহাঁই আৰু অন্য অভিজাতসকলে সমৰ্থন কৰিছিল; তেওঁক বন্দী কৰি নিৰ্বাসিত কৰা হৈছিল।
Q: গোমধৰ কোঁৱৰৰ বিদ্ৰোহৰ উদ্দেশ্য কি আছিল?
A: উদ্দেশ্য আছিল ব্ৰিটিছসকলক খেদি অসমত আহোম শাসন পুনৰুদ্ধাৰ কৰা।
Q: পিয়লি ফুকন কোন আছিল আৰু তেওঁ কি কৰিছিল?
A: পিয়লি ফুকন এজন প্ৰাক্তন বৰবৰুৱা আছিল, যি ১৮৩০ চনত ব্ৰিটিছ উৎখাত কৰি আহোম ৰাজ্য পুনৰুদ্ধাৰ কৰিবলৈ ষড়যন্ত্ৰ গঠন কৰিছিল।
Q: পিয়লি ফুকনক কেনেকৈ শাস্তি দিয়া হৈছিল?
A: তেওঁৰ ষড়যন্ত্ৰ বিশ্বাসঘাতকতাৰ বলি হৈছিল; তেওঁক গ্ৰেপ্তাৰ কৰি ১৮৩০ চনত গুৱাহাটীত ফাঁচী দিয়া হৈছিল, আৰু সহযোগী জীয়াৰাম দুলীয়া বৰুৱাকো শাস্তি দিয়া হৈছিল।
Q: অসমৰ স্বাধীনতা আন্দোলনৰ প্ৰথম শ্বহীদসকলৰ এজন হিচাপে কোনজনক গণ্য কৰা হয়?
A: পিয়লি ফুকনক অসমৰ স্বাধীনতা আন্দোলনৰ প্ৰথম শ্বহীদসকলৰ এজন হিচাপে গণ্য কৰা হয়।

### Line System & Immigration Issues — ADRE, APSC

Q: When was the Line System introduced in Assam?
A: In 1920.
Q: What was the Line System?
A: A British policy in Assam to regulate the settlement of immigrant cultivators in government wastelands.
Q: Who adopted the Line System policy in Assam?
A: The British government in Assam.
Q: What was the main purpose of the Line System?
A: To restrict and regulate the settlement of immigrant cultivators in government wastelands.
Q: What were the imaginary boundary lines drawn under the Line System called?
A: They were called 'lines'.
Q: Under the Line System, where were immigrant settlers to be confined?
A: To certain demarcated 'line' or granted areas.
Q: From which region did large numbers of cultivators migrate to Assam in the early 20th century?
A: From East Bengal (present-day Bangladesh).
Q: Which areas of Assam did the immigrant cultivators mainly settle in?
A: The riverine areas of the Brahmaputra valley and other wastelands.
Q: Name the Brahmaputra valley districts where immigrant cultivators settled in large numbers.
A: Goalpara, Kamrup, Darrang and Nagaon.
Q: Under the Line System, could immigrant settlers settle anywhere they wished?
A: No, they were confined to demarcated areas.
Q: What happened in areas where the local population objected to immigrant settlement?
A: Immigrant settlers were not to be settled in such areas.

A: The Assamese people.

A: Because of the restrictions imposed on their settlement.

A: The Muslim League.

A: The Congress.

A: Gopinath Bordoloi.

A: In 1946.

A: No, it was abolished in 1946.

Q: When and by whom was the Line System introduced in Assam?
A: The Line System was introduced in 1920 by the British government in Assam to regulate the settlement of immigrant cultivators in government wastelands.
Q: What was the main purpose of the Line System?
A: Its main purpose was to restrict and regulate the settlement of immigrant cultivators in government wastelands, confining them to certain demarcated 'line' or granted areas.
Q: From where did the immigrant cultivators come and where did they settle?
A: Large numbers of cultivators migrated from East Bengal (present-day Bangladesh) in the early twentieth century and settled in the riverine areas of the Brahmaputra valley, especially in Goalpara, Kamrup, Darrang and Nagaon.
Q: Why did the Line System satisfy neither the Assamese nor the immigrants?
A: The Assamese criticized it for not effectively checking the inflow of immigrants, while the immigrant community resented the restrictions it imposed on their settlement.
Q: What were the positions of the Congress and the Muslim League on the Line System?
A: The Muslim League demanded the removal of the Line System, while the Congress, led in Assam by Gopinath Bordoloi, wanted it to be retained.
Q: When was the Line System abolished and what was the political consequence?
A: The Line System was abolished in 1946, over the strong opposition of Gopinath Bordoloi and the Assam Congress; the immigration question became a major political issue and contributed to separate 'Momin'/immigrant politics and the Cabinet Mission grouping controversy.
Q: অসমত লাইন প্ৰথা কেতিয়া আৰু কোনে প্ৰৱৰ্তন কৰিছিল?
A: লাইন প্ৰথা ১৯২০ চনত অসমৰ ব্ৰিটিছ চৰকাৰে চৰকাৰী পতিত মাটিত অনুপ্ৰৱেশকাৰী খেতিয়কসকলৰ বসতি নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ কৰাৰ বাবে প্ৰৱৰ্তন কৰিছিল।
Q: লাইন প্ৰথাৰ মূল উদ্দেশ্য কি আছিল?
A: ইয়াৰ মূল উদ্দেশ্য আছিল চৰকাৰী পতিত মাটিত অনুপ্ৰৱেশকাৰী খেতিয়কসকলৰ বসতি সীমিত আৰু নিয়ন্ত্ৰিত কৰা, তেওঁলোকক নিৰ্দিষ্ট সীমাবদ্ধ 'লাইন' বা অনুদান কৰা অঞ্চলত আৱদ্ধ ৰাখি।
Q: অনুপ্ৰৱেশকাৰী খেতিয়কসকল ক'ৰ পৰা আহিছিল আৰু ক'ত বসতি স্থাপন কৰিছিল?
A: বিংশ শতিকাৰ আৰম্ভণিতে বিপুল সংখ্যক খেতিয়ক পূব বংগৰ (বৰ্তমান বাংলাদেশ) পৰা আহিছিল আৰু ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ উপত্যকাৰ নদীসংলগ্ন অঞ্চলত, বিশেষকৈ গোৱালপাৰা, কামৰূপ, দৰং আৰু নগাঁওত বসতি স্থাপন কৰিছিল।
Q: লাইন প্ৰথাই অসমীয়া আৰু অনুপ্ৰৱেশকাৰী কাৰো কিয় সন্তুষ্ট কৰিব পৰা নাছিল?
A: অসমীয়াসকলে ইয়াক অনুপ্ৰৱেশকাৰীৰ সোঁত ফলপ্ৰসূভাৱে ৰোধ কৰিব নোৱাৰাৰ বাবে সমালোচনা কৰিছিল, আনহাতে অনুপ্ৰৱেশকাৰী সমাজে তেওঁলোকৰ বসতিৰ ওপৰত ই আৰোপ কৰা নিষেধাজ্ঞাক অসন্তুষ্ট হৈছিল।
Q: লাইন প্ৰথাৰ ওপৰত কংগ্ৰেছ আৰু মুছলিম লীগৰ অৱস্থান কি আছিল?
A: মুছলিম লীগে লাইন প্ৰথা উঠাই পেলোৱাৰ দাবী কৰিছিল, আনহাতে কংগ্ৰেছে, অসমত গোপীনাথ বৰদলৈৰ নেতৃত্বত, ইয়াক ৰাখি ৰখা বিচাৰিছিল।
Q: লাইন প্ৰথা কেতিয়া বিলুপ্ত হৈছিল আৰু ৰাজনৈতিক পৰিণতি কি আছিল?
A: ১৯৪৬ চনত গোপীনাথ বৰদলৈ আৰু অসম কংগ্ৰেছৰ তীব্ৰ বিৰোধিতা সত্ত্বেও লাইন প্ৰথা বিলুপ্ত হৈছিল; অনুপ্ৰৱেশ সমস্যা এটা প্ৰধান ৰাজনৈতিক বিষয় হৈ পৰিছিল আৰু পৃথক 'মমিন'/অনুপ্ৰৱেশকাৰী ৰাজনীতি তথা কেবিনেট মিছন গ্ৰুপিং বিতৰ্কত অৰিহণা যোগাইছিল।

### Modern Assam History — 300 Practice Questions | ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-history/modern-assam-sec/modern-assam/
Summary: 300 modern Assam history questions with answers for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Covers the Treaty of Yandabo, British rule and the Assam Movement.
Q: When was the Treaty of Yandabo signed?
A: The Treaty of Yandabo was signed in 1826 between the British and the Burmese, and it ended Burmese control over Assam and opened the way for British rule.
Q: When did Assam become a separate province?
A: Assam was separated from Bengal and became a Chief Commissioner's province in 1874, and later a Governor's province in 1921.
Q: What was the Assam Accord?
A: The Assam Accord of 1985 ended the Assam Movement and set 24 March 1971 as the cut-off date for the detection and deletion of illegal migrants from the electoral rolls.

### Partition & Sylhet Referendum (1947) — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-history/modern-assam-sec/partition-sylhet-referendum/

Q: When was the Mountbatten Plan announced?
A: On 3 June 1947.
Q: What was the date of announcement of the Mountbatten Plan?
A: 3 June 1947.
Q: Under the Mountbatten Plan, British India was to be partitioned into which two countries?
A: India and Pakistan.
Q: Which two provinces were to be partitioned under the Mountbatten Plan?
A: Bengal and Punjab.
Q: Which district of Assam was to decide its fate through a referendum?
A: Sylhet district.
Q: Was Sylhet a Muslim-majority district at the time of partition?
A: Yes.
Q: Why was a referendum held in Sylhet in 1947?
A: To let the people of Sylhet decide whether to stay with Assam (India) or join East Bengal (Pakistan).
Q: When was the Sylhet Referendum held?
A: On 6 July 1947.
Q: In which month and year was the Sylhet Referendum held?
A: July 1947.
Q: Who took part in the Sylhet Referendum?
A: The adult population of the Sylhet district.
Q: What was the outcome of the Sylhet Referendum?
A: A majority of voters voted in favour of joining East Bengal/Pakistan.
Q: Did the majority in the Sylhet Referendum vote for India or Pakistan?
A: Pakistan.
Q: Which region was Sylhet merged with after the referendum?
A: East Bengal (later East Pakistan).
Q: From which province was Sylhet detached in 1947?
A: Assam.
Q: In which year was Sylhet merged with East Bengal?
A: 1947.
Q: Did Sylhet remain part of India after the referendum?
A: No, it joined Pakistan.
Q: How did the loss of Sylhet affect the area of Assam?
A: Assam's area shrank.
Q: How did the loss of Sylhet affect the population of Assam?
A: Assam's population decreased.
Q: What happened to the proportion of Assamese-speaking people in Assam after Sylhet was detached?
A: It increased.
Q: Which hill districts of Assam remained with India after partition?
A: Khasi, Jaintia, Garo, Lushai/Mizo and Naga hills.
Q: Did the hill districts of Assam go to Pakistan after partition?
A: No, they remained with India.
Q: What did the loss of Sylhet and the grouping issue teach the leaders of Assam?
A: The need to protect the integrity of Assam.
Q: Along with the loss of Sylhet, which issue made Assam's leaders realise the need to protect the integrity of Assam?
A: The grouping issue.
Q: Was the Mountbatten Plan announced in 1946?
A: No, it was announced on 3 June 1947.
Q: Did the Sylhet Referendum take place before the announcement of the Mountbatten Plan?
A: No, it was held after (in July 1947).

A: Lord Mountbatten (the Mountbatten Plan).

A: Yes, it was then a district of Assam.
Q: Was Sylhet part of Bengal at the time of the Mountbatten Plan?
A: No, it was part of Assam.

A: Yes, that was one of the two options.

A: To stay with Assam (India) or to join East Bengal (Pakistan).

A: No, a majority chose to join East Bengal/Pakistan.

A: No, it was held in July 1947.

A: The adult population.

A: For example, Khasi and Naga hills (also Jaintia, Garo, Lushai/Mizo).

A: No, they remained with India.

A: No, only the adult population of the Sylhet district voted.

Q: Which hill districts of Assam remained with India after partition?
A: The Khasi, Jaintia, Garo, Lushai (Mizo) and Naga hills remained with India.
Q: What lesson did the loss of Sylhet and the grouping issue give to Assam's leaders?
A: They taught the leaders of Assam the need to protect the integrity of Assam.
Q: মাউণ্টবেটেন পৰিকল্পনা কেতিয়া ঘোষণা কৰা হৈছিল আৰু ই কি প্ৰস্তাৱ দিছিল?
A: ই ১৯৪৭ চনৰ ৩ জুনত ঘোষণা কৰা হৈছিল আৰু ব্ৰিটিছ ভাৰতক ভাৰত আৰু পাকিস্তান দুখন দেশত বিভক্ত কৰাৰ প্ৰস্তাৱ দিছিল, লগতে বংগ আৰু পঞ্জাবো বিভক্ত কৰাৰ।
Q: অসমৰ কোনখন জিলাই ৰেফাৰেণ্ডামৰ জৰিয়তে নিজৰ ভাগ্য নিৰ্ণয় কৰিছিল আৰু কেতিয়া?
A: চিলেট জিলাই ৰেফাৰেণ্ডামৰ জৰিয়তে নিজৰ ভাগ্য নিৰ্ণয় কৰিছিল, যিখন ১৯৪৭ চনৰ ৬ জুলাইত অনুষ্ঠিত হৈছিল।
Q: চিলেট ৰেফাৰেণ্ডামৰ ফলাফল কি আছিল?
A: ভোটাৰসকলৰ সংখ্যাগৰিষ্ঠই পূব বংগ (পাকিস্তান)ত যোগদানৰ পক্ষত ভোট দিছিল, সেয়ে চিলেট অসমৰ পৰা বিচ্ছিন্ন হৈ পূব বংগত একীভূত হৈছিল।
Q: চিলেট হেৰুওৱাই অসমৰ ওপৰত কেনে প্ৰভাৱ পেলাইছিল?
A: অসমৰ কালি হ্ৰাস পালে আৰু জনসংখ্যা কমিল, কিন্তু অসমৰ অসমীয়া ভাষী লোকৰ অনুপাত বৃদ্ধি পালে।
Q: বিভাজনৰ পিছত অসমৰ কোনবোৰ পাহাৰীয়া জিলা ভাৰতৰ লগত থাকি গৈছিল?
A: খাচী, জয়ন্তীয়া, গাৰো, লুছাই (মিজো) আৰু নগা পাহাৰ ভাৰতৰ লগত থাকি গৈছিল।
Q: চিলেটৰ ক্ষতি আৰু গোটীকৰণ বিষয়ে অসমৰ নেতাসকলক কি শিক্ষা দিছিল?
A: ই অসমৰ নেতাসকলক অসমৰ অখণ্ডতা ৰক্ষা কৰাৰ প্ৰয়োজনীয়তা শিকাইছিল।

### Peasant Uprisings (Phulaguri & Patharughat) — ADRE, APSC

Q: In which year did the Phulaguri uprising take place?
A: In 1861.
Q: At which village did the Phulaguri uprising take place?
A: At Phulaguri, in the Nagaon (Nowgong) district of Assam.
Q: By what name is the Phulaguri uprising popularly known?
A: Phulaguri Dhewa.
Q: Which British officer was killed by the peasants during the Phulaguri uprising?
A: Lt. Singer, the Magistrate (Assistant Commissioner).
Q: Which tax did the Phulaguri peasants refuse to pay?
A: The opium tax.
Q: What was the main cause of the Phulaguri uprising?
A: The British raised land revenue and imposed heavy taxes, including the opium tax.
Q: In which district of Assam is Phulaguri located?
A: In the Nagaon (Nowgong) district.
Q: How is the Phulaguri uprising regarded in the history of Assam?
A: As one of the first major peasant uprisings against British rule in Assam.
Q: In which year did the Patharughat uprising take place?
A: In 1894.
Q: Where is Patharughat located?
A: In the present Darrang district of Assam.
Q: By what other name is the Patharughat uprising known?
A: Patharughat Raijmel.
Q: What is a 'Raijmel'?
A: A people's assembly (public gathering of the peasants).
Q: On which date did the police open fire on the peasants at Patharughat?
A: On 28 January 1894.
Q: What was the main cause of the Patharughat uprising?
A: The British greatly enhanced the land revenue in Darrang district.

A: The police (and military).

A: No, they were unarmed.

A: As the Patharughat martyrs.

A: The Patharughat Massacre.

A: They organized a peaceful Raijmel (people's assembly).

A: Darrang district.

A: Phulaguri Dhewa (1861) and the Patharughat uprising (1894).

A: Both were protests against the heavy land revenue and taxes imposed by the British.

A: A large number (scores) of people were killed.

A: The Phulaguri Dhewa (in 1861).

A: It signifies an uprising (a mass upheaval or rebellion).

A: They symbolize peasant sacrifice in resistance against oppressive British taxation.

A: The peasants of Darrang district.

A: No. It occurred because the British enhanced the land revenue and imposed heavy taxes such as the opium tax.

Q: When and where did the Phulaguri uprising take place?
A: The Phulaguri uprising took place in 1861 at Phulaguri village in the Nagaon (Nowgong) district of Assam, and it is popularly known as Phulaguri Dhewa.
Q: What was the main cause of the Phulaguri uprising?
A: The British raised the land revenue and imposed heavy taxes, including the opium tax, which the Phulaguri peasants refused to pay.
Q: Which British officer was killed at Phulaguri?
A: Lt. Singer, the Magistrate (Assistant Commissioner), was killed by the peasants during the Phulaguri uprising of 1861.
Q: When, where and why did the Patharughat uprising happen?
A: The Patharughat uprising happened in 1894 in the present Darrang district, because the British had greatly enhanced the land revenue; the peasants organised a Raijmel, or people's assembly, to protest.
Q: What happened at Patharughat on 28 January 1894?
A: On 28 January 1894 the police and military opened fire on unarmed peasants gathered in a peaceful Raijmel at Patharughat; a large number were killed and are remembered as the Patharughat martyrs, and the event is called the Patharughat Massacre.
Q: What did the Phulaguri and Patharughat uprisings have in common?
A: Both were protests by the ordinary peasantry against the heavy land revenue and taxes imposed by the British, and both occurred in rural Assam during the nineteenth century.

A: অসম এছ'চিয়েচন ১৯০৩ চনত গঠন হৈছিল আৰু ই আছিল প্ৰথম সৰ্ব-অসম ৰাজনৈতিক সংগঠন; ইয়াৰ প্ৰতিষ্ঠাৰ সৈতে ঘনিষ্ঠভাৱে জড়িত নেতা আছিল মাণিক চন্দ্ৰ বৰুৱা।
Q: অসমত প্ৰথম কংগ্ৰেছ অধিৱেশন কেতিয়া আৰু ক'ত হৈছিল আৰু সভাপতি কোন আছিল?
A: অসমত অনুষ্ঠিত ভাৰতীয় জাতীয় কংগ্ৰেছৰ প্ৰথম অধিৱেশন ১৯২৬ চনত গুৱাহাটীত হৈছিল, আৰু ইয়াৰ সভাপতিত্ব কৰিছিল এছ. শ্ৰীনিবাস আয়েঙ্গাৰে।
Q: অসম প্ৰাদেশিক কংগ্ৰেছ কমিটি কেতিয়া আৰু কিয় গঠন হৈছিল?
A: APCC, অসমত ভাৰতীয় জাতীয় কংগ্ৰেছৰ প্ৰাদেশিক শাখা, ১৯১৯-১৯২১ চনত কংগ্ৰেছৰ পুনৰ্গঠনৰ সময়ত, মন্টাগু-চেমছফৰ্ড সংস্কাৰৰ পিছত গঠন হৈছিল।
Q: অসম এছ'চিয়েচনে অসমৰ বাবে কি দাবী কৰিছিল?
A: অসম এছ'চিয়েচনে অসমৰ কল্যাণৰ বাবে চৰকাৰৰ আগত দাবী উত্থাপন কৰিছিল, যাৰ ভিতৰত উত্তম প্ৰশাসন, উত্তম উদ্যোগ, আৰু পিছত অসমৰ বাবে পৃথক প্ৰদেশ আছিল।
Q: অসমত কংগ্ৰেছ মন্ত্ৰীসভা কেতিয়া আৰু কাৰ নেতৃত্বত গঠন হৈছিল?
A: ১৯৩৭ চনৰ নিৰ্বাচনৰ পিছত অসমত গোপীনাথ বৰদলৈৰ নেতৃত্বত কংগ্ৰেছ মন্ত্ৰীসভা গঠন হৈছিল।
Q: কোনটো আগতে গঠন হৈছিল, ভাৰতীয় জাতীয় কংগ্ৰেছ নে অসম এছ'চিয়েচন?
A: ভাৰতীয় জাতীয় কংগ্ৰেছ আগতে, ১৮৮৫ চনত গঠন হৈছিল, আনহাতে অসম এছ'চিয়েচন ১৯০৩ চনত গঠন হৈছিল।

Q: What changes took place in the 1972 reorganisation?
A: Manipur and Tripura became full states, while Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh (NEFA) became Union Territories; both of these later became full states in 1987.
Q: Why and to where was Assam's capital shifted in 1972?
A: The capital was shifted from Shillong to Dispur in Guwahati because Shillong went to the new state of Meghalaya; Shillong remained the capital of Meghalaya.
Q: When did the Assam Agitation start, how long did it last and who led it?
A: It started in 1979 and continued for six years, till 1985; it was led jointly by the All Assam Students' Union (AASU) and the All Assam Gana Sangram Parishad (AAGSP), with Prafulla Kumar Mahanta as a prominent AASU leader.
Q: When was the Assam Accord signed and what was its cut-off date?
A: The Assam Accord was signed on 15 August 1985 between the Government of India (Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi) and AASU/AAGSP leaders, with a cut-off date of 25 March 1971; those who entered before 1966 were to be regularised.
Q: ১৯৬৩ চনৰ ১ ডিচেম্বৰত অসমৰ পৰা কোনখন ৰাজ্য আঁতৰোৱা হৈছিল?
A: ১৯৬৩ চনৰ ১ ডিচেম্বৰত নাগালেণ্ড অসমৰ পৰা আঁতৰাই ভাৰতৰ এক সুকীয়া ৰাজ্য হিচাপে গঠন কৰা হৈছিল।
Q: ১৯৭২ চনৰ ২১ জানুৱাৰীত অসমৰ পাহাৰীয়া জিলাসমূহৰ পৰা কোনখন পূৰ্ণ ৰাজ্য সৃষ্টি কৰা হৈছিল?
A: ১৯৭২ চনৰ ২১ জানুৱাৰীত অসমৰ পাহাৰীয়া জিলাসমূহৰ পৰা মেঘালয় পূৰ্ণ ৰাজ্য হিচাপে সৃষ্টি কৰা হৈছিল।
Q: ১৯৭২ চনৰ পুনৰ্গঠনত কি পৰিৱৰ্তন হৈছিল?
A: মণিপুৰ আৰু ত্ৰিপুৰা পূৰ্ণ ৰাজ্য হ'ল, আনহাতে মিজোৰাম আৰু অৰুণাচল প্ৰদেশ (নেফা) কেন্দ্ৰীয় শাসিত অঞ্চল হ'ল; এই দুয়োখন পিছলৈ ১৯৮৭ চনত পূৰ্ণ ৰাজ্য হয়।
Q: ১৯৭২ চনত অসমৰ ৰাজধানী কিয় আৰু ক'লৈ স্থানান্তৰ কৰা হৈছিল?
A: শ্বিলং নতুন ৰাজ্য মেঘালয়লৈ যোৱাৰ বাবে ৰাজধানী শ্বিলঙৰ পৰা গুৱাহাটীৰ দিছপুৰলৈ স্থানান্তৰ কৰা হৈছিল; শ্বিলং মেঘালয়ৰ ৰাজধানী হৈ থাকি গৈছিল।
Q: অসম আন্দোলন কেতিয়া আৰম্ভ হৈছিল, কিমান দিন চলিছিল আৰু কোনে নেতৃত্ব দিছিল?
A: ই ১৯৭৯ চনত আৰম্ভ হৈ ১৯৮৫ লৈকে ছয় বছৰ চলিছিল; অসম ছাত্ৰ সন্থা (আছু) আৰু অসম গণ সংগ্ৰাম পৰিষদ (আগসপ)য়ে যুটীয়াভাৱে নেতৃত্ব দিছিল, প্ৰফুল্ল কুমাৰ মহন্ত এগৰাকী বিশিষ্ট আছু নেতা আছিল।
Q: অসম চুক্তি কেতিয়া স্বাক্ষৰিত হৈছিল আৰু ইয়াৰ কটা-তাৰিখ কি আছিল?
A: অসম চুক্তি ১৯৮৫ চনৰ ১৫ আগষ্টত ভাৰত চৰকাৰ (প্ৰধানমন্ত্ৰী ৰাজীৱ গান্ধী) আৰু আছু/আগসপ নেতাসকলৰ মাজত স্বাক্ষৰিত হৈছিল, কটা-তাৰিখ ১৯৭১ চনৰ ২৫ মাৰ্চ; ১৯৬৬ চনৰ আগতে সোমোৱাসকলক নিয়মিতকৰণ কৰিবলগীয়া আছিল।

### 1857 Revolt in Assam (Maniram Dewan) — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-history/modern-assam-sec/revolt-1857-assam/

Q: Who was Maniram Dewan?
A: A rich Assamese noble and businessman.
Q: What was the real name of Maniram Dewan?
A: Maniram Dutta Barua.
Q: What was Maniram Dewan's official position?
A: He was the Dewan (manager) of the estates of the deposed Ahom queen's family.
Q: Whose estates did Maniram Dewan manage?
A: The estates of the deposed Ahom queen (the family of Purandar Singha).
Q: Which deposed Ahom king was Maniram Dewan a loyal supporter of?
A: Purandar Singha.
Q: What did Maniram Dewan want to restore?
A: The Ahom monarchy.
Q: In which economic activity was Maniram Dewan among the first in Assam?
A: Tea cultivation.
Q: On which crop did Maniram Dewan start cultivation on his own estates?
A: Tea.
Q: In which year were further tea garden leases denied to Maniram Dewan by the British?
A: 1853.
Q: What feeling did the denial of tea garden leases in 1853 create in Maniram Dewan?
A: Deep resentment against the British.
Q: During which revolt did Maniram Dewan conspire to raise an uprising in Assam?
A: The Revolt of 1857.
Q: With the help of which regiment did Maniram Dewan plan his conspiracy?
A: The 40th regiment of the local forces.
Q: Who was the Ahom prince involved in Maniram Dewan's conspiracy?
A: Kandarpeswar Singha.
Q: Who was to be the restored king under Maniram Dewan's plan?
A: Kandarpeswar Singha.
Q: How was Maniram Dewan's conspiracy discovered?
A: It was betrayed by an informer.
Q: After the conspiracy was revealed, what happened to Maniram Dewan?
A: He was arrested.
Q: On what date was Maniram Dewan hanged?
A: 26 February 1858.
Q: At which place was Maniram Dewan hanged?
A: Jorhat.
Q: Who was hanged along with Maniram Dewan?
A: His associate Piyoli Barua.
Q: What punishment was given to Kandarpeswar Singha?
A: He was implicated and imprisoned.
Q: Was there a large military uprising in Assam during the 1857 Revolt?
A: No.
Q: What was the most important event of 1857 in Assam?
A: The Maniram Dewan conspiracy.
Q: How is Maniram Dewan regarded in the freedom struggle of Assam?
A: As one of the first martyrs of the freedom struggle in Assam.
Q: In which year was Maniram Dewan hanged - 1857 or 1858?
A: 1858.
Q: Was Maniram Dewan hanged in the same year (1857) as the main revolt?
A: No, he was hanged in 1858.
Q: Who was hanged with Maniram Dewan - Piyoli Barua or Piyoli Phukan?
A: Piyoli Barua.
Q: Was Maniram Dewan's real reason for revolt the tea trade alone?
A: No, his main aim was to restore the Ahom monarchy.
Q: Who was the proposed king in the Maniram Dewan conspiracy?
A: Kandarpeswar Singha.
Q: To which queen's family did Maniram Dewan serve as Dewan?
A: The deposed Ahom queen, the wife of Purandar Singha.
Q: When did the British deny Maniram Dewan further tea garden leases?
A: In 1853.
Q: Did Maniram Dewan play any role in starting tea cultivation in Assam?
A: Yes, he was among the first to start tea cultivation on his own estates.
Q: Who betrayed the conspiracy of Maniram Dewan?
A: An informer.
Q: After his arrest, what was Maniram Dewan's fate?
A: He was hanged at Jorhat.
Q: Did Kandarpeswar Singha escape punishment?
A: No, he was implicated and imprisoned.
Q: What was the attitude of Assam toward the 1857 Revolt in terms of military action?
A: There was no large military uprising in Assam.
Q: Which regiment did Maniram Dewan plan to use - the 40th or the 14th?
A: The 40th regiment.
Q: When the Ahom monarchy was overthrown, whose side did Maniram Dewan take?
A: He supported the deposed Ahom king Purandar Singha.
Q: What was Maniram Dewan's profession apart from being a noble?
A: He was a businessman.
Q: Where was Maniram Dewan hanged - Jorhat or Guwahati?
A: Jorhat.
Q: Why is Maniram Dewan remembered as a martyr?
A: He sacrificed his life fighting for the restoration of the Ahom kingdom and against British rule.
Q: What was the outcome of the Maniram Dewan conspiracy?
A: The conspiracy failed; he and Piyoli Barua were hanged and Kandarpeswar Singha was imprisoned.
Q: Did the 40th regiment actually rise in revolt in Assam?
A: No, the planned uprising did not take place.
Q: Which year saw the denial of tea leases that angered Maniram Dewan - 1853 or 1857?
A: 1853.
Q: Who was the loyal supporter of Purandar Singha?
A: Maniram Dewan.
Q: What did Maniram Dewan plan to do with the help of the 40th regiment?
A: To raise an uprising in Assam and restore the Ahom kingdom.
Q: Why did Maniram Dewan feel resentment against the British?
A: Because he was denied further tea garden leases in 1853 and the Ahom monarchy had been overthrown.
Q: What title did Maniram Dewan hold as manager of the queen's estates?
A: Dewan.
Q: In Assam, was the 1857 Revolt mainly a military revolt like in northern India?
A: No.

A: 26 February 1858.
Q: Who was Piyoli Barua in relation to Maniram Dewan?
A: He was Maniram Dewan's associate and was hanged with him.
Q: Did the conspiracy of 1857 in Assam succeed in restoring the Ahom kingdom?
A: No.
Q: What plan did Maniram Dewan make during the 1857 Revolt?
A: To raise an uprising in Assam with the 40th regiment and place Kandarpeswar Singha on the throne.

A: The Maniram Dewan conspiracy.
Q: What was the final punishment of Maniram Dewan and Piyoli Barua?
A: Death by hanging.

Q: Who was Maniram Dewan and what was his real name?
A: Maniram Dewan was a rich Assamese noble and businessman whose real name was Maniram Dutta Barua; he served as the Dewan (manager) of the estates of the deposed Ahom queen, the family of Purandar Singha.
Q: Why did Maniram Dewan turn against the British?
A: He was among the first in Assam to cultivate tea, but in 1853 the British denied him further tea garden leases, which created deep resentment against them.
Q: What was the Maniram Dewan conspiracy of 1857?
A: During the Revolt of 1857, Maniram Dewan conspired with the help of the 40th regiment of the local forces to raise an uprising in Assam and restore the Ahom prince Kandarpeswar Singha as king.
Q: How was the conspiracy discovered and what was Maniram Dewan's punishment?
A: It was betrayed by an informer; Maniram Dewan was arrested and hanged on 26 February 1858 at Jorhat, along with his associate Piyoli Barua.
Q: Was there a large military uprising in Assam during the 1857 Revolt?
A: No. There was no large military uprising in Assam during 1857; the Maniram Dewan conspiracy was the most important event of 1857 in Assam.
Q: What happened to Kandarpeswar Singha?
A: The Ahom prince Kandarpeswar Singha was implicated in the conspiracy and imprisoned.
Q: মণিৰাম দেৱান কোন আছিল আৰু তেওঁৰ প্ৰকৃত নাম কি আছিল?
A: মণিৰাম দেৱান এগৰাকী ধনী অসমীয়া সম্ভ্ৰান্ত আৰু ব্যৱসায়ী আছিল, যাৰ প্ৰকৃত নাম মণিৰাম দত্ত বৰুৱা; তেওঁ পদচ্যুত আহোম ৰাণী, পুৰন্দৰ সিংহৰ পৰিয়ালৰ মাটি-সম্পত্তিৰ দেৱান (পৰিচালক) আছিল।
Q: মণিৰাম দেৱান ব্ৰিটিছৰ বিৰুদ্ধে কিয় হৈছিল?
A: তেওঁ অসমত চাহ খেতি কৰা প্ৰথমসকলৰ এজন আছিল, কিন্তু ১৮৫৩ চনত ব্ৰিটিছে তেওঁক অধিক চাহ বাগিচাৰ ঠিকা নাকচ কৰে, যাৰ ফলত ব্ৰিটিছৰ বিৰুদ্ধে গভীৰ ক্ষোভ জন্মে।
Q: ১৮৫৭ চনৰ মণিৰাম দেৱান ষড়যন্ত্ৰ কি আছিল?
A: ১৮৫৭ চনৰ বিদ্ৰোহৰ সময়ত মণিৰাম দেৱানে স্থানীয় বাহিনীৰ ৪০ নং ৰেজিমেণ্টৰ সহায়ত অসমত বিদ্ৰোহ উত্থাপন কৰি আহোম ৰাজকুমাৰ কন্দৰ্পেশ্বৰ সিংহক ৰজা হিচাপে পুনৰুদ্ধাৰ কৰাৰ ষড়যন্ত্ৰ কৰিছিল।
Q: ষড়যন্ত্ৰ কেনেকৈ ধৰা পৰিল আৰু মণিৰাম দেৱানৰ দণ্ড কি আছিল?
A: এগৰাকী গুপ্তচৰে বিশ্বাসঘাতকতা কৰিছিল; মণিৰাম দেৱানক গ্ৰেপ্তাৰ কৰি ১৮৫৮ চনৰ ২৬ ফেব্ৰুৱাৰীত যোৰহাটত, সহযোগী পিয়লি বৰুৱাৰ লগত ফাঁচী দিয়া হৈছিল।
Q: ১৮৫৭ চনৰ বিদ্ৰোহৰ সময়ত অসমত বৃহৎ সামৰিক বিদ্ৰোহ হৈছিলনে?
A: নহয়। ১৮৫৭ চনত অসমত কোনো বৃহৎ সামৰিক বিদ্ৰোহ হোৱা নাছিল; মণিৰাম দেৱান ষড়যন্ত্ৰ আছিল অসমত ১৮৫৭ চনৰ আটাইতকৈ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ ঘটনা।
Q: কন্দৰ্পেশ্বৰ সিংহৰ কি হৈছিল?
A: আহোম ৰাজকুমাৰ কন্দৰ্পেশ্বৰ সিংহক ষড়যন্ত্ৰত জড়িত বুলি গণ্য কৰি কাৰাবাস দিয়া হৈছিল।

### Orunodoi, Jonaki & Sahitya Sabha — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-history/modern-assam-sec/socio-cultural-awakening/
Summary: Practice orunodoi, jonaki & sahitya sabha questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Which was the first magazine/periodical published in the Assamese language?
A: Orunodoi (Arunodoi).
Q: In which year was the Orunodoi magazine started?
A: 1846.
Q: From which place was the Orunodoi magazine published?
A: Sibsagar (Sivasagar).
Q: Which group started the Orunodoi magazine?
A: The American Baptist Missionaries.
Q: Name one American Baptist missionary associated with the publication of Orunodoi.
A: Nathan Brown (or Oliver Cutter or Miles Bronson).
Q: Who was the notable editor of the Orunodoi magazine?
A: Nathan Brown.
Q: Was Orunodoi a monthly or a weekly publication?
A: Monthly.
Q: On which subjects did the Orunodoi magazine publish articles?
A: Religion, science, history, news and literature.
Q: What key role did Orunodoi play in the development of the Assamese language?
A: It played a key role in the development of modern Assamese prose and language.
Q: For how long was the Orunodoi magazine published?
A: For several decades, till about the 1880s.
Q: Trap: Was the Orunodoi magazine started in 1864?
A: No, it was started in 1846.
Q: Trap: Was the Orunodoi magazine published from Guwahati?
A: No, it was published from Sibsagar.
Q: Trap: Was the Orunodoi magazine started by Assamese students?
A: No, it was started by the American Baptist Missionaries.
Q: In which language was the Orunodoi magazine published?
A: Assamese.
Q: Orunodoi was the first magazine published in which language?
A: Assamese.
Q: Which town of Assam is associated with the origin of the Orunodoi magazine?
A: Sibsagar (Sivasagar).
Q: Name three American Baptist missionaries connected with the Orunodoi magazine.
A: Nathan Brown, Oliver Cutter and Miles Bronson.
Q: Trap: The Orunodoi was published as a weekly magazine. True or false?
A: False; it was a monthly magazine.
Q: What did Orunodoi contribute to modern Assamese literature?
A: It played a key role in the development of modern Assamese prose.
Q: Trap: The Orunodoi magazine was started in the twentieth century. True or false?
A: False; it was started in 1846 in the nineteenth century.
Q: In which year was the periodical Jonaki started?
A: 1889.
Q: Which society published the Jonaki periodical?
A: The Asamiya Bhasha Unnati Sadhini Sabha.
Q: In which year was the Asamiya Bhasha Unnati Sadhini Sabha founded?
A: 1888.
Q: In which city was the Asamiya Bhasha Unnati Sadhini Sabha founded?
A: Calcutta.
Q: Who founded the Asamiya Bhasha Unnati Sadhini Sabha?
A: Assamese students.
Q: Name two members of the Asamiya Bhasha Unnati Sadhini Sabha.
A: Chandrakumar Agarwala and Lakshminath Bezbaroa (also Hemchandra Goswami).
Q: Who was the first editor of the Jonaki periodical?
A: Chandrakumar Agarwala.
Q: Who was the greatest writer of the Jonaki era?
A: Lakshminath Bezbaroa.
Q: What is the era of modern Assamese literature marked by the Jonaki periodical called?
A: The Jonaki era (Jonaki Jug).
Q: Which literary movement was born out of the Jonaki era?
A: The romantic movement in Assamese literature.
Q: Was the Jonaki a monthly periodical?
A: Yes, it was a monthly periodical.
Q: Trap: The Jonaki periodical was started in 1846. True or false?
A: False; the Jonaki was started in 1889.
Q: Trap: The Jonaki periodical was published by the American Baptist Missionaries. True or false?
A: False; it was published by the Asamiya Bhasha Unnati Sadhini Sabha.
Q: Trap: Chandrakumar Agarwala was the greatest writer of the Jonaki era. True or false?
A: False; Lakshminath Bezbaroa was the greatest writer, while Chandrakumar Agarwala was the first editor of Jonaki.
Q: What does 'Asamiya Bhasha Unnati Sadhini Sabha' mean in English?
A: Assamese Language Development Society.
Q: Which of these founded the Asamiya Bhasha Unnati Sadhini Sabha: Chandrakumar Agarwala, Nathan Brown or Miles Bronson?
A: Chandrakumar Agarwala, along with other Assamese students.
Q: Which era in Assamese literature is known as the 'Jonaki Jug'?
A: The Jonaki era, which marked the beginning of modern Assamese literature.
Q: Trap: The Asamiya Bhasha Unnati Sadhini Sabha was founded in Guwahati. True or false?
A: False; it was founded in Calcutta in 1888.
Q: Who was Hemchandra Goswami in this context?
A: He was a member of the Asamiya Bhasha Unnati Sadhini Sabha.
Q: Trap: The Jonaki era is known for the realism movement in Assamese literature. True or false?
A: False; the Jonaki era gave birth to the romantic movement.
Q: In which year was the Asam Sahitya Sabha founded?
A: 1917.
Q: Where was the Asam Sahitya Sabha founded?
A: Sivasagar.
Q: Who was the founder and first president of the Asam Sahitya Sabha?
A: Padmanath Gohain Baruah.
Q: When and where was the first session of the Asam Sahitya Sabha held?
A: In December 1917 at Sivasagar.

### Buranjis (Historical Chronicles) — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-literature/ahom-period-lit-sec/buranjis-historical-chronicles/
Summary: Practice buranjis (historical chronicles) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What is a Buranji?
A: A Buranji is a historical chronicle of the Ahom period of Assam, recording events, reigns, and important matters in prose.
Q: What is the origin of the word 'Buranji'?
A: The word 'Buranji' is derived from the Tai-Ahom word, believed to mean 'a storehouse of knowledge' or 'to teach without books'.
Q: In which language were the earliest Buranjis written?
A: The earliest Buranjis were written in the Ahom (Tai) language, and later ones were written in Assamese.
Q: What is the historical importance of the Buranjis?
A: The Buranjis are the most important sources of Assam's history, preserving the political, social, and military records of the Ahom period.
Q: What is the 'Tripura Buranji'?
A: The 'Tripura Buranji' is a 17th-century chronicle written in Assamese describing relations between Assam and Tripura, composed for the Mughal envoy.
Q: Who wrote the 'Tripura Buranji'?
A: The 'Tripura Buranji' was written by an Assamese scholar named Durga Singha, at the behest of the Ahom king.
Q: What is the 'Asam Buranji'?
A: The 'Asam Buranji' is a chronicle of Assam; the notable 'Asam Buranji' was compiled by Harakanta Barua in the 19th century.
Q: Who compiled the famous 'Asam Buranji' of 1858?
A: Harakanta Barua compiled the famous 'Asam Buranji' in 1858.
Q: Who wrote the 'Purani Asam Buranji'?
A: The 'Purani Asam Buranji' was compiled by Kasinath Tamuli Phukan.
Q: What is the 'Kamrupar Buranji'?
A: The 'Kamrupar Buranji' is a chronicle focusing on the history of Kamrup region, part of the Buranji tradition.
Q: Which Ahom king encouraged the writing of Buranjis?
A: Ahom kings from Sukaphaa onwards, especially later kings, encouraged the writing of Buranjis as royal records.
Q: What was the 'Buranji' writing tradition called?
A: The tradition of writing Buranjis was an official court practice, maintained by special officials (Buranji-kakats) in the Ahom court.
Q: What is the 'Satsari Asam Buranji'?
A: The 'Satsari Asam Buranji' is a chronicle of Assam's history arranged in seven parts, a major Buranji text.
Q: Which Buranji describes the reign of Rudra Singha?
A: Chronicles like the 'Satsari Asam Buranji' and various court Buranjis describe the reign of Rudra Singha.
Q: Who translated the 'Tai-Ahom Buranji' tradition into Assamese?
A: Ahom priests and scholars, and later historians, translated the Tai-Ahom Buranjis into Assamese over the centuries.
Q: What is the 'Deodhai' connection to Buranjis?
A: The Deodhai were Ahom priest-chroniclers who preserved and recited the traditional Buranjis.
Q: Which Buranji records the Anglo-Burmese conflict?
A: Later Buranjis and Assamese chronicles of the 19th century record the Anglo-Burmese wars and the events leading to British rule.
Q: What is the 'Swargadeo' tradition in Buranjis?
A: 'Swargadeo' is the title of the Ahom king, and Buranjis record the genealogies and reigns of the Swargadeos.
Q: What is the importance of the 'Tripura Buranji' for the Assamese language?
A: The 'Tripura Buranji' is important as an early specimen of pure Assamese prose, showing the state of the language in the 17th century.
Q: Who was the founder of the Ahom kingdom in Assam?
A: Sukaphaa (Siu-Ka-Pha) was the founder of the Ahom kingdom in Assam, who crossed the Patkai range in 1228 AD.
Q: What is the 'Akal Buranji'?
A: The 'Akal Buranji' is an obscure later chronicle; the term 'akal' refers to untimely events recorded in some chronicles.
Q: Which Buranji is a source for the Moamoria rebellion?
A: Chronicles such as the 'Satsari Asam Buranji' and later Ahom Buranjis provide sources for the Moamoria rebellion.
Q: What is the significance of Buranjis in Assamese prose development?
A: Buranjis are among the earliest specimens of Assamese prose, playing a key role in the development of the written Assamese language.
Q: Who edited and published many Buranjis in the 20th century?
A: Surya Kumar Bhuyan edited and published many Buranjis, preserving them for historical study.
Q: What is the 'Assam Buranji' by Kasinath Tamuli Phukan about?
A: The 'Assam Buranji' (Purani Asam Buranji) by Kasinath Tamuli Phukan records the early history of Assam up to the Ahom period.
Q: What does the 'Tripura Buranji' describe?
A: The 'Tripura Buranji' describes the diplomatic relations between the Ahom kingdom and Tripura and the geography of the region.
Q: Which Buranji is considered an early source for the 'Assamese prose of Ahom era'?
A: The 'Tripura Buranji' is considered an early source of Assamese prose from the Ahom era.
Q: What is the 'Deodhai Asam Buranji'?
A: The 'Deodhai Asam Buranji' is a chronicle preserved by the Deodhai priests, recording Ahom history.
Q: Which Ahom king first established the practice of court Buranjis?
A: The practice of maintaining court Buranjis developed gradually from the reign of Sukaphaa, becoming formal under later kings.
Q: What is 'Buranji Patha' or 'Buranji-kakats'?
A: Buranji-kakats were officials in the Ahom court responsible for maintaining and reading the Buranjis.
Q: Which Buranji describes the battle of Saraighat?
A: The Ahom Buranjis, such as the 'Asam Buranji' traditions, describe the battle of Saraighat (1671) against the Mughals.
Q: What is the relationship between Buranjis and the Ahom administration?
A: Buranjis served as official administrative records, documenting land grants, laws, wars, and royal decrees.
Q: What is the 'Mong Buranji'?
A: The 'Mong Buranji' is a chronicle of the Mong (region/kingdom) in the Tai-Ahom tradition, a type of Buranji.
Q: Who is credited with bringing the Tai Buranji tradition to Assam?
A: Sukaphaa and the Tai-Ahom migrants are credited with bringing the Tai Buranji chronicle tradition to Assam.
Q: Why are Buranjis valuable for the study of the Assamese language?
A: Buranjis preserve the Assamese language as spoken and written in the Ahom period, offering valuable linguistic data.
Q: What is the 'Puranji' spelling variant?
A: 'Puranji' is an older spelling variant of 'Buranji' used in some early texts.
Q: Which is the earliest known Buranji text?
A: The exact earliest Buranji is debated, but the 'Tripura Buranji' (17th century) is among the oldest known Assamese Buranjis.
Q: What is the importance of the Buranji for the study of the Moamoria and the Ahom decline?
A: Later Buranjis record the Moamoria uprising and the decline of the Ahom kingdom, providing crucial historical evidence.
Q: Which of the following is a famous Buranji text?
A: The 'Tripura Buranji' and 'Asam Buranji' are famous Buranji texts of Assam.
Q: Who was the last major compiler of Buranjis?
A: Surya Kumar Bhuyan is regarded as a major modern compiler and editor of the Buranjis in the 20th century.
Q: What is the value of Buranjis as a literary form?
A: Buranjis are valued as the first major prose literature of Assam, blending history with narrative skill.
Q: What is a Buranji and why are the Buranjis important?
A: A Buranji is a historical chronicle of the Ahom period of Assam, recording events, reigns and important matters in prose. The Buranjis are the most important source of Assam's medieval history and are among the earliest specimens of Assamese prose.
Q: In which language were the earliest Buranjis written?
A: The earliest Buranjis were written in the Ahom (Tai) language, brought to Assam by Sukaphaa and the Tai-Ahom. In course of time they were rendered into Assamese, and many later chronicles were composed directly in Assamese.
Q: Who maintained the Buranjis in the Ahom court?
A: The Buranjis were maintained as an official court practice by officials called Buranji-kakats. Traditional lore was also preserved and recited by the Deodhai and Bailung priests.
Q: Which are some famous Buranjis and who edited them in modern times?
A: Famous Buranjis include the Tripura Buranji, the Asam Buranji compiled by Harakanta Barua in 1858, the Purani Asam Buranji of Kasinath Tamuli Phukan and the Satsari Asam Buranji. In the twentieth century Surya Kumar Bhuyan edited and published many of them.
Q: What is the place of the Buranjis in the development of Assamese prose?
A: The Buranjis are among the earliest specimens of Assamese prose. Their plain, factual narrative style helped establish written Assamese and left a lasting model for later historical and literary prose.

### Court & Scientific Literature — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-literature/ahom-period-lit-sec/court-scientific-literature/
Summary: Practice court & scientific literature questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What is the 'Hastividyarnava'?
A: The 'Hastividyarnava' is a 16th-century illustrated treatise on elephant care and management, one of the most important Ahom period works.
Q: Under which Ahom king was the 'Hastividyarnava' written?
A: The 'Hastividyarnava' was written under the patronage of Ahom king Rudra Singha.
Q: What type of literature is the 'Hastividyarnava'?
A: The 'Hastividyarnava' is scientific literature dealing with the biology, training, and management of elephants.
Q: Who composed the 'Hastividyarnava' in Assamese?
A: The 'Hastividyarnava' was rendered into Assamese by Sukumar Barkaith (Sukumar Barkath) under royal orders.
Q: What is 'Ghoranidan' or 'Ghoranidhan'?
A: 'Ghoranidhan' is a scientific text on the care and management of horses written in the Ahom period.
Q: What is 'Dhanvantari' literature?
A: 'Dhanvantari' texts in the Ahom period were works on Ayurveda and medicinal science, named after the divine physician Dhanvantari.
Q: What were the main subjects of scientific literature in the Ahom period?
A: The main subjects were astrology, astronomy, mathematics, Ayurveda, veterinary science (elephants, horses), and medicine.
Q: What is the 'Narada Silpa Sastra'?
A: The 'Narada Silpa Sastra' is an Ahom period text on architecture and sculpture (silpa), attributed to sage Narada.
Q: What is the 'Sankhya Khandana'?
A: The 'Sankhya Khandana' is a later philosophical text, not typically classified as Ahom period scientific literature.
Q: What type of text is 'Bhoutak Katha'?
A: 'Bhoutak Katha' is a text dealing with alchemy and chemistry-related knowledge in the Ahom tradition.
Q: What is the 'Prashna Ratna'?
A: The 'Prashna Ratna' is an astrological text of the Ahom period dealing with predictive queries.
Q: Which king patronized scholars who translated Sanskrit scientific texts?
A: Ahom kings such as Rudra Singha and Siva Singha patronized scholars who translated Sanskrit scientific and religious texts into Assamese.
Q: What is the 'Madan-Mohana' connection to scientific literature?
A: 'Madan Mohana' is a religious/devotional temple name, not a scientific text; it is not part of Ahom scientific literature.
Q: What is 'Dharma Sastra' literature of the Ahom period?
A: Dharma Sastra literature in the Ahom period included legal and ethical texts guiding administration and conduct.
Q: What is the 'Kama Sastra' of the Ahom period?
A: The 'Kama Sastra' was a translated text on the science of love and marriage, part of court literature.
Q: What is 'Kaliyadaman' in the context of court literature?
A: 'Kaliya Daman' is a devotional Ankiya Naat by Sankardev, not a court or scientific text of the Ahom period.
Q: What is 'Asva Sastra' or 'Aswa Chikitsa'?
A: 'Asva Sastra' texts deal with the treatment and management of horses, a veterinary science subject of the Ahom period.
Q: What is 'Gaja Sastra'?
A: 'Gaja Sastra' is the science of elephants, covered in texts like the 'Hastividyarnava'.
Q: Which Ahom king wrote 'Shiva Ratri' and 'Gobar Gita'?
A: Ahom king Siva Singha is credited with devotional works like the 'Gobar Gita' and 'Shiva Ratri'.
Q: What is the 'Siva Ratri' text?
A: The 'Siva Ratri' is a devotional text on the festival of Maha Shivratri, attributed to King Siva Singha.
Q: What was the role of court poets in the Ahom period?
A: Court poets composed panegyrics, genealogies of kings, and translations of Sanskrit works, and recorded royal activities.
Q: What is the 'Nabaratna'?
A: The 'Nabaratna' is a court text of the Ahom period, dealing with gems and precious stones (ratna-sastra).
Q: What is 'Gobar Gita'?
A: The 'Gobar Gita' is a Vaishnavite devotional text attributed to King Siva Singha, glorifying the name of God.
Q: Which science was prominently developed in the Ahom court?
A: Astrology and astronomy were prominently developed in the Ahom court, with many translated almanac and prediction texts.
Q: What is the 'Bhoota Sastra'?
A: The 'Bhoota Sastra' is a text on spirits and supernatural beings, reflecting the traditional belief system of the period.
Q: What is the significance of 'Hastividyarnava' for art?
A: The 'Hastividyarnava' is significant for its detailed illustrations of elephants, a masterpiece of Ahom-period art.
Q: What is 'Chikitsa Ratnamala'?
A: 'Chikitsa Ratnamala' is a medical text on treatment and remedies, part of the Ayurvedic scientific literature of the period.
Q: Who translated the 'Bhagavata' in the Ahom court?
A: Various scholars translated sections of the Bhagavata in the Ahom period, continuing the Vaishnavite tradition, including court renditions.
Q: What is the 'Mangal Kavya' tradition in the Ahom period?
A: Mangal Kavya are devotional narrative poems on deities, composed in the Ahom period, blending religion with court patronage.
Q: What is 'Ratna-sastra'?
A: Ratna-sastra is the science of gems, studied and translated in the Ahom court, dealing with identification and properties of precious stones.
Q: What is the 'Yoga Ratnakar'?
A: 'Yoga Ratnakar' is an Ayurvedic medical text (not the Yoga philosophy text) translated in the Ahom period on medicine.
Q: What is the importance of court literature in the Ahom period?
A: Court literature preserved royal history, promoted Sanskrit translation, and reflected the cultural and intellectual life of the Ahom court.
Q: What is 'Niti Sastra' in Ahom court literature?
A: Niti Sastra texts on ethics and governance were part of Ahom court literature, guiding statecraft.
Q: What is 'Vaidyaka' literature?
A: Vaidyaka literature is medical literature in Sanskrit and Assamese, dealing with diagnosis and treatment in the Ahom period.
Q: Who was the court poet of Rudra Singha?
A: Scholars like Sukumar Barkaith and others served as court poets and translators under Rudra Singha.
Q: What is the 'Jaiminiya Aswamedha'?
A: The 'Jaiminiya Aswamedha' is a Sanskrit epic poem on the Ashvamedha sacrifice by Jaimini, later translated/adapted in Assamese traditions.
Q: What is the significance of scientific literature for Assamese prose?
A: Scientific literature of the Ahom period contributed to the growth of technical Assamese prose in subjects like medicine, astrology, and veterinary science.
Q: Which text on elephants is a masterpiece of Ahom scientific literature?
A: The 'Hastividyarnava' is the masterpiece of Ahom scientific literature on elephants.
Q: What is the 'Amarakosa' connection in the Ahom period?
A: The 'Amarakosa', a Sanskrit lexicon, was used and studied in the Ahom period for learning Sanskrit vocabulary and composing court texts.
Q: What is 'Rasasastra'?
A: Rasasastra is the science of alchemy and mercurial medicines, a branch of scientific literature studied in the Ahom period.
Q: What is the Hastividyarnava and who is it associated with?
A: The Hastividyarnava is an illustrated treatise on the care, training and management of elephants. It is associated with the Ahom king Rudra Singha and was rendered into Assamese by Sukumar Barkaith. Its paintings make it a landmark of Ahom-period art.
Q: What is the Ghoranidan?
A: The Ghoranidan is an Ahom-period scientific text on the care and management of horses, part of the practical veterinary literature produced under royal patronage.
Q: What kind of scientific literature was produced in the Ahom period?
A: The Ahom period produced scientific and technical works on elephants (Hastividyarnava), horses (Ghoranidan), medicine and Ayurveda, and astrology and astronomy, most of them written or translated under royal patronage.
Q: How did royal patronage shape Ahom court literature?
A: Ahom kings such as Rudra Singha and Siva Singha patronised scholars who translated Sanskrit epics, Puranas and technical texts into Assamese and composed devotional and state works. King Siva Singha is credited with the Gobar Gita and the Shiva Ratri.
Q: What is the significance of Ahom-period scientific literature?
A: Ahom-period scientific literature helped develop technical Assamese prose in subjects such as medicine, astrology and veterinary science, and works like the Hastividyarnava also stand out for their art and illustration.

### Charyapada & Folk Songs Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-literature/ancient-pre-vaishnavite-sec/charyapada-folk-songs/
Summary: Practice charyapada & folk songs questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What is Charyapada?
A: Charyapada is a collection of mystical Buddhist songs composed between the 8th and 12th centuries, considered the earliest specimen of Assamese (and related eastern Indo-Aryan) literature.
Q: Who discovered the Charyapada manuscript?
A: Haraprasad Shastri discovered the Charyapada manuscript in 1907 from the royal library of Nepal.
Q: In which script was the Charyapada written?
A: The Charyapada was written in the Gaudi script, an old Bengali-Assamese script.
Q: Who were the composers of the Charyapada?
A: The Charyapada was composed by Buddhist Siddhacharyas such as Luipa, Sarahapa, Kambalabar, Sabaripa, and others.
Q: How many Charyapadas are extant?
A: A total of 47 Charyapadas are extant, but some scholars believe the original number was around 50.
Q: Who is considered the first Charyapada poet?
A: Luipa (Luipada) is considered the first Charyapada poet.
Q: What is the language of Charyapada?
A: The language of Charyapada is 'Sandhya Bhasya' or twilight language, an early form related to Old Assamese and Old Bengali.
Q: Which Buddhist sect's philosophy is reflected in the Charyapada?
A: The philosophy of Vajrayana Buddhism is reflected in the Charyapada songs.
Q: Who wrote the commentary 'Charyagitikosh-vritti' on Charyapada?
A: The commentary 'Charyagitikosh-vritti' was written by Munidatta.
Q: Which is the earliest manuscript of Charyapada?
A: The earliest manuscript of Charyapada is dated 1538 AD and was found in Nepal.
Q: What did Banikanta Kakati say about Charyapada?
A: Banikanta Kakati in his 'Bara Mahanata' and related works argued that the Charyapada language is old Assamese.
Q: What is a 'Bihu geet'?
A: A Bihu geet is an Assamese folk song associated with the Bihu festival, reflecting rural life, love, and nature.
Q: What is a 'Lali geet' or 'Nisaoni lali'?
A: A Lali geet is a lullaby sung by mothers to put babies to sleep in Assamese folk tradition.
Q: What is 'Ainam'?
A: Ainam is a lamentation or mourning song sung at funerals and death rituals in Assamese folk tradition.
Q: What is a 'Tokari geet'?
A: A Tokari geet is a folk song sung to the accompaniment of the Tokari, a stringed instrument, often devotional in nature.
Q: What is 'Deh Bichar' or 'Deh-Bixar Geet'?
A: Deh Bichar geet are philosophical folk songs dealing with the body and soul, popular among the saints.
Q: What is a 'Baramahi geet'?
A: A Baramahi geet is a folk song that describes the feelings of a woman separated from her husband through the twelve months of the year.
Q: What is a 'Biya geet' or 'Biyanam'?
A: Biya geet or Biyanam are wedding songs sung during Assamese marriage ceremonies.
Q: What is 'Jikir'?
A: Jikir is a devotional folk song of the Assamese Muslim community, generally attributed to Azan Fakir (Shah Miran).
Q: Who composed the famous 'Jikir' songs?
A: Azan Fakir (Shah Miran), a 17th-century Sufi saint of Assam, composed the famous Jikir and Zari songs.
Q: What is 'Zari'?
A: Zari is a type of devotional folk song of the Assamese Muslims, usually sung in chorus, dealing with the tragedy of Karbala.
Q: What is 'Kushan geet'?
A: Kushan geet is a category of Assamese folk songs sung by women while performing household tasks like grinding paddy.
Q: What is 'Dhaina geet'?
A: Dhaina geet are folk songs sung during agricultural work, especially in paddy fields.
Q: What is 'Nao geet' or 'Bhatial'?
A: Nao geet are boatmen's songs, while Bhatial is a type of folk song sung by boatmen in the rivers of Assam.
Q: Who is associated with the 'Bhatima' tradition?
A: Bhatima is associated with Madhavdev, who composed devotional songs in this genre praising saints and God.
Q: What is 'Ojapali'?
A: Ojapali is a traditional performing art of Assam that combines narrative songs, dance, and dramatic presentation, sung in folk style.
Q: What is 'Khol' or 'Mridanga' in folk music?
A: Khol (Mridanga) is a traditional clay drum used as the main percussion instrument in Assamese devotional and folk music.
Q: What is 'Gopinath Bordoloi' connection to folk song collection?
A: Gopinath Bordoloi's association is not with folk songs; he was a political leader. Folk song collections were made by scholars like Laxminath Bezbaroa, Birinchi Kumar Barua, and Prafulladatta Goswami.
Q: Who is known as the collector of 'Buranjis' as folk literature?
A: Buranjis are historical chronicles, not folk literature. Surya Kumar Bhuyan is the main scholar who edited and published many Buranjis.
Q: What is 'Nisukoni geet' or 'Ajai geet'?
A: Nisukoni (Ajai) geet are lullabies or songs sung while spinning cotton (Ajai), soothing babies to sleep.
Q: What is 'Phukoni geet'?
A: Phukoni geet are songs sung by women while blowing the fire (phukoni) in the kitchen or hearth in Assamese folk life.
Q: What is 'Gorokhiya geet'?
A: Gorokhiya geet are folk songs sung by cowherds while grazing cattle.
Q: What is 'Huchori'?
A: Huchori is a folk song-and-dance performance by young people during Bihu, especially in the Rongali season, going door to door.
Q: What is 'Kamar geet'?
A: Kamar geet are folk songs sung by blacksmiths (kamar) while working in their furnaces.
Q: Who wrote the book 'Folk-Literature of Assam'?
A: Birinchi Kumar Barua wrote 'Folk-Literature of Assam'.
Q: Which of these is the 'Saptakanda Ramayana' of Madhava Kandali?
A: The Saptakanda Ramayana is not folk literature; it is the Assamese translation of the Ramayana by Madhava Kandali in the 14th century.
Q: What is the folk song 'Bihoo geet' related to?
A: Bihu geet is related to the Bihu festival and agricultural life of Assam.
Q: What is Charyapada?
A: Charyapada is the oldest surviving collection of mystical songs in the Eastern Indo-Aryan languages. It was composed by Buddhist Siddhacharyas between the 8th and 12th centuries CE and is regarded as the earliest specimen of Assamese and related eastern Indo-Aryan literature.
Q: Who discovered the Charyapada manuscript and when?
A: The manuscript was discovered by Haraprasad Shastri in 1907 in the royal library of Nepal. He published the collection in 1916. The only surviving manuscript is dated 1538 CE.
Q: In which language and script was the Charyapada written?
A: Charyapada was written in Sandhya Bhasha, the twilight language, and in the Gaudi script, an old Bengali-Assamese script. A Sanskrit commentary on it, the Charyagitikosh-vritti, was written by Munidatta.
Q: How many Charyapada songs are extant and who were the poets?
A: A total of 47 songs are extant, though some scholars believe the original number was about 50. The chief poets include Luipa, Sarahapa, Kambalapada, Sabaripa, Kanhapa and Bhusukupada, with Luipa traditionally regarded as the first poet.
Q: Why is Charyapada important for Assam competitive exams?
A: It is the starting point of Assamese literary history and a regular part of the Assam Literature section in ADRE, APSC, Assam Police and other recruitment examinations. The questions are factual and repeat often, so the topic is easy to score.
Q: চৰ্যাপদ কি?
A: চৰ্যাপদ হৈছে পূৱ ভাৰতীয় আৰ্য ভাষাৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি সংৰক্ষিত ৰহস্যমূলক গীতৰ সংকলন। ই বৌদ্ধ সিদ্ধাচাৰ্যসকলে খ্ৰীষ্টীয় অষ্টমৰ পৰা দ্বাদশ শতিকাৰ ভিতৰত ৰচনা কৰিছিল আৰু অসমীয়া তথা সংশ্লিষ্ট পূৱ ভাৰতীয় আৰ্য সাহিত্যৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি নিদৰ্শন বুলি গণ্য কৰা হয়।
Q: চৰ্যাপদ পুথিখন কোনে কেতিয়া আৱিষ্কাৰ কৰিছিল?
A: পুথিখন হৰপ্ৰসাদ শাস্ত্ৰীয়ে ১৯০৭ চনত নেপালৰ ৰাজকীয় পুথিভঁৰালত আৱিষ্কাৰ কৰিছিল। তেওঁ ১৯১৬ চনত সংকলনটো প্ৰকাশ কৰিছিল। একমাত্ৰ জীৱিত পুথিখনৰ তাৰিখ খ্ৰীষ্টীয় ১৫৩৮ চন।
Q: চৰ্যাপদ কোন ভাষা আৰু আখৰত লিখা হৈছিল?
A: চৰ্যাপদ সন্ধ্যা ভাষা (গোধূলি ভাষা) আৰু গৌড়ী আখৰত লিখা হৈছিল, যিটো পুৰণি বঙলা-অসমীয়া আখৰ। ইয়াৰ ওপৰত মুনিদত্তই লিখা সংস্কৃত টীকা হৈছে চৰ্যাগীতিকোষ-বৃত্তি।
Q: চৰ্যাপদত কিমানখন গীত আছে আৰু কবিসকল কোন আছিল?
A: মুঠ ৪৭ খন গীত বৰ্তমান আছে, যদিও কিছুমান পণ্ডিতৰ মতে মূল সংখ্যা আছিল প্ৰায় ৫০। প্ৰধান কবিসকলৰ ভিতৰত লুইপা, সৰহাপা, কম্বলপাদ, শৱৰীপা, কান্ধাপা আৰু ভুসুকুপাদ আদি; লুইপাক পৰম্পৰাগতভাৱে প্ৰথম কবি বুলি গণ্য কৰা হয়।
Q: অসমৰ প্ৰতিযোগিতামূলক পৰীক্ষাত চৰ্যাপদ কিয় গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: ই অসমীয়া সাহিত্য ইতিহাসৰ আৰম্ভণি আৰু ADRE, APSC, অসম আৰক্ষী আদি পৰীক্ষাৰ অসম সাহিত্য অংশত নিয়মীয়াকৈ আহে। প্ৰশ্নবোৰ তথ্যভিত্তিক আৰু বাৰে বাৰে পুনৰাবৃত্ত হয়, গতিকে এই বিষয়টো সহজে নম্বৰ পোৱা বিষয়।

### Early Poets & Translations — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-literature/ancient-pre-vaishnavite-sec/early-poets-translations/
Summary: Practice early poets & translations questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Who is considered the first poet of Assamese literature?
A: Hema Saraswati is considered the first poet of Assamese literature, who wrote 'Prahallada Charitra'.
Q: Which is considered the first literary work of Assamese literature?
A: 'Prahallada Charitra' by Hema Saraswati is considered the first literary work of Assamese literature.
Q: Who wrote 'Prahallada Charitra'?
A: Hema Saraswati wrote 'Prahallada Charitra'.
Q: Under whose patronage did Hema Saraswati write?
A: Hema Saraswati wrote under the patronage of King Durlabhanarayana of the Kamata Kingdom.
Q: Who wrote 'Haragauri Vivaha'?
A: Hema Saraswati wrote 'Haragauri Vivaha' (Har-Gauri Vivah), a poem on the marriage of Shiva and Parvati.
Q: Who is the earliest Assamese poet of the Pre-Vaishnavite period after Hema Saraswati?
A: Harihara Vipra is considered an early major poet of the Pre-Vaishnavite period.
Q: What are the famous works of Harihara Vipra?
A: The famous works of Harihara Vipra are 'Babrubahana-Yuddha', 'Lava-Kushar-Yuddha', and 'Jamini-Kunya-Harana'.

A: Harihara Vipra wrote 'Babrubahana-Yuddha'.

A: Madhava Kandali wrote the 'Saptakanda Ramayana', the Assamese translation of the Ramayana.

A: Madhava Kandali wrote in the 14th century (around 1370-1380 AD).
Q: Which is the earliest Assamese translation of the Ramayana?
A: The 'Saptakanda Ramayana' by Madhava Kandali is the earliest Assamese translation of the Ramayana.

A: Ramananda translated the 'Aswamedha Parva' (Ashwamedh) and 'Udyoga Parva' of the Mahabharata into Assamese.
Q: Who translated the Bhagavata Purana into Assamese?
A: The Bhagavata Purana was translated by Ananta Kandali and later popularized by Sankardev and his followers.
Q: Who wrote 'Kumar Harana' and 'Harihar Yuddha'?
A: Ananta Kandali wrote 'Kumar Harana', 'Harihar Yuddha', and translated the 'Katha Bhagavata'.
Q: Who wrote the 'Katha Guru Charita'?
A: The 'Katha Guru Charita' is traditionally attributed to Rama Saraswati (Bhattadeva) or Daitari Thakur, being an early prose work.
Q: What is the 'Katha Bhagavata'?
A: The 'Katha Bhagavata' is the prose translation of the Bhagavata Purana, a landmark in early Assamese prose.
Q: Who wrote 'Katha Bhagavata'?
A: 'Katha Bhagavata' was written by Bhattadeva (Rama Kavi), considered the father of Assamese prose.
Q: Who is called the father of Assamese prose?
A: Bhattadeva (Rama Kavi Saraswati) is called the father of Assamese prose.
Q: What are the two famous prose works of Bhattadeva?
A: The two famous prose works of Bhattadeva are 'Katha Bhagavata' and 'Katha Gita'.
Q: Who wrote the 'Katha Gita'?
A: Bhattadeva (Rama Kavi) wrote the 'Katha Gita', a prose rendering of the Bhagavad Gita.
Q: Who wrote 'Geeti Ramayana'?
A: 'Geeti Ramayana' was composed by Raghunath Mahanta, though its historical dating is debated among scholars.
Q: Who wrote 'Kumar Harana'?
A: 'Kumar Harana' was written by Ananta Kandali.
Q: What is the significance of the 'Saptakanda Ramayana'?
A: The Saptakanda Ramayana is significant as the earliest and most complete translation of the Ramayana in an eastern Indo-Aryan language, later popularized by Sankardev.
Q: Who wrote the 'Kaliya Daman'?
A: 'Kaliya Daman' is an Ankiya Naat written by Sankardev, not a Pre-Vaishnavite work.
Q: Who wrote 'Drona Parva'?
A: 'Drona Parva' was written by Rudra Kandali.
Q: Who wrote 'Satyaki-Pradhana'?
A: 'Satyaki-Pradhana' was written by Rudra Kandali.
Q: Who translated the Bhagavad Gita into Assamese prose?
A: Bhattadeva translated the Bhagavad Gita into Assamese prose as 'Katha Gita'.
Q: Who is the author of 'Anadi Patana'?
A: 'Anadi Patana', a poem on creation, was written by Madhavdev, not by Pre-Vaishnavite poets.
Q: Which Pre-Vaishnavite poet wrote under King Nilambar?
A: Vidyapati and some court poets are associated with King Nilambar; among Assamese writers, Kaviratna Saraswati wrote under King Nilambar's patronage.
Q: What is the 'Lava Kushar Yuddha'?
A: 'Lava Kushar Yuddha' is a poem by Harihara Vipra describing the battle between Lava and Kusha.
Q: Who is known as the pioneer of Assamese translation literature?
A: Madhava Kandali is regarded as the pioneer of Assamese translation literature for his Saptakanda Ramayana.
Q: What are the main works of Hema Saraswati?
A: The main works of Hema Saraswati are 'Prahallada Charitra' and 'Haragauri Vivaha'.
Q: What is 'Nimi Nava Siddha'?
A: 'Nimi Nava Siddha' is a section of Sankardev's Kirtan Ghosha, not a Pre-Vaishnavite work.
Q: Who was the first poet of Assamese literature and what did he write?
A: Hema Saraswati is considered the first poet of Assamese literature. He wrote Prahallada Charitra, regarded as the first literary work of Assamese literature, and Haragauri Vivaha, under the patronage of King Durlabhanarayana of the Kamata kingdom.
Q: Who wrote the Saptakanda Ramayana and under whose patronage?
A: Madhava Kandali wrote the Saptakanda Ramayana in the 14th century, around 1370-1380 CE, under the patronage of King Mahamanikya of the Barahi kingdom. It is the earliest Assamese translation of the Ramayana and the reason he is called the pioneer of Assamese translation literature.
Q: Which Mahabharata parvas were translated during the Pre-Vaishnavite period?
A: Rudra Kandali translated the Drona Parva of the Mahabharata into Assamese, while Ramananda translated the Aswamedha Parva and the Udyoga Parva. These are the main Mahabharata translations associated with the early poets.
Q: Who is called the father of Assamese prose and which works earned him that title?
A: Bhattadeva, also known as Rama Kavi Saraswati, is called the father of Assamese prose. His two famous prose works are the Katha Bhagavata, a prose rendering of the Bhagavata Purana, and the Katha Gita, a prose rendering of the Bhagavad Gita.
Q: Which famous works are often wrongly attributed to the early Pre-Vaishnavite poets?
A: Kaliya Daman is an Ankiya Naat by Sankardev, Anadi Patana was written by Madhavdev, and Nimi Nava Siddha is a section of Sankardev's Kirtan Ghosha. All three belong to the later Vaishnavite age, not to the Pre-Vaishnavite period.
Q: অসমীয়া সাহিত্যৰ প্ৰথম কবি কোন আৰু তেওঁ কি লিখিছিল?
A: হেমা সৰস্বতীক অসমীয়া সাহিত্যৰ প্ৰথম কবি বুলি গণ্য কৰা হয়। তেওঁ প্ৰহ্লাদ চৰিত্ৰ, যিখন অসমীয়া সাহিত্যৰ প্ৰথম সাহিত্যকৃতি, আৰু হৰগৌৰী বিবাহ ৰচনা কৰিছিল, কমতা ৰাজ্যৰ ৰজা দুৰ্লভনাৰায়ণৰ পৃষ্ঠপোষকতাত।
Q: সপ্তকাণ্ড ৰামায়ণ কোনে আৰু কাৰ পৃষ্ঠপোষকতাত লিখিছিল?
A: মাধৱ কন্দলীয়ে চতুৰ্দশ শতিকাত, প্ৰায় ১৩৭০-১৩৮০ খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দত, বৰাহী ৰাজ্যৰ ৰজা মহামাণিক্যৰ পৃষ্ঠপোষকতাত সপ্তকাণ্ড ৰামায়ণ ৰচনা কৰিছিল। ই ৰামায়ণৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি অসমীয়া অনুবাদ আৰু এই কৰ্মৰ বাবেই তেওঁক অনুবাদ সাহিত্যৰ পথিকৃৎ বোলা হয়।
Q: পূৰ্ব-বৈষ্ণৱ যুগত মহাভাৰতৰ কোনবোৰ পৰ্ব অনুবাদ কৰা হৈছিল?
A: ৰুদ্ৰ কন্দলীয়ে মহাভাৰতৰ দ্ৰোণ পৰ্ব অসমীয়ালৈ অনুবাদ কৰিছিল, আনহাতে ৰামানন্দই অশ্বমেধ পৰ্ব আৰু উদ্যোগ পৰ্ব অনুবাদ কৰিছিল। এওঁলোকৰ অনুবাদেই আদি কবিসকলৰ সৈতে জড়িত প্ৰধান মহাভাৰত অনুবাদ।
Q: অসমীয়া গদ্যৰ জনক কোন আৰু তেওঁক সেই উপাধি কি ৰচনাই দিছে?
A: ভট্টদেৱ, ৰাম কবি সৰস্বতী বুলিও জনা যায়, তেওঁক অসমীয়া গদ্যৰ জনক বোলা হয়। তেওঁৰ দুখন বিখ্যাত গদ্য ৰচনা হৈছে ভাগৱত পুৰাণৰ গদ্য ৰূপ কথা ভাগৱত আৰু ভগৱদ গীতাৰ গদ্য ৰূপ কথা গীতা।
Q: প্ৰাৰম্ভিক পূৰ্ব-বৈষ্ণৱ কবিসকললৈ কোনবোৰ বিখ্যাত ৰচনা ভুলকৈ আৰোপ কৰা হয়?
A: কালিয়া দমন শংকৰদেৱৰ আঙ্কীয়া নাট, আনাদি পটন মাধৱদেৱৰ ৰচনা, আৰু নিমি নৱ সিদ্ধ শংকৰদেৱৰ কিৰ্তন ঘোষাৰ এটা অংশ। এই তিনিওটা পিছৰ বৈষ্ণৱ যুগৰ, পূৰ্ব-বৈষ্ণৱ যুগৰ নহয়।

### Arunodoi Era & Missionaries — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-literature/modern-era-arunodoi-jonaki-sec/arunodoi-era-missionaries/
Summary: Practice arunodoi era & missionaries questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: When was the first issue of 'Arunodoi' published?
A: The first issue of 'Arunodoi' was published in January 1846.
Q: What is 'Arunodoi'?
A: 'Arunodoi' was the first Assamese newspaper/periodical, published monthly by the American Baptist Missionaries.
Q: Who was the first editor of 'Arunodoi'?
A: Nathan Brown is generally considered the first editor of 'Arunodoi'.
Q: Where was 'Arunodoi' published from?
A: 'Arunodoi' was published from Sibsagar (Sivasagar) mission press.
Q: Which organization published 'Arunodoi'?
A: The American Baptist Mission (ABM) published 'Arunodoi'.
Q: Who was Nathan Brown?
A: Nathan Brown was an American Baptist missionary who played a key role in the development of modern Assamese prose and published 'Arunodoi'.
Q: What dictionary did Nathan Brown compile?
A: Nathan Brown compiled the 'Assamese-English Dictionary' published in 1848.
Q: Who compiled the famous dictionary 'A Dictionary in Assamese and English'?
A: Miles Bronson compiled 'A Dictionary in Assamese and English' published in 1867.
Q: What is the contribution of the missionaries to Assamese language?
A: The missionaries established the first printing press in Assam, published newspapers, compiled dictionaries, translated the Bible, and developed Assamese prose and grammar.
Q: What is the importance of 'Arunodoi' in Assamese literature?
A: 'Arunodoi' is important as the first Assamese periodical that introduced modern journalism, essays, and prose writing to Assamese readers.
Q: Who started the first printing press in Assam?
A: The American Baptist Missionaries started the first printing press in Assam at Sibsagar.
Q: What was the first book printed in Assamese?
A: The New Testament (Bible) was among the first books printed in Assamese by the missionaries.
Q: Who translated the Bible into Assamese?
A: The American Baptist Missionaries, including Nathan Brown and Miles Bronson, translated the Bible into Assamese.
Q: What is 'Grammar of the Assamese Language'?
A: The 'Grammar of the Assamese Language' is a grammar book compiled by Nathan Brown in 1848.
Q: What was the role of Miles Bronson in Assamese literature?
A: Miles Bronson compiled the Assamese-English dictionary, translated religious texts, and contributed to Assamese prose.
Q: Who was the Assamese scholar who assisted the missionaries in Bible translation?
A: Jaduram Deka Baruah assisted the missionaries in translating the Bible into Assamese.
Q: What is the significance of the Sibsagar mission press?
A: The Sibsagar mission press was the first printing press in Assam, which printed 'Arunodoi' and many early Assamese books.
Q: What is 'Arunodoi' in Assamese means?
A: 'Arunodoi' means the rising sun or dawn.
Q: Who wrote the essay 'Bhakti Rasaraja'?
A: 'Bhakti Rasaraja' is a Vaishnavite text; it is not related to the Arunodoi era directly.
Q: Which Assamese writer wrote in 'Arunodoi'?
A: Assamese scholars like Anandaram Dhekiyal Phukan, Hemchandra Barua, and others contributed essays to 'Arunodoi'.
Q: Who wrote 'A Few Remarks on the Assamese Language'?
A: Anandaram Dhekiyal Phukan wrote 'A Few Remarks on the Assamese Language' in 1855.
Q: What is the contribution of Anandaram Dhekiyal Phukan?
A: Anandaram Dhekiyal Phukan wrote essays, promoted the Assamese language, and was associated with 'Arunodoi' and 'Asam Bilashini'.
Q: What is the 'Asam Bilashini'?
A: 'Asam Bilashini' was an Assamese periodical published in the 19th century by Jagneswar Sarma, promoting the language.
Q: What is the 'Orunodoi' spelling variation?
A: The periodical was spelled 'Orunodoi' in English by the missionaries, the same as 'Arunodoi'.
Q: What is the importance of missionary printing in Assamese education?
A: Missionary printing produced school textbooks, religious books, and periodicals that advanced Assamese education.
Q: Who wrote 'Assamese Grammar' in the missionary period?
A: Nathan Brown wrote the first scientific 'Assamese Grammar' (Grammar of the Assamese Language) in 1848.
Q: What is 'Asam Rachana'?
A: 'Asam Rachana' was a periodical; the term 'Asam' spelling was used by missionaries and early writers.
Q: Which newspaper followed 'Arunodoi' in the 19th century?
A: Periodicals like 'Asam Bilashini', 'Assam News', and others followed 'Arunodoi' in the 19th century.
Q: What was the main objective of 'Arunodoi'?
A: The main objective of 'Arunodoi' was religious and general information dissemination, education, and the spread of the Assamese language.
Q: What is 'Ratan' (Ratna) in the context of early Assamese magazines?
A: There is no major 'Ratan' magazine; early Assamese magazines were 'Arunodoi', 'Asam Bilashini', and later 'Jonaki'.
Q: What is the 'Asomiya Bhashar Utsah'?
A: The 'Asomiya Bhashar Utsah' (A Few Remarks) is a work by Anandaram Dhekiyal Phukan advocating the Assamese language.
Q: Who introduced the Bengali-language controversy that missionaries opposed?
A: In the 1870s, some officials tried to replace Assamese with Bengali in schools; missionaries and Assamese scholars opposed it, and Assamese was restored in 1873.
Q: What is the role of Hemchandra Barua in the Arunodoi period?
A: Hemchandra Barua contributed essays and poems to 'Arunodoi' and later compiled the 'Hemkosh' dictionary.
Q: What is 'Hemkosh'?
A: 'Hemkosh' is the first etymological dictionary of the Assamese language, compiled by Hemchandra Barua and published in 1900.
Q: Who is known as the first Assamese essayist?
A: Anandaram Dhekiyal Phukan is considered one of the earliest modern Assamese essayists, writing in the Arunodoi period.
Q: What is the 'Amar Jivan'?
A: 'Amar Jivan' is not a periodical of the Arunodoi era; it relates to later works on biography.
Q: What was the contribution of the missionaries to Assamese journalism?
A: The missionaries founded the first Assamese periodical 'Arunodoi', laying the foundation of Assamese journalism.
Q: Who wrote 'Bakti Bakti'?
A: There is no known work titled 'Bakti Bakti' in Assamese literature; the term may be a confusion with devotional (bhakti) texts.
Q: What is the importance of the missionary dictionaries?
A: The missionary dictionaries by Nathan Brown and Miles Bronson standardized Assamese vocabulary and aided language study.
Q: What is 'Bani' (magazine) in Assamese journalism?
A: 'Bani' was a later Assamese magazine; it is not part of the Arunodoi era.
Q: Who is the missionary associated with the first translation of the Bible into Assamese?
A: Nathan Brown is chiefly associated with the first translation of the Bible into Assamese.
Q: What is 'Sibsagar' importance in the Arunodoi era?
A: Sibsagar was the headquarters of the Baptist mission in Assam, where 'Arunodoi' was published and the first printing press operated.
Q: What is 'Gunabhiram Barua' connection to the Arunodoi period?
A: Gunabhiram Barua wrote essays and the first Assamese drama 'Ram-Navami', connected with the early modern period after Arunodoi.
Q: What is Arunodoi and when did it begin?
A: Arunodoi was the first Assamese periodical. Its first issue appeared in January 1846 from Sibsagar, published by the American Baptist Mission.
Q: Who were the missionaries behind the Arunodoi era?
A: The American Baptist Missionaries. Nathan Brown is regarded as the first editor of Arunodoi, and Miles Bronson compiled a famous Assamese-English dictionary.
Q: Why is the year 1873 important?
A: In 1873 Assamese was restored in the schools of Assam after an attempt in the 1870s to replace it with Bengali.
Q: How did the missionaries help the Assamese language?
A: They set up the first printing press in Assam, published the periodical Arunodoi, compiled dictionaries and a grammar, translated the Bible, and developed printed Assamese prose.
Q: Which dictionaries came before Hemkosh?
A: The missionary dictionaries came first: Nathan Brown's Assamese-English Dictionary (1848) and Miles Bronson's A Dictionary in Assamese and English (1867), before Hemchandra Barua's Hemkosh (1900).
Q: অৰুণোদই কি আৰু ই কেতিয়া আৰম্ভ হৈছিল?
A: 'অৰুণোদই' প্ৰথম অসমীয়া আলোচনী। ইয়াৰ প্ৰথম সংখ্যা ১৮৪৬ চনৰ জানুৱাৰী মাহত শিৱসাগৰৰ পৰা প্ৰকাশ হৈছিল, আমেৰিকান বেপ্টিষ্ট মিছনৰ দ্বাৰা।
Q: অৰুণোদই যুগৰ লগত জড়িত মিছনাৰীসকল কোন আছিল?
A: আমেৰিকান বেপ্টিষ্ট মিছনাৰীসকল। নাথান ব্ৰাউনক 'অৰুণোদই'ৰ প্ৰথম সম্পাদক বুলি গণ্য কৰা হয়, আৰু মাইলছ ব্ৰনছনে এখন বিখ্যাত অসমীয়া-ইংৰাজী অভিধান সংকলন কৰিছিল।
Q: ১৮৭৩ চন কিয় গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: ১৮৭০ৰ দশকত অসমীয়াৰ সলনি বঙলা প্ৰৱৰ্তনৰ প্ৰচেষ্টাৰ পিছত ১৮৭৩ চনত অসমৰ বিদ্যালয়ত অসমীয়া পুনৰ প্ৰৱৰ্তন হৈছিল।
Q: মিছনাৰীসকলে অসমীয়া ভাষাক কেনেকৈ সহায় কৰিছিল?
A: তেওঁলোকে অসমত প্ৰথম ছপাশাল স্থাপন কৰিছিল, 'অৰুণোদই' প্ৰকাশ কৰিছিল, অভিধান আৰু ব্যাকৰণ সংকলন কৰিছিল, বাইবেল অনুবাদ কৰিছিল আৰু ছপা অসমীয়া গদ্য বিকশিত কৰিছিল।
Q: হেমকোষৰ আগতে কোনবোৰ অভিধান আছিল?
A: মিছনাৰী অভিধানবোৰ আগেয়ে আছিল: নাথান ব্ৰাউনৰ Assamese-English Dictionary (১৮৪৮) আৰু মাইলছ ব্ৰনছনৰ A Dictionary in Assamese and English (১৮৬৭); তাৰ পিছতহে হেমচন্দ্ৰ বৰুৱাৰ হেমকোষ (১৯০০)।

### Early Modern Novels, Poems & Drama — ADRE, APSC

Q: Which is considered the first Assamese novel?

Q: Who wrote 'Bhanumati'?

Q: Who is known as the 'Scott of Assam'?

Q: What is 'Miri-Jiyori'?
A: 'Miri-Jiyori' is the first novel by Rajanikanta Bordoloi, published in 1894, depicting the life of the Miri (Mising) community.
Q: Who wrote 'Miri-Jiyori'?
A: 'Miri-Jiyori' was written by Rajanikanta Bordoloi.
Q: What is 'Manomati'?

### Jonaki Era (Romantic Movement) — ADRE, APSC

Q: When was the 'Jonaki' magazine first published?
A: The 'Jonaki' magazine was first published in 1889.
Q: What is the 'Jonaki' magazine?
A: 'Jonaki' (the glow-worm/moonlight) was a literary magazine of the Assamese romantic period, started in 1889, that shaped modern Assamese literature.
Q: Where was 'Jonaki' published from?
A: 'Jonaki' was first published from Calcutta (Kolkata) by Assamese students.
Q: Who was the first editor of 'Jonaki'?
A: Chandrakumar Agarwala was the first editor of 'Jonaki'.

Q: What is the Jonaki era in Assamese literature?
A: The Jonaki era (late 19th to early 20th century) is the romantic period of Assamese literature, marked by lyrical poetry, romance, and a national awakening.

A: Laxminath Bezbaroa is often called the father of modern Assamese literature.

A: লক্ষ্মীনাথ বেজবৰুৱাক সাহিত্যৰথী হিচাপে সন্মান জনোৱা হয় আৰু তেওঁক আধুনিক অসমীয়া সাহিত্যৰ পিতৃ বুলি কোৱা হয়। তেওঁ শ্ৰীৰামপদ, বামুণ গোসাঁই আৰু কৃপানাথ ছদ্মনামেৰে লিখিছিল।

A: The Asam Sahitya Sabha was founded on 26 December 1917 at Sivasagar, in Assam.
Q: Who was the first president of the Asam Sahitya Sabha?
A: Padmanath Gohain Baruah was the founder-president and the first president of the Asam Sahitya Sabha.
Q: What is the official journal of the Asam Sahitya Sabha?
A: The Asam Sahitya Sabha Patrika is the official journal. Its first issue appeared in October 1927, with Chandradhar Barua as founder editor.
Q: Which was the first modern Assamese literary magazine and who started it?
A: Jonaki (1889), started by Chandra Kumar Agarwala under the Asamiya Bhasa Unnati Sadhini Sabha, is regarded as the first modern Assamese literary magazine.
Q: What is the theme song of the Asam Sahitya Sabha?
A: The theme song is "Siro Senehi Mur Bhaxa Jononi", written by Mitradev Mahanta.
Q: অসম সাহিত্য সভা কেতিয়া আৰু ক'ত প্ৰতিষ্ঠা হৈছিল?
A: অসম সাহিত্য সভা ১৯১৭ চনৰ ২৬ ডিচেম্বৰত শিৱসাগৰত প্ৰতিষ্ঠা হৈছিল।
Q: অসম সাহিত্য সভাৰ প্ৰথম সভাপতি কোন আছিল?
A: পদ্মনাথ গোহাঞি বৰুৱা অসম সাহিত্য সভাৰ প্ৰতিষ্ঠাপক-সভাপতি তথা প্ৰথম সভাপতি আছিল।
Q: অসম সাহিত্য সভাৰ চৰকাৰী আলোচনীখন কোনখন?
A: অসম সাহিত্য সভা পত্ৰিকা চৰকাৰী আলোচনী। ইয়াৰ প্ৰথম সংখ্যা ১৯২৭ চনৰ অক্টোবৰত প্ৰকাশ হৈছিল আৰু চন্দ্ৰধৰ বৰুৱা প্ৰতিষ্ঠাপক সম্পাদক আছিল।
Q: প্ৰথম আধুনিক অসমীয়া সাহিত্য-আলোচনী কোনখন আৰু কোনে আৰম্ভ কৰিছিল?
A: জোনাকী (১৮৮৯), যাৰ আৰম্ভণি অসমীয়া ভাষা উন্নতি সাধিনী সভাৰ অধীনত চন্দ্ৰকুমাৰ আগৰৱালাই কৰিছিল, প্ৰথম আধুনিক অসমীয়া সাহিত্য-আলোচনী হিচাপে গণ্য কৰা হয়।

A: মূল সুৰ হৈছে "চিৰ চেনেহী মোৰ ভাষা জননী", যিটো মিত্ৰদেৱ মহন্তই ৰচনা কৰিছিল।

### Charit Puthis & Early Prose — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-literature/vaishnavite-period-sec/charit-puthis-early-prose/
Summary: Practice charit puthis & early prose questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What are Charit Puthis?
A: Charit Puthis are biographical texts of the Vaishnavite period that narrate the lives of Sankardev, Madhavdev, and other saints.
Q: What is the 'Guru Charit'?
A: The Guru Charit is a hagiographical text describing the lives of Sankardev and Madhavdev, an important early prose work.
Q: Who are the traditional authors of the Guru Charit?
A: The Guru Charit is traditionally attributed to Daitari Thakur (Daityari Thakur) and Rama Charan Thakur.
Q: Which is considered the earliest prose work in Assamese literature?
A: The 'Katha Guru Charit' is generally considered one of the earliest prose works in Assamese literature.
Q: What is the 'Katha Guru Charit'?
A: The Katha Guru Charit is an early prose biography of Sankardev and Madhavdev, written in simple narrative style.
Q: Who wrote the 'Sankardev Charit'?
