A: The 'Sankardev Charit' was written by Rama Charan Thakur and Daitari Thakur (Daityari Thakur).
Q: What is the 'Madhavdev Charit'?
A: The 'Madhavdev Charit' is a biography of Madhavdev, traditionally attributed to Daityari Thakur.
Q: Who is the author of 'Sarala Mahatmya'?
A: 'Sarala Mahatmya' is a later text, and its authorship is attributed to various later writers; it is not one of the classic Charit Puthis.
Q: What is the significance of Charit Puthis in Assamese literature?
A: Charit Puthis are significant as early prose narratives that preserve the history of the Vaishnavite movement and the lives of its saints.
Q: What is 'Katha Bhagavata'?
A: 'Katha Bhagavata' is the prose translation of the Bhagavata Purana by Bhattadeva, a landmark of early Assamese prose.
Q: Who is Bhattadeva?
A: Bhattadeva, also known as Rama Kavi Saraswati, was a Vaishnavite scholar of the 16th century called the father of Assamese prose.
Q: Why is Bhattadeva called the father of Assamese prose?
A: Bhattadeva is called the father of Assamese prose because he wrote the first substantial prose works, 'Katha Bhagavata' and 'Katha Gita', in pure Assamese prose.
Q: What are the main prose works of Bhattadeva?
A: The main prose works of Bhattadeva are 'Katha Bhagavata' and 'Katha Gita'.
Q: Who wrote 'Katha Gita'?
A: 'Katha Gita' was written by Bhattadeva as a prose rendering of the Bhagavad Gita.
Q: What is the difference between the Guru Charit and Katha Guru Charit?
A: The Guru Charit is a longer hagiographical text, while the Katha Guru Charit is an earlier, simpler prose narrative; both describe the lives of the saints.
Q: Who is the author of 'Anadi Patana' - a Charit Puthi or not?
A: No, 'Anadi Patana' is a poem by Madhavdev on creation, not a Charit Puthi.
Q: What is 'Bhakti Ratnakar'?
A: 'Bhakti Ratnakar' is a devotional work by Sankardev based on the Bhagavata Purana, related to the Vaishnavite period.
Q: Which early prose text describes the conversations of the Vaishnavite saints?
A: The 'Katha Guru Charit' describes the conversations and teachings of the Vaishnavite saints.
Q: Who wrote the 'Sankardev Charita' (life of Sankardev) in Assamese prose?
A: The 'Sankardev Charit' was written by Rama Charan Thakur and Daitari Thakur.
Q: What is 'Mantra Samhita'?
A: 'Mantra Samhita' is a later Vaishnavite text; its authorship and content relate to hymns and rituals, distinct from Charit Puthis.
Q: Which Charit Puthi is considered the most important biography of Sankardev?
A: The 'Guru Charit' is considered the most important hagiographical text on the lives of Sankardev and Madhavdev.
Q: What is the historical value of Charit Puthis?
A: Charit Puthis have historical value as they record the social, religious, and cultural life of the Vaishnavite period in Assam.
Q: Who wrote 'Padmapurana' in Assamese?
A: The 'Padmapurana' (Padma Purana) was translated by Durgabara Kayastha, a later work, not a Charit Puthi.
Q: What is the language style of the Katha Guru Charit?
A: The Katha Guru Charit is written in a simple, colloquial Assamese prose style with narrative flow.
Q: Which is the earliest form of Assamese prose literature?
A: The Charit Puthis and Katha texts of the Vaishnavite period represent the earliest form of Assamese prose literature.
Q: Who is the author of 'Ramayan' prose in early Assamese?
A: Early Assamese prose works on the Ramayana are rare; the famous Ramayana in Assamese is the Saptakanda Ramayana by Madhava Kandali (verse), not prose.
Q: What is 'Katha Gita' significance in Assamese prose?
A: 'Katha Gita' is significant as the first prose rendering of the Bhagavad Gita in Assamese, by Bhattadeva.
Q: What are 'Sarala Mahatmya' and 'Guru Purnima' related to?
A: Guru Purnima is the festival honoring the Guru, celebrated in the Sattras; 'Sarala Mahatmya' is a later devotional text, both connected to Vaishnavite tradition.
Q: Who wrote 'Baran Charit' (Varna Charit)?
A: 'Baran Charit' is an obscure later text; among the known Charit Puthis, the Guru Charit and its variants are the most famous.
Q: What does 'Charit' mean in Assamese literature?
A: 'Charit' means biography or the story of a person's life, especially of saints.
Q: Which Charit text describes both Sankardev and Madhavdev together?
A: The 'Guru Charit' describes both Sankardev and Madhavdev together as the Guru pair.
Q: What is the 'Bhagavat' prose of the Vaishnavite period?
A: The 'Katha Bhagavata' of Bhattadeva is the major prose Bhagavata of the Vaishnavite period.
Q: Who translated the 'Bhagavata' into Assamese prose?
A: Bhattadeva translated the Bhagavata into Assamese prose as 'Katha Bhagavata'.
Q: What is the 'Guru Puthi'?
A: 'Guru Puthi' is a general term used for texts relating to the Guru (Sankardev/Madhavdev), including the Charit Puthis.
Q: Which early prose work is attributed to Daitari Thakur?
A: Parts of the Guru Charit and the Madhavdev Charit are attributed to Daitari Thakur.
Q: What is the value of Charit Puthis for Assamese language study?
A: Charit Puthis preserve the colloquial Assamese of the 16th-17th centuries, valuable for linguistic and historical study.
Q: Who wrote the 'Katha Guru'?
A: The 'Katha Guru Charit' is traditionally attributed to Rama Saraswati or the Thakur brothers (Daitari and Rama Charan).
Q: What are Charit Puthis and why are they important?
A: Charit Puthis are biographical texts of the Vaishnavite period that narrate the lives of Sankardev, Madhavdev and other saints. They are important because they are among the earliest Assamese prose works and they preserve the social, religious and cultural history of the period.
Q: Who wrote the Guru Charit and what is its place in Assamese literature?
A: The Guru Charit, also called the Katha Guru Charit, is traditionally attributed to Daitari (Daityari) Thakur and Rama Charan Thakur. It is a biography of Sankardev and is regarded as one of the earliest works of Assamese prose.
Q: Who is called the father of Assamese prose and which works earned him the title?
A: Bhattadeva, also known as Rama Kavi Saraswati, is called the father of Assamese prose. He earned the title through the Katha Bhagavata, his prose rendering of the Bhagavata Purana, and the Katha Gita, his prose rendering of the Bhagavad Gita.
Q: Which is considered one of the earliest prose works in Assamese literature?
A: The Katha Guru Charit is generally considered one of the earliest prose works in Assamese literature. It is written in simple, colloquial Assamese prose and describes the lives of Sankardev and Madhavdev.
Q: What is the language and historical value of the Charit Puthis?
A: The Charit Puthis are written in simple, colloquial Assamese prose. Historically they are valuable because they record the lives of the Vaishnavite saints and the social and religious life of sixteenth and seventeenth century Assam, and they preserve the spoken Assamese of that age.
Q: চৰিত পুথি কি আৰু ই কিয় গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: চৰিত পুথি হৈছে বৈষ্ণৱ যুগৰ জীৱনী-ভিত্তিক ৰচনা, য'ত শংকৰদেৱ, মাধৱদেৱ আৰু আন সন্তসকলৰ জীৱন-কাহিনী বৰ্ণিত। ই অসমীয়া আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি গদ্য ৰচনাসমূহৰ ভিতৰত অন্যতম, আৰু সময়ৰ সামাজিক, ধৰ্মীয় আৰু সাংস্কৃতিক ইতিহাস সংৰক্ষণ কৰে।
Q: গুৰু চৰিত কোনে লিখিছিল আৰু অসমীয়া সাহিত্যত ইয়াৰ স্থান কি?
A: গুৰু চৰিত, যিখনক কথা গুৰু চৰিতও বোলা হয়, পৰম্পৰাগতভাৱে দয়িতাৰী (দৈত্যাৰি) ঠাকুৰ আৰু ৰামচৰণ ঠাকুৰলৈ আৰোপ কৰা হয়। ই শংকৰদেৱৰ জীৱনী আৰু অসমীয়া গদ্যৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি ৰচনাসমূহৰ এটা হিচাপে গণ্য।
Q: অসমীয়া গদ্যৰ জনক কোন আৰু তেওঁক সেই উপাধি কি ৰচনাই দিছে?
A: ভট্টদেৱ, ৰাম কবি সৰস্বতী বুলিও জনা যায়, তেওঁক অসমীয়া গদ্যৰ জনক বোলা হয়। তেওঁ ভাগৱত পুৰাণৰ গদ্য ৰূপ কথা ভাগৱত আৰু ভগৱদ গীতাৰ গদ্য ৰূপ কথা গীতাৰ জৰিয়তে এই উপাধি লাভ কৰিছে।
Q: অসমীয়া সাহিত্যৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি গদ্য ৰচনাৰ ভিতৰত কোনখন গণ্য কৰা হয়?
A: কথা গুৰু চৰিতক সাধাৰণতে অসমীয়া সাহিত্যৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি গদ্য ৰচনাসমূহৰ এটা বুলি গণ্য কৰা হয়। ই সৰল, কথ্য অসমীয়া গদ্যত লিখা আৰু শংকৰদেৱ-মাধৱদেৱৰ জীৱন বৰ্ণনা কৰে।
Q: চৰিত পুথিৰ ভাষা আৰু ঐতিহাসিক মূল্য কি?
A: চৰিত পুথিবোৰ সৰল, কথ্য অসমীয়া গদ্যত লিখা। ঐতিহাসিকভাৱে ই মূল্যৱান কাৰণ ই বৈষ্ণৱ সন্তসকলৰ জীৱন আৰু ষোড়শ-সপ্তদশ শতিকাৰ অসমৰ সামাজিক-ধৰ্মীয় জীৱন লিপিবদ্ধ কৰে, আৰু সেই সময়ৰ কথ্য অসমীয়া সংৰক্ষণ কৰে।

### Sankardev & Madhavdev Works — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/assam-literature/vaishnavite-period-sec/sankardev-madhavdev-works/
Summary: Practice sankardev & madhavdev works questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Who is Srimanta Sankardev?
A: Srimanta Sankardev (1449-1568) was a 15th-16th century saint, poet, playwright, and social reformer who founded the Ekasarana Namadharma in Assam.
Q: When and where was Sankardev born?
A: Sankardev was born in 1449 at Bordowa (Alipukhuri) in present-day Nagaon district of Assam.
Q: What is the 'Kirtan Ghosha'?
A: The Kirtan Ghosha is the magnum opus of Sankardev, a collection of devotional songs (kirtans) on the glory of Lord Krishna.
Q: How many kirtans are there in the Kirtan Ghosha?
A: The Kirtan Ghosha contains 26 kirtans (some editions say 27), divided into 12 sections.
Q: Which is the first kirtan of the Kirtan Ghosha?
A: The first kirtan of the Kirtan Ghosha is 'Narayan Kirtan' (Kirtan Namaparayan).
Q: What is 'Nimi Nava Siddha'?
A: 'Nimi Nava Siddha' is the third kirtan in the Kirtan Ghosha, describing the discussion between King Nimi and nine Siddhas.
Q: What is 'Ajamil Upakhyan'?
A: 'Ajamil Upakhyan' is the eighth kirtan of the Kirtan Ghosha, narrating the story of Ajamila's salvation.
Q: What is the Borgeet?
A: Borgeet are classical devotional songs of the Vaishnavite tradition, composed by Sankardev and Madhavdev.
Q: Who composed the Borgeets?
A: The Borgeets were composed by Sankardev and Madhavdev.
Q: Who composed more Borgeets - Sankardev or Madhavdev?
A: Madhavdev composed more Borgeets (about 120) than Sankardev (about 30).
Q: What is an Ankiya Naat?
A: Ankiya Naat is a one-act play tradition started by Sankardev, combining drama, music, and dance, performed as Bhaona.
Q: What is the first Ankiya Naat of Sankardev?
A: 'Chinhayatra' is considered the first Ankiya Naat of Sankardev.
Q: Name some Ankiya Naats written by Sankardev.
A: Some Ankiya Naats of Sankardev are 'Patni Prasad', 'Keli Gopal', 'Rukmini Haran', 'Parijat Haran', 'Kaliya Daman', 'Ram Vijay', and 'Kansa Vadha'.
Q: What is Bhaona?
A: Bhaona is the theatrical performance of Ankiya Naat plays in Assamese Vaishnavite tradition, initiated by Sankardev.
Q: Which of Sankardev's works is a translation of the Bhagavata Purana?
A: Sankardev translated the first book (Skandha) of the Bhagavata Purana into Assamese as 'Bhakti Ratnakar' and also wrote the 'Bhagavat' sections in the Kirtan Ghosha.
Q: What is 'Rukmini Haran'?
A: 'Rukmini Haran' is both a Kavya (long poem) and an Ankiya Naat by Sankardev, describing Krishna's marriage with Rukmini.
Q: Who is Madhavdev?
A: Madhavdev (1489-1596) was the chief disciple of Sankardev and a major poet, playwright, and composer of the Vaishnavite tradition.
Q: What is the 'Naam Ghosha'?
A: The Naam Ghosha is the magnum opus of Madhavdev, a collection of devotional prayers and verses on the power of God's name.
Q: How many verses are there in the Naam Ghosha?
A: The Naam Ghosha contains about 746 verses (some editions say more) praising the Lord and the Guru.
Q: What is 'Anadi Patana'?
A: 'Anadi Patana' is a poem by Madhavdev describing the creation of the universe and the nature of God.
Q: What is 'Janam Rash' or 'Janma Rash'?
A: 'Janma Rash' is a work by Madhavdev describing the birth and childhood of Krishna.
Q: What is 'Rukminir Haran' by Madhavdev?
A: 'Rukminir Haran' is an Ankiya Naat written by Madhavdev, dramatizing the elopement of Rukmini with Krishna.
Q: What are 'Bhatimas'?
A: Bhatimas are devotional songs composed by Madhavdev in praise of God and the Guru, classified into Ghattana, Padya, and Ragiya Bhatima.
Q: What is the 'Kirtan Ghosha' also called?
A: The Kirtan Ghosha is also called 'Gunamala' (the garland of virtues).
Q: Which work of Sankardev describes the life of Sri Krishna in the form of a garland?
A: The 'Gunamala' (Kirtan Ghosha) describes the life of Krishna in the form of a garland.
Q: Who wrote 'Kansa Vadha'?
A: 'Kansa Vadha' (Kangsa Badh) is an Ankiya Naat written by Sankardev.
Q: Who wrote 'Patni Prasad'?
A: 'Patni Prasad' is an Ankiya Naat written by Sankardev.
Q: What is the Ekasarana Namadharma?
A: Ekasarana Namadharma is the religion founded by Sankardev, based on devotion (bhakti) to a single God, Krishna, through the chanting of His name.
Q: Which book of Sankardev is a translation of the Bhagavad Gita?
A: Sankardev translated the 'Katha Gita' sections of the Bhagavad Gita within his Bhagavata renderings, though the full prose Gita translation is attributed to Bhattadeva.
Q: Who is called the 'Mahapurusha'?
A: Sankardev and Madhavdev are both revered as 'Mahapurusha' (great souls) in Assamese tradition.
Q: What is a 'Sattra'?
A: A Sattra is a Vaishnavite monastery or institution established by Sankardev and his followers for religious and cultural activities.
Q: Which dance form is associated with Sankardev's tradition?
A: Sattriya dance is the classical dance form associated with Sankardev's Vaishnavite tradition.
Q: Who wrote 'Bhaktiratnakar'?
A: Sankardev wrote 'Bhaktiratnakar' (Bhaktiratnakara), a devotional work based on the Bhagavata Purana.
Q: Which is Madhavdev's Ankiya Naat on Rukmini?
A: 'Rukminir Haran' is Madhavdev's Ankiya Naat on Rukmini.
Q: What is the theme of Sankardev's 'Keli Gopal'?
A: 'Keli Gopal' is an Ankiya Naat depicting the playful pastimes (leela) of child Krishna with the cowherd boys.
Q: What is the significance of Madhavdev in Assamese literature?
A: Madhavdev is significant for his devotional poetry, the Naam Ghosha, Borgeets, Bhatimas, and for consolidating the Vaishnavite tradition after Sankardev.
Q: Who founded the Sattra institution?
A: Sankardev founded the Sattra institution for the propagation of Ekasarana Namadharma.
Q: Who founded the Ekasarana Namadharma and what are its main features?
A: Srimanta Sankardev founded the Ekasarana Namadharma. It teaches devotion to a single God, Krishna, mainly through the chanting of his name, and it played down elaborate ritual and caste distinctions. The faith was spread through the Sattra and the Namghar.
Q: Which is the magnum opus of Sankardev and what is it also called?
A: Sankardev's magnum opus is the Kirtan Ghosha, which is also called the Gunamala. It contains about 26 kirtans (some editions say 27) that describe the life and glory of Krishna.
Q: What is the Naam Ghosha and who composed it?
A: The Naam Ghosha is the magnum opus of Madhavdev, Sankardev's chief disciple. It is a collection of about 746 verses on the power of God's name and is recited daily in the Namghar.
Q: What is the difference between an Ankiya Naat and a Bhaona?
A: An Ankiya Naat is the one-act play composed by Sankardev, such as Chinhayatra or Rukmini Haran. Bhaona is the theatrical performance of such a play, combining drama, music and dance.
Q: Who composed more Borgeet, and what are Bhatimas?
A: Madhavdev composed more Borgeet, about 120, against about 30 by Sankardev. Bhatimas are devotional songs composed by Madhavdev in praise of God and the Guru, and they are of three kinds: Ghattana, Padya and Ragiya.
Q: একশৰণ নামধৰ্ম কোনে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল আৰু ইয়াৰ মূল বৈশিষ্ট্য কি?
A: শ্ৰীমন্ত শংকৰদেৱে একশৰণ নামধৰ্ম প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল। ই একেশ্বৰ, কৃষ্ণৰ প্ৰতি ভক্তি, মূলত তেওঁৰ নাম স্মৰণৰ জৰিয়তে, আৰু বিস্তৃত কৰ্মকাণ্ড আৰু জাতিভেদৰ ওপৰত গুৰুত্ব কমাইছিল। সত্ৰ আৰু নামঘৰৰ জৰিয়তে এই ধৰ্ম বিয়পিছিল।
Q: শংকৰদেৱৰ শ্ৰেষ্ঠ ৰচনা কোনখন আৰু ইয়াক আন কি বোলা হয়?
A: শংকৰদেৱৰ শ্ৰেষ্ঠ ৰচনা কীৰ্তন ঘোষা, যিখনক গুণমালাও বোলা হয়। ইয়াত কৃষ্ণৰ জীৱন আৰু মহিমা বৰ্ণনা কৰা প্ৰায় ২৬টা কীৰ্তন (কিছুমান সংস্কৰণত ২৭) আছে।
Q: নাম ঘোষা কি আৰু কোনে ৰচনা কৰিছিল?
A: নাম ঘোষা মাধৱদেৱৰ শ্ৰেষ্ঠ ৰচনা, যি ঈশ্বৰৰ নামৰ শক্তি সম্পৰ্কে প্ৰায় ৭৪৬টা পদৰ সংকলন আৰু নামঘৰত প্ৰতিদিনে পাঠ কৰা হয়।
Q: আঙ্কীয়া নাট আৰু ভাওনাৰ পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: আঙ্কীয়া নাট হৈছে শংকৰদেৱে ৰচনা কৰা একাঙ্কিক নাট, যেনে চিহ্নযাত্ৰা বা ৰুক্মিণী হৰণ। ভাওনা হৈছে তেনে নাটৰ মঞ্চ পৰিবেশন, য'ত নাট, সংগীত আৰু নৃত্য একত্ৰিত হয়।
Q: বেছি বৰগীত কোনে ৰচনা কৰিছিল, আৰু ভাটিমা কি?
A: মাধৱদেৱে শংকৰদেৱতকৈ বেছি বৰগীত ৰচনা কৰিছিল, প্ৰায় ১২০টা, শংকৰদেৱৰ প্ৰায় ৩০টাৰ বিপৰীতে। ভাটিমা হৈছে মাধৱদেৱে ঈশ্বৰ আৰু গুৰুৰ স্তুতিত ৰচনা কৰা ভক্তিমূলক গীত, যিবোৰ ঘট্টনা, পদ্য আৰু ৰাগীয়া এই তিনি প্ৰকাৰ।

### Act East Policy & Border Trade — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/assam-economy-sec/assam-act-east-border-trade/
Summary: Practice act east policy & border trade questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Which policy was renamed as 'Act East Policy' in 2014?
A: The 'Look East Policy' was renamed as 'Act East Policy' in 2014.
Q: When was the Look East Policy first launched?
A: The Look East Policy was launched in 1991 by the government of P.V. Narasimha Rao.
Q: Which ministry is primarily responsible for implementing the Act East Policy?
A: The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) leads the Act East Policy, supported by the Ministry of DoNER.
Q: What is the key objective of the Act East Policy for Assam and the North East?
A: To integrate the North East with Southeast Asian economies and boost connectivity and trade.
Q: Which neighbouring country shares the longest international border with Assam?
A: Bangladesh shares the longest international border with Assam (about 263 km).
Q: Which district of Assam shares a border with Bhutan?
A: Districts like Baksa, Udalguri, Kokrajhar, Chirang and Sivasagar (in part) share borders with Bhutan.
Q: Which is the major border trade point between Assam and Bangladesh?
A: Karimganj (Sutarkandi) and Dhubri are major border trade points with Bangladesh.
Q: Which international land custom station (LCS) in Assam facilitates trade with Bangladesh?
A: The Sutarkandi (Karimganj) Land Customs Station facilitates India-Bangladesh trade in Assam.
Q: What is a 'border haat' in the context of India-Bangladesh border trade?
A: A border haat is a weekly market held at the border where local people of both countries buy and sell items.
Q: Which is the first border haat operational on the India-Bangladesh border?
A: The first border haats were set up in Meghalaya (Kalaichar) and Tripura; Assam's border haats were opened later.
Q: Which corridor connects the North East to Bangladesh ports under Act East?
A: The India-Bangladesh corridor via Chittagong and Mongla ports connects the North East to the sea.
Q: Which initiative aims to develop the Kaladan multi-modal transit corridor?
A: The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project connects the North East to Myanmar's Sittwe port.
Q: What is the BCIM corridor?
A: The BCIM Economic Corridor links Bangladesh, China, India and Myanmar as a regional connectivity initiative.
Q: Which organisation was formed to promote the ASEAN-India cooperation in the region?
A: The ASEAN-India partnership is promoted through summits, the ASEAN-India FTA and the Act East Policy.
Q: Which India-Bangladesh rail link from Assam enhances bilateral trade?
A: The Agartala-Akhaura rail link and the proposed Jogighopa links enhance rail trade with Bangladesh.
Q: Which state of India is the primary gateway for Act East trade from Assam?
A: Assam itself, along with Manipur and Tripura, serves as the gateway, with Guwahati as the regional hub.
Q: Which river-based trade route links Assam to Bangladesh under the protocol on inland water transit?
A: The Brahmaputra (NW-2) connects to Bangladesh waterways under the India-Bangladesh protocol routes.
Q: What is the importance of the Sutarkandi LCS for Assam's trade?
A: It is a major point for export of coal, tea, fruits and other products from the Barak valley to Bangladesh.
Q: Which year saw the first India-Bangladesh border haat being mooted for Assam?
A: Border haats for Assam were approved around 2017-2018 under the 2016 bilateral protocol.
Q: Which trade items are traditionally exported from Assam to Bangladesh?
A: Tea, coal, stone chips, fruits, spices, bamboo and bamboo products are exported to Bangladesh.
Q: Which government body promotes export from Assam?
A: The Directorate of Industries and Commerce, FIEO and the Ministry of DoNER promote exports from Assam.
Q: Which is the major export product of Assam to Southeast Asia?
A: Tea is the major export product of Assam to Southeast Asian and global markets.
Q: Which Indian city is considered the 'Gateway to the North East' for Act East trade?
A: Guwahati is considered the 'Gateway to the North East' for Act East trade.
Q: Which international airport in Assam facilitates air cargo for border trade?
A: The Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport at Guwahati handles air cargo for trade.
Q: What is the role of the Land Ports Authority of India (LPAI) in Assam?
A: LPAI develops and manages land ports and land custom stations to facilitate cross-border trade.
Q: Which Indian state borders Bhutan, facilitating trade through Gelephu and other points?
A: Assam borders Bhutan, with trade points like Darranga (Tamulpur) facilitating bilateral commerce.
Q: Which mega project connects Assam to Myanmar for trade under the India-Myanmar corridor?
A: The India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway connects NE India (including via Assam) to Southeast Asia.
Q: Which river port in Assam is being developed for transit trade to Bangladesh?
A: The Pandu port and the Dhubri port are being developed for transit trade to Bangladesh via NW-2.
Q: What is the significance of the Asian Highway Network for Assam?
A: The Asian Highway connects Assam's road network to Southeast Asia, boosting trade and connectivity.
Q: Which bilateral agreement provides for using Chittagong port for NE transit?
A: The 2018 India-Bangladesh MoU allows the use of Chittagong and Mongla ports for NE cargo.
Q: Which scheme of the Government of India funds border infrastructure in Assam?
A: The Border Area Development Programme (BADP) funds border infrastructure in Assam.
Q: Which tea-based product is a major export of Assam to China and Russia?
A: Orthodox and CTC teas of Assam are major exports, especially to Russia and the Middle East.
Q: What is the 'Act East' advantage for the tourism sector of Assam?
A: Better connectivity with Southeast Asia boosts inbound tourism and cultural exchange for Assam.
Q: Which railway project connects the North East to Myanmar under regional connectivity?
A: The proposed Jiribam-Imphal-Moreh rail link connects to Myanmar, enhancing Act East connectivity.
Q: Which is the main constraint for border trade in Assam historically?
A: Lack of adequate infrastructure, border fencing issues and connectivity bottlenecks have constrained border trade.
Q: When was the Act East Policy launched and which policy did it replace?
A: The Look East Policy was launched in 1991 under the government of P.V. Narasimha Rao, and it was renamed the Act East Policy in 2014. The Act East Policy is led by the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), supported by the Ministry of DoNER, and aims to integrate the North East with Southeast Asian economies through connectivity and trade.
Q: Which country shares the longest international border with Assam?
A: Bangladesh shares the longest international border with Assam, about 263 km, mainly in the districts of Karimganj, Cachar, Dhubri and South Salmara. Assam also borders Bhutan, through districts such as Baksa, Udalguri, Kokrajhar and Chirang.
Q: What are the major border trade points of Assam?
A: The Sutarkandi Land Customs Station in Karimganj is a major trade point with Bangladesh, used for exporting coal, tea, fruits and other products from the Barak valley, and Dhubri is another important point. Trade with Bhutan takes place through points such as Darranga in Tamulpur. A border haat is a weekly market where local people from both countries trade.
Q: Which connectivity corridors are important for the Act East Policy?
A: Important corridors include the India-Bangladesh corridor using Chittagong and Mongla ports, the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project linking to Myanmar's Sittwe port, the India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway, the BCIM Economic Corridor and the Asian Highway Network. The Agartala-Akhaura rail link and the Brahmaputra river route also strengthen connectivity.
Q: What are the main constraints on border trade in Assam?
A: Historically, border trade has been constrained by lack of adequate infrastructure, border fencing issues and connectivity bottlenecks. The Border Area Development Programme (BADP) funds border infrastructure, and bodies such as the Directorate of Industries and Commerce, FIEO and the Ministry of DoNER promote exports from Assam.
Q: এক্ট ইষ্ট নীতি কেতিয়া আৰম্ভ হৈছিল আৰু কোন নীতিক সলনি কৰিছিল?
A: লুক ইষ্ট নীতি ১৯৯১ চনত পি.ভি. নৰসিংহ ৰাওৰ চৰকাৰৰ অধীনত আৰম্ভ কৰা হৈছিল, আৰু ২০১৪ চনত ইয়াক এক্ট ইষ্ট নীতি নাম দিয়া হৈছিল। এক্ট ইষ্ট নীতিক বৈদেশিক পৰিক্ৰমা মন্ত্ৰালয় (MEA) য়ে নেতৃত্ব দিয়ে, DoNER মন্ত্ৰালয়ে সহায় কৰে, আৰু ই সংযোগ তথা বাণিজ্যৰ জৰিয়তে উত্তৰ-পূবক দক্ষিণ-পূব এছিয়াৰ অৰ্থনীতিসমূহৰ সৈতে সংহত কৰাৰ লক্ষ্য ৰাখে।
Q: কোন দেশে অসমৰ সৈতে আটাইতকৈ দীঘল আন্তৰ্জাতিক সীমান্ত ভাগ কৰে?
A: বাংলাদেশে অসমৰ সৈতে আটাইতকৈ দীঘল আন্তৰ্জাতিক সীমান্ত ভাগ কৰে, প্ৰায় ২৬৩ কিলোমিটাৰ, মূলতঃ কৰিমগঞ্জ, কাছাৰ, ধুবুৰী আৰু দক্ষিণ ছালমাৰা জিলাত। অসমে ভূটানৰ সৈতেও সীমান্ত ভাগ কৰে, বাক্সা, ওদালগুৰি, কোকৰাঝাৰ আৰু চিৰাঙৰ দৰে জিলাৰ জৰিয়তে।
Q: অসমৰ প্ৰধান সীমান্ত বাণিজ্য কেন্দ্ৰসমূহ কি?
A: কৰিমগঞ্জৰ সুতাৰকান্দি লেণ্ড কাষ্টম ষ্টেচন বাংলাদেশৰ সৈতে এটা প্ৰধান বাণিজ্য কেন্দ্ৰ, যি বৰাক উপত্যকাৰ পৰা কয়লা, চাহ, ফল আৰু অন্যান্য সামগ্ৰী ৰপ্তানিৰ বাবে ব্যৱহৃত হয়, আৰু ধুবুৰী আন এক গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ কেন্দ্ৰ। ভূটানৰ সৈতে বাণিজ্য তামুলপুৰৰ দৰাংগাৰ দৰে কেন্দ্ৰৰ জৰিয়তে হয়। সীমান্ত হাট এটা সাপ্তাহিক বজাৰ য'ত দুয়ো দেশৰ স্থানীয় লোকে বাণিজ্য কৰে।
Q: এক্ট ইষ্ট নীতিৰ বাবে কোনবোৰ সংযোগ কৰিডৰ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ কৰিডৰসমূহৰ ভিতৰত চট্টগ্ৰাম আৰু মংলা বন্দৰ ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা ভাৰত-বাংলাদেশ কৰিডৰ, ম্যানমাৰৰ চিটৱে বন্দৰৰ সৈতে সংযোগ কৰা কলাদান বহুমুখী ট্ৰানজিট পৰিবহণ প্ৰকল্প, ভাৰত-ম্যানমাৰ-থাইলেণ্ড ত্ৰিপাক্ষিক মহাসড়ক, BCIM অৰ্থনৈতিক কৰিডৰ আৰু এছিয়ান মহাসড়ক নেটৱৰ্ক অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত। আগৰতলা-আখাউৰা ৰে'ল সংযোগ আৰু ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ নদী পথেও সংযোগ সবল কৰে।
Q: অসমত সীমান্ত বাণিজ্যৰ প্ৰধান সীমাবদ্ধতাসমূহ কি?
A: ঐতিহাসিকভাৱে, সীমান্ত বাণিজ্য যথেষ্ট আন্তঃগাঁথনিৰ অভাৱ, সীমান্ত তৰ্জনী সমস্যা আৰু সংযোগৰ বাধাৰ দ্বাৰা সীমাবদ্ধ আছিল। সীমান্ত অঞ্চল উন্নয়ন কাৰ্যসূচী (BADP) য়ে সীমান্ত আন্তঃগাঁথনি বিত্ত দিয়ে, আৰু ঔদ্যোগিক তথা বাণিজ্য অধিকাৰী, FIEO আৰু DoNER মন্ত্ৰালয়ৰ দৰে সংস্থাই অসমৰ পৰা ৰপ্তানি প্ৰচাৰ কৰে।

### Agriculture & Horticulture — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/assam-economy-sec/assam-agriculture-horticulture/
Summary: Practice agriculture & horticulture questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What is the main staple food crop of Assam?
A: Rice (paddy). Assam is predominantly a rice-producing state and rice is the staple food of the people.
Q: What is the Assamese name for the autumn rice crop sown in May-June and harvested in August-September?
A: Ahu rice, which is the autumn or pre-kharif rice variety grown in upland areas.
Q: Which rice variety of Assam is grown during the winter season (sown June-July, harvested November-December) and is the most important?
A: Sali (winter) rice, which is the main and most extensive rice crop of the state.
Q: Which rice variety of Assam is cultivated in low-lying areas using winter/summer irrigation and harvested in summer?
A: Boro rice, which is grown during the winter-spring season (November to May) in low-lying and swampy areas.
Q: Which high-yielding rice variety developed in Assam is popular for its short duration and good yield?
A: Ranjit, which is a popular semi-dwarf high-yielding Sali rice variety of Assam.
Q: Name the famous aromatic rice variety of Assam, mainly grown in the upper Assam districts.
A: Joha rice, which is a short-grain aromatic rice prized for its fragrance and taste.
Q: True or False: Paddy is the only major cereal crop grown in Assam.
A: False. Besides paddy, Assam also grows maize, wheat, pulses, oilseeds and millets in limited areas.
Q: Which fibre crop is traditionally an important cash crop of Assam grown in the Barak valley and parts of the Brahmaputra valley?
A: Jute, which is a major commercial fibre crop of the state.
Q: Which district of Assam is the leading producer of jute?
A: Dhubri district, along with Goalpara and Barpeta, is among the leading jute producers of the state.
Q: Name the major oilseed crop grown in Assam.
A: Mustard (rapeseed-mustard) is the major oilseed crop of the state, grown mainly in the winter season.
Q: Which district is known as the 'Rice Bowl of Assam'?
A: Dibrugarh district is often referred to as the 'Rice Bowl of Assam' due to its high paddy production.
Q: What is the primary irrigation source used by farmers in the Brahmaputra valley?
A: Monsoon rainfall supplemented by riverine water, low-lift pumps, and tube wells, since rainfall is abundant but seasonal.
Q: Which major river project on the Brahmaputra basin supports irrigation in the Karbi Anglong and Nagaon regions?
A: The Dhansiri irrigation project and the Karbi Anglong irrigation schemes, fed by the Dhansiri river system.
Q: Which is the principal horticultural fruit of Assam in terms of production?
A: Banana is the principal horticultural fruit of Assam in terms of area and production.
Q: Which district of Assam is famous for the production of oranges (mandarin)?
A: Tinsukia district, especially the Margherita region, and also Golaghat's Karbi foothills, are known for oranges.
Q: Which fruit of Assam is known by the local name 'Mitha Khol' or the 'Queen of Fruits' in some references?
A: Pineapple, which is a major horticultural fruit of the state, especially grown in the Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao hills.
Q: What is the 'Bhut Jolokia' or King Chilli, and why is it famous?
A: It is a very hot chilli variety of Assam which was recognised as one of the world's hottest chillies and holds a GI tag.
Q: Which spice crop, known for its strong aroma, is widely grown in Assam and used in food and traditional medicine?
A: Ginger and turmeric are the main spice crops of Assam, with Nagaon and Karbi Anglong being major producers.
Q: Name the chilli variety of Assam that received the GI tag along with being called 'King Chilli'.
A: Bhut Jolokia (Capsicum chinense), which received the Geographical Indication tag in 2008.
Q: What is the main objective of the 'Assam Agribusiness and Rural Transformation Project (APART)'?
A: To transform agriculture in Assam by improving market linkages, agribusiness and value addition for small and marginal farmers.
Q: Which central scheme provides financial assistance for the development of the horticulture sector across India, including Assam?
A: The Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH).
Q: What does the term APMC stand for in agricultural marketing?
A: Agricultural Produce Market Committee, which regulates agricultural markets in the state.
Q: True or False: Assam has a well-established network of APMCs in all district headquarters.
A: True. Assam has APMCs established at various market centres, with the Assam Agricultural Produce and Livestock Marketing (Promotion and Facilitation) Act governing them.
Q: Which organisation provides crop insurance coverage to farmers of Assam?
A: The Agriculture Insurance Company of India (AIC), under schemes like the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY).
Q: Which is the apex agricultural university of Assam?
A: Assam Agricultural University (AAU), located at Jorhat, established in 1969.
Q: Which variety of Assam's Ahu rice is known as a traditional short-duration variety?
A: Traditional Ahu varieties like 'Kola Ahu' and 'Lahi' are short-duration local varieties.
Q: Which annual cattle fair of Assam is also associated with the sale and trading of agricultural animals and goods?
A: The Jonbeel Mela, where traditional barter trade of local produce takes place.
Q: Which department of the Government of Assam is responsible for agriculture and farmer welfare?
A: The Department of Agriculture, assisted by the Directorate of Agriculture, with the Minister of Agriculture heading it.
Q: What is the area under paddy cultivation in Assam roughly as a percentage of the net sown area?
A: Around 70% of the net sown area of the state is under paddy cultivation.
Q: Which district of Assam is the leading producer of rice?
A: Dibrugarh and Nagaon districts are among the leading rice-producing districts of the state.
Q: Which scheme of the Government of India provides direct income support to small and marginal farmers, including those in Assam?
A: The Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN), which provides Rs 6,000 per year to eligible farmers.
Q: What is the main reason for the low productivity of agriculture in Assam?
A: Dependence on rain-fed farming, traditional cultivation methods, frequent floods, and small fragmented landholdings.
Q: Which of the following is a major vegetable crop grown in Assam: (a) Cauliflower, (b) Potato, (c) both?
A: Option (c). Both cauliflower and potato are major vegetable crops, with potato increasingly important in the kharif and rabi seasons.
Q: Which river island of Assam is known for its unique rice cultivation that survives annual floods?
A: Majuli island, where the indigenous Sali rice is grown using traditional flood-adaptive practices.
Q: Which government scheme provides free fertilisers and seeds to small farmers of Assam?
A: Schemes like the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Samman and the state's 'Chief Minister's Samagra Gramya Unnayan Yojana' components support input distribution to farmers.
Q: What are the three main rice crops grown in Assam?
A: Assam grows Ahu, Sali and Boro rice. Ahu is the autumn crop sown in May-June and harvested in August-September. Sali is the main winter crop sown in June-July and harvested in November-December. Boro is grown in low-lying areas with irrigation from November to May and harvested in summer.
Q: Which is the famous aromatic rice of Assam and where is it grown?
A: Joha is the famous aromatic short-grain rice of Assam. It is grown mainly in the upper Assam districts and is prized for its fragrance and taste. Ranjit is a separate high-yielding semi-dwarf Sali variety of the state.
Q: Which horticultural crops is Assam known for?
A: Assam is known for banana, which is the principal fruit, pineapple of the Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao hills, oranges of Tinsukia and the Karbi foothills, and spices such as ginger and turmeric. The Bhut Jolokia or King Chilli is the most famous, a GI-tagged chilli recognised as one of the world hottest.
Q: Which schemes help farmers in Assam?
A: PM-KISAN gives direct income support of Rs 6,000 per year to eligible farmers. Crop insurance is provided under PMFBY through the Agriculture Insurance Company of India, the MIDH supports horticulture, and the APART project improves market linkages and value addition for small and marginal farmers.
Q: Why is agricultural productivity in Assam low?
A: Agricultural productivity in Assam is low mainly because of dependence on rain-fed farming, traditional cultivation methods, frequent floods and erosion, and small fragmented landholdings. The seasonal nature of the monsoon and limited assured irrigation add to the problem.
Q: অসমত খেতি কৰা তিনিটা মূল ধান শস্য কি?
A: অসমে আহু, শালি আৰু বৰো ধান খেতি কৰে। আহু আহি শস্য মে'-জুনত সিঁচা আৰু আগষ্ট-ছেপ্টেম্বৰত দখা হয়। শালি মূল শীত শস্য জুন-জুলাইত সিঁচা আৰু নৱেম্বৰ-ডিচেম্বৰত দখা হয়। বৰো নিম্নভূমিত সেঁচৰে নৱেম্বৰৰ পৰা মে'লৈ খেতি কৰি গ্ৰীষ্মত দখা হয়।
Q: অসমৰ বিখ্যাত সুগন্ধি ধান কোনটো আৰু ক'ত খেতি হয়?
A: জহা অসমৰ বিখ্যাত সুগন্ধি চুটি দানা ধান। ই মুখ্যতঃ উজনি অসমৰ জিলাসমূহত খেতি হয় আৰু সুগন্ধি তথা সোৱাদৰ বাবে মূল্যৱান। ৰঞ্জিত ৰাজ্যখনৰ এটা পৃথক উচ্চ ফলনশীল অৰ্ধ-বামন শালি প্ৰজাতি।
Q: অসম কোনবোৰ উদ্যান শস্যৰ বাবে জনাজাত?
A: অসম কলৰ বাবে জনাজাত, যিটো মূল ফল, কাৰ্বি আংলং আৰু ডিমা হাছাও পাহাৰৰ আনাৰস, তিনিচুকীয়া আৰু কাৰ্বি পাদদেশৰ কমলা, আৰু আদা-হালধিৰ দৰে মছলাৰ বাবে জনাজাত। ভোট জলকীয়া বা ৰজা জলকীয়া আটাইতকৈ বিখ্যাত, বিশ্বৰ আটাইতকৈ উষ্ণ জলকীয়াসমূহৰ এটা হিচাপে স্বীকৃত GI টেগ পোৱা জলকীয়া।
Q: অসমত কৃষকসকলক কোনবোৰ আঁচনিয়ে সহায় কৰে?
A: PM-KISAN য়ে যোগ্য কৃষকসকলক বছৰি ৬,০০০ টকা পোনপটীয়া আয় সহায় দিয়ে। শস্য বীমা ভাৰত কৃষি বীমা কোম্পানীৰ জৰিয়তে PMFBY ৰ অধীনত প্ৰদান কৰা হয়, MIDH য়ে উদ্যান শস্যক সহায় কৰে, আৰু APART প্ৰকল্পই সৰু আৰু প্ৰান্তীয় কৃষকসকলৰ বাবে বজাৰ সংযোগ আৰু মূল্য সংযোজন উন্নত কৰে।
Q: অসমত কৃষি উৎপাদনশীলতা কম কিয়?
A: অসমত কৃষি উৎপাদনশীলতা কম হোৱাৰ মূল কাৰণ হৈছে বৰষুণনিৰ্ভৰ খেতি, পৰম্পৰাগত খেতি পদ্ধতি, বাৰে বাৰে হোৱা বান আৰু ক্ষয়, আৰু সৰু টুকুৰা মাটিৰ জোখ। বাৰিষাৰ ঋতুভিত্তিক প্ৰকৃতি আৰু সীমিত নিশ্চিত সেঁচে সমস্যাটো বঢ়ায়।

### Allied Activities (Fisheries, Forestry & Livestock)
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/assam-economy-sec/assam-allied-primary-activities/
Summary: Practice allied activities (fisheries, forestry & livestock) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free.
Q: What is the local name of the large natural water bodies (oxbow lakes) in Assam used for fisheries?
A: Beels, which are wetland water bodies formed by old river courses and extensively used for fish cultivation.
Q: Which is the largest beel (wetland) of Assam?
A: The Deepor Beel, located near Guwahati, which is a Ramsar site.
Q: Which beel of Assam is a Ramsar site and famous for hosting migratory birds?
A: Deepor Beel is a Ramsar site; other important wetlands include Urpad Beel, Sone Beel and Chandubi Beel.
Q: Which scheme of the Government of India provides financial assistance for the development of fisheries in Assam?
A: The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY).
Q: Which species of fish is the most important freshwater fish cultured in Assam's beels?
A: Rohu (Labeo rohita), along with Catla and Mrigal, are the major Indian major carps cultured in the state.
Q: Which fish species, known as the 'river dolphin's companion' name, is culturally significant in Assam and found in the Brahmaputra?
A: The Gangetic river dolphin is a mammal; the culturally significant fish is the Pabho/Putitor Mahseer. However, the Hilsa (Sillong) is the most cherished fish of Assam.
Q: What is the Assamese name of the Hilsa fish?
A: Sillong, which is highly prized in Assamese cuisine and comes from the sea via the Brahmaputra.
Q: What is the main economic use of the Deepor Beel besides fisheries?
A: It serves as a source of water supply, and it supports biodiversity, pisciculture and tourism-related livelihoods.
Q: What percentage of Assam's land area is covered by forest?
A: About 35-36% of the state's total geographical area is recorded as forest area, with a significant portion being reserved forests.
Q: Which forest type covers the largest area in Assam?
A: Tropical moist deciduous forests and tropical wet evergreen/semi-evergreen forests are the main natural forest types of the state.
Q: Which timber tree of Assam is prized for its use in construction and furniture?
A: Sal (Shorea robusta), Teak, and Hollong are major timber species; Hollong is the tallest tree and the state tree of Assam is Hollong (Dipterocarpus retusus).
Q: Which sanctuary of Assam is famous for the one-horned rhinoceros and is economically important for ecotourism?
A: Kaziranga National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is the main home of the one-horned rhinoceros.
Q: Which national park of Assam is home to the golden langur and is the largest river island forest?
A: Manas National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and Project Tiger reserve, is famous for the golden langur.
Q: Which wildlife sanctuary of Assam is the largest and famous for elephants and was historically a royal hunting ground?
A: The Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary is famous for rhinos, but the largest sanctuary is the Sonai-Rupai; historically, the Nameri National Park area was a royal hunting reserve.
Q: Which district of Assam has the highest livestock population?
A: Nagaon district has one of the highest livestock populations in the state.
Q: Which breed of cattle is native to Assam?
A: The Assam Hill cattle breed (also known as Nagaon or Dhubri local types) is the indigenous cattle breed of the state.
Q: True or False: Assam has a higher population of ducks than most other Indian states.
A: True. Assam has one of the largest duck populations in India, reflecting the importance of duck-rearing in its wetland economy.
Q: Which region of Assam is famous for pig rearing as a livelihood?
A: The tribal hill districts like Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao have high pig population, where pig rearing is a traditional occupation.
Q: Which central scheme aims at the development of the dairy sector in Assam?
A: The National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD) and the Dairy Processing & Infrastructure Development Fund (DIDF).
Q: Which cooperative dairy federation of Assam markets milk products under the 'Purabi' brand?
A: The Assam Cooperative Milk Producers' Federation Limited (WAMUL), which markets milk under the 'Purabi' brand.
Q: Where is the headquarters of WAMUL located?
A: At Guwahati (Pandu area), from where its processing plants operate.
Q: Which species of goat is the indigenous breed of Assam?
A: The Assam local (indigenous) goat breed, often improved with Beetal and Black Bengal crosses.
Q: Which wetland bird of Assam is of high economic importance for birdwatching tourism?
A: The Spot-billed Pelican and various migratory ducks and geese in beels like Deepor Beel attract birdwatchers.
Q: Which river dolphins found in the Brahmaputra are classified as an endangered aquatic species?
A: The Ganges river dolphin (Platanista gangetica), which is found in the Brahmaputra and is an endangered species.
Q: What is the main objective of the 'Assam State Aquaculture Mission'?
A: To boost fish production in the state through scientific aquaculture, seed production and farmer training.
Q: Which lake of Assam is famous for the annual Amur carp farming and recreational fishing?
A: Chandubi Lake, located near the Meghalaya border, supports aquaculture and is a tourist destination.
Q: Which department of the Government of Assam handles animal husbandry and veterinary services?
A: The Department of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary (AH&V), headed by the Minister of AH&V.
Q: Which of the following is the state fish of Assam?
A: The Ganges river dolphin is the state aquatic animal, while the state fish is the Pabho (Ompok pabda).
Q: Which animal is the state animal of Assam?
A: The one-horned rhinoceros (Rhinoceros unicornis) is the state animal of Assam.
Q: Which bird is the state bird of Assam?
A: The White-winged Wood Duck (Deo Hah) is the state bird of Assam.
Q: What is the contribution of the forestry sector to Assam's GSDP approximately?
A: The forestry sector contributes roughly 3-4% to Assam's GSDP, mostly through timber, bamboo, fuelwood and minor forest produce.
Q: Which minor forest produce of Assam is highly valued for its medicinal properties?
A: Agarwood (from the Agar tree) and various medicinal herbs are highly valued minor forest produces of Assam.
Q: Which sanctuary of Assam was the first to be declared a Tiger Reserve?
A: Manas National Park was declared a Tiger Reserve in 1973 under Project Tiger.
Q: Which wetland of Assam has been included in the Ramsar list besides Deepor Beel?
A: As of recent years, Urpad Beel (Bongaigaon) has also been declared a Ramsar site; more sites continue to be added.
Q: Which farming practice combining fish with rice is common in Assam's rural economy?
A: Rice-fish farming, where fish are cultured in paddy fields during the flooded season, boosting farmer income.
Q: What are beels and which is the largest beel of Assam?
A: Beels are large natural wetlands or oxbow lakes formed by old river courses, widely used for fish cultivation in Assam. The largest beel is Deepor Beel near Guwahati, which is a Ramsar site and is famous for migratory birds. Urpad Beel, Sone Beel and Chandubi Lake are other important wetlands.
Q: Which are the state symbols of Assam?
A: The one-horned rhinoceros is the state animal, the White-winged Wood Duck or Deo Hah is the state bird, the Hollong is the state tree, the Ganges river dolphin is the state aquatic animal, and the Pabho (Ompok pabda) is the state fish.
Q: How much forest area does Assam have and what does forestry contribute?
A: About 35 to 36 per cent of Assam's geographical area is recorded as forest area. The forestry sector contributes roughly 3 to 4 per cent of the state's GSDP, mainly through timber, bamboo, fuelwood and minor forest produce such as Agarwood and medicinal herbs.
Q: Which national parks of Assam are World Heritage Sites?
A: Kaziranga National Park, famous for the one-horned rhinoceros, and Manas National Park, famous for the golden langur and a Project Tiger reserve, are the two UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Assam. Manas was declared a Tiger Reserve in 1973.
Q: Which organisation markets milk products in Assam and under what brand?
A: The Assam Cooperative Milk Producers' Federation Limited, known as WAMUL, markets milk and milk products under the Purabi brand. Its headquarters is at Pandu in Guwahati, and dairy development is supported by NPDD and DIDF.
Q: বিল কি আৰু অসমৰ বৃহত্তম বিল কোনটো?
A: বিল হৈছে পুৰণি নদী পথৰ পৰা গঠিত বৃহৎ প্ৰাকৃতিক জলাভূমি বা অক্সবো হ্ৰদ, যিবোৰ অসমত মাছ চাষত বহুলভাৱে ব্যৱহৃত। বৃহত্তম বিল হৈছে গুৱাহাটীৰ ওচৰৰ দীপোৰ বিল, যিটো ৰামছাৰ সাইট আৰু পৰিভ্ৰমী চৰাইৰ বাবে বিখ্যাত। উৰ্পদ বিল, ছোন বিল আৰু চান্দুবি হ্ৰদ আন গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ জলাভূমি।
Q: অসমৰ ৰাজ্যিক প্ৰতীকসমূহ কি?
A: এক শিঙৰ গঁড় ৰাজ্যিক জন্তু, বগা ডেউকীয়া হাবি হাঁহ বা দেউ হাঁহ ৰাজ্যিক চৰাই, হোলোং ৰাজ্যিক গছ, গংগা নদী ডলফিন ৰাজ্যিক জলীয় জন্তু, আৰু পাভ (Ompok pabda) ৰাজ্যিক মাছ।
Q: অসমত কিমান বনাঞ্চল আছে আৰু বন খণ্ডই কিমান অৱদান আগবঢ়ায়?
A: অসমৰ ভৌগোলিক এলেকাৰ প্ৰায় ৩৫ ৰ পৰা ৩৬ শতাংশ বনাঞ্চল হিচাপে পঞ্জীভুক্ত। বন খণ্ডই ৰাজ্যখনৰ GSDP ত প্ৰায় ৩ ৰ পৰা ৪ শতাংশ অৱদান আগবঢ়ায়, মূলতঃ কাঠ, বাঁহ, জ্বালানী কাঠ আৰু আগৰু কাঠ তথা ঔষধি গছ-গছনিৰ দৰে সামান্য বনজ সম্পদৰ জৰিয়তে।
Q: অসমৰ কোনবোৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান বিশ্ব ঐতিহ্য স্থল?
A: এক শিঙৰ গঁড়ৰ বাবে বিখ্যাত কাজিৰঙা ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান আৰু সোণালী লাংগুৰ তথা প্ৰজেক্ট টাইগাৰ সংৰক্ষিত এলেকা হিচাপে বিখ্যাত মানস ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান অসমৰ দুটা ইউনেস্কো বিশ্ব ঐতিহ্য স্থল। মানসক ১৯৭৩ চনত টাইগাৰ ৰিজাৰ্ভ ঘোষণা কৰা হৈছিল।
Q: অসমত কোন সংস্থাই আৰু কি ব্ৰেণ্ডত দুগ্ধজাত সামগ্ৰী বিক্ৰী কৰে?
A: অসম সমবায় দুগ্ধ উৎপাদক ফেডাৰেচন লিমিটেড, WAMUL নামেৰে জনাজাত, পূৰবী ব্ৰেণ্ডত দুধ আৰু দুগ্ধজাত সামগ্ৰী বিক্ৰী কৰে। ইয়াৰ সদৰ কাৰ্যালয় গুৱাহাটীৰ পান্দুত, আৰু দুগ্ধ উন্নয়ন NPDD তথা DIDF য়ে সহায় কৰে।

### State Budget & Flagship Schemes — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/assam-economy-sec/assam-budget-flagship-schemes/
Summary: Practice state budget & flagship schemes questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What is the name of the flagship scheme of Assam that provides monthly financial assistance to poor women?
A: The Orunodoi scheme.
Q: What is the current monthly amount provided under the Orunodoi scheme?
A: Rs 1,000 per month, increased from the initial Rs 830.
Q: In which year was the Orunodoi scheme launched?
A: In December 2020.
Q: Who is the main target beneficiary of the Orunodoi scheme?
A: Women who are heads of economically weaker households.
Q: Kanaklata Mahila Sabalikaran Yojana is named after which freedom fighter?
A: Kanaklata Barua, who laid down her life while hoisting the national flag during the Quit India movement of 1942.
Q: Under which mission is the Kanaklata Mahila Sabalikaran Yojana implemented?
A: The Assam State Rural Livelihoods Mission (ASRLM).
Q: The Kanaklata Mahila Sabalikaran Yojana primarily organises rural women into what?
A: Self-Help Groups (SHGs).
Q: Which scheme provides interest-free loans to women Self-Help Groups in Assam?
A: The Vistarita Kanaklata Mahila Sabalikaran Yojana (extended KAMS).
Q: What is the full form of SVAYEM?
A: Swami Vivekananda Assam Youth Empowerment Scheme, a self-employment scheme for youth.
Q: SVAYEM provides financial support for what purpose?
A: To help educated unemployed youth set up micro-enterprises for self-employment.
Q: SVAYEM was launched in which year?
A: 2018.
Q: Pragyan Bharti Scheme of Assam provides what facility to economically weaker students?
A: Free education, including school fee reimbursement, in private schools.
Q: Pragyan Bharti Scheme is aimed at which group of students?
A: Meritorious students from economically weaker sections studying in private English-medium schools.
Q: Which Assam government scheme provides health insurance cover up to Rs 5 lakh for economically weaker families?
A: Atal Amrit Abhiyan.
Q: Atal Amrit Abhiyan was launched in which year?
A: 2018.
Q: Mukhya Mantri Lok Sewa Arogya Yojana provides health coverage to which group?
A: State government employees, pensioners and their dependents.
Q: Which schemes of Assam provide cashless treatment facilities to their beneficiaries?
A: Atal Amrit Abhiyan and Mukhya Mantri Lok Sewa Arogya Yojana both provide cashless treatment.
Q: Jyotisman Aru Arogya — the schemes of the Assam government bearing this name belong to which sector?
A: The health sector.
Q: Mission Basundhara is related to which subject?
A: Land rights — providing land pattas (records) to eligible landless people and digitising land records.
Q: Mission Basundhara was launched in which year?
A: 2021.
Q: What is the slogan or objective of Amrit Brikhya Andolan?
A: 'One family, one tree' — a mass tree plantation movement.
Q: Amrit Brikhya Andolan was launched in which year?
A: 2021.
Q: In Assam, schemes providing benefits to persons with disabilities (divyangjan) are run under which initiative?
A: The Deendayal Divyangjan initiative, such as assistance for aids and appliances for the disabled.
Q: Who presents the annual state budget of Assam?
A: The Finance Minister of Assam.
Q: Who was the Finance Minister of Assam who presented the 2024-25 budget?
A: Ajanta Neog.
Q: In which month is the Assam state budget usually presented?
A: February.
Q: What is the approximate gross size of the Assam state budget for 2024-25?
A: About Rs 2.99 lakh crore (gross), i.e., roughly Rs 3 lakh crore.
Q: In a state budget, the excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts is called what?
A: Revenue deficit.
Q: Expenditure that creates physical assets like roads and bridges is known as what?
A: Capital expenditure.
Q: Which Act regulates the fiscal discipline of the Assam state government?
A: The Assam Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2005.
Q: Which scheme of Assam provides a monthly financial incentive to girl students pursuing higher education?
A: The Nijut Moina scheme.
Q: Which of the following is a central government financial inclusion scheme implemented in Assam?
A: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY).
Q: True or False: The scheme providing land rights to the landless was later extended as Mission Basundhara 2.0 and 3.0.
A: True.
Q: 'Orunodoi' in the Assamese language literally means what?
A: The new dawn, i.e., the first light of the rising sun.
Q: Which of the following is a central scheme and NOT a state-specific Assam scheme?
A: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY).
Q: What is the Orunodoi scheme and how much does it provide?
A: The Orunodoi scheme, launched in December 2020, is a flagship Assam scheme that provides monthly financial assistance to poor women who are heads of economically weaker households. The amount was initially Rs 830 per month and was later increased to Rs 1,000 per month. In Assamese, 'Orunodoi' literally means the new dawn, or the first light of the rising sun.
Q: What is the Kanaklata Mahila Sabalikaran Yojana?
A: The Kanaklata Mahila Sabalikaran Yojana is implemented under the Assam State Rural Livelihoods Mission (ASRLM) and primarily organises rural women into Self-Help Groups (SHGs). It is named after the freedom fighter Kanaklata Barua, who laid down her life while hoisting the national flag during the Quit India movement of 1942. The Vistarita Kanaklata Mahila Sabalikaran Yojana provides interest-free loans to women's SHGs.
Q: Which Assam schemes provide health insurance to the needy?
A: The Atal Amrit Abhiyan, launched in 2018, provides health insurance cover up to Rs 5 lakh for economically weaker families, while the Mukhya Mantri Lok Sewa Arogya Yojana provides health coverage to state government employees, pensioners and their dependents. Both schemes offer cashless treatment facilities to their beneficiaries.
Q: What is the objective of Mission Basundhara?
A: Mission Basundhara, launched in 2021, is related to land rights. It provides land pattas (records) to eligible landless people and digitises land records, and it was later extended as Mission Basundhara 2.0 and 3.0. The Amrit Brikhya Andolan, also launched in 2021, is a mass tree plantation movement with the slogan 'one family, one tree'.
Q: Who presents the Assam state budget and what is its approximate size?
A: The annual state budget of Assam is presented by the Finance Minister; Ajanta Neog presented the 2024-25 budget, and budgets are usually presented in February. The gross size of the 2024-25 budget was about Rs 2.99 lakh crore. The fiscal discipline of the state is regulated by the Assam Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2005.
Q: ওৰুণোদই আঁচনি কি আৰু ই কিমান প্ৰদান কৰে?
A: ওৰুণোদই আঁচনি, ২০২০ চনৰ ডিচেম্বৰত আৰম্ভ, এটা পতাকা অসম আঁচনি যি আৰ্থনৈতিকভাৱে দুৰ্বল পৰিয়ালৰ মুৰব্বী দৰিদ্ৰ মহিলালৈ মাহেকীয়া আৰ্থিক সহায় প্ৰদান কৰে। প্ৰাৰম্ভিক ধন মাহেকত ৮৩০ টকা আছিল আৰু পিছত মাহেকত ১,০০০ টকালৈ বৃদ্ধি কৰা হৈছিল। অসমীয়াত, 'ওৰুণোদই' ৰ আক্ষৰিক অৰ্থ নতুন পুৱা, বা উদয় হওঁতে সূৰ্যৰ প্ৰথম পোহৰ।
Q: কনকলতা মহিলা সবলীকৰণ যোজনা কি?
A: কনকলতা মহিলা সবলীকৰণ যোজনা অসম ৰাজ্যিক গ্ৰাম্য জীৱিকা মিছন (ASRLM) ৰ অধীনত ৰূপায়িত হয় আৰু মূলতঃ গ্ৰাম্য মহিলাক স্ব-সহায়ক গোট (SHG) ত সংগঠিত কৰে। ই স্বাধীনতা সংগ্ৰামী কনকলতা বৰুৱাৰ নামেৰে নামকৰণ কৰা হৈছে, যিয়ে ১৯৪২ চনৰ ভাৰত ত্যাগ আন্দোলনত ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় পতাকা উত্তোলন কৰি প্ৰাণ আহুতি দিছিল। বিিস্তাৰিতা কনকলতা মহিলা সবলীকৰণ যোজনাই মহিলা SHG লৈ সুদমুক্ত ঋণ প্ৰদান কৰে।
Q: কোন অসম আঁচনিয়ে অভাৱী লোকলৈ স্বাস্থ্য বীমা প্ৰদান কৰে?
A: অতল অমৃত অভিযান, ২০১৮ চনত আৰম্ভ, আৰ্থনৈতিকভাৱে দুৰ্বল পৰিয়াললৈ ৫ লাখ টকালৈ স্বাস্থ্য বীমা কভাৰ প্ৰদান কৰে, আনহাতে মুখ্যমন্ত্ৰী লোক সেৱা আৰোগ্য যোজনাই ৰাজ্য চৰকাৰৰ কৰ্মচাৰী, পেঞ্চনাৰ আৰু তেওঁলোকৰ নিৰ্ভৰশীলসকলক স্বাস্থ্য কভাৰ প্ৰদান কৰে। দুয়োখন আঁচনিয়ে হিতাধিকাৰীসকলক নগদমুক্ত চিকিৎসা সুবিধা দিয়ে।
Q: মিছন বাসুন্ধৰাৰ উদ্দেশ্য কি?
A: মিছন বাসুন্ধৰা, ২০২১ চনত আৰম্ভ, ভূমি অধিকাৰৰ সৈতে সম্পৰ্কিত। ই যোগ্য ভূমিহীন লোকলৈ ভূমি পাট্টা (নথি) প্ৰদান কৰে আৰু ভূমি নথি ডিজিটেল কৰে, আৰু পিছত ইয়াক মিছন বাসুন্ধৰা ২.০ আৰু ৩.০ লৈ সম্প্ৰসাৰিত কৰা হৈছিল। অমৃত বিক্ষ্য আন্দোলন, ২০২১ চনত আৰম্ভ, 'এক পৰিয়াল, এক গছ' স্লোগানৰে এক গণ গছ ৰোপণ আন্দোলন।
Q: অসম ৰাজ্যিক বাজেট কোনে উপস্থাপন কৰে আৰু ইয়াৰ প্ৰায় আকাৰ কিমান?
A: অসমৰ বছৰেকীয়া ৰাজ্যিক বাজেট বিত্ত মন্ত্ৰীয়ে উপস্থাপন কৰে; অজন্তা নেওগে ২০২৪-২৫ বাজেট উপস্থাপন কৰিছিল, আৰু বাজেটসমূহ সাধাৰণতে ফেব্ৰুৱাৰীত উপস্থাপন কৰা হয়। ২০২৪-২৫ বাজেটৰ মুঠ আকাৰ প্ৰায় ২.৯৯ লাখ কোটি টকা। ৰাজ্যখনৰ বিত্তীয় শৃংখলা অসম বিত্তীয় দায়বদ্ধতা আৰু বাজেট ব্যৱস্থাপনা (FRBM) আইন, ২০০৫ ৰ জৰিয়তে নিয়ন্ত্ৰিত হয়।

### Floods, Erosion & Ecological Impact — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/assam-economy-sec/assam-floods-erosion-ecology/
Summary: Practice floods, erosion & ecological impact questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Which river is the main cause of annual floods in Assam?
A: The Brahmaputra and its tributaries.
Q: Approximately what percentage of Assam's total area is flood-prone?
A: About 40% of the state's area.
Q: When did the systematic construction of embankments begin in Assam?
A: After the devastating floods of 1954, which followed the great 1950 earthquake.
Q: Which body was constituted in 1980 for flood control in the Brahmaputra valley?
A: The Brahmaputra Board.
Q: Where is the headquarters of the Brahmaputra Board located?
A: Guwahati.
Q: Majuli, the world's largest river island, is shrinking mainly due to what?
A: River erosion (bank cutting) by the Brahmaputra.
Q: What are 'chars' in the context of the Brahmaputra river?
A: Sandbars or silt islands that form in the river and are inhabited by people.
Q: The 1950 Great Assam Earthquake changed the course of which river?
A: The Brahmaputra and its tributaries.
Q: What is the main purpose of the embankments built along the Brahmaputra?
A: To contain flood waters and protect human habitation and farmland.
Q: Floods in Assam cause major damage to which sector of the economy?
A: Agriculture, as standing crops are destroyed every year.
Q: When the Brahmaputra floods, what is the main threat to Kaziranga National Park?
A: Flooding submerges the grasslands, forcing animals like rhinos to migrate to higher ground, and many die in the process.
Q: True or False: During Kaziranga floods, the highway NH-27 (formerly NH-37) turns into a death trap for animals fleeing the water.
A: True. Animals fleeing the floods are often hit by vehicles on the highway.
Q: Which wetland near Guwahati is the only Ramsar Site in Assam?
A: Deepor Beel.
Q: In which year was Deepor Beel declared a Ramsar site?
A: 2002.
Q: The Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA) was established under which Act?
A: The Disaster Management Act, 2005.
Q: The National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) was established in which year?
A: 2006.
Q: Which NDRF battalion is located at Patgaon, Guwahati?
A: The 1st Battalion of the NDRF.
Q: Which of the following is a major cause of erosion in Assam?
A: All of the above — deforestation, the high sediment load of the rivers and shifting river courses.
Q: The Brahmaputra is known by which name in Tibet?
A: Tsangpo (Yarlung Tsangpo).
Q: The Brahmaputra enters Bangladesh under which name?
A: Jamuna.
Q: National Waterway 2 in India is on which river?
A: The Brahmaputra, from Dhubri to Sadiya.
Q: Climate change is likely to make Assam's floods how?
A: More frequent and more intense.
Q: Wetlands in Assam are important for which of the following functions?
A: All of the above — flood regulation, groundwater recharge, biodiversity and livelihoods.
Q: Which body manages disaster response at the district level in Assam?
A: The District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA).
Q: True or False: The area of Majuli has reduced significantly over the decades due to river erosion.
A: True. Majuli has lost a large part of its area to erosion by the Brahmaputra.
Q: What is the state-level response force of Assam for disasters called?
A: The State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), Assam.
Q: Floods in Assam mainly occur during which season?
A: The monsoon season (June to September), especially in July and August.
Q: The Barak river causes floods in which valley of Assam?
A: The Barak valley in southern Assam (Cachar region).
Q: What is the main human-induced factor that worsens floods and erosion in Assam?
A: Deforestation and encroachment on wetlands and riverbeds.
Q: The area of Kaziranga National Park is flooded by which river?
A: The Brahmaputra, as the park lies on its southern bank.
Q: Which of the following is an anti-erosion measure commonly used in Assam?
A: All of the above — concrete spurs with boulders, geo-bags, and bio-engineering such as planting vetiver grass.
Q: Which organisation prepares the master plan for the Brahmaputra basin?
A: The Brahmaputra Board.
Q: True or False: Severe floods in Assam can affect more than one crore people.
A: True. In extreme flood years, over one crore people have been affected in Assam.
Q: Which major river carries a very high sediment load, a key factor in Assam's erosion problems?
A: The Brahmaputra, one of the highest sediment-carrying rivers in the world.
Q: Which forces are deployed for rescue and relief operations during major floods in Assam?
A: The NDRF, along with the SDRF, the Army and central paramilitary forces.
Q: What causes the annual floods in Assam and how much area is flood-prone?
A: The Brahmaputra and its numerous tributaries are the main cause of annual floods in Assam. About 40 per cent of the state's area is flood-prone, and floods occur mainly during the monsoon season from June to September, especially in July and August. The Barak river floods the Barak valley in southern Assam.
Q: Why is Majuli shrinking and what are chars?
A: Majuli, the largest river island in the world, is shrinking mainly because of river erosion and bank cutting by the Brahmaputra; it has lost a large part of its area over the decades. Chars are sandbars or silt islands that form in the river and are inhabited by people who are especially vulnerable to floods and erosion.
Q: Which is the only Ramsar site in Assam and when was it declared?
A: Deepor Beel, a wetland near Guwahati, is the only Ramsar site in Assam and was declared in 2002. Wetlands perform vital functions such as flood regulation, groundwater recharge, biodiversity support and livelihoods, and are important for flood control.
Q: Which institutions manage disasters and flood control in Assam?
A: The Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA) was established under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, and District Disaster Management Authorities manage district-level response. The State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) Assam and the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF, established 2006, with its 1st Battalion at Patgaon in Guwahati) carry out rescue operations. The Brahmaputra Board, constituted in 1980 with headquarters at Guwahati, prepares the master plan for the Brahmaputra basin.
Q: What is the ecological impact of floods on Kaziranga?
A: During floods in Kaziranga National Park, which lies on the southern bank of the Brahmaputra, the grasslands are submerged and animals such as rhinos are forced to migrate to higher ground, and many die in the process. The highway NH-27 (formerly NH-37) turns into a death trap for animals fleeing the water as they are often hit by vehicles.
Q: অসমত বছৰেকীয়া বানপানীৰ কাৰণ কি আৰু কিমান এলাকা বান-প্ৰৱণ?
A: ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ আৰু ইয়াৰ অসংখ্য উপনদী অসমত বছৰেকীয়া বানপানীৰ মূল কাৰণ। ৰাজ্যখনৰ প্ৰায় ৪০ শতাংশ এলাকা বান-প্ৰৱণ, আৰু বানপানী মূলতঃ জুনৰ পৰা ছেপ্তেম্বৰলৈ বৰ্ষাকালত হয়, বিশেষকৈ জুলাই আৰু আগষ্টত। বৰাক নদীয়ে দক্ষিণ অসমৰ বৰাক উপত্যকাত বানপানী কৰে।
Q: মাজুলী কিয় সংকুচিত হৈছে আৰু চৰ কি?
A: মাজুলী, বিশ্বৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ নদী দ্বীপ, ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰৰ নদী খহনীয়া আৰু পাৰ কটাৰ বাবে মূলতঃ সংকুচিত হৈছে; ই দশকজুৰি ইয়াৰ এটা ডাঙৰ অংশ হেৰুৱাইছে। চৰ হৈছে বালি বা পলসৰ দ্বীপ যিবোৰ নদীত গঠন হয় আৰু বানপানী তথা খহনীয়াৰ প্ৰতি বিশেষভাৱে অসুৰক্ষিত মানুহৰ দ্বাৰা বসবাস কৰা হয়।
Q: অসমৰ একমাত্ৰ ৰামছাৰ স্থল কোনটো আৰু কেতিয়া ঘোষণা কৰা হৈছিল?
A: গুৱাহাটীৰ ওচৰৰ দীপোৰ বিল অসমৰ একমাত্ৰ ৰামছাৰ স্থল আৰু ২০০২ চনত ঘোষণা কৰা হৈছিল। জলাভূমিয়ে বান নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ, ভূগৰ্ভস্থ জল পুনৰ্ভৰণ, জৈৱবৈচিত্ৰ্য সমৰ্থন আৰু জীৱিকাৰ দৰে অত্যাৱশ্যকীয় কাৰ্য সম্পন্ন কৰে, আৰু বান নিয়ন্ত্ৰণৰ বাবে গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ।
Q: অসমত দুৰ্যোগ আৰু বান নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ কোনবোৰ প্ৰতিষ্ঠানে পৰিচালনা কৰে?
A: অসম ৰাজ্যিক দুৰ্যোগ ব্যৱস্থাপনা প্ৰাধিকৰণ (ASDMA) দুৰ্যোগ ব্যৱস্থাপনা আইন, ২০০৫ ৰ অধীনত প্ৰতিষ্ঠিত হৈছিল, আৰু জিলা দুৰ্যোগ ব্যৱস্থাপনা প্ৰাধিকৰণে জিলা পৰ্যায়ৰ সঁহাৰি পৰিচালনা কৰে। ৰাজ্যিক দুৰ্যোগ সঁহাৰি বাহিনী (SDRF) অসম আৰু ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় দুৰ্যোগ সঁহাৰি বাহিনী (NDRF, ২০০৬ চনত প্ৰতিষ্ঠিত, ১ম বেটেলিয়ন গুৱাহাটীৰ পাটগাঁৱত) য়ে উদ্ধাৰ অভিযান চলায়। ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ ব'ৰ্ড, ১৯৮০ চনত গঠিত আৰু গুৱাহাটীত সদৰ, য়ে ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ বেছিনৰ মূল পৰিকল্পনা প্ৰস্তুত কৰে।
Q: কাজিৰঙাত বানপানীৰ পৰিৱেশ প্ৰভাৱ কি?
A: কাজিৰঙা ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যানত, যি ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰৰ দক্ষিণ পাৰত অৱস্থিত, বানপানীৰ সময়ত ঘাঁহনি ডুব যায় আৰু গঁড়ৰ দৰে জন্তুক উঁচু ঠাইলৈ স্থানান্তৰিত হ'বলৈ বাধ্য কৰায়, আৰু বহুতে এই প্ৰক্ৰিয়াত প্ৰাণ হেৰুৱায়। মহাসড়ক NH-27 (পূৰ্বতে NH-37) পানীৰ পৰা পলোৱা জন্তুৰ বাবে মৃত্যুফান্দলৈ ৰূপান্তৰিত হয় কাৰণ সিহঁত প্ৰায়ে বাহনৰ খুন্দাত পৰে।

### Growth Metrics & Demography — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/assam-economy-sec/assam-macro-profile-demographics/
Summary: Practice growth metrics & demography questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What is the full form of GSDP?
A: Gross State Domestic Product. It is the total monetary value of all goods and services produced within the state in a given year.
Q: Which indicator measures the total income produced within the geographical boundary of Assam?
A: Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP). It includes the income earned by all residents and non-residents within the state's boundaries.
Q: NSDP stands for ______.
A: Net State Domestic Product. It is obtained by subtracting the depreciation of fixed capital from GSDP.
Q: Which ministry of the Government of India releases the official estimates of GSDP of Assam?
A: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) through the National Accounts Division.
Q: True or False: GSDP of Assam is measured at both current prices and constant prices.
A: True. Current prices reflect the prevailing market rates while constant prices use a base year to remove the effect of inflation.
Q: Per capita income of a state is calculated by dividing which two figures?
A: It is calculated by dividing NSDP (or GSDP) by the mid-year estimated population of the state.
Q: Which state ranks first in India in terms of per capita income among major states, with Assam well below the national average?
A: Goa (or Sikkim in smaller states). Assam's per capita income has historically remained below the national average.
Q: Which sector contributes the highest share to Assam's GSDP?
A: The tertiary (services) sector contributes the highest share, followed by the primary and secondary sectors.
Q: Assam's economy is largely characterised as a mixed economy with a strong base in which sector?
A: The primary sector, particularly agriculture and allied activities, which employs a large share of the workforce.
Q: According to the Census of India 2011, what was the population of Assam?
A: Approximately 3.12 crore (31.2 million) people as per the 2011 Census.
Q: Which census recorded the first population count of Assam in the modern sense?
A: The Census of 1872 (the first all-India census), conducted during the British period.
Q: What is the population density of Assam as per the 2011 Census (persons per sq km)?
A: 397 persons per square kilometre, which is higher than the national average of 382.
Q: Which district of Assam recorded the highest population density in the 2011 Census?
A: Kamrup Metropolitan district, which includes Guwahati city.
Q: What was the sex ratio (females per 1000 males) of Assam as per the 2011 Census?
A: 954 females per 1000 males, higher than the national average of 943.
Q: What is the literacy rate of Assam as per the 2011 Census?
A: 72.19%, which is below the national average of 74.04%. Male literacy is 77.85% and female literacy is 66.27%.
Q: Which district of Assam recorded the highest literacy rate in the 2011 Census?
A: Kamrup Metropolitan district with around 88.66% literacy rate.
Q: Which district of Assam recorded the lowest literacy rate in the 2011 Census?
A: Dhubri district, with a literacy rate of about 58.34%.
Q: True or False: Assam has a higher urbanisation rate than the national average.
A: False. Assam's urbanisation rate (about 14.08% in 2011) is much lower than the national average of 31.16%.
Q: What is the name of the largest urban agglomeration of Assam?
A: Guwahati (Guwahati Urban Agglomeration), which is the largest city and commercial hub of the state.
Q: How many districts did Assam have at the time of the 2011 Census?
A: 27 districts at the time of the 2011 Census; subsequently the number has been increased to 35.
Q: Which is the most populous district of Assam as per the 2011 Census?
A: Nagaon district, followed by Dhubri and Kamrup (Rural).
Q: Which is the least populous district of Assam as per the 2011 Census?
A: Hailakandi district among the then-existing districts; among new ones, South Salmara is very small.
Q: What is the decadal population growth rate of Assam between 2001 and 2011?
A: About 16.93%, which was slightly higher than the national decadal growth of 17.64% during the same period.
Q: In which census decade did Assam record its highest ever decadal population growth rate?
A: The decade 1971-1981, largely attributed to large-scale migration during the Bangladesh Liberation War period.
Q: According to the 2011 Census, what percentage of Assam's population lives in rural areas?
A: About 85.92% of the population lives in rural areas and only about 14.08% in urban areas.
Q: Which are the two most populous urban areas of Assam after Guwahati?
A: Silchar and Dibrugarh are the second and third most populous urban centres of the state.
Q: Which tribal community is the largest in Assam in terms of population?
A: The Bodo community, which is the largest plains tribal community of Assam.
Q: The Demographic Trends report of Assam has historically shown a higher proportion of which religious group compared to the national average?
A: The proportion of Muslims in Assam is higher than the national average, with a significant share of the total population.
Q: Which city is projected to be the primary driver of urban growth in Assam in demographic projections?
A: Guwahati, which is expected to continue growing rapidly as the region's biggest urban centre.
Q: In the new district reorganisation, how many total districts does Assam currently have (as of 2023-24)?
A: Assam now has 35 districts after the creation of new districts in 2023.
Q: Which of the following best describes Assam's demographic transition as per recent trends: (a) high birth rate and high death rate, (b) declining fertility and rising life expectancy, (c) negative growth?
A: Option (b). Assam is experiencing declining fertility rates and rising life expectancy, indicating a maturing demographic transition.
Q: Which organisation conducts the decennial census of India, whose data forms the base for Assam's demographic statistics?
A: The Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
Q: Which district has the lowest population density in Assam as per the 2011 Census?
A: Karbi Anglong district among the then-existing districts, owing to its hilly terrain.
Q: True or False: The female literacy rate of Assam is higher than the national female literacy rate.
A: True. Assam's female literacy rate (66.27%) is slightly higher than the national female literacy rate of 65.46%.
Q: What is the main reason for the low urbanisation rate of Assam compared to all-India?
A: The predominantly agrarian economy with dispersed rural settlements and fewer large industrial towns.
Q: What is the difference between GSDP and NSDP?
A: GSDP is the total money value of all goods and services produced within the geographical boundary of Assam in a year. NSDP is obtained by deducting the depreciation of fixed capital from GSDP. GSDP is estimated at current prices and at constant prices, while NSDP is used to calculate per capita income.
Q: How is per capita income of Assam calculated?
A: Per capita income is calculated by dividing the Net State Domestic Product (or GSDP) by the mid-year estimated population of the state. It is the standard measure used to compare the standard of living of one state with another, and Assam's per capita income has historically remained below the national average.
Q: Which sector contributes the highest share to Assam GSDP and which sector employs the most people?
A: The tertiary or services sector contributes the highest share to Assam GSDP, followed by the primary and secondary sectors. However, in terms of employment, the primary sector, particularly agriculture and allied activities, supports the largest share of the workforce.
Q: What are the key demographic figures of Assam as per the 2011 Census?
A: As per the 2011 Census, Assam had a population of about 3.12 crore, a density of 397 persons per square kilometre and a sex ratio of 954 females per 1000 males. The literacy rate was 72.19 per cent, with male literacy at 77.85 per cent and female literacy at 66.27 per cent.
Q: Why is the urbanisation rate of Assam lower than the national average?
A: Assam's urbanisation rate was only about 14.08 per cent against the national average of 31.16 per cent. The main reason is the predominantly agrarian economy with dispersed rural settlements and very few large industrial towns, which keeps a very large share of the population in rural areas.
Q: GSDP আৰু NSDP ৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: GSDP হৈছে এটা বছৰত অসমৰ ভৌগোলিক সীমাৰ ভিতৰত উৎপাদিত সকলো সামগ্ৰী আৰু সেৱাৰ মুঠ আৰ্থিক মূল্য। NSDP GSDP ৰ পৰা স্থিৰ মূলধনৰ হ্ৰাস বাদ দি পোৱা যায়। GSDP বৰ্তমান মূল্য আৰু ধ্ৰুৱক মূল্য দুয়োটাতে অনুমান কৰা হয়, আনহাতে NSDP মূৰ পিছাকৈ আয় গণনা কৰিবলৈ ব্যৱহাৰ হয়।
Q: অসমৰ মূৰ পিছাকৈ আয় কেনেকৈ গণনা কৰা হয়?
A: মূৰ পিছাকৈ আয় নিকা ৰাজ্যিক দেশজ উৎপাদন (বা GSDP) ক ৰাজ্যখনৰ মধ্য-বছৰ অনুমানিক জনসংখ্যাৰ দ্বাৰা ভাগ কৰি গণনা কৰা হয়। এখন ৰাজ্যৰ জীৱনযাত্ৰাৰ স্তৰ আন এখনৰ সৈতে তুলনা কৰিবলৈ এইটোৱেই মানক মাপ, আৰু অসমৰ মূৰ পিছাকৈ আয় ঐতিহাসিকভাৱে ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় গড়তকৈ তলত থাকে।
Q: অসমৰ GSDP ত কোনটো খণ্ডই সৰ্বাধিক অংশ আগবঢ়ায় আৰু কোনটো খণ্ডই সৰ্বাধিক লোকক নিয়োজিত কৰে?
A: তৃতীয় বা সেৱা খণ্ডই অসমৰ GSDP ত সৰ্বাধিক অংশ আগবঢ়ায়, তাৰ পিছতে প্ৰাথমিক আৰু দ্বিতীয় খণ্ড। কিন্তু নিয়োগৰ ক্ষেত্ৰত প্ৰাথমিক খণ্ড, বিশেষকৈ কৃষি আৰু সংশ্লিষ্ট কাৰ্য্যকলাপে আটাইতকৈ বেছি শ্ৰমিক শক্তি ধৰি ৰাখে।
Q: ২০১১ লোকপিয়ল অনুসৰি অসমৰ মূল জনসংখ্যাগত তথ্য কি?
A: ২০১১ লোকপিয়ল অনুসৰি অসমৰ জনসংখ্যা প্ৰায় ৩.১২ কোটি, ঘনত্ব প্ৰতি বৰ্গ কিলোমিটাৰত ৩৯৭ জন আৰু লিংগ অনুপাত প্ৰতি ১০০০ পুৰুষত ৯৫৪ গৰাকী মহিলা আছিল। সাক্ষৰতাৰ হাৰ ৭২.১৯ শতাংশ, পুৰুষ সাক্ষৰতা ৭৭.৮৫ শতাংশ আৰু মহিলা সাক্ষৰতা ৬৬.২৭ শতাংশ আছিল।
Q: অসমৰ নগৰীয়াকৰণৰ হাৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় গড়তকৈ কম কিয়?
A: অসমৰ নগৰীয়াকৰণৰ হাৰ মাত্ৰ প্ৰায় ১৪.০৮ শতাংশ আছিল, ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় গড় ৩১.১৬ শতাংশৰ বিপৰীতে। মূল কাৰণ হৈছে বিক্ষিপ্ত গ্ৰাম্য বসতি আৰু অতি কম সংখ্যক বৃহৎ শিল্প নগৰসহ প্ৰধানকৈ কৃষিভিত্তিক অৰ্থনীতি, যিয়ে জনসংখ্যাৰ অতি বৃহৎ অংশ গ্ৰাম্য অঞ্চলত ৰাখে।

### Manufacturing, MSME & Handloom — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/assam-economy-sec/assam-manufacturing-msme-handloom/
Summary: Practice manufacturing, msme & handloom questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Which is the premier state agency for industrial development in Assam?
A: The Assam Industrial Development Corporation (AIDC) is the premier agency for industrial development.
Q: When was the Assam Industrial Development Corporation (AIDC) established?
A: AIDC was established in 1962 to promote industrial development in Assam.
Q: What is the primary role of AIDC in the industrial sector?
A: AIDC provides term loans, equity participation and financial assistance to medium and large industries.
Q: Which scheme promotes micro and small enterprises in Assam through financial support?
A: The PMEGP (Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme) promotes micro and small enterprises with subsidy.
Q: Which handloom village of Assam is known as the 'Manchester of Assam' for silk weaving?
A: Sualkuchi in Kamrup district is known as the 'Manchester of Assam' for its silk weaving industry.
Q: Which type of silk produced in Assam is the rarest and unique in the world?
A: Muga silk, produced only in Assam, is the rarest and unique golden-coloured silk in the world.
Q: Which is the most widely produced silk in Assam?
A: Eri silk is the most widely produced silk in Assam, mostly spun from castor-fed eri worms.
Q: Which silk is also called 'Endi' or 'Errandi' silk in Assam?
A: Eri silk is also known as 'Endi' or 'Errandi' silk in Assam.
Q: Which variety of mulberry silk is produced in Assam?
A: The 'Pat' (mulberry) silk variety is produced in Assam, mainly in Kamrup and adjacent areas.
Q: Which government body promotes sericulture and handloom development in Assam?
A: The Directorate of Sericulture and the Directorate of Handloom and Textiles promote these sectors in Assam.
Q: Which organisation is the apex agency for sericulture development in India?
A: The Central Silk Board (CSB) is the apex agency for sericulture development in India.
Q: Which traditional Assamese handloom product is an inseparable part of Assamese culture?
A: The Gamosa, a white rectangular cotton cloth with red borders, is an inseparable part of Assamese culture.
Q: Which fabric is used to make the traditional Assamese 'Mekhela Chador'?
A: The Mekhela Chador is traditionally woven from mulberry (pat) or muga silk.
Q: Which scheme provides financial assistance to handloom weavers in Assam?
A: Schemes like the National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP) and Yarn Supply Scheme assist weavers.
Q: What is the approximate number of handloom weavers in Assam?
A: Assam has over 12 lakh handloom weavers, making it one of the largest handloom states in India.
Q: Which is the major industrial estate of Assam located near Guwahati?
A: The Amingaon Industrial Estate near Guwahati is a major industrial estate in Assam.
Q: Which agency develops industrial areas and estates in Assam?
A: The Assam Small Industries Development Corporation (ASIDC) develops industrial estates and areas.
Q: Which Assam government scheme provides seed capital to young entrepreneurs?
A: The Swami Vivekananda Assam Youth Empowerment Scheme (SVAYEM) provides seed capital to young entrepreneurs.
Q: What is the full form of the scheme PMEGP?
A: PMEGP stands for Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme.
Q: Which organization implements PMEGP in Assam?
A: The KVIC (Khadi and Village Industries Commission) and state KVIB implement PMEGP.
Q: Which Assam-based refinery company was set up as a subsidiary of OIL?
A: Numaligarh Refinery Limited (NRL) was set up as a subsidiary of Oil India Limited.
Q: Which fertilizer plant of Assam is located at Namrup?
A: The Brahmaputra Valley Fertilizer Corporation (BVFCL) plant is located at Namrup.
Q: Which cement plant is located at Bokajan in Assam?
A: The Cement Corporation of India (CCI) plant is located at Bokajan in Karbi Anglong.
Q: What is the major jute processing centre of Assam?
A: The jute mills are mainly located in the Barak valley, especially around Silchar and Karimganj.
Q: Which industrial policy of Assam was launched in 2019?
A: The Assam Industrial Policy 2019 was launched to promote investment and industrial growth.
Q: Which scheme of Assam offers incentives for setting up new industrial units?
A: The Assam Industrial Policy 2019 provides incentives like capital subsidy, interest subsidy and power subsidy.
Q: Which industry is the largest agro-based industry in Assam?
A: The tea industry is the largest agro-based industry in Assam.
Q: What is the role of the Assam State Co-operative Marketing Society (ASCM) in the economy?
A: ASCM markets agricultural and co-operative products, facilitating trade for farmers.
Q: Which bamboo-based industry is being promoted under the North East bamboo policy?
A: Bamboo furniture, handicrafts, flooring and bamboo shoot processing industries are being promoted.
Q: Which organisation provides financial support to MSMEs in Assam?
A: The Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) and state financial corporations support MSMEs.
Q: What is the target of the 'Make in Assam' initiative?
A: The 'Make in Assam' initiative aims to boost local manufacturing and attract investment in the state.
Q: Which Assam textile park was approved for muga silk processing?
A: The proposed Assam Silk Textile Park aims to develop the muga and eri silk value chain.
Q: Which agency is responsible for skill development for industry in Assam?
