Shareholders are owners, whereas debenture holders are creditors of the company.
Q: What are depositories and what is DEMAT form?
A: A depository holds securities in electronic form on behalf of investors, in the same way that a bank holds money. India has two main depositories, the National Securities Depository Limited and the Central Depository Services Limited, and NSDL was the first. When securities are held electronically they are said to be in dematerialised, or DEMAT, form, which is safer and easier to transfer than physical certificates.
Q: মুদ্ৰা বজাৰ আৰু মূলধন বজাৰৰ পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: মুদ্ৰা বজাৰে চুটি-ম্যাদী ধনৰ, সাধাৰণতে এবছৰলৈকে, লেনদেন কৰে, আৰু ইয়াৰ আহিলাত ট্ৰেজাৰী বিল, কল মানি, ৰেপো, বাণিজ্যিক পে'পাৰ আৰু আমানত প্ৰমাণপত্ৰ অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত। মূলধন বজাৰে দীৰ্ঘম্যাদী ধনৰ লেনদেন কৰে আৰু ইয়াৰ আহিলাত শ্বেয়াৰ, ডিবেঞ্চাৰ আৰু বণ্ড অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত। মুদ্ৰা বজাৰ ভাৰতীয় ৰিজাৰ্ভ বেংকে আৰু মূলধন বজাৰ SEBI য়ে নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ কৰে।
Q: ভাৰতীয় ছিকিউৰিটিজ বজাৰত SEBI ৰ ভূমিকা কি?
A: ভাৰতীয় ছিকিউৰিটিজ আৰু এক্সচেঞ্জ ব’ৰ্ড (SEBI) য়ে বিনিয়োগকাৰীসকলৰ স্বাৰ্থ সুৰক্ষা কৰে, ছিকিউৰিটিজ বজাৰৰ উন্নয়ন প্ৰসাৰ কৰে আৰু বজাৰ তথা ইয়াৰ মধ্যস্থতাকাৰীসকলক নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ কৰে। ই ১৯৮৮ চনত প্ৰতিষ্ঠা আৰু ১৯৯২ চনত বিধিবদ্ধ ক্ষমতা লাভ কৰিছিল। ই ষ্টক এক্সচেঞ্জ, দালাল, মিউচুৱেল ফাণ্ড, ডিপজিটৰি আৰু বিদেশী পৰ্টফলিঅ বিনিয়োগ নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ কৰে আৰু ইনচাইডাৰ ট্ৰেডিংৰ দৰে অনুচিত কাৰ্যৰ বিৰুদ্ধে ব্যৱস্থা লয়।
Q: প্ৰাথমিক বজাৰ আৰু গৌণ বজাৰৰ পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: প্ৰাথমিক বজাৰ হৈছে য'ত ছিকিউৰিটি প্ৰথমবাৰৰ বাবে জাৰি কৰা হয় আৰু কোম্পানীয়ে সংগ্ৰহ কৰা ধন পায়, যেনে প্ৰাথমিক ৰাজহুৱা প্ৰস্তাৱত। গৌণ বজাৰ হৈছে য'ত ইতিমধ্যে জাৰি কৰা ছিকিউৰিটি বিনিয়োগকাৰীসকলৰ মাজত বাণিজ্য কৰা হয়, যেনে ষ্টক এক্সচেঞ্জত। প্ৰাথমিক বজাৰে সঞ্চয় উদ্যোগলৈ পৰিচালিত কৰে, আনহাতে গৌণ বজাৰে বিনিয়োগকাৰীক তৰলতা দিয়ে।
Q: শ্বেয়াৰ আৰু ডিবেঞ্চাৰৰ পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: শ্বেয়াৰে কোম্পানীত মালিকীস্বত্ব সূচায় আৰু ধাৰকক লাভৰ লগত পৰিৱৰ্তনশীল লভ্যাংশৰ অধিকাৰ আৰু কোম্পানীত ভোটৰ অধিকাৰ দিয়ে। ডিবেঞ্চাৰ হৈছে কোম্পানীয়ে সংগ্ৰহ কৰা ঋণ আৰু ই স্থিৰ সুতৰ হাৰ বহন কৰে যি কোম্পানীয়ে লাভ কৰক বা নকৰক পৰিশোধ কৰিব লাগে। শ্বেয়াৰধাৰীসকল মালিক, আনহাতে ডিবেঞ্চাৰধাৰীসকল কোম্পানীৰ ঋণদাতা।
Q: ডিপজিটৰি কি আৰু DEMAT ৰূপ কি?
A: ডিপজিটৰিয়ে বেংকে ধন ৰখাৰ দৰে বিনিয়োগকাৰীসকলৰ হৈ ছিকিউৰিটি ইলেক্ট্ৰনিক ৰূপত ৰাখে। ভাৰতত দুটা প্ৰধান ডিপজিটৰি আছে, ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় ছিকিউৰিটিজ ডিপজিটৰি লিমিটেড আৰু কেন্দ্ৰীয় ডিপজিটৰি সেৱা লিমিটেড, আৰু NSDL প্ৰথম আছিল। ছিকিউৰিটি ইলেক্ট্ৰনিকভাৱে ৰাখিলে তাক ডিমেটেৰিয়েলাইজড বা DEMAT ৰূপ বোলা হয়, যি ভৌতিক প্ৰমাণপত্ৰতকৈ সুৰক্ষিত আৰু স্থানান্তৰ কৰিবলৈ সহজ।

### Central Flagship Welfare Schemes — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/central-flagship-welfare-schemes/
Summary: Practice central flagship welfare schemes questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: In which year was the MGNREGA Act enacted?
A: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) was enacted in 2005.
Q: What is the full name of MGNREGA?
A: MGNREGA stands for Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act.
Q: How many days of guaranteed wage employment does MGNREGA provide?
A: MGNREGA provides 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in a financial year to each rural household.
Q: PM-KISAN scheme was launched in which year?
A: The Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme was launched in February 2019.
Q: What is the annual financial benefit under PM-KISAN to each eligible farmer family?
A: Under PM-KISAN, each eligible farmer family receives ₹6,000 per year in three instalments of ₹2,000.
Q: PM-KISAN provides income support to which category of farmers?
A: PM-KISAN provides income support to all landholding farmer families in India.
Q: The Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana was launched in which year?
A: The Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana was launched in June 2015.
Q: What is the objective of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana?
A: The objective of PMAY is to provide affordable housing (pucca houses) to eligible urban and rural households.
Q: The Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PMJAY) was launched in which year?
A: PMJAY was launched on 23 September 2018.
Q: What is the annual health cover provided per family under Ayushman Bharat PMJAY?
A: Ayushman Bharat PMJAY provides a health cover of ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation.
Q: Who are the beneficiaries of Ayushman Bharat PMJAY?
A: PMJAY covers the bottom 40% of the Indian population as per the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) data.
Q: The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana was launched in which year?
A: The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana was launched on 1 May 2016.
Q: What is the main objective of the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana?
A: PMUY aims to provide free LPG connections to poor rural households to protect women's health.
Q: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana was launched in which year?
A: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana was launched on 28 August 2014.
Q: What is the full form of PMJDY?
A: PMJDY stands for Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, a financial inclusion scheme.
Q: What is the key feature of the PMJDY savings account?
A: PMJDY provides a zero-balance savings account with a RuPay debit card and accident insurance cover.
Q: The Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana provides financial assistance to whom?
A: PMMVY provides financial assistance to pregnant and lactating mothers for their first child.
Q: What is the amount of financial assistance provided under PM Matru Vandana Yojana?
A: PMMVY provides ₹5,000 in instalments to eligible pregnant and lactating mothers.
Q: The Poshan Abhiyaan was launched in which year?
A: The Poshan Abhiyaan (National Nutrition Mission) was launched in 2018.
Q: What is the main objective of the Poshan Abhiyaan?
A: The Poshan Abhiyaan aims to reduce stunting, undernutrition and anaemia among children and women.
Q: The Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on which date?
A: The Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on 2 October 2014.
Q: Which ministry administers the urban component of the Swachh Bharat Mission?
A: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs administers the urban component of the Swachh Bharat Mission.
Q: The Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme was launched in which year?
A: The Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme was launched on 22 January 2015.
Q: What is the objective of Beti Bachao Beti Padhao?
A: BBBP aims to address the declining child sex ratio and ensure the survival, protection and education of the girl child.
Q: The Skill India Mission was launched on which date?
A: The Skill India Mission was launched on 15 July 2015 on the occasion of World Youth Skills Day.
Q: The Start-Up India initiative was launched in which year?
A: The Start-Up India initiative was launched on 16 January 2016.
Q: The Stand-Up India scheme was launched in which year?
A: The Stand-Up India scheme was launched on 5 April 2016.
Q: Stand-Up India provides bank loans to which categories of entrepreneurs?
A: Stand-Up India provides loans to Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and women entrepreneurs.
Q: The National Food Security Act was enacted in which year?
A: The National Food Security Act (NFSA) was enacted in 2013.
Q: What is the entitlement of subsidised foodgrains per person per month under the NFSA?
A: Under NFSA, eligible persons are entitled to 5 kg of subsidised foodgrains per person per month.
Q: The Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana was launched in which year?
A: The Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) was launched in 2015.
Q: What is the full form of DDU-GKY?
A: DDU-GKY stands for Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana.
Q: What is the objective of DDU-GKY?
A: DDU-GKY aims to provide skill training and wage employment to rural youth from poor households.
Q: What is the objective of Mission Indradhanush?
A: Mission Indradhanush aims to achieve full immunisation coverage of all children and pregnant women against vaccine-preventable diseases.
Q: The Shram Suvidha portal was launched for which purpose?
A: The Shram Suvidha portal was launched to facilitate transparent and labour law compliant registration and compliance reporting by employers.
Q: What is MGNREGA and what is its main guarantee?
A: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was enacted in 2005. It guarantees at least one hundred days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members are willing to do unskilled manual work. It is a demand-driven scheme, so the work has to be provided when it is demanded, and it also creates durable rural assets such as roads, ponds and check dams.
Q: What are the benefits under PM-KISAN and Ayushman Bharat?
A: PM-KISAN, launched in 2019, provides income support of six thousand rupees a year to eligible farmer families, paid in three instalments of two thousand rupees directly into bank accounts. Ayushman Bharat PMJAY, launched in 2018, provides health cover of five lakh rupees per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation to poor and vulnerable families identified from the socio-economic census.
Q: What is the Swachh Bharat Mission and when was it launched?
A: The Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on 2 October 2014 to make the country open defecation free and to improve solid and liquid waste management. It has two components, urban and rural. The urban component is administered by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, and the mission works through the construction of household and community toilets along with awareness campaigns.
Q: What is the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana?
A: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, launched in 2014, is the national mission for financial inclusion. It provides a basic savings bank account with no minimum balance requirement, along with a RuPay debit card, accident insurance and an overdraft facility. It has brought a large number of unbanked households into the formal banking system and supports direct benefit transfer.
Q: What are the main skill development schemes of the central government?
A: The Skill India Mission, launched in 2015, is the umbrella programme for skilling, and the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana is its flagship certification scheme. The Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana provides placement-linked skill training to rural youth. Mission Indradhanush, though a health scheme, also relies on outreach and awareness, while the Shram Suvidha portal simplifies labour law compliance for employers and workers.
Q: MGNREGA কি আৰু ইয়াৰ প্ৰধান নিশ্চিতি কি?
A: মহাত্মা গান্ধী ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় গ্ৰাম্য নিয়োগ নিশ্চিতি আইন ২০০৫ চনত গৃহীত হৈছিল। ই প্ৰতিটো গ্ৰাম্য পৰিয়ালক, যাৰ প্ৰাপ্তবয়স্ক সদস্যসকলে অপদক্ষ শাৰীৰিক কাম কৰিবলৈ ইচ্ছা কৰে, এটা বিত্তীয় বছৰত কমেও এশ দিনৰ দৰমহাৰ নিয়োগ নিশ্চিত কৰে। ই চাহিদা-চালিত আঁচনি, সেয়ে চাহিদা কৰিলে কাম দিব লাগে, আৰু ই পথ, পুখুৰী আৰু বান্ধৰ দৰে টিকি থকা গ্ৰাম্য সম্পদো নিৰ্মাণ কৰে।
Q: PM-KISAN আৰু আয়ুষ্মান ভাৰতৰ সুবিধা কি কি?
A: PM-KISAN, ২০১৯ চনত আৰম্ভ, যোগ্য কৃষক পৰিয়ালক বছৰি ছয় হাজাৰ টকাৰ আয় সমৰ্থন দিয়ে, দুহাজাৰ টকাৰ তিনিটা কিস্তিত পোনপটীয়াকৈ বেংক একাউণ্টত জমা কৰা হয়। আয়ুষ্মান ভাৰত PMJAY, ২০১৮ চনত আৰম্ভ, সামাজিক-অৰ্থনৈতিক গণনাৰ পৰা চিনাক্ত দৰিদ্ৰ আৰু দুৰ্বল পৰিয়ালক মাধ্যমিক আৰু তৃতীয় স্তৰৰ চিকিৎসালয় ভৰ্তিৰ বাবে বছৰি পাঁচ লাখ টকাৰ স্বাস্থ্য সুৰক্ষা দিয়ে।
Q: স্বচ্ছ ভাৰত মিছন কি আৰু কেতিয়া আৰম্ভ হৈছিল?
A: স্বচ্ছ ভাৰত মিছন ২০১৪ চনৰ ২ অক্টোবৰত দেশখনক মুক্ত শৌচাচাৰিতামুক্ত কৰিবলৈ আৰু কঠিন তথা তৰল আৱৰ্জনা পৰিচালনা উন্নত কৰিবলৈ আৰম্ভ কৰা হৈছিল। ইয়াৰ দুটা অংশ আছে, চহৰীয়া আৰু গ্ৰাম্য। চহৰীয়া অংশ নগৰীয়া উন্নয়ন মন্ত্ৰালয়ে পৰিচালনা কৰে, আৰু মিছনখন ঘৰুৱা তথা সমুদায়িক শৌচালয় নিৰ্মাণ আৰু সজাগতা অভিযানৰ জৰিয়তে কাম কৰে।
Q: প্ৰধানমন্ত্ৰী জন ধন যোজনা কি?
A: প্ৰধানমন্ত্ৰী জন ধন যোজনা, ২০১৪ চনত আৰম্ভ, আৰ্থিক অন্তৰ্ভুক্তিৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় মিছন। ই ন্যূনতম জমা আৱশ্যকতাবিহীন মৌলিক সঞ্চয় বেংক একাউণ্ট, ৰূপে ডেবিট কাৰ্ড, দুৰ্ঘটনা বীমা আৰু অৱড্ৰাফ্ট সুবিধা দিয়ে। ই বৃহৎ সংখ্যক অ-বেংকড পৰিয়ালক আনুষ্ঠানিক বেংকিং ব্যৱস্থালৈ আনি প্ৰত্যক্ষ সুবিধা স্থানান্তৰক সহায় কৰিছে।
Q: কেন্দ্ৰ চৰকাৰৰ প্ৰধান দক্ষতা উন্নয়ন আঁচনি কি কি?
A: দক্ষতা ভাৰত মিছন, ২০১৫ চনত আৰম্ভ, দক্ষতা প্ৰদানৰ ছাতা কাৰ্যসূচী, আৰু প্ৰধানমন্ত্ৰী কৌশল বিকাশ যোজনা ইয়াৰ প্ৰধান প্ৰমাণপত্ৰ আঁচনি। দীন দয়াল উপাধ্যায় গ্ৰাম্য কৌশল্য যোজনা গ্ৰাম্য যুৱক-যুৱতীক নিয়োগ-সংযুক্ত দক্ষতা প্ৰশিক্ষণ দিয়ে। শ্ৰম সুবিধা প’ৰ্টেল প্ৰতিষ্ঠান আৰু কৰ্মীৰ বাবে শ্ৰম আইন পালন সহজ কৰে।

### Commercial Banking, NPAs & Financial Inclusion — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/commercial-banking-npa-inclusion/
Summary: Practice commercial banking, npas & financial inclusion questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual.
Q: What are scheduled commercial banks?
A: Scheduled commercial banks are those banks included in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934, which makes them eligible for RBI facilities.
Q: When was the first round of nationalization of 14 major commercial banks carried out?
A: The first round of nationalization of 14 major commercial banks was carried out on 19 July 1969.
Q: How many banks were nationalized in the second round in 1980?
A: Six banks were nationalized in the second round in 1980.
Q: What was the total number of banks nationalized in 1969?
A: Fourteen banks were nationalized in 1969.
Q: In which year was the State Bank of India formed and from which bank was it created?
A: The State Bank of India was formed in 1955 from the nationalization of the Imperial Bank of India.
Q: In 2017, how many banks were merged into the State Bank of India?
A: In April 2017, five associate banks and Bharatiya Mahila Bank were merged into SBI, making it six banks in all.
Q: What is a Non-Performing Asset (NPA)?
A: An NPA is a loan or advance whose interest or principal instalment remains overdue for a period of more than 90 days.
Q: After how many days of overdue does a loan become an NPA?
A: A loan becomes an NPA if the interest or principal remains overdue for more than 90 days.
Q: What is the SARFAESI Act, 2002?
A: The SARFAESI Act, 2002 empowers banks and financial institutions to recover non-performing assets by enforcing security interests without the intervention of courts.
Q: What is the main purpose of the SARFAESI Act?
A: The main purpose of the SARFAESI Act is to enable banks to recover bad loans quickly by selling the mortgaged assets of defaulters without court intervention.
Q: What is the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016?
A: The IBC, 2016 is the comprehensive law for time-bound resolution of insolvency and bankruptcy of companies, with a single unified framework.
Q: Which committee's recommendations led to the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code?
A: The Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee, chaired by T. K. Vishwanathan, submitted the report that led to the IBC, 2016.
Q: What is an Asset Reconstruction Company (ARC)?
A: An ARC is a company that buys non-performing assets (bad loans) from banks at a discounted price and tries to recover them.
Q: What are Basel norms?
A: Basel norms are international banking standards on capital adequacy and risk management, set by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision of the Bank for International Settlements.
Q: What is the minimum CRAR required for Indian banks under Basel norms?
A: The minimum Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) required for Indian banks is 9 percent.
Q: What is capital adequacy in banking?
A: Capital adequacy is the ratio of a bank's capital to its risk-weighted assets, ensuring that the bank has enough capital to absorb potential losses.
Q: When was the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) launched?
A: PMJDY was launched on 28 August 2014 as a national mission for financial inclusion.
Q: What is the slogan of the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana?
A: The slogan of PMJDY is Mera Khata, Bhagya Vidhata.
Q: What are payment banks?
A: Payment banks are niche banks that accept demand deposits (up to a limit), provide payment services and remittances, but cannot lend money.
Q: Which was the first payment bank to start operations in India?
A: Airtel Payments Bank was the first payment bank to begin operations in India, starting in 2017.
Q: What are small finance banks?
A: Small finance banks are banks that focus on financial inclusion, providing loans and savings services primarily to small farmers, micro and small industries and unorganized sectors.
Q: What is BBPS (Bharat Bill Payment System)?
A: BBPS is an integrated bill payment system launched by NPCI that provides interoperable and recurring bill payment services across India.
Q: What is financial literacy?
A: Financial literacy is the ability to understand and effectively use various financial skills, including budgeting, saving, investing and managing debt.
Q: What is the priority sector lending target for commercial banks in India?
A: Commercial banks have to lend 40 percent of their Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) to the priority sector.
Q: Name two sectors that come under priority sector lending.
A: Agriculture, micro and small enterprises (MSME), education, housing and weaker sections are the main constituents of priority sector lending.
Q: What is the Lead Bank Scheme?
A: Under the Lead Bank Scheme, introduced in 1969 on the recommendation of the Nariman Committee, one bank in each district takes the lead in coordinating credit and banking development.
Q: Under which Act were the Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) established?
A: Regional Rural Banks were established under the Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976.
Q: What was the first Regional Rural Bank of India?
A: Prathama Bank, sponsored by Syndicate Bank and set up on 2 October 1975, was the first RRB of India.
Q: In what proportion are Regional Rural Banks owned?
A: RRBs are jointly owned by the central government, the state government and the sponsor bank in the ratio of 50:15:35.
Q: What are cooperative banks?
A: Cooperative banks are banks organized on the cooperative principle, owned and operated by their members, mainly serving agriculture and rural areas.
Q: What is the Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) framework of the RBI?
A: The PCA framework imposes financial and regulatory restrictions on banks with weak capital, high NPAs or poor profitability, to help them recover.
Q: What does scheduled status of a bank mean?
A: A scheduled bank is one included in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934, and hence eligible for RBI facilities and liquidity support.
Q: Who regulates urban cooperative banks in India?
A: Urban cooperative banks are regulated by the RBI, while rural cooperative banks are supervised mainly through NABARD and the state governments.
Q: What is NABARD?
A: NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) is the apex institution for rural credit in India, established in 1982.
Q: What is the maximum amount of deposit a payment bank can accept from an individual?
A: A payment bank can accept deposits up to ₹2 lakh from an individual customer.
Q: What is a scheduled commercial bank?
A: A scheduled commercial bank is a bank included in the Second Schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. To be included, a bank must have a minimum paid-up capital and reserves and must satisfy the Reserve Bank that its affairs are not conducted in a manner harmful to depositors. Scheduled banks become eligible for liquidity support from the Reserve Bank and for membership of clearing houses.
Q: What is an NPA and how is it resolved?
A: A non-performing asset is a loan on which the interest or principal instalment has remained overdue for more than ninety days. Banks resolve bad loans through legal instruments such as the SARFAESI Act of 2002, which allows them to sell the mortgaged assets of defaulters without going to court, and the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code of 2016, which provides a time-bound framework. Asset reconstruction companies also buy bad loans and attempt recovery.
Q: What are Basel norms and what is the CRAR requirement in India?
A: Basel norms are international standards on capital adequacy and risk management issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision under the Bank for International Settlements. They require banks to hold a minimum amount of capital against risk-weighted assets. Indian banks follow Basel III and are required by the Reserve Bank to maintain a minimum capital to risk-weighted assets ratio of nine per cent, which is above the international minimum.
Q: What is the difference between payment banks and small finance banks?
A: Payment banks accept demand deposits up to two lakh rupees per customer and provide payment and remittance services, but they cannot lend. Small finance banks focus on financial inclusion by giving loans and savings services primarily to small farmers, micro and small industries and the unorganised sector, and they can lend. Airtel Payments Bank was the first payment bank to begin operations in India.
Q: What is the priority sector lending target and what does it cover?
A: Commercial banks in India must lend forty per cent of their adjusted net bank credit to the priority sector. The priority sector includes agriculture, micro and small enterprises, education, housing and weaker sections. The idea is to ensure that sectors important for employment and development receive adequate credit even though they may not always attract private finance on their own.
Q: অনুসূচিত বাণিজ্যিক বেংক কি?
A: অনুসূচিত বাণিজ্যিক বেংক হৈছে ভাৰতীয় ৰিজাৰ্ভ বেংক আইন, ১৯৩৪ ৰ দ্বিতীয় অনুসূচীত অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত বেংক। অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত হ'বলৈ বেংকৰ ন্যূনতম পৰিশোধিত মূলধন আৰু সংৰক্ষিত নিধি থাকিব লাগে আৰু ৰিজাৰ্ভ বেংক সন্তুষ্ট হ'ব লাগে যে বেংকৰ কাৰ্য আমানতকাৰীৰ বাবে ক্ষতিকাৰক নহয়। অনুসূচিত বেংকসমূহ ৰিজাৰ্ভ বেংকৰ পৰা তৰলতা সহায় আৰু ক্লিয়াৰিং হাউছৰ সদস্যপদৰ বাবে যোগ্য হয়।
Q: NPA কি আৰু ইয়াক কেনেকৈ সমাধান কৰা হয়?
A: অনুত্পাদনশীল সম্পদ হৈছে এনে ঋণ য'ত সুত বা মূল কিস্তি নব্বৈ দিনতকৈ বেছি বাকী থাকে। বেংকসমূহে ২০০২ চনৰ SARFAESI আইন, যি আদালতলৈ যোৱাৰ অবিহনে খেলনাদাৰীৰ বন্ধকী সম্পদ বিক্ৰী কৰিবলৈ দিয়ে, আৰু ২০১৬ চনৰ অসুবিধা আৰু দেউলিয়া সংহিতা আইন, যি সময়সীমাবদ্ধ কাঠামো দিয়ে, আদি আইনী আহিলাৰ জৰিয়তে মন্দ ঋণ সমাধান কৰে। সম্পদ পুনৰ্গঠন কোম্পানীসমূহেও মন্দ ঋণ কিনি আদায়ৰ চেষ্টা কৰে।
Q: বেছেল নাম কি আৰু ভাৰতত CRAR ৰ দাবী কি?
A: বেছেল নাম হৈছে বাছেল কমিটি অন বেংকিং ছুপাৰভিজনে বেংক ফৰ ইন্টাৰনেশ্যনেল চেটলমেণ্টছৰ অধীনত জাৰি কৰা মূলধন পৰ্যাপ্ততা আৰু বিপদ পৰিচালনাৰ আন্তৰ্জাতিক মানদণ্ড। এইবোৰে বেংকসমূহক বিপদ-ভাৰযুক্ত সম্পদৰ বিপৰীতে ন্যূনতম মূলধন ৰাখিবলৈ দাবী কৰে। ভাৰতীয় বেংকসমূহে বাছেল III অনুসৰণ কৰে আৰু ৰিজাৰ্ভ বেংকে ন্যূনতম ন· শতাংশ CRAR ৰাখিবলৈ দাবী কৰে, যি আন্তৰ্জাতিক ন্যূনতমতকৈ বেছি।
Q: পৰিশোধ বেংক আৰু ক্ষুদ্ৰ বিত্ত বেংকৰ পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: পৰিশোধ বেংকে গ্ৰাহক প্ৰতি দু লাখ টকলৈকে চাহিদা আমানত গ্ৰহণ কৰে আৰু পৰিশোধ তথা ৰেমিটেঞ্চ সেৱা দিয়ে, কিন্তু ঋণ দিব নোৱাৰে। ক্ষুদ্ৰ বিত্ত বেংকসমূহে মূলতঃ ক্ষুদ্ৰ কৃষক, অণু আৰু ক্ষুদ্ৰ উদ্যোগ আৰু অসংগঠিত খণ্ডক ঋণ আৰু সঞ্চয় সেৱা দি আৰ্থিক অন্তৰ্ভুক্তিত গুৰুত্ব দিয়ে, আৰু তেওঁলোকে ঋণ দিব পাৰে। এয়াৰটেল পে'মেণ্টচ বেংক ভাৰতত কাৰ্য আৰম্ভ কৰা প্ৰথম পৰিশোধ বেংক আছিল।
Q: অগ্ৰাধিকাৰ খণ্ড ঋণৰ লক্ষ্য কি আৰু ই কি সামৰি লয়?
A: ভাৰতত বাণিজ্যিক বেংকসমূহে তেওঁলোকৰ সমন্বিত নিকা বেংক ঋণৰ চল্লিশ শতাংশ অগ্ৰাধিকাৰ খণ্ডলৈ দিব লাগে। অগ্ৰাধিকাৰ খণ্ডত কৃষি, অণু আৰু ক্ষুদ্ৰ উদ্যোগ, শিক্ষা, বাসস্থান আৰু দুৰ্বল শ্ৰেণী অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত। উদ্দেশ্য হৈছে নিয়োগ আৰু উন্নয়নৰ বাবে গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ খণ্ডসমূহে তেওঁলোকৰ নিজৰ বলত ব্যক্তিগত বিত্ত আকৰ্ষণ নকৰিলেও পৰ্যাপ্ত ঋণ লাভ কৰাটো নিশ্চিত কৰা।

### Core Industries & Manufacturing (Make in India) — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/core-industries-make-in-india/
Summary: Practice core industries & manufacturing (make in india) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual.
Q: When was the 'Make in India' initiative launched?
A: The Make in India initiative was launched on 25 September 2014.
Q: Who launched the Make in India initiative?
A: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the Make in India initiative.
Q: What is the Index of Industrial Production (IIP)?
A: IIP is an index that measures the growth of industries in the economy, covering the sectors of mining, manufacturing and electricity.
Q: Which agency publishes the IIP in India?
A: The National Statistics Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation publishes the IIP.
Q: What is the current base year of the IIP?
A: The current base year of the IIP is 2017-18, revised from 2011-12.
Q: Which three sectors does the IIP cover?
A: The IIP covers mining, manufacturing and electricity.
Q: What is the weight of manufacturing in the IIP?
A: Manufacturing has a weight of about 77.6 percent in the IIP.
Q: How many items are included in the IIP basket?
A: The IIP basket includes 407 items.
Q: What is the Eight Core Industries index?
A: It is a monthly combined index of eight core infrastructure industries that measures their growth.
Q: Name the eight core industries of India.
A: Coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement and electricity.
Q: Which agency publishes the Eight Core Industries index?
A: The Office of the Economic Adviser in the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) publishes it.
Q: What is the combined weight of the eight core industries in the IIP?
A: The combined weight of the eight core industries in the IIP is about 40.27 percent.
Q: Which of the eight core industries has the highest weight in the index?
A: Refinery products have the highest weight among the eight core industries.
Q: What is the target for manufacturing's share in GDP under the Make in India initiative?
A: The target is to raise manufacturing's share in GDP to 25 percent.
Q: What is the current approximate share of manufacturing in India's GDP?
A: Manufacturing contributes about 17 percent of India's GDP.
Q: What does PLI stand for?
A: PLI stands for Production Linked Incentive.
Q: When was the PLI scheme launched?
A: The PLI scheme was launched in March 2020, initially for large-scale electronics manufacturing.
Q: In how many sectors has the PLI scheme been announced?
A: The PLI scheme has been announced in 14 sectors.
Q: What is the objective of the PLI scheme?
A: To boost domestic manufacturing and exports by providing incentives based on incremental production.
Q: What is the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC)?
A: DMIC is a mega industrial corridor project between Delhi and Mumbai with manufacturing zones and supporting infrastructure.
Q: Which country is collaborating with India in the DMIC project?
A: Japan is collaborating with India in the DMIC project.
Q: When was the DMIC project launched?
A: The DMIC project was launched in 2011-12.
Q: Which city is known as the 'Detroit of Asia' for the automobile industry?
A: Chennai is known as the 'Detroit of Asia'.
Q: Which company is India's largest automobile manufacturer by volume?
A: Maruti Suzuki is India's largest automobile manufacturer by volume.
Q: Which is a major defence public sector undertaking in India?
A: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) and Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) are major defence PSUs.
Q: What is the share of textiles in India's GDP?
A: The textile sector contributes about 2 to 3 percent of India's GDP.
Q: What is India's position in world cotton production?
A: India is the largest producer of cotton in the world.
Q: Which PSU is the largest producer of coal in the world?
A: Coal India Limited (CIL) is the largest producer of coal in the world.
Q: What does SAIL stand for?
A: SAIL stands for Steel Authority of India Limited.
Q: When was SAIL formed?
A: SAIL was formed in 1973.
Q: What is the target of the National Manufacturing Policy?
A: To raise manufacturing's share in GDP to 25 percent and create 100 million additional jobs.
Q: When was the National Manufacturing Policy announced?
A: The National Manufacturing Policy was announced in 2011.
Q: Which PSU is India's flagship crude oil and natural gas producer?
A: The Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) is India's flagship crude oil and gas producer.
Q: What is India's rank in world manufacturing output?
A: India is among the world's six largest manufacturing countries.
Q: Which PSU is a major producer of fertilisers in India?
A: National Fertilisers Limited (NFL) is a major fertiliser producer in the public sector.
Q: What are the eight core industries of India?
A: The eight core industries are coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement and electricity. They are called core industries because their output is used by almost every other sector of the economy and because they together carry a weight of about forty per cent in the Index of Industrial Production. The Index of Eight Core Industries measures their monthly production.
Q: Which core industry has the highest and the lowest weight?
A: Among the eight core industries, refinery products carry the highest weight of about twenty-eight per cent, followed by electricity and steel. Fertiliser carries the lowest weight of about two and a half per cent. Because the weights do not always match everyday impressions, candidates should memorise the order rather than guess it in the examination hall.
Q: Who releases the Index of Eight Core Industries?
A: The Index of Eight Core Industries is released by the Office of the Economic Adviser in the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. It uses 2011-12 as the base year and is published every month with a lag of about one month. It is different from the Index of Industrial Production, which is compiled by the National Statistical Office.
Q: What is the objective of the Make in India programme?
A: Make in India, launched on 25 September 2014, aims to make India a global hub for manufacturing, design and innovation. Its main objectives are to increase the share of manufacturing in gross domestic product, to create large-scale employment, to attract foreign direct investment and to develop world-class infrastructure. It initially identified twenty-five sectors for focused development, and later Production Linked Incentive schemes strengthened the same push.
Q: What is the Production Linked Incentive scheme?
A: The Production Linked Incentive scheme provides a financial incentive to companies that is linked to the additional sales they achieve from production in India. It encourages firms to expand manufacturing, improve competitiveness and build domestic supply chains, and it covers sectors such as electronics, pharmaceuticals, automobiles and textiles. The scheme is an important instrument of the government's effort to raise the manufacturing share of the economy.
Q: ভাৰতৰ আঠটা মূল খণ্ড কি কি?
A: আঠটা মূল খণ্ড হৈছে কয়লা, কেঁচা তেল, প্ৰাকৃতিক গেছ, শোধনাগাৰৰ সামগ্ৰী, সাৰ, ইস্পাত, চিমেণ্ট আৰু বিদ্যুৎ। ইহঁতক মূল খণ্ড বোলা হয় কাৰণ ইহঁতৰ উৎপাদন অৰ্থনীতিৰ প্ৰায় প্ৰতিটো খণ্ডই ব্যৱহাৰ কৰে আৰু কাৰণ একেলগে ইহঁতে ঔদ্যোগিক উৎপাদন সূচকাংকত প্ৰায় চল্লিশ শতাংশ ভাৰ বহন কৰে। আঠটা মূল খণ্ডৰ সূচকাংকই তেওঁলোকৰ মাহেকীয়া উৎপাদন জোখে।
Q: কোনটো মূল উদ্যোগৰ ভাৰ আটাইতকৈ বেছি আৰু আটাইতকৈ কম?
A: আঠটা মূল খণ্ডৰ ভিতৰত শোধনাগাৰৰ সামগ্ৰীয়ে প্ৰায় আঠাইশ শতাংশৰ সৰ্বাধিক ভাৰ বহন কৰে, তাৰ পিছতে বিদ্যুৎ আৰু ইস্পাত। সাৰে প্ৰায় আঢ়ৈ শতাংশৰ আটাইতকৈ কম ভাৰ বহন কৰে। ভাৰসমূহে সদায় দৈনন্দিন ধাৰণাৰ লগত নমিলে, সেয়ে প্ৰাৰ্থীয়ে পৰীক্ষা হলে অনুমান কৰাৰ পৰিৱৰ্তে ক্ৰম মনত ৰখা উচিত।
Q: আঠটা মূল খণ্ডৰ সূচকাংক কোনে প্ৰকাশ কৰে?
A: আঠটা মূল খণ্ডৰ সূচকাংক বাণিজ্য আৰু উদ্যোগ মন্ত্ৰালয়ৰ অধীনত উদ্যোগ প্ৰসাৰ আৰু আভ্যন্তৰীণ বাণিজ্য বিভাগৰ অৰ্থনৈতিক উপদেষ্টাৰ কাৰ্যালয়ে প্ৰকাশ কৰে। ই ২০১১-১২ ভিত্তি বছৰ ব্যৱহাৰ কৰে আৰু প্ৰায় এমাহৰ বিলম্বেৰে প্ৰতি মাহে প্ৰকাশ কৰা হয়। ই ঔদ্যোগিক উৎপাদন সূচকাংকৰ পৰা পৃথক, যি ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় পৰিসংখ্যা কাৰ্যালয়ে সংকলন কৰে।
Q: মেক ইন ইণ্ডিয়া কাৰ্যসূচীৰ উদ্দেশ্য কি?
A: ২০১৪ চনৰ ২৫ ছেপ্তেম্বৰত আৰম্ভ কৰা মেক ইন ইণ্ডিয়াৰ লক্ষ্য ভাৰতক উৎপাদন, অৱশিষ্ট আৰু উদ্ভাৱনৰ এক বিশ্বব্যাপী কেন্দ্ৰ কৰি তোলা। ইয়াৰ মূল উদ্দেশ্যসমূহ হৈছে মুঠ ঘৰুৱা উৎপাদনত উৎপাদনৰ অংশ বঢ়োৱা, বৃহৎ জোখত কৰ্মসংস্থাপন সৃষ্টি কৰা, প্ৰত্যক্ষ বিদেশী বিনিয়োগ আকৰ্ষণ কৰা আৰু বিশ্বমানৰ আন্তঃগাঁথনি নিৰ্মাণ কৰা। ই আৰম্ভণিতে মনোযোগী বিকাশৰ বাবে পঁচিশটা খণ্ড চিনাক্ত কৰিছিল, আৰু পিছত উৎপাদন সংযুক্ত প্ৰণোদনা আঁচনিয়ে একে প্ৰচেষ্টাক সবল কৰিছিল।
Q: উৎপাদন সংযুক্ত প্ৰণোদনা আঁচনি কি?
A: উৎপাদন সংযুক্ত প্ৰণোদনা আঁচনিয়ে কোম্পানীসমূহক ভাৰতত উৎপাদনৰ পৰা লাভ কৰা অতিৰিক্ত বিক্ৰীৰ লগত সংযুক্ত এক আৰ্থিক প্ৰণোদনা দিয়ে। ই প্ৰতিষ্ঠানসমূহক উৎপাদন বিস্তাৰ, প্ৰতিযোগিতা উন্নত আৰু ঘৰুৱা যোগান শৃংখলা নিৰ্মাণত উৎসাহিত কৰে, আৰু ই ইলেক্ট্ৰনিক্স, ঔষধ, অটোমোবাইল আৰু বস্ত্ৰৰ দৰে খণ্ড সামৰে। আঁচনিটো অৰ্থনীতিৰ উৎপাদন অংশ বঢ়োৱাৰ চৰকাৰৰ প্ৰচেষ্টাৰ এটা গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ সঁজুলি।

### Demographics & Human Development (Census, HDI) — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/demographics-hdi-census-india/
Summary: Practice demographics & human development (census, hdi) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual.
Q: What was the total population of India as per the Census 2011?
A: The total population of India as per Census 2011 was 121.08 crore, often rounded to about 121 crore.
Q: Which ministry conducts the decennial Census in India?
A: The Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, conducts the decennial Census.
Q: In which year was the first census of independent India conducted?
A: The first census of independent India was conducted in 1951.
Q: In which year was the first census in India conducted during British rule?
A: The first all-India census was conducted in 1872 during British rule, under the supervision of Lord Mayo.
Q: What is the term for the number of females per 1000 males in a population?
A: It is called the sex ratio, expressed as the number of females per 1000 males.
Q: As per Census 2011, what was the sex ratio of India?
A: As per Census 2011, the sex ratio of India was 943 females per 1000 males.
Q: What was the literacy rate of India as per Census 2011?
A: The overall literacy rate of India as per Census 2011 was 74.04 percent.
Q: Which state has the highest literacy rate in India as per Census 2011?
A: Kerala has the highest literacy rate of about 94 percent as per Census 2011.
Q: What is the population growth rate of India as per Census 2011 compared to the previous decade?
A: The decadal population growth rate of India during 2001-2011 was 17.70 percent, a decline from 21.54 percent in the previous decade.
Q: What is the term for the ratio of dependents (children and aged) to the working-age population?
A: It is called the dependency ratio, which measures the load on the working-age population.
Q: What does 'demographic dividend' refer to?
A: Demographic dividend refers to the economic growth potential that results from a shift in the age structure towards a larger working-age population and smaller dependent population.
Q: What is the full form of HDI?
A: HDI stands for Human Development Index, published by the UNDP in its annual Human Development Report.
Q: Which organization publishes the Human Development Report?
A: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) publishes the annual Human Development Report.
Q: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Human Development Index?
A: HDI is based on three components - health (life expectancy), education and income (GNI per capita); military expenditure is not a component.
Q: Health in the HDI is measured by which indicator?
A: Health in the HDI is measured by life expectancy at birth.
Q: Education in the HDI is measured by which indicators?
A: Education in HDI is measured by mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling.
Q: Income in the HDI is measured by which indicator?
A: Income in HDI is measured by Gross National Income (GNI) per capita, adjusted for purchasing power parity.
Q: As per the latest UNDP Human Development Report, India is placed in which category of human development?
A: India falls in the medium human development category as per the recent UNDP Human Development Report.
Q: Which country topped the UNDP Human Development Index for several recent years?
A: Switzerland has topped the UNDP Human Development Index in several recent reports.
Q: The HDI value ranges between which two numbers?
A: The HDI value ranges between 0 and 1.
Q: Which of the following statements is TRUE about India's age structure?
A: India has a young population with a large proportion in the working-age group, giving it a demographic dividend advantage.
Q: Which of the following indices is released by NITI Aayog to measure the progress of states towards the SDGs?
A: NITI Aayog releases the SDG India Index to measure the progress of states and Union Territories towards the Sustainable Development Goals.
Q: The Census 2021 in India was postponed primarily due to what reason?
A: The Census 2021 was postponed primarily due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
Q: What is the term for the difference between the birth rate and the death rate of a population?
A: The difference between the birth rate and the death rate is called the natural growth rate of population.
Q: Which stage of the demographic transition theory is characterized by low birth rate and low death rate?
A: The third/late stage of the demographic transition is characterized by both low birth rate and low death rate, leading to near-stable population.
Q: As per Census 2011, which state has the highest population in India?
A: Uttar Pradesh has the highest population among Indian states as per Census 2011.
Q: Which state has the lowest population density among major states as per Census 2011?
A: Arunachal Pradesh has the lowest population density in India, with just 17 persons per square kilometre as per Census 2011.
Q: What is the national average population density of India as per Census 2011?
A: The national average population density of India as per Census 2011 was 382 persons per square kilometre.
Q: The population of India is projected to surpass which country to become the most populous nation?
A: India surpassed China to become the world's most populous nation in 2023.
Q: What is the sex ratio at birth (number of girls per 1000 boys) indicator used to measure in India?
A: The sex ratio at birth is used to detect gender imbalance, reflecting practices like female foeticide and skewed child sex ratio.
Q: Which institution publishes the 'National Family Health Survey' (NFHS) in India?
A: The National Family Health Survey is conducted by the International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS) under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
Q: Which of the following is a consequence of a high dependency ratio in a country?
A: A high dependency ratio puts pressure on the working population to support more dependents, reducing per capita savings and growth.
Q: As per Census 2011, India's child sex ratio (0-6 years) was how many girls per 1000 boys?
A: India's child sex ratio (0-6 years) was 919 girls per 1000 boys as per Census 2011, the lowest since independence.
Q: Which of the following is the most densely populated state of India as per Census 2011?
A: Bihar is the most densely populated state of India as per Census 2011, with about 1106 persons per square kilometre.
Q: What is the full form of UNDP?
A: UNDP stands for the United Nations Development Programme, which publishes the Human Development Report.
Q: When was the first census held in India?
A: The first census in India was conducted in 1872 during the time of Lord Mayo, but it was not complete or synchronous. The first complete and synchronous census covering the whole country was held in 1881 under Lord Ripon. Since then a census has been conducted every ten years, and the 2011 Census was the fifteenth in the series and the seventh after independence.
Q: Who publishes the Human Development Index and what does it measure?
A: The Human Development Index is published by the United Nations Development Programme in its annual Human Development Report. It measures average achievement in three dimensions: a long and healthy life, access to knowledge, and a decent standard of living. It was designed to look beyond income alone and is expressed as a value between zero and one.
Q: What are the three components of the Human Development Index?
A: The health component is measured by life expectancy at birth, the education component by mean years of schooling of adults and expected years of schooling of children, and the income component by Gross National Income per capita at purchasing power parity. Since 2010 these three dimension indices have been combined using the geometric mean.
Q: What is the demographic dividend?
A: A demographic dividend is the economic advantage a country enjoys when the share of its working-age population is large relative to its dependent population. With fewer dependants, savings and investment rise and growth can accelerate. However, the advantage is temporary, and it can only be converted into real growth if the young population is educated, healthy and able to find productive employment.
Q: Which states lead and lag on literacy and sex ratio?
A: According to the 2011 Census, Kerala recorded both the highest literacy rate of about 94 per cent and the highest sex ratio of 1084. Bihar had the lowest literacy rate of about 61.8 per cent, and Haryana had the lowest sex ratio of 879. These state-level comparisons are among the most frequently repeated facts in examinations.
Q: ভাৰতত প্ৰথম লোকপিয়ল কেতিয়া হৈছিল?
A: ভাৰতত প্ৰথম লোকপিয়ল ১৮৭২ চনত লৰ্ড মেয়'ৰ সময়ত হৈছিল, কিন্তু সেয়া সম্পূৰ্ণ বা সিংক্ৰণিক নাছিল। গোটেই দেশ সামৰি প্ৰথম পূৰ্ণ আৰু সিংক্ৰণিক লোকপিয়ল লৰ্ড ৰিপনৰ সময়ত ১৮৮১ চনত হৈছিল। তেতিয়াৰ পৰা প্ৰতি দহ বছৰত এবাৰ লোকপিয়ল হয়, আৰু ২০১১ চনৰ লোকপিয়ল শৃংখলাৰ পঞ্চদশ আৰু স্বাধীনতাৰ পিছত সপ্তম আছিল।
Q: মানৱ উন্নয়ন সূচকাংক কোনে প্ৰকাশ কৰে আৰু ই কি জোখে?
A: মানৱ উন্নয়ন সূচকাংক ৰাষ্ট্ৰসংঘৰ উন্নয়ন কাৰ্যসূচীয়ে ইয়াৰ বাৰ্ষিক মানৱ উন্নয়ন প্ৰতিবেদনত প্ৰকাশ কৰে। ই তিনিটা মাত্ৰাত গড় অৰ্জন জোখে: দীঘলীয়া আৰু সুস্থ জীৱন, জ্ঞানলৈ প্ৰৱেশ, আৰু শালীন জীৱনযাত্ৰাৰ স্তৰ। ই কেৱল আয়ৰ বাহিৰলৈ চাবলৈ সৃষ্টি কৰা হৈছিল আৰু শূন্যৰ পৰা একৰ মাজত মূল্য হিচাপে প্ৰকাশ কৰা হয়।
Q: মানৱ উন্নয়ন সূচকাংকৰ তিনিটা উপাদান কি কি?
A: স্বাস্থ্য উপাদান জন্মৰ সময়ত আয়ুষ্কালৰ দ্বাৰা জোখা হয়, শিক্ষা উপাদান প্ৰাপ্তবয়স্কৰ শিক্ষাৰ গড় বছৰ আৰু শিশুৰ প্ৰত্যাশিত শিক্ষাৰ বছৰৰ দ্বাৰা, আৰু আয় উপাদান ক্ৰয় ক্ষমতা সমতাৰে মুঠ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় আয় প্ৰতি ব্যক্তিৰ দ্বাৰা। ২০১০ চনৰ পৰা এই তিনিটা মাত্ৰাৰ সূচকাংক গুণোত্তৰ মধ্যমে সংমিশ্ৰণ কৰা হয়।
Q: জনগাঁথনিগত লভ্যাংশ কি?
A: জনগাঁথনিগত লভ্যাংশ হৈছে এখন দেশে উপভোগ কৰা আৰ্থিক সুবিধা যেতিয়া কৰ্মক্ষম বয়সৰ জনসংখ্যাৰ অংশ নিৰ্ভৰশীল জনসংখ্যাৰ তুলনাত বেছি হয়। নিৰ্ভৰশীল কম হ'লে সঞ্চয় আৰু বিনিয়োগ বাঢ়ে আৰু বৃদ্ধি দ্ৰুত হ'ব পাৰে। কিন্তু এই সুবিধা অস্থায়ী, আৰু যুৱ জনসংখ্যা শিক্ষিত, সুস্থ আৰু উৎপাদনশীল কৰ্মসংস্থাপন পাব পৰা হ'লেহে ইয়াক প্ৰকৃত বৃদ্ধিলৈ ৰূপান্তৰ কৰিব পাৰি।
Q: সাক্ষৰতা আৰু লিংগ অনুপাতত কোন ৰাজ্য আগশাৰীত আৰু পিছপৰ?
A: ২০১১ লোকপিয়ল অনুসৰি কেৰালাই প্ৰায় ৯৪ শতাংশ সৰ্বাধিক সাক্ষৰতা আৰু ১০৮৪ ৰ সৰ্বাধিক লিংগ অনুপাত দুয়োটা লাভ কৰিছিল। বিহাৰৰ সাক্ষৰতাৰ হাৰ আটাইতকৈ কম, প্ৰায় ৬১.৮ শতাংশ, আৰু হাৰিয়ানাৰ লিংগ অনুপাত আটাইতকৈ কম, ৮৭৯। এই ৰাজ্যিক তুলনাসমূহ পৰীক্ষাত সঘনাই দোহাৰি অহা তথ্যসমূহৰ এটা।

### Digital Infrastructure & FinTech — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/digital-infrastructure-fintech-india/
Summary: Practice digital infrastructure & fintech questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: When was the Digital India programme launched?
A: The Digital India programme was launched on 1 July 2015 by the Government of India.
Q: What is the vision of the Digital India programme?
A: The vision of Digital India is to transform India into a digitally empowered society and a knowledge economy.
Q: What is BharatNet?
A: BharatNet (earlier known as NOFN) is the flagship project of the Government of India to connect all gram panchayats with high-speed broadband network.
Q: Which ministry implements the BharatNet project?
A: The Department of Telecommunications under the Ministry of Communications implements BharatNet, with BSNL as a major executing agency.
Q: What is UPI?
A: UPI (Unified Payments Interface) is an instant real-time payment system developed by NPCI that allows money transfer between any two bank accounts through a mobile platform.
Q: In which year was UPI launched in India?
A: UPI was launched on 11 April 2016 by the Reserve Bank of India and NPCI.
Q: What is the full form of NPCI?
A: NPCI stands for National Payments Corporation of India, the umbrella organisation for retail payments in India.
Q: When was NPCI established?
A: NPCI was established in 2008, with the approval of the Reserve Bank of India, to build a robust retail payments system.
Q: What is Aadhaar?
A: Aadhaar is a 12-digit unique identification number issued by the UIDAI to residents of India, based on their biometric and demographic data.
Q: Under which Act does Aadhaar get its legal backing?
A: Aadhaar gets its legal backing from the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016.
Q: What is UIDAI?
A: UIDAI, the Unique Identification Authority of India, is the statutory body (established under the Aadhaar Act 2016) that issues Aadhaar numbers.
Q: What is India Stack?
A: India Stack is a set of open APIs and digital public infrastructure (Aadhaar, e-KYC, UPI, DigiLocker, ONDC, etc.) that enables paperless, cashless and presence-less service delivery.
Q: What is e-KYC?
A: e-KYC is electronic Know Your Customer verification, which uses Aadhaar-based authentication to verify a customer's identity instantly for opening accounts and services.
Q: What is BHIM?
A: BHIM (Bharat Interface for Money) is a UPI-based mobile app launched by NPCI in 2016 for easy digital payments and instant money transfer.
Q: What is RuPay and which organisation developed it?
A: RuPay is India's indigenous card payment network developed by NPCI and launched in 2012, providing an alternative to Visa and Mastercard.
Q: What is DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer)?
A: DBT is a scheme under which government subsidies and benefits are transferred directly into the bank accounts of beneficiaries, eliminating middlemen.
Q: When was the Direct Benefit Transfer scheme launched?
A: The DBT scheme was launched on 1 January 2013 by the Government of India.
Q: What is the JAM trinity?
A: JAM trinity refers to the combination of Jan Dhan accounts, Aadhaar and Mobile numbers, which together enable targeted delivery of subsidies through DBT.
Q: In which year was the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) launched?
A: PMJDY was launched on 28 August 2014 as a national mission for financial inclusion.
Q: What is DigiLocker?
A: DigiLocker is a cloud-based platform under Digital India where citizens can store, access and share their documents in digital form, issued by government agencies.
Q: Which ministry launched the DigiLocker platform?
A: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) launched DigiLocker.
Q: How many pillars does the Digital India programme have?
A: The Digital India programme is built on nine pillars of growth areas.
Q: What is CERT-In?
A: CERT-In (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team) is the national nodal agency responsible for cyber security, cyber incident response and cyber crisis management in India.
Q: Which is the nodal agency for cyber security in India?
A: CERT-In under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology is the nodal agency for cyber security in India.
Q: What role does NPCI play in the UPI system?
A: NPCI operates and develops the UPI platform, facilitating interoperability between different banks and payment apps.
Q: Which of the following is a popular UPI-based payment app in India: PhonePe, Western Union, SWIFT?
A: PhonePe is a popular UPI-based payment app in India; Western Union and SWIFT are international money transfer systems, not UPI apps.
Q: What is a fintech company?
A: A fintech (financial technology) company uses technology to provide financial services such as payments, lending, wealth management and insurance.
Q: Which is the parent company of the fintech Paytm?
A: Paytm is operated by One97 Communications Ltd, a leading Indian fintech company.
Q: What is digital literacy?
A: Digital literacy is the ability to use digital technologies, devices and the internet to access information, communicate and conduct financial transactions.
Q: Which scheme was launched in 2017 to make rural citizens digitally literate?
A: The Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan (PMGDISHA) was launched in 2017 to make rural citizens digitally literate.
Q: What is cryptocurrency?
A: Cryptocurrency is a digital or virtual currency that uses cryptography for security and operates on a decentralised network such as blockchain.
Q: Is Bitcoin considered legal tender in India?
A: No, Bitcoin is not legal tender in India; the RBI has not granted it legal tender status and has cautioned about its risks.
Q: What is the CBDC (Central Bank Digital Currency) launched by RBI and when was its pilot started?
A: CBDC, called the Digital Rupee (e₹), is the RBI's digital currency; its pilot was launched in 2022.
Q: What is IMPS and when was it launched?
A: IMPS (Immediate Payment Service) is a 24x7 instant interbank money transfer service launched by NPCI in 2010.
Q: Which institution regulates digital payment systems like UPI in India?
A: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) regulates digital payment systems in India, while NPCI operates the UPI platform.
Q: What is the Digital India programme and when was it launched?
A: The Digital India programme was launched on 1 July 2015 with the vision of transforming India into a digitally empowered society and a knowledge economy. It rests on nine pillars covering broadband connectivity, universal mobile access, e-governance, electronic delivery of services, electronics manufacturing and information technology for jobs. BharatNet is its flagship connectivity project for linking gram panchayats.
Q: What is UPI and who developed it?
A: UPI, the Unified Payments Interface, is an instant real-time payment system that allows money to be transferred between any two bank accounts through a mobile platform. It was developed by the National Payments Corporation of India and launched on 11 April 2016. NPCI operates and develops the platform and ensures interoperability between different banks and payment applications, while the Reserve Bank regulates digital payment systems.
Q: What is the India Stack and what are its main components?
A: The India Stack is a set of open APIs and digital public infrastructure that enables paperless, cashless and presence-less delivery of services. Its main components include Aadhaar for identity, e-KYC for instant verification, UPI for payments, DigiLocker for documents and the Open Network for Digital Commerce. It allows services to be built on top of shared public digital rails.
Q: What is the JAM trinity and how does it help welfare delivery?
A: The JAM trinity is the combination of Jan Dhan accounts, Aadhaar and mobile numbers. Jan Dhan accounts provide a bank account, Aadhaar provides a unique identity and mobile numbers allow authentication and communication. Together they make direct benefit transfer possible, so that subsidies and benefits reach the intended beneficiary directly without middlemen, reducing leakage and delay.
Q: What is the difference between cryptocurrency and the central bank digital currency?
A: A cryptocurrency is a digital or virtual currency that uses cryptography and operates on a decentralised network such as a blockchain; it is not issued by the government, and Bitcoin is not legal tender in India. The central bank digital currency, called the digital rupee, is issued by the Reserve Bank of India and is a sovereign liability, and its pilot was launched in 2022.
Q: ডিজিটেল ইণ্ডিয়া কাৰ্যসূচী কি আৰু কেতিয়া আৰম্ভ হৈছিল?
A: ডিজিটেল ইণ্ডিয়া কাৰ্যসূচী ২০১৫ চনৰ ১ জুলাইত ভাৰতক ডিজিটেলভাৱে সশক্ত সমাজ তথা জ্ঞান অৰ্থনীতিলৈ ৰূপান্তৰিত কৰাৰ দৃষ্টিভংগীৰে আৰম্ভ কৰা হৈছিল। ই নটা স্তম্ভৰ ওপৰত থিয়, য'ত ব্ৰডবেণ্ড সংযোগ, সাৰ্বজনীন ম’বাইল প্ৰৱেশ, ই-গভৰ্নেঞ্চ, সেৱাৰ ইলেক্ট্ৰনিক প্ৰদান, ইলেক্ট্ৰনিক্স উৎপাদন আৰু কামৰ বাবে তথ্য প্ৰযুক্তি অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত। ভাৰতনেট ইয়াৰ গাঁও পঞ্চায়ত সংযোগৰ প্ৰধান প্ৰকল্প।
Q: UPI কি আৰু ইয়াক কোনে বিকশিত কৰিছিল?
A: UPI, একীকৃত পৰিশোধ ইন্টাৰফে\'চ, হৈছে এক তৎক্ষণাত বাস্তৱ-সময় পৰিশোধ ব্যৱস্থা যি ম’বাইল প্লেটফৰ্মৰ জৰিয়তে যিকোনো দুটা বেংক একাউণ্টৰ মাজত ধন স্থানান্তৰ কৰিবলৈ দিয়ে। ইয়াক ভাৰতীয় ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় পৰিশোধ নিগমে বিকশিত কৰি ২০১৬ চনৰ ১১ এপ্ৰিলত আৰম্ভ কৰিছিল। NPCI য়ে প্লেটফৰ্ম চলায় আৰু বিকশিত কৰে তথা বিভিন্ন বেংক আৰু পৰিশোধ এপৰ মাজত আন্তঃকাৰ্যক্ষমতা নিশ্চিত কৰে, আনহাতে ৰিজাৰ্ভ বেংকে ডিজিটেল পৰিশোধ ব্যৱস্থা নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ কৰে।
Q: ইণ্ডিয়া ষ্টেক কি আৰু ইয়াৰ প্ৰধান উপাদান কি কি?
A: ইণ্ডিয়া ষ্টেক হৈছে মুক্ত API আৰু ডিজিটেল ৰাজহুৱা আন্তঃগাঁথনিৰ এটা গোট যিয়ে কাগজহীন, নগদহীন আৰু উপস্থিতিহীন সেৱা প্ৰদান সক্ষম কৰে। ইয়াৰ প্ৰধান উপাদানত পৰিচয়ৰ বাবে আধাৰ, তৎক্ষণাত সত্যাপনৰ বাবে ই-কেওৱাইচি, পৰিশোধৰ বাবে UPI, নথিপত্ৰৰ বাবে ডিজিলকাৰ আৰু মুক্ত ডিজিটেল বাণিজ্য নেটৱৰ্ক অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত। ই ভাগ-বতৰা ৰাজহুৱা ডিজিটেল ৰে\'লৰ ওপৰত সেৱা গঢ়িবলৈ দিয়ে।
Q: জাম ত্ৰিমূৰ্তি কি আৰু ই কল্যাণ প্ৰদানত কেনেকৈ সহায় কৰে?
A: জাম ত্ৰিমূৰ্তি হৈছে জন ধন একাউণ্ট, আধাৰ আৰু ম’বাইল নম্বৰৰ সংমিশ্ৰণ। জন ধন একাউণ্টে বেংক একাউণ্ট, আধাৰে অনন্য পৰিচয় আৰু ম’বাইল নম্বৰে প্ৰমাণীকৰণ তথা যোগাযোগ সম্ভৱ কৰে। একেলগে এইবোৰে প্ৰত্যক্ষ সুবিধা স্থানান্তৰ সম্ভৱ কৰে, যাতে ৰাজসাহায্য আৰু সুবিধা মধ্যস্থতাকাৰী অবিহনে পোনপটীয়াকৈ প্ৰাপ্য সুবিধাভোগীলৈ যায়, অপচয় আৰু পলম কমায়।
Q: ক্ৰিপ্টোকাৰেন্সি আৰু কেন্দ্ৰীয় বেংক ডিজিটেল মুদ্ৰাৰ পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: ক্ৰিপ্টোকাৰেন্সি হৈছে এনে ডিজিটেল বা ভাৰ্চুৱেল মুদ্ৰা যি ক্ৰিপ্টোগ্ৰাফী ব্যৱহাৰ কৰে আৰু ব্লকচেইনৰ দৰে বিকেন্দ্ৰীভূত নেটৱৰ্কত চলে; ই চৰকাৰে জাৰি নকৰে, আৰু বাইটকইন ভাৰতত আইনী মুদ্ৰা নহয়। কেন্দ্ৰীয় বেংক ডিজিটেল মুদ্ৰা, ডিজিটেল টকা নামেৰে জনাজাত, ভাৰতীয় ৰিজাৰ্ভ বেংকে জাৰি কৰে আৰু ই এক সাৰ্বভৌম দায়, আৰু ইয়াৰ পাইলট ২০২২ চনত আৰম্ভ কৰা হৈছিল।

### Foreign Trade, FDI/FPI & International Bodies (WTO, IMF
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/foreign-trade-fdi-wto-imf-wb/
Summary: Practice foreign trade, fdi/fpi & international bodies (wto, imf, world bank) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam.
Q: In which year was the World Trade Organization (WTO) established?
A: The WTO was established in 1995 as the successor to GATT.
Q: GATT was signed in which year?
A: GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade) was signed in 1947.
Q: Which principle of the WTO ensures that member countries grant equal treatment to all trading partners?
A: The Most Favoured Nation (MFN) principle ensures equal treatment for all trading partners.
Q: What is the headquarters of the WTO?
A: The WTO headquarters is located in Geneva, Switzerland.
Q: Who established the IMF and World Bank at the Bretton Woods Conference in 1944?
A: The IMF and the World Bank were established by 44 allied nations at the Bretton Woods Conference in July 1944.
Q: Which organization of the World Bank Group provides loans to private sector enterprises in developing countries?
A: The International Finance Corporation (IFC) provides loans to the private sector.
Q: Which institution of the World Bank Group provides concessional loans to the poorest countries?
A: The International Development Association (IDA) provides concessional loans to the poorest countries.
Q: What is the full form of IMF?
A: IMF stands for International Monetary Fund.
Q: Which international body provides temporary financial assistance to member countries facing BoP problems?
A: The IMF provides temporary financial assistance to member countries facing balance of payments problems.
Q: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) was established in which year?
A: The ADB was established in 1966 with headquarters in Manila, Philippines.
Q: Which new development bank was set up by the BRICS countries?
A: The New Development Bank (NDB) was set up by the BRICS countries in 2014.
Q: What is the headquarters of the New Development Bank (NDB)?
A: The NDB headquarters is in Shanghai, China.
Q: SAARC was founded in which year?
A: SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) was founded in 1985.
Q: What is the difference between FDI and FPI?
A: FDI is direct investment in physical assets with management control, while FPI is portfolio investment in financial assets without management control.
Q: Which sector allows 100% FDI through the automatic route?
A: Many sectors such as single-brand retail, renewable energy and most manufacturing allow 100% FDI through the automatic route.
Q: In FDI policy, what is the 'automatic route'?
A: Under the automatic route, FDI is allowed without prior approval of the government or the RBI.
Q: In FDI policy, what is the 'approval route'?
A: Under the approval route, FDI requires prior approval from the government, usually through the concerned ministry.
Q: Which nodal agency is responsible for FDI policy formulation in India?
A: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) is the nodal agency for FDI policy.
Q: DPIIT comes under which ministry?
A: DPIIT functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
Q: In which year was the 'Make in India' initiative launched?
A: The 'Make in India' initiative was launched on 25 September 2014.
Q: The Foreign Trade Policy 2023 is valid for which period?
A: The Foreign Trade Policy 2023 is valid from 1 April 2023 to 31 March 2028.
Q: What is the major export destination of India as per recent trade data?
A: The United States has been India's largest export destination in recent years.
Q: Which country is the largest source of FDI inflows into India in recent years?
A: Singapore, followed by Mauritius and the USA, has been a major source of FDI inflows into India in recent years.
Q: What is a Free Trade Agreement (FTA)?
A: An FTA is an agreement between countries to reduce or eliminate tariffs on trade in goods and services.
Q: What is the difference between FTA and PTA?
A: A PTA (Preferential Trade Agreement) covers a limited set of goods with partial tariff cuts, while an FTA covers a wider range of goods and services with deeper liberalisation.
Q: Which of the following is a portfolio investment — FDI, FPI, ECB, or Export earnings?
A: FPI (Foreign Portfolio Investment) is portfolio investment in financial assets.
Q: Which body regulates FPI in India?
A: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) regulates Foreign Portfolio Investment.
Q: What is the FDI limit in the defence sector in India?
A: FDI up to 74% is allowed in the defence sector through the automatic route.
Q: What is the FDI limit in the insurance sector in India?
A: FDI up to 74% is allowed in the insurance sector in India.
Q: In which year was India admitted as a founding member of the WTO?
A: India was a founding member of the WTO when it came into effect on 1 January 1995.
Q: Which commodity is India's largest agricultural export?
A: Basmati rice and marine products are among India's largest agricultural exports.
Q: Which agreement replaced GATT as the global trade regulator?
A: The Marrakesh Agreement established the WTO in 1995, which replaced GATT.
Q: What is the major import item of India by value?
A: Crude petroleum is India's largest import item by value.
Q: Which of the following is NOT a member of the BRICS group?
A: The BRICS group consists of Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa; countries like Japan are not members.
Q: Which international body adjudicates trade disputes between member countries?
A: The WTO's Dispute Settlement Body (DSB) adjudicates trade disputes between member countries.
Q: What is the World Trade Organization and how did it replace GATT?
A: The World Trade Organization was established in 1995 through the Marrakesh Agreement as the successor to the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, which had been signed in 1947. It provides a rules-based framework for international trade based on non-discrimination, and it has a Dispute Settlement Body to settle trade disputes. Its headquarters is in Geneva, and India was a founding member.
Q: What is the difference between FDI and FPI?
A: Foreign direct investment is investment in physical assets that brings a lasting interest and management control in a business, and it is considered stable because it is committed for the long term. Foreign portfolio investment is investment in financial assets such as shares and bonds without management control, and it is more volatile because it can be withdrawn quickly. FDI is regulated through DPIIT policy, while FPI is regulated by SEBI.
Q: What are the automatic route and the approval route for FDI?
A: Under the automatic route, foreign direct investment is allowed without prior approval from the government or the Reserve Bank of India, and many sectors including most manufacturing allow up to one hundred per cent through this route. Under the approval route, prior approval is required, usually obtained through the concerned administrative ministry. The route and the sectoral limit together determine how much investment is permitted and how it may enter.
Q: What is the difference between an FTA and a PTA?
A: A free trade agreement is an arrangement between countries to reduce or eliminate tariffs on a wide range of goods and services. A preferential trade agreement covers a limited set of goods and provides only partial tariff concessions. An FTA therefore offers deeper and broader liberalisation than a PTA. India has signed several such agreements to expand market access for its exporters.
Q: What are the main institutions of the World Bank Group?
A: The World Bank Group includes the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development, which lends to middle-income countries; the International Development Association, which gives concessional loans and grants to the poorest countries; the International Finance Corporation, which lends to the private sector; the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, which provides political risk insurance; and the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes, which settles investment disputes.
Q: বিশ্ব বাণিজ্য সংস্থা কি আৰু ই GATT ক কেনেকৈ প্ৰতিস্থাপন কৰিছিল?
A: বিশ্ব বাণিজ্য সংস্থা ১৯৯৫ চনত মাৰাকেছ চুক্তিৰ জৰিয়তে শুল্ক আৰু বাণিজ্যৰ সাধাৰণ চুক্তিৰ উত্তৰাধিকাৰী হিচাপে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰা হৈছিল, যি ১৯৪৭ চনত স্বাক্ষৰিত হৈছিল। ই অ-পক্ষপাতিত্বৰ ওপৰত আধাৰিত আন্তৰ্জাতিক বাণিজ্যৰ বাবে নিয়ম-আধাৰিত কাঠামো দিয়ে, আৰু বাণিজ্য বিবাদ নিষ্পত্তিৰ বাবে বিবাদ নিষ্পত্তি সংস্থা আছে। ইয়াৰ মুখ্য কাৰ্যালয় জেনেভাত, আৰু ভাৰত প্ৰতিষ্ঠাপক সদস্য আছিল।
Q: FDI আৰু FPI ৰ পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: প্ৰত্যক্ষ বিদেশী বিনিয়োগ হৈছে ভৌতিক সম্পদত কৰা বিনিয়োগ যি এটা ব্যৱসায়ত স্থায়ী আগ্ৰহ আৰু পৰিচালনা নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ আনে, আৰু ই দীৰ্ঘম্যাদীভাৱে প্ৰতিশ্ৰুত বাবে স্থিৰ বুলি গণ্য কৰা হয়। বিদেশী পৰ্টফলিঅ বিনিয়োগ হৈছে শ্বেয়াৰ আৰু বণ্ডৰ দৰে বিত্তীয় সম্পদত কৰা বিনিয়োগ, পৰিচালনা নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ অবিহনে, আৰু ই লগে লগে ওলাই যাব পৰা বাবে অধিক অস্থিৰ। FDI DPIIT নীতিৰ জৰিয়তে আৰু FPI SEBI য়ে নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ কৰে।
Q: FDI ৰ স্বয়ংক্ৰিয় পথ আৰু অনুমোদন পথ কি কি?
A: স্বয়ংক্ৰিয় পথৰ অধীনত প্ৰত্যক্ষ বিদেশী বিনিয়োগ চৰকাৰ বা ভাৰতীয় ৰিজাৰ্ভ বেংকৰ পূৰ্ব অনুমোদন অবিহনে অনুমোদিত, আৰু বেছিভাগ উৎপাদনকে ধৰি বহু খণ্ডয়ে এই পথেৰে এশ শতাংশলৈকে অনুমতি দিয়ে। অনুমোদন পথৰ অধীনত পূৰ্ব অনুমোদন প্ৰয়োজন, সাধাৰণতে সংশ্লিষ্ট প্ৰশাসনিক মন্ত্ৰালয়ৰ জৰিয়তে লাভ কৰা হয়। পথ আৰু খণ্ডভিত্তিক সীমাই একেলগে কিমান বিনিয়োগ অনুমোদিত আৰু কেনেকৈ প্ৰৱেশ কৰিব পাৰে সেয়া নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰে।
Q: FTA আৰু PTA ৰ পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: মুক্ত বাণিজ্য চুক্তি হৈছে দেশসমূহৰ মাজত বিস্তৃত সামগ্ৰী আৰু সেৱাৰ শুল্ক হ্ৰাস বা আঁতৰোৱাৰ ব্যৱস্থা। অগ্ৰাধিকাৰ বাণিজ্য চুক্তিয়ে সীমিত সামগ্ৰী সামৰি লয় আৰু কেৱল আংশিক শুল্ক ৰেহাই দিয়ে। সেয়ে FTA য়ে PTA তকৈ গভীৰ আৰু বিস্তৃত উদাৰীকৰণ দিয়ে। ভাৰতে ৰপ্তানিকাৰীসকলৰ বাবে বজাৰ প্ৰৱেশ বিস্তাৰ কৰিবলৈ কেইবাখনো এনে চুক্তি স্বাক্ষৰ কৰিছে।
Q: বিশ্ব বেংক গোটৰ প্ৰধান প্ৰতিষ্ঠানসমূহ কি কি?
A: বিশ্ব বেংক গোটত পুনৰ্গঠন আৰু উন্নয়নৰ বাবে আন্তৰ্জাতিক বেংক, যি মধ্য আয়ৰ দেশসমূহক ঋণ দিয়ে; আন্তৰ্জাতিক উন্নয়ন সংস্থা, যি আটাইতকৈ দৰিদ্ৰ দেশসমূহক ৰাজসাহায্যমূলক ঋণ আৰু অনুদান দিয়ে; আন্তৰ্জাতিক বিত্ত নিগম, যি ব্যক্তিগত খণ্ডক ঋণ দিয়ে; বহুপাক্ষিক বিনিয়োগ গেৰাণ্টি সংস্থা, যি ৰাজনৈতিক বিপদ বীমা দিয়ে; আৰু বিনিয়োগ বিবাদ নিষ্পত্তিৰ আন্তৰ্জাতিক কেন্দ্ৰ অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত।

### Green Revolution & Farm Subsidies (MSP, PDS) — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/green-revolution-msp-pds-subsidies/
Summary: Practice green revolution & farm subsidies (msp, pds) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: In which decade did the Green Revolution take place in India?
A: The Green Revolution in India took place mainly in the late 1960s.
Q: Who is known as the father of the Green Revolution?
A: Norman Borlaug, an American agronomist, is known as the father of the Green Revolution.
Q: Who is called the father of the Green Revolution in India?
A: Dr. M.S. Swaminathan is called the father of the Green Revolution in India.
Q: Which varieties of seeds were the main instrument of the Green Revolution?
A: High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds were the main instrument of the Green Revolution.
Q: Norman Borlaug was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in which year?
A: Norman Borlaug was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970 for his contributions to the Green Revolution.
Q: Which two states were the primary beneficiaries of the Green Revolution in India?
A: Punjab and Haryana were the primary beneficiaries of the Green Revolution in India.
Q: Which of the following was a key component of the Green Revolution package?
A: High yielding variety seeds, chemical fertilisers, pesticides and assured irrigation were key components of the Green Revolution package.
Q: Which revolution in India was aimed at increasing milk production?
A: The White Revolution, led by Dr. Verghese Kurien under Operation Flood, was aimed at increasing milk production.
Q: What is the Minimum Support Price (MSP)?
A: MSP is the minimum price announced by the government at which it purchases farmers' crops, protecting them from price fluctuations.
Q: Which agency is responsible for procuring food grains at MSP in India?
A: The Food Corporation of India (FCI), along with state agencies, procures food grains at MSP.
Q: On whose recommendation is the MSP fixed by the government of India?
A: MSP is fixed on the recommendation of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP).
Q: Which of the following is NOT a statutory or notified MSP crop?
A: Tea and vegetables are not notified MSP crops; MSP covers cereals, pulses, oilseeds, cotton, sugarcane and some commercial crops.
Q: What does PDS stand for in the context of food distribution in India?
A: PDS stands for the Public Distribution System, through which food grains and essential commodities are distributed at subsidised rates.
Q: Which system was introduced in India for the targeted distribution of food grains to the poor?
A: The Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) was introduced in 1997 for the distribution of food grains to the poor at subsidised prices.
Q: The stock of food grains maintained by the government for emergency needs is called what?
A: The stock of food grains maintained by the government for emergency needs is called the buffer stock.
Q: In which year was the Food Corporation of India (FCI) established?
A: The Food Corporation of India was established in 1965.
Q: Which Act provides a legal right to subsidised food grains to eligible households in India?
A: The National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013 provides a legal right to subsidised food grains to eligible households.
Q: As per the NFSA 2013, how much food grain is entitled to a priority household per person per month?
A: As per NFSA 2013, each member of a priority household is entitled to 5 kg of food grain per person per month at subsidised prices.
Q: What is the subsidised issue price of wheat under the NFSA 2013?
A: Under the NFSA 2013, the issue price of wheat is 2 rupees per kg.
Q: What is the subsidised issue price of rice under the NFSA 2013?
A: Under the NFSA 2013, the issue price of rice is 3 rupees per kg.
Q: Which of the following is a major subsidy given by the Government of India to farmers?
A: Fertiliser subsidy, food subsidy, power subsidy and irrigation subsidy are major subsidies provided to farmers in India.
Q: The fertiliser subsidy in India is mainly provided on which fertilisers?
A: The fertiliser subsidy in India is mainly provided on urea, DAP, potash and complex fertilisers, with urea being the most heavily subsidised.
Q: Which scheme provides income support of 6000 rupees per year to small and marginal farmers?
A: The PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi) scheme provides 6000 rupees per year to eligible small and marginal farmers in three instalments.
Q: In which year was the PM-KISAN scheme launched?
A: The PM-KISAN scheme was launched in February 2019.
Q: What is meant by 'Evergreen Revolution'?
A: The Evergreen Revolution refers to a concept of sustainable agriculture that aims to increase productivity without harming the environment, as advocated by Dr. M.S. Swaminathan.
Q: Which of the following is a major drawback of the Green Revolution in India?
A: Regional disparity, overuse of chemicals, groundwater depletion and neglect of pulses and oilseeds are major drawbacks of the Green Revolution.
Q: The concept of the 'second Green Revolution' in India emphasizes which of the following?
A: The second Green Revolution emphasises sustainable agriculture, focus on dryland and rain-fed farming, pulses, oilseeds and balanced use of inputs.
Q: Which committee recommended that MSP should be at least 50 percent above the cost of production (A2+FL)?
A: The National Commission on Farmers headed by Dr. M.S. Swaminathan recommended that MSP should be at least 50 percent above the cost of production.
Q: What is the main objective of the buffer stock policy in India?
A: The buffer stock policy aims to maintain food security by ensuring availability of food grains for PDS and for stabilising prices during shortages.
Q: Which of the following is the largest component of the food subsidy bill of the Government of India?
A: The difference between the MSP/cost of procurement and the subsidised issue price under the NFSA is the largest component of the food subsidy bill.
Q: Which of the following programmes was started for the distribution of food to the poorest households at highly subsidised rates?
A: The Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) provides 35 kg of food grains per family per month at highly subsidised rates to the poorest households.
Q: Under the Antyodaya Anna Yojana, the issue price of wheat and rice is what?
A: Under AAY, wheat is issued at 2 rupees per kg and rice at 3 rupees per kg, matching the NFSA issue prices.
Q: Which of the following states has the highest coverage of the Public Distribution System in terms of ration card holders?
A: Uttar Pradesh has the highest number of ration card holders, followed by West Bengal and Bihar.
Q: What is the primary aim of the 'One Nation One Ration Card' scheme?
A: The One Nation One Ration Card scheme enables migrant workers and beneficiaries to access their food grains from any fair price shop across the country.
Q: Which of the following is TRUE about the Green Revolution?
A: The Green Revolution made India self-sufficient in food grains, especially in wheat, within a short span of time.
Q: What was the Green Revolution and who led it in India?
A: The Green Revolution was a technological programme that raised food grain output through high-yielding seeds, fertilisers, pesticides and irrigation, beginning in India in the mid-1960s. M.S. Swaminathan is regarded as the father of the Green Revolution in India, while the American scientist Norman Borlaug, who developed the dwarf wheat varieties, is called its father globally and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.
Q: Who recommends and who announces the minimum support price?
A: The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices, set up in 1965, recommends the minimum support price after studying the cost of cultivation and market conditions. The government considers the recommendation and announces the minimum support price for major crops before the sowing season. The Food Corporation of India then undertakes procurement at that price.
Q: What is the public distribution system and how did the National Food Security Act change it?
A: The public distribution system sells subsidised food grains and other essentials through fair price shops. It became a targeted system in 1997 and was given a legal foundation by the National Food Security Act of 2013, which covers about sixty-seven per cent of the population. Under the Act, priority households receive five kilograms per person per month and Antyodaya families receive thirty-five kilograms per family per month.
Q: What are the cost concepts A2, A2 plus FL and C2?
A: A2 is the actual paid-out cost incurred by the farmer, such as seeds, fertiliser, labour wages and irrigation charges. A2 plus FL adds the imputed value of the farmer's own and family labour to this paid-out cost. C2 is the most comprehensive concept and additionally includes the imputed rent on owned land and interest on owned capital, so it gives the full economic cost of production.
Q: Why is the Green Revolution criticised despite its success?
A: Although the Green Revolution made India self-sufficient in food grains, it widened regional disparities because its benefits were concentrated in irrigated areas of Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh. It encouraged wheat and rice monoculture, depleted groundwater, degraded soil through excessive fertiliser and pesticide use, and favoured farmers who could afford the costly input package, thereby increasing income inequality.
Q: সেউজ বিপ্লৱ কি আছিল আৰু ভাৰতত ইয়াৰ নেতৃত্ব কোনে দিছিল?
A: সেউজ বিপ্লৱ আছিল এক প্ৰযুক্তিগত কাৰ্যসূচী, যিয়ে উচ্চ উৎপাদনশীল বীজ, সাৰ, কীটনাশক আৰু পানীৰ যোগানৰ জৰিয়তে খাদ্যশস্যৰ উৎপাদন বঢ়াইছিল, আৰু ভাৰতত ১৯৬০ ৰ দশকৰ মাজভাগত আৰম্ভ হৈছিল। এম.এছ. স্বামীনাথনক ভাৰতত সেউজ বিপ্লৱৰ পিতৃ বুলি গণ্য কৰা হয়, আনহাতে চুটি গমৰ জাত বিকশিত কৰা আমেৰিকান বিজ্ঞানী নৰ্মান বৰলাউগক বিশ্বত ইয়াৰ পিতৃ বোলা হয় আৰু তেওঁ ১৯৭০ চনত নোবেল শান্তি বঁটা লাভ কৰিছিল।
Q: ন্যূনতম সহায়ক মূল্য কোনে পৰামৰ্শ দিয়ে আৰু কোনে ঘোষণা কৰে?
A: ১৯৬৫ চনত প্ৰতিষ্ঠিত কৃষি ব্যয় আৰু মূল্য আয়োগে খেতিৰ ব্যয় আৰু বজাৰ অৱস্থা অধ্যয়ন কৰি ন্যূনতম সহায়ক মূল্যৰ পৰামৰ্শ দিয়ে। চৰকাৰে পৰামৰ্শ বিবেচনা কৰি বপন ঋতুৰ আগতে প্ৰধান শস্যৰ বাবে ন্যূনতম সহায়ক মূল্য ঘোষণা কৰে। তাৰপিছত ভাৰতীয় খাদ্য নিগমে সেই মূল্যত ক্ৰয় কৰে।
Q: ৰাজহুৱা বিতৰণ ব্যৱস্থা কি আৰু ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় খাদ্য সুৰক্ষা আইনে ইয়াক কেনেকৈ সলনি কৰিলে?
A: ৰাজহুৱা বিতৰণ ব্যৱস্থাই ন্যায্য মূল্যৰ দোকানৰ জৰিয়তে ৰাজসাহায্যপ্ৰাপ্ত খাদ্যশস্য আৰু আন অপৰিহাৰ্য সামগ্ৰী বিক্ৰী কৰে। ই ১৯৯৭ চনত লক্ষ্যভিত্তিক ব্যৱস্থা হৈছিল আৰু ২০১৩ চনৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় খাদ্য সুৰক্ষা আইনে ইয়াক আইনী ভিত্তি দিছিল, যি জনসংখ্যাৰ প্ৰায় সাতষট্টি শতাংশ সামৰে। আইন অনুসৰি অগ্ৰাধিকাৰ পৰিয়ালে মাহেকত প্ৰতি ব্যক্তি পাঁচ কিলোগ্ৰাম আৰু অন্ত্যোদয় পৰিয়ালে মাহেকত প্ৰতি পৰিয়াল পঁয়ত্ৰিশ কিলোগ্ৰাম লাভ কৰে।
Q: ব্যয় ধাৰণা A2, A2 যোগ FL আৰু C2 কি কি?
A: A2 হৈছে খেতিয়কে কৰা প্ৰকৃত নগদ খৰচ, যেনে বীজ, সাৰ, শ্ৰমৰ মজুৰি আৰু পানীৰ যোগানৰ খৰচ। A2 ৰ লগত FL যোগ কৰিলে এই নগদ খৰচৰ লগত খেতিয়কৰ নিজা আৰু পৰিয়ালৰ শ্ৰমৰ অনুমিত মূল্য যোগ হয়। C2 আটাইতকৈ বিস্তৃত ধাৰণা আৰু ইয়াৰ লগত নিজা মাটিৰ অনুমিত ভাড়া আৰু নিজা মূলধনৰ সুতও যোগ হয়, সেয়ে ই উৎপাদনৰ সম্পূৰ্ণ আৰ্থিক ব্যয় দিয়ে।
Q: সফলতা সত্ত্বেও সেউজ বিপ্লৱক কিয় সমালোচনা কৰা হয়?
A: সেউজ বিপ্লৱে ভাৰতক খাদ্যশস্যত আত্মনিৰ্ভৰশীল কৰি তুলিছিল যদিও ইয়াৰ সুবিধা পাঞ্জাব, হাৰিয়ানা আৰু পশ্চিম উত্তৰ প্ৰদেশৰ পানীযুক্ত অঞ্চলত কেন্দ্ৰীভূত হোৱাৰ বাবে আঞ্চলিক অসমতা বঢ়াইছিল। ই গম আৰু ধানৰ একক শস্য খেতিক উৎসাহিত কৰিছিল, ভূগৰ্ভস্থ পানী শেষ কৰিছিল, সাৰ-কীটনাশকৰ অতি ব্যৱহাৰে মাটি নষ্ট কৰিছিল, আৰু ব্যয়বহুল ইনপুট পেকেজ কিনিব পৰা খেতিয়কক সুবিধা দি আয়ৰ অসমতা বঢ়াইছিল।

### Agriculture & Cropping Patterns — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/india-agriculture-cropping-patterns/
Summary: Practice agriculture & cropping patterns questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Which is the most important food crop of India?
A: Rice is the most important food crop of India, cultivated mainly in the kharif season.
Q: Rice is a crop of which cropping season in India?
A: Rice is primarily a kharif crop, sown with the onset of the southwest monsoon.
Q: Which crop is considered the staple food of north India and is the second most important food crop after rice?
A: Wheat is the staple food of north India and the second most important food crop after rice.
Q: Wheat is a crop of which cropping season?
A: Wheat is a rabi crop, sown in winter (October-December) and harvested in spring.
Q: Which of the following is NOT a rabi crop?
A: Maize, along with rice, is primarily a kharif crop; wheat, barley, gram and mustard are rabi crops.
Q: Which of the following is a kharif crop?
A: Paddy, maize, jowar, bajra, cotton, sugarcane and pulses like moong are kharif crops.
Q: Which crops are grown in the zaid season in India?
A: Zaid crops are grown in the short summer season between rabi and kharif, including watermelon, cucumber, muskmelon and fodder crops.
Q: Which of the following is a zaid crop?
A: Watermelon and cucumber are examples of zaid crops grown in the short summer season.
Q: Which among the following is the largest producer of pulses in India?
A: Madhya Pradesh is the largest producer of pulses in India.
Q: Which crop is known as the 'golden fibre' of India?
A: Jute is known as the 'golden fibre' of India.
Q: Which state is the largest producer of sugarcane in India?
A: Uttar Pradesh is the largest producer of sugarcane in India.
Q: Which crop requires a warm and humid climate and is the main cash crop of Assam?
A: Tea requires a warm and humid climate and is the main cash crop of Assam.
Q: Which of the following states is the largest producer of tea in India?
A: Assam is the largest producer of tea in India, accounting for about half of the country's tea production.
Q: Which is the leading cotton producing state in India?
A: Gujarat is the leading cotton producing state in India.
Q: Which of the following crops was improved during the Green Revolution using high yielding varieties?
A: Wheat and rice were the principal crops improved during the Green Revolution through high yielding varieties.
Q: Which is the most important oilseed crop of India?
A: Groundnut is the most important oilseed crop of India, followed by mustard and rapeseed.
Q: Which irrigation method is most efficient in saving water for agricultural use?
A: Drip and sprinkler irrigation are the most efficient methods for saving water in agriculture.
Q: Which of the following is a high yielding variety of wheat developed in India?
A: Kalyan Sona and Sonora-64 are high yielding varieties of wheat developed in India during the Green Revolution.
Q: Which organization provides credit and refinance facilities for agriculture in India?
A: NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) provides credit and refinance facilities for agriculture and rural development in India.
Q: In which year was NABARD established?
A: NABARD was established in 1982 by an act of Parliament.
Q: The Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme provides what to farmers?
A: The Kisan Credit Card scheme provides short-term credit to farmers for purchasing seeds, fertilisers, pesticides and other agricultural needs.
Q: Which scheme provides crop insurance to farmers against crop failure due to natural calamities?
A: The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) provides crop insurance to farmers against crop failure due to natural calamities, pests and diseases.
Q: In which year was the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana launched?
A: The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana was launched in 2016.
Q: What is contract farming?
