A: Contract farming is an agreement between farmers and buyers (processing or marketing firms) where farmers produce crops under a pre-agreed price and quality arrangement.
Q: What is vertical farming?
A: Vertical farming is the practice of growing crops in vertically stacked layers, often indoors using controlled environment agriculture and soilless techniques.
Q: What is the current approximate share of agriculture in India's GDP?
A: Agriculture contributes roughly 15 to 18 percent to India's GDP, though it employs over 40 percent of the workforce.
Q: Which of the following soils is most suitable for the cultivation of cotton?
A: Black (regur) soil is most suitable for cotton cultivation.
Q: Which of the following is a major source of irrigation in India?
A: Canals, wells and tube wells are the major sources of irrigation in India, with wells and tube wells being the most dominant.
Q: India's agriculture is often called a 'gamble in the monsoon' because of what?
A: India's agriculture is called a gamble in the monsoon because a large part of crop production depends on the uncertain and uneven rainfall of the southwest monsoon.
Q: Which of the following is the main source of irrigation water in Assam?
A: Assam is largely rain-fed and depends mainly on the abundant monsoon rainfall, with rivers and low-lying fields supporting cultivation.
Q: Which crop is known as the 'king of coarse grains' in India?
A: Jowar (sorghum) is often called the 'king of coarse grains' in India.
Q: Which of the following factors contributed most to the success of the Green Revolution in Punjab and Haryana?
A: The availability of assured irrigation, high yielding variety seeds, chemical fertilisers and better infrastructure contributed most to the success in Punjab and Haryana.
Q: What is the principal objective of the MSP (Minimum Support Price) policy in India?
A: The MSP policy aims to protect farmers from a fall in prices by guaranteeing a minimum price for their produce, ensuring income stability.
Q: Which of the following crops is NOT generally covered under MSP in India?
A: Tea, jute-like commercial cash crops except notified ones, and vegetables are generally not covered under MSP; MSP covers staples like wheat, rice and pulses.
Q: Which of the following is a major rice producing state of India?
A: West Bengal is the largest rice producing state in India, followed by Uttar Pradesh and Punjab.
Q: What are the three cropping seasons of India?
A: India has three cropping seasons. Kharif crops are sown with the arrival of the south-west monsoon in June and harvested in September and October, and include rice, maize and cotton. Rabi crops are sown in October and November and harvested in March and April, and include wheat and gram. Zaid is the short summer season from March to June when melons, cucumber and fodder are grown.
Q: Which state is the largest producer of rice and wheat in India?
A: West Bengal is the largest producer of rice in India, though Punjab records the highest rice productivity per hectare. Uttar Pradesh is the largest producer of wheat. Remember that production and productivity are different measures, and this distinction is often used to set a trap in objective questions.
Q: What is cropping intensity?
A: Cropping intensity is the gross cropped area expressed as a percentage of the net sown area. A value above one hundred per cent shows that some fields are cultivated more than once in a year, which happens where irrigation and short-duration varieties are available. Higher cropping intensity increases total output without bringing more land under cultivation.
Q: What is meant by minimum support price?
A: The minimum support price is the price at which the government promises to purchase a crop from farmers if the open market price falls below that level. It is recommended by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices and announced before the sowing season for major crops. It protects farmers from a sharp fall in prices after a good harvest and supports food security through public procurement.
Q: Which soil is best for cotton and which is the most widespread soil in India?
A: Black soil, also called regur soil, is best for cotton because it retains moisture and is rich in clay. Alluvial soil is the most widespread and most fertile soil in India and supports intensive cultivation in the northern plains and river valleys. The two should not be confused in examinations.
Q: ভাৰতৰ তিনিটা শস্য ঋতু কি কি?
A: ভাৰতত তিনিটা শস্য ঋতু আছে। খৰিফ শস্য জুনত দক্ষিণ-পশ্চিম মৌচুমী অহাৰ লগে লগে বপন কৰা হয় আৰু সেপ্টেম্বৰ-অক্টোবৰত চপোৱা হয়, য'ত ধান, মাকৈ আৰু কপাহ আদি অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত। ৰবি শস্য অক্টোবৰ-নৱেম্বৰত বপন আৰু মাৰ্চ-এপ্ৰিলত চপোৱা হয়, য'ত গম আৰু বুট আদি অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত। জায়দ মাৰ্চৰ পৰা জুনলৈকে চুটি গৰমৰ ঋতু, যেতিয়া তৰমুজ, তিয়ঁহ আৰু পশুখাদ্য খেতি কৰা হয়।
Q: ভাৰতত ধান আৰু গমৰ সৰ্বাধিক উৎপাদক কোন ৰাজ্য?
A: ভাৰতত ধানৰ সৰ্বাধিক উৎপাদক পশ্চিম বংগ, যদিও পাঞ্জাবে হেক্টৰ প্ৰতি সৰ্বাধিক ধান উৎপাদনশীলতা লাভ কৰে। গমৰ সৰ্বাধিক উৎপাদক উত্তৰ প্ৰদেশ। মনত ৰাখিব যে উৎপাদন আৰু উৎপাদনশীলতা বেলেগ বেলেগ মাপ, আৰু এই পাৰ্থক্য বস্তুনিষ্ঠ প্ৰশ্নত ফান্দ ৰখাৰ বাবে সঘনাই ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা হয়।
Q: শস্যৰ তীব্ৰতা কি?
A: শস্যৰ তীব্ৰতা হৈছে নিকা বপন ক্ষেত্ৰৰ শতাংশ হিচাপে প্ৰকাশ কৰা মুঠ শস্য ক্ষেত্ৰ। একশ শতাংশতকৈ বেছি মানে কিছু পথাৰ বছৰত এবাৰতকৈ বেছি খেতি কৰা হয়, যি পানীৰ যোগান আৰু চুটি সময়ৰ জাত উপলব্ধ হ'লে হয়। উচ্চ শস্য তীব্ৰতাই অধিক মাটি খেতিৰ তললৈ অনাৰ অবিহনে মুঠ উৎপাদন বঢ়ায়।
Q: ন্যূনতম সহায়ক মূল্য মানে কি?
A: ন্যূনতম সহায়ক মূল্য হৈছে সেই মূল্য য'ত মুক্ত বজাৰ মূল্য সেই স্তৰতকৈ কম গ'লে চৰকাৰে খেতিয়কৰ পৰা শস্য ক্ৰয় কৰাৰ প্ৰতিশ্ৰুতি দিয়ে। ই কৃষি ব্যয় আৰু মূল্য আয়োগে পৰামৰ্শ দিয়ে আৰু বপন ঋতুৰ আগতে প্ৰধান শস্যৰ বাবে ঘোষণা কৰে। ই ভাল চপোৱাৰ পিছত মূল্যৰ তীব্ৰ পতনৰ পৰা খেতিয়কক ৰক্ষা কৰে আৰু ৰাজহুৱা ক্ৰয়ৰ জৰিয়তে খাদ্য সুৰক্ষাক সহায় কৰে।
Q: কপাহৰ বাবে কোনটো মাটি শ্ৰেষ্ঠ আৰু ভাৰতত আটাইতকৈ বিস্তৃত মাটি কোনটো?
A: ক'লা মাটি, যাক ৰেগুৰ মাটিও বোলা হয়, আৰ্দ্ৰতা ধৰি ৰখা আৰু মাটি-কাদোত সমৃদ্ধ হোৱাৰ বাবে কপাহৰ বাবে শ্ৰেষ্ঠ। পলসুৱা মাটি ভাৰতত আটাইতকৈ বিস্তৃত আৰু উৰ্বৰ মাটি আৰু উত্তৰৰ সমভূমি আৰু নদী উপত্যকাত নিবিড় খেতিক সহায় কৰে। পৰীক্ষাত এই দুটাক মিলাই পেলোৱা উচিত নহয়।

### Allied Sectors (Animal Husbandry, Dairy, Fisheries)
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/india-allied-sectors-dairy-fisheries/
Summary: Practice allied sectors (animal husbandry, dairy, fisheries) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free.
Q: Who is known as the 'Father of the White Revolution' in India?
A: Dr. Verghese Kurien, the architect of Operation Flood, is known as the father of the White Revolution.
Q: What is Operation Flood also called?
A: Operation Flood is also called the White Revolution.
Q: When was Operation Flood launched?
A: Operation Flood was launched in 1970 and was implemented in three phases over 1970-1996.
Q: Which organization implemented Operation Flood?
A: The National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) implemented Operation Flood.
Q: When was the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) established?
A: The NDDB was established in 1965 at Anand, Gujarat.
Q: What is AMUL?
A: AMUL is a dairy brand of the Gujarat Co-operative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF).
Q: Where is AMUL headquartered?
A: AMUL is headquartered at Anand in Gujarat.
Q: In which year was GCMMF formed?
A: GCMMF was formed in 1973.
Q: What is the 'Anand Pattern'?
A: The Anand Pattern is the three-tier cooperative structure of village dairy societies, district unions and a state federation, pioneered in Anand.
Q: True or False: India is the largest producer of milk in the world.
A: True. India has been the world's largest milk producer for over two decades.
Q: What is India's approximate annual milk production?
A: India produces about 230 million tonnes of milk annually (2022-23).
Q: What is the per capita availability of milk in India?
A: The per capita availability of milk in India is about 460 grams per day.
Q: What is the share of dairying in the total value of agricultural GVA?
A: Dairying contributes about 5 percent of the total value of agricultural GVA.
Q: Who founded the Kaira District Co-operative Milk Producers' Union, the origin of Amul?
A: Tribhuvandas Patel founded the union in 1946 with technical support from Verghese Kurien.
Q: Which ministry is responsible for animal husbandry and dairying in India?
A: The Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying.
Q: What is the Livestock Census?
A: The Livestock Census is a complete count of livestock in the country conducted every five years, the first being held in 1919.
Q: Which livestock census was the 20th census conducted in India?
A: The 20th Livestock Census was conducted in 2019 (2018-19) and its results were released in 2021.
Q: What is the share of the livestock sector in agriculture GVA?
A: The livestock sector contributes about 30 percent of the agriculture GVA.
Q: What is the contribution of livestock to India's total GDP?
A: The livestock sector contributes about 4 to 5 percent of India's total GDP.
Q: Which species accounts for the largest population in the Livestock Census of India?
A: Cattle account for the largest population in the livestock census.
Q: What is the Rashtriya Gokul Mission?
A: It is a scheme launched in 2014 for the genetic improvement of the cattle population to increase milk production.
Q: What is the Blue Revolution?
A: The Blue Revolution refers to the rapid development of the fisheries sector in India.
Q: Who is regarded as the father of the Blue Revolution in India?
A: Dr. Arun Krishnan is regarded as the father of the Blue Revolution in India.
Q: When was the integrated 'Blue Revolution' scheme launched?
A: The integrated Blue Revolution scheme was launched in 2015-16.
Q: What is NFDB and when was it established?
A: NFDB is the National Fisheries Development Board, established in 2006 with its headquarters at Hyderabad.
Q: When was the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) launched?
A: The PMMSY was launched in 2020.
Q: What is the total outlay of the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana?
A: PMMSY has a total outlay of ₹20,050 crore for the period 2020-21 to 2024-25.
Q: What is the share of inland fisheries in India's total fish production?
A: Inland fisheries contribute about 70 percent while marine fisheries contribute about 30 percent.
Q: What is India's rank in world fish production?
A: India is the second largest producer of fish in the world.
Q: Which state is the largest producer of fish in India?
A: Andhra Pradesh is the largest producer of fish in India.
Q: What is aquaculture?
A: Aquaculture is the farming of fish, shrimp and other aquatic organisms in controlled water bodies.
Q: What is India's approximate annual fish production?
A: India produces about 17.5 million tonnes of fish annually (2022-23).
Q: What is the major item of India's marine product export?
A: Frozen shrimp is the major item of India's marine product exports.
Q: What does MPEDA stand for?
A: MPEDA stands for the Marine Products Export Development Authority, set up in 1972.
Q: What is India's rank in world egg production?
A: India is the second largest producer of eggs in the world.
Q: What is the White Revolution and who is its father?
A: The White Revolution, also known as Operation Flood, was a programme launched in 1970 to make India self-sufficient in milk and to raise the income of dairy farmers. It was implemented by the National Dairy Development Board in three phases under the leadership of Verghese Kurien, who is called the father of the White Revolution. It made India the largest milk producer in the world and spread the Anand pattern of dairy cooperatives.
Q: What is the Anand pattern of dairy cooperatives?
A: The Anand pattern is a three-tier cooperative structure in which village dairy societies collect milk from farmer members, district unions process the milk, and a state federation handles marketing and brand building. Farmers own the entire chain, so they receive a fair share of the consumer's rupee. The Kaira District Cooperative Milk Producers' Union, known by the brand Amul, is the model that inspired dairy cooperatives across the country.
Q: What is the Blue Revolution?
A: The Blue Revolution refers to the rapid development of fisheries and aquaculture, launched in India in 1985-86 to increase fish production and build allied infrastructure. India is now the second largest producer of fish in the world and the second largest aquaculture producer. The National Fisheries Development Board at Hyderabad and the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana are the main instruments of current fisheries policy.
Q: Which are the important buffalo and cattle breeds of India?
A: The Murrah buffalo of Haryana is the best known for high milk yield, followed by Jaffarabadi, Mehsana, Surti and Nili-Ravi. Among milch cattle, the important breeds are Gir, Sahiwal, Red Sindhi and Tharparkar, while Kankrej and Ongole are dual-purpose and Hallikar and Khillari are draught breeds. Candidates should remember the home state and the purpose of each breed.
Q: Which state leads in fish production and where is the National Fisheries Development Board located?
A: Andhra Pradesh is the leading fish producing state in India, followed by West Bengal and Gujarat. Inland fisheries now contribute a larger share of total fish production than marine fisheries. The National Fisheries Development Board, which coordinates the development of the fisheries sector, is headquartered at Hyderabad in Telangana.
Q: শ্বেত বিপ্লৱ কি আৰু ইয়াৰ পিতৃ কোন?
A: শ্বেত বিপ্লৱ, যাক অপাৰেশ্যন ফ্লাডও বোলা হয়, ১৯৭০ চনত আৰম্ভ কৰা এক কাৰ্যসূচী আছিল, যি ভাৰতক দুগ্ধত আত্মনিৰ্ভৰশীল কৰিবলৈ আৰু দুগ্ধ খেতিয়কৰ আয় বঢ়াবলৈ লক্ষ্য লৈছিল। ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় দুগ্ধ উন্নয়ন পৰিষদে ইয়াক ভাৰ্জিছ কুৰিয়েনৰ নেতৃত্বত তিনিটা পৰ্যায়ত ৰূপায়ণ কৰিছিল, যাক শ্বেত বিপ্লৱৰ পিতৃ বোলা হয়। ই ভাৰতক বিশ্বৰ সৰ্বাধিক দুগ্ধ উৎপাদক কৰি তুলিছিল আৰু আনন্দ ধৰণৰ দুগ্ধ সমবায় বিস্তাৰ কৰিছিল।
Q: দুগ্ধ সমবায়ৰ আনন্দ ধৰণ কি?
A: আনন্দ ধৰণ হৈছে এক তিনিস্তৰীয়া সমবায় গাঁথনি য'ত গাঁও দুগ্ধ সমিতিয়ে সদস্য খেতিয়কৰ পৰা দুগ্ধ সংগ্ৰহ কৰে, জিলা সংঘে দুগ্ধ প্ৰক্ৰিয়াকৰণ কৰে, আৰু ৰাজ্যিক মহাসংঘে বিপণন আৰু ব্ৰেণ্ড নিৰ্মাণ কৰে। খেতিয়কসকলে গোটেই শৃংখলাৰ মালিক, সেয়ে তেওঁলোকে গ্ৰাহকৰ টকাৰ এটা ন্যায্য অংশ পায়। কাইৰা জিলা দুগ্ধ উৎপাদক সমবায় সংঘ, অমুল ব্ৰেণ্ডৰ জৰিয়তে পৰিচিত, দেশজুৰি দুগ্ধ সমবায়ক অনুপ্ৰাণিত কৰা আৰ্হি।
Q: নীল বিপ্লৱ কি?
A: নীল বিপ্লৱে মীন পালন আৰু জলজ পালনৰ দ্ৰুত বিকাশক সূচায়, যি ভাৰতত ১৯৮৫-৮৬ চনত মাছ উৎপাদন বৃদ্ধি আৰু সংশ্লিষ্ট আন্তঃগাঁথনি নিৰ্মাণৰ বাবে আৰম্ভ কৰা হৈছিল। ভাৰত এতিয়া বিশ্বৰ দ্বিতীয় সৰ্বাধিক মাছ উৎপাদক আৰু দ্বিতীয় সৰ্বাধিক জলজ পালন উৎপাদক। হাইদৰাবাদৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় মীন উন্নয়ন পৰিষদ আৰু প্ৰধানমন্ত্ৰী মত্স্য সম্পদ যোজনা বৰ্তমান মীন নীতিৰ মূল সঁজুলি।
Q: ভাৰতৰ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ ম'হ আৰু গৰুৰ জাত কি কি?
A: হাৰিয়ানাৰ মুৰ্ৰাহ ম'হ উচ্চ দুগ্ধ উৎপাদনৰ বাবে আটাইতকৈ পৰিচিত, তাৰ পিছতে জাফৰাবাদী, মেহচানা, চুৰ্তি আৰু নীলি-ৰাভি। দুগ্ধ গৰুৰ ভিতৰত গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ জাত হৈছে গীৰ, চাহিৱাল, ৰেড সিন্ধী আৰু থাৰপাৰ্কাৰ, আনহাতে কাংক্ৰেজ আৰু ওংগলে দ্বৈত উদ্দেশ্যৰ আৰু হাল্লিকৰ আৰু খিল্লাৰী হালধৰা জাত। প্ৰাৰ্থীয়ে প্ৰতিটো জাতৰ ৰাজ্য আৰু উদ্দেশ্য মনত ৰখা উচিত।
Q: মাছ উৎপাদনত কোন ৰাজ্য আগশাৰী আৰু ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় মীন উন্নয়ন পৰিষদ ক'ত অৱস্থিত?
A: ভাৰতত অন্ধ্ৰ প্ৰদেশ আগশাৰী মাছ উৎপাদক ৰাজ্য, তাৰ পিছতে পশ্চিম বংগ আৰু গুজৰাট। অন্তঃস্থল মীন পালনে এতিয়া মুঠ মাছ উৎপাদনৰ সামুদ্ৰিক মীন পালনতকৈ বেছি অংশ আগবঢ়ায়। মীন খণ্ডৰ বিকাশ সমন্বয় কৰা ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় মীন উন্নয়ন পৰিষদৰ মুখ্য কাৰ্যালয় তেলেংগানাৰ হাইদৰাবাদত অৱস্থিত।

### Industrial Policies & Reforms (1991 Policy) — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/industrial-policies-1991-reforms/
Summary: Practice industrial policies & reforms (1991 policy) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: When was the first Industrial Policy Resolution of independent India announced?
A: The first Industrial Policy Resolution was announced in 1948.
Q: Which industries were under exclusive State monopoly in the IPR 1948?
A: Arms and ammunition, atomic energy and railways were under exclusive State monopoly.
Q: When was the second Industrial Policy Resolution adopted?
A: The second IPR was adopted in 1956, based on the Mahalanobis model of the Second Five Year Plan.
Q: Into how many categories did the IPR 1956 divide industries?
A: The IPR 1956 divided industries into three categories: Schedule A (exclusive State), Schedule B (State and private) and Schedule C (private).
Q: When was the New Industrial Policy of 1991 announced?
A: The New Industrial Policy was announced on 24 July 1991.
Q: Who was the Prime Minister of India during the 1991 economic reforms?
A: P.V. Narasimha Rao was the Prime Minister during the 1991 reforms.
Q: Who was the Finance Minister who presented the 1991-92 budget?
A: Dr. Manmohan Singh was the Finance Minister who presented the 1991-92 budget.
Q: What does LPG stand for in the context of the 1991 reforms?
A: LPG stands for Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation.
Q: What is the 1991 industrial policy also known as?
A: It is known as the LPG policy (Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation).
Q: What was abolished under the New Industrial Policy 1991?
A: The industrial licensing system was abolished except for a small list of industries.
Q: Which Act was replaced by FEMA in 1999?
A: FERA (Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973) was replaced by FEMA.
Q: What does FEMA stand for and when was it enacted?
A: FEMA stands for the Foreign Exchange Management Act, enacted in 1999.
Q: What is disinvestment?
A: Disinvestment is the sale of the government's equity stake in public sector enterprises to private investors.
Q: When was the Disinvestment Commission set up?
A: The Disinvestment Commission was set up in 1996.
Q: Which department of the Ministry of Finance handles disinvestment?
A: The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) handles disinvestment.
Q: What is the MRTP Act?
A: The MRTP Act (Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969) controlled monopolies and restrictive trade practices in the country.
Q: Which Act replaced the MRTP Act?
A: The Competition Act, 2002 replaced the MRTP Act.
Q: When was the Competition Commission of India established?
A: The Competition Commission of India was established in 2009 under the Competition Act, 2002.
Q: What is 'exit policy' in the context of the 1991 reforms?
A: Exit policy allows loss-making and sick industrial units to close down smoothly, often through Voluntary Retirement Schemes.
Q: What is the objective of the Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS) in PSUs?
A: VRS aims to reduce excess manpower in public sector units as part of the exit policy.
Q: What did the Industrial Policy of 1977 emphasize?
A: The Industrial Policy 1977 emphasized the development of small-scale, cottage and village industries.
Q: Who was the Prime Minister when the Industrial Policy 1977 was announced?
A: Morarji Desai was the Prime Minister when the Industrial Policy 1977 was announced.
Q: What was the objective of the New Industrial Policy 1991 regarding the public sector?
A: Its objective was to reduce the role of the public sector and restrict it to strategic areas.
Q: How many industries were reserved for the public sector under the 1991 policy?
A: Eight industries were reserved for the public sector, reduced from 17 in the 1956 policy.
Q: Which industries are reserved for the public sector in India today?
A: Arms and ammunition (defence), atomic energy and railway transport are reserved for the public sector.
Q: What is 'liberalisation'?
A: Liberalisation means the removal of government controls, licensing and restrictions on the economy and industry.
Q: What is 'globalisation' in the Indian economic context?
A: Globalisation is the integration of the Indian economy with the world economy through trade, investment and technology flows.
Q: What is a 'Navratna' PSU?
A: Navratna is a status given to select PSUs with strong financial performance that enjoy greater financial and operational autonomy.
Q: When was the Navratna scheme introduced?
A: The Navratna scheme was introduced in 1997.
Q: What was the main objective of industrial licensing under the 1956 policy?
A: The main objective was to regulate and control the establishment and expansion of industries according to plan priorities.
Q: Which industries remained under licensing even after the 1991 reforms?
A: Industries related to safety, security and hazardous chemicals, such as alcohol and cigarettes, remained under licensing.
Q: What did the Industrial Policy Statement of 1980 do?
A: Announced by Indira Gandhi's government, it relaxed restrictions on large industries and promoted modernisation and economic federalism.
Q: What was the foreign investment provision in the 1991 industrial policy?
A: Automatic approval was granted for foreign direct investment (FDI) up to 51 percent in many sectors.
Q: What is the primary objective of the New Industrial Policy 1991?
A: To make Indian industry competitive by freeing it from bureaucratic controls and integrating it with the global economy.
Q: What was the role change of the public sector under the 1991 policy?
A: The public sector was shifted from commercial activities to strategic, core and infrastructure activities only.
Q: Why is the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 important?
A: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 is called the economic constitution of India because it defined the country's industrial structure for decades. It adopted a socialistic pattern of society and classified industries into Schedule A with seventeen industries reserved for the state, Schedule B with twelve industries open to both state and private enterprise, and Schedule C containing the rest, mainly for the private sector. It also strengthened the licensing system.
Q: What were the main causes of the 1991 economic reforms?
A: The reforms were forced by a severe balance of payments crisis in which foreign exchange reserves fell to about two weeks of imports. A very high fiscal deficit, double-digit inflation, the rise in oil prices and the fall in remittances during the Gulf War, and the collapse of the Soviet Union together created the crisis. India sought assistance from the International Monetary Fund, whose conditions required structural reform.
Q: What is meant by the LPG reforms?
A: LPG stands for liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation, the three pillars of the New Industrial Policy of 1991. Liberalisation removed licensing and other controls and gave industry greater freedom. Privatisation involved reducing the role of the state through disinvestment and greater autonomy for public enterprises. Globalisation opened the economy to foreign trade and foreign direct investment. Together they integrated India with the world economy.
Q: What happened to the MRTP Act and FERA under the reforms?
A: The Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act of 1969, which controlled the growth of large business houses, was replaced by the Competition Act of 2002, which set up the Competition Commission of India to prevent anti-competitive practices. The Foreign Exchange Regulation Act of 1973 was replaced by the Foreign Exchange Management Act of 1999, which made the management of foreign exchange more liberal and business-friendly.
Q: What were the results of the 1991 industrial policy?
A: The reforms raised the overall growth rate of the economy, produced a boom in the services sector, increased foreign direct investment and gave consumers far greater choice. On the other hand, critics argue that growth was not accompanied by enough job creation, that the share of manufacturing did not rise as expected, and that inequality and regional imbalance persisted. These mixed results are frequently discussed in examinations.
Q: ১৯৫৬ চনৰ ঔদ্যোগিক নীতি প্ৰস্তাৱ কিয় গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: ১৯৫৬ চনৰ ঔদ্যোগিক নীতি প্ৰস্তাৱক ভাৰতৰ আৰ্থিক সংবিধান বোলা হয় কাৰণ ই দশকধৰি দেশৰ ঔদ্যোগিক গাঁথনি নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰিছিল। ই সমাজবাদী সমাজৰ আৰ্হি গ্ৰহণ কৰি উদ্যোগসমূহক A তালিকাত ৰাজ্যৰ বাবে সংৰক্ষিত সোতৰটা, B তালিকাত ৰাজ্য আৰু ব্যক্তিগত উদ্যোগ দুয়োৰে বাবে মুকলি বাৰটা, আৰু C তালিকাত বাকীসমূহ, মূলতঃ ব্যক্তিগত খণ্ডৰ বাবে শ্ৰেণীবদ্ধ কৰিছিল। ই অনুজ্ঞাপত্ৰ ব্যৱস্থাও সবল কৰিছিল।
Q: ১৯৯১ ৰ আৰ্থিক সংস্কাৰৰ মূল কাৰণ কি আছিল?
A: সংস্কাৰ এক গুৰুতৰ ভুৱন-লেনদেন সংকটৰ বাবে বাধ্যতামূলক হৈছিল, য'ত বিদেশী মুদ্ৰাৰ ভঁৰাল প্ৰায় দুসপ্তাহৰ আমদানিৰ সমানলৈ নামিছিল। অতি উচ্চ ৰাজকোষীয় ঘাটি, দুটা অংকৰ মূল্যস্ফীতি, উপসাগৰীয় যুদ্ধৰ সময়ত তেলৰ মূল্য বৃদ্ধি আৰু প্ৰেৰণ হ্ৰাস, আৰু ছোভিয়েট সংঘৰ পতনে একেলগে সংকট সৃষ্টি কৰিছিল। ভাৰতে আন্তঃৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় মুদ্ৰা নিধিৰ পৰা সহায় বিচাৰিছিল, যাৰ চৰ্তসমূহে গাঁথনিগত সংস্কাৰৰ দাবী কৰিছিল।
Q: LPG সংস্কাৰ মানে কি?
A: LPG মানে উদাৰীকৰণ, ব্যক্তিকৰণ আৰু বিশ্বায়ন, ১৯৯১ চনৰ নতুন ঔদ্যোগিক নীতিৰ তিনিটা স্তম্ভ। উদাৰীকৰণে অনুজ্ঞাপত্ৰ আৰু আন নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ আঁতৰাই উদ্যোগক বৃহত্তৰ স্বাধীনতা দিছিল। ব্যক্তিকৰণে বিনিয়োগ প্ৰত্যাহাৰ আৰু ৰাজহুৱা উদ্যোগক বৃহত্তৰ স্বয়ংচালিত ক্ষমতাৰ জৰিয়তে ৰাজ্যৰ ভূমিকা হ্ৰাস কৰিছিল। বিশ্বায়নে অৰ্থনীতিক বিদেশী বাণিজ্য আৰু প্ৰত্যক্ষ বিদেশী বিনিয়োগলৈ মুকলি কৰিছিল। একেলগে ই ভাৰতক বিশ্ব অৰ্থনীতিৰ লগত সংযুক্ত কৰিছিল।
Q: সংস্কাৰৰ অধীনত MRTP আইন আৰু FERA কি হ'ল?
A: বৃহৎ ব্যৱসায় গোষ্ঠীৰ বৃদ্ধি নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ কৰা ১৯৬৯ চনৰ একচেটিয়া আৰু নিষিদ্ধ বাণিজ্য ব্যৱহাৰ আইনক ২০০২ চনৰ প্ৰতিযোগিতা আইনেৰে প্ৰতিস্থাপন কৰা হৈছিল, যিয়ে প্ৰতিযোগিতাবিৰোধী ব্যৱহাৰ ৰোধ কৰিবলৈ ভাৰতীয় প্ৰতিযোগিতা আয়োগ স্থাপন কৰিছিল। ১৯৭৩ চনৰ বিদেশী বিনিময় নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ আইনক ১৯৯৯ চনৰ বিদেশী বিনিময় ব্যৱস্থাপনা আইনেৰে প্ৰতিস্থাপন কৰা হৈছিল, যিয়ে বিদেশী মুদ্ৰাৰ ব্যৱস্থাপনাক অধিক উদাৰ আৰু ব্যৱসায়-বান্ধৱ কৰি তুলিছিল।
Q: ১৯৯১ চনৰ ঔদ্যোগিক নীতিটিৰ ফলাফল কি আছিল?
A: সংস্কাৰে অৰ্থনীতিৰ সামগ্ৰিক বৃদ্ধিৰ হাৰ বঢ়াইছিল, সেৱা খণ্ডত উত্থান সৃষ্টি কৰিছিল, প্ৰত্যক্ষ বিদেশী বিনিয়োগ বৃদ্ধি কৰিছিল আৰু গ্ৰাহকক বহু বেছি বিকল্প দিছিল। আনহাতে সমালোচকসকলে যুক্তি দিয়ে যে বৃদ্ধিৰ লগত পৰ্যাপ্ত কৰ্ম সৃষ্টি হোৱা নাছিল, উৎপাদন খণ্ডৰ অংশ আশানুৰূপে নাবাঢ়িল, আৰু অসমতা আৰু আঞ্চলিক বৈষম্য থাকি গ'ল। এই মিশ্ৰিত ফলাফল পৰীক্ষাত সঘনাই আলোচনা কৰা হয়।

### Inflation & Price Indices (CPI, WPI) — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/inflation-price-indices-cpi-wpi/
Summary: Practice inflation & price indices (cpi, wpi) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What is the full form of CPI?
A: CPI stands for Consumer Price Index, which measures the average change over time in the prices of a basket of goods and services consumed by households.
Q: What does WPI measure?
A: WPI (Wholesale Price Index) measures the average change in prices of goods at the wholesale level, i.e., prices at which goods are traded in bulk.
Q: Which is the current base year for the Consumer Price Index in India?
A: The current base year for the Consumer Price Index in India is 2012.
Q: What is the base year for the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) in India?
A: The base year for the Wholesale Price Index in India is 2011-12.
Q: Who publishes the Consumer Price Index for the whole country (combined) in India?
A: The National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation publishes the national combined Consumer Price Index.
Q: Who publishes the Wholesale Price Index in India?
A: The Office of the Economic Adviser in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry publishes the Wholesale Price Index in India.
Q: Inflation caused by an increase in aggregate demand beyond the economy's capacity to produce is known as what?
A: It is known as demand-pull inflation.
Q: Inflation caused by an increase in the cost of production, such as rising wages or raw material prices, is called what?
A: It is called cost-push inflation.
Q: Which index is used by the Reserve Bank of India as the main measure of inflation for monetary policy in India?
A: The Reserve Bank of India uses the headline Consumer Price Index (Combined CPI) as the main measure of inflation for monetary policy.
Q: What is the inflation target set by the Government of India for the RBI under flexible inflation targeting?
A: The inflation target for the RBI is 4 percent, with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2 percent.
Q: Which committee recommended the adoption of flexible inflation targeting in India?
A: The committee headed by Urjit Patel recommended the adoption of flexible inflation targeting in India.
Q: Which statutory body sets the policy interest rate to meet the inflation target in India?
A: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Reserve Bank of India sets the policy interest rate (repo rate) to meet the inflation target.
Q: The rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks is known as what?
A: The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks against securities.
Q: What is 'core inflation'?
A: Core inflation is the measure of inflation excluding volatile items like food and fuel prices.
Q: Which of the following is an example of hyperinflation?
A: Hyperinflation refers to extremely high and accelerating inflation, where prices rise by more than 50 percent per month, as seen in Germany in the 1920s.
Q: Stagflation refers to a situation of what?
A: Stagflation is a situation where high inflation coexists with stagnant economic growth and high unemployment.
Q: What is the term for a continuous fall in the general price level?
A: A continuous fall in the general price level is known as deflation.
Q: A reduction in the rate of inflation over a period of time is known as what?
A: A reduction in the rate of inflation is known as disinflation.
Q: Which of the following indexes is used for calculating Dearness Allowance (DA) for government employees in India?
A: The All India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW) is used for calculating Dearness Allowance for government employees.
Q: Which CPI is used for the revision of minimum wages for agricultural labourers in India?
A: The Consumer Price Index for Agricultural Labourers (CPI-AL) is used for revising minimum wages of agricultural labourers.
Q: The GDP deflator is considered a better measure of inflation than WPI because it covers what?
A: The GDP deflator covers all final goods and services produced in the economy, including services, unlike WPI which covers only wholesale goods.
Q: Which index does not include services in its basket?
A: The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) does not include services in its basket of goods.
Q: A sustained increase in the general price level in an economy is called what?
A: A sustained increase in the general price level is called inflation.
Q: What is the Producer Price Index (PPI) primarily intended to measure?
A: PPI measures the average change in prices received by domestic producers for their output, i.e., prices at the producer level.
Q: Which of the following is a measure of 'cost-push inflation'?
A: A rise in the price of crude oil or raw materials is a measure/cause of cost-push inflation, as it raises production costs.
Q: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has how many members?
A: The MPC has six members - three from the RBI and three external members nominated by the government.
Q: Who is the ex-officio chairperson of the Monetary Policy Committee?
A: The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India is the ex-officio chairperson of the Monetary Policy Committee.
Q: Inflation in the range of 3 to 10 percent per annum is generally known as what type of inflation?
A: Inflation of 3 to 10 percent per annum is generally known as walking inflation or moderate inflation.
Q: Which of the following is a direct impact of high inflation on the economy?
A: High inflation reduces the purchasing power of money, eroding the real income of fixed-income earners.
Q: The 'hawala' traders and hoarders profiting from inflation contribute to which type of inflation?
A: Hoarding and black-marketing create artificial scarcity that contributes to speculative or demand-pull inflation.
Q: Which of the following is NOT a type of inflation based on rate?
A: Creeping, walking, running and galloping/hyperinflation are types based on rate; 'structural inflation' is not a rate-based classification.
Q: Which item has the highest weight in India's CPI (Combined) basket?
A: Food and beverages have the highest weight in India's combined CPI basket.
Q: In the WPI basket of India, which commodity group has the highest weight?
A: Manufactured products have the highest weight in India's WPI basket, followed by primary articles and fuel and power.
Q: Which of the following statements about deflation is TRUE?
A: Deflation is a general fall in prices which increases the real value of money and can lead to a recessionary spiral.
Q: The RBI's monetary policy committee meets how many times in a year typically?
A: The MPC typically meets at least four times a year to decide the policy rates.
Q: What is the main difference between WPI and CPI?
A: The Wholesale Price Index measures price changes in the wholesale market and covers only goods, not services, while the Consumer Price Index measures retail prices of a basket of goods and services actually consumed by households. Because the CPI reflects the cost of living, it is used by the Reserve Bank of India for inflation targeting, whereas the WPI is used mainly for analysing wholesale price trends.
Q: Who releases the CPI and the WPI in India?
A: The Consumer Price Index is released by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation. The Wholesale Price Index is released by the Office of the Economic Adviser in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The CPI-IW for industrial workers is compiled separately by the Labour Bureau.
Q: What is India's inflation target and who decides it?
A: India's flexible inflation-targeting framework, adopted through the Reserve Bank of India Act amendment of 2016, sets a target of four per cent consumer price inflation with a tolerance band of two to six per cent. The target is set by the government in consultation with the RBI, and the six-member Monetary Policy Committee chaired by the RBI Governor takes the decisions needed to achieve it.
Q: Who gains and who loses from inflation?
A: Debtors gain because they repay loans in money of reduced value, while creditors lose for the same reason. People on fixed incomes such as pensioners, and savers holding cash or fixed deposits, lose purchasing power, whereas traders and producers who can raise their prices faster than their costs tend to gain. Moderate inflation is therefore accepted, but high inflation harms most households.
Q: What is core inflation?
A: Core inflation is the rate of inflation calculated after excluding the most volatile items, typically food and fuel, from the price index. It is used because food and fuel prices can swing sharply due to seasonal or global factors and can hide the underlying trend. A rising core inflation figure usually signals that price pressure is spreading through the whole economy.
Q: WPI আৰু CPI ৰ মূল পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: পাইকাৰী মূল্য সূচকাংকই পাইকাৰী বজাৰৰ মূল্য পৰিৱৰ্তন জোখে আৰু কেৱল সামগ্ৰী সামৰে, সেৱা নহয়, আনহাতে ভোক্তা মূল্য সূচকাংকই পৰিয়ালে প্ৰকৃততে উপভোগ কৰা সামগ্ৰী-সেৱাৰ টোপোলাৰ খুচুৰা মূল্য জোখে। CPI য়ে জীৱনযাত্ৰাৰ ব্যয় প্ৰতিফলিত কৰাৰ বাবে ভাৰতীয় ৰিজাৰ্ভ বেংকে ইয়াক মূল্যস্ফীতি লক্ষ্যৰ বাবে ব্যৱহাৰ কৰে, আনহাতে WPI প্ৰধানকৈ পাইকাৰী মূল্যৰ প্ৰৱণতা বিশ্লেষণত ব্যৱহাৰ হয়।
Q: ভাৰতত CPI আৰু WPI কোনে প্ৰকাশ কৰে?
A: ভোক্তা মূল্য সূচকাংক পৰিসংখ্যা আৰু কাৰ্যসূচী ৰূপায়ণ মন্ত্ৰালয়ৰ অধীনত ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় পৰিসংখ্যা কাৰ্যালয়ে প্ৰকাশ কৰে। পাইকাৰী মূল্য সূচকাংক বাণিজ্য আৰু উদ্যোগ মন্ত্ৰালয়ৰ অৰ্থনৈতিক উপদেষ্টাৰ কাৰ্যালয়ে প্ৰকাশ কৰে। কৰ্মীসকলৰ বাবে CPI-IW শ্ৰম ছাত্ৰই সুকীয়াকৈ সংকলন কৰে।
Q: ভাৰতৰ মূল্যস্ফীতি লক্ষ্য কি আৰু কোনে নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰে?
A: ২০১৬ চনৰ ভাৰতীয় ৰিজাৰ্ভ বেংক আইন সংশোধনীৰ জৰিয়তে গ্ৰহণ কৰা নমনীয় মূল্যস্ফীতি লক্ষ্য আঁচনিয়ে চাৰি শতাংশ ভোক্তা মূল্য মূল্যস্ফীতিৰ লক্ষ্য নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰে, দুইৰ পৰা ছয় শতাংশ সহনশীল পট্টিৰ সৈতে। লক্ষ্য চৰকাৰে আৰ.বি.আই.ৰ পৰামৰ্শত নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰে, আৰু আৰ.বি.আই. গৱৰ্ণৰৰ নেতৃত্বত ছয়জনীয়া মুদ্ৰা নীতি সমিতিয়ে ইয়াক লাভ কৰাৰ বাবে প্ৰয়োজনীয় সিদ্ধান্ত লয়।
Q: মূল্যস্ফীতিত কোনে লাভ আৰু কোনে ক্ষতি কৰে?
A: ঋণগ্ৰহণকাৰীয়ে লাভ কৰে কাৰণ তেওঁলোকে কম মূল্যৰ টকাৰে ঋণ পৰিশোধ কৰে, আনহাতে ঋণদাতাই একেটা কাৰণতে ক্ষতি কৰে। পেন্সনধাৰীৰ দৰে স্থিৰ আয়ৰ লোক আৰু নগদ বা স্থিৰ জমা ৰখা সঞ্চয়কাৰীসকলে ক্ৰয় ক্ষমতা হেৰুৱায়, আনহাতে নিজৰ খৰচতকৈ দ্ৰুতগতিত মূল্য বঢ়াব পৰা ব্যৱসায়ী আৰু উৎপাদকে লাভ কৰিবলৈ ধৰে। সেয়ে মধ্যমীয়া মূল্যস্ফীতি গ্ৰহণ কৰা হয়, কিন্তু উচ্চ মূল্যস্ফীতিয়ে অধিকাংশ পৰিয়ালৰ ক্ষতি কৰে।
Q: মূল মূল্যস্ফীতি কি?
A: মূল মূল্যস্ফীতি হৈছে মূল্য সূচকাংকৰ পৰা আটাইতকৈ অস্থিৰ বস্তু, সাধাৰণতে খাদ্য আৰু ইন্ধন, বাদ দি গণনা কৰা মূল্যস্ফীতিৰ হাৰ। খাদ্য আৰু ইন্ধনৰ মূল্য ঋতু বা বিশ্ব কাৰণত তীক্ষ্ণভাৱে ওপৰ-তল হ'ব পাৰে আৰু মূল প্ৰৱণতা ঢাকি ৰাখিব পাৰে, সেয়ে ইয়াক ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা হয়। বঢ়া মূল মূল্যস্ফীতিৰ সংখ্যাই সাধাৰণতে মূল্যৰ চাপ গোটেই অৰ্থনীতিত বিয়পি পৰিছে বুলি সংকেত দিয়ে।

### MSME, Handloom & Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/msme-handloom-psus-india/
Summary: Practice msme, handloom & public sector undertakings (psus) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free.
Q: When was the MSME Development Act passed?
A: The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act was passed in 2006.
Q: On what basis is the new MSME classification (2020) done?
A: The new classification is based on both investment and annual turnover.
Q: What is the definition of a micro enterprise under the 2020 criteria?
A: A micro enterprise has investment up to ₹1 crore and turnover up to ₹5 crore.
Q: What is the definition of a small enterprise under the 2020 criteria?
A: A small enterprise has investment up to ₹10 crore and turnover up to ₹50 crore.
Q: What is the definition of a medium enterprise under the 2020 criteria?
A: A medium enterprise has investment up to ₹50 crore and turnover up to ₹250 crore.
Q: What is Udyam registration?
A: Udyam registration is a simple online registration portal for MSMEs, launched in 2020.
Q: Which ministry administers the MSME sector in India?
A: The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises administers the sector.
Q: What is the contribution of the MSME sector to India's GDP?
A: The MSME sector contributes about 30 percent of India's GDP.
Q: What is the share of MSMEs in India's manufacturing output?
A: MSMEs contribute about 37 to 38 percent of India's manufacturing output.
Q: What is the share of MSMEs in India's total exports?
A: MSMEs contribute about 45 percent of India's total exports.
Q: Approximately how many people are employed in the MSME sector?
A: The MSME sector provides employment to about 11 crore people.
Q: What percentage of MSMEs in India are micro enterprises?
A: Over 99 percent of MSMEs in India are micro enterprises.
Q: What is the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)?
A: KVIC is a statutory body established in 1957 for the promotion of khadi and village industries.
Q: Who is known as the father of khadi?
A: Mahatma Gandhi is known as the father of khadi.
Q: When is National Handloom Day celebrated?
A: National Handloom Day is celebrated on 7 August every year.
Q: Which historical event does National Handloom Day commemorate?
A: It commemorates the launch of the Swadeshi Movement in 1905.
Q: What is the 'Khadi Mark'?
A: Khadi Mark is a certification label introduced in 2013 to ensure that a product is genuine khadi.
Q: Which sector is the second largest employer in rural India after agriculture?
A: The handloom sector is the second largest employer in rural India after agriculture.
Q: What is the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM)?
A: NRLM is a scheme launched in 2011 to promote self-help groups and rural livelihoods.
Q: What is a Maharatna PSU?
A: Maharatna is the highest status given to top-performing central PSUs with very large net worth and financial strength.
Q: What is the net worth criterion for Maharatna status?
A: A PSU needs a minimum net worth of ₹10,000 crore to be eligible for Maharatna status.
Q: Which PSU was the first to receive Maharatna status?
A: Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) was the first to receive Maharatna status in 2010.
Q: What is a Navratna PSU?
A: A Navratna PSU is one with strong financial performance that enjoys enhanced autonomy and higher investment powers.
Q: What are the categories of Miniratna PSUs?
A: Miniratna PSUs are divided into Miniratna Category I and Miniratna Category II.
Q: What is a CPSE?
A: A CPSE (Central Public Sector Enterprise) is a public sector company in which the central government holds a majority stake.
Q: What is strategic disinvestment?
A: Strategic disinvestment is the sale of government equity along with the transfer of management control to a private buyer.
Q: What is BIFR?
A: BIFR is the Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction, set up in 1987 under the SICA, 1985 to revive sick industries.
Q: When was SICA enacted?
A: SICA, the Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, was enacted in 1985.
Q: Which body replaced BIFR?
A: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) replaced BIFR after the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.
Q: What is SIDBI and when was it established?
A: SIDBI is the Small Industries Development Bank of India, established in 1990.
Q: What is MUDRA?
A: MUDRA is the Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency Ltd, set up in 2015 to fund micro enterprises.
Q: What are the three categories of MUDRA loans?
A: The three categories are Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishor (₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh) and Tarun (₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh).
Q: What is the maximum amount of a MUDRA loan?
A: The maximum amount of a MUDRA loan is ₹10 lakh.
Q: What is the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana?
A: It is a scheme launched in April 2015 to provide collateral-free loans up to ₹10 lakh to non-corporate small business entities.
Q: What is the NSIC?
A: NSIC is the National Small Industries Corporation, established in 1955 to assist small industries.
Q: How are MSMEs classified in India at present?
A: MSMEs are classified by a combination of investment in plant and machinery or equipment and annual turnover. Following the revision effective from 1 April 2025, a micro enterprise has investment up to two and a half crore rupees and turnover up to ten crore rupees, a small enterprise up to twenty-five crore and one hundred crore rupees respectively, and a medium enterprise up to one hundred and twenty-five crore and five hundred crore rupees respectively.
Q: Why is the MSME sector called the backbone of the Indian economy?
A: The MSME sector contributes about thirty per cent of the gross domestic product and nearly forty-five per cent of exports, and it employs more than eleven crore people, making it the largest employer after agriculture. It produces a wide range of goods, supports large industry as an ancillary supplier, and generates employment at relatively low capital cost, which is why it is described as the backbone of the economy.
Q: What are the Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna categories?
A: These are categories created to grant greater autonomy to well-performing public sector enterprises. A Maharatna company can invest up to five thousand crore rupees in a project without government approval, a Navratna up to one thousand crore rupees, and Miniratna companies have lower ceilings. The status is based on financial performance such as average turnover or net profit and requires a positive net worth.
Q: What is the significance of the handloom sector and National Handloom Day?
A: The handloom sector is one of the largest rural employers after agriculture and is closely tied to India's cultural heritage. The government declared 2010 to 2020 as the Decade of Handloom and observes National Handloom Day on 7 August to recognise the contribution of weavers. The Handloom Mark certifies genuine handloom products, and Assam is especially known for Muga and Eri silk and the weaving centre of Sualkuchi.
Q: What is disinvestment and which body oversees it?
A: Disinvestment is the sale of a part of the government's equity holding in a public sector enterprise in order to raise resources, improve efficiency and widen public participation. It reduces the government's stake and does not necessarily mean full privatisation. The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management, under the Ministry of Finance, oversees the disinvestment programme.
Q: বৰ্তমান ভাৰতত MSME কেনেকৈ শ্ৰেণীবদ্ধ কৰা হয়?
A: MSME যন্ত্ৰ-পাতি বা সঁজুলিত বিনিয়োগ আৰু বছৰেকীয়া বৰ্তন-বিক্ৰীৰ সংমিশ্ৰণৰ দ্বাৰা শ্ৰেণীবদ্ধ কৰা হয়। ২০২৫ চনৰ ১ এপ্ৰিলৰ পৰা বলবৎ সংশোধন অনুসৰি অণু উদ্যোগৰ বিনিয়োগ আঢ়ৈ কোটি টকলৈকে আৰু বৰ্তন দহ কোটি টকলৈকে, ক্ষুদ্ৰ উদ্যোগৰ ক্ৰমে পঁচিশ কোটি আৰু এশ কোটি টকলৈকে, আৰু মধ্যম উদ্যোগৰ ক্ৰমে এশ পঁচিশ কোটি আৰু পাঁচশ কোটি টকলৈকে।
Q: MSME খণ্ডক ভাৰতীয় অৰ্থনীতিৰ মেৰুদণ্ড কিয় বোলা হয়?
A: MSME খণ্ডই মুঠ ঘৰুৱা উৎপাদনৰ প্ৰায় ত্ৰিশ শতাংশ আৰু ৰপ্তানিত প্ৰায় পঞ্চল্লিশ শতাংশ অৱদান আগবঢ়ায়, আৰু ই এঘাৰ কোটিৰো অধিক লোকক কৰ্মসংস্থাপন দিয়ে, যাৰ বাবে কৃষিৰ পিছত ই আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ নিয়োগকৰ্তা। ই বিস্তৃত সামগ্ৰী উৎপাদন কৰে, সহায়ক যোগানকাৰী হিচাপে বৃহৎ উদ্যোগক সহায় কৰে, আৰু তুলনামূলকভাৱে কম মূলধন খৰচত কৰ্মসংস্থাপন সৃষ্টি কৰে, সেয়েহে ইয়াক অৰ্থনীতিৰ মেৰুদণ্ড বোলা হয়।
Q: মহাৰত্ন, নৱৰত্ন আৰু মিনিৰত্ন শ্ৰেণী কি কি?
A: এইবোৰ ভাল কাম কৰা ৰাজহুৱা খণ্ডৰ উদ্যোগসমূহক বৃহত্তৰ স্বয়ংচালিত ক্ষমতা দিবলৈ সৃষ্টি কৰা শ্ৰেণী। মহাৰত্ন কোম্পানীয়ে চৰকাৰী অনুমতি অবিহনে কোনো প্ৰকল্পত পাঁচ হাজাৰ কোটি টকলৈকে বিনিয়োগ কৰিব পাৰে, নৱৰত্নই এহাজাৰ কোটি টকলৈকে, আৰু মিনিৰত্ন কোম্পানীৰ সীমা কম। মৰ্যাদা গড় বৰ্তন বা নিকা লাভৰ দৰে আৰ্থিক কাৰ্যদক্ষতাৰ ওপৰত আধাৰিত আৰু ধনাত্মক নিকা মূল্যৰ প্ৰয়োজন।
Q: তাঁতশাল খণ্ডৰ গুৰুত্ব আৰু ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় তাঁতশাল দিৱসৰ তাৎপৰ্য কি?
A: তাঁতশাল খণ্ড কৃষিৰ পিছত আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ গ্ৰাম্য নিয়োগকৰ্তাসমূহৰ এটা আৰু ভাৰতৰ সাংস্কৃতিক ঐতিহ্যৰ লগত ঘনিষ্ঠভাৱে জড়িত। চৰকাৰে ২০১০ ৰ পৰা ২০২০ লৈ তাঁতশালৰ দশক ঘোষণা কৰিছিল আৰু তাতীবসকলৰ অৱদান স্বীকৃতি দিবলৈ ৭ আগষ্টত ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় তাঁতশাল দিৱস পালন কৰে। তাঁতশাল মাৰ্কে প্ৰকৃত তাঁতশাল সামগ্ৰী প্ৰমাণিত কৰে, আৰু অসম বিশেষকৈ মূগা আৰু এৰী ৰেচম আৰু সুৱালকুচি তাঁত বোৱা কেন্দ্ৰৰ বাবে জনাজাত।
Q: বিনিয়োগ প্ৰত্যাহাৰ কি আৰু কোন সংস্থাই ইয়াৰ তদাৰক কৰে?
A: বিনিয়োগ প্ৰত্যাহাৰ হৈছে সম্পদ সংগ্ৰহ, দক্ষতা উন্নত আৰু ৰাজহুৱা অংশগ্ৰহণ বিস্তাৰ কৰাৰ বাবে ৰাজহুৱা খণ্ডৰ উদ্যোগত চৰকাৰৰ অংশীদাৰীত্বৰ এটা অংশ বিক্ৰী। ই চৰকাৰৰ অংশ হ্ৰাস কৰে আৰু অৱশ্যে সম্পূৰ্ণ ব্যক্তিকৰণ বুজাব নালাগে। বিত্ত মন্ত্ৰালয়ৰ অধীনত বিনিয়োগ প্ৰত্যাহাৰ আৰু ৰাজহুৱা সম্পদ ব্যৱস্থাপনা বিভাগে বিনিয়োগ প্ৰত্যাহাৰ কাৰ্যসূচীৰ তদাৰক কৰে।

### GDP, GNP, NNP & National Income — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/national-income-gdp-gnp-nnp/
Summary: Practice gdp, gnp, nnp & national income questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What is the full form of GDP?
A: GDP stands for Gross Domestic Product, which is the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given period.
Q: Which organization is responsible for the estimation of national income in India?
A: The National Statistical Office (NSO), under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, is responsible for estimating national income in India.
Q: Who was the chairman of the first National Income Committee of India in 1949?
A: Prof. P.C. Mahalanobis was the chairman of the first National Income Committee of India, formed in 1949.
Q: Who was the famous Indian economist associated with the estimation of India's first national income in 1931-32?
A: Prof. V.K.R.V. Rao made the first systematic estimate of India's national income for 1931-32.
Q: Which is the current base year used by India for computing national income and GDP estimates?
A: India's current base year for GDP and national income estimates is 2011-12.
Q: GDP at market price minus depreciation is known as what?
A: GDP at market price minus depreciation is known as Net Domestic Product (NDP) at market price.
Q: What does GNP stand for in national income accounting?
A: GNP stands for Gross National Product, which is GDP plus net factor income earned from abroad.
Q: What is the difference between GNP and NNP?
A: NNP (Net National Product) is obtained by deducting depreciation from GNP, i.e., NNP = GNP - Depreciation.
Q: National income of a country is equal to which aggregate?
A: National income is equal to Net National Product at factor cost (NNP at factor cost).
Q: What is the difference between GDP at market price and GDP at factor cost?
A: GDP at market price includes indirect taxes and excludes subsidies, while GDP at factor cost is market price minus net indirect taxes (indirect taxes minus subsidies).
Q: Which of the following is excluded while calculating GDP?
A: Intermediate goods and the value of second-hand goods are excluded while calculating GDP to avoid double counting.
Q: Which concept measures the money value of all final goods and services produced in a country adjusted for inflation?
A: Real GDP measures the money value of final goods and services adjusted for inflation using a base year price.
Q: Nominal GDP is measured at which prices?
A: Nominal GDP is measured at current year market prices, without adjusting for inflation.
Q: What is the GDP deflator?
A: GDP deflator is the ratio of nominal GDP to real GDP multiplied by 100, used to measure the price level of all goods and services in the economy.
Q: Which of the following is NOT a method of measuring national income?
A: All three methods - income, expenditure and output (product) method - are used to measure national income; there is no separate fourth standard method like 'comparative method'.
Q: Which method measures national income by adding up wages, rent, interest and profits?
A: The Income Method measures national income by adding up factor incomes like wages, rent, interest and profits.
Q: The output (product) method of national income measurement is also known as what?
A: The output method is also known as the value-added method or net product method.
Q: Which authority compiles the Consumer Price Index and national accounts statistics in India?
A: The National Statistical Office (NSO) of the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation compiles the Consumer Price Index and national accounts statistics in India.
Q: What was the earlier name of the National Statistical Office (NSO)?
A: The NSO was earlier called the Central Statistical Office (CSO), which was merged with NSSO to form NSO in 2019.
Q: What does NSSO stand for?
A: NSSO stands for National Sample Survey Office, which conducts socio-economic surveys in India.
Q: Which year's data is used as the base for India's current GDP series?
A: India's current GDP series is based on 2011-12 as the base year.
Q: In the new GDP series of 2011-12 base, which measure is used as the key indicator of economic growth?
A: In the new series, Gross Value Added (GVA) at basic prices is used as the key indicator of economic growth.
Q: What is Gross Value Added (GVA)?
A: GVA is the measure of the value of goods and services produced in an economy, calculated as GDP minus net product taxes (indirect taxes minus subsidies).
Q: Which sector contributes the largest share to India's GVA?
A: The services (tertiary) sector contributes the largest share to India's GVA, followed by industry and agriculture.
Q: Per capita income is obtained by dividing national income by which factor?
A: Per capita income is obtained by dividing national income by the total population of the country.
Q: Which among the following is included in national income of India?
A: Income from the services of factors of production produced within the domestic territory and net factor income from abroad is included in national income; capital gains and transfer payments are excluded.
Q: Which of the following is a transfer payment?
A: Pension and unemployment allowance are transfer payments, as they are made without any corresponding productive service.
Q: What is the term for GDP expressed in terms of constant prices?
A: GDP expressed in constant prices is called Real GDP.
Q: In the income method of national income, 'mixed income of self-employed' is included in which category?
A: Mixed income of self-employed is included in the category of operating surplus or as a part of factor incomes in the income method.
Q: Which of the following statements is true about the GDP deflator?
A: The GDP deflator reflects the price of all final goods and services produced domestically, unlike WPI or CPI which cover a basket of selected goods.
Q: Which committee recommended the shift to the 2011-12 base year for national accounts?
A: The committee headed by Dr. Abhijit Sen recommended the revision of the base year to 2011-12 for national accounts.
Q: What does GDP at factor cost represent?
A: GDP at factor cost represents the cost of all factors of production used in producing goods and services, equal to GDP at market price minus net indirect taxes.
Q: India's GDP ranks among the world's largest economies; as per recent estimates, India is the how many largest economy in the world?
A: As per recent estimates, India is the world's fifth largest economy by nominal GDP.
Q: Which of the following is NOT counted in the national income of a country?
A: Sale and purchase of shares and old/second-hand goods is not counted in national income as it does not add to the current flow of production.
Q: Which institution in India used to release the 'National Income Statistics' annually before the formation of NSO?
A: The Central Statistical Office (CSO) used to release National Income Statistics annually before it merged into the National Statistical Office.
Q: What is the difference between GDP and GNP?
A: GDP measures the value of final goods and services produced within the domestic territory of a country, no matter who produces them. GNP measures the value produced by the normal residents of the country, whether they produce it at home or abroad. GNP equals GDP plus net factor income from abroad, so a country with positive NFIA has a GNP higher than its GDP.
Q: Why is NNP at factor cost called National Income?
A: NNP is obtained after deducting depreciation from GNP, which gives the net output of the nation. When indirect taxes are removed and subsidies added, the figure represents the total income actually received by the factors of production, that is land, labour, capital and enterprise. This factor-cost figure is the definition of National Income used by economists.
Q: What are the three methods of measuring national income?
A: The product or value-added method sums net value added by all producing units, the income method sums all factor incomes such as wages, rent, interest and profit, and the expenditure method sums final expenditure on consumption, investment, government spending and net exports. In principle all three yield the same total because every expenditure is someone's income.
Q: What is the difference between real GDP and nominal GDP?
A: Nominal GDP is measured at current prices and therefore changes when prices change, even if output is unchanged. Real GDP is measured at the prices of a fixed base year and reflects only changes in the quantity of goods and services produced. Real GDP is used to measure economic growth in a meaningful way because it removes the effect of inflation.
Q: Which body releases India's national income estimates and on which base year?
A: The National Statistical Office, under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, releases India's national income estimates. The present series uses 2011-12 as the base year, which replaced the earlier base year of 2004-05, and the estimates are published both at current and constant prices.
Q: GDP আৰু GNP ৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: GDP এ এখন দেশৰ ঘৰুৱা ভূখণ্ডৰ ভিতৰত উৎপাদিত চূড়ান্ত সামগ্ৰী-সেৱাৰ মূল্য জোখে, যিয়ে উৎপাদন কৰে সেয়া নিৰ্বিশেষে। GNP এ দেশখনৰ স্বাভাৱিক বাসিন্দাসকলে উৎপাদন কৰা মূল্য জোখে, তেওঁলোকে ঘৰত বা বিদেশত উৎপাদন কৰা নিৰ্বিশেষে। GNP = GDP + বিদেশৰ পৰা নিকা কাৰক আয়, সেয়ে ধনাত্মক NFIA থকা দেশৰ GNP GDP তকৈ বেছি।
Q: কাৰক ব্যয়ত NNP ক ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় আয় বুলি কিয় কোৱা হয়?
A: GNP ৰ পৰা অৱক্ষয় বাদ দিলে ৰাষ্ট্ৰৰ নিকা উৎপাদন পোৱা যায়। পৰোক্ষ কৰ আঁতৰাই ৰাজসাহায্য যোগ কৰিলে সংখ্যাটোৱে উৎপাদনৰ কাৰকসমূহ, অৰ্থাৎ ভূমি, শ্ৰম, মূলধন আৰু উদ্যোগে প্ৰকৃততে পোৱা মুঠ আয় সূচায়। এই কাৰক-ব্যয় সংখ্যাটোৱেই অৰ্থনীতিবিদসকলে ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় আয়ৰ সংজ্ঞা।
Q: ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় আয় জোখাৰ তিনিটা পদ্ধতি কি কি?
A: উৎপাদন বা মূল্য সংযোজন পদ্ধতিয়ে সকলো উৎপাদন এককৰ নিকা মূল্য সংযোজন যোগ কৰে, আয় পদ্ধতিয়ে মজুৰি, ভাড়া, সুত আৰু লাভৰ দৰে সকলো কাৰক আয় যোগ কৰে, আৰু ব্যয় পদ্ধতিয়ে উপভোগ, বিনিয়োগ, চৰকাৰী ব্যয় আৰু নিকা ৰপ্তানিৰ চূড়ান্ত ব্যয় যোগ কৰে। নীতিগতভাৱে তিনিওটাই একে মুঠ দিয়ে কাৰণ প্ৰতিটো ব্যয় আন কাৰোবাৰ আয়।
Q: প্ৰকৃত আৰু নামমাত্ৰ GDP ৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: নামমাত্ৰ GDP বৰ্তমান মূল্যত জোখা হয়, সেয়ে উৎপাদন অপৰিৱৰ্তিত থাকিলেও মূল্য সলনি হ'লে ই সলনি হয়। প্ৰকৃত GDP এটা নিৰ্দিষ্ট ভিত্তি বছৰৰ মূল্যত জোখা হয় আৰু কেৱল উৎপাদিত সামগ্ৰী-সেৱাৰ পৰিমাণৰ পৰিৱৰ্তন প্ৰতিফলিত কৰে। মূল্যস্ফীতিৰ প্ৰভাৱ আঁতৰোৱাৰ বাবে আৰ্থিক বৃদ্ধি অৰ্থপূৰ্ণভাৱে জোখাৰ বাবে প্ৰকৃত GDP ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা হয়।
Q: ভাৰতৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় আয়ৰ অনুমান কোনে আৰু কোন ভিত্তি বছৰত প্ৰকাশ কৰে?
A: পৰিসংখ্যা আৰু কাৰ্যসূচী ৰূপায়ণ মন্ত্ৰালয়ৰ অধীনত ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় পৰিসংখ্যা কাৰ্যালয়ে ভাৰতৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় আয়ৰ অনুমান প্ৰকাশ কৰে। বৰ্তমান শৃংখলাত ২০১১-১২ ভিত্তি বছৰ, যিয়ে পূৰ্বৰ ২০০৪-০৫ ভিত্তি বছৰক প্ৰতিস্থাপন কৰিছে, আৰু অনুমানসমূহ বৰ্তমান তথা ধ্ৰুৱক দুয়ো মূল্যত প্ৰকাশ কৰা হয়।

### Physical Infrastructure (Highways, Railways, Ports
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/physical-infrastructure-nh-rail-ports-aviation/
Summary: Practice physical infrastructure (highways, railways, ports, aviation) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police.
Q: What is Bharatmala Pariyojana?
A: Bharatmala Pariyojana is a flagship umbrella programme of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways for the development of national highways, economic corridors, border roads and expressways across India.
Q: In which year was Bharatmala Pariyojana launched?
A: Bharatmala Pariyojana was launched in 2017; its Phase-I was approved by the Union Cabinet in October 2017.
Q: What is the Golden Quadrilateral project?
A: The Golden Quadrilateral is a national highway network connecting the four metropolitan cities of Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata, developed under the National Highways Development Project.
Q: What is the full form of NHAI and when was it established?
A: NHAI stands for National Highways Authority of India, established in 1988 under the National Highways Authority of India Act, 1988.
Q: Which agency implements the Golden Quadrilateral project?
A: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) implements the Golden Quadrilateral project.
Q: Which is the longest national highway of India?
A: NH-44, running from Srinagar to Kanyakumari (about 3,745 km), is the longest national highway of India.
Q: What is Sagarmala?
A: Sagarmala is a port-led development programme aimed at modernizing ports and promoting coastal economic development, under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.
Q: In which year was the Sagarmala programme launched?
A: The Sagarmala programme was approved and launched in 2015.
Q: Which is the largest container-handling port of India?
A: Jawaharlal Nehru Port (JNPT), also known as Nhava Sheva, located near Mumbai, is the largest container-handling port of India.
Q: Which is the oldest major port of India?
A: Kolkata Port, commissioned in 1870, is the oldest major port of India.
Q: Which is the largest natural harbour port of India?
A: Mumbai Port is the largest natural harbour port of India.
Q: Which is the deepest land-locked port of India?
A: Visakhapatnam Port in Andhra Pradesh is the deepest land-locked port of India.
Q: Which port was developed after independence to take over the traffic that earlier went to Karachi?
A: Kandla Port (now Deendayal Port) in Gujarat was developed after independence to handle the traffic that earlier passed through Karachi.
Q: How many major ports does India have after the recent additions?
A: India has 14 major ports, comprising the 12 traditional major ports plus Vadhvan Port and Galathea Bay Port added in 2024.
Q: Which ministry administers the major ports of India?
A: The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways administers the major ports of India.
Q: Which is the oldest artificial harbour port of India?
A: Chennai Port is the oldest artificial harbour port of India.
Q: What are Dedicated Freight Corridors?
A: Dedicated Freight Corridors are exclusive high-capacity railway lines meant only for freight traffic, being built by DFCCIL.
Q: What is the full form of DFCCIL?
A: DFCCIL stands for Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited.
Q: Name the two sanctioned Dedicated Freight Corridors of India.
A: The two sanctioned Dedicated Freight Corridors are the Eastern DFC (Ludhiana to Dankuni) and the Western DFC (JNPT to Dadri).
Q: What is the width of the broad gauge used by Indian Railways?
A: The broad gauge used by Indian Railways has a width of 1,676 millimetres (1.676 metres).
Q: Name the three gauges historically used by Indian Railways.
A: Indian Railways historically used broad gauge (1,676 mm), metre gauge (1,000 mm) and narrow gauge (762 mm or 610 mm).
Q: When did the first passenger train run in India and between which places?
A: The first passenger train ran on 16 April 1853 from Bori Bunder (Bombay) to Thane, a distance of about 34 kilometres.
Q: Which railway zone has its headquarters in Mumbai?
A: Central Railway has its headquarters in Mumbai (Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus).
Q: Which is the newest railway zone of India?
A: South Coast Railway, with its headquarters at Visakhapatnam, is the newest railway zone, created in 2019.
Q: What is the UDAN scheme?
A: UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) is the Regional Connectivity Scheme launched in 2017 to make air travel affordable for the common man by connecting unserved and underserved airports.
Q: Which ministry implements the UDAN scheme?
A: The Ministry of Civil Aviation implements the UDAN scheme, in coordination with the Airports Authority of India and airlines.
Q: When was the Airports Authority of India (AAI) constituted?
A: The Airports Authority of India was constituted on 1 April 1995 by the merger of the International Airports Authority of India and the National Airports Authority.
Q: Which was the first airport of India built under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model?
A: Cochin (Kochi) International Airport was the first Indian airport built under the PPP model, becoming operational in 1999.
Q: Which was the first metro rail system of India and in which year did it start?
A: Kolkata Metro, which started operations in 1984, was the first metro rail system of India and also the first underground metro.
Q: What is the National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP)?
A: NIP is a flagship initiative announced in 2019 to provide world-class infrastructure, with a projected investment of about ₹111 lakh crore during FY2020-25.
Q: Which department coordinates the National Infrastructure Pipeline?
A: The Department of Economic Affairs, under the Ministry of Finance, coordinates the National Infrastructure Pipeline.
Q: Which sectors dominate the investment under the National Infrastructure Pipeline?
A: Energy (power), roads, urban infrastructure and railways are the top sectors dominating investment under NIP.
Q: What is NIIF?
A: NIIF, the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund, is India's quasi-sovereign wealth fund created for financing infrastructure projects.
Q: When was NIIF established?
A: NIIF was established in 2015, announced in the Union Budget 2015-16.
Q: Which institution provides long-term financing for infrastructure projects in India?
A: India Infrastructure Finance Company Ltd (IIFCL) provides long-term debt financing for infrastructure projects, along with NIIF and other financial institutions.
Q: What is Bharatmala Pariyojana and when was it launched?
A: Bharatmala Pariyojana is a flagship umbrella programme of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways for developing national highways, economic corridors, border roads and expressways across India. It was launched in 2017, with Phase I approved by the Union Cabinet in October 2017. Its objective is to improve road connectivity, reduce travel time and lower logistics costs so that trade and industry become more competitive.
Q: What is Sagarmala and what are the important ports of India?
A: Sagarmala is a port-led development programme launched in 2015 under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways to modernise ports and promote coastal economic development. Jawaharlal Nehru Port is the largest container-handling port, Kolkata is the oldest major port, Mumbai Port is the largest natural harbour, Visakhapatnam is the deepest land-locked port and Chennai is the oldest artificial harbour. India now has fourteen major ports.
Q: What are Dedicated Freight Corridors and which ones are sanctioned?
A: Dedicated Freight Corridors are exclusive high-capacity railway lines meant only for freight traffic, and they are being built by the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited. Two corridors are sanctioned: the Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor from Ludhiana to Dankuni and the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor from Jawaharlal Nehru Port to Dadri. They are meant to speed up freight movement and free up capacity on the passenger network.
Q: What is the UDAN scheme and who implements it?
A: UDAN, which stands for Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik, is the Regional Connectivity Scheme launched in 2017 to make air travel affordable for the common citizen by connecting unserved and underserved airports. It is implemented by the Ministry of Civil Aviation, in coordination with the Airports Authority of India and the airlines. The Airports Authority of India was constituted on 1 April 1995.
Q: What is the National Infrastructure Pipeline and who coordinates it?
A: The National Infrastructure Pipeline is a flagship initiative announced in 2019 to provide world-class infrastructure, with a projected investment of about one hundred and eleven lakh crore rupees during the period from 2020 to 2025. It is coordinated by the Department of Economic Affairs under the Ministry of Finance, and energy, roads, urban infrastructure and railways are the leading sectors. The National Investment and Infrastructure Fund, established in 2015, is a quasi-sovereign wealth fund for infrastructure finance.
Q: ভাৰতমালা পৰিয়োজনা কি আৰু কেতিয়া আৰম্ভ হৈছিল?
A: ভাৰতমালা পৰিয়োজনা হৈছে পথ পৰিবহণ আৰু মহাসড়ক মন্ত্ৰালয়ৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় মহাসড়ক, অৰ্থনৈতিক কৰিডৰ, সীমান্ত পথ আৰু দ্ৰুপথ বিকাশৰ প্ৰধান ছাতা কাৰ্যসূচী। ই ২০১৭ চনত আৰম্ভ কৰা হৈছিল, আৰু প্ৰথম পৰ্যায় কেন্দ্ৰীয় মন্ত্ৰীসভাই ২০১৭ চনৰ অক্টোবৰত অনুমোদন কৰিছিল। ইয়াৰ উদ্দেশ্য পথ সংযোগ উন্নত কৰা, যাত্ৰাৰ সময় কমোৱা আৰু লজিষ্টিক খৰচ কমাই বাণিজ্য তথা উদ্যোগ অধিক প্ৰতিযোগিতামূলক কৰা।
Q: সাগৰমালা কি আৰু ভাৰতৰ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ বন্দৰসমূহ কি কি?
A: সাগৰমালা হৈছে ২০১৫ চনত জাহাজ চলাচল তথা জলপথ মন্ত্ৰালয়ৰ অধীনত বন্দৰ আধুনিকীকৰণ আৰু উপকূলীয় অৰ্থনৈতিক উন্নয়ন প্ৰসাৰৰ বাবে আৰম্ভ কৰা বন্দৰ-চালিত উন্নয়ন কাৰ্যসূচী। জৱাহৰলাল নেহৰু বন্দৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ কণ্টেইনাৰ পৰিচালনা কৰা বন্দৰ, কলকাতা আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি প্ৰধান বন্দৰ, মুম্বাই আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ প্ৰাকৃতিক বন্দৰ, বিশাখাপট্টনম আটাইতকৈ গভীৰ আৰু চেন্নাই আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি কৃত্ৰিম বন্দৰ। ভাৰতত এতিয়া চৈধ্যটা প্ৰধান বন্দৰ আছে।
Q: সমৰ্পিত মালবাহী কৰিডৰ কি আৰু কোনবোৰ অনুমোদিত?
A: সমৰ্পিত মালবাহী কৰিডৰ হৈছে কেৱল মালবাহী পৰিবহণৰ বাবে নিৰ্মিত বিশেষ উচ্চ ক্ষমতাৰ ৰে\'লপথ, আৰু এইবোৰ সমৰ্পিত মালবাহী কৰিডৰ নিগম লিমিটেডে নিৰ্মাণ কৰি আছে। দুটা কৰিডৰ অনুমোদিত: লুধিয়ানাৰ পৰা ডানকুনীলৈ পূৱ সমৰ্পিত মালবাহী কৰিডৰ আৰু জৱাহৰলাল নেহৰু বন্দৰৰ পৰা দাদৰীলৈ পশ্চিম সমৰ্পিত মালবাহী কৰিডৰ। ইহঁতৰ উদ্দেশ্য মালবাহী চলাচল দ্ৰুত কৰা আৰু যাত্ৰীবাহী নেটৱৰ্কত ক্ষমতা মুকলি কৰা।
Q: UDAN আঁচনি কি আৰু কোনে ৰূপায়ণ কৰে?
A: UDAN, যাৰ অৰ্থ উড়ে দেশ কা আাম নাগৰিক, হৈছে ২০১৭ চনত আৰম্ভ কৰা আঞ্চলিক সংযোগ আঁচনি যি সেৱাহীন আৰু অসম্পূৰ্ণভাৱে সেৱা পোৱা বিমানবন্দৰসমূহ সংযোগ কৰি সাধাৰণ নাগৰিকৰ বাবে বিমান ভ্ৰমণ সুলভ কৰে। ই বেসামৰিক বিমান পৰিবহণ মন্ত্ৰালয়ে বিমানবন্দৰ প্ৰাধিকৰণ আৰু বিমান সংস্থাসমূহৰ সৈতে সমন্বয় কৰি ৰূপায়ণ কৰে। ভাৰতীয় বিমানবন্দৰ প্ৰাধিকৰণ ১৯৯৫ চনৰ ১ এপ্ৰিলত গঠন কৰা হৈছিল।
Q: ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় আন্তঃগাঁথনি পাইপলাইন কি আৰু কোনে সমন্বয় কৰে?
A: ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় আন্তঃগাঁথনি পাইপলাইন হৈছে ২০১৯ চনত ঘোষণা কৰা প্ৰধান পদক্ষেপ যি বিশ্বমানৰ আন্তঃগাঁথনি প্ৰদানৰ লক্ষ্য ৰাখে, ২০২০ ৰ পৰা ২০২৫ চনৰ সময়ছোৱাত প্ৰায় এশ এঘাৰ লাখ কোটি টকা বিনিয়োগৰ প্ৰক্ষেপণসহ। ই অৰ্থ মন্ত্ৰালয়ৰ অধীনত অৰ্থনৈতিক পৰিক্ৰমা বিভাগে সমন্বয় কৰে, আৰু শক্তি, পথ, চহৰীয়া আন্তঃগাঁথনি আৰু ৰে\'লৱে আগশাৰীৰ খণ্ড। ২০১৫ চনত প্ৰতিষ্ঠিত ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় বিনিয়োগ আৰু আন্তঃগাঁথনি নিধি আন্তঃগাঁথনি বিত্তৰ বাবে অৰ্ধ-সাৰ্বভৌম সম্পদ নিধি।

### Five-Year Plans History & NITI Aayog — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/planning-history-niti-aayog/
Summary: Practice five-year plans history & niti aayog questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: In which year was the Planning Commission established in India?
A: The Planning Commission was established on 15 March 1950.
Q: Who was the first Chairman of the Planning Commission?
A: Jawaharlal Nehru, as the Prime Minister, was the first Chairman of the Planning Commission.
Q: The First Five Year Plan covered which period?
A: The First Five Year Plan covered the period 1951-56.
Q: Which model was the basis of the First Five Year Plan?
A: The First Five Year Plan was based on the Harrod-Domar growth model.
Q: Which sector received the highest allocation in the First Five Year Plan?
A: Agriculture received the highest allocation in the First Five Year Plan.
Q: Which model was the basis of the Second Five Year Plan?
A: The Second Five Year Plan was based on the Mahalanobis model emphasising heavy industry.
Q: Who designed the Second Five Year Plan model?
A: The model for the Second Five Year Plan was designed by statistician P.C. Mahalanobis.
Q: Which plan was drafted by M.N. Roy in 1944?
A: M.N. Roy drafted the 'People's Plan' in 1944.
Q: The 'Gandhi Plan' was drafted by whom?
A: The 'Gandhi Plan' was drafted by Sriman Narayan Agarwal in 1944.
Q: The 'Bombay Plan' was prepared by a group of prominent industrialists in which year?
A: The 'Bombay Plan' was prepared in 1944 by a group of leading industrialists including J.R.D. Tata.
Q: What was the main objective of the Third Five Year Plan?
A: The main objective of the Third Plan was self-reliance and self-sustaining growth of the economy.
Q: The period from 1966 to 1969 is known as what in Indian planning history?
A: The period 1966-69 is known as the 'plan holiday' when no Five Year Plan was in operation.
Q: During the plan holiday (1966-69), which annual plans were implemented?
A: Three annual plans were implemented during 1966-67, 1967-68 and 1968-69.
Q: Who introduced the concept of the 'rolling plan' in India?
A: The concept of the rolling plan was suggested by Gunnar Myrdal, and later advocated by D.T. Lakdawala.
Q: Which plan gave importance to the slogan 'Garibi Hatao' (remove poverty)?
A: The Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-79) gave importance to the slogan 'Garibi Hatao' with emphasis on poverty removal and self-reliance.
Q: Which plan is also called the 'Gadgil Plan'?
A: The Third Five Year Plan (1961-66) is also known as the 'Gadgil Plan' as it was drafted under D.R. Gadgil.
Q: The Gadgil formula is used for the distribution of what?
A: The Gadgil formula was used for the distribution of central assistance to states for development plans.
Q: What is the specific weightage given to the population criterion in the Gadgil formula?
A: Population had the highest weightage of 60% in the Gadgil formula for distribution of central assistance.
Q: In which year was the NITI Aayog established?
A: The NITI Aayog was established on 1 January 2015.
Q: NITI Aayog replaced which institution?
A: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission.
Q: What is the full form of NITI in NITI Aayog?
A: NITI stands for National Institution for Transforming India.
Q: Who is the ex-officio Chairperson of the NITI Aayog?
A: The Prime Minister of India is the ex-officio Chairperson of the NITI Aayog.
Q: Who was the first Vice-Chairman of the NITI Aayog?
A: Arvind Panagariya was the first Vice-Chairman of the NITI Aayog.
Q: In which year was the 12th Five Year Plan, the last Five Year Plan, completed?
A: The 12th Five Year Plan covered 2012-17 and ended in 2017.
Q: Which committee recommended the abolition of the Planning Commission?
A: The suggestion to replace the Planning Commission with NITI Aayog was announced by the government; the move drew on recommendations for reforming planning bodies.
Q: What is the 'Aspirational Districts Programme' of the NITI Aayog?
A: The Aspirational Districts Programme aims to rapidly transform the most backward districts of India across several development indicators.
Q: The 'National Development Agenda' is a programme of which institution?
A: The National Development Agenda is a programme of the NITI Aayog.
Q: Who was the Prime Minister when the Planning Commission was abolished in 2014?
A: Narendra Modi was the Prime Minister when the Planning Commission was abolished in 2014.
Q: Which Five Year Plan achieved the highest GDP growth rate of over 8%?
A: The 11th Five Year Plan (2007-12) achieved an average GDP growth rate of about 8%.
Q: The Planning Commission was set up by which Government Resolution?
A: The Planning Commission was set up by a Government of India Resolution dated 15 March 1950.
Q: Which plan emphasised 'Food, Work and Productivity'?
A: The Fourth Five Year Plan (1969-74) emphasised 'Food, Work and Productivity'.
Q: Which famous economist served as the Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission and is called the architect of the Indian planning model?
A: P.C. Mahalanobis served as an important architect of Indian planning, though D.R. Gadgil and others also served as Deputy Chairman.
Q: In which year did the NITI Aayog release the National Multidimensional Poverty Index?
A: The NITI Aayog released the first National Multidimensional Poverty Index in November 2021.
Q: Which of the following is a core objective of the NITI Aayog?
A: Fostering cooperative federalism and formulating strategic long-term vision for the economy are core objectives of the NITI Aayog.
Q: The NITI Aayog launched the 'Atal Innovation Mission' to promote what?
A: The Atal Innovation Mission was launched to promote a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship in schools and across the country.
Q: When was the Planning Commission set up and who was its first Chairman?
A: The Planning Commission was established on 15 March 1950 by a resolution of the Government of India. The Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, was its first Chairman, since the Prime Minister has always been the Chairman of the Commission. The Commission prepared the Five-Year Plans and allocated resources for development until it was replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015.
Q: What were the Harrod-Domar and Mahalanobis models?
A: The Harrod-Domar model, which stresses savings and investment as the drivers of growth, formed the basis of the First Five-Year Plan, and agriculture received the highest allocation under it. The Mahalanobis model, designed by the statistician P. C. Mahalanobis, formed the basis of the Second Five-Year Plan and emphasised the development of heavy industry, which shaped India's industrial base.
Q: What is the plan holiday in Indian planning history?
A: The plan holiday refers to the period from 1966 to 1969, when no Five-Year Plan was in operation because of economic difficulties and the pressures of war and drought. During this gap, three annual plans were implemented for 1966-67, 1967-68 and 1968-69. The next full plan began in 1969 with the Fourth Five-Year Plan.
Q: What is the NITI Aayog and how does it differ from the Planning Commission?
A: The NITI Aayog, or National Institution for Transforming India, was established on 1 January 2015 and replaced the Planning Commission. Unlike the old Commission, which allocated resources to states, the NITI Aayog works as a policy think tank and promotes cooperative federalism, in which the centre and states act as partners. The Prime Minister is its ex-officio Chairperson, and Arvind Panagariya was its first Vice-Chairman.
Q: What is the Aspirational Districts Programme?
A: The Aspirational Districts Programme of the NITI Aayog aims to rapidly transform the most backward districts of India across several development indicators. It focuses on areas such as health and nutrition, education, agriculture and basic infrastructure, and it uses competitive and cooperative methods to improve outcomes. It is one of the flagship programmes of the NITI Aayog.
Q: পৰিকল্পনা আয়োগ কেতিয়া স্থাপন কৰা হৈছিল আৰু ইয়াৰ প্ৰথম অধ্যক্ষ কোন আছিল?
A: পৰিকল্পনা আয়োগ ১৯৫০ চনৰ ১৫ মাৰ্চত ভাৰত চৰকাৰৰ এটা প্ৰস্তাৱৰ জৰিয়তে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰা হৈছিল। প্ৰধানমন্ত্ৰী জৱাহৰলাল নেহৰু ইয়াৰ প্ৰথম অধ্যক্ষ আছিল, কাৰণ প্ৰধানমন্ত্ৰীয়ে সদায় আয়োগৰ অধ্যক্ষ হৈ আহিছে। আয়োগে পঞ্চবৰ্ষীয় পৰিকল্পনা প্ৰস্তুত কৰিছিল আৰু ২০১৫ চনত নীতি আয়োগে ইয়াক প্ৰতিস্থাপন কৰালৈকে উন্নয়নৰ বাবে সম্পদ আবণ্টন কৰিছিল।
Q: হেৰড-ডোমাৰ আৰু মহালানোবিছ আৰ্হি কি আছিল?
A: হেৰড-ডোমাৰ আৰ্হি, যি বৃদ্ধিৰ চালক হিচাপে সঞ্চয় আৰু বিনিয়োগৰ ওপৰত গুৰুত্ব দিয়ে, প্ৰথম পঞ্চবৰ্ষীয় পৰিকল্পনাৰ ভিত্তি আছিল, আৰু ইয়াৰ অধীনত কৃষিয়ে সৰ্বাধিক বিনিয়োগ লাভ কৰিছিল। মহালানোবিছ আৰ্হি, পৰিসংখ্যাবিদ পি. চি. মহালানোবিছে বিকশিত কৰা, দ্বিতীয় পঞ্চবৰ্ষীয় পৰিকল্পনাৰ ভিত্তি আছিল আৰু গধুৰ উদ্যোগৰ বিকাশৰ ওপৰত গুৰুত্ব দিছিল, যি ভাৰতৰ औद्योगिक ভিত্তি গঢ় দিছিল।
Q: ভাৰতীয় পৰিকল্পনাৰ ইতিহাসত পৰিকল্পনা বিৰতি কি?
A: পৰিকল্পনা বিৰতি বলতে ১৯৬৬ ৰ পৰা ১৯৬৯ চনলৈকে সময়ছোৱাক বুজায়, যেতিয়া অৰ্থনৈতিক কঠিনতা আৰু যুদ্ধ তথা খৰাং পৰিস্থিতিৰ চাপত কোনো পঞ্চবৰ্ষীয় পৰিকল্পনা চলি নাছিল। এই ব্যৱধানত ১৯৬৬-৬৭, ১৯৬৭-৬৮ আৰু ১৯৬৮-৬৯ চনৰ বাবে তিনিটা বাৰ্ষিক পৰিকল্পনা ৰূপায়ণ কৰা হৈছিল। পৰৱৰ্তী পূৰ্ণ পৰিকল্পনা ১৯৬৯ চনত চতুৰ্থ পঞ্চবৰ্ষীয় পৰিকল্পনাৰে আৰম্ভ হৈছিল।
Q: নীতি আয়োগ কি আৰু ই পৰিকল্পনা আয়োগৰ পৰা কেনেকৈ পৃথক?
A: নীতি আয়োগ, বা ৰূপান্তৰকাৰী ভাৰতৰ বাবে ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় প্ৰতিষ্ঠান, ২০১৫ চনৰ ১ জানুৱাৰীত প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰা হৈছিল আৰু ই পৰিকল্পনা আয়োগক প্ৰতিস্থাপন কৰিছিল। ৰাজ্যসমূহলৈ সম্পদ আবণ্টন কৰা পুৰণি আয়োগৰ বিপৰীতে, নীতি আয়োগে এক নীতি চিন্তা থলী হিচাপে কাম কৰে আৰু সহযোগিতা মূলক সংঘীয়তা প্ৰসাৰ কৰে, য'ত কেন্দ্ৰ আৰু ৰাজ্যসমূহে অংশীদাৰ হিচাপে কাম কৰে। প্ৰধানমন্ত্ৰী ইয়াৰ পদাধিকাৰিক অধ্যক্ষ, আৰু অৰবিন্দ পনাগৰিয়া প্ৰথম উপাধ্যক্ষ আছিল।
Q: এস্পিৰেচনেল ডিষ্ট্ৰিক্টছ কাৰ্যসূচী কি?
A: নীতি আয়োগৰ এস্পিৰেচনেল ডিষ্ট্ৰিক্টছ কাৰ্যসূচীয়ে কেইবাটাও উন্নয়ন সূচকত ভাৰতৰ আটাইতকৈ পিছপৰা জিলাসমূহক দ্ৰুতভাৱে ৰূপান্তৰিত কৰাৰ লক্ষ্য ৰাখে। ই স্বাস্থ্য আৰু পুষ্টি, শিক্ষা, কৃষি আৰু মৌলিক আন্তঃগাঁথনিৰ দৰে ক্ষেত্ৰত গুৰুত্ব দিয়ে, আৰু ফলাফল উন্নত কৰিবলৈ প্ৰতিযোগিতামূলক তথা সহযোগিতা মূলক পদ্ধতি ব্যৱহাৰ কৰে। ই নীতি আয়োগৰ প্ৰধান কাৰ্যসূচীসমূহৰ এটা।

### Poverty, Inequality & Unemployment — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/poverty-inequality-unemployment-india/
Summary: Practice poverty, inequality & unemployment questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Which committee defined the poverty line in India on the basis of calorie intake?
A: The Y.K. Alagh Committee (1979) defined the poverty line on the basis of calorie intake of 2400 and 2100 calories.
Q: Which committee recommended the poverty line in India in 2009?
A: The Tendulkar Committee recommended the poverty line in India in 2009.
Q: What is the Tendulkar Committee poverty line per capita per day (at 2011-12 prices)?
A: The Tendulkar Committee fixed the rural poverty line at about ₹33 per day and urban at about ₹47 per day at 2011-12 prices.
Q: Which committee was constituted to review the Tendulkar poverty line methodology?
