A: The Rangarajan Committee was constituted in 2012 to review the Tendulkar methodology.
Q: What is the full form of BPL?
A: BPL stands for Below Poverty Line.
Q: Poverty ratio is also known as which measure?
A: Poverty ratio is also known as the Head Count Ratio (HCR).
Q: The Gini coefficient is used to measure what?
A: The Gini coefficient is used to measure income or wealth inequality.
Q: What is the range of the Gini coefficient?
A: The Gini coefficient ranges from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (perfect inequality).
Q: If the Gini coefficient of India increases, what does it indicate?
A: An increase in the Gini coefficient indicates rising income inequality in India.
Q: Which survey of India is the primary source of unemployment statistics?
A: The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) is the primary source of unemployment statistics in India.
Q: What is the full form of PLFS?
A: PLFS stands for Periodic Labour Force Survey.
Q: Which organization conducts the PLFS in India?
A: The National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) under the Ministry of Statistics conducts the PLFS.
Q: NSSO stands for which organization?
A: NSSO stands for National Sample Survey Office.
Q: Which type of unemployment occurs when workers are temporarily out of work while changing jobs?
A: Frictional unemployment occurs when workers are temporarily unemployed while moving between jobs.
Q: Which type of unemployment arises due to a mismatch between skills and available jobs?
A: Structural unemployment arises due to a mismatch between the skills of workers and the requirements of available jobs.
Q: Which type of unemployment is common in Indian agriculture during off-season?
A: Seasonal unemployment is common in Indian agriculture during the non-cropping season.
Q: Disguised unemployment is most prevalent in which sector?
A: Disguised unemployment is most prevalent in the agriculture sector where more workers are employed than needed.
Q: What is disguised unemployment?
A: Disguised unemployment exists when people appear employed but their marginal productivity is zero or negligible.
Q: Which type of unemployment is associated with the business cycle?
A: Cyclical unemployment is associated with downturns in the business cycle.
Q: Unemployment arising during a recession is called what?
A: Unemployment arising during a recession is called cyclical or demand-deficit unemployment.
Q: The 'Skill India' mission was launched in which year?
A: The Skill India mission was launched on 15 July 2015.
Q: What is the headcount ratio in poverty measurement?
A: Headcount ratio is the proportion of the population living below the poverty line.
Q: The NITI Aayog released the National MPI for which year?
A: The NITI Aayog released the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) for 2023 based on NFHS-5 data.
Q: Who developed the global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)?
A: The global MPI was developed by the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and the UNDP.
Q: What is a gig economy?
A: A gig economy is a labour market characterised by short-term, flexible and freelance jobs, often through digital platforms.
Q: Which of the following is an example of the gig economy workforce?
A: Cab and food delivery partners working on digital platforms such as Ola, Uber and Zomato are gig economy workers.
Q: What is the unemployment rate?
A: The unemployment rate is the percentage of the labour force that is unemployed and seeking work.
Q: What is the difference between the usual status and current weekly status of unemployment?
A: Usual status measures employment over the past year, while current weekly status measures employment during the reference week.
Q: Which of the following schemes provides urban employment to unskilled workers?
A: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) provides rural employment; urban schemes include programmes like the National Urban Livelihoods Mission.
Q: Which commission estimated that poverty ratio in India was about 22% in 2011-12?
A: The Tendulkar Committee methodology estimated the poverty ratio at about 21.9% in 2011-12.
Q: What does MPI stand for in poverty measurement?
A: MPI stands for Multidimensional Poverty Index.
Q: How many indicators are used in the National MPI of India?
A: The National MPI of India uses 12 indicators across three dimensions: health, education and living standards.
Q: Which of the following is a dimension of the Multidimensional Poverty Index — Health, Fashion, Tourism, or Transport?
A: Health is a dimension of the MPI along with education and living standards.
Q: According to the NITI Aayog MPI 2023, India's poverty headcount ratio fell to what level?
A: According to the NITI Aayog MPI 2023, India's multidimensional poverty headcount ratio fell to 14.96%.
Q: Which group in India experiences the highest incidence of multidimensional poverty?
A: Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes, along with rural households, experience the highest incidence of multidimensional poverty in India.
Q: How is the poverty line defined in India?
A: The poverty line has historically been defined in terms of calorie intake. The Y. K. Alagh Committee of 1979 used a norm of two thousand four hundred calories in rural areas and two thousand one hundred calories in urban areas. The Tendulkar Committee shifted to a wider basket including food, education and health, fixing the rural line at about thirty-three rupees per day and the urban line at about forty-seven rupees per day at 2011-12 prices.
Q: What is the Gini coefficient and what does it measure?
A: The Gini coefficient is a measure of income or wealth inequality, derived from the Lorenz curve, and it ranges from zero to one. A value of zero means perfect equality, where everyone has the same income, and a value of one means perfect inequality. A rise in the coefficient indicates that inequality is increasing, and a fall indicates that the distribution is becoming more equal.
Q: What are the main types of unemployment?
A: The main types are frictional unemployment, which occurs while workers move between jobs; structural unemployment, caused by a mismatch between skills and available jobs; seasonal unemployment, common in agriculture during the off season; disguised unemployment, where more people appear employed than are needed, mainly in agriculture; and cyclical unemployment, associated with downturns in the business cycle and recessions.
Q: What is the Multidimensional Poverty Index?
A: The Multidimensional Poverty Index measures poverty not only by income but also by deprivations in health, education and living standards. The global index was developed by the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative and the United Nations Development Programme. India's national index, released by the NITI Aayog, uses twelve indicators across three dimensions, and as per the 2023 index the headcount ratio fell to about fourteen point nine six per cent.
Q: What is the gig economy and why is it important for employment policy?
A: The gig economy is a labour market characterised by short-term, flexible and freelance jobs, often mediated through digital platforms. Cab and food delivery partners working through platforms such as Ola, Uber and Zomato are examples of gig workers. It is important for policy because these workers usually lack the social security and benefits associated with regular employment, so their protection has become a major concern.
Q: ভাৰতত দৰিদ্ৰতাৰেখ কেনেকৈ সংজ্ঞায়িত কৰা হয়?
A: দৰিদ্ৰতাৰেখ ইতিহাসগতভাৱে কেলৰি গ্ৰহণৰ দ্বাৰা সংজ্ঞায়িত কৰা হৈছে। ১৯৭৯ চনৰ ৱাই. কে. আলাগ সমিতিয়ে গ্ৰামাঞ্চলত দুহাজাৰ চাৰিশ আৰু চহৰাঞ্চলত দুহাজাৰ এশ কেলৰিৰ মানদণ্ড ব্যৱহাৰ কৰিছিল। তেন্দুলকাৰ সমিতিয়ে খাদ্য, শিক্ষা আৰু স্বাস্থ্য অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত বহল টোপোলালৈ স্থানান্তৰিত হৈ ২০১১-১২ মূল্যত গ্ৰাম্য ৰেখা প্ৰায় তেত্ৰিশ টকা আৰু চহৰীয়া ৰেখা প্ৰায় সাতচল্লিশ টকা দৈনিক নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰিছিল।
Q: গিনি সহগ কি আৰু ই কি জোখে?
A: গিনি সহগ হৈছে আয় বা সম্পদৰ বৈষম্যৰ এক জোখ, যি লৰেঞ্জ বক্ৰৰ পৰা লোৱা হয় আৰু শূন্যৰ পৰা একলৈকে থাকে। শূন্য মানে নিখুঁত সমতা, য'ত সকলোৰে একে আয়, আৰু এক মানে নিখুঁত অসমতা। সহগ বৃদ্ধি হ'লে বৈষম্য বাঢ়ি আছে বুলি সূচায়, আৰু হ্ৰাস হ'লে বিতৰণ অধিক সমান হৈ আছে বুলি সূচায়।
Q: বেকাৰত্বৰ প্ৰধান প্ৰকাৰ কি কি?
A: প্ৰধান প্ৰকাৰসমূহ হৈছে ঘৰ্ষণমূলক বেকাৰত্ব, যি কৰ্মীয়ে চাকৰি সলনি কৰোঁতে হয়; গাঁথনিগত বেকাৰত্ব, যি দক্ষতা আৰু উপলব্ধ চাকৰিৰ অমিলৰ পৰা হয়; ঋতুভিত্তিক বেকাৰত্ব, যি কৃষিত অশস্য ঋতুত সাধাৰণ; ছদ্ম বেকাৰত্ব, য'ত প্ৰয়োজনতকৈ অধিক লোক নিয়োজিত যেন লাগে, মূলতঃ কৃষিত; আৰু চক্ৰীয় বেকাৰত্ব, যি ব্যৱসায় চক্ৰৰ অৱনতি তথা মন্দাৰ লগত জড়িত।
Q: বহুমাত্ৰিক দৰিদ্ৰতা সূচকাংক কি?
A: বহুমাত্ৰিক দৰিদ্ৰতা সূচকাংকে দৰিদ্ৰতাক কেৱল আয়ৰ দ্বাৰা নহয়, স্বাস্থ্য, শিক্ষা আৰু জীৱনযাত্ৰাৰ মানত বঞ্চনাৰ দ্বাৰাও জোখে। বিশ্ব সূচকাংক অক্সফৰ্ড পভাৰ্টি এণ্ড হিউমেন ডেভেলপমেণ্ট ইনিচিয়েটিভ আৰু ৰাষ্ট্ৰসংঘৰ উন্নয়ন কাৰ্যসূচীয়ে বিকশিত কৰিছিল। নীতি আয়োগে প্ৰকাশ কৰা ভাৰতৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় সূচকাংকত তিনি মাত্ৰাত বাৰটা সূচক ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা হয়, আৰু ২০২৩ চনৰ সূচকাংক অনুসৰি মুঠ সংখ্যা অনুপাত প্ৰায় চৈধ্য দশমিক ছনব্বৈ শতাংশলৈ হ্ৰাস পাইছিল।
Q: গিগ অৰ্থনীতি কি আৰু নিয়োগ নীতিত ই কিয় গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: গিগ অৰ্থনীতি হৈছে এনে এক শ্ৰমবজাৰ যি চুটি-ম্যাদী, নমনীয় আৰু ফ্ৰিলাঞ্চ কামৰ দ্বাৰা বৈশিষ্ট্যযুক্ত, প্ৰায়ে ডিজিটেল প্লেটফৰ্মৰ মাজত। অলা, উবাৰ আৰু জোমাটোৰ দৰে প্লেটফৰ্মৰ জৰিয়তে কাম কৰা টেক্সি আৰু খাদ্য যোগান অংশীদাৰসকল গিগ কৰ্মীৰ উদাহৰণ। নীতিত ই গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ কাৰণ এই কৰ্মীসকলৰ সাধাৰণতে নিয়মীয়া নিয়োগৰ সামাজিক সুৰক্ষা আৰু সুবিধা নাথাকে, সেয়ে তেওঁলোকৰ সুৰক্ষা এটা প্ৰধান চিন্তা হৈ পৰিছে।

### Reserve Bank of India (RBI) & Monetary Policy — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/rbi-monetary-policy/
Summary: Practice reserve bank of india (rbi) & monetary policy questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual.
Q: When was the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) established?
A: The Reserve Bank of India was established on 1 April 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
Q: Under which Act was the RBI established?
A: RBI was established under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
Q: When was the RBI nationalized?
A: The RBI was nationalized on 1 January 1949, when its ownership passed to the Government of India.
Q: Who was the first Governor of the RBI?
A: Sir Osborne Smith was the first Governor of the RBI (1935-37).
Q: Who was the first Indian Governor of the RBI?
A: C. D. Deshmukh (1943-49) was the first Indian Governor of the RBI.
Q: Who is the present Governor of the RBI (as of 2026)?
A: Sanjay Malhotra is the present Governor of the RBI, having taken charge in December 2024.
Q: What is the repo rate?
A: Repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities.
Q: What is the reverse repo rate?
A: Reverse repo rate is the rate at which the RBI borrows money from commercial banks by selling securities.
Q: What is CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio)?
A: CRR is the percentage of a bank's total deposits that must be kept with the RBI in the form of cash.
Q: What is SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio)?
A: SLR is the percentage of a bank's net demand and time liabilities that must be maintained in liquid assets like cash, gold and unencumbered government securities.
Q: What is MSF (Marginal Standing Facility)?
A: MSF is an emergency overnight borrowing window through which banks can borrow funds from the RBI at a penal rate against approved government securities.
Q: What is LTRO (Long Term Repo Operations)?
A: LTRO is a tool through which the RBI provides long-term funds (of one to three years tenor) to banks at the repo rate to ease liquidity.
Q: What is the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) and when did it become statutory?
A: The MPC is the committee that decides the policy repo rate, and it became statutory in 2016 through an amendment to the RBI Act.
Q: How many members does the Monetary Policy Committee have?
A: The MPC has six members, of which three are from the RBI (including the Governor) and three are external members appointed by the government.
Q: Who is the Chairperson of the Monetary Policy Committee?
A: The Governor of the RBI is the ex-officio Chairperson of the Monetary Policy Committee.
Q: What is the inflation target set for the RBI under flexible inflation targeting?
A: The RBI has to keep inflation at 4 percent, with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2 percent (that is, between 2 and 6 percent).
Q: Which committee recommended the adoption of flexible inflation targeting for India?
A: The Urjit Patel Committee (2014) recommended the adoption of flexible inflation targeting for India.
Q: Under which section of the RBI Act was flexible inflation targeting incorporated?
A: Flexible inflation targeting was incorporated in Section 45ZA of the RBI Act, 1934 through the amendment of 2016.
Q: What is M1 in the measurement of money supply?
A: M1, the narrow money, is the sum of currency with the public and demand deposits held with banks.
Q: What is M3 in the measurement of money supply?
A: M3, the broad money, is equal to M1 plus time deposits with banks, and is also called aggregate monetary resources.
Q: Which measure of money supply is called aggregate monetary resources?
A: M3 is called aggregate monetary resources.
Q: What is M0 or reserve money?
A: M0 or reserve money is the sum of currency in circulation and the deposits of banks and others held with the RBI.
Q: Give two examples of quantitative tools of monetary policy.
A: Quantitative tools include repo rate, reverse repo rate, CRR, SLR and Open Market Operations, which affect the total money supply in the economy.
Q: Give two examples of qualitative (selective) tools of monetary policy.
A: Qualitative tools include moral suasion, margin requirements, credit rationing and regulation of consumer credit, which direct credit to specific sectors.
Q: What are Open Market Operations (OMO)?
A: OMOs are the buying and selling of government securities by the RBI in the open market to regulate money supply and liquidity in the economy.
Q: What is the Bank Rate?
A: Bank Rate is the standard rate at which the RBI lends long-term funds to commercial banks and discounts bills of exchange.
Q: What is the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF)?
A: LAF is the framework through which the RBI manages daily liquidity using the repo rate (as the rate of absorption/injection) and reverse repo operations.
Q: Why is the RBI known as the lender of last resort?
A: RBI is called the lender of last resort because it comes to the rescue of banks and financial institutions in financial distress by lending them funds.
Q: What is the role of the RBI as banker to the government?
A: As banker to the government, the RBI manages the government's accounts, receives and makes payments on its behalf, and manages its borrowings.
Q: Who issues the one rupee note in India?
A: The one rupee note is issued by the Government of India (Ministry of Finance) and is signed by the Finance Secretary.
Q: Which institution has the sole right to issue currency notes (except the one rupee note) in India?
A: The RBI has the sole right to issue currency notes in India, except the one rupee note which is issued by the Government of India.
Q: Which Act governs the regulation of commercial banks in India?
A: Commercial banks in India are regulated by the RBI under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
Q: Who appoints the Governor of the RBI?
A: The Governor of the RBI is appointed by the Government of India.
Q: Against what securities do banks borrow under the Marginal Standing Facility?
A: Under MSF, banks borrow overnight against government securities within the limits of their SLR holdings.
Q: What is the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) introduced by the RBI in 2022?
A: The Standing Deposit Facility is a tool through which banks can park surplus liquidity with the RBI, and it now acts as the floor of the interest rate corridor.
Q: When was the RBI established and when was it nationalized?
A: The Reserve Bank of India was established on 1 April 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. It was initially a private shareholders' institution and was nationalized on 1 January 1949, when its ownership passed to the Government of India.
Q: What is the difference between repo rate and reverse repo rate?
A: The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities, so it is the rate at which banks borrow from the RBI. The reverse repo rate is the rate at which the RBI borrows money from commercial banks by selling securities to them, so it is the rate at which banks park funds with the RBI.
Q: What is the Monetary Policy Committee and what is its inflation target?
A: The Monetary Policy Committee decides the policy repo rate and became statutory in 2016 through an amendment to the RBI Act. It has six members, three from the RBI including the Governor and three external members appointed by the government, with the Governor as ex-officio Chairperson. The RBI has to keep inflation at four per cent with a tolerance band of plus or minus two per cent, that is, between two and six per cent.
Q: What is the difference between M1 and M3?
A: M1, called narrow money, is the sum of currency with the public and demand deposits held with banks. M3, called broad money, is equal to M1 plus time deposits with banks, and it is also known as aggregate monetary resources. M3 is the more commonly used measure of overall money supply.
Q: What are quantitative and qualitative tools of monetary policy?
A: Quantitative tools affect the total volume of money and credit in the economy and include the repo rate, reverse repo rate, CRR, SLR and open market operations. Qualitative or selective tools direct credit towards particular sectors or purposes and include moral suasion, margin requirements, credit rationing and the regulation of consumer credit.
Q: RBI কেতিয়া প্ৰতিষ্ঠা আৰু কেতিয়া ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয়কৰণ কৰা হৈছিল?
A: ভাৰতীয় ৰিজাৰ্ভ বেংক ১৯৩৫ চনৰ ১ এপ্ৰিলত ভাৰতীয় ৰিজাৰ্ভ বেংক আইন, ১৯৩৪ ৰ অধীনত প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰা হৈছিল। ই আৰম্ভণিতে এক ব্যক্তিগত শ্বেয়াৰধাৰক প্ৰতিষ্ঠান আছিল আৰু ১৯৪৯ চনৰ ১ জানুৱাৰীত ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয়কৰণ কৰা হৈছিল, যেতিয়া ইয়াৰ গৰাকিত্ব ভাৰত চৰকাৰৰ হাতলৈ যায়।
Q: ৰেপ’ হাৰ আৰু ৰিভাৰ্ছ ৰেপ’ হাৰৰ পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: ৰেপ’ হাৰ হৈছে সেই হাৰ য'ত RBI য়ে চৰকাৰী প্ৰতিভূতিৰ বিনিময়ত বাণিজ্যিক বেংকসমূহক স্বল্পম্যাদী ধন ঋণ দিয়ে, অৰ্থাৎ বেংকে RBI ৰ পৰা ধন ধাৰ কৰাৰ হাৰ। ৰিভাৰ্ছ ৰেপ’ হাৰ হৈছে সেই হাৰ য'ত RBI য়ে বেংকসমূহক প্ৰতিভূতি বিক্ৰী কৰি ধন ধাৰ কৰে, অৰ্থাৎ বেংকসমূহে RBI ৰ ওচৰত ধন ৰখাৰ হাৰ।
Q: মুদ্ৰা নীতি সমিতি কি আৰু ইয়াৰ মুদ্ৰাস্ফীতি লক্ষ্য কি?
A: মুদ্ৰা নীতি সমিতিয়ে নীতি ৰেপ’ হাৰ নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰে আৰু ২০১৬ চনত ভাৰতীয় ৰিজাৰ্ভ বেংক আইনৰ সংশোধনীৰ জৰিয়তে বিধিবদ্ধ হৈছিল। ইয়াত ছজন সদস্য আছে, গভৰ্ণৰসহ RBI ৰ তিনিজন আৰু চৰকাৰে নিয়োগ কৰা তিনিজন বাহ্যিক সদস্য, গভৰ্ণৰ পদাধিকাৰী অধ্যক্ষ হিচাপে। RBI য়ে মুদ্ৰাস্ফীতি চাৰি শতাংশত ৰাখিব লাগে, যোগ বা বিয়োগ দুই শতাংশ সহনশীলতা বেণ্ডৰ সৈতে, অৰ্থাৎ দুইৰ পৰা ছয় শতাংশৰ মাজত।
Q: M1 আৰু M3 ৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: M1, যাক সংকীৰ্ণ ধন বোলা হয়, হৈছে ৰাইজৰ ওচৰত থকা মুদ্ৰা আৰু বেংকত থকা চাহিদা জমাৰ যোগফল। M3, যাক বিস্তৃত ধন বোলা হয়, M1 লগত বেংকত থকা সময় জমাৰ সমান, আৰু ইয়াক সামগ্ৰিক মুদ্ৰা সম্পদও বোলা হয়। সামগ্ৰিক ধনৰ যোগানৰ বাবে M3 ৰ ব্যৱহাৰ বেছি।
Q: মুদ্ৰা নীতিৰ পৰিমাণগত আৰু গুণগত সঁজুলি কি কি?
A: পৰিমাণগত সঁজুলিয়ে অৰ্থনীতিত ধন আৰু ঋণৰ মুঠ পৰিমাণ প্ৰভাৱিত কৰে আৰু ইয়াত ৰেপ’ হাৰ, ৰিভাৰ্ছ ৰেপ’ হাৰ, CRR, SLR আৰু মুক্ত বজাৰ কাৰ্য্যকলাপ অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত। গুণগত বা নিৰ্বাচনী সঁজুলিয়ে নিৰ্দিষ্ট খণ্ড বা উদ্দেশ্যলৈ ঋণ পৰিচালিত কৰে আৰু ইয়াত নৈতিক প্ৰবৃত্তি, মাৰ্জিনৰ প্ৰয়োজনীয়তা, ঋণ ৰেচনিং আৰু গ্ৰাহক ঋণৰ নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত।

### Services Sector (IT, Telecom, Tourism) — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/services-sector-it-telecom-tourism/
Summary: Practice services sector (it, telecom, tourism) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: What is the share of the services sector in India's GDP?
A: The services sector contributes about 55 percent of India's GDP.
Q: What is the approximate share of services in India's total employment?
A: Services contribute about 30 percent of India's total employment.
Q: What does GATS stand for?
A: GATS stands for the General Agreement on Trade in Services, a WTO treaty concluded in 1995.
Q: Which organisation administers GATS?
A: The World Trade Organization (WTO) administers GATS.
Q: What is NASSCOM and when was it set up?
A: NASSCOM is the National Association of Software and Service Companies, established in 1988.
Q: Which city is known as the 'Silicon Valley of India'?
A: Bengaluru is known as the 'Silicon Valley of India'.
Q: When was Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) founded?
A: TCS was founded in 1968.
Q: When and by whom was Infosys founded?
A: Infosys was founded in 1981 by N.R. Narayana Murthy and six other colleagues.
Q: Which major Indian IT company was founded by the Premji family?
A: Wipro, founded in 1945 and later built into a leading IT firm by Azim Premji.
Q: What is the contribution of the IT-BPM industry to India's GDP?
A: The IT-BPM industry contributes about 7 to 8 percent of India's GDP.
Q: Which is India's largest IT company by revenue?
A: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) is India's largest IT company by revenue.
Q: What is India's position in the world IT services market?
A: India is the world's largest outsourcing destination and among the top exporters of IT services.
Q: When was Reliance Jio launched for the general public?
A: Reliance Jio was launched for the public on 5 September 2016.
Q: Who launched Reliance Jio?
A: Reliance Jio was launched by Mukesh Ambani-led Reliance Industries.
Q: What is the approximate number of telecom subscribers in India?
A: India has over 1.1 billion (about 115 crore) telecom subscribers.
Q: Which telecom operator has the largest subscriber base in India?
A: Reliance Jio has the largest subscriber base in India.
Q: What is Digital India?
A: Digital India is a flagship programme launched on 1 July 2015 to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.
Q: Which ministry implements Digital India?
A: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) implements Digital India.
Q: What is the 'Incredible India' campaign?
A: It is a tourism promotion campaign launched by the Ministry of Tourism in 2002.
Q: What is the approximate contribution of tourism to India's GDP?
A: Tourism contributes roughly 7 percent of India's GDP, with estimates varying between about 5 and 9 percent including indirect impact.
Q: How many jobs does the tourism sector support in India?
A: The tourism sector supports about 4 crore (42 million) jobs in India.
Q: What is 'Atithi Devo Bhava'?
A: It is a campaign launched in 2010 to promote hospitality towards tourists in India.
Q: What is a Global Capability Centre (GCC)?
A: A GCC is an offshore centre set up by a multinational company in India to carry out IT, engineering and business services.
Q: Approximately how many Global Capability Centres operate in India?
A: Over 1,500 GCCs operate in India, with estimates indicating around 1,600 or more.
Q: What is ITES?
A: ITES stands for IT-Enabled Services, which include services such as BPO (Business Process Outsourcing).
Q: What is the share of services in India's total exports?
A: Services account for about 40 percent of India's total exports.
Q: Which sector attracts the largest share of FDI inflows into India?
A: The services sector attracts the largest share of FDI inflows into India.
Q: When was the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) established?
A: TRAI was established in 1997.
Q: What is BharatNet?
A: BharatNet is a government project to provide broadband connectivity to all gram panchayats and rural areas.
Q: What was the main impact of the 'Jio revolution' in telecom?
A: It brought affordable 4G data, massive internet adoption and a digital revolution in Indian telecom.
Q: When was the first National Telecom Policy announced?
A: The first National Telecom Policy was announced in 1994.
Q: Which Indian city is another major hub for IT and startups along with Bengaluru?
A: Hyderabad is a major IT and startup hub, along with Pune and the National Capital Region.
Q: What is the 'Swadesh Darshan' scheme?
A: It is a scheme launched in 2014-15 for the development of theme-based tourism circuits in India.
Q: What is the role of tourism as a foreign exchange earner for India?
A: Tourism is one of India's leading sources of foreign exchange earnings.
Q: When was the Union Ministry of Tourism created as a separate ministry?
A: The Union Ministry of Tourism was created as a separate ministry in 1967.
Q: What is the contribution of the services sector to India's economy?
A: The services sector contributes about fifty-five per cent of India's gross domestic product and about thirty per cent of total employment. It accounts for about forty per cent of total exports and attracts the largest share of foreign direct investment inflows into the country.
Q: What is NASSCOM and when was it established?
A: NASSCOM stands for the National Association of Software and Service Companies. It was established in 1988 and is the main industry body representing India's information technology and business process management sector. It works with the government on policy and promotes the growth of the industry.
Q: What was the significance of Reliance Jio's launch?
A: Reliance Jio was launched for the public on 5 September 2016 by the Mukesh Ambani-led Reliance Industries. It brought affordable 4G data, massive internet adoption and a digital revolution in Indian telecom, and it now has the largest subscriber base in India. Its entry sharply lowered data prices and expanded digital access.
Q: What is GATS and who administers it?
A: GATS is the General Agreement on Trade in Services, a treaty concluded in 1995 that provides the framework for liberalising international trade in services. It is administered by the World Trade Organization. It is important for India because the country is a major exporter of services and benefits from easier movement of skilled professionals.
Q: What are the major government campaigns and schemes for tourism?
A: The Incredible India campaign was launched by the Ministry of Tourism in 2002 to promote the country as a tourist destination. The Atithi Devo Bhava campaign was launched in 2010 to promote hospitality towards tourists. The Swadesh Darshan scheme was launched in 2014-15 for developing theme-based tourism circuits. Tourism contributes roughly seven per cent of GDP and supports about four crore jobs.
Q: ভাৰতৰ অৰ্থনীতিত সেৱা খণ্ডৰ অৱদান কি?
A: সেৱা খণ্ডই ভাৰতৰ মুঠ ঘৰুৱা উৎপাদনৰ প্ৰায় পঞ্চান্ন শতাংশ আৰু মুঠ নিয়োগৰ প্ৰায় ত্ৰিশ শতাংশ অৱদান আগবঢ়ায়। ই মুঠ ৰপ্তানিৰ প্ৰায় চল্লিশ শতাংশ আৰু দেশলৈ সৰ্বাধিক বৈদেশিক প্ৰত্যক্ষ বিনিয়োগ আকৰ্ষণ কৰে।
Q: NASSCOM কি আৰু কেতিয়া প্ৰতিষ্ঠা হৈছিল?
A: NASSCOM ৰ অৰ্থ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় চফ্টৱেৰ আৰু সেৱা কোম্পানী সন্থা। ই ১৯৮৮ চনত প্ৰতিষ্ঠা হৈছিল আৰু ভাৰতৰ তথ্যপ্ৰযুক্তি তথা ব্যৱসায় প্ৰক্ৰিয়া পৰিচালনা খণ্ডক প্ৰতিনিধিত্ব কৰা প্ৰধান উদ্যোগ সংস্থা। ই চৰকাৰৰ সৈতে নীতিৰ ওপৰত কাম কৰে আৰু উদ্যোগৰ বৃদ্ধিক প্ৰচাৰ কৰে।
Q: ৰিলায়েন্স জিঅ’ৰ আৰম্ভণিৰ তাৎপৰ্য কি আছিল?
A: ৰিলায়েন্স জিঅ’ মুকেশ আম্বানী নেতৃত্বাধীন ৰিলায়েন্স ইণ্ডাষ্ট্ৰীজে ২০১৬ চনৰ ৫ ছেপ্টেম্বৰত ৰাইজৰ বাবে আৰম্ভ কৰিছিল। ই সুলভ ৪G ডাটা, ব্যাপক ইণ্টাৰনেট গ্ৰহণ আৰু ভাৰতীয় টেলিকমত এটা ডিজিটেল বিপ্লৱ আনিছিল, আৰু এতিয়া ইয়াৰ ভাৰতত আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ গ্ৰাহক ভিত্তি আছে। ইয়াৰ প্ৰৱেশে ডাটা মূল্য তীব্ৰভাৱে কমাইছিল আৰু ডিজিটেল প্ৰৱেশ বহলাইছিল।
Q: GATS কি আৰু ইয়াক কোনে পৰিচালনা কৰে?
A: GATS হৈছে General Agreement on Trade in Services, ১৯৯৫ চনত সম্পন্ন হোৱা এটা চুক্তি যি আন্তৰ্জাতিক সেৱা বাণিজ্য উদাৰীকৰণৰ গাঁথনি প্ৰদান কৰে। ইয়াক বিশ্ব বাণিজ্য সংস্থাই পৰিচালনা কৰে। ভাৰতৰ বাবে ই গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ কাৰণ দেশখন সেৱাৰ এটা প্ৰধান ৰপ্তানিকাৰী আৰু দক্ষ পেছাদাৰীৰ সহজ চলাচলৰ পৰা লাভৱান হয়।
Q: পৰ্যটনৰ প্ৰধান চৰকাৰী অভিযান আৰু আঁচনি কি কি?
A: Incredible India অভিযান পৰ্যটন মন্ত্ৰালয়ে ২০০২ চনত দেশখনক পৰ্যটন গন্তব্যস্থল হিচাপে প্ৰচাৰ কৰিবলৈ আৰম্ভ কৰিছিল। Atithi Devo Bhava অভিযান ২০১০ চনত পৰ্যটকৰ প্ৰতি আতিথ্য প্ৰচাৰ কৰিবলৈ আৰম্ভ কৰিছিল। Swadesh Darshan আঁচনি ২০১৪-১৫ চনত থীম-ভিত্তিক পৰ্যটন বৃত্ত বিকাশৰ বাবে আৰম্ভ কৰিছিল। পৰ্যটনে GDP ৰ প্ৰায় সাত শতাংশ অৱদান আগবঢ়ায় আৰু প্ৰায় চাৰি কোটি চাকৰি সমৰ্থন কৰে।

### Union Budget, Taxation (GST) & Fiscal Policy — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/union-budget-gst-fiscal-policy/
Summary: Practice union budget, taxation (gst) & fiscal policy questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the Annual Financial Statement (Union Budget) presented?
A: The Annual Financial Statement is presented under Article 112 of the Constitution.
Q: Who presents the Union Budget in the Lok Sabha?
A: The Union Finance Minister presents the Union Budget in the Lok Sabha.
Q: Which type of expenditure is defined as expenditure that does not create assets and reduces liabilities?
A: Revenue expenditure does not create assets and reduces liabilities.
Q: Capital expenditure of the government creates assets; what does it generally also reduce?
A: Capital expenditure generally creates assets and also reduces the liabilities of the government.
Q: What is revenue deficit?
A: Revenue deficit is the excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts of the government.
Q: Fiscal deficit is the difference between total expenditure and what?
A: Fiscal deficit is the excess of total expenditure over total non-borrowed receipts (revenue receipts plus non-debt capital receipts).
Q: What is primary deficit?
A: Primary deficit is fiscal deficit minus interest payments of the government.
Q: Which Act was passed in 2003 to bring fiscal discipline in India?
A: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act was passed in 2003.
Q: What is the target fiscal deficit under the FRBM Act as a percentage of GDP?
A: The FRBM Act originally targeted a fiscal deficit of 3% of GDP.
Q: Which committee recommended the FRBM Act framework in India?
A: The FRBM framework was based on the recommendations of the E.A.S. Sarma Committee.
Q: Which tax is considered a direct tax?
A: Income tax is a direct tax because its burden falls directly on the taxpayer.
Q: Which of the following is an indirect tax — GST, Income Tax, Corporate Tax, or Wealth Tax?
A: GST is an indirect tax; the others are direct taxes.
Q: In which year was GST implemented in India?
A: GST was implemented in India on 1 July 2017.
Q: Which constitutional amendment introduced GST in India?
A: The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 introduced GST in India.
Q: What is the constitutional status of the GST Council?
A: The GST Council is a constitutional body established under Article 279A of the Constitution.
Q: Who is the ex-officio Chairperson of the GST Council?
A: The Union Finance Minister is the ex-officio Chairperson of the GST Council.
Q: Which GST rate is applied to most essential and daily-use items?
A: Most essential items are taxed at 0% or 5% under GST; basic necessities generally attract 5% or are exempt.
Q: Which GST slabs were fixed for goods in India?
A: The main GST slabs for goods are 5%, 12%, 18% and 28%, apart from the 0% rate.
Q: What is a cess in the context of taxation?
A: A cess is a tax levied on tax collected for a specific purpose and it is not shared with states.
Q: In the new tax regime under Section 115BAC, what is the income exemption limit for salaried individuals?
A: Under the new tax regime, annual income up to ₹3 lakh is exempt from tax.
Q: Which tax is levied on the profits of companies in India?
A: Corporate tax is levied on the profits of companies in India.
Q: What does TDS stand for in income tax?
A: TDS stands for Tax Deducted at Source, where tax is deducted at the time of payment.
Q: A vote on account is generally taken to meet which kind of expenditure?
A: A vote on account is taken to meet the interim expenditure of the government pending the passage of the full budget.
Q: How much expenditure can be covered by a vote on account?
A: A vote on account usually covers expenditure for two months, but it can be extended up to three to four months.
Q: What is supplementary grant in the budget process?
A: Supplementary grant is additional money sought from Parliament when the approved budget amount is insufficient for a financial year.
Q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the Consolidated Fund of India?
A: Article 266 deals with the Consolidated Fund of India and the Consolidated Fund of States.
Q: Which fund was created by the government under Article 267 of the Constitution?
A: The Contingency Fund of India was created under Article 267 of the Constitution.
Q: Who administers the Contingency Fund of India?
A: The President of India administers the Contingency Fund of India.
Q: In which month is the Union Budget traditionally presented in India?
A: The Union Budget is traditionally presented on 1 February.
Q: What is the difference between revenue deficit and fiscal deficit called?
A: There is no single name for the difference; fiscal deficit minus interest payments gives primary deficit, while revenue deficit is a component of the fiscal deficit.
Q: Which committee recommended the abolition of the plan and non-plan expenditure classification?
A: The B.K. Chaturvedi Committee recommended the abolition of the plan and non-plan expenditure classification.
Q: Which tax is levied on the transfer of goods and services and is collected by both Centre and States?
A: GST is levied on the supply of goods and services and is shared between the Centre (CGST) and States (SGST).
Q: Which of the following taxes was subsumed into GST — Service Tax, Income Tax, Corporate Tax, or Wealth Tax?
A: Service Tax was subsumed into GST along with many other indirect taxes.
Q: Which committee recommended the goods and services tax in India?
A: The Kelkar Task Force on fiscal consolidation recommended the introduction of GST in India.
Q: What is the maximum marginal rate of income tax for individuals in the old tax regime (excluding cess)?
A: The maximum marginal rate of income tax for individuals in the old regime is 30%.
Q: What is the Union Budget and under which Article is it presented?
A: The Union Budget is the annual statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the central government for a financial year. Constitutionally it is called the Annual Financial Statement and is presented under Article 112 of the Constitution of India by the Union Finance Minister in the Lok Sabha.
Q: What is the difference between revenue expenditure and capital expenditure?
A: Revenue expenditure neither creates assets nor reduces liabilities; examples are salaries, pensions, interest and subsidies. Capital expenditure creates durable assets such as roads, dams and machines, or reduces the liabilities of the government. The distinction matters because only capital expenditure adds to the productive capacity of the economy.
Q: What is fiscal deficit and how is it different from primary deficit?
A: Fiscal deficit is the excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings, and it shows the total borrowing requirement of the government. Primary deficit is the fiscal deficit minus interest payments on past debt, and it shows the current fiscal position after removing the burden of past borrowing.
Q: What is the FRBM Act and what targets did it set?
A: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act was passed in 2003 to bring fiscal discipline, based on the recommendations of the E.A.S. Sarma Committee. It originally targeted a fiscal deficit of 3 per cent of GDP and the elimination of the revenue deficit. The FRBM Review Committee of 2017 under N.K. Singh recommended a debt-to-GDP ratio of 60 per cent.
Q: What is GST and how does the GST Council work?
A: GST is a destination-based indirect tax on consumption introduced on 1 July 2017 by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016, with the motto One Nation, One Tax. The GST Council is a constitutional body under Article 279A, chaired by the Union Finance Minister, and its decisions require a three-fourths majority in which the centre has one-third and the states two-thirds of the voting weight.
Q: কেন্দ্ৰীয় বাজেট কি আৰু কেতিয়া কোন ধাৰাৰ অধীনত উপস্থাপন কৰা হয়?
A: কেন্দ্ৰীয় বাজেট হৈছে বিত্তীয় বছৰ এটাৰ বাবে কেন্দ্ৰীয় চৰকাৰৰ অনুমানিত প্ৰাপ্তি আৰু ব্যয়ৰ বাৰ্ষিক বিবৃতি। সাংবিধানিকভাৱে ইয়াক বাৰ্ষিক বিত্তীয় বিৱৰণী বোলা হয় আৰু ভাৰতীয় সংবিধানৰ ১১২ নং ধাৰাৰ অধীনত কেন্দ্ৰীয় বিত্ত মন্ত্ৰীয়ে লোকসভাত উপস্থাপন কৰে।
Q: ৰাজহ ব্যয় আৰু মূলধন ব্যয়ৰ মাজৰ পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: ৰাজহ ব্যয়ে সম্পদ সৃষ্টি নকৰে বা দায় হ্ৰাস নকৰে; উদাহৰণ দৰমহা, পেঞ্চন, সুত আৰু ৰেহাই। মূলধন ব্যয়ে ৰাস্তা, বান্ধ আৰু যন্ত্ৰৰ দৰে স্থায়ী সম্পদ সৃষ্টি কৰে, নাইবা চৰকাৰৰ দায় হ্ৰাস কৰে। এই পাৰ্থক্য গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ কাৰণ কেৱল মূলধন ব্যয়েই অৰ্থনীতিৰ উৎপাদন ক্ষমতা বৃদ্ধি কৰে।
Q: ৰাজকোষীয় ঘাটি কি আৰু প্ৰাথমিক ঘাটিৰ পৰা ই কেনেকৈ পৃথক?
A: ৰাজকোষীয় ঘাটি হৈছে মুঠ ব্যয় ঋণ বাদ দি মুঠ প্ৰাপ্তিতকৈ বেছি হোৱা অৱস্থা, আৰু ই চৰকাৰৰ মুঠ ঋণৰ প্ৰয়োজন দেখুৱায়। প্ৰাথমিক ঘাটি হৈছে ৰাজকোষীয় ঘাটিৰ পৰা অতীতৰ ঋণৰ সুত পৰিশোধ বাদ দিলে পোৱা ঘাটি, আৰু ই অতীতৰ ঋণৰ ভাৰ আঁতৰাই বৰ্তমান ৰাজকোষীয় অৱস্থা দেখুৱায়।
Q: FRBM আইন কি আৰু ই কি লক্ষ্য নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰিছিল?
A: ৰাজকোষীয় দায়বদ্ধতা আৰু বাজেট ব্যৱস্থাপনা আইন ২০০৩ চনত ৰাজকোষীয় শৃংখলা আনিবলৈ E.A.S. সৰ্মা সমিতিৰ সুপাৰিশৰ আধাৰত পাছ কৰা হৈছিল। ই মূলতঃ GDP ৰ ৩ শতাংশ ৰাজকোষীয় ঘাটি আৰু ৰাজহ ঘাটি শূন্য কৰাৰ লক্ষ্য নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰিছিল। ২০১৭ চনত এন.কে. সিঙৰ নেতৃত্বত FRBM পুনৰীক্ষণ সমিতিয়ে ৬০ শতাংশ ঋণ-GDP অনুপাতৰ সুপাৰিশ কৰিছিল।
Q: GST কি আৰু GST পৰিষদে কেনেকৈ কাম কৰে?
A: GST হৈছে ২০১৬ চনৰ ১০১ সংখ্যক সাংবিধানিক সংশোধনী আইনৰ দ্বাৰা ২০১৭ চনৰ ১ জুলাইত প্ৰচলিত ভোগৰ ওপৰত গন্তব্যস্থল-ভিত্তিক পৰোক্ষ কৰ, যাৰ মত One Nation, One Tax। GST পৰিষদ ২৭৯ক নং ধাৰাৰ অধীনত এটা সাংবিধানিক সংস্থা, অধ্যক্ষ কেন্দ্ৰীয় বিত্ত মন্ত্ৰী, আৰু ইয়াৰ সিদ্ধান্তৰ বাবে চাৰিৰ তিনি অংশ সংখ্যাগৰিষ্ঠতা লাগে, য'ত কেন্দ্ৰৰ এক তৃতীয়াংশ আৰু ৰাজ্যসমূহৰ দু-তৃতীয়াংশ ভোটৰ ভাৰ থাকে।

### Agriculture: Tea, Rice, Jute & Silk — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/assam-geography-sec/agriculture-tea-rice-jute-silk/
Summary: Practice agriculture: tea, rice, jute & silk questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What is the main crop of Assam?
A: Paddy (rice).
Q: What is the staple food crop of Assam?
A: Rice.
Q: What are the three seasons of rice cultivation in Assam?
A: Ahu (autumn), Sali (winter) and Boro (summer) paddy.
Q: Which is the main rice crop of Assam?
A: Sali (winter) paddy, which is the main crop.
Q: What is 'Ahu' paddy?
A: An early (autumn) paddy sown in March-April and harvested in June-July.
Q: What is 'Sali' paddy?
A: The main winter paddy sown in June-July and harvested in November-December.
Q: What is 'Boro' paddy?
A: A summer paddy grown in low-lying areas with irrigation in January-May.
Q: Which crop is known as the 'cash crop' of Assam?
A: Tea.
Q: What percentage of India's tea production comes from Assam?
A: About 50% to 52% of India's tea production.
Q: Which district is the largest tea producing district of Assam?
A: Dibrugarh district.
Q: What is the tea growing region of Assam called?
A: The Brahmaputra valley and the Barak valley are the two tea belts.
Q: When was tea first discovered in Assam?
A: In 1823, by Robert Bruce.
Q: Who discovered the tea plants in Assam?
A: Robert Bruce (and later his brother C.A. Bruce).
Q: Which is the main variety of tea grown in Assam?
A: The Assam variety (Camellia assamica).
Q: What is jute?
A: A fibre crop grown mainly in the Barak valley of Assam.
Q: In which region of Assam is jute mainly cultivated?
A: The Barak valley (Cachar, Karimganj and Hailakandi) and some parts of the Brahmaputra valley.
Q: Which silk is exclusive to Assam and found nowhere else in the world?
A: Muga silk (golden silk).
Q: What is the name of the silkworm that produces muga silk?
A: Antheraea assamensis.
Q: Which silk is known as 'golden silk'?
A: Muga silk.
Q: What are the three main types of silk produced in Assam?
A: Muga, Eri (Endi) and Pat silk.
Q: Which silk is produced from the castor-fed silkworm?
A: Eri (Endi) silk.
Q: Which district of Assam is famous for muga silk production?
A: Sivasagar, Lakhimpur, Darrang and Kamrup are major muga producing districts.
Q: What is the famous cotton cloth woven in Assam?
A: The gamosa and the traditional Assamese cotton textiles.
Q: What is the main irrigation source for agriculture in Assam?
A: The monsoon rainfall and the floodwater of the rivers.
Q: Which cash crop is grown in the hill districts of Karbi Anglong?
A: Rubber, and also spices like ginger.
Q: What is the main occupation of the people of Assam?
A: Agriculture.
Q: What is the main crop and staple food of Assam, and what are the three rice seasons?
A: Rice, or paddy, is the main crop and staple food of Assam. It is grown in three seasons: ahu, the early autumn paddy sown in March-April and harvested in June-July; sali, the main winter paddy sown in June-July and harvested in November-December; and boro, the summer paddy grown in low-lying fields with irrigation from January to May. Sali is the single most important of the three.
Q: How important is tea to Assam and where is it grown?
A: Tea is the cash crop and the most important industry of Assam, and the state produces about 50 to 52 per cent of India's tea. It is grown in two belts, the Brahmaputra valley and the Barak valley, and the leading tea-producing district is Dibrugarh. Tea was discovered in Assam in 1823 by Robert Bruce, and the local Camellia assamica variety is the basis of the industry.
Q: Which silk of Assam is found nowhere else in the world?
A: Muga silk, the golden silk, is exclusive to Assam and is produced by the silkworm Antheraea assamensis. The other two silks of the state are eri, produced from the castor-fed silkworm, and pat, the white mulberry silk. The major muga-producing districts are Sivasagar, Lakhimpur, Darrang and Kamrup. Handloom weaving, including the gamosa, is closely linked to the silk tradition.
Q: In which region of Assam is jute mainly grown?
A: Jute, a fibre crop, is grown mainly in the Barak valley, in the districts of Cachar, Karimganj and Hailakandi, and in some parts of the Brahmaputra valley. It is one of the main cash crops of the south of the state. In the hill districts, rubber and spices such as ginger have become important commercial crops alongside the traditional crops of the plains.
Q: What are the two research and marketing centres of the Assam tea industry?
A: The two centres are the Tocklai Tea Research Institute at Jorhat, which is the oldest tea research institute in the world, and the Guwahati Tea Auction Centre, the largest tea auction centre of the state. Jorhat is often called the tea capital of Assam because of Tocklai, while Guwahati is where most of the state's tea is bought and sold at auction.
Q: অসমৰ মূল শস্য আৰু মূল খাদ্য কি, আৰু ধানৰ তিনিটা ঋতু কি কি?
A: ধান অসমৰ মূল শস্য আৰু মূল খাদ্য। ই তিনিটা ঋতুত খেতি কৰা হয়: আহু, প্ৰাৰম্ভিক শৰৎ ধান মাৰ্চ-এপ্ৰিলত সিচা আৰু জুন-জুলাইত কটা; শালি, মূল শীত ধান জুন-জুলাইত সিচা আৰু নৱেম্বৰ-ডিচেম্বৰত কটা; আৰু বৰো, জানুৱাৰীৰ পৰা মে'লৈ সিঞ্চনৰ সহায়ত নিম্ন অঞ্চলত খেতি কৰা গ্ৰীষ্ম ধান। তিনিটাৰ ভিতৰত শালি আটাইতকৈ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ।
Q: অসমৰ বাবে চাহ কিমান গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ আৰু ই ক'ত খেতি কৰা হয়?
A: চাহ অসমৰ নগদ শস্য আৰু আটাইতকৈ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ উদ্যোগ, আৰু ৰাজ্যই ভাৰতৰ চাহৰ প্ৰায় ৫০ৰ পৰা ৫২ শতাংশ উৎপাদন কৰে। ই দুটা বেল্টত খেতি কৰা হয়, ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ উপত্যকা আৰু বৰাক উপত্যকা, আৰু আগশাৰীৰ চাহ উৎপাদনকাৰী জিলা ডিব্ৰুগড়। চাহ ১৮২৩ চনত ৰবাৰ্ট ব্ৰুচে অসমত আৱিষ্কাৰ কৰিছিল, আৰু স্থানীয় কামেলিয়া অসমিকা প্ৰজাতি উদ্যোগটোৰ ভেটি।
Q: অসমৰ কোন ৰেচম পৃথিৱীৰ আন ক'তো নাই?
A: মুগা ৰেচম, সোণালী ৰেচম, অসমৰ একচেটিয়া আৰু এন্থেৰিয়া অসমেন্সিছ ৰেচম পৰুৱাই উৎপাদন কৰে। ৰাজ্যখনৰ আন দুবিধ ৰেচম হৈছে এৰী, এৰণ্ডি খোৱা ৰেচম পৰুৱাৰ পৰা উৎপন্ন, আৰু পাট, বগা নুনি ৰেচম। মুখ্য মুগা উৎপাদনকাৰী জিলা শিৱসাগৰ, লখিমপুৰ, দৰং আৰু কামৰূপ। গামোচাকে ধৰি তাঁতশাল বয়ন ৰেচম পৰম্পৰাৰ সৈতে নিবিড়ভাৱে জড়িত।
Q: অসমত মৰাপাট মূলত কোন অঞ্চলত খেতি কৰা হয়?
A: মৰাপাট, এটা আঁহ শস্য, মূলত বৰাক উপত্যকাত, কাছাৰ, কৰিমগঞ্জ আৰু হাইলাকান্দি জিলাত, আৰু ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ উপত্যকাৰ কিছু অংশত খেতি কৰা হয়। ই ৰাজ্যখনৰ দক্ষিণৰ মূল নগদ শস্যসমূহৰ এটা। পাহাৰীয়া জিলাবোৰত ৰবাৰ আৰু আদাৰ দৰে মছলা সমভূমিৰ পৰম্পৰাগত শস্যৰ লগতে গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ বাণিজ্যিক শস্য হৈ উঠিছে।
Q: অসম চাহ উদ্যোগৰ দুটা গৱেষণা আৰু বিপণন কেন্দ্ৰ কি?
A: দুটা কেন্দ্ৰ হৈছে যোৰহাটৰ টোকলাই চাহ গৱেষণা প্ৰতিষ্ঠান, যি বিশ্বৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি চাহ গৱেষণা প্ৰতিষ্ঠান, আৰু গুৱাহাটী চাহ নিলাম কেন্দ্ৰ, ৰাজ্যখনৰ বৃহত্তম চাহ নিলাম কেন্দ্ৰ। টোকলাইৰ বাবে যোৰহাটক প্ৰায়ে অসমৰ চাহ ৰাজধানী বুলি কোৱা হয়, আনহাতে গুৱাহাটীত ৰাজ্যখনৰ বেছিভাগ চাহ নিলামত কিনা-বেচা কৰা হয়।

### Inter-State & International Borders — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/assam-geography-sec/borders-interstate-international-assam/
Summary: Practice inter-state & international borders questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Which country shares the international border with Assam?
A: Bhutan and Bangladesh.
Q: Which state of India shares its border with Assam?
A: Seven states: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram and West Bengal.
Q: Which district of Assam shares the international border with Bhutan?
A: Kokrajhar, Chirang, Baksa, Udalguri, Darrang, Sonitpur and Bishwanath districts.
Q: Which district of Assam shares the border with Bangladesh?
A: Dhubri and Karimganj districts.
Q: Which district of Assam shares its border with Arunachal Pradesh?
A: Tinsukia, Dibrugarh, Lakhimpur, Dhemaji, Sonitpur, Biswanath and Baksa districts.
Q: Which district of Assam shares its border with Nagaland?
A: Golaghat, Jorhat, Sivasagar and Charaideo districts.
Q: Which district of Assam shares its border with Manipur?
A: Cachar and Hailakandi districts.
Q: Which district of Assam shares its border with Meghalaya?
A: Kamrup, Goalpara, Karbi Anglong, Dima Hasao, Cachar, Karimganj and West Karbi Anglong.
Q: Which district of Assam shares its border with Tripura?
A: Hailakandi district.
Q: Which district of Assam shares its border with Mizoram?
A: Cachar, Hailakandi and Karimganj districts.
Q: Which district of Assam shares its border with West Bengal?
A: Kokrajhar, Dhubri and Chirang districts.
Q: Which is the longest inter-state border of Assam?
A: The border with Arunachal Pradesh is the longest.
Q: What is the total length of the international border of Assam?
A: About 288 kilometres with Bhutan and Bangladesh.
Q: What is the length of the Assam-Bhutan border?
A: About 267 kilometres.
Q: What is the length of the Assam-Bangladesh border?
A: About 21 to 22 kilometres.
Q: Which river forms a part of the border between Assam and Meghalaya?
A: The Simsang river and parts of the Kopili river area.
Q: Which river separates Assam from Arunachal Pradesh in some parts?
A: The Brahmaputra and its tributaries like the Siang and the Dibang areas.
Q: Which is the main border town of Assam on the Bhutan border?
A: Samdrup Jongkhar is on the Bhutan side, and the Assam side has Darrang's border areas.
Q: Which is the main land customs station of Assam on the Bangladesh border?
A: The Karimganj land customs station.
Q: Which river separates Assam from Bangladesh in the Dhubri area?
A: The Brahmaputra (Jamuna) river in the Dhubri area.
Q: Which pass connects Assam with Bhutan?
A: The passes of the Bhutan hills in the north, like the Buxa area route.
Q: Which is the border district of Assam on the south-west side?
A: Kokrajhar and Dhubri districts.
Q: Which river flows into Bangladesh from the Barak valley of Assam?
A: The Barak river, which becomes the Surma and later the Meghna.
Q: Which is the easternmost point of the border of Assam?
A: The Sadiya region in Tinsukia district.
Q: Which district of Assam is surrounded by other states?
A: Karimganj is surrounded by Bangladesh, Tripura and Mizoram on most sides.
Q: Which is the westernmost border point of Assam?
A: The Dhubri area on the West Bengal and Bangladesh border.
Q: With which countries and how many states does Assam share its borders?
A: Assam shares international borders with two countries, Bhutan and Bangladesh, and its total international border is about 288 kilometres. Within India it shares borders with seven states: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram and West Bengal. The border with Bhutan is about 267 kilometres long and the border with Bangladesh is only about 21 to 22 kilometres long.
Q: Which is the longest inter-state border of Assam and which districts lie along it?
A: The longest inter-state border of Assam is with Arunachal Pradesh. The districts along this border are Tinsukia, Dibrugarh, Lakhimpur, Dhemaji, Sonitpur, Biswanath and Baksa, and the Brahmaputra with its tributaries such as the Siang and the Dibang marks parts of this boundary. The border with Meghalaya is also long but shorter than the border with Arunachal Pradesh.
Q: Which rivers form the boundaries of Assam?
A: Between Assam and Meghalaya the Simsang and the Kopili mark parts of the boundary, and between Assam and Arunachal Pradesh the Brahmaputra and its tributaries the Siang and the Dibang mark the boundary. On the western side in Dhubri the boundary with Bangladesh follows the Brahmaputra, which in Bangladesh is called the Jamuna, and the Barak flows out of Assam into Bangladesh where it becomes the Surma and later the Meghna.
Q: What are the main land customs station and border town of Assam?
A: On the Bangladesh border the main land customs station of Assam is at Karimganj, which is an important centre of trade. On the Bhutan border the important neighbouring town is Samdrup Jongkhar in Bhutan, reached through the Darrang and Sonitpur side, and many routes into Bhutan pass through the Bhutan hills and the Buxa area. Karimganj district is notable as it is surrounded by Bangladesh, Tripura and Mizoram on different sides.
Q: Which are the easternmost and westernmost parts of Assam?
A: The easternmost part of Assam lies near Sadiya in Tinsukia district, and the westernmost part lies in the Dhubri area. The south-western border districts are Kokrajhar and Dhubri. Keeping these extremes in mind helps in map-based questions and in matching districts with directions, and it is useful to remember that Dhubri also lies along the Bangladesh border formed by the Brahmaputra.
Q: অসমে কোন কোন দেশ আৰু কিমান ৰাজ্যৰ সৈতে সীমা ভাগ কৰে?
A: অসমে দুখন দেশ, ভূটান আৰু বাংলাদেশৰ সৈতে আন্তঃৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় সীমা ভাগ কৰে, আৰু ইয়াৰ মুঠ আন্তঃৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় সীমা প্ৰায় ২৮৮ কিলোমিটাৰ। ভাৰতৰ ভিতৰত ই সাতখন ৰাজ্যৰ সৈতে সীমা ভাগ কৰে: অৰুণাচল প্ৰদেশ, নাগালেণ্ড, মণিপুৰ, মেঘালয়, ত্ৰিপুৰা, মিজোৰাম আৰু পশ্চিম বংগ। ভূটানৰ সৈতে সীমা প্ৰায় ২৬৭ কিলোমিটাৰ আৰু বাংলাদেশৰ সৈতে সীমা কেৱল প্ৰায় ২১ৰ পৰা ২২ কিলোমিটাৰ।
Q: অসমৰ দীঘলতম আন্তঃৰাজ্যিক সীমা কোনখন ৰাজ্যৰ সৈতে আৰু কোনবোৰ জিলা ইয়াৰ কাষত?
A: অসমৰ দীঘলতম আন্তঃৰাজ্যিক সীমা অৰুণাচল প্ৰদেশৰ সৈতে। এই সীমাৰ কাষৰ জিলাবোৰ হৈছে তিনিচুকীয়া, ডিব্ৰুগড়, লখিমপুৰ, ধেমাজি, শোণিতপুৰ, বিশ্বনাথ আৰু বাক্সা, আৰু ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ আৰু ইয়াৰ উপনদী ছিয়াং আৰু দিবাংয়ে এই সীমাৰ অংশ চিহ্নিত কৰে। মেঘালয়ৰ সৈতে সীমাও দীঘল কিন্তু অৰুণাচল প্ৰদেশৰ সীমাতকৈ চুটি।
Q: কোনবোৰ নদীয়ে অসমৰ সীমা গঠন কৰে?
A: অসম আৰু মেঘালয়ৰ মাজত ছিমছাং আৰু কপিলীয়ে সীমাৰ অংশ চিহ্নিত কৰে, আৰু অসম আৰু অৰুণাচল প্ৰদেশৰ মাজত ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ আৰু ইয়াৰ উপনদী ছিয়াং আৰু দিবাংয়ে সীমা চিহ্নিত কৰে। পশ্চিমে ধুবুৰীত বাংলাদেশৰ সৈতে সীমাই ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰক অনুসৰণ কৰে, যাক বাংলাদেশত যমুনা বোলা হয়, আৰু বৰাক অসমৰ পৰা বাংলাদেশলৈ বৈ গৈ শুৰ্মা আৰু পিছত মেঘনা হয়।
Q: অসমৰ মূল স্থল শুল্ক কেন্দ্ৰ আৰু সীমান্ত নগৰ কি?
A: বাংলাদেশ সীমান্তত অসমৰ মূল স্থল শুল্ক কেন্দ্ৰ কৰিমগঞ্জত, যি বাণিজ্যৰ এক গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ কেন্দ্ৰ। ভূটান সীমান্তত গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ ছিঙৰ নগৰ ভূটানৰ সমদ্ৰুপ জোংখৰ, য'ত দৰং আৰু শোণিতপুৰ দিশেৰে গৈ পোৱা যায়, আৰু ভূটানলৈ যোৱা বহু পথ ভূটান পাহাৰ আৰু বক্সা অঞ্চলৰ মাজেৰে যায়। কৰিমগঞ্জ জিলা বিশেষ কাৰণ ই বিভিন্ন দিশৰ পৰা বাংলাদেশ, ত্ৰিপুৰা আৰু মিজোৰামেৰে আগুৰি আছে।
Q: অসমৰ আটাইতকৈ পূব আৰু আটাইতকৈ পশ্চিমৰ অংশ কি?
A: অসমৰ আটাইতকৈ পূবৰ অংশ তিনিচুকীয়া জিলাৰ ছদিয়াৰ ওচৰত, আৰু আটাইতকৈ পশ্চিমৰ অংশ ধুবুৰী অঞ্চলত। দক্ষিণ-পশ্চিমৰ সীমান্ত জিলাবোৰ কোকৰাঝাৰ আৰু ধুবুৰী। এই চৰমবোৰ মনত ৰখাই মানচিত্ৰ-ভিত্তিক প্ৰশ্ন আৰু জিলা-দিশ মিলোৱা প্ৰশ্নত সহায় কৰে, আৰু ধুবুৰী ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰই গঠন কৰা বাংলাদেশ সীমাৰ কাষতো অৱস্থিত বুলি মনত ৰখা উপযোগী।

### Brahmaputra & Barak Valley — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/assam-geography-sec/brahmaputra-barak-valley/
Summary: Practice brahmaputra & barak valley questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Where does the Brahmaputra river originate?
A: From the Chemayungdung glacier in the Kailash range of the Himalayas in Tibet.
Q: What is the Tibetan name of the Brahmaputra river?
A: Tsangpo (Yarlung Tsangpo).
Q: Through which mountain range does the Brahmaputra enter India?
A: The Eastern Himalayas, near Sadiya in Arunachal Pradesh.
Q: What is the name of the Brahmaputra after it enters Arunachal Pradesh?
A: Siang (Dihang).
Q: What is the total length of the Brahmaputra river?
A: About 2,900 km, of which about 900 km flows through Assam.
Q: Which is the largest river valley in Assam?
A: The Brahmaputra valley.
Q: Where does the Brahmaputra enter Bangladesh?
A: Near Dhubri in Assam, after which it is known as the Jamuna in Bangladesh.
Q: Where does the Brahmaputra finally meet the sea?
A: It merges with the Ganga (Padma) and the Meghna before falling into the Bay of Bengal.
Q: Where does the Barak river originate?
A: From the hills of Manipur.
Q: Which is the largest river of the Barak valley?
A: The Barak river.
Q: Which districts are part of the Barak valley?
A: Cachar, Karimganj and Hailakandi.
Q: What is the Barak river known as in Bangladesh?
A: It splits into the Surma and the Kushiyara.
Q: Which is the only major tributary joining the Brahmaputra from the south in the lower reaches?
A: The Manas river.
Q: What type of river is the Brahmaputra in terms of flow?
A: It is a braided river with a large number of channels and sandbars.
Q: Which is the largest river island in the world located in Assam?
A: Majuli, formed by the Brahmaputra river.
Q: What is the characteristic feature of the Brahmaputra's north bank?
A: Steeper slopes and erosion, with fewer tributaries from the north.
Q: Which is the main river system of South Assam?
A: The Barak river system.
Q: What is the annual flood problem mainly caused by in Assam?
A: The heavy monsoon discharge of the Brahmaputra and its tributaries.
Q: Which valley is known as the tea valley of Assam?
A: The Brahmaputra valley, especially the upper Assam region.
Q: Which river is called the 'sorrow of Assam'?
A: The Brahmaputra, due to its frequent devastating floods.
Q: Which is the longest bridge over the Brahmaputra in Assam?
A: The Bhupen Hazarika Setu (Dhola-Sadiya bridge).
Q: Which tributary of the Brahmaputra is known as the 'Lohit'?
A: The Lohit river, a major tributary joining from Arunachal Pradesh.
Q: What is the average width of the Brahmaputra in Assam?
A: It ranges from about 1 km to 18 km in different stretches.
Q: Which is the deepest point of the Brahmaputra?
A: Near Sadiya, where the depth exceeds 38 metres at some places.
Q: Which are the major tributaries of the Brahmaputra from the north?
A: Subansiri, Siang, Dibang, Lohit, Dhansiri (north) and Sankosh.
Q: What is the name of the Brahmaputra before it enters India?
A: Yarlung Tsangpo (in Tibet).
Q: Why is the Brahmaputra called a braided river?
A: A braided river carries a very heavy load of silt and sand, and instead of flowing in one deep channel it breaks up into many shifting channels separated by sandbars and islands. The Brahmaputra shows this pattern all along its course in Assam, which is why its bed keeps changing, its banks erode quickly and new chaporis and islands appear and disappear over time.
Q: Is the Barak river a part of the Brahmaputra system?
A: No. The Brahmaputra and the Barak are two independent river systems. The Brahmaputra rises in Tibet and flows across northern Assam, while the Barak rises in the hills of Manipur and drains southern Assam. They meet the sea by different routes and are separated for their entire course by the hills of Meghalaya and the Barail range.
Q: Which districts make up the Barak valley and why are they flood-prone?
A: The Barak valley consists of Cachar, Karimganj and Hailakandi. The valley lies in a bowl surrounded by hills, so when the monsoon is heavy the Barak and its tributaries fill up quickly and the water has nowhere to spread. This makes the valley one of the most flood-prone parts of Assam, and local floods can occur even when the rest of the state is comparatively dry.
Q: How did Majuli come into existence?
A: Majuli is a river island created by the Brahmaputra and its distributaries. Over centuries the river changed its course and left behind a large landmass between its channels. Today it is regarded as the largest river island in the world and is also the centre of Assamese Vaishnavite culture, with many satras located on it.
Q: What should a candidate remember about the Brahmaputra for Assam exams?
A: Focus on five things: the source at the Chemayungdung glacier, the Tibetan name Yarlung Tsangpo, the entry into India near Sadiya where it is called the Siang or Dihang, the total length of about 2,900 kilometres with about 900 kilometres in Assam, and its exit near Dhubri into Bangladesh where it becomes the Jamuna. These five facts answer the majority of questions asked on this river.
Q: ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰক শাখা-প্ৰশাখাযুক্ত নদী কিয় বোলা হয়?
A: শাখা-প্ৰশাখাযুক্ত নদীয়ে অতি বেছি পলস আৰু বালি কঢ়িয়াই আনে আৰু এটা গভীৰ খালত নবৈ বলচৰ আৰু দ্বীপেৰে পৃথক হৈ অসংখ্য সলনীয়া খালত ভাগ হৈ যায়। ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰই অসমৰ গোটেই পথত এই ধৰণ দেখুৱায়, সেইকাৰণেই ইয়াৰ বিছনা সদায় সলনি হয়, পাৰ খহনীয়া হয় আৰু নতুন চাপৰি তথা দ্বীপ সৃষ্টি আৰু ধ্বংস হৈ থাকে।
Q: বৰাক নদী ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ ব্যৱস্থাৰ এটা অংশ নেকি?
A: নহয়। ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ আৰু বৰাক দুটা স্বতন্ত্ৰ নদী ব্যৱস্থা। ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ তিব্বতৰ পৰা ওলাই উত্তৰ অসমৰ মাজেৰে বৈ যায়, আনহাতে বৰাক মণিপুৰৰ পাহাৰৰ পৰা ওলাই দক্ষিণ অসম নিষ্কাশন কৰে। ইহঁতে বেলেগ বেলেগ পথেৰে সাগৰত পৰে আৰু মেঘালয়ৰ পাহাৰ তথা বৰাইল শ্ৰেণীয়ে গোটেই পথটোত ইহঁতক পৃথক কৰি ৰাখে।
Q: বৰাক উপত্যকাত কোনবোৰ জিলা পৰে আৰু ই কিয় বানপ্ৰৱণ?
A: বৰাক উপত্যকাত কাছাৰ, কৰিমগঞ্জ আৰু হাইলাকান্দি জিলা পৰে। উপত্যকাটো পাহাৰৰে আগুৰা এটা চৰুৰ দৰে, গতিকে মৌচুমী বৰষুণ বেছি হ'লে বৰাক আৰু ইয়াৰ উপনদীবোৰ লগে লগে ভৰি পৰে আৰু পানী বিয়পিবলৈ ঠাই নাথাকে। ইয়াৰ ফলত এই উপত্যকা অসমৰ আটাইতকৈ বানপ্ৰৱণ অংশসমূহৰ এটা হৈ পৰিছে আৰু ৰাজ্যখনৰ অন্য অংশ শুকান থাকিলেও ইয়াত স্থানীয় বানপানী হ'ব পাৰে।
Q: মাজুলী কেনেকৈ সৃষ্টি হৈছিল?
A: মাজুলী ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ আৰু ইয়াৰ উপশাখাবোৰে সৃষ্টি কৰা এখন নদী-দ্বীপ। শতিকাজুৰি নদীয়ে নিজৰ গতি সলনি কৰাৰ ফলত ইয়াৰ খালবোৰৰ মাজত এটা ডাঙৰ ভূ-ভাগ ৰৈ যায়। আজি ই পৃথিৱীৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ নদী-দ্বীপ হিচাপে পৰিগণিত আৰু অসমীয়া বৈষ্ণৱ সংস্কৃতিৰ কেন্দ্ৰও, য'ত বহু সত্ৰ অৱস্থিত।
Q: অসমৰ পৰীক্ষাৰ বাবে ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰৰ বিষয়ে কি মনত ৰখা উচিত?
A: পাঁচটা কথাত গুৰুত্ব দিয়ক: চেমায়ুংদুং হিমবাহত উৎপত্তি, তিব্বতী নাম যাৰলুং চাংপো, সাদিয়াৰ ওচৰত ভাৰতত প্ৰৱেশ য'ত ইয়াক সিয়াং বা দিহাং বোলা হয়, মুঠ দীঘ প্ৰায় ২,৯০০ কিলোমিটাৰ যাৰ ৯০০ কিলোমিটাৰ অসমত, আৰু ধুবুৰীৰ ওচৰত বাংলাদেশলৈ গৈ যমুনা হোৱা। এই পাঁচটা তথ্যই এই নদীৰ ওপৰত সোধা অধিকাংশ প্ৰশ্নৰ উত্তৰ দিয়ে।

### Brahmaputra River Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/assam-geography-sec/brahmaputra-river/
Summary: 50 questions on the Brahmaputra river with answers for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Covers its source, tributaries, islands, floods and importance to Assam.
Q: Where is the source of the Brahmaputra river?
A: It rises from the Chemayungdung glacier near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet and is called the Yarlung Tsangpo there.
Q: Which is the largest river island in the Brahmaputra?
A: Majuli is one of the largest river islands in the world and lies in the Brahmaputra in Assam.
Q: What is the Brahmaputra called in Bangladesh?
A: After entering Bangladesh the Brahmaputra is called the Jamuna, and it later joins the Ganga to form the Padma.

### Climate, Monsoon & Floods — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/assam-geography-sec/climate-monsoon-floods-assam/
Summary: Practice climate, monsoon & floods questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What type of climate does Assam have?
A: A humid subtropical climate with heavy rainfall.
Q: What is the average annual rainfall of Assam?
A: About 2,500 mm to 3,000 mm.
Q: Which is the wettest place in Assam?
A: Mawsynram in Meghalaya is the wettest overall, but in Assam the northern districts receive high rainfall.
Q: Which monsoon brings most of the rainfall to Assam?
A: The South-West monsoon.
Q: During which months does Assam receive the maximum rainfall?
A: June to September.
Q: What is the average temperature of Assam in summer?
A: About 25°C to 32°C.
Q: What is the average winter temperature of Assam?
A: About 10°C to 15°C.
Q: Which are the main seasons of Assam?
A: Winter, Pre-monsoon, Monsoon and Retreating monsoon.
Q: What is the 'Kalbaisakhi' or 'Bordoisila'?
A: The local thunderstorm which occurs in the pre-monsoon season (April-May) in Assam.
Q: What is the main cause of the floods in Assam?
A: The heavy monsoon rainfall and the siltation of the Brahmaputra and its tributaries.
Q: How many times in a year does Assam generally experience floods?
A: Generally two to three waves of floods during the monsoon season.
Q: Which is the flood-prone district of Assam?
A: Most districts of the Brahmaputra valley, especially Morigaon, Nagaon, Barpeta and Dhubri, are flood-prone.
Q: Which organization manages the flood control in Assam?
A: The Brahmaputra Board and the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA).
Q: What is the Brahmaputra Board?
A: A statutory body set up in 1980 for the planning of flood control and development of the Brahmaputra valley.
Q: What is the effect of floods on the agriculture of Assam?
A: It damages the paddy crops and reduces agricultural productivity.
Q: What is the annual loss caused by floods in Assam estimated at?
A: The floods cause enormous losses of life, property and crops every year.
Q: Which wind is responsible for the heavy rainfall of Assam?
A: The moisture-laden south-west monsoon winds from the Bay of Bengal.
Q: What is the average humidity of Assam?
A: It is high throughout the year, ranging between 70% and 90%.
Q: Which is the coldest region of Assam?
A: The hill district of Dima Hasao (North Cachar Hills).
Q: What is the main source of the monsoon rainfall of Assam?
A: The Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea branches of the south-west monsoon.
Q: Which place of Assam receives the highest rainfall?
A: The northern districts like Lakhimpur and Dhemaji receive very high rainfall.
Q: What is the effect of the retreating monsoon on Assam?
A: It brings light rainfall and the onset of the winter season.
Q: Which river system is responsible for the floods in the Barak valley?
A: The Barak river and its tributaries.
Q: What is the role of embankments in flood control in Assam?
A: They are constructed along the rivers to prevent the water from overflowing, though they often breach.
Q: Which is the largest river of Assam responsible for most of its floods?
A: The Brahmaputra.
Q: What is the percentage of Assam's area that is flood-prone?
A: About 40% of the area of Assam is flood-prone.
Q: What type of climate does Assam have and how much rain does it receive?
A: Assam has a humid subtropical climate. Its average annual rainfall is generally between about 2,500 and 3,000 millimetres, most of it falling during the south-west monsoon from June to September. Humidity remains high throughout the year, usually between 70 and 90 per cent, and the northern districts receive some of the heaviest rain in the region.
Q: What is Kalbaisakhi or Bordoisila?
A: Kalbaisakhi is the violent pre-monsoon thunderstorm that occurs in Assam in April and May, and in Assamese it is popularly called Bordoisila. These storms come suddenly with strong winds, thunder and heavy short showers. They can damage crops and trees, but they also cool the air and prepare the soil for the coming monsoon, which is why they are both feared and welcomed.
Q: What are the main causes of floods in Assam?
A: The main causes are the extremely heavy monsoon rainfall in the catchment, the siltation that raises river beds, and the braided, shifting nature of the Brahmaputra which causes bank erosion and breaches embankments. Deforestation and rapid runoff in the hills, and the hill-locked Barak valley in the south, add to the problem. Together these factors make about 40 per cent of the state flood-prone.
Q: Which agencies handle flood control and disaster management in Assam?
A: The Brahmaputra Board, set up in 1980, is the statutory body for planning flood control and the development of the Brahmaputra valley. The Assam State Disaster Management Authority, ASDMA, is responsible for disaster preparedness, relief and rescue during floods. Together with the state water resources department, these agencies carry out embankment work, early warning and relief operations.
Q: How many waves of floods does Assam usually face in a year?
A: Assam generally experiences about two to three waves of floods during a single monsoon season. The first wave usually comes with the early heavy rain, and later waves follow as the monsoon continues and the rivers remain full. The Barak valley also floods, but its floods are shorter and more local because the valley is smaller and surrounded by hills.
Q: অসমৰ জলবায়ু কেনে আৰু ই কিমান বৰষুণ পায়?
A: অসমৰ জলবায়ু আৰ্দ্ৰ উপক্ৰান্তীয়। ইয়াৰ বছৰেকীয়া গড় বৰষুণ সাধাৰণতে প্ৰায় ২,৫০০ৰ পৰা ৩,০০০ মিলিমিটাৰ, যাৰ মূল অংশ জুনৰ পৰা ছেপ্তেম্বৰলৈ দক্ষিণ-পশ্চিম মৌচুমীকালত পৰে। আৰ্দ্ৰতা বছৰজুৰি বেছি থাকে, সাধাৰণতে ৭০ৰ পৰা ৯০ শতাংশ, আৰু উত্তৰ জিলাসমূহত অঞ্চলটোৰ আটাইতকৈ বেছি বৰষুণ হয়।
Q: কালবৈশাখী বা বৰদৈচিলা কি?
A: কালবৈশাখী হৈছে এপ্ৰিল আৰু মে' মাহত অসমত হোৱা তীব্ৰ পূৰ্ব-মৌচুমী বজ্ৰপাত-ধুমুহা, আৰু অসমীয়াত ইয়াক জনপ্ৰিয়ভাৱে বৰদৈচিলা বোলা হয়। এই ধুমুহাবোৰ হঠাতে প্ৰবল বতাহ, বজ্ৰপাত আৰু বেছি চুটি বৰষুণৰ সৈতে আহে। ইহঁতে শস্য তথা গছৰ ক্ষতি কৰিব পাৰে, কিন্তু বতাহ শীতল কৰি অহা মৌচুমীৰ বাবে মাটি সাজুও কৰে, সেয়েহে ইহঁতক ভয় আৰু আদৰণি দুয়ো কৰা হয়।
Q: অসমত বানপানীৰ প্ৰধান কাৰণবোৰ কি?
A: প্ৰধান কাৰণবোৰ হৈছে জলগ্ৰহণ অঞ্চলত পৰা অতি বেছি মৌচুমী বৰষুণ, নদীৰ বিছনা ওখ কৰা পলস জমা, আৰু ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰৰ শাখা-প্ৰশাখাযুক্ত তথা গতিশীল প্ৰকৃতি যিয়ে পাৰ খহনীয়া আৰু বান্ধ ভাঙন ঘটায়। পাহাৰত বন ধ্বংস আৰু দ্ৰুত প্ৰবাহ, আৰু দক্ষিণৰ পাহাৰে আগুৰা বৰাক উপত্যকাই সমস্যা বঢ়ায়। এই কাৰকবোৰৰ ফলত ৰাজ্যখনৰ প্ৰায় ৪০ শতাংশ বানপ্ৰৱণ।
Q: অসমত বান নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ আৰু দুৰ্যোগ পৰিচালনা কোনে কৰে?
A: ১৯৮০ চনত গঠিত ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ ব'ৰ্ড হৈছে বান নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ তথা ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ উপত্যকাৰ বিকাশৰ পৰিকল্পনাৰ আইনী সংস্থা। অসম ৰাজ্যিক দুৰ্যোগ পৰিচালনা কৰ্তৃপক্ষ (ASDMA) বানৰ সময়ত দুৰ্যোগ প্ৰস্তুতি, সাহায্য আৰু উদ্ধাৰৰ বাবে দায়বদ্ধ। ৰাজ্যিক জলসম্পদ বিভাগৰ সৈতে এই সংস্থাবোৰে বান্ধৰ কাম, আগতীয়া সতৰ্কবাণী আৰু সাহায্য অভিযান চলায়।
Q: অসমত বছৰি সাধাৰণতে কিমান ঢৌ বান আহে?
A: অসমত এটা মৌচুমীকালত সাধাৰণতে প্ৰায় দুইৰ পৰা তিনি বাৰ বানৰ ঢৌ আহে। প্ৰথম ঢৌটো সাধাৰণতে আগতীয়া বেছি বৰষুণৰ সৈতে আহে, আৰু মৌচুমী চলি থকাৰ লগে লগে নদীবোৰ ভৰি থকাৰ ফলত পিছৰ ঢৌবোৰ আহে। বৰাক উপত্যকাও বানে, কিন্তু উপত্যকাটো সৰু আৰু পাহাৰে আগুৰা হোৱাৰ বাবে ইয়াৰ বান চুটি আৰু স্থানীয়।

### Population, Density & Literacy — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/assam-geography-sec/demography-population-density-literacy-assam/
Summary: Practice population, density & literacy questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What is the population of Assam as per the 2011 Census?
A: About 3.12 crore (31,205,576).
Q: What is the population density of Assam as per the 2011 Census?
A: 398 persons per square kilometre.
Q: What is the literacy rate of Assam as per the 2011 Census?
A: 72.19%.
Q: What is the male literacy rate of Assam?
A: 77.85%.
Q: What is the female literacy rate of Assam?
A: 66.27%.
Q: What is the sex ratio of Assam as per the 2011 Census?
A: 958 females per 1000 males.
Q: What is the child sex ratio of Assam?
A: 962 females per 1000 males.
Q: What is the decadal growth rate of the population of Assam (2001-2011)?
A: 16.93%.
Q: Which is the most populous district of Assam?
A: Nagaon district.
Q: Which is the least populous district of Assam?
A: Dima Hasao (earlier North Cachar Hills).
Q: Which district has the highest population density of Assam?
A: Kamrup (Metropolitan), which includes Guwahati city.
Q: Which district has the lowest population density of Assam?
A: Dima Hasao district.
Q: Which district has the highest literacy rate in Assam?
A: Kamrup (Metropolitan) district.
Q: Which district has the lowest literacy rate in Assam?
A: Dhubri district.
Q: What is the urban population percentage of Assam?
A: About 14.07% of the total population.
Q: What is the rural population percentage of Assam?
A: About 85.93% of the total population.
Q: What is the rank of Assam in terms of population among Indian states?
A: About 14th position.
Q: What is the total number of districts in Assam?
A: As of recent reorganization, 35 districts (with new districts created after 2011).
Q: Which is the largest district of Assam by area?
A: Karbi Anglong (before its division into East and West).
Q: Which is the smallest district of Assam by area?
A: Kamrup (Metropolitan).
Q: What is the main reason for the higher density of population in the Brahmaputra valley?
A: Fertile alluvial soil, adequate rainfall and better communication.
Q: What is the population of Guwahati city (as per the 2011 Census)?
A: About 9.57 lakh.
Q: What is the main cause of the slow decline of the sex ratio in Assam?
A: Female foeticide, neglect of girl children and migration factors.
Q: What is the share of Scheduled Tribes in the population of Assam?
A: About 12.4% of the total population.
Q: What is the share of Scheduled Castes in the population of Assam?
A: About 7.1% of the total population.
Q: Which census year is the latest completed census in Assam?
A: The 2011 Census.
Q: What are the population, density and literacy figures of Assam as per the 2011 Census?
A: As per the 2011 Census, the population of Assam is about 3.12 crore (31,205,576), the density is 398 persons per square kilometre, and the literacy rate is 72.19 per cent. The male literacy rate is 77.85 per cent and the female literacy rate is 66.27 per cent. The decadal growth rate for 2001-2011 was 16.93 per cent, and Assam ranks about 14th among Indian states in population.
Q: Which districts of Assam have the extremes of population, density and literacy?
A: Nagaon is the most populous district and Dima Hasao the least populous. Kamrup (Metropolitan) has the highest population density and Dima Hasao the lowest. Kamrup (Metropolitan) also has the highest literacy rate, while Dhubri has the lowest. By area, Karbi Anglong was the largest district before its division and Kamrup (Metropolitan) is the smallest. After the recent reorganisation the state has about 35 districts.
Q: What is the sex ratio of Assam and why has it been declining?
A: The sex ratio of Assam as per the 2011 Census is 958 females per 1000 males, and the child sex ratio is 962 females per 1000 males. Both are better than the all-India figures, yet the sex ratio has been slowly declining. The main causes are female foeticide, the neglect of girl children and factors linked to migration. Improving female literacy and health and strictly enforcing the law against sex determination are the main remedies.
Q: What is the rural-urban split and the social composition of Assam's population?
A: Assam is overwhelmingly rural: about 85.93 per cent of the population is rural and only about 14.07 per cent is urban, even though Guwahati is a large city with about 9.57 lakh people. Among the social groups, the Scheduled Tribes form about 12.4 per cent of the population and the Scheduled Castes about 7.1 per cent. These shares are important for reservation, welfare schemes and the distribution of resources.
Q: Why is the population density higher in the Brahmaputra valley?
A: The population density is higher in the Brahmaputra valley because of fertile alluvial soil, adequate rainfall and better communication. These conditions support intensive agriculture, trade and settlement, so the plains carry most of the state's people. The hill districts, by contrast, have steep slopes, thinner soils, large reserved forests and poorer connectivity, which is why Dima Hasao has the lowest density in the state.
Q: ২০১১ চনৰ লোকপিয়ল অনুযায়ী অসমৰ জনসংখ্যা, জনঘনত্ব আৰু সাক্ষৰতা কিমান?
A: ২০১১ চনৰ লোকপিয়ল অনুযায়ী অসমৰ জনসংখ্যা প্ৰায় ৩.১২ কোটি (৩১,২০৫,৫৭৬), জনঘনত্ব বৰ্গ কিলোমিটাৰত ৩৯৮ জন, আৰু সাক্ষৰতাৰ হাৰ ৭২.১৯ শতাংশ। পুৰুষ সাক্ষৰতাৰ হাৰ ৭৭.৮৫ শতাংশ আৰু মহিলা সাক্ষৰতাৰ হাৰ ৬৬.২৭ শতাংশ। ২০০১-২০১১ চনৰ দশকীয় বৃদ্ধিৰ হাৰ ১৬.৯৩ শতাংশ, আৰু জনসংখ্যাৰ দিশত অসম ভাৰতীয় ৰাজ্যসমূহৰ ভিতৰত প্ৰায় ১৪তম।
Q: অসমৰ কোন জিলাবোৰ জনসংখ্যা, জনঘনত্ব আৰু সাক্ষৰতাৰ চৰমত আছে?
A: নগাঁও সৰ্বাধিক জনসংখ্যাৰ জিলা আৰু দিমা হাচাও সৰ্বনিম্ন। কামৰূপ (মহানগৰ)ৰ সৰ্বাধিক জনঘনত্ব আৰু দিমা হাচাওৰ সৰ্বনিম্ন। কামৰূপ (মহানগৰ)ৰ সাক্ষৰতাৰ হাৰো সৰ্বাধিক, আনহাতে ধুবুৰীৰ সৰ্বনিম্ন। মাটিকালিৰ দিশত বিভাজনৰ আগতে কাৰ্বি আংলং বৃহত্তম জিলা আছিল আৰু কামৰূপ (মহানগৰ) সৰ্বনিম্ন। শেহতীয়া পুনৰ্গঠনৰ পিছত ৰাজ্যখনত প্ৰায় ৩৫ খন জিলা।
Q: অসমৰ লিংগ অনুপাত কিমান আৰু ই কিয় হ্ৰাস পাইছে?
A: ২০১১ চনৰ লোকপিয়ল অনুযায়ী অসমৰ লিংগ অনুপাত ১০০০ পুৰুষৰ বিপৰীতে ৯৫৮ মহিলা, আৰু শিশু লিংগ অনুপাত ১০০০ পুৰুষৰ বিপৰীতে ৯৬২ মহিলা। দুয়োটা সমগ্ৰ ভাৰতৰ হিচাপতকৈ ভাল, তথাপি লিংগ অনুপাত লাহে লাহে হ্ৰাস পাই আহিছে। মূল কাৰণ হৈছে ভ্ৰূণ হত্যা, ছোৱালী শিশুৰ অৱহেলা আৰু পৰিযায়নৰ সৈতে জড়িত কাৰক। মহিলা সাক্ষৰতা আৰু স্বাস্থ্যৰ উন্নতি, আৰু লিংগ নিৰ্ণয়ৰ বিৰুদ্ধে আইন কঠোৰভাৱে বলবৎ কৰাই মূল প্ৰতিকাৰ।
Q: অসমৰ গাঁৱলীয়া-চহৰীয়া বিভাজন আৰু জনসংখ্যাৰ সামাজিক গঠন কি?
A: অসম অতি গাঁৱলীয়া: জনসংখ্যাৰ প্ৰায় ৮৫.৯৩ শতাংশ গাঁৱলীয়া আৰু মাত্ৰ প্ৰায় ১৪.০৭ শতাংশ চহৰীয়া, যদিও গুৱাহাটী প্ৰায় ৯.৫৭ লাখ মানুহৰ এখন ডাঙৰ চহৰ। সামাজিক গোটসমূহৰ ভিতৰত অনুসূচিত জনজাতিয়ে জনসংখ্যাৰ প্ৰায় ১২.৪ শতাংশ আৰু অনুসূচিত জাতিয়ে প্ৰায় ৭.১ শতাংশ। এই অংশবোৰ সংৰক্ষণ, কল্যাণ আঁচনি আৰু সম্পদ বিতৰণৰ বাবে গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ।
Q: ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ উপত্যকাত জনঘনত্ব কিয় বেছি?
A: উৰ্বৰ পলসুৱা মাটি, যথেষ্ট বৰষুণ আৰু ভাল যাতায়াতৰ বাবে ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ উপত্যকাত জনঘনত্ব বেছি। এই অৱস্থাই নিবিড় কৃষি, বাণিজ্য আৰু বসতিক সমৰ্থন কৰে, সেইকাৰণেই সমভূমিয়ে ৰাজ্যখনৰ বেছিভাগ মানুহ বহন কৰে। ইয়াৰ বিপৰীতে পাহাৰীয়া জিলাবোৰত তীক্ষ্ণ ঢাল, পাতল মাটি, বিস্তীৰ্ণ সংৰক্ষিত বন আৰু দুৰ্বল সংযোগ আছে, সেইকাৰণেই দিমা হাচাওৰ জনঘনত্ব ৰাজ্যখনত সৰ্বনিম্ন।

### Forest Types & Area Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/assam-geography-sec/forest-types-area-assam/
Summary: Practice forest types & area questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What percentage of Assam's total geographical area is covered by forest?
A: About 35% to 36% is under forest and tree cover.
Q: Which type of forest covers the largest area in Assam?
A: Tropical wet evergreen forests and tropical moist deciduous forests.
Q: Which forests are found in the lower reaches of the Brahmaputra valley?
A: Tropical moist deciduous and semi-evergreen forests.
Q: Which type of forest is found in the upper reaches of the Brahmaputra valley?
A: Tropical wet evergreen forests.
Q: Which forests are found in the hill districts of Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao?
A: Subtropical evergreen and montane (temperate) forests.
Q: Which is the main forest type of the Barak valley?
A: Tropical wet evergreen and semi-evergreen forests.
Q: Which trees are found in the tropical wet evergreen forests of Assam?
A: Hollong, Nahor, Ajhar, Mekang and Nahar trees.
Q: Which is the tallest tree of the Assam rainforest?
A: The Hollong tree (Dipterocarpus macrocarpus).
Q: What are the grassland areas of Assam called?
A: They are called 'khayer' or floodplain grasslands, like those of Kaziranga.
Q: Which is the largest forest division of Assam?
A: The Karbi Anglong forest division is among the largest in area.
Q: What is the total recorded forest area of Assam?
A: About 26,000 to 27,000 square kilometres.
Q: Which forest type covers the Kaziranga National Park?
A: Tropical moist deciduous forests and alluvial grasslands.
Q: Which bamboo species is abundant in the forests of Assam?
A: Muli (Melocanna) and Jati (Bambusa) bamboo species.
Q: Which sanctuary of Assam is known for its semi-evergreen forests?
A: The Nameri and the Dibru-Saikhowa sanctuaries have semi-evergreen forests.
Q: What is the main forest product of the forests of Assam?
A: Timber, bamboo and cane.
Q: Which is the main timber tree of the tropical moist deciduous forests of Assam?
A: Sal (Shorea robusta) and Teak.
Q: What is the 'reserved forest' in Assam?
A: A forest notified for protection and conservation under the Forest Act.
Q: Which district has the highest forest cover in Assam?
A: Karbi Anglong has the highest forest cover.
Q: Which type of forest is found along the river banks of the Brahmaputra?
A: Riverine (riparian) forests and grasslands.
Q: What is the main vegetation of the Manas National Park?
A: Tropical moist deciduous forests, alluvial grasslands and bamboo forests.
Q: Which rare tree is found in the Dehing-Patkai rainforest?
A: The Hollong, and the giant tree species of the lowland evergreen forests.
Q: What is the trend of the forest cover in Assam in recent years?
A: There has been a slight decrease in dense forest cover but an increase in open forest cover.
Q: Which forest is famous for the 'Sal' trees in Assam?
A: The Sal forests of the western districts like the Nameri area and the lower Brahmaputra region.
Q: Which is the main cause of the depletion of forests in Assam?
A: Jhum cultivation, illegal felling, encroachment and floods.
Q: What is the forest cover percentage of Assam as per the latest State of Forest Report?
A: About 36% of the geographical area is under forest cover.
Q: Which tree species is found in the subtropical forests of the Barail range?
A: Species like the Nahor, the Ajar and the Orchid-bearing trees of the moist forests.
Q: What percentage of Assam is under forest?
A: According to the latest State of Forest Report, forest and tree cover together account for about 36 per cent of Assam's geographical area. The recorded forest area, which is a legal rather than a green-cover measure, is about 26,000 to 27,000 square kilometres. The two figures are often confused, but they answer different questions and should be remembered separately.
Q: Which forest type covers the largest area in Assam?
A: The tropical wet evergreen forests and the tropical moist deciduous forests together cover the largest area. The wet evergreen forests dominate the upper Brahmaputra valley, the Barak valley and the eastern hills, while the moist deciduous forests dominate the lower Brahmaputra valley. Subtropical and montane forests are important but occupy a much smaller area in the hills of Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao.
Q: What is the tallest tree of Assam and what are the common bamboos?
A: The tallest tree of the Assam rainforest is the Hollong, Dipterocarpus macrocarpus, which is also the state tree. Among the common bamboos, the two most widespread are Muli (Melocanna) and Jati (Bambusa). Both bamboo and cane are major forest products, and along with timber and fuelwood they support the rural economy of the state.
Q: Which district has the highest forest cover in Assam?
A: Karbi Anglong has the highest forest cover in Assam, and it also has one of the largest forest divisions in the state. Dima Hasao follows with a high proportion of forest land.
