The two hill districts together account for a very large share of the state's total forest area because of their rugged terrain, low population density and extensive reserved forests.
Q: What are the main threats to the forests of Assam?
A: The main threats are jhum or shifting cultivation in the hills, illegal felling, encroachment on forest land, and floods and riverbank erosion. Forest fires, mining and quarrying, and the spread of roads and settlements add to the pressure. Because the causes are linked, conservation in Assam works on several fronts at once - protecting reserved forests, settling rights fairly and restoring degraded land.
Q: অসমৰ কিমান শতাংশ বনাঞ্চল আছে?
A: শেহতীয়া বন প্ৰতিবেদন অনুযায়ী বন আৰু গছ আৱৰণ একেলগে অসমৰ ভৌগোলিক মাটিকালিৰ প্ৰায় ৩৬ শতাংশ। আনহাতে নথিভুক্ত বনাঞ্চল, যি সেউজ আৱৰণৰ পৰিমাপ নহয় আইনী পৰিমাপ, প্ৰায় ২৬,০০০ৰ পৰা ২৭,০০০ বৰ্গ কিলোমিটাৰ। দুটা হিচাপ সঘনাই লগাই পেলোৱা হয়, কিন্তু দুয়ে ভিন্ন প্ৰশ্নৰ উত্তৰ দিয়ে আৰু সুকীয়াকৈ মনত ৰখা উচিত।
Q: অসমত সৰ্বাধিক মাটিকালি কোন বন প্ৰকাৰে আৱৰি আছে?
A: ক্ৰান্তীয় আৰ্দ্ৰ চিৰসেউজ বন আৰু ক্ৰান্তীয় আৰ্দ্ৰ পতনশীল বন একেলগে সৰ্বাধিক মাটিকালি আৱৰি আছে। আৰ্দ্ৰ চিৰসেউজ বনে ওপৰ ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ উপত্যকা, বৰাক উপত্যকা আৰু পূবৰ পাহাৰত প্ৰাধান্য লাভ কৰে, আনহিতে আৰ্দ্ৰ পতনশীল বনে তলৰ ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ উপত্যকাত। উপ-ক্ৰান্তীয় আৰু পৰ্বতীয়া বন গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ কিন্তু কাৰ্বি আংলং আৰু দিমা হাচাওৰ পাহাৰত অনেক কম মাটিকালিত সীমাবদ্ধ।
Q: অসমৰ আটাইতকৈ ওখ গছ আৰু সাধাৰণ বাঁহবোৰ কি?
A: অসমৰ বৰ্ষাৰণ্যৰ আটাইতকৈ ওখ গছ হৈছে হলং, Dipterocarpus macrocarpus, যি ৰাজ্যিক গছো। সাধাৰণ বাঁহবোৰৰ ভিতৰত আটাইতকৈ বিস্তৃত হৈছে মুলি (Melocanna) আৰু জাতি (Bambusa)। বাঁহ আৰু বেত দুয়োটা মুখ্য বনজ সামগ্ৰী, আৰু কাঠ তথা ইন্ধন কাঠৰ লগতে ই ৰাজ্যখনৰ গাঁৱলীয়া অৰ্থনীতিক ধৰি ৰাখে।
Q: অসমত সৰ্বাধিক বনাঞ্চল থকা জিলা কোনখন?
A: কাৰ্বি আংলংত অসমৰ সৰ্বাধিক বনাঞ্চল আছে, আৰু ই ৰাজ্যখনৰ আটাইতকৈ বৃহৎ বন বিভাগসমূহৰ এটা। দিমা হাচাও বনাঞ্চলৰ উচ্চ অনুপাতৰ সৈতে ইয়াৰ পিছতেই আছে। দুখন পাহাৰীয়া জিলাই দুৰ্গম ভূ-প্ৰকৃতি, কম জনঘনত্ব আৰু বিস্তীৰ্ণ সংৰক্ষিত বনৰ বাবে ৰাজ্যখনৰ মুঠ বনাঞ্চলৰ অতি বৃহৎ অংশ আগুৰি আছে।
Q: অসমৰ বনৰ প্ৰতি প্ৰধান ভাবুকিবোৰ কি?
A: প্ৰধান ভাবুকিবোৰ হৈছে পাহাৰত ঝুম বা স্থানান্তৰিত খেতি, অবৈধ গছ কটা, বন মাটিত দখল, আৰু বানপানী তথা নদীপাৰ খহনীয়া। বনৰ জুই, খনি আৰু খনন, আৰু পথ তথা বসতিৰ বিস্তাৰে চাপ বঢ়ায়। কাৰণবোৰ জড়িত হোৱাৰ বাবে অসমত সংৰক্ষণে একেসময়তে কেইবাটাও দিশত কাম কৰে - সংৰক্ষিত বন সুৰক্ষা, অধিকাৰ ন্যায্যভাৱে নিষ্পত্তি আৰু ক্ষয়প্ৰাপ্ত মাটি পুনৰুদ্ধাৰ।

### Hills: Karbi Anglong & Dima Hasao — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/assam-geography-sec/hills-karbi-dima-hasao/
Summary: Practice hills: karbi anglong & dima hasao questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Which are the two hill districts of Assam?
A: Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao.
Q: What was the former name of Dima Hasao district?
A: North Cachar Hills district.
Q: What was the former name of Karbi Anglong district?
A: United Mikir and North Cachar Hills district.
Q: What is the headquarters of Karbi Anglong district?
A: Diphu.
Q: What is the headquarters of Dima Hasao district?
A: Haflong.
Q: What is the highest peak of the Barail Range?
A: Temple Peak (Laike) in the North Cachar Hills.
Q: What is the highest peak of the Karbi Anglong hills?
A: Singhasan (Dhengdhenjan) peak, about 1,360 metres high.
Q: Which hill range lies between the Brahmaputra valley and the Barak valley?
A: The Meghalaya plateau extension and the North Cachar (Barail) hills.
Q: Which is the only hill station of Assam?
A: Haflong.
Q: What is the main language spoken by the Karbi people?
A: Karbi (Mikir).
Q: Which tribe is mainly found in Dima Hasao district?
A: The Dimasa (Kachari) tribe.
Q: Which river flows through the Karbi Anglong hills?
A: The Dhansiri river.
Q: What is the area of Karbi Anglong district?
A: About 10,434 square kilometres, the largest district of Assam.
Q: What is the area of Dima Hasao district?
A: About 4,890 square kilometres.
Q: Which is the major town of Dima Hasao district?
A: Haflong, the district headquarters.
Q: Which national highway passes through Karbi Anglong connecting it with the rest of Assam?
A: NH-36 (Guwahati to Dimapur) and NH-39 (through the hills).
Q: What is the main occupation of the people of Karbi Anglong?
A: Agriculture, especially jhum (shifting) cultivation and paddy cultivation.
Q: Which mineral is found in the Karbi Anglong hills?
A: Limestone and coal are found in the hill areas.
Q: Which reserved forest is located in Dima Hasao district?
A: The Dima Hasao area has several reserved forests like the Jatinga and Umrangso areas.
Q: What is Jatinga in Dima Hasao famous for?
A: The mysterious phenomenon of bird suicide, where birds are attracted to light at night.
Q: Which peak of Karbi Anglong is considered the highest point of the district?
A: Singhasan peak.
Q: What type of climate does the hill district of Dima Hasao have?
A: A cool temperate climate due to the high elevation.
Q: Which river originates from the North Cachar (Barail) hills?
A: The Barak river and several of its tributaries.
Q: What is the ethnic festival celebrated by the Karbi community?
A: The Rongker festival.
Q: Which is the headquarters of the Dima Hasao Autonomous Council?
A: Haflong.
Q: Under which Schedule of the Constitution are Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao covered?
A: The Sixth Schedule.
Q: Which are the only two hill districts of Assam?
A: The two hill districts of Assam are Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao. Both lie to the south of the Brahmaputra valley, are largely hilly, and enjoy special administrative arrangements under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution through their autonomous councils. Karbi Anglong is the larger district, while Dima Hasao is the smaller of the two.
Q: What is the constitutional basis for the hill districts of Assam?
A: Both districts are covered by the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution, which provides for autonomous district councils in the hill areas of the north-eastern states. This is why Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao have autonomous councils with powers over land, forests and local administration, which ordinary districts of Assam do not have.
Q: Why is Haflong important?
A: Haflong is the headquarters of Dima Hasao district and is the only hill station of Assam. It stands at a high elevation, so its climate is cooler than the plains, and it is known for its scenery, its lakes and its role as the base for visiting the district. The headquarters of the Dima Hasao Autonomous Council is also located at Haflong.
Q: What is the Jatinga phenomenon?
A: Jatinga, a small place in Dima Hasao district, is known for a much-discussed phenomenon in which birds are said to fly towards lights on dark, misty nights and fall to the ground. It has been widely written about and attracts researchers and visitors, and it is one of the most commonly asked Dima Hasao facts in competitive examinations.
Q: What is jhum cultivation and where is it practised in Assam?
A: Jhum, or shifting cultivation, is a traditional method in which a patch of hillside forest is cleared and cultivated for a few years and then left fallow so that the soil can recover. It is practised mainly by the communities of the hill districts such as Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao, alongside settled paddy farming in the flatter parts of those districts.
Q: অসমৰ একমাত্ৰ দুখন পাহাৰীয়া জিলা কোন?
A: অসমৰ দুখন পাহাৰীয়া জিলা হৈছে কাৰ্বি আংলং আৰু ডিমা হাছাও। দুয়োখন ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ উপত্যকাৰ দক্ষিণত অৱস্থিত, প্ৰায় সম্পূৰ্ণৰূপে পাহাৰীয়া, আৰু সংবিধানৰ ষষ্ঠ অনুসূচীৰ অধীনত স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদৰ জৰিয়তে বিশেষ প্ৰশাসনিক ব্যৱস্থা উপভোগ কৰে। কাৰ্বি আংলং ডাঙৰ, আনহাতে ডিমা হাছাও সৰু।
Q: অসমৰ পাহাৰীয়া জিলাসমূহৰ সাংবিধানিক ভিত্তি কি?
A: দুয়োখন জিলা সংবিধানৰ ষষ্ঠ অনুসূচীৰ অধীনত আছে, যি উত্তৰ-পূব ৰাজ্যবোৰৰ পাহাৰীয়া অঞ্চলত স্বায়ত্তশাসিত জিলা পৰিষদৰ ব্যৱস্থা কৰে। সেয়েহে কাৰ্বি আংলং আৰু ডিমা হাছাওত মাটি, বনাঞ্চল আৰু স্থানীয় প্ৰশাসনৰ ওপৰত ক্ষমতা থকা স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদ আছে, যি অসমৰ সাধাৰণ জিলাবোৰত নাই।
Q: হাফলং কিয় গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: হাফলং ডিমা হাছাও জিলাৰ সদৰ আৰু অসমৰ একমাত্ৰ পাহাৰীয়া ষ্টেচন। ই উচ্চতাত অৱস্থিত হোৱাৰ বাবে ইয়াৰ জলবায়ু সমতলতকৈ শীতল, আৰু ইয়াৰ দৃশ্য, হ্ৰদ আৰু জিলা ভ্ৰমণৰ কেন্দ্ৰ হিচাপে জনাজাত। ডিমা হাছাও স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদৰ সদৰো হাফলঙত অৱস্থিত।
Q: জাটিংগাৰ পৰিঘটনা কি?
A: ডিমা হাছাও জিলাৰ সৰু ঠাই জাটিংগা এটা বহুল চৰ্চিত পৰিঘটনাৰ বাবে জনাজাত, য'ত অন্ধকাৰ আৰু কুঁৱলীৰ ৰাতি চৰাইবোৰ পোহৰলৈ উৰি গৈ মাটিত পৰে বুলি কোৱা হয়। এই বিষয়ে বহুলভাৱে লিখা হৈছে আৰু ই গৱেষক তথা পৰ্যটকক আকৰ্ষণ কৰে; প্ৰতিযোগিতামূলক পৰীক্ষাত ডিমা হাছাওৰ সঘনাই সোধা তথ্যসমূহৰ এটা এইটো।
Q: ঝুম খেতি কি আৰু অসমত ক'ত কৰা হয়?
A: ঝুম বা পৰিবৰ্তনশীল খেতি এটা পৰম্পৰাগত পদ্ধতি, য'ত পাহাৰৰ ঢালৰ অৰণ্যৰ এটা টুকুৰা কাটি কেইবছৰমান খেতি কৰা হয় আৰু তাৰ পিছত মাটি পুনৰ সজীৱ হ'বলৈ পৰিত্যক্ত অৱস্থাত এৰি দিয়া হয়। ই মূলতঃ কাৰ্বি আংলং আৰু ডিমা হাছাওৰ দৰে পাহাৰীয়া অঞ্চলৰ জনগোষ্ঠীয়ে কৰে, লগতে সেই জিলাসমূহৰ সমতল অংশত স্থিৰ ধান খেতিও কৰে।

### Industries: Refineries & Tea Gardens — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/assam-geography-sec/industries-refineries-tea-gardens/
Summary: Practice industries: refineries & tea gardens questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Which is the oldest refinery of India located in Assam?
A: The Digboi refinery.
Q: When was the Digboi refinery established?
A: In 1901.
Q: When was the Guwahati refinery established?
A: In 1962.
Q: When was the Bongaigaon refinery established?
A: In 1979.
Q: Which refinery is located at Numaligarh?
A: The Numaligarh Refinery Limited (NRL).
Q: When was the Numaligarh refinery established?
A: In 1999.
Q: How many oil refineries are there in Assam?
A: Four refineries: Digboi, Guwahati, Bongaigaon and Numaligarh.
Q: Which is the largest refinery of Assam?
A: The Numaligarh refinery, with a capacity of about 3 million tonnes per year.
Q: Where is the Bongaigaon refinery located?
A: At Dhaligaon in Chirang district (Bongaigaon region).
Q: Which organization established the Guwahati refinery?
A: Indian Oil Corporation (IOC).
Q: What is the total installed refining capacity of Assam?
A: About 7 million tonnes per year.
Q: Which is the most important industry of Assam?
A: The tea industry.
Q: How many tea gardens are there in Assam?
A: Over 800 tea estates in the organized sector, with thousands of small tea growers.
Q: Which is the oldest tea garden of Assam?
A: The Chabua tea garden in Dibrugarh district.
Q: What is the biggest tea research institute of India located in Assam?
A: The Tocklai Tea Research Institute at Jorhat.
Q: Which is the largest tea auction centre of Assam?
A: The Guwahati Tea Auction Centre.
Q: What is the Tocklai Tea Research Institute known for?
A: It is the oldest tea research institute in the world, established in 1911.
Q: Which industry is the largest employer in Assam?
A: The tea industry.
Q: What is the main agro-based industry of the Barak valley?
A: Tea processing, jute mills and sugarcane-based industries.
Q: Which is the major petrochemical project of Assam?
A: The Assam Gas Cracker Project at Lepetkata.
Q: Which company runs the tea gardens of Assam in the public sector?
A: The Assam Tea Corporation Limited (ATCL).
Q: What is the Jorhat known for in the tea industry?
A: It is known as the 'tea capital' of Assam and has the Tocklai research centre.
Q: What is the main product of the Assam silk industry?
A: Muga, Eri and Pat silk textiles and garments.
Q: Which is the largest paper mill of Assam?
A: The Nagaon Paper Mill (Hindustan Paper Corporation) at Jagiroad.
Q: Which is the main cement producing centre of Assam?
A: Bokajan in Karbi Anglong and Umrangso in Dima Hasao.
Q: What is the main cottage industry of Assam?
A: Handloom and handicrafts, especially silk weaving and bamboo-cane crafts.
Q: Which is the most important industry and the largest employer of Assam?
A: The tea industry is both the most important industry and the largest employer of Assam. The state has more than 800 tea estates in the organised sector, besides thousands of small tea growers, and produces about half of India's tea. The oldest tea garden is the Chabua tea garden in Dibrugarh district, and the industry is supported by the Tocklai Tea Research Institute at Jorhat and the Guwahati Tea Auction Centre.
Q: How many oil refineries are there in Assam and when were they set up?
A: Assam has four oil refineries. The Digboi refinery is the oldest in India. The Guwahati refinery was established in 1962 by the Indian Oil Corporation, the Bongaigaon refinery in 1979 at Dhaligaon in Chirang district, and the Numaligarh refinery in 1999. The Numaligarh refinery is the largest, with a capacity of about 3 million tonnes a year, and the state's total refining capacity is about 7 million tonnes a year.
Q: Which is the largest paper mill and the main cement-producing centres of Assam?
A: The largest paper mill of Assam is the Nagaon Paper Mill of the Hindustan Paper Corporation at Jagiroad. The main cement-producing centres are Bokajan in Karbi Anglong and Umrangso in Dima Hasao, both of which use local limestone. The cement industry is therefore directly linked to the mineral deposits of the two hill districts rather than to the plains.
Q: What is the main petrochemical project of Assam and who runs it?
A: The main petrochemical project of Assam is the Assam Gas Cracker Project at Lepetkata near Dibrugarh, run by Brahmaputra Cracker and Polymer Limited (BCPL). It uses natural gas from the oil fields as its feedstock to produce polymers and plastics. Together with the oil fields at Duliajan and Naharkatia, it makes the Dibrugarh region the petrochemical hub of the state.
Q: What is the main cottage industry of Assam?
A: The main cottage industry of Assam is handloom and handicrafts, especially silk weaving and bamboo and cane crafts. Silk weaving of muga and eri, the traditional gamosa, and articles of bamboo, cane, bell metal and brass are found in almost every district and give employment to a large number of rural families, particularly women. Handicrafts and handloom are therefore both an economic activity and an important part of Assamese culture.
Q: অসমৰ আটাইতকৈ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ উদ্যোগ আৰু বৃহত্তম নিয়োগকৰ্তা কোনটো?
A: চাহ উদ্যোগ অসমৰ আটাইতকৈ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ উদ্যোগ আৰু বৃহত্তম নিয়োগকৰ্তা দুয়োটা। ৰাজ্যখনত সংগঠিত খণ্ডত ৮০০ৰো অধিক চাহ এষ্টেট আছে, হাজাৰ হাজাৰ ক্ষুদ্ৰ চাহ খেতিয়কৰ বাহিৰেও, আৰু ই ভাৰতৰ প্ৰায় আধা চাহ উৎপাদন কৰে। আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি চাহ বাগিচা ডিব্ৰুগড় জিলাৰ চাবুৱা চাহ বাগিচা, আৰু উদ্যোগটো যোৰহাটৰ টোকলাই চাহ গৱেষণা প্ৰতিষ্ঠান আৰু গুৱাহাটী চাহ নিলাম কেন্দ্ৰই সমৰ্থন কৰে।
Q: অসমত কিমানখন তেল শোধনাগাৰ আছে আৰু কেতিয়া স্থাপিত হৈছিল?
A: অসমত চাৰিখন তেল শোধনাগাৰ আছে। ডিগবৈ শোধনাগাৰ ভাৰতৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি। গুৱাহাটী শোধনাগাৰ ১৯৬২ চনত ইণ্ডিয়ান অইল কৰ্পৰেচনে, বঙাইগাঁও শোধনাগাৰ ১৯৭৯ চনত চিৰাং জিলাৰ ঢালিগাঁৱত, আৰু নুমলিগড় শোধনাগাৰ ১৯৯৯ চনত স্থাপন কৰিছিল। নুমলিগড় শোধনাগাৰ আটাইতকৈ বৃহৎ, বছৰি প্ৰায় ৩ মিলিয়ন টন ক্ষমতাৰ, আৰু ৰাজ্যখনৰ মুঠ শোধন ক্ষমতা বছৰি প্ৰায় ৭ মিলিয়ন টন।
Q: অসমৰ আটাইতকৈ বৃহৎ কাগজ কল আৰু মূল চিমেণ্ট উৎপাদন কেন্দ্ৰ কি?
A: অসমৰ আটাইতকৈ বৃহৎ কাগজ কল জাগীৰোডত হিন্দুস্তান পেপাৰ কৰ্পৰেচনৰ নগাঁও কাগজ কল। মূল চিমেণ্ট উৎপাদন কেন্দ্ৰ কাৰ্বি আংলঙৰ বোকাজান আৰু দিমা হাচাওৰ উমৰাংছো, দুয়োটা স্থানীয় চূণশিল ব্যৱহাৰ কৰে। গতিকে চিমেণ্ট উদ্যোগখন সমভূমিৰ সৈতে নহয়, দুখন পাহাৰীয়া জিলাৰ খনিজ মজুতৰ সৈতে প্ৰত্যক্ষভাৱে জড়িত।
Q: অসমৰ মুখ্য পেট্ৰোকেমিকেল প্ৰকল্প কোনটো আৰু কোনে পৰিচালনা কৰে?
A: অসমৰ মুখ্য পেট্ৰোকেমিকেল প্ৰকল্প ডিব্ৰুগড়ৰ ওচৰত লেপেতকাতাত থকা অসম গেছ ক্ৰেকাৰ প্ৰকল্প, যি ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ ক্ৰেকাৰ এণ্ড পলিমাৰ লিমিটেড (BCPL)-এ পৰিচালনা কৰে। ই তেলক্ষেত্ৰৰ পৰা অহা প্ৰাকৃতিক গেছক কেঁচামাল হিচাপে ব্যৱহাৰ কৰি পলিমাৰ আৰু প্লাষ্টিক উৎপাদন কৰে। দুলিয়াজান আৰু নাহৰকটীয়াৰ তেলক্ষেত্ৰৰ সৈতে ই ডিব্ৰুগড় অঞ্চলক ৰাজ্যখনৰ পেট্ৰোকেমিকেল কেন্দ্ৰ কৰি তোলে।
Q: অসমৰ মূল কুটীৰ শিল্প কি?
A: অসমৰ মূল কুটীৰ শিল্প তাঁত আৰু হস্তশিল্প, বিশেষকৈ ৰেচম বয়ন আৰু বাঁহ-বেতৰ সামগ্ৰী। মুগা আৰু এৰীৰ ৰেচম বয়ন, পৰম্পৰাগত গামোচা, আৰু বাঁহ, বেত, কাঁহ-পিতলৰ সামগ্ৰী প্ৰায় প্ৰতিখন জিলাত পোৱা যায় আৰু বহু গাঁৱলীয়া পৰিয়াল, বিশেষকৈ মহিলাক নিয়োগ দিয়ে। গতিকে হস্তশিল্প আৰু তাঁত একেসময়তে অৰ্থনৈতিক কাৰ্য আৰু অসমীয়া সংস্কৃতিৰ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ অংশ।

### Minerals: Oil, Gas, Coal & Limestone — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/assam-geography-sec/minerals-oil-gas-coal-limestone/
Summary: Practice minerals: oil, gas, coal & limestone questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Which is the oldest oil field of India located in Assam?
A: Digboi oil field.
Q: When was oil first struck at Digboi?
A: In 1867, and commercial production began in 1889.
Q: Which is the oldest oil refinery of India located in Assam?
A: The Digboi refinery.
Q: Which is the largest oil field of Assam?
A: The Moran and Naharkatia oil fields are among the largest, along with the Lakwa field.
Q: Which organization is responsible for oil exploration in Assam?
A: Oil India Limited (OIL) and Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC).
Q: Where is the headquarters of Oil India Limited?
A: Duliajan, in Dibrugarh district of Assam.
Q: Which is the oldest oil well of Asia located in Assam?
A: The Digboi well No.1, drilled in 1867.
Q: Which district is the largest producer of oil in Assam?
A: Dibrugarh district (including Duliajan, Moran and Naharkatia).
Q: Where is the biggest gas processing plant of Assam located?
A: At Duliajan.
Q: Which is the main coal producing district of Assam?
A: Tinsukia district (at Ledo, Margherita and Tipong).
Q: What type of coal is found in the Margherita coalfields of Assam?
A: High-grade bituminous coking coal.
Q: Which is the major coal field of Assam?
A: The Makum coalfield in Tinsukia district.
Q: Where is limestone found in Assam?
A: In the Karbi Anglong, Dima Hasao and parts of Goalpara and Kamrup districts.
Q: Which area of Assam has the largest limestone deposit?
A: The Kapili and Umrangso areas of Dima Hasao and Karbi Anglong.
Q: What is the main use of the limestone of Assam?
A: For the production of cement.
Q: Which cement factory uses the limestone of Assam?
A: The cement plants at Bokajan (Karbi Anglong) and Umrangso (Dima Hasao).
Q: Which is the largest gas field of Assam?
A: The Lakwa gas field in Sivasagar district.
Q: What is natural gas mainly used for in Assam?
A: For power generation, fertilizer production and as feedstock for petrochemical industries.
Q: Where is the Assam Gas Cracker Project located?
A: At Lepetkata, near Dibrugarh.
Q: Which company operates the Assam Gas Cracker Project?
A: Brahmaputra Cracker and Polymer Limited (BCPL).
Q: Which minerals other than coal are found in Assam?
A: Limestone, crude oil, natural gas, silica sand and minor minerals.
Q: Which is the main petrochemical hub of Assam?
A: Duliajan and the Dibrugarh region.
Q: Which is the main oil bearing area of the Barak valley?
A: The Badarpur and Patharia areas of Karimganj.
Q: What is the total crude oil production of Assam?
A: Assam produces about 3 million tonnes of crude oil annually.
Q: Which is the oldest refinery of Assam after Digboi?
A: The Guwahati refinery, established in 1962.
Q: Which district of Assam is famous for the 'coal city'?
A: Tinsukia, especially Margherita, known for its coal mines.
Q: Which is the oldest oil field and refinery of India, and where is it?
A: Both are at Digboi in Tinsukia district of Assam. Digboi is the oldest oil field of India, where oil was first struck in 1867 and commercial production began in 1889, and the Digboi refinery is the oldest refinery in the country. The Digboi well No. 1, drilled in 1867, is regarded as the oldest oil well of Asia, which makes Digboi one of the most important places in the industrial history of the region.
Q: How many oil refineries are there in Assam and which is the largest?
A: Assam has four oil refineries: Digboi, Guwahati (1962), Bongaigaon (1979) and Numaligarh (1999). The Numaligarh Refinery Limited is the largest, with a capacity of about 3 million tonnes per year. The total installed refining capacity of the state is about 7 million tonnes per year, and the refineries are operated by Indian Oil Corporation and Numaligarh Refinery Limited.
Q: Where is the headquarters of Oil India Limited and the largest gas field of Assam?
A: The headquarters of Oil India Limited is at Duliajan in Dibrugarh district, which is also the state's largest oil-producing district and the site of the biggest gas processing plant. The largest gas field of Assam, however, is the Lakwa gas field in Sivasagar district. Exploration and production in the state are carried out mainly by Oil India Limited and the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation.
Q: Which district produces coal in Assam and what type of coal is found there?
A: Tinsukia district is the main coal-producing district of Assam, with mines at Ledo, Margherita and Tipong and the major Makum coalfield. The coal of the Margherita area is high-grade bituminous coking coal, useful both for industry and for thermal power. Because of these mines, Tinsukia, and especially Margherita, is often called the coal city of Assam.
Q: Where is limestone found in Assam and what is it used for?
A: Limestone is found in the Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao hills and in parts of Goalpara and Kamrup districts, with the largest deposits in the Kapili and Umrangso areas. Its main use is the production of cement, and the two cement plants that depend on it are at Bokajan in Karbi Anglong and Umrangso in Dima Hasao. Limestone is thus the mineral that links the hills of Assam to the construction industry.
Q: ভাৰতৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি তেলক্ষেত্ৰ আৰু শোধনাগাৰ কোনটো, আৰু ক'ত?
A: দুয়োটা অসমৰ তিনিচুকীয়া জিলাৰ ডিগবৈত। ডিগবৈ ভাৰতৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি তেলক্ষেত্ৰ, য'ত ১৮৬৭ চনত প্ৰথমবাৰ তেল পোৱা গৈছিল আৰু ১৮৮৯ চনত বাণিজ্যিক উৎপাদন আৰম্ভ হৈছিল, আৰু ডিগবৈ শোধনাগাৰ দেশৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি শোধনাগাৰ। ১৮৬৭ চনত খনন কৰা ডিগবৈ কূপ নং ১ক এছিয়াৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি তেলকূপ বুলি গণ্য কৰা হয়, যিয়ে ডিগবৈক অঞ্চলটোৰ ঔদ্যোগিক ইতিহাসৰ এটা অতি গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ স্থান কৰি তোলে।
Q: অসমত কিমানখন তেল শোধনাগাৰ আছে আৰু আটাইতকৈ বৃহৎ কোনখন?
A: অসমত চাৰিখন তেল শোধনাগাৰ আছে: ডিগবৈ, গুৱাহাটী (১৯৬২), বঙাইগাঁও (১৯৭৯) আৰু নুমলিগড় (১৯৯৯)। নুমলিগড় ৰিফাইনাৰী লিমিটেড আটাইতকৈ বৃহৎ, বছৰি প্ৰায় ৩ মিলিয়ন টন ক্ষমতাৰ। ৰাজ্যখনৰ মুঠ স্থাপিত শোধন ক্ষমতা প্ৰায় ৭ মিলিয়ন টন, আৰু শোধনাগাৰবোৰ ইণ্ডিয়ান অইল কৰ্পৰেচন আৰু নুমলিগড় ৰিফাইনাৰী লিমিটেডে পৰিচালনা কৰে।
Q: অইল ইণ্ডিয়া লিমিটেডৰ মুখ্য কাৰ্যালয় আৰু অসমৰ বৃহত্তম গেছক্ষেত্ৰ ক'ত?
A: অইল ইণ্ডিয়া লিমিটেডৰ মুখ্য কাৰ্যালয় ডিব্ৰুগড় জিলাৰ দুলিয়াজানত, যি ৰাজ্যখনৰ সৰ্বাধিক তেল উৎপাদনকাৰী জিলা আৰু আটাইতকৈ বৃহৎ গেছ প্ৰচেছিং প্লাণ্টৰ ঠাইও। কিন্তু অসমৰ আটাইতকৈ বৃহৎ গেছক্ষেত্ৰ শিৱসাগৰ জিলাৰ লাকুৱা গেছক্ষেত্ৰ। ৰাজ্যখনত অনুসন্ধান আৰু উৎপাদন মূলত অইল ইণ্ডিয়া লিমিটেড আৰু তেল আৰু প্ৰাকৃতিক গেছ নিগমে কৰে।
Q: অসমৰ কোন জিলাত কয়লা উৎপাদন হয় আৰু তাত কি ধৰণৰ কয়লা পোৱা যায়?
A: তিনিচুকীয়া জিলা অসমৰ মূল কয়লা উৎপাদনকাৰী জিলা, লেডো, মাৰ্ঘেৰিটা আৰু টিপংৰ খনি আৰু মুখ্য মাকুম কয়লাক্ষেত্ৰৰ সৈতে। মাৰ্ঘেৰিটা অঞ্চলৰ কয়লা উচ্চ-শ্ৰেণীৰ বিটুমিনাছ ককিং কয়লা, যি উদ্যোগ আৰু তাপবিদ্যুৎ উৎপাদন দুয়োটাৰে বাবে উপযোগী। এই খনিবোৰৰ বাবে তিনিচুকীয়া, বিশেষকৈ মাৰ্ঘেৰিটাক, অসমৰ কয়লা চহৰ বুলি কোৱা হয়।
Q: অসমত চূণশিল ক'ত পোৱা যায় আৰু ইয়াৰ ব্যৱহাৰ কি?
A: চূণশিল কাৰ্বি আংলং আৰু দিমা হাচাও পাহাৰত আৰু গোৱালপাৰা তথা কামৰূপ জিলাৰ কিছু অংশত পোৱা যায়, আটাইতকৈ বৃহৎ মজুত কপিলী আৰু উমৰাংছো অঞ্চলত। ইয়াৰ মূল ব্যৱহাৰ চিমেণ্ট উৎপাদন, আৰু ইয়াৰ ওপৰত নিৰ্ভৰ কৰা দুখন চিমেণ্ট প্লাণ্ট কাৰ্বি আংলঙৰ বোকাজান আৰু দিমা হাচাওৰ উমৰাংছোত। এইদৰে চূণশিলে অসমৰ পাহাৰক নিৰ্মাণ উদ্যোগৰ সৈতে সংযোগ কৰে।

### National Parks & Wildlife Sanctuaries — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/assam-geography-sec/national-parks-wls-assam/
Summary: Practice national parks & wildlife sanctuaries questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: How many national parks are there in Assam?
A: Seven national parks.
Q: Which is the oldest national park of Assam?
A: Kaziranga National Park.
Q: In which year was Kaziranga National Park established?
A: In 1905 as a reserve forest, and declared a national park in 1974.
Q: Which animal is Kaziranga National Park famous for?
A: The one-horned rhinoceros.
Q: In which districts is Kaziranga National Park located?
A: Golaghat, Nagaon, Sonitpur and Karbi Anglong.
Q: In which year was Kaziranga declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
A: In 1985.
Q: Which national park of Assam is located on the bank of the Manas river?
A: Manas National Park.
Q: In which year was Manas National Park declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
A: In 1985.
Q: Which animal is the Manas National Park famous for?
A: The tiger, elephant, and the golden langur.
Q: In which district is the Manas National Park located?
A: Chirang and Baksa districts (on the foothills of the Bhutan Himalayas).
Q: Which is the smallest national park of Assam?
A: Rajiv Gandhi Orang National Park.
Q: In which district is the Orang National Park located?
A: Darrang and Sonitpur districts.
Q: Which animal is Orang National Park famous for?
A: The one-horned rhinoceros and tigers.
Q: Which national park of Assam is a tiger reserve?
A: Manas National Park and Nameri National Park.
Q: In which district is Nameri National Park located?
A: Sonitpur district.
Q: Which national park is known for the white-winged wood duck?
A: Nameri National Park (also Dibru-Saikhowa).
Q: Which national park of Assam is located on the island formed by the Brahmaputra and Lohit rivers?
A: Dibru-Saikhowa National Park.
Q: Which animal is Dibru-Saikhowa National Park famous for?
A: The white-winged wood duck and feral horses.
Q: Which is the largest wildlife sanctuary of Assam?
A: Bornadi Wildlife Sanctuary is small; the largest sanctuary area-wise is the Nambor-Doigrung sanctuary complex.
Q: How many wildlife sanctuaries are there in Assam?
A: About 18 wildlife sanctuaries.
Q: Which wildlife sanctuary is famous for the golden langur in Assam?
A: The Chakrashila Wildlife Sanctuary.
Q: Which is the only sanctuary of Assam dedicated to the hoolock gibbon?
A: The Gibbon Wildlife Sanctuary (Hoollongapar) in Jorhat.
Q: Which sanctuary of Assam is located in the Diphu reserve forest?
A: The Garampani Wildlife Sanctuary in Karbi Anglong.
Q: Which bird sanctuary of Assam is famous for migratory birds?
A: The Pobitora is a wildlife sanctuary; the Deepor Beel Bird Sanctuary near Guwahati is famous for migratory birds.
Q: Which wildlife sanctuary of Assam is known for the one-horned rhinoceros?
A: Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary in Marigaon district.
Q: Which is the smallest wildlife sanctuary of Assam?
A: Bornadi Wildlife Sanctuary is among the smallest, in Udalguri district.
Q: How many national parks and wildlife sanctuaries does Assam have?
A: Assam has seven national parks and about eighteen wildlife sanctuaries. The national parks are Kaziranga, Manas, Nameri, Rajiv Gandhi Orang, Dibru-Saikhowa, Dehing-Patkai and Raimona. The sanctuaries include Pobitora, Chakrashila, Gibbon (Hoollongapar), Garampani, Bornadi and Deepor Beel, among others, and they protect forests, grasslands and wetlands across the state.
Q: Which national parks of Assam are UNESCO World Heritage Sites?
A: Kaziranga National Park and Manas National Park are both UNESCO World Heritage Sites, and both were inscribed in 1985. Kaziranga is listed for its grasslands and its one-horned rhinoceros population, while Manas is listed for its rich mix of forest, grassland and riverine habitat and its tiger, elephant and golden langur.
Q: Which sanctuary is famous for the golden langur and which for the hoolock gibbon?
A: Chakrashila Wildlife Sanctuary is the best-known home of the golden langur in Assam. The hoolock gibbon, India's only ape, is specially protected in the Gibbon Wildlife Sanctuary, also called Hoollongapar, near Jorhat. Remembering these two pairs - Chakrashila with the golden langur and Hoollongapar with the hoolock gibbon - answers a large number of one-line questions.
Q: What makes Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary special?
A: Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary in Marigaon district is famous for the one-horned rhinoceros. Although it is a relatively small area, it supports one of the densest rhino populations in the world, which makes it a favourite example in questions about rhino conservation in Assam, alongside Kaziranga and Orang.
Q: Which national park in Assam is located on an island?
A: Dibru-Saikhowa National Park lies on an island formed by the Brahmaputra and the Lohit rivers in the eastern part of Assam. It is known for its wetland habitat, the white-winged wood duck and a population of feral horses, and it is one of the most distinctive protected areas in the state.
Q: অসমত কিমানখন ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান আৰু বন্যপ্ৰাণী অভয়াৰণ্য আছে?
A: অসমত সাতখন ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান আৰু প্ৰায় আঠখন বন্যপ্ৰাণী অভয়াৰণ্য আছে। ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যানসমূহ হৈছে কাজিৰঙা, মানস, নামেৰি, ৰাজীৱ গান্ধী ওৰাং, ডিব্ৰু-শৈখোৱা, দিহিং-পাটকাই আৰু ৰাইমনা। অভয়াৰণ্যসমূহৰ ভিতৰত পবিতৰা, চক্ৰশিলা, গিবন (হুলুঙাপাৰ), গৰমপনি, বৰনদী আৰু দীপৰ বিল আদি পৰে, আৰু ইহঁতে ৰাজ্যজুৰি অৰণ্য, তৃণভূমি তথা জলাশয় সুৰক্ষা দিয়ে।
Q: অসমৰ কোনবোৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান ইউনেস্কো বিশ্ব ঐতিহ্য ক্ষেত্ৰ?
A: কাজিৰঙা ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান আৰু মানস ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান দুয়োখন ইউনেস্কো বিশ্ব ঐতিহ্য ক্ষেত্ৰ, আৰু দুয়োখন ১৯৮৫ চনত তালিকাভুক্ত হৈছিল। কাজিৰঙা ইয়াৰ তৃণভূমি আৰু এশিঙীয়া গঁড়ৰ বাবে, আনহাতে মানস ইয়াৰ অৰণ্য, তৃণভূমি আৰু নদীপ্ৰবাহ বাসস্থানৰ সমৃদ্ধ মিশ্ৰণ আৰু বাঘ, হাতী তথা সোণালী বান্দৰৰ বাবে তালিকাভুক্ত।
Q: কোন অভয়াৰণ্য সোণালী বান্দৰৰ বাবে আৰু কোনখন হলৌ বান্দৰৰ বাবে বিখ্যাত?
A: চক্ৰশিলা বন্যপ্ৰাণী অভয়াৰণ্য অসমত সোণালী বান্দৰৰ আটাইতকৈ পৰিচিত আবাস। হলৌ বান্দৰ, ভাৰতৰ একমাত্ৰ এপ, যোৰহাটৰ ওচৰৰ গিবন বন্যপ্ৰাণী অভয়াৰণ্যত, যাক হুলুঙাপাৰ বুলিও কোৱা হয়, বিশেষভাৱে সুৰক্ষিত। এই দুটা যুগল মনত ৰাখিলে - চক্ৰশিলা সোণালী বান্দৰৰ সৈতে আৰু হুলুঙাপাৰ হলৌ বান্দৰৰ সৈতে - বহু এক-শাৰীৰ প্ৰশ্নৰ উত্তৰ পোৱা যায়।
Q: পবিতৰা বন্যপ্ৰাণী অভয়াৰণ্যক বিশেষ কি কৰি তোলে?
A: মৰিগাঁও জিলাৰ পবিতৰা বন্যপ্ৰাণী অভয়াৰণ্য এশিঙীয়া গঁড়ৰ বাবে বিখ্যাত। যদিও ই তুলনামূলকভাৱে সৰু এলেকা, ই পৃথিৱীৰ আটাইতকৈ ঘন গঁড় জনসংখ্যাৰ এটা ধাৰণ কৰে, যাৰ বাবে কাজিৰঙা আৰু ওৰাঙৰ লগতে অসমত গঁড় সংৰক্ষণৰ ওপৰত সোধা প্ৰশ্নত ই এটা প্ৰিয় উদাহৰণ।
Q: অসমৰ কোনখন ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান এখন দ্বীপত অৱস্থিত?
A: ডিব্ৰু-শৈখোৱা ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান অসমৰ পূব অংশত ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ আৰু লোহিত নদীৰ পৰা গঠিত এখন দ্বীপত অৱস্থিত। ইয়াৰ জলাশয় বাসস্থান, শ্বেত-পক্ষ ডুবৰি চৰাই আৰু বনৰীয়া ঘোঁৰাৰ এটা জনসংখ্যাৰ বাবে ই জনাজাত, আৰু ই ৰাজ্যখনৰ অন্যতম সুকীয়া সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল।

### National Parks & Sanctuaries of Assam — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/assam-geography-sec/national-parks/
Summary: 60 questions on the national parks and wildlife sanctuaries of Assam for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Covers Kaziranga, Manas, Nameri and Dibru-Saikhowa.
Q: How many national parks are there in Assam?
A: Assam has seven national parks: Kaziranga, Manas, Nameri, Orang, Dibru-Saikhowa, Raimona and Dihing Patkai.
Q: Which national park is famous for the one-horned rhinoceros?
A: Kaziranga National Park is famous for the great one-horned rhinoceros and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Q: Which sanctuaries are UNESCO World Heritage Sites?
A: Kaziranga and Manas national parks are the two UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Assam.

### Power: Hydro & Thermal Projects — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/assam-geography-sec/power-hydro-thermal-assam/
Summary: Practice power: hydro & thermal projects questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Which is the largest hydroelectric project of Assam?
A: The Karbi Langpi hydroelectric project.
Q: Which river is the Karbi Langpi hydroelectric project built on?
A: The Karbi Langpi river, a tributary of the Kopili river.
Q: Where is the Karbi Langpi hydroelectric project located?
A: In West Karbi Anglong district.
Q: Which is the largest thermal power plant of Assam?
A: The Bongaigaon Thermal Power Plant.
Q: Where is the Bongaigaon Thermal Power Plant located?
A: At Salakati in Kokrajhar district.
Q: Where is the Namrup Thermal Power Station located?
A: At Namrup in Dibrugarh district.
Q: What is the main fuel of the Namrup Thermal Power Station?
A: Natural gas.
Q: Which is the first hydroelectric power station of Assam?
A: The Umtru hydropower station on the Umtru river.
Q: When was the Umtru hydroelectric project established?
A: It was commissioned in 1960.
Q: Which agency generates electricity in Assam?
A: The Assam Power Generation Corporation Limited (APGCL).
Q: Which organization distributes electricity in Assam?
A: The Assam Power Distribution Company Limited (APDCL).
Q: What is the total installed power capacity of Assam?
A: About 600 to 700 MW from state sources, with additional shares from central projects.
Q: Which is the main source of thermal power in Assam?
A: Natural gas and coal.
Q: Where is the Chandrapur Thermal Power Project located?
A: At Chandrapur in Kamrup district.
Q: Which is the largest power plant in the North-East operated by NTPC?
A: The Bongaigaon Thermal Power Station (NTPC).
Q: What is the Karbi Langpi project's installed capacity?
A: About 100 MW.
Q: Which river has a potential for micro-hydel projects in Assam?
A: The Kopili, the Diyung and the Barak rivers have such potential.
Q: What is the main hindrance to power development in Assam?
A: Transmission losses, floods and shortage of funds.
Q: Which is the newest hydroelectric project proposed on the Dihing river?
A: The Lower Dihing and the Dehing-Patkai area projects are under study.
Q: What is the installed capacity of the Namrup Thermal Power Station?
A: About 226 MW (in stages).
Q: Which is the main consumer of electricity in Assam?
A: The domestic and the tea industry sectors.
Q: What is the role of the North Eastern Electric Power Corporation (NEEPCO) in Assam?
A: It develops major hydroelectric projects in the North-East, including in Assam.
Q: Which is the grid that connects the power system of Assam?
A: The North-East grid of the national power grid.
Q: What is the potential of solar energy in Assam?
A: There is growing potential, and the state is promoting solar parks.
Q: Which thermal plant uses the coal of the Makum coalfield?
A: The Margherita thermal plant and other coal-based units of the area.
Q: Which is the main hydropower share of Assam from central projects?
A: The share from the NEEPCO projects like Kopili and Khandong.
Q: Which is the largest hydroelectric project of Assam and where is it?
A: The largest hydroelectric project of Assam is the Karbi Langpi project in West Karbi Anglong district, with an installed capacity of about 100 megawatts. It is built on the Karbi Langpi river, which is a tributary of the Kopili river. The first hydroelectric station of the state, however, was the Umtru station on the Umtru river, which was commissioned in 1960.
Q: Which is the largest thermal power plant of Assam and what fuel does it use?
A: The largest thermal power plant of Assam is the Bongaigaon Thermal Power Plant, located at Salakati in Kokrajhar district. It is the largest power plant of the North-East operated by NTPC. The other important station, the Namrup Thermal Power Station in Dibrugarh district, runs mainly on natural gas and has a capacity of about 226 megawatts, while coal-based units such as Margherita use coal from the Makum coalfield.
Q: Which agencies generate and distribute electricity in Assam?
A: Electricity in Assam is generated by the Assam Power Generation Corporation Limited (APGCL) and distributed by the Assam Power Distribution Company Limited (APDCL). The state also receives a share of power from central projects, and the North Eastern Electric Power Corporation (NEEPCO) develops major hydroelectric projects in the region. The state's grid is connected to the North-East grid of the national power grid.
Q: What is the total installed power capacity of Assam from state sources?
A: The total installed capacity of Assam from state sources is about 600 to 700 megawatts, to which an additional share from central projects is added. The largest single hydro source within the state is the Karbi Langpi project at about 100 megawatts, and the largest thermal source is the Bongaigaon plant. Assam is connected to the North-East grid, which helps meet demand when local generation is short.
Q: What are the main problems and future prospects of the power sector in Assam?
A: The main problems are transmission losses, disruption caused by floods and a shortage of funds for new projects. On the future side, Assam is promoting renewable energy, especially solar power through solar parks and rooftop installations, and studying small hydro projects on the hill streams and the proposed schemes on the Dihing river. Renewables are important because they can reach remote hill areas where extending the main grid is difficult and costly.
Q: অসমৰ আটাইতকৈ বৃহৎ জলবিদ্যুৎ প্ৰকল্প কোনটো আৰু ক'ত?
A: অসমৰ আটাইতকৈ বৃহৎ জলবিদ্যুৎ প্ৰকল্প পশ্চিম কাৰ্বি আংলং জিলাৰ কাৰ্বি লাংপি প্ৰকল্প, প্ৰায় ১০০ মেগাৱাট স্থাপিত ক্ষমতাৰ। ই কাৰ্বি লাংপি নদীৰ ওপৰত নিৰ্মিত, যি কপিলী নদীৰ উপনদী। কিন্তু ৰাজ্যখনৰ প্ৰথম জলবিদ্যুৎ কেন্দ্ৰ আছিল উমত্ৰু নদীৰ ওপৰত উমত্ৰু কেন্দ্ৰ, যি ১৯৬০ চনত কাৰ্যক্ষম হৈছিল।
Q: অসমৰ আটাইতকৈ বৃহৎ তাপবিদ্যুৎ কেন্দ্ৰ কোনটো আৰু ই কি ইন্ধন ব্যৱহাৰ কৰে?
A: অসমৰ আটাইতকৈ বৃহৎ তাপবিদ্যুৎ কেন্দ্ৰ বঙাইগাঁও তাপবিদ্যুৎ কেন্দ্ৰ, কোকৰাঝাৰ জিলাৰ শালাকাটিত অৱস্থিত। ই NTPC-য়ে পৰিচালনা কৰা উত্তৰ-পূৰ্বাঞ্চলৰ বৃহত্তম বিদ্যুৎ কেন্দ্ৰ। আন গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ কেন্দ্ৰ নামৰূপ তাপবিদ্যুৎ কেন্দ্ৰ ডিব্ৰুগড় জিলাত, যি মূলত প্ৰাকৃতিক গেছেৰে চলে আৰু প্ৰায় ২২৬ মেগাৱাট ক্ষমতাৰ, আনহাতে মাৰ্ঘেৰিটাৰ দৰে কয়লা-ভিত্তিক এককে মাকুম কয়লাক্ষেত্ৰৰ কয়লা ব্যৱহাৰ কৰে।
Q: অসমত কোন সংস্থাই বিদ্যুৎ উৎপাদন আৰু বিতৰণ কৰে?
A: অসমত বিদ্যুৎ অসম পাৱাৰ জেনেৰেচন কৰ্পৰেচন লিমিটেড (APGCL)-এ উৎপাদন কৰে আৰু অসম পাৱাৰ ডিষ্ট্ৰিবিউচন কোম্পানী লিমিটেড (APDCL)-এ বিতৰণ কৰে। ৰাজ্যই কেন্দ্ৰীয় প্ৰকল্পৰ পৰাও বিদ্যুৎ অংশ লাভ কৰে, আৰু উত্তৰ-পূব বিদ্যুৎ নিগম (NEEPCO)-এ অঞ্চলটোত মুখ্য জলবিদ্যুৎ প্ৰকল্প বিকাশ কৰে। ৰাজ্যখনৰ গ্ৰিড ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় বিদ্যুৎ গ্ৰিডৰ উত্তৰ-পূব গ্ৰিডৰ সৈতে সংযুক্ত।
Q: ৰাজ্যিক উৎসৰ পৰা অসমৰ মুঠ স্থাপিত বিদ্যুৎ ক্ষমতা কিমান?
A: ৰাজ্যিক উৎসৰ পৰা অসমৰ মুঠ স্থাপিত ক্ষমতা প্ৰায় ৬০০ৰ পৰা ৭০০ মেগাৱাট, যাৰ সৈতে কেন্দ্ৰীয় প্ৰকল্পৰ অতিৰিক্ত অংশ যোগ হয়। ৰাজ্যখনৰ ভিতৰৰ আটাইতকৈ বৃহৎ একক জল উৎস কাৰ্বি লাংপি প্ৰকল্প প্ৰায় ১০০ মেগাৱাট, আৰু আটাইতকৈ বৃহৎ তাপ উৎস বঙাইগাঁও কেন্দ্ৰ। স্থানীয় উৎপাদন কম হ'লে উত্তৰ-পূব গ্ৰিডে চাহিদা পূৰণ কৰাত সহায় কৰে।
Q: অসমৰ বিদ্যুৎ খণ্ডৰ মূল সমস্যা আৰু ভৱিষ্যতৰ সম্ভাৱনা কি?
A: মূল সমস্যা হৈছে পৰিবহণ ক্ষতি, বানপানীৰ পৰা হোৱা বাধা আৰু নতুন প্ৰকল্পৰ বাবে ধনৰ অভাৱ। ভৱিষ্যতৰ ফালে অসমে নবীকৰণযোগ্য শক্তি, বিশেষকৈ সৌৰ উদ্যান আৰু ছাদত স্থাপনৰ জৰিয়তে সৌৰ শক্তি প্ৰচাৰ কৰিছে, আৰু পাহাৰৰ জুৰি তথা দিহিং নদীৰ প্ৰস্তাৱিত আঁচনিৰ সৰু জলবিদ্যুৎ প্ৰকল্প অধ্যয়ন কৰিছে। নবীকৰণযোগ্য শক্তি গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ কাৰণ ই দূৰৱৰ্তী পাহাৰীয়া অঞ্চলত উপনীত হ'ব পাৰে য'ত মূল গ্ৰিড বিস্তাৰ কঠিন আৰু ব্যয়বহুল।

### Ramsar Sites & Endemic Flora, Fauna — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/assam-geography-sec/ramsar-endemic-flora-fauna-assam/
Summary: Practice ramsar sites & endemic flora, fauna questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What is a Ramsar site?
A: A wetland site designated under the Ramsar Convention for its international importance.
Q: Where was the Ramsar Convention held?
A: In Ramsar, Iran, in 1971.
Q: When did the Ramsar Convention come into force?
A: In 1975.
Q: How many Ramsar sites are there in Assam?
A: One - the Deepor Beel.
Q: When was the Deepor Beel designated as a Ramsar site?
A: In 2002.
Q: Where is the Deepor Beel located?
A: Near Guwahati in the Kamrup district.
Q: Which endangered species is found in the Deepor Beel?
A: The greater adjutant stork and the Bengal florican.
Q: Which is the state animal of Assam?
A: The one-horned rhinoceros.
Q: Which is the state bird of Assam?
A: The white-winged wood duck (Deo Hah).
Q: Which is the state tree of Assam?
A: The Hollong tree (Dipterocarpus macrocarpus).
Q: Which is the state flower of Assam?
A: The Fox tail orchid (Kopou phool - Rhynchostylis retusa).
Q: Which animal is endemic to the Brahmaputra river?
A: The Ganges river dolphin (susuk).
Q: Which is the only ape found in India, found in Assam?
A: The hoolock gibbon.
Q: Which endemic primate is found only in the Manas region of Assam and Bhutan?
A: The golden langur.
Q: Which is the largest deer found in Assam?
A: The swamp deer (Barasingha).
Q: Which wild buffalo is found in Assam?
A: The wild water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis), found in the floodplains.
Q: Which endemic bird is found in the Namdapha and Dehing-Patkai region?
A: The white-winged wood duck and the Bengal florican.
Q: What is the national aquatic animal of India found in the Brahmaputra?
A: The Ganges river dolphin.
Q: Which type of vegetation is found in the Kaziranga floodplain?
A: Tall elephant grasses and tropical wet evergreen forests.
Q: Which endemic fish species is found in the rivers of Assam?
A: The pabho (Gudusia chapra), chital and the famous 'Na-mach' or the hilsa-like riverine species.
Q: Which plant is used traditionally in Assam for making 'gamosa'?
A: Cotton is used, while the endi, muga and pat silks come from silkworms feeding on specific plants.
Q: Which rare orchid is found in the forests of Assam?
A: The Vanda coerulea (blue orchid) and Rhynchostylis retusa (Kopou).
Q: Which is the most important endemic mammal of the Kaziranga National Park?
A: The Indian one-horned rhinoceros.
Q: Which termite-resistant timber tree is endemic to Assam's forests?
A: The Hollong tree, which is the tallest tree of Assam's rainforests.
Q: Which butterfly species endemic to Assam is protected?
A: The golden birdwing and the Kaiser-i-hind are found in the forests of Assam.
Q: What is the main threat to the endemic species of Assam?
A: Habitat loss due to floods, deforestation and encroachment.
Q: How many Ramsar sites does Assam have and which is it?
A: Assam has one Ramsar site, the Deepor Beel, which was designated in 2002. It is located near Guwahati in Kamrup district and is a large wetland important for migratory birds, for endangered species such as the greater adjutant stork and the Bengal florican, and for absorbing flood water in and around the city.
Q: What are the state symbols of Assam?
A: The state animal of Assam is the one-horned rhinoceros, the state bird is the white-winged wood duck, the state tree is the Hollong tree (Dipterocarpus macrocarpus) and the state flower is the foxtail orchid or Kopou phool (Rhynchostylis retusa). These four symbols are asked so often that they should be memorised together as a single set.
Q: Which rare animals of Assam are considered endemic?
A: The golden langur is a rare primate found only in the Manas region of Assam and neighbouring Bhutan. The hoolock gibbon, India's only ape, is another speciality of the region's forests. The Ganges river dolphin lives in the Brahmaputra system, and the wild water buffalo and swamp deer inhabit the floodplains, while the white-winged wood duck and Bengal florican are the best-known endangered birds.
Q: What kind of vegetation is found in the Kaziranga floodplain?
A: The Kaziranga floodplain is dominated by tall elephant grass mixed with patches of tropical wet evergreen forest. This combination of dense grass and scattered forest gives the one-horned rhinoceros the cover and food it needs, and it also supports a wide range of birds and other animals, which is one reason Kaziranga has become such an important conservation area.
Q: What are the main threats to the endemic species of Assam?
A: The main threats are habitat loss and fragmentation caused by floods, riverbank erosion, deforestation and encroachment, along with poaching and the illegal wildlife trade. Wetlands such as Deepor Beel also face siltation and pollution. Because these pressures work together, conservation in Assam tries to protect habitats, restore wetlands, keep wildlife corridors open and involve local communities.
Q: অসমত কিমানটা ৰামছাৰ স্থান আছে আৰু কোনটো?
A: অসমত এটা ৰামছাৰ স্থান আছে - দীপৰ বিল, যি ২০০২ চনত চিহ্নিত কৰা হৈছিল। ই কামৰূপ জিলাত গুৱাহাটীৰ ওচৰত অৱস্থিত আৰু পৰিভ্ৰমী চৰাই, গ্ৰেটাৰ এডজুটেণ্ট ষ্টৰ্ক তথা বেংগল ফ্ল'ৰিকানৰ দৰে বিপন্ন প্ৰজাতি, আৰু চহৰৰ চাৰিওফালে বানৰ পানী শোষণৰ বাবে এখন গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ ডাঙৰ জলাশয়।
Q: অসমৰ ৰাজ্যিক প্ৰতীকসমূহ কি?
A: অসমৰ ৰাজ্যিক প্ৰাণী এশিঙীয়া গঁড়, ৰাজ্যিক চৰাই শ্বেত-পক্ষ ডুবৰি, ৰাজ্যিক গছ হলং (Dipterocarpus macrocarpus) আৰু ৰাজ্যিক ফুল শিয়াল-নেজি অৰ্কিড বা কপৌ ফুল (Rhynchostylis retusa)। এই চাৰিটা প্ৰতীক ইমান সঘনাই সোধা হয় যে একে গোট হিচাপেই মনত ৰখা উচিত।
Q: অসমৰ কোনবোৰ বিৰল প্ৰাণী স্থানীয় বুলি গণ্য কৰা হয়?
A: সোণালী বান্দৰ এটা বিৰল প্ৰাইমেট যি মাত্ৰ অসমৰ মানস অঞ্চল আৰু ওচৰৰ ভূটানতহে পোৱা যায়। হলৌ বান্দৰ, ভাৰতৰ একমাত্ৰ এপ, অঞ্চলটোৰ অৰণ্যৰ আন এক বিশেষত্ব। গংগা ডলফিন ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ ব্যৱস্থাত বাস কৰে, আৰু বনৰীয়া ম'হ তথা পানী-হৰিণে বানপথাৰত বাস কৰে, আনহাতে শ্বেত-পক্ষ ডুবৰি আৰু বেংগল ফ্ল'ৰিকান আটাইতকৈ পৰিচিত বিপন্ন চৰাই।
Q: কাজিৰঙাৰ বানপথাৰত কেনেধৰণৰ উদ্ভিদ পোৱা যায়?
A: কাজিৰঙাৰ বানপথাৰত ওখ হাতীঘাঁহ গ্ৰীষ্মমণ্ডলীয় আৰ্দ্ৰ চিৰসেউজ অৰণ্যৰ টুকুৰাৰ সৈতে মিহলি হৈ প্ৰধান। ঘন ঘাঁহ আৰু সিঁচৰতি অৰণ্যৰ এই সংমিশ্ৰণে এশিঙীয়া গঁড়ক প্ৰয়োজনীয় আশ্ৰয় আৰু খাদ্য দিয়ে, আৰু ই বহল পৰিসৰৰ চৰাই তথা অন্য প্ৰাণীকো ধাৰণ কৰে, যি কাজিৰঙা ইমান গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ সংৰক্ষণ অঞ্চল হোৱাৰ এটা কাৰণ।
Q: অসমৰ স্থানীয় প্ৰজাতিৰ প্ৰতি প্ৰধান ভাবুকিবোৰ কি?
A: প্ৰধান ভাবুকিবোৰ হৈছে বানপানী, নদীপাৰ খহনীয়া, বন ধ্বংস আৰু অধিগ্ৰহণৰ ফলত হোৱা বাসস্থান বিনাশ আৰু খণ্ডন, লগতে চোৰাং চিকাৰ তথা অবৈধ বন্যপ্ৰাণী বাণিজ্য। দীপৰ বিলৰ দৰে জলাশয়ে পলস জমা আৰু প্ৰদূষণৰ সন্মুখীন হয়। এই চাপবোৰ একেলগে কাম কৰাৰ বাবে অসমত সংৰক্ষণে বাসস্থান সুৰক্ষা, জলাশয় পুনৰুদ্ধাৰ, কৰিডৰ মুকলি ৰখা আৰু স্থানীয় জনতাক জড়িত কৰাৰ চেষ্টা কৰে।

### Tiger Reserves & Biosphere Reserve — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/assam-geography-sec/tiger-biosphere-reserves-assam/
Summary: Practice tiger reserves & biosphere reserve questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: How many tiger reserves are there in Assam?
A: Four tiger reserves.
Q: Which are the tiger reserves of Assam?
A: Manas, Nameri, Orang and Dehing-Patkai tiger reserves.
Q: When was the Manas National Park declared a tiger reserve?
A: In 1973-74, under Project Tiger.
Q: When was Nameri declared a tiger reserve?
A: In 2000.
Q: When was the Orang tiger reserve declared?
A: In 2016.
Q: When was the Dehing-Patkai tiger reserve declared?
A: In 2020.
Q: In which district is the Dehing-Patkai tiger reserve located?
A: Tinsukia and Dibrugarh districts.
Q: What is the river associated with the Manas tiger reserve?
A: The Manas river.
Q: What is the river associated with Nameri tiger reserve?
A: The Jia-Bhoroli (Kameng) river.
Q: Which biosphere reserve is present in Assam?
A: The Manas biosphere reserve (shared with the Manas National Park).
Q: In which year was the Manas biosphere reserve declared?
A: In 1989.
Q: What is the core area of the Manas biosphere reserve?
A: The Manas National Park.
Q: Which species is the key protected animal of the Nameri tiger reserve?
A: The royal Bengal tiger.
Q: What is Project Tiger?
A: A national programme launched in 1973 for the conservation of tigers and their habitats.
Q: What is the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)?
A: A statutory body set up in 2005 to oversee the management of tiger reserves in India.
Q: Which is the largest tiger reserve of Assam by area?
A: Manas tiger reserve.
Q: Which animal of the Dehing-Patkai rainforest is a threatened species?
A: The tiger, elephant and hoolock gibbon.
Q: What type of forest is the Dehing-Patkai region?
A: A lowland tropical evergreen rainforest, part of the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot.
Q: Which river flows through the Nameri tiger reserve?
A: The Jia-Bhoroli river.
Q: What is the total area of the Manas biosphere reserve?
A: About 2,837 square kilometres.
Q: Which biosphere reserve is shared between Assam and Arunachal Pradesh?
A: The Manas biosphere reserve extends into both states.
Q: Which is the main tiger habitat of the Orang tiger reserve?
A: The grasslands and riverine forests of the Orang National Park.
Q: Which endangered primate is found in the Manas biosphere reserve?
A: The golden langur.
Q: What is the elephant corridor associated with the Dehing-Patkai region?
A: The region forms an important elephant habitat connecting forests of Assam and Arunachal Pradesh.
Q: Which tiger reserve of Assam was earlier a wildlife sanctuary?
A: Orang, which was earlier a wildlife sanctuary.
Q: Which is the highest priority tiger reserve under Project Tiger in Assam?
A: Manas tiger reserve.
Q: Which are the four tiger reserves of Assam?
A: The four tiger reserves of Assam are Manas, Nameri, Orang and Dehing-Patkai. Manas was the first, brought under Project Tiger in 1973-74, followed by Nameri in 2000, Orang in 2016 and Dehing-Patkai in 2020. Together they protect a wide range of habitats, from the Manas river valley and the Jia-Bhoroli riverbanks to the grasslands of Orang and the rainforest of Dehing-Patkai.
Q: What is Project Tiger and when did it begin?
A: Project Tiger is a national conservation programme launched in 1973 to protect tigers and their habitats in India. It introduced the model of a tiger reserve with a core area free of human activity and a buffer zone around it. The programme is now overseen by the National Tiger Conservation Authority, which was set up in 2005, and Manas was one of the earliest reserves to come under it in Assam.
Q: Which is the only biosphere reserve in Assam and what is its core area?
A: The Manas Biosphere Reserve is the biosphere reserve associated with Assam. It was declared in 1989 and its core area is the Manas National Park. It covers about 2,837 square kilometres and extends into Arunachal Pradesh, so it protects an entire landscape rather than a single protected area, and it is also important for species such as the golden langur.
Q: Why is Dehing-Patkai important for wildlife?
A: Dehing-Patkai, declared a tiger reserve in 2020, protects a lowland tropical evergreen rainforest in Tinsukia and Dibrugarh districts. This forest is part of the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot and is home to the tiger, the elephant and the hoolock gibbon. The reserve also forms an important elephant corridor linking the forests of Assam with those of Arunachal Pradesh, which makes it valuable well beyond its own boundaries.
Q: Which rivers are associated with the Manas and Nameri tiger reserves?
A: The Manas Tiger Reserve is associated with the Manas river, which gives the reserve and the national park their name. The Nameri Tiger Reserve is associated with the Jia-Bhoroli, also called the Kameng, river, which flows along its boundary. Remembering these two pairs helps answer several one-line questions about the reserves and their geography.
Q: অসমৰ চাৰিটা বাঘ সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল কোনবোৰ?
A: অসমৰ চাৰিটা বাঘ সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল হৈছে মানস, নামেৰি, ওৰাং আৰু দিহিং-পাটকাই। মানস প্ৰথমটো, ১৯৭৩-৭৪ চনত প্ৰজেক্ট টাইগাৰৰ অধীনলৈ অনা হৈছিল, তাৰ পিছত নামেৰি ২০০০, ওৰাং ২০১৬ আৰু দিহিং-পাটকাই ২০২০ চনত। ইহঁতে একেলগে মানস নদী উপত্যকা আৰু জিয়া-ভৰলীৰ পাৰৰ পৰা ওৰাঙৰ তৃণভূমি তথা দিহিং-পাটকাইৰ বৰ্ষাৰণ্যলৈকে বহল পৰিসৰৰ বাসস্থান সুৰক্ষা দিয়ে।
Q: প্ৰজেক্ট টাইগাৰ কি আৰু ই কেতিয়া আৰম্ভ হৈছিল?
A: প্ৰজেক্ট টাইগাৰ ১৯৭৩ চনত ভাৰতত বাঘ আৰু তেওঁলোকৰ বাসস্থান সুৰক্ষাৰ বাবে আৰম্ভ কৰা এক ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় সংৰক্ষণ কাৰ্যসূচী। ই বাঘ সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চলৰ আৰ্হি সৃষ্টি কৰিলে, যাৰ মূল অঞ্চল মানৱ কাৰ্যকলাপৰ পৰা মুক্ত তথা চাৰিওফালে বাফাৰ অঞ্চল থাকে। এতিয়া এই কাৰ্যসূচী ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় বাঘ সংৰক্ষণ কৰ্তৃপক্ষ (NTCA) য়ে চোৱাচিতা কৰে, যি ২০০৫ চনত গঠিত হৈছিল, আৰু অসমত মানস আটাইতকৈ আগতীয়াকৈ ইয়াৰ অধীনলৈ অহা সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চলসমূহৰ এটা।
Q: অসমৰ একমাত্ৰ জীৱমণ্ডল সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল কোন আৰু ইয়াৰ মূল অঞ্চল কি?
A: অসমৰ সৈতে জড়িত জীৱমণ্ডল সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল হৈছে মানস জীৱমণ্ডল সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল। ই ১৯৮৯ চনত ঘোষণা কৰা হৈছিল আৰু ইয়াৰ মূল অঞ্চল হৈছে মানস ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান। ই প্ৰায় ২,৮৩৭ বৰ্গ কিলোমিটাৰ আগুৰি অৰুণাচল প্ৰদেশলৈকে বিস্তৃত, গতিকে ই এখন সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল নহয়, এটা গোটেই ভূ-দৃশ্যপট সুৰক্ষা দিয়ে, আৰু সোণালী বান্দৰৰ দৰে প্ৰজাতিৰ বাবেও গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ।
Q: বন্যপ্ৰাণীৰ বাবে দিহিং-পাটকাই কিয় গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: দিহিং-পাটকাই, ২০২০ চনত বাঘ সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল হিচাপে ঘোষিত, তিনিচুকীয়া আৰু ডিব্ৰুগড় জিলাত নিম্নভূমিৰ গ্ৰীষ্মমণ্ডলীয় চিৰসেউজ বৰ্ষাৰণ্য সুৰক্ষা দিয়ে। এই অৰণ্য ইণ্ডো-বাৰ্মা জৈৱবৈচিত্ৰ্য হটস্পটৰ অংশ আৰু বাঘ, হাতী তথা হলৌ বান্দৰৰ ঘৰ। সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চলটোৱে অসমৰ অৰণ্যক অৰুণাচল প্ৰদেশৰ অৰণ্যৰ সৈতে সংযোগ কৰা এটা গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ হাতী কৰিডৰো গঠন কৰে, যাৰ বাবে ই নিজৰ সীমাৰ বাহিৰতো মূল্যৱান।
Q: মানস আৰু নামেৰি বাঘ সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চলৰ সৈতে কোনবোৰ নদী জড়িত?
A: মানস বাঘ সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল মানস নদীৰ সৈতে জড়িত, যি সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল আৰু ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যানক নাম দিছে। নামেৰি বাঘ সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল জিয়া-ভৰলী, যাক কামেং বুলিও কোৱা হয়, নদীৰ সৈতে জড়িত, যি ইয়াৰ সীমাৰ কাষে বৈ যায়। এই দুটা যুগল মনত ৰাখিলে সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চলসমূহ আৰু সিহঁতৰ ভূগোলৰ ওপৰত কেইবাটাও এক-শাৰীৰ প্ৰশ্নৰ উত্তৰ দিয়া সহজ হয়।

### Transport: NH, Railways & Waterways — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/assam-geography-sec/transport-nh-railways-waterways-assam/
Summary: Practice transport: nh, railways & waterways questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Which is the longest National Highway of Assam?
A: National Highway 31 (now renumbered as NH 27).
Q: Which National Highway passes through the Barak valley of Assam?
A: National Highway 44 (now NH 6), via Silchar.
Q: Which National Highway connects Guwahati with Shillong?
A: NH 6 (earlier NH 40).
Q: Which is the main bridge on the Brahmaputra connecting the north and south banks?
A: The Saraighat bridge at Guwahati.
Q: When was the Saraighat bridge opened for traffic?
A: In 1962.
Q: Which is the second bridge on the Brahmaputra in Guwahati?
A: The Narengi-Kuruwa bridge (new Saraighat).
Q: Which is the longest bridge over the Brahmaputra?
A: The Bogibeel bridge near Dibrugarh.
Q: When was the Bogibeel bridge inaugurated?
A: On 25 December 2018.
Q: Which is the longest river bridge of India located in Assam?
A: The Bhupen Hazarika Setu (Dhola-Sadiya bridge) over the Lohit river.
Q: When was the Dhola-Sadiya bridge inaugurated?
A: On 26 May 2017.
Q: Which river does the Dhola-Sadiya bridge cross?
A: The Lohit river.
Q: Which is the first railway station of Assam?
A: The Dibrugarh railway station, opened in 1882.
Q: Which is the biggest railway station of Assam?
A: The Guwahati railway station.
Q: Which railway zone covers Assam?
A: The North-East Frontier Railway (NFR).
Q: Where is the headquarters of the North-East Frontier Railway?
A: At Maligaon, Guwahati.
Q: Which river is the main waterway of Assam?
A: The Brahmaputra river.
Q: Which is the National Waterway 2 of India?
A: The Brahmaputra river from Sadiya to Dhubri.
Q: When was the Brahmaputra declared as National Waterway 2?
A: In 1988.
Q: Which is the National Waterway 6 of India?
A: The Barak river from Lakhipur to Bhanga.
Q: Which is the main inland water transport terminal of Assam?
A: The Pandu port in Guwahati.
Q: Which is the oldest airport of Assam?
A: The Mohanbari airport at Dibrugarh.
Q: Which is the biggest airport of Assam?
A: The Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport at Borjhar, Guwahati.
Q: What is the length of the National Waterway 2 in Assam?
A: About 891 kilometres.
Q: Which National Highway connects Dibrugarh with Tinsukia?
A: NH 27 (earlier NH 37) in that stretch.
Q: Which is the main waterway connecting the Barak valley with Bangladesh?
A: The Barak river, flowing into the Surma river of Bangladesh.
Q: What is the total length of the road network of Assam?
A: About 92,000 to 94,000 kilometres (including PWD and rural roads).
Q: Which is the longest National Highway of Assam and which highway serves the Barak valley?
A: The longest National Highway of Assam is NH 31, now renumbered as NH 27, which runs through the Brahmaputra valley. The Barak valley is served by NH 44, now NH 6, which passes through Silchar, and the same NH 6 also connects Guwahati with Shillong, where it was earlier known as NH 40. In the east, the Dibrugarh-Tinsukia stretch is part of NH 27, formerly NH 37.
Q: Which are the main bridges over the Brahmaputra and when were they opened?
A: The Saraighat bridge at Guwahati, opened for traffic in 1962, was the classic first bridge over the Brahmaputra in the state, and the Narengi-Kuruwa bridge is the second bridge at Guwahati. The longest bridge over the Brahmaputra is the Bogibeel bridge near Dibrugarh, inaugurated on 25 December 2018. The longest river bridge of India in Assam is the Bhupen Hazarika Setu or Dhola-Sadiya bridge over the Lohit, inaugurated on 26 May 2017.
Q: Which is the first railway station of Assam and which railway zone covers the state?
A: The first railway station of Assam was Dibrugarh, opened in 1882, while the biggest railway station today is Guwahati. The state lies in the North-East Frontier Railway (NFR) zone, whose headquarters is at Maligaon in Guwahati. The railway is especially important because it is less affected by floods than roads and carries most long-distance traffic between Assam and the rest of the country.
Q: Which are the national waterways of Assam and what is the main inland terminal?
A: The Brahmaputra is National Waterway 2, running from Sadiya to Dhubri over a length of about 891 kilometres, and it was declared a national waterway in 1988. The Barak river, from Lakhipur to Bhanga, is National Waterway 6 and connects the Barak valley with Bangladesh through the Surma and Meghna. The main inland water transport terminal of Assam is the Pandu port in Guwahati.
Q: Which are the oldest and the biggest airports of Assam?
A: The oldest airport of Assam is the Mohanbari airport at Dibrugarh, and the biggest is the Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport at Borjhar in Guwahati. The Guwahati airport is the main gateway to the North-East and handles the largest volume of air traffic in the state, while the smaller airports and airstrips serve remote districts.
Q: অসমৰ দীঘলতম ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় ঘাইপথ কোনটো আৰু বৰাক উপত্যকাক কোন ঘাইপথে সেৱা আগবঢ়ায়?
A: অসমৰ দীঘলতম ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় ঘাইপথ NH 31, এতিয়া NH 27 নামাংকিত, যি ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ উপত্যকাৰ মাজেৰে যায়। বৰাক উপত্যকাক NH 44, এতিয়া NH 6,ৱে সেৱা আগবঢ়ায়, যি শিলচৰৰ মাজেৰে যায়, আৰু একেই NH 6-এ গুৱাহাটীক শ্বিলঙৰ সৈতে সংযোগ কৰে, য'ত ই পূৰ্বতে NH 40 নামে জনাজাত আছিল। পূবত ডিব্ৰুগড়-তিনিচুকীয়া খণ্ড NH 27 ৰ অংশ, পূৰ্বতে NH 37।
Q: ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰৰ ওপৰত মূল দলংবোৰ কি আৰু কেতিয়া মুকলি হৈছিল?
A: গুৱাহাটীৰ শৰাইঘাট দলং ১৯৬২ চনত যান-বাহনৰ বাবে মুকলি হৈছিল আৰু ই ৰাজ্যখনৰ ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰৰ ওপৰত ধ্ৰুপদী প্ৰথম দলং, আৰু নাৰেঙ্গী-কুৰুৱা দলং গুৱাহাটীৰ দ্বিতীয় দলং। ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰৰ ওপৰত দীঘলতম দলং ডিব্ৰুগড়ৰ ওচৰত বগীবিল দলং, ২০১৮ চনৰ ২৫ ডিচেম্বৰত উদ্বোধন কৰা হৈছিল। অসমত ভাৰতৰ দীঘলতম নদী দলং হৈছে লোহিতৰ ওপৰত ভূপেন হাজৰিকা দলং বা ঢলা-ছদিয়া দলং, ২০১৭ চনৰ ২৬ মে'ত উদ্বোধন কৰা হৈছিল।
Q: অসমৰ প্ৰথম ৰেল ষ্টেচন কোনটো আৰু ৰাজ্যখন কোন ৰেল জ'নত?
A: অসমৰ প্ৰথম ৰেল ষ্টেচন ডিব্ৰুগড়, ১৮৮২ চনত মুকলি হোৱা, আনহাতে আজি বৃহত্তম ৰেল ষ্টেচন গুৱাহাটী। ৰাজ্যখন উত্তৰ-পূব সীমান্ত ৰেল (NFR) জ'নৰ অধীনত, যাৰ মুখ্য কাৰ্যালয় গুৱাহাটীৰ মালিগাঁৱত। ৰেল বিশেষভাৱে গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ কাৰণ ই পথতকৈ বানপানীৰ দ্বাৰা কম প্ৰভাৱিত হয় আৰু অসম আৰু দেশৰ বাকী অংশৰ মাজৰ বেছিভাগ দীৰ্ঘ-দূৰত্বৰ যাত্ৰা কঢ়িয়ায়।
Q: অসমৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় জলপথবোৰ কি আৰু মূল অন্তৰ্দেশীয় কেন্দ্ৰ কোনটো?
A: ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ হৈছে ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় জলপথ ২, ছদিয়াৰ পৰা ধুবুৰীলৈ প্ৰায় ৮৯১ কিলোমিটাৰ দৈৰ্ঘ্যৰ, আৰু ১৯৮৮ চনত ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় জলপথ হিচাপে ঘোষিত হৈছিল। বৰাক নদী, লক্ষীপুৰৰ পৰা ভাঙ্গালৈ, ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় জলপথ ৬ আৰু ই বৰাক উপত্যকাক শুৰ্মা আৰু মেঘনাৰ জৰিয়তে বাংলাদেশৰ সৈতে সংযোগ কৰে। অসমৰ মূল অন্তৰ্দেশীয় জল পৰিবহণ কেন্দ্ৰ গুৱাহাটীৰ পান্দু ঘাট।
Q: অসমৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি আৰু বৃহত্তম বিমানবন্দৰ কোনটো?
A: অসমৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি বিমানবন্দৰ ডিব্ৰুগড়ৰ মোহনবাৰী বিমানবন্দৰ, আৰু বৃহত্তম গুৱাহাটীৰ বৰঝাৰত অৱস্থিত লোকপ্ৰিয় গোপীনাথ বৰদলৈ আন্তঃৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় বিমানবন্দৰ। গুৱাহাটী বিমানবন্দৰ উত্তৰ-পূবৰ মূল প্ৰৱেশদ্বাৰ আৰু ৰাজ্যখনত বেছিভাগ বিমান যাত্ৰা ইয়াৰ পৰা চলোৱা হয়, আনহাতে সৰু বিমানবন্দৰ তথা এয়াৰষ্ট্ৰিপে দূৰৱৰ্তী জিলাবোৰক সেৱা আগবঢ়ায়।

### Major Tribes & Distribution — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/assam-geography-sec/tribes-distribution-assam/
Summary: Practice major tribes & distribution questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Which is the largest tribe of Assam?
A: The Bodo (Boro) tribe.
Q: Which is the second largest tribe of Assam?
A: The Mishing (Miri) tribe.
Q: Where are the Bodos mainly concentrated in Assam?
A: In the Bodoland Territorial Region (Kokrajhar, Chirang, Baksa and Udalguri).
Q: Which tribe celebrates the Bwisagu festival?
A: The Bodo tribe.
Q: Which tribe celebrates the Ali-Ai-Ligang festival?
A: The Mishing tribe.
Q: Which is the largest hill tribe of Assam?
A: The Karbi tribe.
Q: Where are the Karbis mainly found?
A: In Karbi Anglong district.
Q: Which festival is celebrated by the Karbi tribe?
A: The Rongker festival.
Q: Where is the Dimasa tribe mainly found?
A: In Dima Hasao district.
Q: Which tribe is known as the 'Sonowal Kachari'?
A: The Sonowal Kachari is a sub-group of the Kachari tribe in the Brahmaputra valley.
Q: Which tribe lives in the Nagaon and the adjoining areas of the south bank?
A: The Tiwa (Lalung) tribe.
Q: Which tribe inhabits the north-eastern parts of the Brahmaputra valley?
A: The Deuri tribe.
Q: Which is the main tribe of the North Cachar Hills?
A: The Dimasa and the Hmar tribes.
Q: Which tribe is found in the south-eastern parts of the Brahmaputra valley (Sivasagar area)?
A: The Muttock (Matak) community, associated with the Ahom rule.
Q: Which tribe celebrates the Bohag Bihu with unique traditions?
A: All the tribes of Assam celebrate Bihu, especially the Misings with Ali-Ai-Ligang.
Q: Which tribe of Assam is known for the 'Moirang' dance?
A: The Deuri tribe, who perform the Moirang dance.
Q: Which tribe practices the 'Husori' and 'Bihu' traditions?
A: The Bodos and the other plains tribes of Assam.
Q: Which tribe lives in the Baksa district?
A: The Bodo and the Rabha tribes.
Q: Where is the Rabha tribe mainly found?
A: In Goalpara, Kamrup and the adjoining areas of lower Assam.
Q: Which tribe of the Barak valley is important?
A: The Hmar, the Kuki and the Dimasa (in the adjoining hill areas).
Q: Which tribe celebrates the 'Me-dam-me-phi' ceremony?
A: The Tai-Ahom community.
Q: Which tribe is the native of the Dima Hasao hills?
A: The Dimasa tribe.
Q: Which tribe is famous for the 'Wan' dance?
A: The Bodo tribe performs the Bagurumba and other folk dances.
Q: What is the total Scheduled Tribe population share of the hills of Assam?
A: The hills (Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao) are predominantly tribal areas.
Q: Which tribe of Assam is known for the 'Chomangkan' festival?
A: The Karbi tribe.
Q: Which is the main festival of the Bodo community?
A: Bwisagu (Bihu) in April.
Q: Which is the largest tribe of Assam and which is the largest hill tribe?
A: The Bodo, also written Boro, are the largest tribe of Assam and the largest plains tribe, and they dominate the Bodoland Territorial Region covering Kokrajhar, Chirang, Baksa and Udalguri. The Karbi, earlier called Mikir, are the largest hill tribe of the state and live mainly in Karbi Anglong, which is a Sixth Schedule area. The Mishing, earlier called Miri, are the second largest tribe overall.
Q: Which festivals are associated with the Bodo, Mishing, Karbi and Dimasa tribes?
A: The Bodo celebrate Bwisagu in April, similar in spirit to Bihu, and their most famous dance is Bagurumba. The Mishing celebrate Ali-Ai-Ligang in February before the sowing season. The Karbi celebrate Rongker in spring for the well-being of the village and perform Chomangkan in honour of the dead. The Dimasa celebrate Bisu, a harvest festival similar to Bihu, and the Rabha celebrate Baikho.
Q: Which autonomous councils are linked with the tribes of Assam?
A: Three tribal areas of Assam - Karbi Anglong, Dima Hasao and the Bodoland Territorial Region - come under the Sixth Schedule. Other communities have their own councils, including the Rabha Hasong Autonomous Council, the Mising Autonomous Council, the Deori Autonomous Council, the Tiwa Autonomous Council, the Sonowal Kachari Autonomous Council, the Thengal Kachari Autonomous Council, the Moran Autonomous Council and the Matak Autonomous Council.
Q: In which districts are the major tribes of Assam concentrated?
A: The Bodo dominate the Bodoland Territorial Region, that is Kokrajhar, Chirang, Baksa and Udalguri, and are also found in Nagaon, Sonitpur and Darrang. The Karbi are concentrated in Karbi Anglong and the Dimasa in Dima Hasao. The Mishing live along the Brahmaputra in Dhemaji, Lakhimpur, Sivasagar and Majuli, while the Rabha are concentrated in Goalpara, Kamrup and Dhubri. The two hill districts are predominantly tribal.
Q: What is the share of the Scheduled Tribe population in Assam?
A: According to the 2011 Census, the Scheduled Tribe population of Assam is about 38.84 lakh, which is roughly 12.45 per cent of the state's total population. The Bodo form the largest share among the Scheduled Tribes, followed by the Mishing, the Karbi and the Rabha. The tribal population is concentrated in Karbi Anglong, Dima Hasao and the Bodoland Territorial Region.
Q: অসমৰ বৃহত্তম জনজাতি কোনটো আৰু বৃহত্তম পাহাৰীয়া জনজাতি কোনটো?
A: বড়ো (বোড়ো) অসমৰ বৃহত্তম জনজাতি আৰু বৃহত্তম সমতলীয় জনজাতি, আৰু তেওঁলোকে কোকৰাঝাৰ, চিৰাং, বাক্সা আৰু ওদালগুৰিৰ বড়োলেণ্ড টেৰিটোৰিয়েল ৰিজিয়নত আধিপত্য বিস্তাৰ কৰে। কাৰ্বি (পূৰ্বতে মিকিৰ) ৰাজ্যখনৰ বৃহত্তম পাহাৰীয়া জনজাতি আৰু মূলত কাৰ্বি আংলঙত বাস কৰে, যি ষষ্ঠ অনুসূচীৰ অঞ্চল। মিচিং (পূৰ্বতে মিৰি) সামগ্ৰিকভাৱে দ্বিতীয় বৃহত্তম জনজাতি।
Q: বড়ো, মিচিং, কাৰ্বি আৰু দিমাছা জনজাতিৰ সৈতে কোন উৎসৱবোৰ জড়িত?
A: বড়োসকলে এপ্ৰিল মাহত বিহুৰ দৰে বিৱচাগু পালন কৰে, আৰু তেওঁলোকৰ আটাইতকৈ বিখ্যাত নৃত্য বাগুৰুম্বা। মিচিংসকলে সিঁচনৰ আগতে ফেব্ৰুৱাৰী মাহত আলি-আই-লিগাং পালন কৰে। কাৰ্বিসকলে গাঁৱৰ মংগলৰ বাবে বসন্তকালত ৰংকেৰ পালন কৰে আৰু মৃতকৰ সন্মানত চমাংকান পৰিবেশন কৰে। দিমাছাসকলে বিহুৰ দৰে শস্য-উৎসৱ বিছু পালন কৰে, আৰু ৰাভাসকলে বাইখো পালন কৰে।
Q: অসমৰ জনজাতিসমূহৰ সৈতে কোনবোৰ স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদ জড়িত?
A: অসমৰ তিনি জনজাতীয় অঞ্চল - কাৰ্বি আংলং, ডিমা হাছাও আৰু বড়োলেণ্ড টেৰিটোৰিয়েল ৰিজিয়ন - ষষ্ঠ অনুসূচীৰ অধীনত। আন সম্প্ৰদায়সমূহৰ নিজা পৰিষদ আছে, যাৰ ভিতৰত ৰাভা হাচং স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদ, মিচিং স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদ, দেউৰী স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদ, টিৱা স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদ, সোণোৱাল কছাৰী স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদ, ঠেঙাল কছাৰী স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদ, মৰাণ স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদ আৰু মটক স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদ অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত।
Q: অসমৰ প্ৰধান জনজাতিসমূহ কোনবোৰ জিলাত কেন্দ্ৰীভূত?
A: বড়োসকলে বড়োলেণ্ড টেৰিটোৰিয়েল ৰিজিয়ন, অৰ্থাৎ কোকৰাঝাৰ, চিৰাং, বাক্সা আৰু ওদালগুৰিত আধিপত্য বিস্তাৰ কৰে, আৰু নগাঁও, শোণিতপুৰ তথা দৰংতো পোৱা যায়। কাৰ্বিসকল কাৰ্বি আংলঙত আৰু দিমাছাসকল ডিমা হাছাওত কেন্দ্ৰীভূত। মিচিংসকলে ধেমাজি, লখিমপুৰ, শিৱসাগৰ আৰু মাজুলীত ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰৰ কাষত বাস কৰে, আনহাতে ৰাভাসকল গোৱালপাৰা, কামৰূপ আৰু ধুবুৰীত কেন্দ্ৰীভূত। দুখন পাহাৰীয়া জিলা সংখ্যাগৰিষ্ঠভাৱে জনজাতীয়।
Q: অসমত অনুসূচিত জনজাতি জনসংখ্যাৰ অংশ কিমান?
A: ২০১১ চনৰ জনগণনা অনুসৰি অসমৰ অনুসূচিত জনজাতি জনসংখ্যা প্ৰায় ৩৮.৮৪ লাখ, যি ৰাজ্যখনৰ মুঠ জনসংখ্যাৰ প্ৰায় ১২.৪৫ শতাংশ। অনুসূচিত জনজাতিসমূহৰ ভিতৰত বড়োৱে বৃহত্তম অংশ গঠন কৰে, তাৰ পিছত মিচিং, কাৰ্বি আৰু ৰাভা। জনজাতীয় জনসংখ্যা কাৰ্বি আংলং, ডিমা হাছাও আৰু বড়োলেণ্ড টেৰিটোৰিয়েল ৰিজিয়নত কেন্দ্ৰীভূত।

### Major Tributaries, Majuli & Wetlands — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/assam-geography-sec/tributaries-majuli-wetlands/
Summary: Practice major tributaries, majuli & wetlands questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Which is the largest tributary of the Brahmaputra?
A: The Subansiri river.
Q: What is the length of the Subansiri river?
A: About 442 km, originating in Tibet.
Q: Which tributary of the Brahmaputra forms the boundary between Assam and Meghalaya?
A: The Manas river.
Q: Which tributary is known for the Manas National Park?
A: The Manas river, on whose bank the Manas National Park is located.
Q: Which is the famous tributary that flows through Nagaon district?
A: The Kolong river.
Q: Which tributary of the Brahmaputra is called the 'Dhansiri'?
A: The Dhansiri (south) river, flowing through Golaghat and Dima Hasao.
Q: Which tributary joins the Brahmaputra near Guwahati?
A: The Bharalu river (a small tributary flowing through the city).
Q: Which river is a tributary of the Barak river?
A: The Kushiyara, Jiri, Sonai and Chiri rivers are tributaries of the Barak.
Q: Which is the largest river island in the world?
A: Majuli, in the Brahmaputra river in Assam.
Q: In which district is Majuli located?
A: In Majuli district (carved out of Jorhat in 2016).
Q: Which rivers form the island of Majuli?
A: The Brahmaputra in the south and the Subansiri in the north.
Q: What is the main threat to Majuli island?
A: Erosion caused by the Brahmaputra river.
Q: Which river island is known as the cultural capital of Assamese Vaishnavism?
A: Majuli, with its numerous Satras (Vaishnava monasteries).
Q: Which is the largest wetland of Assam?
A: The Deepor Beel, near Guwahati.
Q: What is 'Beel' in Assamese?
A: A large wetland or lake, usually oxbow lakes formed by rivers.
Q: Which wetland of Assam is a Ramsar site?
A: Deepor Beel.
Q: Which beel is famous for the winter migration of birds?
A: Deepor Beel, near Guwahati.
Q: Which beel is associated with the famous Sualkuchi silk village?
A: The Chandubi beel, near the Assam-Meghalaya border.
Q: Which wetland is formed due to an earthquake?
A: The Chandubi beel, formed during the 1897 earthquake.
Q: Which tributary of the Brahmaputra flows through the Kaziranga National Park?
A: The Dhansiri (south) river flows along the boundary of the park.
Q: What is the total number of major tributaries of the Brahmaputra?
A: The Brahmaputra has about 100 tributaries, of which the major ones number over 40.
Q: Which river is the boundary between Assam and Nagaland?
A: The Dhansiri river.
Q: Which wetland of Assam is known for the rare Gangetic dolphin?
A: The Brahmaputra river system and beels like the Bordoibam-Bilmukh bird sanctuary area.
Q: Which is the longest tributary of the Barak river?
A: The Kushiyara river.
Q: What is the main cause of the formation of the wetlands (beels) of Assam?
A: The changing course of the rivers and erosion, creating oxbow lakes.
Q: Which is the second largest river island in the world?
A: Some sources consider Majuli the largest; the second largest in the Brahmaputra is the Umananda or other smaller islands.
Q: Which is the largest tributary of the Brahmaputra and how long is it?
A: The Subansiri is the largest tributary of the Brahmaputra. It originates in Tibet and is about 442 kilometres long. It joins the Brahmaputra on the north bank and is known for carrying a very large volume of water, which is why the Subansiri's flow is closely watched during the monsoon.
Q: What exactly is a beel?
A: A beel is a large wetland or lake in Assam, usually an oxbow lake formed when a river changed its course and left a loop of water behind. Beels are important for fish, for birds and for absorbing flood water, and many of them, such as Deepor Beel near Guwahati, are protected as wetlands of national and international importance.
Q: Why is Majuli under threat?
A: Majuli is threatened by erosion from the Brahmaputra. Because the river is braided and shifts its channels constantly, its banks at Majuli are eaten away year after year, and the island has lost a large part of its area over the past century. This has forced many families to move and has put the satras and the island's culture under pressure.
Q: How were the wetlands of Assam formed?
A: Most of Assam's beels were formed by the changing course of rivers. When a river abandons a loop or a channel, the water left behind becomes a wetland or oxbow lake. Others, like Chandubi Beel, are associated with geological events such as the earthquake of 1897. Over time siltation and human activity reduce their size, which is why wetland conservation is an important issue in the state.
Q: Which rivers should a candidate connect with Nagaon and Guwahati?
A: The Kolong is the river most closely associated with Nagaon district, and it has an important place in the district's history and culture. The Bharalu is the small river associated with Guwahati; it flows through the city and drains much of its rainwater into the Brahmaputra. Remembering these two pairs makes several one-line questions very easy.
Q: ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ উপনদী কোন আৰু ই কিমান দীঘল?
A: ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ উপনদী হৈছে সুবনশিৰি। ই তিব্বতৰ পৰা ওলাই প্ৰায় ৪৪২ কিলোমিটাৰ দীঘল। ই উত্তৰ পাৰৰ পৰা ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰত মিলি যায় আৰু অতি বিশাল পানী কঢ়িয়াই অনাৰ বাবে মৌচুমীকালত সুবনশিৰিৰ প্ৰবাহ ওচৰৰ পৰা লক্ষ্য কৰা হয়।
Q: বিল মানে ঠিক কি?
A: অসমত বিল মানে এটা ডাঙৰ জলাশয় বা হ্ৰদ, সাধাৰণতে নদীয়ে গতি সলনি কৰি এৰি থৈ যোৱা গড় ভঙা হ্ৰদ। বিল মাছ, চৰাই আৰু বানৰ পানী শোষণৰ বাবে গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ, আৰু গুৱাহাটীৰ ওচৰৰ দীপৰ বিলৰ দৰে বহু বিল ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় তথা আন্তৰ্জাতিক গুৰুত্বৰ জলাশয় হিচাপে সুৰক্ষিত।
Q: মাজুলী কিয় বিপদত আছে?
A: মাজুলী ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰৰ খহনীয়াৰ বাবে বিপদত আছে। নদীখন শাখা-প্ৰশাখাযুক্ত আৰু সদায় নিজৰ খাল সলনি কৰে, গতিকে মাজুলীৰ পাৰ বছৰি বাৰ বছৰ ক্ষয় হয় আৰু এশ বছৰত দ্বীপটোৱে নিজৰ এক ডাঙৰ অংশ হেৰুৱাইছে। ইয়াৰ ফলত বহু পৰিয়াল উঠিবলগীয়া হৈছে আৰু সত্ৰ তথা দ্বীপটোৰ সংস্কৃতি চাপত পৰিছে।
Q: অসমৰ জলাশয়বোৰ কেনেকৈ সৃষ্টি হৈছিল?
A: অসমৰ অধিকাংশ বিল নদীৰ গতি পৰিৱৰ্তনেৰে সৃষ্টি হৈছিল। নদীয়ে এটা গড় বা খাল এৰি থৈ গ'লে ৰৈ যোৱা পানী জলাশয় বা গড় ভঙা হ্ৰদ হৈ পৰে। আন কিছুমান, যেনে চান্দুবী বিল, ১৮৯৭ চনৰ ভূমিকম্পৰ দৰে ভূতাত্ত্বিক ঘটনাৰ সৈতে জড়িত। সময় যোৱাৰ লগে লগে পলস আৰু মানৱ কাৰ্যই ইহঁতৰ আকাৰ কমাই আনে, সেয়েহে ৰাজ্যখনত জলাশয় সংৰক্ষণ এক গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ বিষয়।
Q: নগাঁও আৰু গুৱাহাটীৰ সৈতে কোনবোৰ নদী জড়িত বুলি প্ৰাৰ্থীয়ে মনত ৰখা উচিত?
A: নগাঁও জিলাৰ সৈতে আটাইতকৈ নিবিড়ভাৱে জড়িত নদী হৈছে কলং, আৰু জিলাখনৰ ইতিহাস তথা সংস্কৃতিত ইয়াৰ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ স্থান আছে। গুৱাহাটীৰ সৈতে জড়িত সৰু নদী হৈছে ভৰলু; ই চহৰখনৰ মাজেৰে বৈ চহৰৰ বহু বৰষুণৰ পানী ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰলৈ নিয়ে। এই দুটা যুগল মনত ৰাখিলে কেইবাটাও এক-শাৰীৰ প্ৰশ্ন অতি সহজ হৈ পৰে।

### Dwarf Planets, Asteroids, Comets & Meteors — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/astronomical-geography-sec/dwarf-planets-asteroids-comets-meteors/
Summary: Practice dwarf planets, asteroids, comets & meteors questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: What is a dwarf planet?
A: A dwarf planet is a celestial body that orbits the Sun, has enough mass for a round shape, but has not cleared its orbit of other objects.
Q: Who defined the term 'dwarf planet'?
A: The International Astronomical Union (IAU) defined the term 'dwarf planet' in 2006.
Q: Name the five recognized dwarf planets.
A: The five recognized dwarf planets are Ceres, Pluto, Haumea, Makemake, and Eris.
Q: Where is Pluto located?
A: Pluto is located in the Kuiper Belt, a region beyond Neptune's orbit.
Q: When was Pluto reclassified from a planet to a dwarf planet?
A: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006 by the IAU.
Q: Who discovered Pluto?
A: Pluto was discovered by Clyde Tombaugh in 1930.
Q: What is the Kuiper Belt?
A: The Kuiper Belt is a disc-shaped region beyond Neptune's orbit containing icy bodies, dwarf planets, and short-period comets.
Q: What is an asteroid?
A: An asteroid is a small rocky body that orbits the Sun, mainly found in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.
Q: What is the largest asteroid?
A: Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt, so large that it is classified as a dwarf planet.
Q: What is a comet?
A: A comet is an icy body that, when near the Sun, develops a glowing coma and tail from evaporating ice and dust.
Q: What are the parts of a comet?
A: A comet consists of a nucleus, coma, hydrogen envelope, and two tails - the dust tail and ion tail.
Q: What is Halley's Comet's orbital period?
A: Halley's Comet has an orbital period of about 76 years.
Q: Where do long-period comets come from?
A: Long-period comets are believed to come from the Oort Cloud, a distant spherical shell of icy bodies surrounding the solar system.
Q: What is the difference between a meteoroid, meteor, and meteorite?
A: A meteoroid is a small rock in space; a meteor is the streak of light when it burns in the atmosphere; a meteorite is the piece that survives and lands on Earth.
Q: What is a meteor shower?
A: A meteor shower occurs when Earth passes through the debris trail left by a comet, causing many meteors to appear.
Q: What is the Perseid meteor shower associated with?
A: The Perseid meteor shower is associated with comet Swift-Tuttle.
Q: What is the Oort Cloud?
A: The Oort Cloud is a hypothesized spherical cloud of icy objects surrounding the solar system, the source of long-period comets.
Q: What is Eris?
A: Eris is a dwarf planet in the scattered disc beyond the Kuiper Belt, and is the most massive known dwarf planet.
Q: What is Ceres?
A: Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt and the only dwarf planet located in the inner solar system.
Q: What is a near-Earth object (NEO)?
A: A near-Earth object is an asteroid or comet whose orbit brings it close to Earth's orbit.
Q: What is a fireball?
A: A fireball is an unusually bright meteor, brighter than Venus, that explodes or streaks across the sky.
Q: What is the Chicxulub crater linked to?
A: The Chicxulub crater in Mexico is linked to the asteroid impact that is believed to have caused the extinction of the dinosaurs about 66 million years ago.
Q: What are the names of the inner and outer asteroid zones?
A: The main asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter, and the Trojan asteroids share Jupiter's orbit; the Kuiper Belt lies beyond Neptune.
Q: What is the Tunguska event?
A: The Tunguska event was a massive explosion in Siberia in 1908, believed to be caused by an asteroid or comet airburst.
Q: What is the difference between an asteroid and a comet?
A: An asteroid is mostly rocky and found in the inner solar system, while a comet is mostly icy and develops a tail when near the Sun.
Q: What is a dwarf planet and how many are recognised?
A: A dwarf planet orbits the Sun, has enough mass for its own gravity to make it nearly round, has not cleared the neighbourhood around its orbit, and is not a moon. The International Astronomical Union recognises five dwarf planets: Ceres, Pluto, Haumea, Makemake and Eris. The 2006 definition reclassified Pluto from a planet to a dwarf planet.
Q: Where is the asteroid belt and which is its largest object?
A: The main asteroid belt lies between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter. Ceres, which is also classified as a dwarf planet, is the largest object in the belt and contains about one-third of its total mass. Other large asteroids are Vesta, Pallas and Juno.
Q: What are the parts of a comet and where does its tail point?
A: A comet has a nucleus, a coma and a tail. The nucleus is the solid icy core, the coma is the glowing cloud of gas and dust around it, and the tail is the long trail of gas and dust. The tail always points away from the Sun because of the solar wind and radiation pressure.
Q: What is the difference between a meteoroid, a meteor and a meteorite?
A: A meteoroid is a small rocky or metallic body travelling in space. When it enters the atmosphere and burns up, the glowing streak is called a meteor or shooting star. If a piece survives and reaches the Earth's surface, it is called a meteorite. Most meteors burn up in the mesosphere.
Q: What is Halley's Comet and where do short and long period comets come from?
A: Halley's Comet is the most famous short-period comet, returning about every 76 years; it was last seen in 1986 and is expected around 2061. Short-period comets come from the Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune, while long-period comets come from the distant Oort Cloud.
Q: বামন গ্ৰহ কি আৰু কেইটা স্বীকৃত?
