Q: Which pass connects Uttarakhand with Tibet?
A: The Lipulekh pass.
Q: Which is the famous pass of the Manas-Bhutan route?
A: The Bomdila pass in Arunachal Pradesh.
Q: Which pass connects Arunachal Pradesh with Tibet?
A: The Dihang (Bomdila) and the Tawang pass routes.
Q: Which is the highest peak of the Western Himalayas?
A: Nanga Parbat, at 8,126 metres.
Q: Which is the highest peak of the Pir Panjal range?
A: Indrasan peak.
Q: Which peak of the Assam Himalayas is the highest?
A: The Gorichen peak, at about 6,488 metres, in Arunachal Pradesh.
Q: Which is the famous peak of the Naga hills?
A: Saramati, at 3,826 metres, on the India-Myanmar border.
Q: Which is the highest peak of the Khasi hills?
A: Lum Shyllong, at 1,968 metres.
Q: Which is the highest peak of the Shillong plateau?
A: Lum Shyllong.
Q: Which is the highest peak of the Patkai range?
A: The peaks of the Patkai Bum, including the Saramati.
Q: Which pass is used by the pilgrims going to Kailash Mansarovar?
A: The Lipulekh pass.
Q: Which is the highest peak of the Ladakh range?
A: Rakaposhi and the peaks around the Siachen glacier.
Q: Which is the famous peak of the Garhwal Himalayas?
A: Nanda Devi and Kamet.
Q: Which is the highest peak of the Kumaon Himalayas?
A: Nanda Devi.
Q: Which pass connects the Nainital area with the hills?
A: The Niti and the Juhar passes.
Q: Which is the famous peak of the Himalayas of Nepal?
A: Mount Everest, Annapurna and Dhaulagiri.
Q: Which is the highest peak of the Peninsular India?
A: Anamudi.
Q: Which pass connects Mizoram with Myanmar?
A: The Tiddim (Rih) pass route.
Q: Which is the highest peak in the world, in India and in the Eastern Himalayas?
A: The highest peak in the world is Mount Everest at about 8,848 metres in the Nepal Himalayas. The highest peak of India is K2, also called Godwin Austen, at 8,611 metres, which is also the highest peak of the Karakoram range. The highest peak of the Eastern Himalayas in India is Kangchenjunga at 8,586 metres, and Nanga Parbat at 8,126 metres is the highest peak of the Western Himalayas.
Q: Which peak belongs to which range among the major Indian mountains?
A: K2 belongs to the Karakoram, Kamet to the Zanskar range, Nanda Devi to the Garhwal and Kumaon Himalayas, and Gorichen to the Assam Himalayas of Arunachal Pradesh. In the peninsula, Dhupgarh is the highest peak of the Satpura, Guru Shikhar of the Aravali, Sadbhavana Shikhar of the Vindhya, Doddabetta of the Nilgiri, Mahendragiri of the Eastern Ghats and Anamudi of the Western Ghats.
Q: Which passes connect Kashmir, Ladakh, Jammu and Srinagar?
A: The Zoji La pass connects Kashmir with Ladakh and is used on the Srinagar-Leh route, while the Banihal pass connects Jammu with Srinagar. The Khardung La in Ladakh is one of the highest motorable passes in the world, and the Karakoram pass once linked Ladakh with Tibet on the old trade route. These passes keep the far northern regions connected through the year.
Q: Which passes connect India with Tibet and which one is used for Kailash Mansarovar?
A: The Nathu La connects Sikkim with Tibet, the Shipki La connects Himachal Pradesh with Tibet along the Sutlej, and the Lipulekh connects Uttarakhand with Tibet. The Lipulekh pass is the route used by pilgrims going to Kailash Mansarovar, and the Karakoram pass also linked Ladakh with Tibet in the past. Each of these passes has great strategic importance.
Q: Which passes are important in the north-east and along the Myanmar border?
A: In the north-east, the Bomdila and the Dihang routes serve the Manas-Bhutan area of Arunachal Pradesh, and the Tawang and Sela routes lead towards the frontier with Tibet. The Tiddim or Rih pass route connects Mizoram with Myanmar, and the Saramati peak rises on the India-Myanmar border. These passes are vital for defence as well as for trade and the movement of communities.
Q: বিশ্ব, ভাৰত আৰু পূব হিমালয়ৰ সৰ্বোচ্চ শৃংগ কোনটো?
A: বিশ্বৰ সৰ্বোচ্চ শৃংগ মাউণ্ট এভাৰেষ্ট প্ৰায় ৮,৮৪৮ মিটাৰ, নেপাল হিমালয়ত। ভাৰতৰ সৰ্বোচ্চ শৃংগ K2, যাক গডউইন অষ্টিন বুলিও কোৱা হয়, ৮,৬১১ মিটাৰ, যি কৰাকোৰাম শ্ৰেণীৰো সৰ্বোচ্চ শৃংগ। ভাৰতত পূব হিমালয়ৰ সৰ্বোচ্চ শৃংগ কাঞ্চনজঙ্ঘা ৮,৫৮৬ মিটাৰ, আৰু নাংগা পৰ্বত ৮,১২৬ মিটাৰ পশ্চিম হিমালয়ৰ সৰ্বোচ্চ শৃংগ।
Q: ভাৰতৰ প্ৰধান পৰ্বতসমূহৰ কোনটো শৃংগ কোন শ্ৰেণীৰ?
A: K2 কৰাকোৰামৰ, কামেট জাংস্কাৰ শ্ৰেণীৰ, নন্দা দেৱী গঢ়ৱাল আৰু কুমায়ূন হিমালয়ৰ, আৰু গৰীচেন অৰুণাচল প্ৰদেশৰ অসম হিমালয়ৰ। উপদ্বীপত ধূপগড় সৎপুৰাৰ, গুৰু শিখৰ অৰাৱলীৰ, সদভাৱনা শিখৰ বিন্ধ্যৰ, দোদাবেট্টা নীলগিৰিৰ, মহেন্দ্ৰগিৰি পূব ঘাটৰ আৰু আনামুডি পশ্চিম ঘাটৰ সৰ্বোচ্চ শৃংগ।
Q: কাশ্মীৰ, লাডাখ, জম্মু আৰু শ্ৰীনগৰক কোনবোৰ গিৰিপথে সংযোগ কৰে?
A: জোজি লা গিৰিপথে কাশ্মীৰক লাডাখৰ সৈতে সংযোগ কৰে আৰু শ্ৰীনগৰ-লেহ পথত ব্যৱহৃত হয়, আনহাতে বানিহাল গিৰিপথে জম্মুক শ্ৰীনগৰৰ সৈতে। লাডাখৰ খাৰডুং লা বিশ্বৰ উচ্চতম বাহনযোগ্য গিৰিপথসমূহৰ এটা, আৰু কৰাকোৰাম গিৰিপথে পুৰণি বাণিজ্য পথেৰে লাডাখক তিব্বতৰ সৈতে সংযোগ কৰিছিল।
Q: কোনবোৰ গিৰিপথে ভাৰতক তিব্বতৰ সৈতে সংযোগ কৰে আৰু কৈলাস মনসৰোবৰৰ বাবে কোনটো ব্যৱহৃত হয়?
A: নাথু লাই চিকিমক তিব্বতৰ সৈতে, শিপকি লাই সতলুজৰ কাষেৰে হিমাচল প্ৰদেশক তিব্বতৰ সৈতে, আৰু লিপুলেখে উত্তৰাখণ্ডক তিব্বতৰ সৈতে সংযোগ কৰে। লিপুলেখ গিৰিপথ কৈলাস মনসৰোবৰলৈ যোৱা তীৰ্থযাত্ৰীসকলে ব্যৱহাৰ কৰে, আৰু কৰাকোৰাম গিৰিপথেও অতীতত লাডাখক তিব্বতৰ সৈতে সংযোগ কৰিছিল।
Q: উত্তৰ-পূব আৰু ম্যানমাৰ সীমান্তত কোনবোৰ গিৰিপথ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: উত্তৰ-পূবত বমডিলা আৰু দিহাং পথে অৰুণাচল প্ৰদেশৰ মনস-ভুটান অঞ্চলৰ সেৱা কৰে, আৰু তৱাং তথা সেলা পথ তিব্বতৰ সীমান্তৰফালে লৈ যায়। টিডিম বা ৰিহ গিৰিপথে মিজোৰামক ম্যানমাৰৰ সৈতে সংযোগ কৰে, আৰু ভাৰত-ম্যানমাৰ সীমাত সৰমতী শৃংগ উত্থিত। এই গিৰিপথবোৰ প্ৰতিৰক্ষাৰ লগতে বাণিজ্য আৰু সম্প্ৰদায়ৰ চলাচলৰ বাবে অতি প্ৰয়োজনীয়।

### National Parks, WLS & Biosphere Reserves — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/indian-geography-sec/national-parks-wls-biosphere-india/
Summary: Practice national parks, wls & biosphere reserves questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: Which is the largest national park of India?
A: Hemis National Park in Ladakh.
Q: Which is the oldest national park of India?
A: Jim Corbett National Park in Uttarakhand.
Q: When was the Jim Corbett National Park established?
A: In 1936, as the Hailey National Park.
Q: Which national park of India is famous for the one-horned rhinoceros?
A: Kaziranga National Park in Assam.
Q: When was Kaziranga declared a National Park?
A: In 1974.
Q: Which river flows through the Kaziranga National Park?
A: The Brahmaputra river.
Q: Which national park of India is famous for the tigers?
A: Ranthambore National Park in Rajasthan.
Q: Which national park of India is known for the 'Gir lions'?
A: Gir National Park in Gujarat.
Q: Which is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic lion in India?
A: The Gir Forest in Gujarat.
Q: Which national park is famous for the swamp deer in Assam?
A: The Dibru-Saikhowa National Park.
Q: Which is the largest wildlife sanctuary of Assam?
A: The Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary is among the largest reserves for rhinos.
Q: Which wildlife sanctuary of Assam is famous for the golden langur?
A: The Chakrashila Wildlife Sanctuary.
Q: Which national park is the natural habitat of the golden langur?
A: The Manas National Park.
Q: Which is the first biosphere reserve of India?
A: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.
Q: When was the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve established?
A: In 1986.
Q: How many biosphere reserves are there in India?
A: 18 biosphere reserves.
Q: Which biosphere reserve of India is in the North-East?
A: The Manas, the Nokrek and the Dibru-Saikhowa biosphere reserves.
Q: Where is the Nokrek Biosphere Reserve located?
A: In Meghalaya.
Q: Which national park of India is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
A: Kaziranga, Manas and Sundarbans.
Q: When was Kaziranga declared a World Heritage Site?
A: In 1985.
Q: Which is the largest tiger reserve of India?
A: Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve in Andhra Pradesh.
Q: Which is the first tiger reserve of India?
A: The Jim Corbett Tiger Reserve.
Q: Which sanctuary of India is famous for the wild ass?
A: The Wild Ass Sanctuary in Gujarat (Kutch).
Q: Which sanctuary of India is known for the migratory birds?
A: The Keoladeo Ghana National Park (Bharatpur) in Rajasthan.
Q: Which national park of Assam is known as the 'Big Five' habitat?
A: The Manas National Park.
Q: Which is the only floating national park of the world?
A: The Keibul Lamjao National Park in Manipur.
Q: Which deer is protected in the Keibul Lamjao National Park?
A: The Sangai (Brow-antlered deer).
Q: Which is the smallest national park of India?
A: The South Button Island National Park in the Andamans.
Q: Which national park of India is in the Andaman and Nicobar islands?
A: The Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park and the Campbell Bay National Park.
Q: Which is the largest wildlife sanctuary of India?
A: The Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary in Gujarat.
Q: Which biosphere reserve of India is in the Himalayas?
A: The Nanda Devi and the Khangchendzonga biosphere reserves.
Q: Which national park of Tamil Nadu is famous for the elephants?
A: The Mudumalai National Park.
Q: Which is the oldest wildlife sanctuary of Assam?
A: The Pabho Wildlife Sanctuary, declared in 1980.
Q: Which national park of India is known for the 'Birds Paradise'?
A: The Keoladeo National Park.
Q: Which national park of India is the habitat of the snow leopard?
A: The Hemis National Park in Ladakh.
Q: What is the difference between a national park, a wildlife sanctuary and a biosphere reserve?
A: A national park is reserved strictly for wildlife, with no grazing, cultivation or human settlement allowed. A wildlife sanctuary is also protected, but limited human activity such as grazing may be permitted. A biosphere reserve is larger and has three zones - a strictly protected core, a buffer for research and a transition zone where people live and work sustainably. All of them are protected mainly under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
Q: Which are the largest, oldest and smallest national parks of India?
A: The largest national park is Hemis National Park in Ladakh, which is also the habitat of the snow leopard. The oldest is Jim Corbett National Park in Uttarakhand, established in 1936 as the Hailey National Park. The smallest is the South Button Island National Park in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The only floating national park in the world is Keibul Lamjao in Manipur, famous for the Sangai or brow-antlered deer.
Q: Which national parks are famous for the rhino, the lion and the tiger in India?
A: Kaziranga National Park in Assam is world-famous for the one-horned rhinoceros; it was declared a national park in 1974 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985. Gir National Park in Gujarat is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic lion. Ranthambore National Park in Rajasthan is famous for tigers, and the Manas National Park of Assam is known for the golden langur as well as being a Big Five habitat.
Q: What are the biosphere reserves of India and which was the first?
A: The first biosphere reserve of India is the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, established in 1986, and there are about 18 biosphere reserves in the country. In the Himalayas the important ones are the Nanda Devi and Khangchendzonga biosphere reserves. In the North-East, the Manas, Nokrek and Dibru-Saikhowa biosphere reserves are located, with Nokrek in Meghalaya. A biosphere reserve combines conservation with sustainable use by local communities.
Q: Which protected areas of Assam and the North-East are asked in exams?
A: In Assam, Kaziranga is famous for the one-horned rhino, Manas for the golden langur and the Big Five, Dibru-Saikhowa for the swamp deer and Pobitora as a major rhino reserve. The Chakrashila Wildlife Sanctuary is known for the golden langur, and the oldest wildlife sanctuary of Assam is the Pabho (Pabha) Wildlife Sanctuary, declared in 1980. Kaziranga, Manas and the Sundarbans are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
Q: ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান, বন্যপ্ৰাণী অভয়াৰণ্য আৰু জীৱমণ্ডল সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চলৰ মাজত কি পাৰ্থক্য?
A: ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান বন্যপ্ৰাণীৰ বাবে কঠোৰভাৱে সংৰক্ষিত, য'ত চৰণ, খেতি বা মানৱ বসতি অনুমোদিত নহয়। বন্যপ্ৰাণী অভয়াৰণ্যও সংৰক্ষিত, কিন্তু চৰণৰ দৰে সীমিত মানৱ কাৰ্যকলাপ অনুমোদিত হ'ব পাৰে। জীৱমণ্ডল সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল তাতকৈ ডাঙৰ আৰু তিনিটা মণ্ডল থাকে - কঠোৰভাৱে সংৰক্ষিত মূল, গৱেষণাৰ বাবে বাফাৰ আৰু পৰিবৰ্তন মণ্ডল য'ত মানুহে বহনক্ষমভাৱে বাস আৰু কাম কৰে। এইবোৰ মূলত বন্যপ্ৰাণী (সংৰক্ষণ) আইন, ১৯৭২ৰ অধীনত সংৰক্ষিত।
Q: ভাৰতৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ, পুৰণি আৰু সৰু ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান কোন?
A: আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান লাডাখৰ হেমিছ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান, যি তুষাৰ চিতাৰ বাসস্থানো। আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি উত্তৰাখণ্ডৰ জিম কৰ্বেট ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান, ১৯৩৬ চনত হেইলি ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান হিচাপে স্থাপিত। আটাইতকৈ সৰু আন্দামান-নিকোবৰ দ্বীপপুঞ্জৰ ছাউথ বাটন আইলেণ্ড ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান। পৃথিৱীৰ একমাত্ৰ ভাসমান ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান মণিপুৰৰ কেইবুল লামজাও, ছাংগাই বা ভ্ৰু-শিংযুক্ত হৰিণৰ বাবে বিখ্যাত।
Q: ভাৰতত গঁড়, সিংহ আৰু বাঘৰ বাবে কোনবোৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান বিখ্যাত?
A: অসমৰ কাজিৰঙা ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান এশিঙীয়া গঁড়ৰ বাবে বিশ্ববিখ্যাত; ই ১৯৭৪ চনত ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান আৰু ১৯৮৫ চনত ইউনেস্কো বিশ্ব ঐতিহ্য ক্ষেত্ৰ হিচাপে ঘোষিত হয়। গুজৰাটৰ গিৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান এছিয়াটিক সিংহৰ একমাত্ৰ স্বাভাৱিক বাসস্থান। ৰাজস্থানৰ ৰণথম্বোৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান বাঘৰ বাবে বিখ্যাত, আৰু অসমৰ মানস ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান সোণালী লাংগুৰ তথা বিগ ফাইভ বাসস্থান হিচাপে জনাজাত।
Q: ভাৰতৰ জীৱমণ্ডল সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চলসমূহ কি আৰু প্ৰথমটো কোন আছিল?
A: ভাৰতৰ প্ৰথম জীৱমণ্ডল সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল নীলগিৰি জীৱমণ্ডল সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল, ১৯৮৬ চনত স্থাপিত, আৰু দেশত প্ৰায় ১৮টা জীৱমণ্ডল সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল আছে। হিমালয়ত গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ দুটা নন্দা দেৱী আৰু খাংচেনজংগা। উত্তৰ-পূবত মানস, নকৰেক আৰু ডিব্ৰু-চৈখোৱা জীৱমণ্ডল সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল আছে, নকৰেক মেঘালয়ত। জীৱমণ্ডল সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চলে সংৰক্ষণৰ সৈতে স্থানীয় সমাজৰ বহনক্ষম ব্যৱহাৰ একত্ৰিত কৰে।
Q: অসম আৰু উত্তৰ-পূবৰ কোনবোৰ সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল পৰীক্ষাত সোধা হয়?
A: অসমত কাজিৰঙা এশিঙীয়া গঁড়ৰ বাবে, মানস সোণালী লাংগুৰ আৰু বিগ ফাইভৰ বাবে, ডিব্ৰু-চৈখোৱা দল-হৰিণৰ বাবে আৰু পবিতৰা প্ৰধান গঁড় সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল হিচাপে বিখ্যাত। চক্ৰশিলা বন্যপ্ৰাণী অভয়াৰণ্য সোণালী লাংগুৰৰ বাবে জনাজাত, আৰু অসমৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি বন্যপ্ৰাণী অভয়াৰণ্য পাভো (পাভা) বন্যপ্ৰাণী অভয়াৰণ্য, ১৯৮০ চনত ঘোষিত। কাজিৰঙা, মানস আৰু সুন্দৰবন ইউনেস্কো বিশ্ব ঐতিহ্য ক্ষেত্ৰ।

### Himalayas, Plains, Plateau, Islands & Coasts — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/indian-geography-sec/physical-himalayas-plains-plateau-islands/
Summary: Practice himalayas, plains, plateau, islands & coasts questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: What is the total length of the Himalayas?
A: About 2,400 kilometres.
Q: What are the three main parallel ranges of the Himalayas?
A: Himadri (Greater Himalayas), Himachal (Lesser Himalayas) and Shiwalik (Outer Himalayas).
Q: Which is the highest peak of India?
A: K2 (Godwin Austen), at 8,611 metres, in the Karakoram range.
Q: Which is the highest peak of the Great Himalayas located entirely in India?
A: Nanda Devi, at 7,816 metres.
Q: Which is the highest peak of the Eastern Himalayas?
A: Kangchenjunga, at 8,586 metres.
Q: What is the average height of the Himadri range?
A: About 6,000 metres.
Q: What are the longitudinal divisions of the Himalayas?
A: Punjab Himalayas, Kumaon Himalayas, Nepal Himalayas and Assam Himalayas.
Q: Which is the largest delta of India?
A: The Sundarbans delta, formed by the Ganga and the Brahmaputra.
Q: What is the total length of the Indian coastline?
A: About 7,516.6 kilometres.
Q: Which is the western coastal plain of India?
A: The Konkan coast in the north and the Malabar coast in the south.
Q: Which is the eastern coastal plain of India?
A: The Coromandel coast (south) and the Northern Circars (north).
Q: Which is the largest island group of India?
A: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal.
Q: Which is the largest island of India?
A: Middle Andaman island in the Andaman group.
Q: Which is the largest island of the Lakshadweep group?
A: Andrott island.
Q: What are the Lakshadweep islands made of?
A: They are coral islands.
Q: Which is the northernmost point of India?
A: Indira Col (Siachen), in the Karakoram range.
Q: Which is the southernmost point of India?
A: Indira Point, in the Nicobar Islands.
Q: Which is the easternmost point of India?
A: Kibithu, in Arunachal Pradesh.
Q: Which is the westernmost point of India?
A: Guhar Moti, in Gujarat.
Q: Which is the highest plateau of India?
A: The Ladakh plateau.
Q: What is the Deccan Plateau made of?
A: Basaltic lava rocks (Deccan Trap).
Q: Which is the highest peak of the Deccan Plateau?
A: Anamudi, at 2,695 metres, in Kerala.
Q: What are the western and eastern edges of the Deccan Plateau called?
A: The Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats.
Q: Which is the highest peak of the Western Ghats?
A: Anamudi.
Q: Which is the highest peak of the Eastern Ghats?
A: Mahendragiri, in Odisha.
Q: What is the name of the northern plains of India?
A: The Indo-Gangetic plains.
Q: What are the three sections of the northern plains?
A: Bhabar, Terai and the alluvial plains.
Q: Which is the largest river island in the world?
A: Majuli, in Assam.
Q: Which is the smallest state of India by area?
A: Goa.
Q: Which is the largest state of India by area?
A: Rajasthan.
Q: Which is the longest coastline state of India?
A: Gujarat.
Q: What is the total area of India?
A: About 3.28 million square kilometres.
Q: Which is the widest part of the Himalayas?
A: The Kashmir Himalayas, about 400 kilometres wide.
Q: Which is the narrowest part of the Himalayas?
A: The Assam Himalayas, about 100 to 200 kilometres wide.
Q: Which is the famous pass connecting India with Tibet?
A: The Nathu La pass in Sikkim.
Q: What are the three parallel ranges of the Himalayas and their average heights?
A: The three parallel ranges are the Himadri or Greater Himalayas, the Himachal or Lesser Himalayas and the Shiwalik or Outer Himalayas. The Himadri is the highest and most continuous range, with an average height of about 6,000 metres, and contains almost all the great peaks. The Himachal lies below it, and the Shiwalik is the youngest and lowest range. The range is widest in Kashmir, about 400 kilometres, and narrowest in Assam, about 100 to 200 kilometres.
Q: Which is the highest peak of India and which is the highest peak of the Eastern Himalayas?
A: The highest peak of India is K2, also called Godwin Austen, at 8,611 metres in the Karakoram range. The highest peak of the Eastern Himalayas is Kangchenjunga at 8,586 metres, while the highest peak of the Great Himalayas lying entirely within India is Nanda Devi at 7,816 metres. The Gorichen peak is the highest of the Assam Himalayas.
Q: What are the main physical divisions of India and what is the largest delta?
A: India is divided into the Himalayas, the Indo-Gangetic plains, the Peninsular Plateau and the coastal plains with the islands. The northern plains are made of Bhabar, Terai and the alluvial plains of Bhangar and Khadar. The largest delta of India is the Sundarbans, formed at the mouth of the Ganga and the Brahmaputra, and the Peninsular Plateau is the oldest landmass, built of Deccan Trap basalt.
Q: What is the total coastline of India and which are its coasts and island groups?
A: The total coastline of India, including the islands, is about 7,516.6 kilometres. The western coast has the Konkan and the Malabar coasts with Kanara in between, while the eastern coast has the Northern Circars and the Coromandel coast. The Andaman and Nicobar Islands form the largest island group, with Middle Andaman as its largest island, and Lakshadweep is a group of coral islands whose largest island is Andrott.
Q: Which are the extreme points of India and which states hold the size records?
A: The northernmost point of India is Indira Col in the Siachen area, the southernmost is Indira Point in the Nicobar Islands, the easternmost is Kibithu in Arunachal Pradesh and the westernmost is Guhar Moti in Gujarat. Among the states, Rajasthan is the largest by area, Goa is the smallest and Gujarat has the longest coastline. Majuli in Assam is the largest river island in the world.
Q: হিমালয়ৰ তিনি সমান্তৰাল শ্ৰেণী কি আৰু তেওঁলোকৰ গড় উচ্চতা কিমান?
A: তিনিটা সমান্তৰাল শ্ৰেণী হৈছে হিমাদ্ৰী বা বৃহৎ হিমালয়, হিমাচল বা ক্ষুদ্ৰ হিমালয় আৰু শিৱালিক বা বাহ্য হিমালয়। হিমাদ্ৰী সৰ্বোচ্চ আৰু আটাইতকৈ অবিচ্ছিন্ন শ্ৰেণী, গড় উচ্চতা প্ৰায় ৬,০০০ মিটাৰ, আৰু প্ৰায় সকলো মহান শৃংগ ইয়াত আছে। হিমাচল ইয়াৰ তলত আৰু শিৱালিক আটাইতকৈ নৱীন আৰু নিম্ন শ্ৰেণী। এই শ্ৰেণী কাশ্মীৰত প্ৰায় ৪০০ কিলোমিটাৰ বহল আৰু অসমত প্ৰায় ১০০ৰ পৰা ২০০ কিলোমিটাৰ সংকীৰ্ণ।
Q: ভাৰতৰ সৰ্বোচ্চ শৃংগ কোনটো আৰু পূব হিমালয়ৰ সৰ্বোচ্চ শৃংগ কোনটো?
A: ভাৰতৰ সৰ্বোচ্চ শৃংগ K2, যাক গডউইন অষ্টিন বুলিও কোৱা হয়, কৰাকোৰাম শ্ৰেণীত ৮,৬১১ মিটাৰ। পূব হিমালয়ৰ সৰ্বোচ্চ শৃংগ কাঞ্চনজঙ্ঘা ৮,৫৮৬ মিটাৰ, আনহাতে সম্পূৰ্ণ ভাৰতত থকা বৃহৎ হিমালয়ৰ সৰ্বোচ্চ শৃংগ নন্দা দেৱী ৭,৮১৬ মিটাৰ। অসম হিমালয়ৰ সৰ্বোচ্চ শৃংগ গৰীচেন।
Q: ভাৰতৰ প্ৰধান প্ৰাকৃতিক বিভাগসমূহ কি আৰু বৃহত্তম ব-দ্বীপ কোনটো?
A: ভাৰতক হিমালয়, ইন্দো-গাঙ্গেয় সমভূমি, উপদ্বীপীয় মালভূমি আৰু দ্বীপসহ উপকূলীয় সমভূমিত বিভক্ত কৰা হয়। উত্তৰৰ সমভূমি ভাবৰ, তৰাই আৰু বাংগৰ তথা খাদৰৰ পলস সমভূমিৰে গঠিত। ভাৰতৰ বৃহত্তম ব-দ্বীপ সুন্দৰবন, যি গংগা আৰু ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰৰ মুখত গঠিত, আৰু উপদ্বীপীয় মালভূমি আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি ভূখণ্ড, ডেকান ট্ৰেপ বেচল্টেৰে গঢ়া।
Q: ভাৰতৰ মুঠ উপকূল কিমান আৰু ইয়াৰ উপকূল তথা দ্বীপ গোটসমূহ কি?
A: দ্বীপসমূহ ধৰি ভাৰতৰ মুঠ উপকূল প্ৰায় ৭,৫১৬.৬ কিলোমিটাৰ। পশ্চিম উপকূলত কোংকণ আৰু মালাবাৰ উপকূল, মাজত কানাড়া, আনহাতে পূব উপকূলত উত্তৰ চিৰকাৰ আৰু ক'ৰমণ্ডল উপকূল। আন্দামান আৰু নিকোবৰ দ্বীপপুঞ্জ বৃহত্তম দ্বীপ গোট, যাৰ বৃহত্তম দ্বীপ মাজ আন্দামান, আৰু লাক্ষাদ্বীপ প্ৰবাল দ্বীপৰ গোট যাৰ বৃহত্তম দ্বীপ আন্দ্ৰট।
Q: ভাৰতৰ চৰম বিন্দুবোৰ কি আৰু আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ ৰাজ্য কোনবোৰ?
A: ভাৰতৰ উত্তৰতম বিন্দু ছিয়াচেন অঞ্চলৰ ইন্দিৰা ক'ল, দক্ষিণতম নিকোবৰ দ্বীপপুঞ্জৰ ইন্দিৰা পইণ্ট, পূবতম অৰুণাচল প্ৰদেশৰ কিবিথু আৰু পশ্চিমতম গুজৰাটৰ গুহাৰ ম'তি। ৰাজ্যসমূহৰ ভিতৰত ৰাজস্থান মাটিকালিৰে বৃহত্তম, গোৱা সৰ্বনাম আৰু গুজৰাটৰ আটাইতকৈ দীঘল উপকূল। অসমৰ মাজুলী বিশ্বৰ বৃহত্তম নদী-দ্বীপ।

### Rivers: Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra & Peninsular — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/indian-geography-sec/rivers-indus-ganga-brahmaputra-peninsular/
Summary: Practice rivers: indus, ganga, brahmaputra & peninsular questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual.
Q: Which is the longest river of India?
A: The Ganga, with a total length of about 2,525 kilometres.
Q: Which is the longest river of the world flowing through India?
A: The Indus river.
Q: Where does the Ganga originate?
A: From the Gangotri glacier in Uttarakhand.
Q: What is the name of the source stream of the Ganga?
A: Bhagirathi.
Q: At which place does the Alaknanda meet the Bhagirathi?
A: At Devprayag.
Q: Where does the Ganga fall into the sea?
A: Into the Bay of Bengal through the Sundarbans delta.
Q: Which is the longest tributary of the Ganga?
A: The Yamuna.
Q: Where does the Yamuna originate?
A: From the Yamunotri glacier in Uttarakhand.
Q: Which is the largest tributary of the Ganga by discharge?
A: The Son and the Ghaghara are major tributaries.
Q: Where does the Brahmaputra originate?
A: From the Chemayungdung glacier near Manasarovar in Tibet.
Q: What is the name of the Brahmaputra in Tibet?
A: Tsangpo.
Q: Through which region does the Brahmaputra enter India?
A: Through Arunachal Pradesh (at the Namcha Barwa area).
Q: What is the name of the Brahmaputra in Arunachal Pradesh?
A: Dihang (Siang).
Q: Which is the largest river of the Barak valley?
A: The Barak river.
Q: What is the name of the Barak river in Bangladesh?
A: Surma and later Meghna.
Q: Which is the longest peninsular river of India?
A: The Godavari, with a length of about 1,465 kilometres.
Q: Where does the Godavari originate?
A: From the Trimbakeshwar hills in Nashik, Maharashtra.
Q: Which is the second longest river of the Peninsular India?
A: The Krishna river.
Q: Where does the Krishna originate?
A: From Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra.
Q: Which is the southernmost river of India?
A: The Kaveri river.
Q: Where does the Kaveri originate?
A: From Brahmagiri in the Western Ghats, Karnataka.
Q: Which river is known as the 'Ganga of the South'?
A: The Kaveri river.
Q: Which is the west-flowing major river of the Peninsular India?
A: The Narmada and the Tapi.
Q: Where does the Narmada originate?
A: From the Amarkantak plateau in Madhya Pradesh.
Q: Which is the river that flows through a rift valley in India?
A: The Narmada river.
Q: Which river forms the largest waterfall of India?
A: The Sharavati river forms the Jog falls.
Q: Which river is the longest tributary of the Brahmaputra in Assam?
A: The Subansiri river.
Q: Which is the major north-bank tributary of the Brahmaputra?
A: The Subansiri, Siang, Dibang, Lohit and the Manas.
Q: Which is the major south-bank tributary of the Brahmaputra?
A: The Kopili, Dihing, Dhansiri and the Burhidihing.
Q: Which river flows through the Mawsynram region of Meghalaya?
A: The Umiam river and its tributaries.
Q: Which river is called the 'Sorrow of Bengal'?
A: The Damodar river.
Q: Which river is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
A: The Kosi river.
Q: Which river flows through the Thar desert?
A: The Luni river.
Q: Which is the longest river of the North-East India?
A: The Brahmaputra.
Q: Which river of India flows into the Arabian Sea?
A: The Narmada, Tapi, Sabarmati and the Mahi.
Q: Which is the longest river of India and which is the longest river flowing through India?
A: The longest river of India is the Ganga, with a length of about 2,525 kilometres, rising as the Bhagirathi from the Gangotri glacier and reaching the Bay of Bengal through the Sundarbans delta. The longest river of the world that flows through India is the Indus, which rises near Mansarovar in Tibet, enters India in Ladakh and reaches the Arabian Sea. The Ganga is the larger river within India, while the Indus has the longer total course.
Q: What are the main tributaries of the Ganga and which is the longest one?
A: The longest tributary of the Ganga is the Yamuna, which rises from the Yamunotri glacier, while the Ghaghara is the largest tributary by volume of water. On the left bank the important tributaries are the Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi and Mahananda, and on the right bank they are the Yamuna, Son, Chambal, Betwa and Ken. The Damodar is called the Sorrow of Bengal and the Kosi the Sorrow of Bihar.
Q: What are the different names of the Brahmaputra and its main tributaries?
A: The Brahmaputra rises from the Chemayungdung glacier near Manasarovar in Tibet, where it is called the Tsangpo. It enters India in Arunachal Pradesh as the Dihang or Siang and is called the Brahmaputra after the Siang joins the Dibang and the Lohit at Sadiya. Its main north-bank tributaries are the Subansiri, Siang, Dibang, Lohit and Manas, with the Subansiri the largest in Assam, and its main south-bank tributaries are the Kopili, Dihing, Dhansiri and Burhidihing.
Q: Which are the longest peninsular rivers of India and where do they originate?
A: The longest peninsular river is the Godavari, about 1,465 kilometres, rising from the Trimbakeshwar hills near Nashik in Maharashtra, and it is called the Dakshin Ganga. The Krishna is the second longest peninsular river and rises near Mahabaleshwar, while the Kaveri rises from Brahmagiri in the Western Ghats and is known as the Ganga of the South. The Mahanadi is another important east-flowing peninsular river.
Q: Which rivers of India flow westwards and which special rivers should be remembered?
A: The Narmada, rising from the Amarkantak plateau, and the Tapi are the two great west-flowing peninsular rivers, and both flow through rift valleys and form estuaries instead of deltas. The Sabarmati, the Mahi and the Luni also reach the Arabian Sea, with the Luni flowing through the Thar desert. The Sharavati river forms the Jog falls, one of the highest waterfalls in India, and the Barak is the main river of the Barak valley, becoming the Surma and later the Meghna in Bangladesh.
Q: ভাৰতৰ দীঘলতম নদী কোনটো আৰু ভাৰতৰ মাজেৰে বৈ যোৱা দীঘলতম নদী কোনটো?
A: ভাৰতৰ দীঘলতম নদী গংগা, প্ৰায় ২,৫২৫ কিলোমিটাৰ দীঘল, ভাগীৰথী হিচাপে গঙ্গোত্ৰী হিমবাহৰ পৰা উৎপন্ন আৰু সুন্দৰবন ব-দ্বীপৰ জৰিয়তে বংগোপসাগৰত পৰে। ভাৰতৰ মাজেৰে বৈ যোৱা বিশ্বৰ দীঘলতম নদী সিন্ধু, যি তিব্বতৰ মনসৰোবৰৰ ওচৰত উৎপন্ন, লাডাখত ভাৰতত প্ৰৱেশ কৰে আৰু আৰব সাগৰত পৰে। ভাৰতৰ ভিতৰত গংগা ডাঙৰ, আনহাতে সিন্ধুৰ মুঠ গতি দীঘল।
Q: গংগাৰ মূল উপনদীসমূহ কি আৰু দীঘলতম কোনটো?
A: গংগাৰ দীঘলতম উপনদী যমুনা, যি যমুনোত্ৰী হিমবাহৰ পৰা উৎপন্ন, আনহাতে ঘাগৰা পানীৰ পৰিমাণৰ ফালৰ পৰা বৃহত্তম উপনদী। বাওঁ পাৰৰ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ উপনদী ৰামগংগা, গোমতী, ঘাগৰা, গণ্ডক, কোশী আৰু মহানন্দা, আৰু সোঁ পাৰৰ যমুনা, সোণ, চম্বল, বেটৱা আৰু কেন। দামোদৰক বংগৰ দুখ আৰু কোশীক বিহাৰৰ দুখ বুলি কোৱা হয়।
Q: ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰৰ বিভিন্ন নাম কি আৰু ইয়াৰ মূল উপনদীসমূহ কি?
A: ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ তিব্বতৰ মনসৰোবৰৰ ওচৰৰ চেমায়ুংডুং হিমবাহৰ পৰা উৎপন্ন, য'ত ইয়াক ছাংপো বুলি কোৱা হয়। ই অৰুণাচল প্ৰদেশত দিহাং বা ছিয়াং হিচাপে ভাৰতত প্ৰৱেশ কৰে আৰু ছদিয়াত ছিয়াঙে দিবাং তথা লোহিতৰ সৈতে মিলাৰ পিছত ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ বুলি কোৱা হয়। ইয়াৰ মূল উত্তৰ-পাৰৰ উপনদী সুবনসিৰী, ছিয়াং, দিবাং, লোহিত আৰু মনস, অসমত সুবনসিৰী বৃহত্তম, আৰু মূল দক্ষিণ-পাৰৰ উপনদী কপিলী, দিহিং, ধনসিৰী আৰু বুঢ়িদিহিং।
Q: ভাৰতৰ দীঘলতম উপদ্বীপীয় নদীসমূহ কোনবোৰ আৰু তেওঁলোক ক'ত উৎপন্ন?
A: দীঘলতম উপদ্বীপীয় নদী গোদাবৰী, প্ৰায় ১,৪৬৫ কিলোমিটাৰ, মহাৰাষ্ট্ৰৰ নাছিকৰ ওচৰৰ ত্ৰ্যম্বকেশ্বৰ পাহাৰৰ পৰা উৎপন্ন, আৰু ইয়াক দক্ষিণ গংগা বুলি কোৱা হয়। কৃষ্ণা দ্বিতীয় দীঘলতম উপদ্বীপীয় নদী আৰু মহাবালেশ্বৰৰ ওচৰত উৎপন্ন, আনহাতে কাবেৰী পশ্চিম ঘাটৰ ব্ৰহ্মগিৰিৰ পৰা উৎপন্ন আৰু দক্ষিণৰ গংগা নামে জনাজাত। মহানদী আন এটা গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ পূবমুখী উপদ্বীপীয় নদী।
Q: ভাৰতৰ কোনবোৰ নদীয়ে পশ্চিমলৈ বৈ আৰু কোনবোৰ বিশেষ নদী মনত ৰখা উচিত?
A: অমৰকণ্টক মালভূমিৰ পৰা উৎপন্ন নৰ্মদা আৰু তাপ্তী দুটা মহান পশ্চিমমুখী উপদ্বীপীয় নদী, আৰু দুয়োটা ফাটল উপত্যকাৰ মাজেৰে বৈ ব-দ্বীপৰ সলনি মোহনা গঠন কৰে। সবৰমতী, মাহী আৰু লুণীয়েও আৰব সাগৰত পৰে, লুণী থৰ মৰুভূমিৰ মাজেৰে বৈ। শৰাৱতী নদীয়ে জগ জলপ্ৰপাত গঠন কৰে, ভাৰতৰ আটাইতকৈ উচ্চ জলপ্ৰপাতসমূহৰ এটা, আৰু বৰাক বৰাক উপত্যকাৰ মূল নদী, যি বাংলাদেশত শুৰ্মা আৰু পিছত মেঘনা হৈ পৰে।

### Tiger Reserves, Ramsar Sites & Conservation Projects
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/indian-geography-sec/tiger-reserves-ramsar-conservation-india/
Summary: Practice tiger reserves, ramsar sites & conservation projects questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free.
Q: When was the Project Tiger launched in India?
A: On 1 April 1973.
Q: Which is the first tiger reserve of India?
A: The Jim Corbett Tiger Reserve.
Q: How many tiger reserves are there in India?
A: About 55 tiger reserves.
Q: Which is the largest tiger reserve of India?
A: The Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve in Andhra Pradesh.
Q: Which is the smallest tiger reserve of India?
A: The Bor Tiger Reserve in Maharashtra.
Q: Which tiger reserve of Assam is famous for its tigers?
A: The Kaziranga Tiger Reserve and the Orang Tiger Reserve.
Q: When was the Kaziranga Tiger Reserve established?
A: In 2006.
Q: Which is the second tiger reserve of Assam?
A: The Orang Tiger Reserve.
Q: Which tiger reserve has the highest tiger density in the world?
A: The Kaziranga Tiger Reserve.
Q: Which is the state with the highest number of tigers in India?
A: Madhya Pradesh.
Q: Which is the tiger capital of India?
A: The Nagpur, known as the 'tiger capital'.
Q: Which organization runs the Project Tiger?
A: The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA).
Q: What is the tiger census called in India?
A: The All India Tiger Estimation.
Q: When was the last tiger census done in India?
A: In 2022 (released in 2023).
Q: What is the tiger population of India as per the 2022 census?
A: 3,682 tigers.
Q: Which tiger reserve of India is famous for the Bengal tiger in the Sundarbans?
A: The Sundarbans Tiger Reserve in West Bengal.
Q: Which is the first Ramsar site of India?
A: The Chilika Lake in Odisha.
Q: When was the Chilika Lake declared a Ramsar site?
A: In 1981.
Q: How many Ramsar sites are there in India?
A: About 85 Ramsar sites.
Q: Which is the largest Ramsar site of India?
A: The Sundarbans Wetland.
Q: Which Ramsar site is in Assam?
A: The Deepor Beel, near Guwahati.
Q: When was the Deepor Beel declared a Ramsar site?
A: In 2002.
Q: Which bird is the main attraction of the Deepor Beel?
A: The migratory birds like the storks and the eagles.
Q: Which is the state with the highest number of Ramsar sites in India?
A: Tamil Nadu.
Q: Which is the Ramsar Convention?
A: An international treaty for the conservation of wetlands, signed in 1971.
Q: Which is the largest freshwater lake of India?
A: The Wular Lake in Jammu and Kashmir.
Q: Which wetland of Assam is famous for the migratory birds?
A: The Deepor Beel and the Sone Beel.
Q: Which is the largest wetland of the Barak valley?
A: The Sone Beel in Karimganj.
Q: What is the main cause of the decline of the tiger population in India?
A: Poaching, habitat loss and the decline of the prey base.
Q: Which tiger reserve of India is in the Manas area?
A: The Manas Tiger Reserve in Assam.
Q: When was the Manas Tiger Reserve established?
A: In 2008.
Q: Which is the largest wetland of India?
A: The Sundarbans Wetland.
Q: Which Ramsar site is in the Himalayas?
A: The Wular Lake and the Renuka Lake.
Q: Which is the highest peak of the tiger conservation areas of India?
A: The tiger reserves of the Himalayan foothills.
Q: Which state has the highest number of tigers in the North-East?
A: Assam.
Q: When was Project Tiger launched and which is the first tiger reserve of India?
A: Project Tiger was launched on 1 April 1973 and is run by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA). The first tiger reserve of India is the Jim Corbett Tiger Reserve in Uttarakhand. There are now about 55 tiger reserves in the country, and the tiger is protected as an umbrella species because conserving a large forest for the tiger also conserves the countless other plants and animals in it.
Q: Which are the largest and smallest tiger reserves, and which state has the most tigers?
A: The largest tiger reserve of India is the Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve in Andhra Pradesh and the smallest is the Bor Tiger Reserve in Maharashtra. Madhya Pradesh has the highest number of tigers of any state, and Assam has the highest number in the North-East. Nagpur is popularly called the tiger capital of India. Kaziranga Tiger Reserve, established in 2006, is described as having the highest tiger density in the world.
Q: What is the tiger population of India according to the latest census?
A: The national tiger census is called the All India Tiger Estimation. The most recent exercise was carried out in 2022 and the results were released in 2023, putting India's tiger population at 3,682. This success is attributed to Project Tiger and the network of tiger reserves. The main causes of the earlier decline of tigers were poaching, habitat loss and the decline of the prey base.
Q: What is the Ramsar Convention and what are the Ramsar sites of India?
A: The Ramsar Convention is an international treaty signed at Ramsar in Iran in 1971 for the conservation and wise use of wetlands. A wetland listed under it is called a Ramsar site, and India has about 85 Ramsar sites. The first Ramsar site of India is Chilika Lake in Odisha, declared in 1981, and the largest is the Sundarbans Wetland. The largest freshwater lake of India is Wular Lake, and Tamil Nadu has the highest number of Ramsar sites.
Q: Which Ramsar sites and wetlands are in Assam?
A: The Deepor Beel near Guwahati is the best-known Ramsar site of Assam and was declared in 2002. It is famous for its migratory birds, including storks and eagles. The Sone Beel in Karimganj is the largest wetland of the Barak valley, and along with the Deepor Beel it is among the Assam wetlands most known for migratory birds. Wetlands store flood water, recharge groundwater and support fisheries, and their main threats are encroachment, pollution and siltation.
Q: প্ৰজেক্ট টাইগাৰ কেতিয়া আৰম্ভ হৈছিল আৰু ভাৰতৰ প্ৰথম বাঘ সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল কোন?
A: প্ৰজেক্ট টাইগাৰ ১৯৭৩ চনৰ ১ এপ্ৰিলত আৰম্ভ কৰা হৈছিল আৰু ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় বাঘ সংৰক্ষণ কৰ্তৃপক্ষ (NTCA)ই পৰিচালনা কৰে। ভাৰতৰ প্ৰথম বাঘ সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল উত্তৰাখণ্ডৰ জিম কৰ্বেট বাঘ সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল। দেশত এতিয়া প্ৰায় ৫৫টা বাঘ সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল আছে, আৰু বাঘক ছত্ৰী প্ৰজাতি হিচাপে ৰক্ষা কৰা হয় কাৰণ বাঘৰ বাবে এখন ডাঙৰ বন সংৰক্ষণ কৰিলে তাত থকা অসংখ্য উদ্ভিদ আৰু জীৱ-জন্তুও ৰক্ষা পায়।
Q: আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ আৰু সৰু বাঘ সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল কোন, আৰু কোন ৰাজ্যত আটাইতকৈ বেছি বাঘ?
A: ভাৰতৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ বাঘ সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল অন্ধ্ৰপ্ৰদেশৰ নাগাৰ্জুনসাগৰ-শ্ৰীশৈলম আৰু আটাইতকৈ সৰু মহাৰাষ্ট্ৰৰ বোৰ বাঘ সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল। যিকোনো ৰাজ্যতকৈ বেছি বাঘ মধ্য প্ৰদেশত, আৰু উত্তৰ-পূবত আটাইতকৈ বেছি অসমত। নাগপুৰক জনপ্ৰিয়ভাৱে ভাৰতৰ বাঘৰ ৰাজধানী বোলা হয়। কাজিৰঙা বাঘ সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চল, ২০০৬ চনত স্থাপিত, পৃথিৱীৰ আটাইতকৈ বেছি বাঘৰ ঘনত্ব থকা বুলি কোৱা হয়।
Q: শেহতীয়া গণনা অনুসৰি ভাৰতৰ বাঘৰ জনসংখ্যা কিমান?
A: ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় বাঘ গণনাক সৰ্বভাৰতীয় বাঘ অনুমান বোলা হয়। শেহতীয়া অভিযান ২০২২ চনত কৰা হৈছিল আৰু ফলাফল ২০২৩ চনত প্ৰকাশ কৰা হৈছিল, যিয়ে ভাৰতৰ বাঘৰ জনসংখ্যা ৩,৬৮২ দেখুৱাইছিল। এই সফলতা প্ৰজেক্ট টাইগাৰ আৰু বাঘ সংৰক্ষিত অঞ্চলৰ জালৰ বাবে বুলি কোৱা হয়। আগতে বাঘ হ্ৰাসৰ প্ৰধান কাৰণ আছিল চোৰাং চিকাৰ, বাসস্থান হ্ৰাস আৰু চিকাৰ-ভাৰ হ্ৰাস।
Q: ৰামছাৰ সন্মিলন কি আৰু ভাৰতৰ ৰামছাৰ স্থানসমূহ কি?
A: ৰামছাৰ সন্মিলন ১৯৭১ চনত ইৰাণৰ ৰামছাৰত স্বাক্ষৰিত জলাশয়ৰ সংৰক্ষণ আৰু বুদ্ধিমান ব্যৱহাৰৰ বাবে এক আন্তৰ্জাতিক চুক্তি। ইয়াৰ অধীনত তালিকাভুক্ত জলাশয়ক ৰামছাৰ স্থান বোলা হয়, আৰু ভাৰতত প্ৰায় ৮৫টা ৰামছাৰ স্থান আছে। ভাৰতৰ প্ৰথম ৰামছাৰ স্থান ওড়িশাৰ চিলিকা হ্ৰদ, ১৯৮১ চনত ঘোষিত, আৰু আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ সুন্দৰবন জলাশয়। ভাৰতৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ মিঠা পানীৰ হ্ৰদ ৱুলাৰ হ্ৰদ, আৰু তামিলনাডুত আটাইতকৈ বেছি ৰামছাৰ স্থান।
Q: অসমত কোনবোৰ ৰামছাৰ স্থান আৰু জলাশয় আছে?
A: গুৱাহাটীৰ ওচৰৰ দীপৰ বিল অসমৰ আটাইতকৈ পৰিচিত ৰামছাৰ স্থান আৰু ২০০২ চনত ঘোষিত। ই পৰিভ্ৰমী চৰাইৰ বাবে বিখ্যাত, য'ত শঙ্খচিল আৰু ঈগল আদি। কৰিমগঞ্জৰ ছোন বিল বৰাক উপত্যকাৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ জলাশয়, আৰু দীপৰ বিলৰ সৈতে ই পৰিভ্ৰমী চৰাইৰ বাবে অসমৰ আটাইতকৈ জনাজাত জলাশয়সমূহৰ ভিতৰত। জলাশয়ে বানপানীৰ পানী ৰাখে, ভূ-গৰ্ভস্থ পানী পুনঃভৰ্তি কৰে আৰু মাছপালনক সহায় কৰে, আৰু ইয়াৰ প্ৰধান ভাবুকি বেদখল, প্ৰদূষণ আৰু পলি।

### Highways, Railways, Ports & Waterways — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/indian-geography-sec/transport-highways-railways-ports-india/
Summary: Practice highways, railways, ports & waterways questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: What is the total length of the road network of India?
A: About 63 lakh kilometres, the second largest in the world.
Q: Which is the longest National Highway of India?
A: NH 44, from Srinagar to Kanyakumari.
Q: What is the length of the NH 44?
A: About 3,745 kilometres.
Q: Which is the longest National Highway of the world?
A: The NH 44 was once part of the Asian Highway, but the Pan-American is the longest.
Q: What is the 'Golden Quadrilateral'?
A: The highway network connecting Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata.
Q: What is the total length of the Golden Quadrilateral?
A: About 5,846 kilometres.
Q: What is the 'North-South Corridor' of India?
A: The highway connecting Srinagar with Kanyakumari.
Q: Which is the longest railway zone of India?
A: The Northern Railway.
Q: What is the total length of the railway network of India?
A: About 68,000 kilometres.
Q: When was the first railway started in India?
A: In 1853, between Mumbai and Thane.
Q: Which is the longest railway platform of India?
A: The Gorakhpur railway station in Uttar Pradesh.
Q: Which is the longest railway tunnel of India?
A: The Pir Panjal tunnel in Jammu and Kashmir.
Q: What is the length of the Pir Panjal railway tunnel?
A: About 11.2 kilometres.
Q: Which is the busiest railway station of India?
A: The Howrah railway station in West Bengal.
Q: Which is the first railway station of Assam?
A: The Dibrugarh railway station, opened in 1882.
Q: Which railway zone covers the North-East India?
A: The North-East Frontier Railway (NFR).
Q: Where is the headquarters of the NFR?
A: At Maligaon, Guwahati.
Q: How many major ports are there in India?
A: 13 major ports.
Q: Which is the largest port of India?
A: The Mumbai Port and the Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva).
Q: Which is the oldest port of India?
A: The Kolkata port (Calcutta).
Q: Which is the deepest port of India?
A: The Visakhapatnam port.
Q: Which is the largest container port of India?
A: The Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva).
Q: Which is the easternmost major port of India?
A: The Kolkata and the Paradip ports.
Q: Which is the newest major port of India?
A: The Vadhavan port in Maharashtra (announced recently).
Q: How many national waterways are there in India?
A: About 111 national waterways.
Q: Which is the National Waterway 1 of India?
A: The Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system.
Q: Which is the National Waterway 2 of India?
A: The Brahmaputra river.
Q: Which is the National Waterway 3 of India?
A: The West Coast Canal in Kerala.
Q: Which is the longest National Waterway of India?
A: The NW 1 (Ganga system), about 1,620 kilometres.
Q: Which is the largest river port of India?
A: The Kolkata port on the Hooghly river.
Q: Which is the southernmost major port of India?
A: The Tuticorin port in Tamil Nadu.
Q: Which is the westernmost major port of India?
A: The Kandla (Deendayal) port in Gujarat.
Q: Which is the only major port of the North-East India?
A: There is no major port; the nearest is Kolkata.
Q: What is the 'Inland Waterways Authority of India'?
A: The authority that develops and regulates the national waterways.
Q: When was the Inland Waterways Authority of India established?
A: In 1986.
Q: Which is the longest National Highway of India and what is its length?
A: The longest National Highway of India is NH-44, which runs for about 3,745 kilometres from Srinagar in Jammu and Kashmir to Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu. It was formed by merging several older highways such as the old NH-1A, NH-1, NH-2 and NH-3, and it passes through many states of northern, central and southern India.
Q: When and between which places did the first train run in India?
A: The first train in India ran on 16 April 1853 between Bori Bunder in Mumbai and Thane, covering a distance of about 34 kilometres. In Assam the first railway station was Dibrugarh, opened in 1882, and the North-East Frontier Railway with its headquarters at Maligaon, Guwahati, now covers the whole region.
Q: Which is the longest national waterway and what is National Waterway 2?
A: The longest national waterway is National Waterway 1 (NW-1), the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system, which is about 1,620 kilometres long and runs from Haldia to Prayagraj. National Waterway 2 (NW-2) is the Brahmaputra river from Sadiya to Dhubri, which is the most important waterway for Assam. The Inland Waterways Authority of India regulates them.
Q: Which are the oldest, deepest and largest container ports of India?
A: The Kolkata port is the oldest major port of India and the only major riverine port. The Visakhapatnam port is the deepest port of India. The largest container port of India is the Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva) near Mumbai. India has 13 major ports in total, and there is no major port in the North-East.
Q: What is the North-East Frontier Railway and where is its headquarters?
A: The North-East Frontier Railway (NFR) is the railway zone that covers the whole of North-East India. Its headquarters is at Maligaon in Guwahati, Assam. The Saraighat Bridge at Guwahati was the first rail-cum-road bridge over the Brahmaputra, and the Bogibeel Bridge in Assam is the longest rail-cum-road bridge of India.
Q: ভাৰতৰ আটাইতকৈ দীঘল ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় ঘাইপথ কোন আৰু ইয়াৰ দীঘল কিমান?
A: ভাৰতৰ আটাইতকৈ দীঘল ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় ঘাইপথ হ'ল NH-44, যি জম্মু-কাশ্মীৰৰ শ্ৰীনগৰৰ পৰা তামিলনাডুৰ কন্যাকুমাৰীলৈ প্ৰায় ৩,৭৪৫ কিলোমিটাৰ দীঘল। ই পুৰণি NH-1A, NH-1, NH-2 আৰু NH-3 আদি কেইবাখনো ঘাইপথ একত্ৰিত কৰি গঠিত, আৰু উত্তৰ, মধ্য তথা দক্ষিণ ভাৰতৰ বহু ৰাজ্যৰ মাজেৰে পাৰ হয়।
Q: ভাৰতত প্ৰথম ৰে'ল কেতিয়া আৰু কোন কোন ঠাইৰ মাজত চলিছিল?
A: ভাৰতৰ প্ৰথম ৰে'ল ১৮৫৩ চনৰ ১৬ এপ্ৰিলত মুম্বাইৰ ব'ৰি বন্দৰ আৰু থানেৰ মাজত চলিছিল, প্ৰায় ৩৪ কিলোমিটাৰ দূৰত্ব অতিক্ৰম কৰি। অসমত প্ৰথম ৰে'ল ষ্টেচন ডিব্ৰুগড়, ১৮৮২ চনত মুকলি হৈছিল, আৰু মুখ্য কাৰ্যালয় মালিগাঁও, গুৱাহাটীত থকা উত্তৰ-পূব সীমান্ত ৰে'লৱে এতিয়া গোটেই অঞ্চলটো সামৰি লয়।
Q: আটাইতকৈ দীঘল ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় জলপথ কোন আৰু ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় জলপথ ২ কি?
A: আটাইতকৈ দীঘল ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় জলপথ হ'ল ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় জলপথ ১ (NW-1), গংগা-ভাগীৰথী-হুগলী নদী প্ৰণালী, যি প্ৰায় ১,৬২০ কিলোমিটাৰ দীঘল আৰু হালদিয়াৰ পৰা প্ৰয়াগৰাজলৈ যায়। ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় জলপথ ২ (NW-2) হৈছে সাদিয়াৰ পৰা ধুবৰীলৈ ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ নদী, যি অসমৰ বাবে আটাইতকৈ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ জলপথ। ভাৰতীয় অন্তৰ্দেশীয় জলপথ প্ৰাধিকৰণে ইহঁতক নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ কৰে।
Q: ভাৰতৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি, গভীৰ আৰু ডাঙৰ কন্টেইনাৰ বন্দৰ কোনবোৰ?
A: কলিকতা বন্দৰ ভাৰতৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি প্ৰধান বন্দৰ আৰু একমাত্ৰ প্ৰধান নদী-বন্দৰ। বিশাখাপট্টনম বন্দৰ ভাৰতৰ আটাইতকৈ গভীৰ বন্দৰ। ভাৰতৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ কন্টেইনাৰ বন্দৰ হ'ল মুম্বাইৰ ওচৰৰ জৱাহৰলাল নেহৰু বন্দৰ (নভা শেৱা)। ভাৰতত মুঠ ১৩ টা প্ৰধান বন্দৰ আছে, আৰু উত্তৰ-পূবত কোনো প্ৰধান বন্দৰ নাই।
Q: উত্তৰ-পূব সীমান্ত ৰে'লৱে কি আৰু ইয়াৰ মুখ্য কাৰ্যালয় ক'ত?
A: উত্তৰ-পূব সীমান্ত ৰে'লৱে (NFR) হৈছে গোটেই উত্তৰ-পূব ভাৰত সামৰি লোৱা ৰে'ল মণ্ডল। ইয়াৰ মুখ্য কাৰ্যালয় অসমৰ গুৱাহাটীৰ মালিগাঁৱত। গুৱাহাটীৰ শৰাইঘাট দলং ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰৰ ওপৰত প্ৰথম ৰে'ল-পথ দলং আছিল, আৰু অসমৰ বগীবিল দলং ভাৰতৰ আটাইতকৈ দীঘল ৰে'ল-পথ দলং।

### Natural Vegetation & Forest Types — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/indian-geography-sec/vegetation-forest-types-india/
Summary: Practice natural vegetation & forest types questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What is the total forest cover of India as per the latest State of Forest Report?
A: About 21.71% of the geographical area.
Q: What percentage of the forest cover does the tree cover add to India?
A: About 24.62% together (forest + tree cover).
Q: What are the major types of forests in India?
A: Tropical evergreen, tropical deciduous, thorn, montane, mangrove and littoral forests.
Q: Which forest type covers the largest area of India?
A: Tropical deciduous forests.
Q: What is the other name of the tropical deciduous forests?
A: Monsoon forests.
Q: What is the percentage of the tropical deciduous forests of the total forest area of India?
A: About 65% of the total forest area.
Q: Where are the tropical evergreen forests found in India?
A: In the Western Ghats, the North-East and the Andaman islands.
Q: Which is the main tree of the tropical deciduous forests?
A: Teak, Sal and Bamboo.
Q: Where are the thorn forests found in India?
A: In the semi-arid regions of Rajasthan, Gujarat and Punjab.
Q: What is the main tree of the thorn forests?
A: Kikar, Babul and Khair.
Q: Where are the mangrove forests found in India?
A: In the deltas and the coastal areas, especially the Sundarbans.
Q: Which is the largest mangrove forest of the world?
A: The Sundarbans.
Q: Which tree is the main species of the Sundarbans?
A: Sundari tree.
Q: What are the littoral forests?
A: Forests along the sea coasts, with salt-tolerant species.
Q: What is the montane forest?
A: Forests found at high altitudes in the Himalayas and the other mountains.
Q: What type of forest is found in the foothills of the Himalayas?
A: Tropical wet deciduous and semi-evergreen forests.
Q: Which type of forest is found in the Eastern Himalayan belt?
A: Sub-tropical and temperate forests, including rhododendron forests.
Q: What is the 'sacred groves' in the North-East?
A: Community-protected forest patches of the tribal people.
Q: What is the main vegetation of the 'Terai' region?
A: Tall grasses, swampy vegetation and sal forests.
Q: Which forest type is found around the Tropic of Cancer region?
A: Tropical dry deciduous and thorn forests.
Q: Which forest is known as the 'lungs of the Earth'?
A: The tropical rainforests, like the Amazon and the Dehing-Patkai.
Q: Which is the largest rainforest of India?
A: The Dehing-Patkai rainforest in Assam.
Q: Which forest of India is famous for the 'Hollong' trees?
A: The Jeypore rainforest of Assam.
Q: What is the cause of the decline of the forest area in the North-East?
A: Jhum cultivation, logging and encroachment.
Q: What is the 'Van Mahotsav'?
A: The tree plantation festival of India, celebrated in the first week of July.
Q: What is the National Forest Policy of India?
A: It aims to maintain at least one-third of the total land area under forest.
Q: What is the total recorded forest area of the North-East India?
A: More than 65% of the region is forested.
Q: Which state of the North-East has the lowest forest cover?
A: Assam, among the eight states of the region.
Q: Which is the main bamboo producing state of India?
A: Mizoram.
Q: What is the 'shifting cultivation' called in the North-East?
A: Jhum cultivation.
Q: Which forest type grows in the areas of 100 to 200 cm rainfall?
A: Moist deciduous forests.
Q: Which forest type grows in the areas of 50 to 100 cm rainfall?
A: Dry deciduous forests.
Q: Which is the most important tree of the evergreen forests of the Western Ghats?
A: Rosewood, Ebony and Mahogany.
Q: What is the 'sal' tree mainly used for?
A: For timber and railway sleepers.
Q: Which is the national tree of India?
A: The Banyan (Ficus benghalensis) tree.
Q: How much of India is under forest cover and what is the National Forest Policy target?
A: As per the latest State of Forest Report, the forest cover of India is about 21.71 per cent of the geographical area, and the forest and tree cover together is about 24.62 per cent. The National Forest Policy of 1988 aims to maintain at least one-third, or about 33 per cent, of the total land area of the country under forest or tree cover, with a higher target for the hills. The North-East is the most forested region, with more than 65 per cent of its area under recorded forest.
Q: What are the major forest types of India and which type covers the largest area?
A: The major types are tropical evergreen, tropical deciduous, thorn and scrub, montane and mangrove or littoral forests. The tropical deciduous forests, also called monsoon forests, cover the largest area, about 65 per cent of the total forest area of India. Rainfall decides the type: evergreen forests need more than 200 centimetres, moist deciduous about 100 to 200 centimetres, dry deciduous about 50 to 100 centimetres and thorn forests below about 50 centimetres.
Q: Where are the evergreen, deciduous, thorn and mangrove forests found in India?
A: The tropical evergreen forests grow in the Western Ghats, the North-East and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, with rosewood, ebony and mahogany. The deciduous forests, with teak and sal, are the most widespread. The thorn forests occur in the semi-arid regions of Rajasthan, Gujarat and Punjab with kikar, babul and khair. The mangrove forests grow in the deltas and coastal areas, and the Sundarbans is the largest mangrove forest in the world, with the sundari as its main tree.
Q: What is special about the forests of the North-East and what threatens them?
A: The North-East is part of the Eastern Himalayan biodiversity hotspot and has more than 65 per cent of its area under recorded forest. Its people protect sacred groves, community woods preserved by tradition. The Dehing-Patkai forest is the largest rainforest of India and the Jeypore rainforest is famous for its Hollong trees, while Mizoram is the leading bamboo-producing state. The forests are threatened mainly by jhum cultivation, commercial logging and encroachment.
Q: How do the montane forests of the Himalayas change with height and what is Van Mahotsav?
A: In the Himalayas the vegetation changes with altitude: the foothills have tropical wet deciduous and semi-evergreen forests, the Terai is known for tall grasses and sal, and higher up come sub-tropical and temperate forests of oak, deodar, pine and rhododendron, followed by alpine pastures and snow. The Eastern Himalayan belt is especially rich in sub-tropical and temperate species. Van Mahotsav is the tree-planting festival of India, celebrated in the first week of July, started to involve people in increasing the green cover.
Q: ভাৰতত কিমান বনাঞ্চল আছে আৰু ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় বন নীতিৰ লক্ষ্য কি?
A: শেহতীয়া বন-স্থিতি প্ৰতিবেদন অনুসৰি ভাৰতৰ বনাঞ্চল ভৌগোলিক কালিৰ প্ৰায় ২১.৭১ শতাংশ, আৰু বন আৰু গছ-আৱৰণ একেলগে প্ৰায় ২৪.৬২ শতাংশ। ১৯৮৮ চনৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় বন নীতিয়ে দেশৰ মুঠ ভূমিৰ অন্তত এক তৃতীয়াংশ, অৰ্থাৎ প্ৰায় ৩৩ শতাংশ, বন বা গছ-আৱৰণৰ অধীনত ৰখাৰ লক্ষ্য ৰাখিছে, পাহাৰৰ বাবে তাতকৈ বেছি। উত্তৰ-পূব আটাইতকৈ বনসমৃদ্ধ অঞ্চল, য'ত ৬৫ শতাংশতকৈ বেছি ৰেকৰ্ড কৰা বনাঞ্চল।
Q: ভাৰতৰ প্ৰধান বনৰ প্ৰকাৰ কি আৰু কোনটোৱে আটাইতকৈ বেছি কালি ঢাকে?
A: প্ৰধান প্ৰকাৰ হৈছে ক্ৰান্তীয় চিৰসেউজ, ক্ৰান্তীয় পৰ্ণপাতী, কঁইটীয়া আৰু গুল্ম, পৰ্বতীয় আৰু মেনগ্ৰোভ বা লিট'ৰেল বন। ক্ৰান্তীয় পৰ্ণপাতী বন, যাক মৌচুমী বনও কোৱা হয়, আটাইতকৈ বেছি কালি ঢাকে, ভাৰতৰ মুঠ বনাঞ্চলৰ প্ৰায় ৬৫ শতাংশ। বৰষুণে প্ৰকাৰ নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰে: চিৰসেউজৰ বাবে ২০০ চেন্টিমিটাৰতকৈ বেছি, আৰ্দ্ৰ পৰ্ণপাতী প্ৰায় ১০০-২০০, শুকান পৰ্ণপাতী প্ৰায় ৫০-১০০ আৰু কঁইটীয়া বন প্ৰায় ৫০ চেন্টিমিটাৰৰ তলত।
Q: ভাৰতত চিৰসেউজ, পৰ্ণপাতী, কঁইটীয়া আৰু মেনগ্ৰোভ বন ক'ত পোৱা যায়?
A: ক্ৰান্তীয় চিৰসেউজ বন পশ্চিম ঘাট, উত্তৰ-পূব আৰু আন্দামান-নিকোবৰ দ্বীপপুঞ্জত গজে, য'ত ৰোজউড, এবনি আৰু মহাগনি থাকে। চেগুন আৰু শালৰ পৰ্ণপাতী বন আটাইতকৈ বিয়পা। কঁইটীয়া বন ৰাজস্থান, গুজৰাট আৰু পঞ্জাবৰ অৰ্ধ-শুকান অঞ্চলত কিকৰ, বাবুল আৰু খেৰেৰে থাকে। মেনগ্ৰোভ বন ব-দ্বীপ আৰু উপকূলত গজে, আৰু সুন্দৰবন পৃথিৱীৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ মেনগ্ৰোভ বন, যাৰ প্ৰধান গছ সুন্দৰী।
Q: উত্তৰ-পূবৰ বনৰ বিশেষত্ব কি আৰু ইয়াৰ প্ৰতি কি ভাবুকি?
A: উত্তৰ-পূব পূব হিমালয়ৰ জীৱবৈচিত্ৰ্য হটস্পটৰ অংশ আৰু ইয়াৰ ৬৫ শতাংশতকৈ বেছি কালি ৰেকৰ্ড কৰা বনাঞ্চল। ইয়াৰ মানুহে ৰীতি-নীতিৰে ৰক্ষা কৰা পবিত্ৰ বন সংৰক্ষণ কৰে। ডিহিং-পাটকাই বন ভাৰতৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ বৰ্ষাৰণ্য আৰু জয়পুৰ বৰ্ষাৰণ্য হলঙ গছৰ বাবে বিখ্যাত, আনহাতে মিজোৰাম আগশাৰী বাঁহ-উৎপাদক ৰাজ্য। বনসমূহ মূলত ঝুম খেতি, বাণিজ্যিক কাঠ-কটা আৰু বেদখলৰ দ্বাৰা বিপন্ন।
Q: হিমালয়ৰ পৰ্বতীয় বন উচ্চতাৰ লগত কেনেকৈ সলনি হয় আৰু বনমহোৎসৱ কি?
A: হিমালয়ত উদ্ভিদ উচ্চতাৰ লগত সলনি হয়: পদূলিত ক্ৰান্তীয় আৰ্দ্ৰ পৰ্ণপাতী আৰু অৰ্ধ-চিৰসেউজ বন, টেৰাই ওখ ঘাঁহ আৰু শালৰ বাবে বিখ্যাত, আৰু ওপৰলৈ উপ-ক্ৰান্তীয় তথা নাতিশীতোষ্ণ বনত ওক, দেৱদাৰ, পাইন আৰু ৰ'ড'ডেনড্ৰন, তাৰ পিছত আল্পাইন চৰণভূমি আৰু বৰফ। পূব হিমালয়ৰ বেল্ট উপ-ক্ৰান্তীয় আৰু নাতিশীতোষ্ণ প্ৰজাতিৰে বিশেষভাৱে সমৃদ্ধ। বনমহোৎসৱ ভাৰতৰ গছ-ৰোপণ উৎসৱ, জুলাইৰ প্ৰথম সপ্তাহত পালন কৰা হয়, সেউজ আৱৰণ বঢ়োৱাত মানুহক জড়িত কৰিবলৈ আৰম্ভ কৰা হৈছিল।

### Atmosphere Layers, Winds & Cyclones — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/world-geography-sec/atmosphere-layers-winds-cyclones/
Summary: Practice atmosphere layers, winds & cyclones questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What is the atmosphere?
A: The blanket of gases surrounding the Earth.
Q: What is the main gas of the atmosphere?
A: Nitrogen (about 78%).
Q: What is the second most abundant gas of the atmosphere?
A: Oxygen (about 21%).
Q: What are the five layers of the atmosphere?
A: Troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere and exosphere.
Q: Which is the lowest layer of the atmosphere?
A: The troposphere.
Q: In which layer do we live and weather occurs?
A: The troposphere.
Q: What is the average height of the troposphere?
A: About 13 to 14 kilometres.
Q: Which layer contains the ozone layer?
A: The stratosphere.
Q: What does the ozone layer protect us from?
A: From the harmful ultraviolet rays of the sun.
Q: In which layer does the temperature increase with height?
A: In the stratosphere and the thermosphere.
Q: In which layer do the meteors burn up?
A: The mesosphere.
Q: Which layer contains the ionosphere used for radio communication?
A: The thermosphere.
Q: Which is the uppermost layer of the atmosphere?
A: The exosphere.
Q: What is 'air pressure'?
A: The weight of the air pressing down on the Earth's surface.
Q: What are the permanent winds?
A: The trade winds, the westerlies and the polar easterlies.
Q: Which winds blow from the subtropical high to the equatorial low?
A: The trade winds.
Q: What are the trade winds called in the northern hemisphere?
A: The North-East trade winds.
Q: Which winds blow from the horse latitudes to the polar region?
A: The westerlies.
Q: What are the seasonal winds of India?
A: The monsoon winds.
Q: What is a cyclone?
A: A system of low pressure with strong winds rotating around a centre.
Q: What is the centre of a cyclone called?
A: The eye of the cyclone.
Q: What is the 'eye' of the cyclone?
A: The calm centre of the cyclone.
Q: What are the cyclones of the Pacific Ocean called?
A: Typhoons.
Q: What are the cyclones of the Atlantic Ocean called?
A: Hurricanes.
Q: What are the cyclones of the Indian Ocean called?
A: Cyclones.
Q: In which direction do the cyclones rotate in the northern hemisphere?
A: Anti-clockwise.
Q: What are the cyclones of the Bay of Bengal called?
A: Cyclonic storms.
Q: What is the main cause of the cyclone formation?
A: The warm ocean waters and the low pressure over the sea.
Q: What is the 'cyclone warning' system of India called?
A: The IMD cyclone warning system.
Q: What is the effect of the global warming on the cyclones?
A: It increases their frequency and intensity.
Q: What is the composition of the atmosphere?
A: The atmosphere is a mixture of gases in which nitrogen is the most abundant at about 78 per cent, followed by oxygen at about 21 per cent. Argon forms about 0.93 per cent and carbon dioxide about 0.04 per cent. Although carbon dioxide and water vapour are present in small amounts, they are very important because they absorb heat and cause the greenhouse effect, and water vapour is essential for cloud formation and rainfall.
Q: What are the layers of the atmosphere and which is the most important for weather?
A: The atmosphere has five layers - the troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere and exosphere. The troposphere is the lowest layer, extending about 8 kilometres at the poles and 18 kilometres at the equator, and it is where all weather such as clouds, rain and storms occur. The stratosphere contains the ozone layer, the mesosphere is where meteors burn up, and the thermosphere contains the ionosphere where the aurora occurs.
Q: What causes winds and what are the planetary winds?
A: Winds are caused by differences in air pressure, as air moves from a high-pressure area to a low-pressure area. The rotation of the Earth deflects these winds to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere, which is called the Coriolis effect. The three permanent or planetary winds are the trade winds, which blow towards the equator; the westerlies, which blow towards the poles; and the polar easterlies.
Q: What is the difference between a cyclone and an anticyclone?
A: A cyclone is an area of low pressure in which winds blow inwards and rise, producing clouds, rain and storms; in the Northern Hemisphere cyclonic winds rotate anticlockwise and in the Southern Hemisphere clockwise. An anticyclone is an area of high pressure in which winds blow outwards and descend, bringing clear and dry weather. A tornado is a smaller but extremely violent rotating column of air.
Q: What are the local names of tropical cyclones in different regions?
A: A tropical cyclone is a violent storm that forms over warm oceans and is known by different local names. It is called a hurricane in the North Atlantic and the eastern Pacific, a typhoon in the western Pacific and the China Sea, a cyclone in the Indian Ocean, and a willy-willy in Australia. The three main types of rainfall are convectional, orographic or relief, and cyclonic or frontal rainfall.
Q: বায়ুমণ্ডলৰ গঠন কি?
A: বায়ুমণ্ডল গেছৰ মিশ্ৰণ, য'ত নাইট্ৰজেন আটাইতকৈ বেছি প্ৰায় ৭৮ শতাংশ, তাৰ পিছত অক্সিজেন প্ৰায় ২১ শতাংশ। আৰ্গন প্ৰায় ০.৯৩ শতাংশ আৰু কাৰ্বন ডাইঅক্সাইড প্ৰায় ০.০৪ শতাংশ। কাৰ্বন ডাইঅক্সাইড আৰু জলীয় বাষ্প কম পৰিমাণত থাকিলেও অতি গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ, কাৰণ ইহঁতে তাপ শোষণ কৰি গ্ৰীণহাউছ প্ৰভাৱ ঘটায়, আৰু জলীয় বাষ্প ডাৱৰ আৰু বৰষুণৰ বাবে অপৰিহাৰ্য।
Q: বায়ুমণ্ডলৰ স্তৰসমূহ কি আৰু বতৰৰ বাবে কোনটো আটাইতকৈ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: বায়ুমণ্ডলৰ পাঁচটা স্তৰ - ট্ৰ'প'স্ফিয়াৰ, ষ্ট্ৰেট'স্ফিয়াৰ, মেছ'স্ফিয়াৰ, থাৰ্ম'স্ফিয়াৰ আৰু এক্স'স্ফিয়াৰ। ট্ৰ'প'স্ফিয়াৰ আটাইতকৈ তলৰ স্তৰ, মেৰুত প্ৰায় ৮ কিলোমিটাৰ আৰু বিষুৱৰেখাত ১৮ কিলোমিটাৰলৈকে বিস্তৃত, আৰু ইয়াতেই ডাৱৰ, বৰষুণ আৰু ধুমুহাৰ দৰে সকলো বতৰ ঘটে। ষ্ট্ৰেট'স্ফিয়াৰত অ'জন স্তৰ, মেছ'স্ফিয়াৰত উল্কা শেষ হয়, আৰু থাৰ্ম'স্ফিয়াৰত আয়ন'স্ফিয়াৰ তথা অৰৰা থাকে।
Q: বায়ু কিয় হয় আৰু গ্ৰহীয় বায়ুবোৰ কি কি?
A: বায়ুৰ চাপৰ পাৰ্থক্যৰ বাবে বায়ু উচ্চ চাপৰ অঞ্চলৰ পৰা নিম্ন চাপৰ অঞ্চললৈ যায়, তাকেই বায়ু বোলা হয়। পৃথিৱীৰ ঘূৰ্ণনে উত্তৰ গোলাৰ্ধত বায়ু সোঁফালে আৰু দক্ষিণ গোলাৰ্ধত বাওঁফালে বেঁকা কৰে, যাক কৰিঅ'লিছ প্ৰভাৱ বোলা হয়। তিনিটা স্থায়ী বা গ্ৰহীয় বায়ু হৈছে বিষুৱৰেখালৈ বৈ যোৱা বাণিজ্য বায়ু, মেৰুলৈ বৈ যোৱা পশ্চিমীয়া বায়ু আৰু মেৰু পূবীয়া বায়ু।
Q: ঘূৰ্ণীবতাহ আৰু প্ৰতিঘূৰ্ণীবতাহৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: ঘূৰ্ণীবতাহ হৈছে নিম্ন চাপৰ এটা অঞ্চল, য'ত বায়ু ভিতৰলৈ বৈ গৈ ওপৰলৈ উঠে আৰু ডাৱৰ, বৰষুণ তথা ধুমুহা সৃষ্টি কৰে; উত্তৰ গোলাৰ্ধত ঘূৰ্ণীবতাহীয় বায়ু ঘড়ীৰ বিপৰীত দিশত আৰু দক্ষিণ গোলাৰ্ধত ঘড়ীৰ দিশত ঘূৰে। প্ৰতিঘূৰ্ণীবতাহ হৈছে উচ্চ চাপৰ অঞ্চল, য'ত বায়ু বাহিৰলৈ বৈ গৈ তললৈ নামে আৰু পৰিষ্কাৰ তথা শুকান বতৰ আনে। টৰ্ণেড' সৰু কিন্তু অতি হিংস্ৰ ঘূৰ্ণনশীল বায়ুৰ স্তম্ভ।
Q: বিভিন্ন অঞ্চলত গ্ৰীষ্মমণ্ডলীয় ঘূৰ্ণীবতাহৰ স্থানীয় নাম কি কি?
A: গ্ৰীষ্মমণ্ডলীয় ঘূৰ্ণীবতাহ উষ্ণ মহাসাগৰৰ ওপৰত সৃষ্টি হোৱা হিংস্ৰ ধুমুহা, যাক বিভিন্ন স্থানত বিভিন্ন নামেৰে জনা যায়। উত্তৰ আটলান্টিক আৰু পূব প্ৰশান্তত ইয়াক হাৰিকেইন, পশ্চিম প্ৰশান্ত আৰু চীন সাগৰত টাইফুন, ভাৰত মহাসাগৰত ঘূৰ্ণীবতাহ, আৰু অষ্ট্ৰেলিয়াত ৱিলি-ৱিলি বোলা হয়। বৰষুণৰ তিনিটা মূল প্ৰকাৰ হৈছে পৰিচলন, পৰ্বতীয় বা প্ৰাকৃতিক, আৰু ঘূৰ্ণীবতাহীয় বা সন্মুখ বৰষুণ।

### Earth Layers, Plates & Volcanoes — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/world-geography-sec/earth-layers-plates-volcanoes/
Summary: Practice earth layers, plates & volcanoes questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What are the three layers of the Earth?
A: The crust, the mantle and the core.
Q: What is the outermost layer of the Earth called?
A: The crust.
Q: What is the average thickness of the continental crust?
A: About 35 kilometres.
Q: What is the average thickness of the oceanic crust?
A: About 5 kilometres.
Q: Which layer of the Earth is the thickest?
A: The mantle.
Q: What is the thickness of the mantle?
A: About 2,900 kilometres.
Q: What is the innermost layer of the Earth?
A: The inner core.
Q: What is the inner core made of?
A: Solid iron and nickel.
Q: What is the radius of the Earth?
A: About 6,371 kilometres.
Q: What is the temperature of the Earth's core?
A: About 5,000 to 6,000 degrees Celsius.
Q: What is the 'lithosphere'?
A: The solid outer part of the Earth, including the crust and the upper mantle.
Q: What is the 'asthenosphere'?
A: The semi-molten layer of the upper mantle on which the plates move.
Q: Who proposed the theory of continental drift?
A: Alfred Wegener, in 1912.
Q: What is the 'Pangaea'?
A: The supercontinent that existed about 200 million years ago.
Q: How many major tectonic plates are there on the Earth?
A: Seven major plates.
Q: Which is the largest tectonic plate?
A: The Pacific plate.
Q: What is the 'ring of fire'?
A: The belt of volcanoes and earthquakes around the Pacific Ocean.
Q: What happens at the convergent plate boundaries?
A: Plates collide, forming mountains, and causing earthquakes.
Q: What happens at the divergent plate boundaries?
A: Plates move apart, forming new crust and mid-oceanic ridges.
Q: What is a volcano?
A: An opening in the Earth's crust through which magma erupts.
Q: What is magma called when it reaches the surface?
A: Lava.
Q: What are the three types of volcanoes?
A: Active, dormant and extinct.
Q: What is a 'shield volcano'?
A: A broad volcano formed by low-viscosity lava, like Mauna Loa.
Q: What is a 'stratovolcano'?
A: A tall cone-shaped volcano made of layers of lava and ash.
Q: Which is the largest active volcano of the world?
A: Mauna Loa in Hawaii.
Q: What is the 'Mount Fuji'?
A: The highest active volcano of Japan, about 3,776 metres.
Q: Which is the highest volcano of the world?
A: Nevado Ojos del Salado, in the Andes.
Q: What is the 'mid-oceanic ridge'?
A: An underwater mountain range formed at the divergent boundaries.
Q: Which is the longest mountain range of the world?
A: The mid-oceanic ridge system (about 65,000 km), led by the Andes on land.
Q: What is the theory of plate tectonics?
A: The theory that the Earth's lithosphere is divided into moving plates.
Q: What are the three layers of the Earth and which is the thickest?
A: The Earth has three main layers - the crust, the mantle and the core. The crust is the outermost and thinnest layer, about 35 kilometres thick under the continents and about 5 kilometres under the oceans. The mantle is the thickest layer, extending to a depth of about 2,900 kilometres, and the core is the innermost part, with a liquid outer core and a solid inner core made of iron and nickel.
Q: Who proposed the theory of continental drift and what is Pangaea?
A: Alfred Wegener proposed the theory of continental drift in 1912. He said that all the continents were once joined in a single supercontinent called Pangaea, which existed about 200 million years ago and later broke apart to form the present continents. His idea was later developed into the modern theory of plate tectonics, which explains the movement of the Earth's lithospheric plates over the asthenosphere.
Q: What happens at convergent, divergent and transform plate boundaries?
A: At a convergent boundary two plates collide, producing fold mountains, deep ocean trenches and volcanoes through subduction. At a divergent boundary the plates move apart and magma rises to form new crust and mid-oceanic ridges. At a transform boundary the plates slide past each other horizontally, causing earthquakes. The belt of volcanic and seismic activity around the Pacific Ocean is known as the Ring of Fire.
Q: What is the difference between magma and lava?
A: Magma is the molten rock, along with dissolved gases, that lies beneath the Earth's surface. When this molten rock reaches the surface through an opening in the crust it is called lava. Volcanoes are classified by activity as active, dormant or extinct, and by shape as shield volcanoes, such as the low-viscosity Mauna Loa, and composite or stratovolcanoes built of layers of lava and ash.
Q: Which is the largest active volcano and the highest volcano in the world?
A: Mauna Loa in Hawaii is the largest active volcano in the world, formed by low-viscosity lava that gives it a broad shield shape. The highest volcano in the world is Nevado Ojos del Salado in the Andes mountains. Mount Fuji in Japan, about 3,776 metres high, is a well-known composite or stratovolcano and the highest peak of Japan.
Q: পৃথিৱীৰ তিনিটা স্তৰ কি আৰু আটাইতকৈ ডাঠ কোনটো?
A: পৃথিৱীৰ তিনিটা মূল স্তৰ - ভূত্বক, আচ্ছাদনী আৰু কেন্দ্ৰ। ভূত্বক আটাইতকৈ বাহিৰৰ আৰু পাতল স্তৰ, মহাদেশৰ তলত প্ৰায় ৩৫ কিলোমিটাৰ আৰু মহাসাগৰৰ তলত প্ৰায় ৫ কিলোমিটাৰ। আচ্ছাদনী আটাইতকৈ ডাঠ স্তৰ, যি প্ৰায় ২,৯০০ কিলোমিটাৰ গভীৰলৈকে থাকে, আৰু কেন্দ্ৰ আটাইতকৈ ভিতৰৰ অংশ, যাৰ বাহ্যিক কেন্দ্ৰ তৰল আৰু অন্তৰীণ কেন্দ্ৰ লোহা-নিকেলৰ কঠিন।
Q: মহাদেশীয় প্ৰবাহ তত্ত্ব কোনে আগবঢ়াইছিল আৰু পেঞ্জিয়া কি?
A: আলফ্ৰেড ৱেগেনে ১৯১২ চনত মহাদেশীয় প্ৰবাহ তত্ত্ব আগবঢ়াইছিল। তেওঁ কৈছিল যে সকলো মহাদেশ পূৰ্বে পেঞ্জিয়া নামৰ এটা মহা-মহাদেশত সংযুক্ত আছিল, যি প্ৰায় ২০০ মিলিয়ন বছৰ আগতে আছিল আৰু পিছত ভাঙি বৰ্তমান মহাদেশবোৰ গঠিত হৈছিল। তেওঁৰ ধাৰণাটো পিছত আধুনিক প্লেট টেক্টনিক্স তত্ত্বলৈ বিকশিত হয়, যি অস্থেনোস্ফিয়াৰৰ ওপৰত লিথোস্ফিয়াৰ প্লেটৰ গতিবিধি ব্যাখ্যা কৰে।
Q: অভিসাৰী, অপসাৰী আৰু ৰূপান্তৰক প্লেট সীমান্তত কি ঘটে?
A: অভিসাৰী সীমান্তত দুখন প্লেট সংঘৰ্ষ কৰে, যাৰ ফলত অধোগমনৰ জৰিয়তে ভাঁজ পৰ্বত, গভীৰ মহাসাগৰীয় খাত আৰু আগ্নেয়গিৰি সৃষ্টি হয়। অপসাৰী সীমান্তত প্লেটবোৰ পৃথক হয় আৰু মেগমা উঠি নতুন ভূত্বক তথা মধ্য-মহাসাগৰীয় শিখৰ গঠন কৰে। ৰূপান্তৰক সীমান্তত প্লেটবোৰ আনুভূমিকভাৱে পিছলি যায়, যাৰ ফলত ভূমিকম্প হয়। প্ৰশান্ত মহাসাগৰৰ চৌপাশে থকা এই আগ্নেয় আৰু ভূকম্পীয় বলয়ক ফায়াৰ ৰিং বোলা হয়।
Q: মেগমা আৰু লাভাৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: মেগমা হৈছে পৃথিৱীৰ পৃষ্ঠৰ তলত থকা গলিত শিল আৰু দ্ৰৱীভূত গেছ। এই গলিত শিল ভূত্বকৰ এটা মুখেদি পৃষ্ঠত উপনীত হ'লে ইয়াক লাভা বোলা হয়। আগ্নেয়গিৰি সক্ৰিয়তাৰ ভিত্তিত সক্ৰিয়, নিদ্ৰিত বা লুপ্ত আৰু আকৃতিৰ ভিত্তিত শ্বিল্ড আগ্নেয়গিৰি তথা যৌগিক বা ষ্ট্ৰেটো আগ্নেয়গিৰি হিচাপে শ্ৰেণীবদ্ধ কৰা হয়।
Q: বিশ্বৰ বৃহত্তম সক্ৰিয় আৰু সৰ্বোচ্চ আগ্নেয়গিৰি কোনটো?
A: হাৱাইৰ মাউনা লোৱা বিশ্বৰ বৃহত্তম সক্ৰিয় আগ্নেয়গিৰি, যি কম সান্দহৰ লাভাৰে গঠিত হৈ বহল শ্বিল্ড আকৃতি লাভ কৰিছে। বিশ্বৰ সৰ্বোচ্চ আগ্নেয়গিৰি হৈছে এণ্ডেছৰ নেভাডো অ'হ'ছ দেল চালাডো। জাপানৰ মাউণ্ট ফুজি, প্ৰায় ৩,৭৭৬ মিটাৰ উচ্চ, জাপানৰ সৰ্বোচ্চ শৃংগ আৰু এটা বিখ্যাত ষ্ট্ৰেটো আগ্নেয়গিৰি।

### Grasslands & Agricultural Belts — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/world-geography-sec/grasslands-agricultural-belts-world/
Summary: Practice grasslands & agricultural belts questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What are the grasslands?
A: Large areas covered with grasses, where rainfall is moderate.
Q: What are the temperate grasslands of North America called?
A: The Prairies.
Q: What are the temperate grasslands of South America called?
A: The Pampas.
Q: What are the temperate grasslands of Eurasia called?
A: The Steppes.
Q: What are the temperate grasslands of Australia called?
A: The Downs.
Q: What are the tropical grasslands of Africa called?
A: The Savanna.
Q: What are the tropical grasslands of South America called?
A: The Campos and the Llanos.
Q: What are the tropical grasslands of India called?
A: The savanna of the Deccan plateau.
Q: What is the 'steppe' climate?
A: A semi-arid climate of the temperate grasslands.
Q: Which is the largest temperate grassland of the world?
A: The Eurasian Steppe.
Q: What is the 'wheat belt' of the world?
A: The temperate grasslands of the Prairies, the Steppes and the Pampas.
Q: Which is the largest producer of wheat in the world?
A: China.
Q: Which is the largest producer of rice in the world?
A: China.
Q: What is the 'rice bowl' of the world?
A: The Mekong delta and the Indo-Gangetic plains.
Q: Which is the largest producer of cotton in the world?
A: China.
Q: Which is the largest producer of tea in the world?
A: China.
Q: Which is the largest producer of coffee in the world?
A: Brazil.
Q: Which is the largest producer of sugarcane in the world?
A: Brazil.
Q: What is the 'maize belt' of the world?
A: The Corn Belt of the USA.
Q: What is the 'banana republic'?
A: A country highly dependent on banana exports, like in Central America.
Q: Which is the largest producer of maize in the world?
A: The USA.
Q: What is the 'monoculture'?
A: The cultivation of a single crop over a large area.
Q: What is the 'plantation agriculture'?
A: Large-scale cultivation of a single cash crop, like tea, coffee and rubber.
Q: Which is the largest producer of rubber in the world?
A: Thailand.
Q: What is the 'slash and burn' agriculture?
A: A farming method where the forest is cut and burnt for cultivation.
Q: What is the 'shifting cultivation' of the North-East India called?
A: Jhum cultivation.
Q: Which is the largest producer of the pulses in the world?
A: India.
Q: What is the 'dairy belt' of the world?
A: The temperate regions of Europe, New Zealand and the USA.
Q: Which is the largest producer of the milk in the world?
A: India.
Q: What is the 'green revolution'?
A: The increase in food production using high-yielding varieties and fertilisers.
Q: What are the temperate grasslands and their local names?
A: Temperate grasslands lie in the middle latitudes and have fertile soil, making them major wheat-growing regions. They are known by different names in different continents - the Prairies in North America, the Steppes across Eurasia, the Pampas in Argentina, the Veld in South Africa, the Downs in Australia and the Canterbury grasslands in New Zealand. They all grow wheat and support sheep and cattle rearing.
Q: What are the tropical grasslands and where are they found?
A: Tropical grasslands, also called savanna, lie between the tropical rainforest and the hot desert and have a distinct wet and dry season. They are characterised by tall grasses and scattered trees such as the acacia and baobab. The Savanna of Africa is the largest and most famous, while in South America they are known as the Llanos in Venezuela and Colombia and the Campos in Brazil. They are used mainly for grazing.
Q: Which countries are the leading producers of major crops?
A: China and India are the leading producers of rice and wheat, while the United States is the largest producer of maize. Brazil leads in coffee and sugarcane, followed in coffee by Vietnam and Colombia. China and India are the top producers of tea, while Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia lead in rubber. China, India and the United States are important producers of cotton.
Q: What is shifting cultivation and plantation agriculture?
A: Shifting cultivation, also called slash-and-burn farming, is a primitive subsistence system in which a patch of forest is cleared, cultivated for a few years and then abandoned when fertility declines. Plantation agriculture is a single-crop commercial system found in the tropics, in which crops such as tea, coffee, rubber and sugarcane are grown on large estates, mainly for export.
Q: What are the main systems of farming in the world?
A: Farming is divided into subsistence and commercial types. Shifting cultivation and intensive subsistence farming are subsistence systems, with the latter common in monsoon Asia. Commercial grain farming is practised in the Prairies and Steppes, plantation agriculture grows a single crop in the tropics, mixed farming combines crops and livestock as in Europe, and nomadic herding is practised in the dry regions of Africa and Asia.
Q: নাতিশীতোষ্ণ তৃণভূমিবোৰ কি আৰু তেওঁলোকৰ স্থানীয় নাম কি কি?
A: নাতিশীতোষ্ণ তৃণভূমি মধ্য অক্ষাংশত থাকে আৰু ইয়াৰ মাটি উৰ্বৰ, সেয়ে এইবোৰ প্ৰধান গম উৎপাদন অঞ্চল। বিভিন্ন মহাদেশত ইহঁতক বিভিন্ন নামেৰে জনা যায় - উত্তৰ আমেৰিকাত প্ৰেৰী, ইউৰেছিয়াত ষ্টেপ, আৰ্জেণ্টিনাত পাম্পাছ, দক্ষিণ আফ্ৰিকাত ভেল্ড, অষ্ট্ৰেলিয়াত ডাউনছ আৰু নিউজিলেণ্ডত কেণ্টাৰবেৰী। এই সকলোবোৰত গম হয় আৰু ভেড়া-গৰু প্ৰজনন হয়।
Q: গ্ৰীষ্মমণ্ডলীয় তৃণভূমিবোৰ কি আৰু ক'ত পোৱা যায়?
A: গ্ৰীষ্মমণ্ডলীয় তৃণভূমি, যাক ছাভানাও বোলা হয়, গ্ৰীষ্মমণ্ডলীয় বৰষুণৰ বন আৰু বালিৰ মৰুভূমিৰ মাজত থাকে আৰু ইয়াৰ স্পষ্ট আৰ্দ্ৰ তথা শুকান ঋতু আছে। ইয়াৰ বৈশিষ্ট্য ওখ ঘাঁহ আৰু একেছিয়া, বাৱাবৰ দৰে বিচ্ছিন্ন গছ। আফ্ৰিকাৰ ছাভানা আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ আৰু প্ৰসিদ্ধ, আনহাতে দক্ষিণ আমেৰিকাত ভেনিজুৱেলা-কলম্বিয়াত ল্যান'ছ আৰু ব্ৰাজিলত কেম্প'ছ। এইবোৰ মূলতঃ চৰণৰ বাবে ব্যৱহৃত।
Q: প্ৰধান শস্যৰ আগশাৰীৰ উৎপাদক কোন কোন দেশ?
A: ধান আৰু গমৰ আগশাৰীৰ উৎপাদক চীন আৰু ভাৰত, আনহাতে মাকৈৰ বৃহত্তম উৎপাদক আমেৰিকা যুক্তৰাষ্ট্ৰ। কফি আৰু কুঁহিয়াৰত ব্ৰাজিল আগত, কফিত ইয়াৰ পিছত ভিয়েটনাম আৰু কলম্বিয়া। চাহৰ শীৰ্ষ উৎপাদক চীন আৰু ভাৰত, আনহাতে ৰবৰত থাইলেণ্ড, ইণ্ডোনেছিয়া আৰু মালয়েছিয়া আগত। কপাহৰ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ উৎপাদক চীন, ভাৰত আৰু আমেৰিকা যুক্তৰাষ্ট্ৰ।
Q: ছিফটিং খেতি আৰু বাগান কৃষি কি?
A: ছিফটিং খেতি, যাক জুই দি কাটি-জ্বলোৱা খেতিও বোলা হয়, এটা আদিম জীৱিকা পদ্ধতি, য'ত বনৰ এটা অংশ কাটি কেইবছৰ খেতি কৰি উৰ্বৰতা কমিলে এৰি দিয়া হয়। বাগান কৃষি গ্ৰীষ্মমণ্ডলত পোৱা একক-শস্য বাণিজ্যিক পদ্ধতি, য'ত চাহ, কফি, ৰবৰ আৰু কুঁহিয়াৰ ডাঙৰ খেতিপথাৰত মূলতঃ ৰপ্তানিৰ বাবে উৎপাদন কৰা হয়।
Q: বিশ্বত কৃষিৰ প্ৰধান পদ্ধতিসমূহ কি কি?
A: কৃষিক জীৱিকা আৰু বাণিজ্যিক প্ৰকাৰত ভগা হয়। ছিফটিং খেতি আৰু নিবিড় জীৱিকা খেতি জীৱিকা পদ্ধতি, য'ত দ্বিতীয়টো মৌচুমী এছিয়াত সাধাৰণ। বাণিজ্যিক শস্য খেতি প্ৰেৰী আৰু ষ্টেপত কৰা হয়, বাগান কৃষিয়ে গ্ৰীষ্মমণ্ডলত একক শস্য উৎপাদন কৰে, মিশ্ৰিত খেতিয়ে ইউৰোপৰ দৰে ঠাইত শস্য আৰু পশুধন একত্ৰে ৰাখে, আৰু যাযাবৰ পশুপালন আফ্ৰিকা আৰু এছিয়াৰ শুকান অঞ্চলত কৰা হয়।

### International Border Lines — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/world-geography-sec/international-border-lines-world/
Summary: Practice international border lines questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What is the 'Durand Line'?
A: The border between Afghanistan and Pakistan, drawn in 1893.
Q: What is the 'McMahon Line'?
A: The border between India and China in the eastern sector.
Q: Who drew the McMahon Line?
A: Sir Henry McMahon, in 1914.
Q: What is the 'Radcliffe Line'?
A: The border between India and Pakistan, drawn in 1947.
Q: Who drew the Radcliffe Line?
A: Sir Cyril Radcliffe.
Q: What is the 'Siegfried Line'?
A: The defensive line of Germany during the Second World War.
Q: What is the 'Maginot Line'?
A: The defensive line of France along the German border.
Q: What is the 'Hindenburg Line'?
A: The defensive line of Germany in the First World War.
Q: What is the '38th Parallel'?
A: The border between North Korea and South Korea.
Q: What is the '49th Parallel'?
A: The border between the USA and Canada.
Q: What is the '17th Parallel'?
A: The former border between North and South Vietnam.
Q: What is the 'Line of Control' (LOC)?
A: The de facto border between India and Pakistan in Kashmir.
Q: What is the 'Line of Actual Control' (LAC)?
A: The de facto border between India and China.
Q: What is the 'Golan Heights'?
A: A strategic plateau between Israel and Syria.
Q: What is the 'Mannerheim Line'?
A: The defensive line of Finland against the Soviet Union.
Q: What is the 'Oder-Neisse Line'?
A: The border between Germany and Poland, drawn in 1945.
Q: What is the 'Attaturk Line'?
A: The border between Turkey and the Soviet Union.
Q: What is the 'Curzon Line'?
A: The proposed border between Poland and the Soviet Union, named after Lord Curzon.
Q: What is the 'Blue Line' of Lebanon?
A: The border line between Lebanon and Israel.
Q: What is the 'Green Line' of Cyprus?
A: The buffer zone between the Greek and Turkish parts of Cyprus.
Q: What is the 'Purple Line' of 1967?
A: The ceasefire line between Israel and Syria.
Q: What is the 'Black Line'?
A: The line between the Hashemite Kingdom and Palestine (historic).
Q: What is the 'Mason-Dixon Line'?
A: The border between the US states of Pennsylvania and Maryland.
Q: What is the '24th Parallel'?
A: The border line that Pakistan claimed for the Sir Creek dispute.
Q: What is the 'Sixth Parallel'?
A: The border between the North and South of the former Sudan.
Q: Which line separates the USA from Mexico?
A: The Rio Grande border and the artificial line of 1848.
Q: What is the 'Palk Strait line'?
A: The maritime boundary between India and Sri Lanka.
Q: What is the 'Sunderbans border'?
A: The border between India and Bangladesh through the Sundarbans delta.
Q: What is the 'international date line'?
A: An imaginary line from pole to pole where the date changes by a day.
Q: What is the 'equator'?
A: The imaginary line at 0 degrees latitude dividing the Earth into the northern and southern hemispheres.
Q: What are the Durand Line, McMahon Line and Radcliffe Line?
A: The Durand Line is the boundary drawn in 1893 by Sir Mortimer Durand between British India and Afghanistan, and it now separates Afghanistan from Pakistan. The McMahon Line was drawn in 1914 at the Simla Convention by Sir Henry McMahon and makes up the India-China boundary. The Radcliffe Line was drawn in 1947 by Sir Cyril Radcliffe and divided British India into India and Pakistan.
Q: What is the difference between the Line of Control and the Line of Actual Control?
A: The Line of Control, or LoC, separates India and Pakistan in the disputed region of Kashmir and was formalised after the 1972 Simla Agreement. The Line of Actual Control, or LAC, is the de facto boundary between India and China. Both are important for India, but they involve different neighbours and different disputes, so they must not be confused with each other.
Q: What were the Maginot, Siegfried, Hindenburg and Mannerheim lines?
A: The Maginot Line was a strong line of French fortifications built along the border with Germany before the Second World War.
