The Siegfried Line, or Westwall, was the matching German defensive line facing France, and the Hindenburg Line was a major German defensive position in the First World War. The Mannerheim Line was the defensive line built by Finland against the Soviet Union.
Q: Which parallels divide which countries?
A: The 38th Parallel divides North Korea and South Korea, and the 17th Parallel once divided North Vietnam and South Vietnam. The 49th Parallel forms much of the boundary between the United States and Canada, and the 24th Parallel is associated with the India-Pakistan boundary in the Rann of Kutch. The 22nd Parallel forms part of the Egypt-Sudan boundary, and the Mason-Dixon Line came to symbolise the American North-South divide.
Q: What are the Green Line, Blue Line and Purple Line?
A: The Green Line is the United Nations buffer zone that divides Cyprus. The Blue Line is the boundary drawn by the United Nations between Lebanon and Israel, and the Purple Line is the 1967 ceasefire line between Israel and Syria. The Golan Heights, a strategically important plateau on the Israel-Syria border, is a well-known flashpoint in the region.
Q: দুৰাণ্ড ৰেখা, মেকমোহন ৰেখা আৰু ৰেডক্লিফ ৰেখা কি?
A: দুৰাণ্ড ৰেখা হৈছে ১৮৯৩ চনত ছাৰ মৰ্টিমাৰ দুৰাণ্ডে ব্ৰিটিছ ভাৰত আৰু আফগানিস্তানৰ মাজত আঁকা সীমা, যি আজি আফগানিস্তানক পাকিস্তানৰ পৰা পৃথক কৰে। মেকমোহন ৰেখা ১৯১৪ চনত চিমলা সন্মিলনত ছাৰ হেনৰী মেকমোহনে আঁকিছিল আৰু ই ভাৰত-চীন সীমা গঠন কৰে। ৰেডক্লিফ ৰেখা ১৯৪৭ চনত ছাৰ চিৰিল ৰেডক্লিফে আঁকিছিল আৰু ব্ৰিটিছ ভাৰতক ভাৰত আৰু পাকিস্তানত বিভক্ত কৰিছিল।
Q: নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ ৰেখা আৰু প্ৰকৃত নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ ৰেখাৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ ৰেখা, অৰ্থাৎ LoC, কাশ্মীৰৰ বিবাদিত অঞ্চলত ভাৰত আৰু পাকিস্তানক পৃথক কৰে আৰু ১৯৭২ চনৰ চিমলা চুক্তিৰ পিছত আনুষ্ঠানিক ৰূপ লয়। প্ৰকৃত নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ ৰেখা, অৰ্থাৎ LAC, ভাৰত আৰু চীনৰ মাজৰ ডি ফেক্ট' সীমা। দুয়োটা ভাৰতৰ বাবে গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ, কিন্তু ইহঁতৰ চুবুৰীয়া আৰু বিবাদ বেলেগ, সেয়ে ইহঁতক গুলিয়াই নলগাব।
Q: মেজিন', ছিগফ্ৰাইড, হিণ্ডেনবাৰ্গ আৰু মেনাৰহাইম ৰেখা কি আছিল?
A: মেজিন' ৰেখা দ্বিতীয় বিশ্বযুদ্ধৰ আগতে ফ্ৰান্সে জাৰ্মানীৰ সীমাত নিৰ্মাণ কৰা দুৰ্গসমূহৰ এক শক্তিশালী ৰেখা আছিল। ছিগফ্ৰাইড ৰেখা, বা ৱেষ্টৱাল, ফ্ৰান্সৰ মুখামুখি জাৰ্মান প্ৰতিৰক্ষা ৰেখা আছিল, আৰু হিণ্ডেনবাৰ্গ ৰেখা প্ৰথম বিশ্বযুদ্ধত জাৰ্মানীৰ এটা প্ৰধান প্ৰতিৰক্ষা স্থান আছিল। মেনাৰহাইম ৰেখা ফিনলেণ্ডে ছোভিয়েট ইউনিয়নৰ বিৰুদ্ধে নিৰ্মাণ কৰা প্ৰতিৰক্ষা ৰেখা আছিল।
Q: কোন সমান্তৰাল ৰেখাই কোন দেশক বিভক্ত কৰে?
A: ৩৮ সংখ্যাৰ সমান্তৰাল ৰেখাই উত্তৰ কোৰিয়া আৰু দক্ষিণ কোৰিয়াক বিভক্ত কৰে, আৰু ১৭ সংখ্যাৰ সমান্তৰাল ৰেখাই এবাৰ উত্তৰ ভিয়েটনাম আৰু দক্ষিণ ভিয়েটনামক বিভক্ত কৰিছিল। ৪৯ সংখ্যাৰ সমান্তৰাল ৰেখাই আমেৰিকা যুক্তৰাষ্ট্ৰ আৰু কানাডাৰ মাজৰ সীমাৰ বহুখিনি গঠন কৰে, আৰু ২৪ সংখ্যাৰ সমান্তৰাল ৰেখা ৰণ অৱ কচ্চত ভাৰত-পাকিস্তান সীমাৰ সৈতে জড়িত। ২২ সংখ্যাৰ সমান্তৰাল ৰেখা ইজিপ্ত-চুডান সীমাৰ এটা অংশ।
Q: সেউজ ৰেখা, নীলা ৰেখা আৰু বেঙুনীয়া ৰেখা কি?
A: সেউজ ৰেখা হৈছে ৰাষ্ট্ৰসংঘৰ বাফাৰ অঞ্চল, যি চাইপ্ৰাছক বিভক্ত কৰে। নীলা ৰেখা হৈছে ৰাষ্ট্ৰসংঘই লেবানন আৰু ইজৰাইলৰ মাজত আঁকা সীমা, আৰু বেঙুনীয়া ৰেখা হৈছে ইজৰাইল আৰু ছিৰিয়াৰ মাজৰ ১৯৬৭ চনৰ যুদ্ধবিৰতি ৰেখা। গোলান হাইটছ, ইজৰাইল-ছিৰিয়া সীমাৰ এটা কৌশলগতভাৱে গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ মালভূমি, এই অঞ্চলৰ এটা পৰিচিত সংঘাতস্থল।

### Minerals, Oil Belts & Major Sea Routes — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/world-geography-sec/minerals-oil-belts-sea-routes-world/
Summary: Practice minerals, oil belts & major sea routes questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: Which is the largest producer of coal in the world?
A: China.
Q: Which is the largest producer of iron ore in the world?
A: Australia.
Q: Which is the largest producer of petroleum in the world?
A: The USA.
Q: Which is the largest oil producing region of the world?
A: The Middle East (Persian Gulf).
Q: Which country has the largest oil reserves of the world?
A: Venezuela.
Q: What is OPEC?
A: The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries.
Q: When was OPEC founded?
A: In 1960.
Q: Where is the headquarters of OPEC?
A: In Vienna, Austria.
Q: Which is the largest producer of natural gas in the world?
A: The USA.
Q: Which is the largest producer of gold in the world?
A: China.
Q: Which is the largest producer of silver in the world?
A: Mexico.
Q: Which is the largest producer of bauxite in the world?
A: Australia.
Q: Which is the largest producer of copper in the world?
A: Chile.
Q: Which is the largest producer of diamond in the world by volume?
A: Russia.
Q: Which is the largest producer of manganese in the world?
A: South Africa.
Q: Which is the largest producer of uranium in the world?
A: Kazakhstan.
Q: What is the 'oil belt' of the world?
A: The Persian Gulf region of the Middle East.
Q: Which is the world's most important sea route?
A: The Suez Canal route connecting Europe and Asia.
Q: Which sea route connects the Atlantic with the Pacific through the Panama Canal?
A: The Panama route.
Q: Which is the busiest sea route of the world?
A: The North Atlantic route.
Q: What is the 'Cape route'?
A: The sea route around the Cape of Good Hope.
Q: Which is the world's busiest port?
A: The Shanghai port of China.
Q: Which is the largest port of the world by area?
A: The King Abdullah Port of Saudi Arabia.
Q: What is the 'Strait of Hormuz'?
A: The strategic strait connecting the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman.
Q: Why is the Strait of Hormuz important?
A: About 20% of the world's oil passes through it.
Q: Which is the largest oil importing country of the world?
A: China.
Q: What is the 'Arctic route'?
A: The sea route through the Arctic Ocean, made easier by global warming.
Q: Which is the largest producer of tin in the world?
A: China.
Q: Which is the largest producer of zinc in the world?
A: China.
Q: What is the 'Silk Road'?
A: The ancient trade route connecting China with Europe.
Q: Which countries are the leading producers of important minerals?
A: Australia and Brazil are leading producers of iron ore, along with China and India. China, India, the United States and Australia lead in coal production. Guinea, Australia, Brazil and China produce bauxite, the ore of aluminium. Chile is the largest producer of copper, while China, Russia and Australia lead in gold, and Russia and Botswana are important for diamonds.
Q: Where are the largest petroleum reserves and who are the leading producers?
A: The Persian Gulf region holds the largest petroleum reserves on Earth, and Saudi Arabia is one of the largest producers and exporters of oil. Other leading producers include the United States, Russia, Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Canada, Venezuela and Nigeria. Natural gas is produced in largest quantity by the United States and Russia, and OPEC coordinates the policies of many oil-exporting countries.
Q: What are the major oil belts of the world?
A: The major oil belts include the Persian Gulf belt, which is the largest of all; the North Sea belt between Britain and Norway; the Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean belt, where Venezuela's Lake Maracaibo is famous; the Nigeria belt in West Africa; the Ural-Volga and West Siberian belts of Russia; the Alaska belt; and the Gulf of Suez belt in Egypt.
Q: What are the major sea routes of the world and what do they connect?
A: The Suez Canal route links Europe with Asia through the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the Panama Canal route links the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans through Central America, and the Cape of Good Hope route goes around southern Africa towards Asia. The Strait of Malacca carries trade between the Indian Ocean and East Asia, and the Strait of Hormuz is vital for the export of Persian Gulf oil.
Q: Why are the Straits of Hormuz and Malacca so important?
A: The Strait of Hormuz is the outlet through which a large share of the world's petroleum from the Persian Gulf is exported, so any disruption there affects global oil supply. The Strait of Malacca is one of the busiest shipping lanes and carries much of the trade between the Indian Ocean and East Asia. Together with the Suez and Panama canals, these passages control a great part of world trade and are therefore of enormous strategic value.
Q: গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ খনিজৰ আগশাৰীৰ উৎপাদক কোন কোন দেশ?
A: অষ্ট্ৰেলিয়া আৰু ব্ৰাজিল লো-আকৰৰ আগশাৰীৰ উৎপাদক, লগতে চীন আৰু ভাৰত। কয়লা উৎপাদনত চীন, ভাৰত, আমেৰিকা যুক্তৰাষ্ট্ৰ আৰু অষ্ট্ৰেলিয়া আগত। গিনি, অষ্ট্ৰেলিয়া, ব্ৰাজিল আৰু চীনে বক্সাইট উৎপাদন কৰে। চিলি তামৰ বৃহত্তম উৎপাদক, আনহাতে চীন, ৰাছিয়া আৰু অষ্ট্ৰেলিয়া সোণত আৰু ৰাছিয়া তথা বটছৱানা হীৰাত গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ।
Q: আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ খাৰুৱা তেল ভাণ্ডাৰ ক'ত আৰু আগশাৰীৰ উৎপাদক কোন?
A: পাৰ্ছিয়ান উপসাগৰীয় অঞ্চলত পৃথিৱীৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ খাৰুৱা তেল ভাণ্ডাৰ আছে, আৰু ছৌদি আৰব তেলৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ উৎপাদক আৰু ৰপ্তানিকৰ্তাৰ এটা। আন আগশাৰীৰ উৎপাদকৰ ভিতৰত আমেৰিকা যুক্তৰাষ্ট্ৰ, ৰাছিয়া, ইৰাণ, ইৰাক, কুৱেইট, সংযুক্ত আৰব আমিৰশাহী, কানাডা, ভেনিজুৱেলা আৰু নাইজেৰিয়া। প্ৰাকৃতিক গেছ আটাইতকৈ বেছি আমেৰিকা যুক্তৰাষ্ট্ৰ আৰু ৰাছিয়াত উৎপাদন হয়, আৰু OPECএ বহু তেল-ৰপ্তানিকৰ্তা দেশৰ নীতি সমন্বয় কৰে।
Q: বিশ্বৰ প্ৰধান তেল বলয়সমূহ কি কি?
A: প্ৰধান তেল বলয়সমূহৰ ভিতৰত পাৰ্ছিয়ান উপসাগৰীয় বলয়, যি আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ; ব্ৰিটেইন আৰু নৰ্ৱেৰ মাজৰ উত্তৰ সাগৰীয় বলয়; মেক্সিকো উপসাগৰ আৰু কেৰিবিয়ান বলয়, য'ত ভেনিজুৱেলাৰ লেক মাৰাকাইব' বিখ্যাত; পশ্চিম আফ্ৰিকাৰ নাইজেৰিয়া বলয়; ৰাছিয়াৰ ইউৰাল-ভলগা আৰু পশ্চিম ছাইবেৰিয়া বলয়; আলাস্কা বলয়; আৰু ইজিপ্তৰ ছুৱেজ উপসাগৰীয় বলয় অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত।
Q: বিশ্বৰ প্ৰধান সাগৰীয় পথসমূহ কি আৰু ইহঁতে কি জোৰে?
A: ছুৱেজ খাল পথে ভূমধ্যসাগৰ আৰু ৰঙা সাগৰৰ মাজেৰে ইউৰোপক এছিয়াৰ সৈতে জোৰে, পানামা খাল পথে মধ্য আমেৰিকাৰ মাজেৰে আটলান্টিক আৰু প্ৰশান্ত মহাসাগৰক জোৰে, আৰু গুড হ'প ৰাশিৰ পথে দক্ষিণ আফ্ৰিকাক আগুৰি এছিয়ালৈ যায়। মালাক্কা প্ৰণালীয়ে ভাৰত মহাসাগৰ আৰু পূব এছিয়াৰ মাজৰ বাণিজ্য কঢ়িয়াই নিয়ে, আৰু হৰমুজ প্ৰণালী পাৰ্ছিয়ান উপসাগৰৰ তেল ৰপ্তানিৰ বাবে গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ।
Q: হৰমুজ আৰু মালাক্কা প্ৰণালী ইমান গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ কিয়?
A: হৰমুজ প্ৰণালী হৈছে সেই পথ, যাৰ মাজেৰে পাৰ্ছিয়ান উপসাগৰৰ পৰা বিশ্বৰ এক বৃহৎ অংশ খাৰুৱা তেল ৰপ্তানি হয়, সেয়ে তাত যিকোনো বিঘিনি বিশ্বৰ তেল যোগানত প্ৰভাৱ পেলায়। মালাক্কা প্ৰণালী বিশ্বৰ ব্যস্ততম জাহাজ চলাচল পথৰ এটা আৰু ভাৰত মহাসাগৰ তথা পূব এছিয়াৰ মাজৰ বহু বাণিজ্য কঢ়িয়াই নিয়ে। ছুৱেজ আৰু পানামা খালৰ সৈতে এই পথসমূহে বিশ্ব বাণিজ্যৰ এটা ডাঙৰ অংশ নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ কৰে আৰু সেয়ে অসীম কৌশলগত মূল্যৰ।

### Mountains, Deserts, Islands & Earthquakes — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/world-geography-sec/mountains-deserts-islands-earthquakes/
Summary: Practice mountains, deserts, islands & earthquakes questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: What are the three types of mountains?
A: Fold, block and volcanic mountains.
Q: Which is the longest mountain range on land?
A: The Andes of South America.
Q: What is the length of the Andes?
A: About 7,000 kilometres.
Q: Which is the highest mountain range of the world?
A: The Himalayas.
Q: Which is the highest mountain peak of the world?
A: Mount Everest, at 8,848 metres.
Q: Which is the highest peak of Africa?
A: Mount Kilimanjaro, at 5,895 metres.
Q: Which is the highest peak of North America?
A: Mount Denali (McKinley), at 6,190 metres.
Q: Which is the highest peak of South America?
A: Aconcagua, at 6,961 metres.
Q: Which is the highest peak of Australia?
A: Mount Kosciuszko, at 2,228 metres.
Q: Which is the highest peak of Europe?
A: Mount Elbrus, at 5,642 metres.
Q: Which is the highest peak of Antarctica?
A: Mount Vinson, at 4,892 metres.
Q: What is a desert?
A: An area with very low rainfall, less than 25 cm per year.
Q: Which is the largest hot desert of the world?
A: The Sahara desert of Africa.
Q: What is the area of the Sahara desert?
A: About 9 million square kilometres.
Q: Which is the largest cold desert of the world?
A: The Antarctic desert.
Q: Which is the largest desert of Asia?
A: The Gobi desert.
Q: Which is the largest desert of India?
A: The Thar desert of Rajasthan.
Q: Which is the largest island of the world?
A: Greenland.
Q: Which is the largest island of Asia?
A: Borneo.
Q: Which is the second largest island of the world?
A: New Guinea.
Q: Which is the largest island of India?
A: Middle Andaman island.
Q: Which is the largest archipelago of the world?
A: Indonesia.
Q: What is an earthquake?
A: The shaking of the Earth's surface due to the movement of the tectonic plates.
Q: What is the instrument used to measure earthquakes?
A: The seismograph.
Q: What is the scale used to measure the magnitude of an earthquake?
A: The Richter scale.
Q: What is the point of origin of an earthquake inside the Earth called?
A: The focus (hypocentre).
Q: What is the point on the surface directly above the focus called?
A: The epicentre.
Q: Which is the most earthquake-prone zone of India?
A: The North-Eastern region (Zone V).
Q: What is a tsunami?
A: A series of giant ocean waves caused by an underwater earthquake.
Q: What is the 'Richter scale'?
A: A logarithmic scale used to measure the magnitude of earthquakes.
Q: What are the main types of mountains with examples?
A: Mountains are of four main types. Fold mountains form when plates collide and squeeze rock into folds, as in the Himalayas, Andes, Rockies and Alps. Block mountains form when a block of land is uplifted between faults, as in the Vosges and Black Forest. Volcanic mountains are built of lava and ash, such as Mount Fuji and Kilimanjaro. Residual or erosional mountains are worn-down remains such as the Aravalli, Vindhya and Appalachian ranges.
Q: Which are the largest and driest deserts in the world?
A: The Sahara in Africa is the largest hot desert in the world. The Atacama in Chile is considered the driest place on Earth. Cold deserts include the Gobi in Asia and the polar desert of Antarctica, and Antarctica is the largest desert of all if cold deserts are counted. Hot deserts have high daytime temperatures while cold deserts have low temperatures and lie in continental interiors or near the poles.
Q: What is the difference between focus, epicentre and seismic waves?
A: The focus is the point inside the Earth where an earthquake originates, and the epicentre is the point directly above it on the surface, where the shaking is strongest. Energy travels as seismic waves - P-waves are primary, longitudinal and the fastest; S-waves are secondary and transverse and cannot pass through liquids; and surface or L-waves are the slowest but the most destructive. Earthquakes are recorded by a seismograph.
Q: What is the Richter scale and which belt has the most earthquakes?
A: The Richter scale measures the magnitude, or energy, of an earthquake, while the Modified Mercalli scale measures its intensity, or the damage it causes. About 90 per cent of the world's earthquakes occur in the Circum-Pacific belt, also called the Ring of Fire, which encircles the Pacific Ocean. A tsunami is a giant sea wave usually triggered by an undersea earthquake.
Q: Which is the largest island and the largest archipelago in the world?
A: Greenland is the largest island in the world, while Indonesia is the largest archipelago, that is, the largest group of islands. Continental islands such as Great Britain and Sri Lanka lie on the continental shelf, while oceanic islands such as the Hawaiian islands and the Maldives are volcanic or coral in origin. The Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep belong to India.
Q: পৰ্বতৰ মূল প্ৰকাৰসমূহ উদাহৰণসহ কি কি?
A: পৰ্বত চাৰিটা মূল প্ৰকাৰৰ। প্লেট সংঘৰ্ষ কৰি শিল ভাঁজ হৈ ভাঁজ পৰ্বত গঠন হয়, যেনে হিমালয়, এণ্ডেছ, ৰকি আৰু আল্পছ। দুটা ফল্টৰ মাজত এটা অংশ ওপৰলৈ উঠি ব্লক পৰ্বত গঠন হয়, যেনে ভ'জেছ আৰু ব্লেক ফৰেষ্ট। লাভা আৰু ছাইৰে আগ্নেয় পৰ্বত গঠন হয়, যেনে মাউণ্ট ফুজি আৰু কিলিমাঞ্জাৰো। ক্ষয়প্ৰাপ্ত অৱশিষ্ট পৰ্বতৰ ভিতৰত আৰাবল্লী, বিন্ধ্য আৰু আপালেছিয়ান আছে।
Q: বিশ্বৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ আৰু সৰ্বাধিক শুকান মৰুভূমি কোনটো?
A: আফ্ৰিকাৰ চাহাৰা বিশ্বৰ বৃহত্তম উষ্ণ মৰুভূমি। চিলিৰ আটাকামা পৃথিৱীৰ সৰ্বাধিক শুকান ঠাই বুলি গণ্য কৰা হয়। শীতল মৰুভূমিৰ ভিতৰত এছিয়াৰ গোবি আৰু এণ্টাৰ্কটিকাৰ মেৰু মৰুভূমি আছে, আৰু শীতল মৰুভূমি ধৰিলে এণ্টাৰ্কটিকা আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ মৰুভূমি। উষ্ণ মৰুভূমিৰ দিনত উষ্ণতা বেছি আৰু শীতল মৰুভূমি মহাদেশৰ অন্তৰ্ভাগত বা মেৰুৰ ওচৰত থাকে।
Q: উৎস, উপকেন্দ্ৰ আৰু ভূকম্পীয় তৰংগৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: উৎস হৈছে পৃথিৱীৰ ভিতৰত ভূমিকম্প আৰম্ভ হোৱা বিন্দু, আৰু উপকেন্দ্ৰ হৈছে তাৰ ঠিক ওপৰত পৃষ্ঠৰ বিন্দু, য'ত কম্পন আটাইতকৈ বেছি। শক্তি ভূকম্পীয় তৰংগ হিচাপে যায় - P-তৰংগ প্ৰাথমিক, অনুদৈৰ্ঘ্য আৰু দ্ৰুততম; S-তৰংগ দ্বিতীয়, অনুপ্ৰস্থ আৰু তৰলৰ মাজেৰে যাব নোৱাৰে; আৰু পৃষ্ঠ বা L-তৰংগ ধীৰ কিন্তু আটাইতকৈ ধ্বংসাত্মক। ভূমিকম্প ছিজম'গ্ৰাফেৰে লিপিবদ্ধ কৰা হয়।
Q: ৰিখটাৰ স্কেল কি আৰু কোনটো বলয়ত আটাইতকৈ বেছি ভূমিকম্প হয়?
A: ৰিখটাৰ স্কেলে ভূমিকম্পৰ তীব্ৰতা বা শক্তি জোখে, আনহাতে পৰিৱৰ্তিত মাৰ্কেলি স্কেলে ইয়াৰ প্ৰাবল্য বা ক্ষতি জোখে। বিশ্বৰ প্ৰায় ৯০ শতাংশ ভূমিকম্প প্ৰশান্ত মহাসাগৰীয় বলয়ত, অৰ্থাৎ ফায়াৰ ৰিংত ঘটে, যি প্ৰশান্ত মহাসাগৰক আগুৰি আছে। ছুনামি হৈছে সাগৰৰ তলৰ ভূমিকম্পৰ পৰা সৃষ্টি হোৱা বিশাল সাগৰীয় ঢৌ।
Q: বিশ্বৰ বৃহত্তম দ্বীপ আৰু বৃহত্তম দ্বীপপুঞ্জ কোনটো?
A: গ্ৰীণলেণ্ড বিশ্বৰ বৃহত্তম দ্বীপ, আনহাতে ইণ্ডোনেছিয়া বৃহত্তম দ্বীপপুঞ্জ, অৰ্থাৎ দ্বীপৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ সমষ্টি। বৃহৎ ব্ৰিটেইন আৰু শ্ৰীলংকাৰ দৰে মহাদেশীয় দ্বীপ মহাদেশীয় তাকৰাত থাকে, আনহাতে হাৱাই আৰু মালদ্বীপৰ দৰে মহাসাগৰীয় দ্বীপ আগ্নেয় বা প্ৰৱাল উৎপত্তিৰ। আন্দামান-নিকোবৰ আৰু লাক্ষাদ্বীপ ভাৰতৰ অন্তৰ্গত।

### Oceans, Currents, Trenches & Rivers/Lakes — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/world-geography-sec/oceans-currents-trenches-rivers-lakes/
Summary: Practice oceans, currents, trenches & rivers/lakes questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: How many oceans are there in the world?
A: Five oceans.
Q: Which is the largest ocean of the world?
A: The Pacific Ocean.
Q: What is the area of the Pacific Ocean?
A: About 165 million square kilometres.
Q: Which is the second largest ocean of the world?
A: The Atlantic Ocean.
Q: Which is the third largest ocean of the world?
A: The Indian Ocean.
Q: Which is the smallest ocean of the world?
A: The Arctic Ocean.
Q: Which is the deepest ocean of the world?
A: The Pacific Ocean.
Q: What is the deepest point of the world's oceans?
A: The Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean.
Q: What is the depth of the Mariana Trench?
A: About 10,994 metres.
Q: What is the 'Challenger Deep'?
A: The deepest point of the Mariana Trench.
Q: Which is the deepest trench of the Indian Ocean?
A: The Java (Sunda) Trench.
Q: What is an ocean current?
A: The continuous movement of ocean water in a definite direction.
Q: Which is the largest warm ocean current?
A: The Gulf Stream.
Q: Which is the largest cold ocean current?
A: The West Wind Drift (Antarctic Circumpolar).
Q: Which current affects the climate of India?
A: The Indian Ocean monsoon currents and the El Nino effect.
Q: Which is the longest river of the world?
A: The Nile river of Africa.
Q: What is the length of the Nile river?
A: About 6,650 kilometres.
Q: Which is the largest river of the world by discharge?
A: The Amazon river of South America.
Q: Which is the largest river basin of the world?
A: The Amazon basin.
Q: Which river is the longest of South America?
A: The Amazon river.
Q: Which is the longest river of Asia?
A: The Yangtze river of China.
Q: Which is the longest river of Europe?
A: The Volga river of Russia.
Q: Which is the longest river of North America?
A: The Mississippi-Missouri river system.
Q: Which is the largest lake of the world?
A: The Caspian Sea.
Q: Which is the largest freshwater lake of the world?
A: Lake Superior in North America.
Q: Which is the deepest lake of the world?
A: Lake Baikal in Russia.
Q: What is the depth of Lake Baikal?
A: About 1,642 metres.
Q: Which is the highest lake of the world?
A: Lake Titicaca, in the Andes (about 3,812 metres).
Q: Which is the largest lake of Africa?
A: Lake Victoria.
Q: Which river is the source of the Nile?
A: The White Nile and the Blue Nile.
Q: Which is the largest, deepest, smallest and shallowest ocean?
A: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, covering about one third of the Earth's surface, and it contains the Mariana Trench, whose deepest point is the Challenger Deep at about 11,034 metres. The Atlantic is the second largest and the Indian is the third. The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and shallowest, while the Southern Ocean surrounds Antarctica.
Q: What are warm and cold ocean currents with examples?
A: Warm currents flow from near the equator towards the poles and raise the temperature of the coasts they touch; the Gulf Stream and the Kuroshio are examples. Cold currents flow from higher latitudes towards the equator and lower coastal temperatures; the Labrador, Canary and Benguela are examples. The meeting zones of warm and cold currents are the richest fishing grounds in the world, and fog commonly forms there.
Q: Which is the longest river and the largest river in the world?
A: The Nile in Africa is generally regarded as the longest river in the world at about 6,650 kilometres. The Amazon in South America is the largest river by volume of water, or discharge, and has the largest drainage basin, carrying about one fifth of all fresh water entering the oceans. The Ganga-Brahmaputra delta is the largest delta in the world.
Q: What is the difference between a trench and a ridge?
A: A trench is a narrow, very deep depression in the ocean floor, usually formed where an oceanic plate subducts beneath another plate, and the Mariana Trench is the deepest. A mid-oceanic ridge is a long underwater mountain system built at divergent boundaries where new crust forms, such as the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. The ridge system is the longest mountain range on Earth.
Q: Which are the largest, deepest and lowest lakes in the world?
A: The Caspian Sea is the largest lake in the world, though it is called a sea because of its size and salinity. Lake Baikal in Russia is the deepest lake and the largest freshwater lake by volume, while Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake by surface area. The Dead Sea is the lowest point on land and one of the saltiest water bodies, and Lake Titicaca in the Andes is the highest navigable lake.
Q: আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ, গভীৰতম, সৰু আৰু পাতলতম মহাসাগৰ কোনটো?
A: প্ৰশান্ত মহাসাগৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ আৰু গভীৰতম মহাসাগৰ, যি পৃথিৱীৰ পৃষ্ঠৰ প্ৰায় এটা তৃতীয়াংশ আগুৰি আছে, আৰু ইয়াত মাৰিয়ানা খাত আছে, যাৰ গভীৰতম বিন্দু চেলেঞ্জাৰ ডিপ প্ৰায় ১১,০৩৪ মিটাৰ। আটলান্টিক দ্বিতীয় বৃহত্তম আৰু ভাৰত মহাসাগৰ তৃতীয়। উত্তৰ মহাসাগৰ আটাইতকৈ সৰু আৰু পাতলতম, আনহাতে দক্ষিণ মহাসাগৰে এণ্টাৰ্কটিকাক আগুৰি আছে।
Q: উষ্ণ আৰু শীতল সাগৰীয় সোঁতৰ উদাহৰণসহ ব্যাখ্যা কৰক।
A: উষ্ণ সোঁত বিষুৱৰেখাৰ ওচৰৰ পৰা মেৰুলৈ বৈ যায় আৰু যি উপকূল স্পৰ্শ কৰে তাৰ উষ্ণতা বঢ়ায়; গুলফ ষ্ট্ৰিম আৰু কুৰোশিঅ' উদাহৰণ। শীতল সোঁত উচ্চ অক্ষাংশৰ পৰা বিষুৱৰেখালৈ বৈ যায় আৰু উপকূলৰ উষ্ণতা কমায়; লেব্ৰাডৰ, কেনেৰী আৰু বেংগুৱেলা উদাহৰণ। উষ্ণ আৰু শীতল সোঁত লগ লাগা অঞ্চল বিশ্বৰ আটাইতকৈ ধনী মাছ ধৰা ঠাই, আৰু তাত কুঁৱলী সাধাৰণ।
Q: বিশ্বৰ দীঘলতম আৰু বৃহত্তম নদী কোনটো?
A: আফ্ৰিকাৰ নীল নদীক সাধাৰণতে বিশ্বৰ দীঘলতম নদী হিচাপে গণ্য কৰা হয়, যাৰ দীঘ প্ৰায় ৬,৬৫০ কিলোমিটাৰ। দক্ষিণ আমেৰিকাৰ আমাজন পানীৰ পৰিমাণ বা প্ৰবাহৰ ফালৰ পৰা বৃহত্তম নদী আৰু বৃহত্তম জলাশয়ৰ গৰাকী, যি সাগৰত পৰা মুঠ মিঠা পানীৰ প্ৰায় পাঁচ ভাগৰ এভাগ কঢ়িয়াই আনে। গংগা-ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ বদ্বীপ বিশ্বৰ বৃহত্তম বদ্বীপ।
Q: খাত আৰু শিখৰৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: খাত হৈছে সাগৰীয় তলৰ এটা সংকীৰ্ণ, অতি গভীৰ অৱনমন, যি সাধাৰণতে এটা মহাসাগীয় প্লেট আনখনৰ তলত অধোগমন কৰিলে গঠন হয়, আৰু মাৰিয়ানা খাত আটাইতকৈ গভীৰ। মধ্য-মহাসাগৰীয় শিখৰ হৈছে অপসাৰী সীমান্তত নতুন ভূত্বক গঠন হোৱা ঠাইত গঢ়ি উঠা দীঘল পানীৰ তলৰ পৰ্বতমালা, যেনে মধ্য-আটলান্টিক শিখৰ। শিখৰ ব্যৱস্থা পৃথিৱীৰ দীঘলতম পৰ্বতমালা।
Q: বিশ্বৰ বৃহত্তম, গভীৰতম আৰু নিম্নতম হ্ৰদ কোনটো?
A: কাস্পিয়ান সাগৰ বিশ্বৰ বৃহত্তম হ্ৰদ, যদিও আকাৰ আৰু লৱণতাৰ বাবে ইয়াক সাগৰ বোলা হয়। ৰাছিয়াৰ বাইকাল হ্ৰদ গভীৰতম হ্ৰদ আৰু আয়তনৰ ফালৰ পৰা বৃহত্তম মিঠা পানীৰ হ্ৰদ, আনহাতে ছুপিৰিয়ৰ হ্ৰদ পৃষ্ঠকালিৰ ফালৰ পৰা বৃহত্তম মিঠা পানীৰ হ্ৰদ। মৃত সাগৰ স্থলত আটাইতকৈ নিম্ন বিন্দু তথা আটাইতকৈ লৱণীয় জলাশয়ৰ এটা, আৰু এণ্ডেছৰ টিটিকাকা হ্ৰদ সৰ্বোচ্চ নৌচলাচলযোগ্য হ্ৰদ।

### Straits, Canals, Seas & Gulfs — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/geography/world-geography-sec/straits-canals-seas-gulfs/
Summary: Practice straits, canals, seas & gulfs questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What is a strait?
A: A narrow waterway connecting two large water bodies.
Q: Which is the widest strait of the world?
A: The Davis Strait.
Q: Which strait separates India from Sri Lanka?
A: The Palk Strait.
Q: Which strait separates the North and South islands of New Zealand?
A: The Cook Strait.
Q: Which strait separates Sumatra and Malaysia?
A: The Strait of Malacca.
Q: Which strait connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Atlantic Ocean?
A: The Strait of Gibraltar.
Q: Which strait separates Asia from North America?
A: The Bering Strait.
Q: Which strait separates the Black Sea from the Sea of Marmara?
A: The Bosporus Strait.
Q: Which strait separates the Red Sea from the Gulf of Aden?
A: The Bab-el-Mandeb Strait.
Q: What is a canal?
A: An artificial waterway built for navigation and irrigation.
Q: Which canal connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea?
A: The Suez Canal.
Q: When was the Suez Canal opened?
A: In 1869.
Q: What is the length of the Suez Canal?
A: About 193 kilometres.
Q: Which country is the Suez Canal in?
A: Egypt.
Q: Which canal connects the Atlantic Ocean with the Pacific Ocean?
A: The Panama Canal.
Q: When was the Panama Canal opened?
A: In 1914.
Q: What is the length of the Panama Canal?
A: About 82 kilometres.
Q: Which is the largest sea of the world?
A: The South China Sea.
Q: Which is the largest inland sea of the world?
A: The Caspian Sea.
Q: Which is the saltiest sea of the world?
A: The Dead Sea.
Q: Which sea is known as the 'Dead Sea'?
A: The lake between Israel and Jordan, with very high salinity.
Q: Which is the largest gulf of the world?
A: The Gulf of Mexico.
Q: Which is the largest gulf of India?
A: The Gulf of Khambhat (Cambay).
Q: Which gulf separates Arabia from Iran?
A: The Persian Gulf.
Q: Which bay is the largest bay of the world?
A: The Bay of Bengal.
Q: Which gulf is between India and Myanmar?
A: The Bay of Bengal.
Q: Which is the largest gulf of the Indian Ocean?
A: The Bay of Bengal (largest bay).
Q: Which canal is the 'Venice of the East' known for?
A: The Alappuzha backwaters of Kerala.
Q: What is the 'Eight Degree Channel'?
A: The channel separating the Minicoy island from the Maldives.
Q: Which channel separates the Andaman and Nicobar islands?
A: The Ten Degree Channel.
Q: What is a strait and which are the most important straits?
A: A strait is a narrow channel of water that joins two larger water bodies and separates two land masses. Important straits include the Strait of Gibraltar, which links the Atlantic Ocean with the Mediterranean Sea and separates Europe from Africa; the Bosphorus, which links the Black Sea with the Sea of Marmara; the Strait of Hormuz, the world's most important oil route; the Strait of Malacca, one of the busiest shipping lanes; and the Palk Strait, which separates India from Sri Lanka.
Q: What are the differences between the Suez Canal and the Panama Canal?
A: The Suez Canal in Egypt, opened in 1869, joins the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea and gives the shortest sea route between Europe and Asia; it has no locks because both seas are at the same level. The Panama Canal, opened in 1914, joins the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans and uses a system of locks because of the difference in water levels. The Grand Canal of China is the longest man-made waterway in the world.
Q: Which seas are the warmest, saltiest and least salty?
A: The Red Sea, between Africa and the Arabian Peninsula, is one of the warmest and saltiest open seas in the world. The Baltic Sea has very low salinity because of the large amount of fresh water flowing into it. The Dead Sea is technically a lake and one of the saltiest water bodies, while the Mediterranean Sea lies between Europe, Africa and Asia and connects to the Atlantic through the Strait of Gibraltar.
Q: What is the difference between a gulf and a bay?
A: A gulf is a large area of a sea or ocean that is partly surrounded by land, and a bay is similar but usually smaller. The Gulf of Mexico is the largest gulf in the world, and the Bay of Bengal is the largest bay. The Persian Gulf is famous for its petroleum reserves, and the Gulf of Aden and the Gulf of Oman are also important for shipping and oil transport.
Q: Why are straits and canals strategically important?
A: Straits and canals are narrow passages through which ships must travel, so they control trade routes and the movement of navies. The Strait of Hormuz carries much of the world's oil, and the Suez and Panama canals greatly shorten sea journeys between oceans, saving time and cost. Because of this, such waterways have enormous economic and strategic importance, and countries often compete to control them.
Q: প্ৰণালী কি আৰু আটাইতকৈ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ প্ৰণালীবোৰ কোনটো?
A: প্ৰণালী হৈছে দুটা ডাঙৰ জলাশয়ক সংযোগ কৰা আৰু দুখন স্থলভাগক পৃথক কৰা এটা সংকীৰ্ণ জলপথ। গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ প্ৰণালীৰ ভিতৰত জিব্ৰাল্টাৰ প্ৰণালী, যি আটলান্টিক মহাসাগৰক ভূমধ্যসাগৰৰ সৈতে জোৰে আৰু ইউৰোপক আফ্ৰিকাৰ পৰা পৃথক কৰে; বসফৰাছ, যি কৃষ্ণ সাগৰক মাৰ্মাৰা সাগৰৰ সৈতে জোৰে; হৰমুজ প্ৰণালী, বিশ্বৰ আটাইতকৈ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ তেল পথ; মালাক্কা প্ৰণালী, ব্যস্ততম পথৰ এটা; আৰু পাল্ক প্ৰণালী, যি ভাৰতক শ্ৰীলংকাৰ পৰা পৃথক কৰে।
Q: ছুৱেজ খাল আৰু পানামা খালৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: ইজিপ্তৰ ছুৱেজ খাল, ১৮৬৯ চনত খোলা, ভূমধ্যসাগৰক ৰঙা সাগৰৰ সৈতে জোৰে আৰু ইউৰোপ-এছিয়াৰ মাজত আটাইতকৈ চুটি সাগৰীয় পথ দিয়ে; দুই সাগৰৰ স্তৰ একে হোৱা বাবে ইয়াত লক নাই। পানামা খাল, ১৯১৪ চনত খোলা, আটলান্টিক আৰু প্ৰশান্ত মহাসাগৰক জোৰে আৰু পানীৰ স্তৰৰ পাৰ্থক্যৰ বাবে লক ব্যৱস্থা ব্যৱহাৰ কৰে। চীনৰ মহান খাল বিশ্বৰ দীঘলতম মানৱ-নিৰ্মিত জলপথ।
Q: কোন সাগৰ আটাইতকৈ উষ্ণ, লৱণীয় আৰু কম লৱণীয়?
A: আফ্ৰিকা আৰু আৰব উপদ্বীপৰ মাজৰ ৰঙা সাগৰ বিশ্বৰ আটাইতকৈ উষ্ণ আৰু লৱণীয় মুক্ত সাগৰৰ এটা। বাল্টিক সাগৰৰ লৱণতা অতি কম, কাৰণ ইয়ালৈ বহু মিঠা পানী আহে। মৃত সাগৰ কাৰিকৰীভাৱে এটা হ্ৰদ আৰু আটাইতকৈ লৱণীয় জলাশয়ৰ এটা, আনহাতে ভূমধ্যসাগৰ ইউৰোপ, আফ্ৰিকা আৰু এছিয়াৰ মাজত আছে আৰু জিব্ৰাল্টাৰৰ মাজেৰে আটলান্টিকৰ সৈতে সংযুক্ত।
Q: উপসাগৰ আৰু উপহ্ৰদৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: উপসাগৰ হৈছে সাগৰ বা মহাসাগৰৰ এটা বৃহৎ অংশ, যি আংশিকভাৱে স্থলভাগেৰে আগুৰা, আৰু উপহ্ৰদ একেধৰণৰ কিন্তু সাধাৰণতে সৰু। মেক্সিকো উপসাগৰ বিশ্বৰ বৃহত্তম উপসাগৰ, আৰু বংগোপসাগৰ বৃহত্তম উপহ্ৰদ। পাৰ্ছিয়ান উপসাগৰ ইয়াৰ খাৰুৱা তেল ভাণ্ডাৰৰ বাবে বিখ্যাত, আৰু এডেন তথা ওমান উপসাগৰ জাহাজ চলাচল আৰু তেল পৰিবহণৰ বাবে গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ।
Q: প্ৰণালী আৰু খাল কৌশলগতভাৱে গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ কিয়?
A: প্ৰণালী আৰু খাল সংকীৰ্ণ পথ, যাৰ মাজেৰে জাহাজ চলিব লাগে, সেয়ে এইবোৰে বাণিজ্য পথ আৰু নৌসেনাৰ গতিবিধি নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ কৰে। হৰমুজ প্ৰণালীয়ে বিশ্বৰ বহু তেল কঢ়িয়াই নিয়ে, আৰু ছুৱেজ তথা পানামা খালে মহাসাগৰৰ মাজৰ সাগৰীয় যাত্ৰা বহু চুটি কৰে, সময় আৰু খৰচ সাঁচে। এইবাবে এনে জলপথৰ অৰ্থনৈতিক আৰু কৌশলগত গুৰুত্ব অপৰিসীম, আৰু দেশসমূহে প্ৰায়ে ইহঁত নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ কৰিবলৈ প্ৰতিযোগিতা কৰে।

### Ancient Indian Art, Architecture & Literature — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/ancient-indian-history-sec/ancient-art-arch-lit/
Summary: Practice ancient indian art, architecture & literature questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual.
Q: Who originally built the famous Sanchi stupa?
A: Ashoka the Great, as a brick stupa.
Q: Which is the most famous and best-preserved stupa of India?
A: The Great Stupa at Sanchi (Madhya Pradesh).
Q: Which dynasty enlarged and renovated the Sanchi stupa?
A: The Sungas, who added the stone railing and the gateways.
Q: What are the four toranas (gateways) of Sanchi famous for?
A: Their exquisite narrative sculptures depicting Jataka stories.
Q: The sculptures of the Bharhut stupa belong to which period?
A: The Sunga period (2nd century BC).
Q: Which famous stupa of Andhra Pradesh was built in the Satavahana period?
A: The Amaravati stupa.
Q: Which school of art is known for its Greco-Roman influence?
A: The Gandhara school.
Q: Where did the Gandhara school of art flourish?
A: In the north-western region - Taxila, Peshawar and the Kabul valley.
Q: Which stone was used by the artists of the Gandhara school?
A: Grey-blue schist stone.
Q: Which school of art was indigenous and used red sandstone?
A: The Mathura school of art.
Q: Where was the Mathura school of art centred?
A: At Mathura (Uttar Pradesh).
Q: Which Kushan ruler patronised both the Gandhara and Mathura schools?
A: Kanishka.
Q: Which school of art flourished in the Andhra region?
A: The Amravati school (at Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda).
Q: What are the Ajanta caves famous for?
A: Their magnificent Buddhist paintings (frescoes) and sculptures.
Q: When were the Ajanta caves discovered by the British?
A: In 1819, by a British army officer John Smith.
Q: Which painting of Ajanta cave 1 is world-famous?
A: The Padmapani (Bodhisattva) painting.
Q: Where are the Bagh caves located and what are they famous for?
A: In Madhya Pradesh, famous for their ancient Buddhist paintings.
Q: Which cave in Tamil Nadu is famous for its Jaina paintings?
A: The Sittanavasal cave.
Q: Who built the Kailasa temple at Ellora?
A: The Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I (8th century AD).
Q: What makes the Kailasa temple at Ellora unique?
A: It is a monolithic rock-cut temple - the largest such temple in the world, carved out of a single rock.
Q: Where is the famous Trimurti sculpture located?
A: In the Elephanta caves (near Mumbai).
Q: What does the Elephanta Trimurti depict?
A: The three-faced figure of Shiva (Mahesh), showing his three aspects.
Q: Which are the two main styles of Indian temple architecture?
A: The Nagara style (northern) and the Dravida style (southern); the Vesara is the hybrid Chalukyan style.
Q: Which Gupta temple at Deogarh represents the Nagara style?
A: The Dashavatara temple.
Q: Which style does the Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram represent?
A: The Dravida style.
Q: What is the basic feature of a Dravida temple?
A: The pyramidal storeyed tower called the Vimana, above the sanctum.
Q: Which Jaina caves of Odisha are associated with king Kharavela?
A: The Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves.
Q: Who wrote the Ramayana?
A: Maharshi Valmiki.
Q: Why is the Ramayana called the 'Adi Kavya'?
A: Because it is regarded as the first poem (Kavya) of Sanskrit literature.
Q: Who wrote the Mahabharata?
A: Maharshi Vyasa (Vedavyasa).
Q: How many parvas does the Mahabharata contain?
A: Eighteen (18) parvas.
Q: What is the Mahabharata sometimes called?
A: The fifth Veda, because of its immense size and importance.
Q: Who wrote the Natyashastra, the treatise on drama?
A: Bharata Muni.
Q: Who wrote the Ashtadhyayi, the famous Sanskrit grammar?
A: Panini.
Q: Who is the traditional author of the Manusmriti?
A: Manu.
Q: What are the Jataka tales?
A: Buddhist stories about the previous births of the Buddha, which teach moral lessons.
Q: Who wrote the Arthashastra?
A: Kautilya (Chanakya).
Q: Who wrote the Charaka Samhita?
A: Charaka, the ancient physician.
Q: Who is regarded as the father of Indian surgery?
A: Sushruta.
Q: Which text did Sushruta write?
A: The Sushruta Samhita, dealing with surgery.
Q: Who wrote the Panchatantra?
A: Vishnusharma.
Q: What is the Sangam literature?
A: Ancient Tamil literature composed in the assemblies (Sangams) at Madurai, between about 300 BC and 300 AD.
Q: What are the two famous Tamil epics?
A: Shilappadikaram by Ilango Adigal and Manimekalai by Sattanar.
Q: Who wrote the Mrichchakatika (The Little Clay Cart)?
A: King Shudraka.
Q: Who wrote the Swapnavasavadatta?
A: Bhasa, one of the earliest Sanskrit dramatists.
Q: Which is the most celebrated play of Kalidasa?
A: Abhijnanasakuntalam.
Q: Who wrote the Kiratarjuniya?
A: Bharavi.
Q: Who wrote the Dashakumaracharita?
A: Dandin.
Q: Which great Indian contribution in mathematics is world-renowned?
A: The invention of the zero and the decimal place-value system.
Q: Who wrote the Brahmasphutasiddhanta?
A: Brahmagupta (in 628 AD).
Q: Who wrote the Gita Govinda?
A: Jayadeva, a poet of the 12th century, depicting the love of Krishna and Radha.
Q: Which two schools of art flourished in the Kushan period?
A: The two great schools of art of the Kushan period were the Gandhara school and the Mathura school. The Gandhara school used grey schist and showed Greco-Buddhist influence, while the Mathura school used spotted red sandstone and a more Indian style.
Q: Which Mauryan pillar capital is the national emblem of India?
A: The Sarnath Lion Capital, a polished monolithic stone pillar capital of Ashoka, is the national emblem of India. It is one of the finest examples of Mauryan court art.
Q: What are the three styles of Indian temple architecture?
A: The three main styles of Indian temple architecture are the Nagara style of the north (with a curved shikhara), the Dravida style of the south (with a pyramidal vimana and gopuram) and the Vesara style of the Deccan, which blends both. The Dashavatara temple at Deogarh is an early Nagara example.
Q: Where are the famous ancient Indian paintings found?
A: The most famous ancient Indian paintings are the Ajanta cave paintings, which show scenes from the Jataka tales and reached their peak in the Gupta period. The Bagh caves also have important paintings.
Q: Who wrote the Abhijnanashakuntalam and who wrote the Arthashastra?
A: Abhijnanashakuntalam was written by Kalidasa, the greatest Sanskrit poet and dramatist. The Arthashastra, a treatise on statecraft and administration, was written by Kautilya (Chanakya).
Q: Which are the great works of Tamil Sangam literature?
A: The great works of Tamil Sangam literature include the Tolkappiyam (a work on grammar), the Thirukkural of Thiruvalluvar, and the epics Silappadikaram and Manimekalai. They are among the oldest works of Tamil literature.
Q: কুশান কালত কোন দুটা শিল্পশৈলী বিকশিত হৈছিল?
A: কুশান কালৰ দুটা মহান শিল্পশৈলী আছিল গান্ধাৰ শৈলী আৰু মথুৰা শৈলী। গান্ধাৰ শৈলীয়ে ধূসৰ স্কিষ্ট ব্যৱহাৰ কৰি গ্ৰীক-বৌদ্ধ প্ৰভাৱ দেখুৱাইছিল, আনহাতে মথুৰা শৈলীয়ে চিতা থকা ৰঙা বেলেপাথৰ আৰু অধিক ভাৰতীয় ধৰণ ব্যৱহাৰ কৰিছিল।
Q: কোন মৌৰ্য স্তম্ভ শীৰ্ষ ভাৰতৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় প্ৰতীক?
A: অশোকৰ একশিলা মসৃণ শিলৰ স্তম্ভ শীৰ্ষ সাৰনাথ সিংহ শীৰ্ষ ভাৰতৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় প্ৰতীক। ই মৌৰ্য দৰবাৰ কলাৰ এটা শ্ৰেষ্ঠ উদাহৰণ।
Q: ভাৰতীয় মন্দিৰ স্থাপত্যৰ তিনিটা শৈলী কি?
A: ভাৰতীয় মন্দিৰ স্থাপত্যৰ তিনিটা মূল শৈলী হ'ল উত্তৰৰ নাগৰ শৈলী (বক্ৰ শিখৰসহ), দক্ষিণৰ দ্ৰাবিড় শৈলী (পিৰামিডীয় ৱিমান আৰু গোপুৰমসহ) আৰু দাক্ষিণাত্যৰ ৱেসৰ শৈলী, যি দুয়োটাৰ মিশ্ৰণ। দেৱগড়ৰ দশাৱতাৰ মন্দিৰ এটা প্ৰাৰম্ভিক নাগৰ উদাহৰণ।
Q: বিখ্যাত প্ৰাচীন ভাৰতীয় চিত্ৰ ক'ত পোৱা যায়?
A: আটাইতকৈ বিখ্যাত প্ৰাচীন ভাৰতীয় চিত্ৰ অজন্তা গুহাৰ চিত্ৰ, যিয়ে জাতক কাহিনীৰ দৃশ্য দেখুৱায় আৰু গুপ্ত যুগত শিখৰত উপনীত হৈছিল। বাঘ গুহাতো গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ চিত্ৰ আছে।
Q: অভিজ্ঞানশকুন্তলম কোনে লিখিছিল আৰু অৰ্থশাস্ত্ৰ কোনে লিখিছিল?
A: অভিজ্ঞানশকুন্তলম শ্ৰেষ্ঠ সংস্কৃত কবি আৰু নাট্যকাৰ কলিদাসে লিখিছিল। ৰাজনীতি আৰু প্ৰশাসন সম্পৰ্কীয় অৰ্থশাস্ত্ৰ কৌটিল্যই (চাণক্য) লিখিছিল।
Q: তামিল সংগম সাহিত্যৰ মহান ৰচনাসমূহ কি কি?
A: তামিল সংগম সাহিত্যৰ মহান ৰচনাসমূহৰ ভিতৰত তোলকাপ্পিয়ম (ব্যাকৰণৰ ৰচনা), তিৰুৱল্লুৱাৰৰ তিৰুক্কুৰল, আৰু মহাকাব্য শিলপ্পদিকাৰম আৰু মণিমেকলাই আছে। এইবোৰ তামিল সাহিত্যৰ আটাইতকৈ প্ৰাচীন ৰচনা।

### Ancient Indian History — 350 Practice Questions | ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/ancient-indian-history-sec/ancient-india/
Summary: 350 ancient Indian history questions with answers for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Covers the Indus Valley, Vedic age, Mauryas, Guptas, Buddhism and Jainism.
Q: Which period does ancient Indian history cover?
A: It covers the period from prehistoric times up to about the eighth century CE, ending with the decline of the later Guptas.
Q: Who founded the Mauryan empire?
A: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan empire around 322 BCE with the help of Chanakya, also called Kautilya.
Q: Why is the Gupta period called the golden age?
A: Because of major achievements in art, architecture, mathematics, astronomy and Sanskrit literature, including the works of Kalidasa and the discoveries of Aryabhata.

### Gupta Empire Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/ancient-indian-history-sec/gupta-empire/
Summary: Practice gupta empire questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Who founded the Gupta dynasty?
A: Chandragupta I (ruled about 319-335 AD).
Q: When did the Gupta era begin?
A: In 319-320 AD, with the accession of Chandragupta I.
Q: Whom did Chandragupta I marry?
A: Kumaradevi, a princess of the Lichchhavis.
Q: What title did Chandragupta I assume?
A: Maharajadhiraja (king of kings).
Q: Who was the greatest ruler of the Gupta dynasty?
A: Samudragupta (335-380 AD).
Q: Who described Samudragupta as the 'Napoleon of India'?
A: The historian V. A. Smith.
Q: Which inscription records the conquests of Samudragupta?
A: The Allahabad Pillar inscription (Prayag Prashasti).
Q: Who composed the Prayag Prashasti?
A: Harishena, the court poet of Samudragupta.
Q: How did Samudragupta treat the kings of Aryavarta (the north)?
A: He uprooted nine kings and annexed their kingdoms.
Q: How did Samudragupta treat the kings of Dakshinapatha (the south)?
A: He defeated twelve kings but restored their kingdoms, following the policy of Dharma-vijaya.
Q: Which sacrifice did Samudragupta perform?
A: The Ashvamedha sacrifice, to proclaim his supremacy.
Q: What title did Samudragupta take because of his poetic talent?
A: Kaviraja (king of poets).
Q: Which types of coins did Samudragupta issue?
A: Gold coins of many types - the standard, archer, battle-axe and Ashvamedha types.
Q: Who succeeded Samudragupta?
A: His son Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya).
Q: Which Saka ruler was defeated by Chandragupta II?
A: Rudrasimha III, ending the Saka rule in western India.
Q: What title did Chandragupta II assume?
A: Vikramaditya.
Q: Which Chinese pilgrim visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II?
A: Fahien (Fa-Hien), in about 399-414 AD.
Q: What did Fahien write?
A: Fo-Kwo-Ki (A Record of Buddhist Kingdoms).
Q: What did Fahien observe about the Gupta administration?
A: The people were prosperous and happy; there were no severe punishments and no poll tax.
Q: What is the iron pillar at Mehrauli (Delhi) famous for?
A: Its rust-resistant iron; it bears an inscription of Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya).
Q: Who were the Navaratnas (Nine Gems) of the court of Chandragupta II?
A: Nine great scholars including Kalidasa, Varahamihira, Aryabhata, Dhanvantari, Amarasimha and Vararuchi.
Q: Which great poet adorned the court of Chandragupta II?
A: Kalidasa.
Q: Which famous play did Kalidasa write?
A: Abhijnanasakuntalam (The Recognition of Shakuntala).
Q: What are the other major works of Kalidasa?
A: Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava, Meghaduta, Vikramorvasiyam and Malavikagnimitra.
Q: Who wrote the Panchatantra?
A: Vishnusharma.
Q: Who wrote the Kamasutra?
A: Vatsyayana.
Q: Who wrote the Amarakosha (the famous Sanskrit lexicon)?
A: Amarasimha.
Q: Who composed the Aryabhatiya?
A: Aryabhata, in 499 AD.
Q: Who wrote the Brihatsamhita?
A: Varahamihira.
Q: Which university was founded by Kumaragupta I?
A: The Nalanda University (Bihar).
Q: Who repulsed the first Huna invasion?
A: Skandagupta.
Q: Who was the last great ruler of the Gupta dynasty?
A: Skandagupta (455-467 AD).
Q: What title did Skandagupta assume?
A: Vikramaditya.
Q: Which Gupta ruler repaired the Sudarshana lake?
A: Skandagupta, through his governor Parnadatta, as recorded in the Junagadh inscription.
Q: Which inscription provides the first evidence of sati in India?
A: The Eran inscription of 510 AD (of Bhanugupta).
Q: What was the administrative structure of the Gupta empire?
A: The empire was divided into Bhukti (province), Vishaya (district) and Grama (village); the Vishayapati headed a district.
Q: Who was the head of a Gupta district called?
A: Vishayapati.
Q: What were the land grants to Brahmins called in the Gupta period?
A: Agrahara grants (and Devagraha for temples).
Q: Which type of gold coins did the Guptas issue?
A: Gold dinara coins.
Q: Which period is called the 'Golden Age' of ancient India?
A: The Gupta period (4th-6th century AD).
Q: Why is the Gupta age called the 'Golden Age'?
A: Because of remarkable progress in art, architecture, literature, science, and all-round prosperity.
Q: Which rock-cut caves belong to the Gupta period?
A: The Udayagiri caves (Vidisha) and the early Ajanta paintings.
Q: Which famous temple at Deogarh belongs to the Gupta period?
A: The Dashavatara temple.
Q: Which brick temple of the Gupta period is located at Bhitargaon?
A: The Bhitargaon temple, built of brick with terracotta panels.
Q: Which religion was mainly revived under the Guptas?
A: Brahmanism, especially Vaishnavism and Shaivism.
Q: What were the main reasons for the decline of the Gupta empire?
A: Huna invasions, weak successors, the rise of feudatories and administrative decline.
Q: Which Huna rulers weakened the Gupta empire in its last phase?
A: Toramana and his son Mihirakula.
Q: Which city was the capital of the Gupta empire?
A: Pataliputra (with Ujjain as an important cultural centre).
Q: Who is regarded as the greatest Sanskrit dramatist of ancient India?
A: Kalidasa.
Q: Which Gupta ruler's coins depict him as a musician playing the veena?
A: Samudragupta (the 'lyrist' type of his gold coins).
Q: Who founded the Gupta Empire and when did the Gupta era begin?
A: The Gupta Empire was founded by Chandragupta I (c. 319-335 AD), who took the title Maharajadhiraja and started the Gupta era in 319-320 AD. The earlier rulers Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha were his ancestors.
Q: Why is Samudragupta called the Napoleon of India?
A: Samudragupta greatly expanded the Gupta Empire through many conquests, and the historian V. A. Smith called him the "Napoleon of India". His campaigns are recorded in the Prayag (Allahabad) Prashasti composed by his court poet Harisena.
Q: Who was the greatest Gupta ruler and what were his achievements?
A: Chandragupta II, also called Vikramaditya, was the greatest Gupta ruler. He defeated the Western Kshatrapas and took the title Sakari, annexed Gujarat and Ujjain, and patronised the Navratna (nine gems), including Kalidasa. The Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during his reign.
Q: Why is the Gupta period called the Golden Age of India?
A: The Gupta period saw outstanding achievements in art, architecture, literature, science and mathematics. Kalidasa wrote great Sanskrit works, Aryabhata and Varahamihira advanced astronomy, Nalanda University was founded, and temples such as the Dashavatara temple at Deogarh and the Ajanta paintings were created.
Q: Who founded Nalanda University and who repelled the Hunas?
A: Kumaragupta I founded the great university of Nalanda. Skandagupta, the last great Gupta ruler, successfully repelled the Hunas (White Huns).
Q: How was Gupta administration different from Mauryan administration?
A: Mauryan administration was highly centralised, while Gupta administration was more decentralised. The Guptas divided the empire into bhuktis (provinces) and vishayas (districts), gave generous land grants, and relied on officials such as the Uparika, Vishayapati, kumaramatyas and ayuktakas.
Q: গুপ্ত সাম্ৰাজ্য কোনে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল আৰু গুপ্ত যুগ কেতিয়া আৰম্ভ হৈছিল?
A: গুপ্ত সাম্ৰাজ্য চন্দ্ৰগুপ্ত প্ৰথমে (প্ৰায় খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দ ৩১৯-৩৩৫) প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল, যিয়ে মহাৰাজাধিৰাজ উপাধি গ্ৰহণ কৰিছিল আৰু খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দ ৩১৯-৩২০ চনত গুপ্ত যুগ আৰম্ভ কৰিছিল। তেওঁৰ পূৰ্বপুৰুষ শ্ৰীগুপ্ত আৰু ঘটোৎকচ আছিল।
Q: সমুদ্ৰগুপ্তক কিয় ভাৰতৰ নেপোলিয়ন কোৱা হয়?
A: সমুদ্ৰগুপ্তই বহু বিজয়ৰ জৰিয়তে গুপ্ত সাম্ৰাজ্য বহু পৰিমাণে বিস্তাৰ কৰিছিল, আৰু ইতিহাসবিদ ভি. এ. স্মিথে তেওঁক "ভাৰতৰ নেপোলিয়ন" বুলি অভিহিত কৰিছিল। তেওঁৰ অভিযান তেওঁৰ ৰাজসভাৰ কবি হৰিষেণে ৰচনা কৰা প্ৰয়াগ (এলাহাবাদ) প্রশস্তিত লিপিবদ্ধ।
Q: শ্ৰেষ্ঠ গুপ্ত শাসক কোন আছিল আৰু তেওঁৰ অৰ্জন কি আছিল?
A: চন্দ্ৰগুপ্ত দ্বিতীয়, যাক বিক্ৰমাদিত্যও কোৱা হয়, শ্ৰেষ্ঠ গুপ্ত শাসক আছিল। তেওঁ পশ্চিম ক্ষত্ৰপসকলক পৰাস্ত কৰি শকাৰি উপাধি গ্ৰহণ কৰিছিল, গুজৰাট আৰু উজ্জয়িনী অধিগ্ৰহণ কৰিছিল, আৰু কলিদাসকে ধৰি নৱৰত্নক পৃষ্ঠপোষকতা কৰিছিল। তেওঁৰ ৰাজত্বকালত চীনা তীৰ্থযাত্ৰী ফা-হিয়েনে ভাৰত ভ্ৰমণ কৰিছিল।
Q: গুপ্ত কালক কিয় ভাৰতৰ সুৱৰ্ণ যুগ কোৱা হয়?
A: গুপ্ত কালত কলা, স্থাপত্য, সাহিত্য, বিজ্ঞান আৰু গণিতত অসাধাৰণ অৰ্জন হৈছিল। কলিদাসে মহান সংস্কৃত ৰচনা লিখিছিল, আৰ্যভট আৰু বৰাহমিহিৰে জ্যোতিৰ্বিজ্ঞান আগবঢ়াইছিল, নালন্দা বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় প্ৰতিষ্ঠা হৈছিল, আৰু দেৱগড়ৰ দশাৱতাৰ মন্দিৰ তথা অজন্তা চিত্ৰ সৃষ্টি হৈছিল।
Q: নালন্দা বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় কোনে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল আৰু হূণসকলক কোনে প্ৰতিহত কৰিছিল?
A: কুমাৰগুপ্ত প্ৰথমে মহান নালন্দা বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল। স্কন্দগুপ্ত, শেষ মহান গুপ্ত শাসক, সফলভাৱে হূণ (বগা হূণ)সকলক প্ৰতিহত কৰিছিল।
Q: গুপ্ত প্ৰশাসন মৌৰ্য প্ৰশাসনৰ পৰা কেনেকৈ ভিন্ন আছিল?
A: মৌৰ্য প্ৰশাসন অতি কেন্দ্ৰীভূত আছিল, আনহাতে গুপ্ত প্ৰশাসন অধিক বিকেন্দ্ৰীভূত আছিল। গুপ্তসকলে সাম্ৰাজ্যক ভুক্তি (প্ৰদেশ) আৰু বিষয় (জিলা)ত বিভক্ত কৰিছিল, উদাৰ ভূমি অনুদান দিছিল, আৰু উপৰিক, বিষয়পতি, কুমাৰমাত্য আৰু আয়ুক্তকৰ দৰে বিষয়াৰ ওপৰত নিৰ্ভৰ কৰিছিল।

### Indus Valley Civilization — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/ancient-indian-history-sec/indus-valley-civilization/
Summary: Practice indus valley civilization questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What is another name of the Indus Valley Civilization?
A: Harappan Civilization, named after the site of Harappa.
Q: Which is considered the first urban civilization of India?
A: The Indus Valley (Harappan) Civilization.
Q: When and by whom was Harappa first excavated?
A: In 1921 by Daya Ram Sahni.
Q: When and by whom was Mohenjo-daro discovered?
A: In 1922 by R. D. Banerjee.
Q: Who announced the discovery of the Indus Valley Civilization in 1924?
A: John Marshall, the then Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India.
Q: Who first used the name 'Indus Valley Civilization'?
A: John Marshall.
Q: What is the generally accepted date of the Mature Harappan phase?
A: About 2500 BC to 1750 BC.
Q: On which river is Harappa situated?
A: The Ravi river (Punjab, Pakistan).
Q: On which river is Mohenjo-daro situated?
A: The Indus river (Sindh, Pakistan).
Q: Which is the largest site of the Harappan civilization?
A: Mohenjo-daro.
Q: Which is the largest Harappan site located in India?
A: Rakhigarhi (Haryana).
Q: Which is the westernmost site of the Harappan civilization?
A: Sutkagendor (Balochistan, Pakistan).
Q: Which is the easternmost site of the Harappan civilization?
A: Alamgirpur (Uttar Pradesh).
Q: Which is the northernmost site of the Harappan civilization?
A: Manda (Jammu and Kashmir).
Q: Which is the southernmost site of the Harappan civilization?
A: Daimabad (Maharashtra).
Q: Which Harappan site is famous for its dockyard?
A: Lothal (Gujarat).
Q: What was the main building material of the Harappan cities?
A: Burnt (baked) bricks, usually in the ratio 4:2:1.
Q: What were the main features of Harappan town planning?
A: Grid pattern, streets crossing at right angles, and covered drainage system.
Q: Which structure of Mohenjo-daro proves the water management skill of the Harappans?
A: The Great Bath.
Q: With what is the 'Great Granary' associated?
A: Public granaries built at Harappa and Mohenjo-daro for storing grain.
Q: At which site was the bronze 'Dancing Girl' statue found?
A: Mohenjo-daro.
Q: At which site was the steatite 'Priest King' statue found?
A: Mohenjo-daro.
Q: At which site was the famous 'Pashupati seal' discovered?
A: Mohenjo-daro.
Q: What does the 'Pashupati seal' depict?
A: A three-faced seated figure surrounded by animals, identified as a proto-Shiva.
Q: What was the nature of the Harappan script?
A: It was pictographic and has not yet been deciphered.
Q: In which direction was the Harappan script generally written?
A: Generally from right to left.
Q: Which material was mainly used for making Harappan seals?
A: Steatite (soapstone).
Q: What was the main purpose of the Harappan seals?
A: Trade purposes and sealing of goods; they also served as amulets.
Q: What system of weights did the Harappans use?
A: The binary system - 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32... using cubical chert weights.
Q: Which metal was unknown to the Harappan people?
A: Iron.
Q: Which metals were most commonly used by the Harappans?
A: Copper and bronze; gold and silver were also known.
Q: The Harappans were the first in the world to cultivate which crop?
A: Cotton.
Q: Which were the two main crops of the Harappans?
A: Wheat and barley; rice was also grown at Lothal and Rangpur.
Q: At which Harappan sites was evidence of rice cultivation found?
A: Lothal and Rangpur (Gujarat).
Q: Which animal was not known to the Harappans?
A: The horse.
Q: Which site provides the earliest evidence of a ploughed field?
A: Kalibangan (Rajasthan).
Q: In which state and on which river is Kalibangan situated?
A: In Rajasthan, on the banks of the Ghaggar river.
Q: Which Harappan site is famous for its water reservoirs and signboard?
A: Dholavira (Gujarat).
Q: Where is Dholavira located?
A: On the Khadir Bet island in the Rann of Kutch, Gujarat.
Q: Which Harappan site is famous as a bead-making centre?
A: Chanhu-daro (Sindh, Pakistan).
Q: At which site was a terracotta model of a ship found?
A: Lothal.
Q: Who claimed to have found horse bones at Surkotada?
A: A. K. Sharma.
Q: At which site was a bronze model of a chariot found?
A: Daimabad (Maharashtra).
Q: What were the main occupations of the Harappan people?
A: Agriculture, animal husbandry, trade, crafts and industry.
Q: With which foreign land did the Harappans trade?
A: Mesopotamia (modern Iraq); the Indus region was called 'Meluhha' there.
Q: What is 'Meluhha' in Mesopotamian records?
A: The name given to the Indus region in Mesopotamian inscriptions.
Q: What evidence proves the foreign trade of the Harappans?
A: Harappan seals found in Mesopotamia and Mesopotamian seals and weights at Harappan sites.
Q: Did the Harappans have temples?
A: No evidence of a temple or idol worship has been found.
Q: Which animals are commonly depicted on the Harappan seals?
A: Humped bull, unicorn, elephant, rhinoceros and tiger.
Q: What was the general plan of the Harappan cities?
A: A higher citadel in the west and a lower town in the east.
Q: What do the covered drains of Mohenjo-daro indicate?
A: An advanced system of sanitation and public hygiene.
Q: Which deities were mainly worshipped by the Harappans?
A: The Mother Goddess and a male deity (proto-Shiva).
Q: What are the possible reasons for the decline of the Harappan civilization?
A: Floods, climate change, drying up of the Ghaggar and ecological factors; the old 'Aryan invasion' theory is now rejected.
Q: What is another name of the Indus Valley Civilization?
A: It is also called the Harappan Civilization, after Harappa, the first site to be excavated.
Q: When and by whom was Harappa first excavated?
A: Harappa was first excavated in 1921 by Daya Ram Sahni.
Q: Which is the largest site of the Harappan civilization?
A: Mohenjo-daro is the largest site of the civilization, while Rakhigarhi is the largest Harappan site located in India.
Q: Which metal was unknown to the Harappans?
A: Iron was unknown to the Harappans. They used copper and bronze, and also knew gold and silver.
Q: What is the evidence of Harappan foreign trade?
A: Harappan seals found in Mesopotamia, and Mesopotamian seals and weights found at Harappan sites, prove their foreign trade. The Indus region was called Meluhha in Mesopotamian records.
Q: Why did the Indus Valley Civilization decline?
A: It declined around 1900 BC, probably because of floods, climate change and the drying up of the Ghaggar; the old 'Aryan invasion' theory is now rejected.
Q: সিন্ধু সভ্যতাৰ আন এটা নাম কি?
A: ইয়াক হৰপ্পা সভ্যতাও বোলা হয়, কাৰণ প্ৰথম খনন কৰা স্থান আছিল হৰপ্পা।
Q: হৰপ্পা পোনপটীয়াকৈ কেতিয়া আৰু কাৰ দ্বাৰা খনন হৈছিল?
A: হৰপ্পা ১৯২১ চনত দয়া ৰাম সাহনীয়ে পোনপটীয়াকৈ খনন কৰিছিল।
Q: হৰপ্পা সভ্যতাৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ স্থান কোনটো?
A: মহেঞ্জোদাৰো সভ্যতাৰ আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ স্থান, আনহাতে ৰাখীগড়ী ভাৰতত অৱস্থিত আটাইতকৈ ডাঙৰ হৰপ্পা স্থান।
Q: হৰপ্পাবাসীৰ বাবে কোন ধাতু অজ্ঞাত আছিল?
A: লো হৰপ্পাবাসীৰ বাবে অজ্ঞাত আছিল। তেওঁলোকে তাম আৰু ব্ৰঞ্জ ব্যৱহাৰ কৰিছিল, আৰু সোণ-ৰূপো জানিছিল।
Q: হৰপ্পাৰ বিদেশী বাণিজ্যৰ প্ৰমাণ কি?
A: মেছ'পটেমিয়াত পোৱা হৰপ্পা মোহৰ, আৰু হৰপ্পা স্থানত পোৱা মেছ'পটেমিয়াৰ মোহৰ আৰু ওজন, তেওঁলোকৰ বিদেশী বাণিজ্যৰ প্ৰমাণ। মেছ'পটেমিয়াৰ তথ্যত সিন্ধু অঞ্চলক মেলুহা বোলা হৈছিল।
Q: সিন্ধু সভ্যতা কিয় লয় পাইছিল?
A: ই প্ৰায় খ্ৰীষ্টপূৰ্ব ১৯০০ চনত লয় পাইছিল, সম্ভৱতঃ বানপানী, জলবায়ু পৰিৱৰ্তন আৰু ঘগ্গৰ শুকাই যোৱাৰ বাবে; পুৰণি 'আৰ্য্য আক্রমণ' তত্ত্ব এতিয়া নাকচ কৰা হৈছে।

### Rise of Jainism & Buddhism — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/ancient-indian-history-sec/jainism-buddhism/
Summary: Practice rise of jainism & buddhism questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Who was the founder of Jainism in its present form (the 24th Tirthankara)?
A: Mahavira (Vardhamana).
Q: How many Tirthankaras are there in Jainism?
A: 24 Tirthankaras.
Q: Who was the first Tirthankara of Jainism?
A: Rishabhanatha (Adinatha).
Q: Who was the 23rd Tirthankara of Jainism?
A: Parshvanatha.
Q: Where was Mahavira born?
A: At Kundagrama (Kundalpur), near Vaishali in Bihar.
Q: What was the childhood name of Mahavira?
A: Vardhamana.
Q: Who were the parents of Mahavira?
A: Father Siddhartha and mother Trishala.
Q: To which clan did Mahavira belong?
A: The Jnatrika clan, a Kshatriya clan of the Lichchhavis.
Q: At what age did Mahavira renounce the world?
A: At the age of 30.
Q: What is 'Kevala Jnana' in Jainism?
A: The supreme and perfect knowledge attained by Mahavira.
Q: Where did Mahavira attain Kaivalya (enlightenment)?
A: On the bank of the Rijupalika river under a Sal tree, near Jambhikagrama.
Q: Where did Mahavira deliver his first sermon?
A: At Pava.
Q: Where did Mahavira die?
A: At Pava (Bihar).
Q: At what age did Mahavira die?
A: At 72; the Jaina tradition places his death in 527 BC.
Q: What are the five vows (Anuvratas) of Jainism?
A: Ahimsa (non-violence), Satya (truth), Asteya (non-stealing), Brahmacharya (celibacy) and Aparigraha (non-possession).
Q: Which vow did Mahavira add to the four vows of Parshvanatha?
A: Brahmacharya (celibacy).
Q: What are the three Jewels (Triratna) of Jainism?
A: Right faith (Samyak Darshana), right knowledge (Samyak Jnana) and right conduct (Samyak Charitra).
Q: Which doctrine of Jainism says that reality is many-sided?
A: Anekantavada.
Q: Which doctrine of Jainism is the theory of conditional predication?
A: Syadvada.
Q: Why was Mahavira called 'Nirgrantha'?
A: Because he was free from all bonds and attachments.
Q: Who was the chief disciple (Ganadhara) of Mahavira?
A: Indrabhuti Gautama.
Q: In which language were the Jaina canon (Svetambara Agamas) written?
A: In Ardhamagadhi Prakrit.
Q: What are the two main sects of Jainism?
A: Digambara (sky-clad) and Svetambara (white-clad).
Q: At which council did the Digambara-Svetambara split take place?
A: At the Pataliputra council (3rd century BC), under the leadership of Bhadrabahu.
Q: Who led the Jaina monks from Magadha to Karnataka?
A: Bhadrabahu.
Q: Where was the first Jaina council held?
A: At Pataliputra, under Sthulabhadra.
Q: Where and when was the second Jaina council held?
A: At Vallabhi (Gujarat), in the 5th century AD.
Q: Which famous Jaina statue is located at Shravanabelagola?
A: The Gommateshwara (Bahubali) statue.
Q: Who was the founder of Buddhism?
A: Gautama Buddha.
Q: When and where was Gautama Buddha born?
A: Around 563 BC at Lumbini, near Kapilavastu (Nepal).
Q: Who were the parents of Gautama Buddha?
A: King Suddhodana and Queen Mahamaya.
Q: To which clan did Buddha belong?
A: The Shakya (Sakya) clan.
Q: What were the names of Buddha's wife and son?
A: Yashodhara and Rahul.
Q: At what age did Buddha leave his home?
A: At the age of 29.
Q: What is the 'Mahabhinishkramana'?
A: The Great Renunciation - Buddha's departure from his home in search of truth.
Q: Where did Buddha attain enlightenment?
A: At Bodh Gaya, under the Bodhi (peepal) tree on the bank of the river Niranjana.
Q: Where did Buddha deliver his first sermon?
A: At Sarnath (Deer Park), near Varanasi.
Q: What is the first sermon of Buddha called?
A: Dharmachakra Pravartana (Turning of the Wheel of Law).
Q: Where did Buddha die?
A: At Kushinagar (Uttar Pradesh).
Q: What is the 'Mahaparinirvana'?
A: The final passing away of Buddha at Kushinagar at the age of 80 (about 483 BC).
Q: Who offered Buddha his last meal?
A: Chunda, a blacksmith.
Q: What are the Four Noble Truths of Buddhism?
A: Dukkha (suffering), Samudaya (cause of suffering), Nirodha (cessation) and Magga (the path to cessation).
Q: What are the components of the Eightfold Path?
A: Right views, right resolve, right speech, right conduct, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness and right concentration.
Q: What is the 'Middle Path' in Buddhism?
A: The path that avoids the extremes of self-indulgence and self-mortification.
Q: What are the Three Jewels (Triratna) of Buddhism?
A: Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha.
Q: Who were the two chief disciples of Buddha?
A: Sariputta and Moggallana.
Q: Who was the personal attendant of Buddha?
A: Ananda.
Q: What are the Tripitakas?
A: The three baskets - Vinaya Pitaka (rules of discipline), Sutta Pitaka (sermons) and Abhidhamma Pitaka (philosophy).
Q: In which language were the Tripitakas written?
A: In Pali.
Q: Where and under whom was the first Buddhist council held?
A: At Rajgriha in 483 BC, under Mahakassapa, during the reign of Ajatashatru.
Q: Where and under whom was the second Buddhist council held?
A: At Vaishali in 383 BC, under Sabakami; it led to the Sthaviravada-Mahasanghika split.
Q: Where and under whom was the third Buddhist council held?
A: At Pataliputra in about 250 BC, under Moggaliputta Tissa, patronised by Ashoka.
Q: Where and under whom was the fourth Buddhist council held?
A: At Kashmir in the 1st century AD, under Vasumitra, patronised by Kanishka.
Q: Which Mahayana philosopher founded the Madhyamika school?
A: Nagarjuna.
Q: Which Buddhist text records the dialogue between King Milinda (Menander) and Nagasena?
A: The Milindapanha (Questions of Milinda).
Q: Who founded Buddhism and where was he born?
A: Buddhism was founded by Gautama Buddha, who was born as Siddhartha in 563 BC at Lumbini, in present-day Nepal.
Q: How many Tirthankaras are there in Jainism and who was the last?
A: There are 24 Tirthankaras. The first was Rishabhanatha, the 23rd was Parshvanatha, and the 24th and last was Vardhamana Mahavira.
Q: What are the Four Noble Truths of Buddhism?
A: They are: there is suffering (Dukkha); it has a cause (Tanha, craving); it can be ended (Nirodha); and there is a path to end it (Magga), namely the Eightfold Path.
Q: What is the Tripitaka?
A: The Tripitaka, or 'three baskets', is the collection of Buddhist scriptures: the Vinaya Pitaka, the Sutta Pitaka and the Abhidhamma Pitaka.
Q: Where were the first two Buddhist Councils held?
A: The First Buddhist Council was held at Rajgriha in 483 BC and the Second at Vaishali in 383 BC, where the Sangha first split.
Q: What is common between Jainism and Buddhism?
A: Both arose in the 6th century BC in the middle Ganga valley, both were founded by Kshatriyas, both used Prakrit, both rejected the authority of the Vedas and the caste system, and both opposed animal sacrifice.
Q: বৌদ্ধ ধৰ্ম কোনে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল আৰু তেওঁ ক'ত জন্মিছিল?
A: বৌদ্ধ ধৰ্ম গৌতম বুদ্ধই প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল, যি খ্ৰীষ্টপূৰ্ব ৫৬৩ চনত বৰ্তমান নেপালৰ লুম্বিনীত সিদ্ধাৰ্থ হিচাপে জন্মিছিল।
Q: জৈন ধৰ্মত কিমানজন তীৰ্থংকৰ আছে আৰু শেষজন কোন আছিল?
A: জৈন ধৰ্মত ২৪ জন তীৰ্থংকৰ আছে। প্ৰথমজন ঋষভনাথ, ২৩ সংখ্যক পাৰ্শ্বনাথ, আৰু ২৪ সংখ্যক তথা শেষজন বৰ্ধমান মহাবীৰ।
Q: বৌদ্ধ ধৰ্মৰ চাৰিটা আৰ্য সত্য কি?
A: সেইবোৰ হ'ল: দুঃখ (দুক্খ) আছে; তাৰ কাৰণ (তণহা, তৃষ্ণা) আছে; ইয়াৰ অন্ত (নিরোধ) সম্ভৱ; আৰু ইয়াৰ অন্তৰ পথ (মগ্গ) আছে, অৰ্থাৎ অষ্টাঙ্গিক পথ।
Q: ত্ৰিপিটক কি?
A: ত্ৰিপিটক, অৰ্থাৎ 'তিনিটা পিটক', বৌদ্ধ শাস্ত্ৰৰ সংগ্ৰহ: বিনয় পিটক, সুত্ত পিটক আৰু অভিধম্ম পিটক।
Q: প্ৰথম দুটা বৌদ্ধ সংগীতি ক'ত অনুষ্ঠিত হৈছিল?
A: প্ৰথম বৌদ্ধ সংগীতি খ্ৰীষ্টপূৰ্ব ৪৮৩ চনত ৰাজগৃহত আৰু দ্বিতীয় খ্ৰীষ্টপূৰ্ব ৩৮৩ চনত ৱৈশালীত অনুষ্ঠিত হৈছিল, য'ত সংঘ প্ৰথম বিভক্ত হৈছিল।
Q: জৈন ধৰ্ম আৰু বৌদ্ধ ধৰ্মৰ মাজত কি সাধাৰণ আছে?
A: দুয়োটা খ্ৰীষ্টপূৰ্ব ৬ষ্ঠ শতিকাত মধ্য গংগা উপত্যকাত জন্মিছিল, দুয়োটা ক্ষত্ৰিয়সকলে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল, দুয়োটাই প্ৰাকৃত ব্যৱহাৰ কৰিছিল, দুয়োটাই বেদৰ প্ৰামাণ্য আৰু জাতি প্ৰণালী নাকচ কৰিছিল, আৰু দুয়োটাই পশুবলিৰ বিৰোধিতা কৰিছিল।

### Mahajanapadas & Magadha Empire — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/ancient-indian-history-sec/mahajanapadas-magadha/
Summary: Practice mahajanapadas & magadha empire questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: How many Mahajanapadas were there in ancient India?
A: Sixteen (16).
Q: Which were the sixteen Mahajanapadas?
A: Anga, Magadha, Kasi, Kosala, Vajji, Malla, Chedi, Vatsa, Kuru, Panchala, Matsya, Surasena, Ashmaka, Avanti, Gandhara and Kamboja.
Q: Which Mahajanapadas were republican (gana-sangha) in nature?
A: Vajji and Malla.
Q: What was the initial capital of Magadha?
A: Girivraja (Rajagriha).
Q: What was the capital of the Anga Mahajanapada?
A: Champa.
Q: What was the capital of the Kasi Mahajanapada?
A: Varanasi.
Q: What was the capital of the Kosala Mahajanapada?
A: Sravasti (with Ayodhya as a secondary capital).
Q: What was the capital of the Vajji confederacy?
A: Vaishali.
Q: What was the capital of the Vatsa Mahajanapada?
A: Kaushambi.
Q: What was the capital of the Avanti Mahajanapada?
A: Ujjaini (earlier Mahishmati).
Q: What was the capital of the Gandhara Mahajanapada?
A: Taxila (Takshashila).
Q: What was the capital of the Surasena Mahajanapada?
A: Mathura.
Q: What was the capital of the Matsya Mahajanapada?
A: Viratanagara (Bairat).
Q: What was the capital of the Panchala Mahajanapada?
A: Kampilya.
Q: Which were the two towns of the Malla republic?
A: Kusinara (Kushinagar) and Pava.
Q: Which four Mahajanapadas were the most powerful?
A: Magadha, Kosala, Avanti and Vatsa.
Q: Which Mahajanapada ultimately became the most powerful in north India?
A: Magadha.
Q: What were the main reasons for the rise of Magadha?
A: Strategic location, fertile Gangetic plains, iron mines in the Rajmahal hills, elephants, and strong ambitious rulers.
Q: Which was the first ruling dynasty of Magadha in the 6th century BC?
A: The Haryanka dynasty.
Q: Who was the founder of the Haryanka dynasty?
A: Bimbisara.
Q: By what other name was Bimbisara known?
A: Shrenika.
Q: Where was the capital of Bimbisara?
A: Rajagriha (Girivraja).
Q: How did Bimbisara strengthen his position?
A: Through matrimonial alliances - marrying Kosala Devi, the Lichchhavi princess Chellana and a princess of Madra.
Q: Who was the contemporary ruler of Magadha during the time of Buddha?
A: Bimbisara and later his son Ajatashatru.
Q: Who was the son of Bimbisara who imprisoned and killed his father?
A: Ajatashatru.
Q: By what other name was Ajatashatru known?
A: Kunika.
Q: Against which confederacy did Ajatashatru fight a prolonged war?
A: The Vajji (Lichchhavi) confederacy of Vaishali.
Q: Which two new weapons did Ajatashatru use against the Vajjis?
A: The Mahasilakantaka (catapult) and the Rathamushala (a mace-fitted chariot).
Q: Which ruler built a fort at Pataliputra?
A: Ajatashatru built the fort at Pataligrama (later Pataliputra).
Q: Which ruler shifted the capital of Magadha to Pataliputra?
A: Udayin, the son of Ajatashatru.
Q: Under the patronage of which Magadha king was the first Buddhist council held?
A: Ajatashatru (at Rajagriha).
Q: Under which king was the second Buddhist council held?
A: Kalashoka of the Sisunaga dynasty (at Vaishali).
Q: Who founded the Sisunaga dynasty?
A: Sisunaga, who overthrew the Haryanka rulers.
Q: Who was the founder of the Nanda dynasty?
A: Mahapadma Nanda.
Q: What is Mahapadma Nanda called in the Puranas?
A: 'Sarva Kshatrantaka' (destroyer of all Kshatriyas) and 'Ekarat' (sole sovereign).
Q: Which dynasty is described as the first non-Kshatriya dynasty of Magadha?
A: The Nanda dynasty.
Q: Who was the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty?
A: Dhana Nanda.
Q: Which Nanda ruler was a contemporary of Alexander?
A: Dhana Nanda.
Q: What was the capital of the Nandas?
A: Pataliputra.
Q: For what were the Nanda rulers famous?
A: Their enormous wealth and a huge standing army.
Q: Who overthrew Dhana Nanda and established the Maurya dynasty?
A: Chandragupta Maurya, with the help of Chanakya (Kautilya).
Q: Why was Rajagriha considered strategically important for Magadha?
A: It was surrounded by five hills that made it difficult to capture.
Q: Which period is known as the 'Second Urbanisation' of India?
A: The Mahajanapada period (6th century BC), marked by NBPW pottery and punch-marked coins.
Q: Which type of coins first appeared in the Mahajanapada period?
A: Punch-marked silver coins.
Q: Who invaded India in 326 BC?
A: Alexander the Great of Macedonia.
Q: Whom did Alexander defeat at the Battle of Hydaspes (Jhelum)?
A: King Porus (Puru).
Q: Which Mahajanapada lay in the Deccan with its capital at Paithan (Potana)?
A: Ashmaka.
Q: Which Mahajanapadas lay in the far north-west of India?
A: Gandhara and Kamboja.
Q: Which Mahajanapada had its capital at Ujjayini?
A: Avanti, with Ujjayini as its capital.
Q: Who founded the city of Pataliputra at the confluence of the Ganga and Son?
A: Ajatashatru, who built a fort at Pataligrama, later developed into Pataliputra.
Q: How many Mahajanapadas were there and where is the list found?
A: There were sixteen Mahajanapadas. The list is found in the Buddhist text Anguttara Nikaya and the Jain text Bhagavati Sutra.
Q: Which Mahajanapada was a republic?
A: Vajji (and also Malla) were gana-sanghas, that is, republican states, unlike the monarchical Mahajanapadas.
Q: Why did Magadha become the most powerful Mahajanapada?
A: Magadha rose because of its fertile Ganga valley location, protection by rivers and hills, access to iron ore, a large number of war elephants, river trade and ambitious rulers.
Q: Who were the important rulers of the Haryanka dynasty?
A: The important Haryanka rulers were Bimbisara, the founder and first important ruler of Magadha, his son Ajatashatru, and Udayin, who shifted the capital to Pataliputra.
Q: When and where were the first two Buddhist Councils held?
A: The First Buddhist Council was held at Rajgriha in 483 BC and the Second Buddhist Council at Vaishali in 383 BC.
Q: Who was the first historical emperor of India?
A: Mahapadma Nanda, the founder of the Nanda dynasty, is often called the first historical emperor of India; the last Nanda ruler was Dhana Nanda, overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya.
Q: মহাজনপদ কিমানটা আছিল আৰু তালিকা ক'ত পোৱা যায়?
A: ষোল্লটা মহাজনপদ আছিল। তালিকা বৌদ্ধ গ্ৰন্থ অঙ্গুত্তৰ নিকায় আৰু জৈন গ্ৰন্থ ভগৱতী সূত্ৰত পোৱা যায়।
Q: কোনটো মহাজনপদ প্ৰজাতন্ত্ৰ আছিল?
A: ৱজ্জি (আৰু মল্লও) গণ-সংঘ, অৰ্থাৎ প্ৰজাতন্ত্ৰীয় ৰাজ্য আছিল, ৰাজতন্ত্ৰীয় মহাজনপদৰ দৰে নহয়।
Q: মগধ কিয় আটাইতকৈ শক্তিশালী মহাজনপদ হৈছিল?
A: মগধ উৰ্বৰ গংগা উপত্যকাৰ অৱস্থান, নদী আৰু পাহাৰৰ সুৰক্ষা, লো-আকৰৰ প্ৰৱেশ, যথেষ্ট যুদ্ধ-হাতী, নদী বাণিজ্য আৰু উচ্চাকাংক্ষী শাসকসকলৰ বাবে উত্থিত হৈছিল।
Q: হৰ্য্যঙ্ক ৰাজবংশৰ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ শাসকসকল কোন আছিল?
A: হৰ্য্যঙ্ক ৰাজবংশৰ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ শাসক আছিল বিম্বিসাৰ (মগধৰ প্ৰথম গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ শাসক আৰু প্ৰতিষ্ঠাপক), তেওঁৰ পুত্ৰ অজাতশত্ৰু, আৰু উদয়ীন, যি ৰাজধানী পাটলিপুত্ৰলৈ স্থানান্তৰিত কৰিছিল।
Q: প্ৰথম দুটা বৌদ্ধ সংগীতি কেতিয়া আৰু ক'ত অনুষ্ঠিত হৈছিল?
A: প্ৰথম বৌদ্ধ সংগীতি খ্ৰীষ্টপূৰ্ব ৪৮৩ চনত ৰাজগৃহত আৰু দ্বিতীয় বৌদ্ধ সংগীতি খ্ৰীষ্টপূৰ্ব ৩৮৩ চনত ৱৈশালীত অনুষ্ঠিত হৈছিল।
Q: ভাৰতৰ প্ৰথম ঐতিহাসিক সম্ৰাট কোন আছিল?
A: নন্দ ৰাজবংশৰ প্ৰতিষ্ঠাপক মহাপদ্ম নন্দক প্ৰায়ে ভাৰতৰ প্ৰথম ঐতিহাসিক সম্ৰাট বোলা হয়; শেষ নন্দ শাসক আছিল ধন নন্দ, যাক চন্দ্ৰগুপ্ত মৌৰ্যই উৎখাত কৰিছিল।

### Mauryan Empire Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/ancient-indian-history-sec/mauryan-empire/
Summary: Practice mauryan empire questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Who founded the Maurya dynasty?
A: Chandragupta Maurya (about 322 BC).
Q: Who was the mentor of Chandragupta Maurya?
A: Chanakya, also known as Kautilya or Vishnugupta.
Q: Which Nanda ruler was overthrown by Chandragupta?
A: Dhana Nanda.
Q: Which famous book did Kautilya write?
A: The Arthashastra, a treatise on statecraft and administration.
Q: Which play by Vishakhadatta describes the rise of Chandragupta?
A: Mudrarakshasa.
Q: Where was the capital of the Mauryan empire?
A: Pataliputra (modern Patna).
Q: Which Greek general was defeated by Chandragupta Maurya?
A: Seleucus Nikator, about 305 BC.
Q: Who came to the court of Chandragupta as the ambassador of Seleucus?
A: Megasthenes.
Q: What book did Megasthenes write?
A: Indica, describing the Mauryan empire and its administration.
Q: What was Chandragupta Maurya called in Greek accounts?
A: Sandrocottus (Sandrakottos).
Q: Which Mauryan king embraced Jainism and went south with Bhadrabahu?
A: Chandragupta Maurya.
Q: How did Chandragupta Maurya die according to the Jaina tradition?
A: By Sallekhana (fasting unto death) at Shravanabelagola.
Q: Who succeeded Chandragupta Maurya?
A: His son Bindusara.
Q: What was Bindusara called?
A: Amitraghata (slayer of enemies).
Q: Who was the Greek ambassador at the court of Bindusara?
A: Deimachos (Daimachus).
Q: Who was the greatest ruler of the Mauryan dynasty?
A: Ashoka.
Q: In which year was Ashoka coronated?
A: About 269/268 BC (reign 268-232 BC).
Q: In which year did Ashoka conquer Kalinga?
A: In 261 BC, in the 8th/9th year of his reign.
Q: What was the effect of the Kalinga war on Ashoka?
A: Filled with remorse over the bloodshed, he renounced war and embraced Buddhism.
Q: What did Ashoka call himself in his inscriptions?
A: Devanampiya Piyadasi (Beloved of the Gods, of gracious mien).
Q: In which script were most of Ashoka's inscriptions written?
A: Brahmi script.
Q: Which script was used for the north-western inscriptions of Ashoka?
A: Kharosthi script.
Q: In which language were the edicts of Ashoka written?
A: In Prakrit (Pali), the language of the common people.
Q: What is the main theme of Ashoka's Dhamma?
A: A code of moral conduct - non-violence, tolerance, respect for elders, kindness and service to all.
Q: Which is the most famous pillar of Ashoka?
A: The Sarnath pillar, crowned with the Lion Capital.
Q: What was adopted as the National Emblem of India?
A: The Lion Capital of Ashoka's Sarnath pillar (on 26 January 1950).
Q: Whom did Ashoka send to Sri Lanka to spread Buddhism?
A: His son Mahinda and daughter Sanghamitra.
Q: Under which king was the third Buddhist council held?
A: Under Ashoka, at Pataliputra (250 BC), presided by Moggaliputta Tissa.
Q: Which rock edict of Ashoka refers to the Kalinga war?
A: Major Rock Edict XIII.
Q: Which rock edict of Ashoka mentions the Dhamma-vijaya (conquest through Dhamma)?
A: Major Rock Edict XIII.
Q: Which edict of Ashoka stressed religious tolerance?
A: Rock Edict XII.
Q: What were Ashoka's 'Dhamma Mahamattas'?
A: Special officials appointed by Ashoka to propagate and supervise the practice of Dhamma.
Q: Which minor rock edict of Ashoka mentions his name 'Ashoka' directly?
A: The Maski edict (Karnataka).
Q: Which inscription of Ashoka records his visit to Lumbini?
A: The Rummindei (Lumbini) pillar inscription.
Q: What special concession did Ashoka give to Lumbini?
A: He exempted the village of Lumbini from tax and reduced the land revenue to one-eighth.
Q: Where are the separate Kalinga edicts of Ashoka located?
A: At Dhauli and Jaugada (Odisha).
Q: Which cave of Barabar was donated by Ashoka?
A: The Lomas Rishi cave, donated to the Ajivikas.
Q: What was the state's share of the agricultural produce under the Mauryas?
A: One-sixth (Bhaga), the standard land tax.
Q: What were the crown lands cultivated directly by the state called?
A: Sita lands.
Q: Which four cities served as provincial headquarters with viceroys (kumaras)?
A: Taxila, Ujjain, Tosali and Suvarnagiri.
Q: Who was the head of the Mauryan administration?
A: The king, assisted by the Mantriparishad (council of ministers).
Q: Who was the chief collector of revenue in the Mauryan administration?
A: Samaharta, with Sannidhata as the treasurer.
Q: Who was in charge of the royal treasury in the Mauryan state?
A: Sannidhata.
Q: What were the Mauryan spies called?
A: Spashas or gudhapurushas.
Q: What were the coins issued by the Mauryans called?
A: Punch-marked coins (silver and copper).
Q: How did Megasthenes describe the Mauryan army administration?
A: The army was divided into six committees of thirty members each (infantry, cavalry, chariots, elephants, navy and transport).
Q: Who was the last ruler of the Mauryan dynasty?
A: Brihadratha.
Q: Who killed the last Mauryan ruler Brihadratha?
A: His commander-in-chief Pushyamitra Sunga (about 185 BC).
Q: How far did the Mauryan empire extend at its peak?
A: From the Hindukush in the north-west to Mysore in the south, and from Bengal in the east to Afghanistan in the west.
Q: Which Buddhist monk converted Ashoka to Buddhism (per the Divyavadana tradition)?
A: Upagupta.
Q: What was the immediate result of the Kalinga war for Ashoka?
A: He gave up the policy of war (Digvijaya) and adopted the policy of Dhamma-vijaya.
Q: Who founded the Mauryan Empire and when?
A: The Mauryan Empire was founded around 321 BC by Chandragupta Maurya, with the help of his mentor Chanakya (Kautilya), by overthrowing the last Nanda ruler Dhana Nanda.
Q: Which Greek general did Chandragupta defeat and who wrote Indica?
A: Chandragupta defeated Seleucus Nicator, a general of Alexander the Great. Seleucus sent the ambassador Megasthenes to the Mauryan court, and Megasthenes wrote the account called Indica.
Q: Why did Ashoka adopt Dhamma?
A: After the terrible bloodshed of the Kalinga war in 261 BC, Ashoka was filled with remorse, embraced Buddhism and adopted the policy of Dhamma. He appointed Dhamma Mahamatta to spread his ethical teachings.
Q: Which Mauryan pillar capital is India's national emblem?
A: The Sarnath Lion Capital, a polished stone pillar capital of Ashoka, is the national emblem of India.
Q: What was the source of Mauryan administration?
A: The Arthashastra of Kautilya (Chanakya) is the main text that describes Mauryan administration, along with the Indica of Megasthenes and the Ashokan edicts.
Q: Who was the last Mauryan ruler?
A: Brihadratha was the last Mauryan ruler. He was killed by Pushyamitra Shunga in 185 BC, which ended the Mauryan Empire and began the Shunga dynasty.
Q: মৌৰ্য সাম্ৰাজ্য কোনে আৰু কেতিয়া প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল?
A: মৌৰ্য সাম্ৰাজ্য প্ৰায় খ্ৰীষ্টপূৰ্ব ৩২১ চনত চন্দ্ৰগুপ্ত মৌৰ্যই, তেওঁৰ পথপ্ৰদৰ্শক চাণক্য (কৌটিল্য)ৰ সহায়ত, শেষ নন্দ শাসক ধন নন্দক উৎখাত কৰি প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল।
Q: চন্দ্ৰগুপ্তই কোন গ্ৰীক সেনাপতিক পৰাস্ত কৰিছিল আৰু ইণ্ডিকা কোনে লিখিছিল?
A: চন্দ্ৰগুপ্তই মহান আলেকজেণ্ডাৰৰ সেনাপতি চেলুকাছ নিকেটৰক পৰাস্ত কৰিছিল। চেলুকাছে মেগাস্থিনিছ নামৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰদূতক মৌৰ্য দৰবাৰলৈ পঠিয়াইছিল, আৰু মেগাস্থিনিছে ইণ্ডিকা নামৰ বিবৰণ লিখিছিল।
Q: অশোকে কিয় ধম্ম গ্ৰহণ কৰিছিল?
A: খ্ৰীষ্টপূৰ্ব ২৬১ চনৰ কলিঙ্গ যুদ্ধৰ ভয়ানক ৰক্তপাতৰ পিছত অশোক অনুতাপেৰে ভৰি পৰিছিল, বৌদ্ধ ধৰ্ম গ্ৰহণ কৰিছিল আৰু ধম্ম নীতি গ্ৰহণ কৰিছিল। তেওঁ ধম্ম মহামাত্ৰ নিযুক্ত কৰি নিজৰ নৈতিক শিক্ষা প্ৰচাৰ কৰিছিল।
Q: কোন মৌৰ্য স্তম্ভ শীৰ্ষ ভাৰতৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় প্ৰতীক?
A: অশোকৰ মসৃণ শিলৰ স্তম্ভ শীৰ্ষ সাৰনাথ সিংহ শীৰ্ষ ভাৰতৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় প্ৰতীক।
Q: মৌৰ্য প্ৰশাসনৰ উত্স কি আছিল?
A: কৌটিল্য (চাণক্য)ৰ অৰ্থশাস্ত্ৰ মৌৰ্য প্ৰশাসন বৰ্ণনা কৰা মূল গ্ৰন্থ, লগতে মেগাস্থিনিছৰ ইণ্ডিকা আৰু অশোকৰ লিপিসমূহ।
Q: শেষ মৌৰ্য শাসক কোন আছিল?
A: বৃহদ্ৰথ শেষ মৌৰ্য শাসক আছিল। পুষ্যমিত্ৰ শুঙ্গই খ্ৰীষ্টপূৰ্ব ১৮৫ চনত তেওঁক হত্যা কৰিছিল, যাৰ দ্বাৰা মৌৰ্য সাম্ৰাজ্যৰ অন্ত পৰিছিল আৰু শুঙ্গ ৰাজবংশৰ আৰম্ভণি হৈছিল।

### Post-Gupta Period (Harshavardhana, Pallavas, Chalukyas
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/ancient-indian-history-sec/post-gupta-period/
