A: মনচবদাৰী ব্যৱস্থাই অভিজাতসকলৰ পদমৰ্যাদা আৰু সামৰিক দায়িত্ব নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰিছিল, আৰু জাগিৰদাৰী ব্যৱস্থাই তেওঁলোকক ভূমি-ৰাজস্ব দিছিল। অভিজাতৰ সংখ্যা বাঢ়ি ভাল জাগিৰৰ অভাৱ হোৱাত ভূমিৰ বাবে প্ৰচণ্ড প্ৰতিযোগিতা হৈছিল, যিয়ে শাহী নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ দুৰ্বল কৰি মোগল সাম্ৰাজ্যৰ অৱক্ষয়ত অৰিহণা যোগাইছিল।
Q: মোগল সাম্ৰাজ্যৰ অন্তিমত কেতিয়া আৰু কেনেকৈ হৈছিল?
A: ১৮৫৭ চনৰ বিদ্ৰোহত বাহাদুৰ শ্বাহ দ্বিতীয় (বাহাদুৰ শ্বাহ জাফৰ) বিদ্ৰোহীসকলৰ প্ৰতীকী নেতা আছিল। ব্ৰিটিছে বিদ্ৰোহ দমন কৰি ১৮৫৮ চনত তেওঁক পদচ্যুত কৰিছিল, যাৰ ফলত মোগল সাম্ৰাজ্য আনুষ্ঠানিকভাৱে অন্ত পৰিছিল।

### Maratha Empire & Peshwas Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/medieval-indian-history-sec/maratha-empire-peshwas/
Summary: Practice maratha empire & peshwas questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Who was the founder of the Maratha kingdom?
A: Shivaji Bhonsle.
Q: Who was the father of Shivaji?
A: Shahji Bhonsle.
Q: Who was the mother of Shivaji?
A: Jijabai.
Q: Who was the guardian (karve) and tutor of Shivaji?
A: Dadaji Kondadev, who trained Shivaji in administration and military matters.
Q: Which fort did Shivaji capture at the beginning of his career?
A: The fort of Torna.
Q: Which Mughal general was defeated by Shivaji at the battle of Pratapgarh?
A: Afzal Khan, the general of the Bijapur Sultanate.
Q: How was Afzal Khan killed?
A: Shivaji killed him in a personal encounter using 'Wagh Nakh' (tiger claws) and a dagger.
Q: Who was the Mughal general who besieged Shivaji in the fort of Purandar?
A: Jai Singh I.
Q: What was the treaty signed between Shivaji and Jai Singh in 1665 AD?
A: The treaty of Purandar.
Q: When was Shivaji crowned as Chhatrapati?
A: In 1674 AD, at the Raigarh fort.
Q: What title did Shivaji assume at his coronation?
A: Chhatrapati (supreme sovereign).
Q: Who performed the coronation ceremony of Shivaji?
A: Gaga Bhatta, a pandit from Benaras.
Q: What was the naval force of Shivaji called?
A: The Maratha navy, with ports at Colaba and Vijaydurg.
Q: Who was the head of the Maratha navy appointed by Shivaji?
A: Kanhoji Angre was a later famous naval chief.
Q: What was the council of ministers of Shivaji called?
A: The Ashta Pradhan (eight ministers).
Q: Who was the first Peshwa (Prime Minister) in Shivaji's council?
A: Moropant Pingle.
Q: What was the title of the finance minister in the Ashta Pradhan?
A: Amatya (or Majumdar).
Q: Who was the chief of intelligence in Shivaji's council?
A: The Pandit Rao (or Pandit, who looked after religious matters and intelligence).
Q: What was the 'Sardeshmukhi' tax collected by Shivaji?
A: An additional levy of ten percent on lands outside his kingdom.
Q: What was the 'Chauth' tax?
A: One-fourth of the land revenue levied on territories outside the Maratha kingdom as protection money.
Q: Who succeeded Shivaji after his death?
A: Sambhaji, his eldest son.
Q: Who was the second son of Shivaji who ruled as Raja?
A: Rajaram.
Q: Who was the widow of Rajaram who led the Maratha resistance against the Mughals?
A: Tarabai.
Q: Who was the first Peshwa of the later Peshwa dynasty?
A: Balaji Vishwanath.
Q: Which Mughal emperor appointed Balaji Vishwanath as Peshwa?
A: Shahu, the grandson of Shivaji, made the Peshwa office hereditary; he ruled under Chhatrapati Shahu.
Q: Who was the second Peshwa who made the Peshwa office supreme?
A: Baji Rao I.
Q: Who was the greatest Peshwa?
A: Baji Rao I, who extended the Maratha power to Malwa, Gujarat and Bundelkhand.
Q: Who was the mother of Baji Rao I?
A: Radhabai.
Q: Who was the famous general of Baji Rao I who fought in the north?
A: Chimaji Appa, his brother, and Malhar Rao Holkar were prominent generals.
Q: Who succeeded Baji Rao I as Peshwa?
A: Balaji Baji Rao (Nana Saheb).
Q: Which Peshwa built the city of Pune?
A: Balaji Baji Rao, who made Pune the Peshwa capital.
Q: What was the Third Battle of Panipat?
A: The battle fought in 1761 AD between the Marathas and the Afghan forces of Ahmad Shah Abdali.
Q: Who was the Maratha general who fought the Third Battle of Panipat?
A: Sadashiv Rao Bhau, the cousin of the Peshwa.
Q: What was the result of the Third Battle of Panipat?
A: A crushing defeat of the Marathas, which halted their northward expansion.
Q: Who were the prominent chiefs of the Maratha confederacy?
A: The Gaekwads of Baroda, the Holkars of Indore, the Scindias of Gwalior and the Bhonsles of Nagpur.
Q: Who founded the Gaekwad dynasty of Baroda?
A: Pilaji Rao Gaekwad.
Q: Who founded the Holkar dynasty of Indore?
A: Malhar Rao Holkar.
Q: Who founded the Scindia dynasty of Gwalior?
A: Ranoji Scindia.
Q: Who founded the Bhonsle dynasty of Nagpur?
A: Raghuji Bhonsle.
Q: Which English Company signed the Treaty of Bassein with the Peshwa Baji Rao II in 1802 AD?
A: The English East India Company.
Q: Who was the last Peshwa?
A: Baji Rao II.
Q: Which Governor General abolished the office of Peshwa in 1818 AD?
A: Lord Hastings, who annexed the Peshwa's territories after the Third Anglo-Maratha War.
Q: What was the language of the Maratha administration?
A: Marathi and Persian.
Q: Who was the famous woman ruler who ruled as regent of Indore in the 19th century?
A: Ahilyabai Holkar.
Q: Who was the founder of the 'Peshwa' family (Bhat family)?
A: Balaji Vishwanath Bhat.
Q: Which Maratha chief defeated the English in the First Anglo-Maratha War?
A: The war ended with the Treaty of Salbai in 1782, largely a stalemate.
Q: What was the cause of the Second Anglo-Maratha War?
A: The British interference in the internal disputes of the Maratha confederacy after the Treaty of Bassein.
Q: Which battle of the Third Anglo-Maratha War led to the end of Maratha power?
A: The battle of Ashti and Sitabuldi (1818 AD).
Q: What was the capital of Shivaji's kingdom?
A: Raigarh, the fort where he was crowned.
Q: Who was the first Chhatrapati of the Marathas?
A: Shivaji.
Q: Which Peshwa is known for building the Shaniwar Wada in Pune?
A: Balaji Baji Rao (Nana Saheb), who built the Shaniwar Wada.
Q: Who founded the Maratha Empire and when was Shivaji crowned?
A: The Maratha Empire was founded by Shivaji Bhonsle. He was crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad in 1674 AD after building a strong kingdom in the Deccan by fighting the Bijapur Sultanate and the Mughals.
Q: Who was the greatest Peshwa and what did he achieve?
A: Baji Rao I (1720-1740) was the greatest Peshwa. He is said never to have lost a battle. He expanded Maratha power into Malwa, Gujarat and Bundelkhand and carried Maratha arms to the gates of Delhi and beyond.
Q: What were Chauth and Sardeshmukhi?
A: Chauth was one-fourth of the revenue (or produce) collected by Shivaji from neighbouring territories, and Sardeshmukhi was an additional one-tenth. These taxes helped finance his army and administration.
Q: What was the Third Battle of Panipat and what was its result?
A: The Third Battle of Panipat was fought in 1761 AD between the Marathas and the Afghan invader Ahmad Shah Abdali. The Marathas suffered a heavy defeat, which checked their expansion for some time, though they recovered under Madhav Rao.
Q: What were the five parts of the Maratha confederacy?
A: The Maratha confederacy consisted of five chiefs: the Peshwa (Pune), the Gaekwad (Baroda), the Bhonsle (Nagpur), the Scindia (Gwalior) and the Holkar (Indore). Their mutual quarrels weakened the confederacy.
Q: How did the Maratha power come to an end?
A: The British fought three Anglo-Maratha Wars (1775-1782, 1803-1805 and 1817-1818). The Treaty of Bassein (1802) gave the British great influence, and after the Third War the Maratha power ended by 1818 AD, making the British the paramount power in India.
Q: মাৰাঠা সাম্ৰাজ্য কোনে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল আৰু শিৱাজী কেতিয়া অভিষিক্ত হৈছিল?
A: মাৰাঠা সাম্ৰাজ্য শিৱাজী ভোঁচলে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল। বিজাপুৰ চুলতানী আৰু মোগলসকলৰ বিৰুদ্ধে যুদ্ধ কৰি দাক্ষিণাত্যত শক্তিশালী ৰাজ্য গঢ়াৰ পিছত তেওঁ খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দ ১৬৭৪ চনত ৰায়গড়ত ছত্ৰপতি হিচাপে অভিষিক্ত হৈছিল।
Q: শ্ৰেষ্ঠ পেশ্বৱা কোন আছিল আৰু তেওঁ কি অৰ্জন কৰিছিল?
A: বাজী ৰাও প্ৰথম (১৭২০-১৭৪০) শ্ৰেষ্ঠ পেশ্বৱা আছিল। তেওঁ কেতিয়াও যুদ্ধত হৰা নাই বুলি কোৱা হয়। তেওঁ মাৰাঠা শক্তি মালৱা, গুজৰাট আৰু বুন্দেলখণ্ডলৈ বিস্তাৰ কৰিছিল আৰু মাৰাঠা সেনাক দিল্লীৰ দুৱাৰলৈকে আৰু তাৰ বাহিৰলৈকে লৈ গৈছিল।
Q: চৌথ আৰু সৰদেশমুখী কি আছিল?
A: চৌথ আছিল চুবুৰীয়া ভূখণ্ডৰ পৰা শিৱাজীয়ে সংগ্ৰহ কৰা ৰাজস্বৰ এক চতুৰ্থাংশ, আৰু সৰদেশমুখী আছিল অতিৰিক্ত এক দশমাংশ। এই কৰসমূহে তেওঁৰ সেনা আৰু প্ৰশাসনক ধন যোগাইছিল।
Q: তৃতীয় পানিপথ যুদ্ধ কি আছিল আৰু ইয়াৰ ফলাফল কি?
A: তৃতীয় পানিপথ যুদ্ধ খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দ ১৭৬১ চনত মাৰাঠাসকল আৰু আফগান আক্ৰমণকাৰী আহমদ শ্বাহ আব্দালীৰ মাজত হৈছিল। মাৰাঠাসকলে ভয়াৱহ পৰাজয় বৰণ কৰিছিল, যিয়ে কিছুকাল তেওঁলোকৰ বিস্তাৰ ৰখাইছিল, যদিও মাধৱ ৰাওৰ অধীনত তেওঁলোকে পুনৰ শক্তি লাভ কৰিছিল।
Q: মাৰাঠা সংঘৰ পাঁচটা অংশ কি আছিল?
A: মাৰাঠা সংঘ পাঁচজন প্ৰধানৰে গঠিত আছিল: পেশ্বৱা (পুনে), গায়কৱাড় (বৰোদা), ভোঁচলে (নাগপুৰ), চিন্ধিয়া (গোৱালিয়ৰ) আৰু হোলকাৰ (ইন্দোৰ)। তেওঁলোকৰ পাৰস্পৰিক কাজিয়াই সংঘক দুৰ্বল কৰিছিল।
Q: মাৰাঠা শক্তিৰ অন্ত কেনেকৈ পৰিছিল?
A: ব্ৰিটিছে তিনিখন আংলো-মাৰাঠা যুদ্ধ (১৭৭৫-১৭৮২, ১৮০৩-১৮০৫ আৰু ১৮১৭-১৮১৮) কৰিছিল। বাচেইন সন্ধি (১৮০২)ই ব্ৰিটিছক বৃহৎ প্ৰভাৱ দিছিল, আৰু তৃতীয় যুদ্ধৰ পিছত খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দ ১৮১৮ লৈকে মাৰাঠা শক্তিৰ অন্ত পৰিছিল, যাৰ ফলত ব্ৰিটিছ ভাৰতৰ সৰ্বোচ্চ শক্তি হৈ পৰিছিল।

### Medieval Indian History — 350 Questions | ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/medieval-indian-history-sec/medieval-india/
Summary: 350 medieval Indian history questions with answers for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Covers the Delhi Sultanate, Mughals, Vijayanagara and the Bhakti movement.
Q: Who founded the Mughal empire in India?
A: Babur founded the Mughal empire after defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.
Q: What was the mansabdari system?
A: It was the Mughal administrative system that graded officers by rank and fixed their military and civil obligations, introduced in an organised form by Akbar.
Q: Which dynasties ruled the Delhi Sultanate?
A: The Slave, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid and Lodi dynasties ruled Delhi in succession between 1206 and 1526.

### Mughal Empire (Babur to Aurangzeb) & Administration
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/medieval-indian-history-sec/mughal-empire-admin/
Summary: Practice mughal empire (babur to aurangzeb) & administration questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free.
Q: Who was the founder of the Mughal empire in India?
A: Zahir-ud-din Muhammad Babur, who defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526 AD.
Q: Which battle in 1526 AD established the Mughal rule in India?
A: The first battle of Panipat.
Q: Who was Babur's father?
A: Umar Shaikh Mirza, the ruler of Farghana.
Q: Which battle did Babur fight against Rana Sanga?
A: The battle of Khanwa in 1527 AD.
Q: Who was Rana Sanga?
A: The Rajput ruler of Mewar who was defeated by Babur at Khanwa.
Q: Which battle in 1529 AD completed Babur's conquest of North India?
A: The battle of Ghaghra, against the Afghans of Bihar and Bengal.
Q: Who wrote the 'Baburnama'?
A: Babur himself, written in Chagatai Turkish.
Q: Who was the successor of Babur?
A: Humayun, his son.
Q: Who was the Afghan ruler who defeated Humayun and founded the Sur dynasty?
A: Sher Shah Suri (Farid Khan).
Q: Which battle did Sher Shah win over Humayun in 1540 AD?
A: The battle of Kannauj (Bilgram).
Q: What was the revenue system introduced by Sher Shah called?
A: The system of land measurement (Biswa) and classification of land according to fertility.
Q: Which coin was introduced by Sher Shah?
A: The Rupiya (silver coin), the precursor of the modern rupee.
Q: Which road was built by Sher Shah?
A: The Grand Trunk Road from Sonargaon to Peshawar.
Q: Who was Akbar's guardian (regent) in the early years?
A: Bairam Khan.
Q: Which battle of 1556 AD re-established Mughal power under Akbar?
A: The second battle of Panipat, against Hemu.
Q: Who was Hemu?
A: A Hindu general of the Sur dynasty who took the title 'Vikramaditya' and was defeated by Akbar.
Q: Which Mughal emperor abolished the Jizya tax?
A: Akbar, in 1564 AD.
Q: Who was the famous composer of the 'Todar Mal's' revenue system?
A: Raja Todar Mal, the finance minister of Akbar.
Q: What was the revenue system of Todar Mal called?
A: The Dahsala system (Malzabuti), based on the measurement of land and fixing of rates.
Q: What was the Mansabdari system?
A: A system of ranking the nobles and officers of the Mughal empire, introduced by Akbar.
Q: What were the two numbers indicating a Mansabdar's rank called?
A: The Zat (personal rank) and Sawar (cavalry rank).
Q: Who was the head of the Mughal revenue department?
A: The Diwan-i-Kul (Imperial Diwan).
Q: What was the military head of the Mughal empire called?
A: The Mir Bakshi.
Q: Who was the religious head (Sadr-us-Sudur) in the Mughal administration?
A: The Sadr-us-Sudur, the chief judge of religious matters.
Q: Which institution was established by Akbar for religious discussions?
A: The Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri.
Q: What was the new religion introduced by Akbar in 1582 AD?
A: The Din-i-Ilahi (Divine Faith).
Q: Who was the first Guru of the Sikhs who was executed by the Mughals?
A: Guru Arjun Dev, the fifth Sikh Guru, executed by Jahangir.
Q: Which Mughal emperor was known as 'Shehzada Salim' before ascending the throne?
A: Jahangir.
Q: Who was the wife of Jahangir famous for her political influence?
A: Nur Jahan.
Q: Which foreign traveller visited Jahangir's court?
A: Sir Thomas Roe, the English ambassador of King James I.
Q: Who built the Taj Mahal?
A: Shah Jahan, in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
Q: What was the name of Shah Jahan's wife whose tomb is the Taj Mahal?
A: Arjumand Banu Begum, known as Mumtaz Mahal.
Q: Which emperor built the Red Fort of Delhi?
A: Shah Jahan.
Q: Which famous battle of succession took place between Shah Jahan's sons?
A: The war of succession (1658 AD), in which Aurangzeb defeated Dara Shukoh and others.
Q: Who was the eldest son of Shah Jahan who was defeated by Aurangzeb?
A: Dara Shukoh.
Q: Which Mughal emperor built the tomb of Bibi Ka Maqbara?
A: Aurangzeb, for his wife Dilras Banu Begum (Rabi-ud-Daurani).
Q: Which Mughal emperor enforced the Jizya tax again?
A: Aurangzeb.
Q: Which Muslim scholar issued a legal opinion (fatwa) against Aurangzeb?
A: No prominent fatwa was issued; Aurangzeb strictly enforced Islamic law.
Q: Which Maratha ruler was captured and executed by Aurangzeb?
A: Sambhaji, son of Shivaji.
Q: What was the period of Aurangzeb's rule?
A: From 1658 to 1707 AD (about 49 years).
Q: Who was the last great Mughal emperor?
A: Aurangzeb, after whose death the empire declined rapidly.
Q: What was the main cause of the decline of the Mughal empire?
A: The religious and extravagant policies of Aurangzeb, weak successors, and the rise of regional powers.
Q: Which battle marked the beginning of the decline of the Mughals in the 18th century?
A: The battle of Nadir Shah's invasion of Delhi (1739 AD).
Q: Who was the painter of the famous 'Padshahnama'?
A: The Padshahnama was a chronicle of Shah Jahan with paintings by the court artists.
Q: What was the official language of the Mughal court?
A: Persian.
Q: Which Mughal emperor was a patron of the 'Akbarnama' written by Abul Fazl?
A: Akbar.
Q: Who wrote the 'Ain-i-Akbari'?
A: Abul Fazl, the court historian of Akbar.
Q: What was the 'Ijaradari' system?
A: A system of revenue farming in which the right to collect revenue was auctioned to contractors (ijaradars).
Q: Which Mughal emperor introduced the 'Izara' (revenue farming) system on a large scale?
A: Aurangzeb, in the later part of his reign.
Q: What was the Mughal coin minted in gold called?
A: The Mohur.
Q: Which Mughal emperor was a great patron of miniature painting?
A: Jahangir, who had a keen interest in art and nature.
Q: What was the 'Zabt' system in Mughal administration?
A: The system of assessment and collection of land revenue based on land measurement.
Q: Who were the 'Khalisa' lands in the Mughal empire?
A: The crown lands whose revenue went directly to the imperial treasury.
Q: Which Mughal emperor built the Shalimar gardens of Kashmir?
A: Jahangir.
Q: Who founded the Mughal Empire and when?
A: The Mughal Empire was founded by Babur in 1526 AD after he defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat. Babur was a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan and wrote the Baburnama.
Q: Who was the greatest Mughal emperor and why?
A: Akbar (1556-1605) is considered the greatest Mughal emperor. He consolidated and expanded the empire, introduced the Mansabdari system and the Zabti land revenue system, followed the policy of Sulh-i-Kul, abolished the jizya, patronised art and learning, and had the Navratna in his court.
Q: What was the Mansabdari system?
A: The Mansabdari system was introduced by Akbar. Every officer held a mansab (rank) with two parts: Zat (personal status) and Sawar (number of cavalry to be maintained). Ranks ranged from 10 to 5,000 and determined the officer's salary and duties.
Q: What was the Zabti land revenue system?
A: The Zabti system was devised by Raja Todar Mal under Akbar. Revenue was fixed at about one-third of the produce, based on the Dahsala (ten-year average) of prices and yields. It was a fair and scientific system and became the basis of later revenue administration.
Q: Which monuments were built by Shah Jahan?
A: Shah Jahan, called the "Engineer King", built the Taj Mahal at Agra in memory of Mumtaz Mahal, the Red Fort and Jama Masjid at Delhi, the Moti Masjid, and the Peacock Throne.
Q: How did Aurangzeb's policies weaken the Mughal Empire?
A: Aurangzeb reimposed the jizya (1679), fought long and costly wars in the Deccan and against the Marathas, Sikhs and Rajputs, and faced the Jagirdari crisis. Although the empire reached its greatest extent under him, these wars drained its resources and set the stage for its decline after 1707.
Q: মোগল সাম্ৰাজ্য কোনে আৰু কেতিয়া প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল?
A: প্ৰথম পানিপথ যুদ্ধত ইব্ৰাহিম লোদীক পৰাস্ত কৰি খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দ ১৫২৬ চনত বাবৰে মোগল সাম্ৰাজ্য প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল। বাবৰ তৈমুৰ আৰু চেঙ্গিজ খানৰ বংশধৰ আছিল আৰু বাবৰনামা লিখিছিল।
Q: শ্ৰেষ্ঠ মোগল সম্ৰাট কোন আছিল আৰু কিয়?
A: আকবৰ (১৫৫৬-১৬০৫) শ্ৰেষ্ঠ মোগল সম্ৰাট বুলি গণ্য কৰা হয়। তেওঁ সাম্ৰাজ্য সংহত আৰু বিস্তাৰ কৰিছিল, মানচবদাৰী আৰু জাবতী ভূমি ৰাজস্ব ব্যৱস্থা প্ৰৱৰ্তন কৰিছিল, ছুলহ-ই-কুল নীতি অনুসৰণ কৰিছিল, জিজিয়া বিলুপ্ত কৰিছিল, কলা-বিদ্যাক পৃষ্ঠপোষকতা কৰিছিল, আৰু ৰাজসভাত নৱৰত্ন আছিল।
Q: মানচবদাৰী ব্যৱস্থা কি আছিল?
A: মানচবদাৰী ব্যৱস্থা আকবৰে প্ৰৱৰ্তন কৰিছিল। প্ৰতিজন বিষয়াই দুটা অংশৰ মানচব (পদমৰ্যাদা) ৰাখিছিল: জাত (ব্যক্তিগত মৰ্যাদা) আৰু চৱাৰ (ৰাখিবলগীয়া অশ্বাৰোহীৰ সংখ্যা)। পদমৰ্যাদা ১০ৰ পৰা ৫,০০০ লৈ আছিল আৰু ই বিষয়াৰ বেতন তথা কৰ্তব্য নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰিছিল।
Q: জাবতী ভূমি ৰাজস্ব ব্যৱস্থা কি আছিল?
A: জাবতী ব্যৱস্থা আকবৰৰ অধীনত ৰাজা টোডৰ মলে প্ৰস্তুত কৰিছিল। মূল্য আৰু উৎপাদনৰ দহচালা (দহ বছৰৰ গড়)ৰ ভিত্তিত ৰাজস্ব উৎপাদনৰ প্ৰায় এক তৃতীয়াংশ নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰা হৈছিল। ই এক ন্যায্য আৰু বৈজ্ঞানিক ব্যৱস্থা আছিল আৰু পিছৰ ৰাজস্ব প্ৰশাসনৰ ভিত্তি হৈ পৰিছিল।
Q: শ্বাহজাহানে কি কি স্মাৰক নিৰ্মাণ কৰিছিল?
A: শ্বাহজাহান, যাক "স্থপতিবিদ ৰজা" বোলা হয়, আগ্ৰাত মুমতাজ মহলৰ সোঁৱৰণত তাজমহল, দিল্লীত লাল কিল্লা আৰু জামা মছজিদ, মতি মছজিদ, আৰু ময়ূৰ সিংহাসন নিৰ্মাণ কৰিছিল।
Q: আউৰঙ্গজেৱৰ নীতিয়ে মোগল সাম্ৰাজ্যক কেনেকৈ দুৰ্বল কৰিছিল?
A: আউৰঙ্গজেৱে জিজিয়া (১৬৭৯) পুনৰ প্ৰৱৰ্তন কৰিছিল, দাক্ষিণাত্যত আৰু মাৰাঠা, শিখ তথা ৰাজপুতসকলৰ বিৰুদ্ধে দীঘলীয়া আৰু ব্যয়বহুল যুদ্ধ কৰিছিল, আৰু জাগিৰদাৰী সংকটৰ সন্মুখীন হৈছিল। তেওঁৰ অধীনত সাম্ৰাজ্য আটাইতকৈ বিস্তৃত হ'লেও এই যুদ্ধবোৰে ইয়াৰ সম্পদ শুহি লৈছিল আৰু ১৭০৭ৰ পিছত অৱনতিৰ বাট মুকলি কৰিছিল।

### Tripartite Struggle & Early Medieval Dynasties — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/medieval-indian-history-sec/tripartite-struggle-dynasties/
Summary: Practice tripartite struggle & early medieval dynasties questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual.
Q: Which three powers fought the Tripartite Struggle for the mastery of Kannauj?
A: The Palas of Bengal, the Gurjara-Pratiharas of western India and the Rashtrakutas of the Deccan.
Q: Who founded the Pala dynasty of Bengal?
A: Gopala, who was elected by the people to end the anarchy (Matsyanyaya).
Q: Who was the greatest ruler of the Pala dynasty?
A: Dharmapala, who extended the Pala power and captured Kannauj.
Q: Who founded the university of Vikramashila?
A: Dharmapala, the Pala king.
Q: Who was the successor of Dharmapala who carried out raids in northern India?
A: Devapala, who extended the empire from Assam to Orissa and Kashmir.
Q: Which Pala ruler built the famous Odantapuri monastery?
A: Gopala.
Q: Which famous Buddhist scholars belonged to the Pala period?
A: Santarakshita and Dipankara Shrijnana (Atisha).
Q: Who was the last important ruler of the Pala dynasty?
A: Mahipala I, who recovered northern Bengal and Bihar from the Chola invader Rajendra I.
Q: Who founded the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty?
A: Harichandra, who flourished in the Jodhpur region.
Q: Who was the first great ruler of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty?
A: Vatsaraja, who took the title of Rana.
Q: Which Gurjara-Pratihara ruler successfully defended Kannauj against Dharmapala?
A: Nagabhata II, who took the title of Maharajadhiraja.
Q: Who was the greatest ruler of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty?
A: Mihira Bhoja, who ruled for a long period and revived the dynasty's power.
Q: Who built the famous Rameshwar temple and the Kameshwar temple according to the Arab traveller Sulaiman?
A: Mihira Bhoja (identified as Baura by Sulaiman).
Q: Which Arab traveller called the Pratihara ruler 'one of the four great kings of the world'?
A: Sulaiman, who considered the Pratihara ruler Baura (Mihira Bhoja) as one of the four great kings.
Q: Which Pratihara ruler tried to capture the holy city of Kannauj from the Rashtrakutas?
A: Mahendrapala I, son of Mihira Bhoja.
Q: Which Pratihara ruler was defeated by Mahmud of Ghazni in 1018 AD?
A: Rajyapala, who had to flee from Kannauj.
Q: Who founded the Rashtrakuta dynasty?
A: Dantidurga, who performed the Hiranyagarbha ceremony and took the title Maharajadhiraja.
Q: Who was the greatest ruler of the Rashtrakuta dynasty?
A: Amoghavarsha I, who ruled for over 60 years and was a patron of Jainism and literature.
Q: Which Rashtrakuta ruler wrote the Kavirajamarga, the earliest Kannada work on poetics?
A: Amoghavarsha I (with the assistance of a court poet).
Q: Who was Amoghavarsha's famous Jain teacher?
A: Jinasena, who wrote the Adipurana.
Q: Who built the famous rock-cut temple of Kailasa at Ellora?
A: Krishna I, the Rashtrakuta ruler.
Q: Which Rashtrakuta ruler defeated the Gurjara-Pratihara ruler and marched into Kannauj?
A: Indra III, who defeated Mahipala of Kannauj in 916 AD.
Q: Which famous Sanskrit play, 'Karpuramanjari', was written by a Rashtrakuta princess?
A: Karpuramanjari, written by Shilabhattarika, wife of a Rashtrakuta prince.
Q: Who was the last great ruler of the Rashtrakuta dynasty?
A: Krishna III, who fought against the Cholas and Paramaras.
Q: Which dynasty succeeded the Rashtrakutas in the Deccan?
A: The Chalukyas of Kalyani (Western Chalukyas), under Tailapa II.
Q: Who founded the Paramara dynasty of Malwa?
A: Upendra, though the dynasty rose to prominence under Siyaka and Munja.
Q: Who was the greatest ruler of the Paramara dynasty?
A: Bhoja, who was a great patron of learning and wrote works like Saraswati-Kanthabharana.
Q: Which Paramara ruler founded the city of Dhar in Malwa?
A: Bhoja, who made Dhar his capital.
Q: Who founded the Chandela dynasty?
A: Nannuka, a feudatory chief of the Pratiharas.
Q: Who built the famous Khajuraho temples?
A: The Chandela rulers, especially from the time of Yashovarman.
Q: Which Chandela ruler took the title of Kalanjaradhipati?
A: Dhanga, who built the temples of Khajuraho and performed the Hiranyagarbha ceremony.
Q: Who founded the Chauhana (Chahamana) dynasty?
A: Vasudeva, who flourished in the Ajmer region.
Q: Who was the greatest ruler of the Chauhana dynasty?
A: Prithviraj III (Prithviraj Chauhan), the hero of the first battle of Tarain.
Q: Which kingdom's founder was Vigraharaja IV?
A: He was a strong ruler of the Chauhana dynasty who captured Delhi from the Tomars.
Q: Who was the ruler of Delhi before the Chauhans captured it?
A: The Tomars (Tomar dynasty), founded by Anangapala.
Q: Who founded the city of Delhi (Dhillika)?
A: Anangapala, the Tomar ruler.
Q: Which dynasty founded by Mularaja ruled Gujarat in the early medieval period?
A: The Chaulukyas (Solankis) of Gujarat.
Q: Who was the greatest ruler of the Chaulukya dynasty of Gujarat?
A: Kumarapala, who was converted to Jainism by the famous teacher Hemachandra.
Q: Which famous Jain scholar was the mentor of Kumarapala?
A: Hemachandra, who wrote the Siddha-Hema-Shabdanushasana (grammar) and many other works.
Q: Which dynasty ruled Kanauj (Kannauj) before its decline and was founded by Yasovarman?
A: The Varman dynasty of Kannauj, founded by Yasovarman around 790 AD.
Q: Who wrote the 'Ramacharita' describing the exploits of the Pala ruler Ramapala?
A: Sandhyakar Nandi, a poet of the Pala court.
Q: Which dynasty founded by Bhoja II controlled the region of Dahala (Chedi)?
A: The Kalachuri (Chedi) dynasty of Tripuri.
Q: Which Kalachuri ruler fought against the Chalukyas and Paramaras?
A: Kokalla, who was a powerful ruler of the Kalachuri dynasty.
Q: Which dynasty was founded by Nagabhata, and later ruled by Bhoj and Mihira Bhoja?
A: The Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty.
Q: Which Rashtrakuta ruler is known as 'Vallabha'?
A: Dantidurga, who took the title of Vallabha.
Q: What was the title of the Rashtrakuta rulers meaning 'lord of the great kingdom'?
A: Maharajadhiraja.
Q: Who was the founder of the Varman dynasty of Kannauj?
A: Yasovarman.
Q: Which Chinese traveller visited India during the Pala period?
A: No famous Chinese traveller of the Pala period is recorded, though I-tsing visited earlier in the Gupta era.
Q: Which Pratihara ruler is famous for the construction of the temple of Somnath?
A: The Somnath temple predates the Pratiharas; Nagabhata II is credited with its restoration.
Q: Which kingdom was founded in Orissa by Yayati Kesari?
A: The Soma dynasty of Orissa (Kesari dynasty), later followed by the Ganga dynasty.
Q: Who founded the Ganga dynasty of Kalinga (Orissa)?
A: Anantavarman Chodagangadeva, who ruled Kalinga in the 11th century.
Q: Who built the famous Sun Temple of Konark?
A: Narasimhadeva I, the Ganga ruler of Orissa.
Q: Who was the founder of the Sena dynasty of Bengal?
A: Samantha Sena, a petty chief; the dynasty rose under Vijayasena.
Q: Which Sena ruler of Bengal revived Brahmanical Hinduism and was a patron of Sanskrit learning?
A: Ballala Sena, who is believed to have introduced the practice of Kulinism.
Q: Who was the last ruler of the Sena dynasty of Bengal?
A: Lakshmana Sena, who was defeated by Muhammad Bakhtiyar Khalji.
Q: Which famous Chinese traveller visited the court of Harsha?
A: Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang), who stayed in India for about 15 years.
Q: Who was the last ruler of the Harsha's empire after his death?
A: Harsha died without an heir; his empire soon broke up into small states.
Q: Which dynasty of Kannauj ruled after the fall of Harsha's empire?
A: The Varman dynasty of Yasovarman, followed by the Ayudhas.
Q: Who were the Ayudhas who ruled Kannauj?
A: The Ayudha rulers were the successors of Yasovarman who controlled Kannauj before the Pratiharas.
Q: Which king of Kashmir is famous for the construction of the Martand Sun Temple?
A: Lalitaditya Muktapida, the greatest ruler of the Karkota dynasty.
Q: Who wrote the famous historical chronicle 'Rajatarangini' of Kashmir?
A: Kalhana, in the 12th century AD.
Q: Which dynasty was founded in Kashmir by Durlabhavardhana?
A: The Karkota dynasty.
Q: What was the Tripartite Struggle and which three powers were involved?
A: The Tripartite Struggle was a long conflict (about the 8th-10th century AD) among three powers - the Gurjara-Pratiharas, the Palas and the Rashtrakutas - to control Kannauj, the symbol of supremacy over North India.
Q: Why was Kannauj so important in early medieval India?
A: Kannauj had been the capital of Harshavardhana and controlled the fertile Ganga-Yamuna doab and major trade routes. Whoever held Kannauj was seen as the paramount power of northern India.
Q: Who founded the Pala dynasty and who was its greatest ruler?
A: The Pala dynasty was founded by Gopala around 750 AD. Its greatest ruler was Dharmapala, a great patron of Buddhism who is associated with Vikramashila University; his son Devapala further expanded the empire.
Q: Which Rashtrakuta ruler built the Kailasa temple at Ellora?
A: The Kailasa temple at Ellora was built by the Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I. It is a monolithic rock-cut temple and one of the finest examples of Indian rock-cut architecture.
Q: Who was Mihira Bhoja and which dynasty did he belong to?
A: Mihira Bhoja (c. 836-885 AD) was the greatest ruler of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty. He took the title Adivaraha and ruled from Ujjain and later Kannauj.
Q: What was the result of the Tripartite Struggle?
A: All three powers exhausted themselves in the long conflict, and no single empire emerged as the master of North India. This political fragmentation weakened the Rajput states and made them vulnerable to the Turkish invasions after 1192 AD.
Q: ত্ৰিপাক্ষিক সংঘৰ্ষ কি আছিল আৰু তাত কোন তিনিটা শক্তি জড়িত আছিল?
A: ত্ৰিপাক্ষিক সংঘৰ্ষ আছিল প্ৰায় ৮ম-১০ম শতিকাৰ এটা দীঘলীয়া সংঘৰ্ষ, যি তিনিটা শক্তি - গুৰ্জৰ-প্ৰতিহাৰ, পাল আৰু ৰাষ্ট্ৰকূট - ৰ মাজত উত্তৰ ভাৰতৰ মাহাত্ম্যৰ প্ৰতীক কনৌজ নিয়ন্ত্ৰণৰ বাবে হৈছিল।
Q: প্ৰাৰম্ভিক মধ্যযুগীয় ভাৰতত কনৌজ ইমান গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ কিয় আছিল?
A: কনৌজ হৰ্ষবৰ্ধনৰ ৰাজধানী আছিল আৰু উৰ্বৰ গংগা-যমুনা দুআব তথা প্ৰধান বাণিজ্য পথ নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ কৰিছিল। কনৌজ যি ধৰি ৰাখিছিল, তেওঁ উত্তৰ ভাৰতৰ সৰ্বোচ্চ শক্তি বুলি গণ্য হৈছিল।
Q: পাল ৰাজবংশ কোনে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল আৰু শ্ৰেষ্ঠ শাসক কোন আছিল?
A: পাল ৰাজবংশ গোপালে প্ৰায় খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দ ৭৫০ চনত প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল। শ্ৰেষ্ঠ শাসক আছিল ধৰ্মপাল, বৌদ্ধ ধৰ্মৰ মহান পৃষ্ঠপোষক, যি বিক্ৰমশীলা বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ৰ সৈতে জড়িত; তেওঁৰ পুত্ৰ দেৱপালে সাম্ৰাজ্য আৰু বিস্তাৰ কৰিছিল।
Q: এলোৰাৰ কৈলাস মন্দিৰ কোন ৰাষ্ট্ৰকূট শাসকে নিৰ্মাণ কৰিছিল?
A: এলোৰাৰ কৈলাস মন্দিৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰকূট শাসক কৃষ্ণ প্ৰথমে নিৰ্মাণ কৰিছিল। ই এটা একশিলা শিলা-কটা মন্দিৰ আৰু ভাৰতীয় শিলা-কটা স্থাপত্যৰ অন্যতম শ্ৰেষ্ঠ নিদৰ্শন।
Q: মিহিৰ ভোজ কোন আছিল আৰু তেওঁ কোন ৰাজবংশৰ আছিল?
A: মিহিৰ ভোজ (প্ৰায় খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দ ৮৩৬-৮৮৫) গুৰ্জৰ-প্ৰতিহাৰ ৰাজবংশৰ শ্ৰেষ্ঠ শাসক আছিল। তেওঁ আদিবৰাহ উপাধি গ্ৰহণ কৰিছিল আৰু উজ্জয়িনী তথা পিছত কনৌজৰ পৰা শাসন কৰিছিল।
Q: ত্ৰিপাক্ষিক সংঘৰ্ষৰ ফলাফল কি আছিল?
A: দীঘলীয়া সংঘৰ্ষত তিনিও শক্তি ক্ষয়িষ্ণু হৈছিল আৰু উত্তৰ ভাৰতৰ ওপৰত কোনো এটা সাম্ৰাজ্য প্ৰভু হিচাপে আত্মপ্ৰকাশ কৰা নাছিল। এই ৰাজনৈতিক বিভাজনে ৰাজপুত ৰাজ্যবোৰক দুৰ্বল কৰি খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দ ১১৯২ৰ পিছত তুৰ্কী আক্ৰমণৰ সন্মুখীন কৰাইছিল।

### Turkish Invasions (Mahmud of Ghazni & Muhammad Ghori)
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/medieval-indian-history-sec/turkish-invasions/
Summary: Practice turkish invasions (mahmud of ghazni & muhammad ghori) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free.
Q: Who was the founder of the Ghaznavid dynasty?
A: Alptigin, a Turkish slave commander, though his slave Subuktigin established the dynasty's power.
Q: Who was the father of Mahmud of Ghazni?
A: Subuktigin.
Q: In which year did Mahmud of Ghazni ascend the throne of Ghazni?
A: 998 AD.
Q: How many times did Mahmud of Ghazni invade India?
A: Seventeen times, between 1000 and 1027 AD.
Q: Who was the ruler of the Shahi kingdom of Afghanistan and Punjab who fought against Mahmud?
A: Jayapala and his son Anandapala.
Q: In which battle was Jayapala defeated by Mahmud of Ghazni?
A: The battle of Peshawar (1001 AD).
Q: Which city did Mahmud of Ghazni conquer in 1010 AD?
A: Multan.
Q: Which ruler of Kannauj was defeated and humiliated by Mahmud of Ghazni in 1018 AD?
A: Rajyapala, the Pratihara ruler.
Q: Which famous temple did Mahmud of Ghazni destroy in 1025 AD?
A: The Somnath temple in Gujarat.
Q: Which poet composed the Shahnama, an epic of the Ghaznavids?
A: Firdausi, the Persian poet patronised by Mahmud of Ghazni.
Q: Which scholar of the Ghazni court wrote about Indian astronomy and mathematics?
A: Al-Biruni, who wrote the 'Kitab-ul-Hind' (Tahqiq-i-Hind).
Q: What does 'Tahqiq-i-Hind' by Al-Biruni describe?
A: It is a detailed account of Indian religion, philosophy, science and society in the 11th century.
Q: Why is Mahmud of Ghazni mainly remembered in Indian history?
A: For his plundering raids into India, especially the destruction of the Somnath temple.
Q: What was the main motive of Mahmud's invasions of India?
A: To plunder the wealth of the rich Indian temples and kingdoms.
Q: Who was the founder of the Ghurid dynasty?
A: The Ghurids were founded by the Shansabani family; the famous rulers were Ghiyasuddin and Muhammad Ghori (Muizuddin).
Q: Who was the brother of Muhammad Ghori?
A: Ghiyasuddin Ghori (Abu'l Fath Muhammad), the elder brother.
Q: Which ruler of the Gahadvala dynasty was defeated by Muhammad Ghori?
A: Jayachandra, who was defeated at the battle of Chandwar in 1194 AD.
Q: Who was the ruler of Ajmer and Delhi whom Muhammad Ghori fought in the first battle of Tarain?
A: Prithviraj III (Prithviraj Chauhan).
Q: In which year was the first battle of Tarain fought?
A: 1191 AD.
Q: Who won the first battle of Tarain?
A: Prithviraj III defeated Muhammad Ghori.
Q: In which year was the second battle of Tarain fought?
A: 1192 AD.
Q: Who won the second battle of Tarain?
A: Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj III, who was captured and later killed.
Q: Who was appointed as Muhammad Ghori's governor in India after the second battle of Tarain?
A: Qutb-ud-din Aibak, his trusted slave-general.
Q: Which general of Muhammad Ghori conquered Bengal and Bihar?
A: Muhammad Bakhtiyar Khalji.
Q: Which ancient university was destroyed by Muhammad Bakhtiyar Khalji?
A: Nalanda university, which was sacked and burnt.
Q: Who was the ruler of Bengal defeated by Bakhtiyar Khalji?
A: Lakshmana Sena, the last Sena ruler.
Q: In which year was the battle of Chandwar fought?
A: 1194 AD.
Q: Who were the Gahadvalas whose capital was Kannauj?
A: A Rajput dynasty of Kannauj, founded by Chandradeva, who controlled the Gangetic Doab.
Q: Which king of Kannauj built the Jaichand (Jayachandra) kingdom's largest military force against Ghori?
A: Jayachandra, who refused to ally with Prithviraj and was defeated alone at Chandwar.
Q: Who killed Muhammad Ghori?
A: He was assassinated in 1206 AD by a Khokhar tribe while on his way to Ghazni.
Q: Which Turkish general founded the independent Sultanate of Delhi after Ghori's death?
A: Qutb-ud-din Aibak, who founded the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty.
Q: Who succeeded Qutb-ud-din Aibak?
A: Aram Shah, who was soon replaced by Iltutmish (Shams-ud-din Iltutmish).
Q: Which Hindu ruler was the last major king defeated by Ghori to establish Muslim rule in North India?
A: Jayachandra of Kannauj, defeated at the battle of Chandwar.
Q: What was the outcome of the Turkish invasions on Buddhism in India?
A: Buddhism declined sharply in North India as its great centres (Nalanda, Vikramashila) were destroyed.
Q: What did Mahmud of Ghazni take back to Ghazni after his raids?
A: Vast treasures of gold, silver, jewels and thousands of slaves.
Q: Which famous work of Firdausi mentions the Ghaznavid conquests?
A: The Shahnama.
Q: Who wrote 'Tarikh-i-Hind' describing the Ghaznavid rule?
A: Al-Biruni, whose actual work is called 'Tahqiq-i-Hind'.
Q: Which fort did Mahmud of Ghazni capture in 1009 AD?
A: The fort of Nagarkot (Kangra).
Q: Which ruler of the Tomara/Chauhana kingdom did Mahmud encounter at Nagarkot?
A: The ruler of Nagarkot submitted and paid tribute to Mahmud.
Q: In which year did Mahmud of Ghazni destroy the temple of Somnath?
A: 1025 AD.
Q: What did the Somnath temple's destruction demonstrate about the state of Hindu kingdoms?
A: It showed the disunity and weakness of the Hindu states, who failed to unite against the invaders.
Q: Which city did Muhammad Ghori make his base for the conquest of North India?
A: He used Lahore as his Indian headquarters.
Q: Which slave-general of Ghori established the Ghurid rule in the Delhi region?
A: Qutb-ud-din Aibak.
Q: What was the title assumed by Muhammad Ghori?
A: Muiz-ud-din Muhammad bin Sam.
Q: Which kingdom did Muhammad Ghori destroy before turning towards India?
A: The Ghaznavid kingdom of Ghazni and Punjab.
Q: What was the capital of the Ghaznavid kingdom?
A: Ghazni (in present-day Afghanistan).
Q: Which commander of Ghori is famous for conquering Lahore?
A: Qutb-ud-din Aibak.
Q: What was the effect of the Turkish invasions on the Rajput power?
A: The Rajput states were defeated one by one due to their disunity, paving the way for Muslim rule.
Q: Which of the following was NOT a target of Mahmud's raids?
A: South India; his raids were mainly confined to North India, Gujarat and the western regions.
Q: What was the political condition of India before the Turkish invasions?
A: India was divided into several small and warring kingdoms with no unity.
Q: Who was the ruler of Bengal who had to flee to East Bengal due to Bakhtiyar Khalji?
A: Lakshmana Sena, the last Sena king.
Q: Which city was captured by Bakhtiyar Khalji, making it his capital in Bengal?
A: Nadia (Nabadwip), the capital of Lakshmana Sena.
Q: Which work of Al-Biruni gives valuable information about Indian society?
A: Tahqiq-i-Hind (Kitab-ul-Hind).
Q: What was the result of the second battle of Tarain for the Chauhans?
A: Prithviraj was defeated and killed, and the Chauhana power was crushed.
Q: What title did Mahmud of Ghazni assume?
A: Yamin-ud-Daula and Amin-ul-Millat (the Sword of the State and Faith).
Q: Which Rajput ruler is regarded as the last great Hindu king of North India?
A: Prithviraj III (Prithviraj Chauhan).
Q: Who was Mahmud of Ghazni and how many times did he invade India?
A: Mahmud of Ghazni (997-1030 AD) was a Turkish ruler of the Ghaznavid dynasty based at Ghazni in Afghanistan. He invaded India about seventeen times, mainly to plunder wealth and temples. In 1025 AD he plundered the famous Somanatha temple in Gujarat.
Q: Why is Mahmud of Ghazni called an invader and not a ruler of India?
A: Mahmud's campaigns were mainly plundering raids rather than attempts to establish an administration. He annexed only Punjab; the rest of India was not brought under his permanent rule. Hence he is remembered as an invader and "idol breaker".
Q: Who was Muhammad Ghori and how did he differ from Mahmud of Ghazni?
A: Muhammad Ghori was the ruler of Ghor in Afghanistan. Unlike Mahmud, he wanted to establish a permanent empire in India. He defeated Prithviraj Chauhan in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 AD), and his slave-general Qutbuddin Aibak founded the Slave dynasty, beginning the Delhi Sultanate.
Q: What happened in the First and Second Battles of Tarain?
A: In the First Battle of Tarain (1191 AD), Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori. Ghori returned the next year and won the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 AD), in which Prithviraj was defeated and killed.
Q: Who was Al-Biruni and what did he write about India?
A: Al-Biruni was a great scholar in the court of Mahmud of Ghazni. He studied Indian science, religion, philosophy and society and wrote the Kitab-ul-Hind (Tahqiq-i-Hind), one of the most important foreign accounts of early medieval India.
Q: What were the main consequences of the Turkish invasions of India?
A: The Turkish invasions led to the establishment of the Delhi Sultanate, ended Rajput supremacy in North India, introduced Islam as a major religion, and gave rise to a composite Indo-Islamic culture and a new style of architecture. They also caused large-scale destruction, plunder and economic disruption.
Q: মাহমুদ ঘজনী কোন আছিল আৰু তেওঁ কিমানবাৰ ভাৰত আক্ৰমণ কৰিছিল?
A: মাহমুদ ঘজনী (খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দ ৯৯৭-১০৩০) আফগানিস্তানৰ ঘজনীত অৱস্থিত ঘজনৱী ৰাজবংশৰ তুৰ্কী শাসক আছিল। তেওঁ প্ৰায় সোতৰবাৰ ভাৰত আক্ৰমণ কৰিছিল, মূলতঃ ধন-সম্পত্তি আৰু মন্দিৰ লুণ্ঠনৰ বাবে। খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দ ১০২৫ চনত তেওঁ গুজৰাটৰ প্ৰসিদ্ধ সোমনাথ মন্দিৰ লুণ্ঠন কৰিছিল।
Q: মাহমুদ ঘজনীক আক্ৰমণকাৰী বুলি কোৱা হয়, ভাৰতৰ শাসক বুলি নহয় কিয়?
A: মাহমুদৰ অভিযান মূলতঃ প্ৰশাসন প্ৰতিষ্ঠাৰ প্ৰচেষ্টাৰ পৰিৱৰ্তে লুণ্ঠনমূলক অভিযান আছিল। তেওঁ কেৱল পঞ্জাব অধিগ্ৰহণ কৰিছিল; বাকী ভাৰত তেওঁৰ স্থায়ী শাসনৰ অধীনলৈ অহা নাছিল। সেয়েহে তেওঁ আক্ৰমণকাৰী আৰু "মূৰ্তিভঞ্জক" হিচাপে স্মৰণীয়।
Q: মহম্মদ ঘোৰী কোন আছিল আৰু তেওঁ মাহমুদ ঘজনীৰ পৰা কেনেকৈ পৃথক আছিল?
A: মহম্মদ ঘোৰী আফগানিস্তানৰ ঘোৰৰ শাসক আছিল। মাহমুদৰ দৰে নহয়, তেওঁ ভাৰতত স্থায়ী সাম্ৰাজ্য প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিব বিচাৰিছিল। তেওঁ দ্বিতীয় তাৰাইন যুদ্ধ (খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দ ১১৯২)ত পৃথ্বীৰাজ চৌহানক পৰাস্ত কৰিছিল, আৰু তেওঁৰ দাস-সেনাপতি কুতুবুদ্দিন আইবকে গোলাম ৰাজবংশ প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰি দিল্লী চুলতানীৰ আৰম্ভণি কৰিছিল।
Q: প্ৰথম আৰু দ্বিতীয় তাৰাইন যুদ্ধত কি হৈছিল?
A: প্ৰথম তাৰাইন যুদ্ধত (খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দ ১১৯১) পৃথ্বীৰাজ চৌহানে মহম্মদ ঘোৰীক পৰাস্ত কৰিছিল। ঘোৰী পিছৰ বছৰ উভতি আহি দ্বিতীয় তাৰাইন যুদ্ধ (খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দ ১১৯২) জয় কৰিছিল, য'ত পৃথ্বীৰাজ পৰাস্ত আৰু নিহত হৈছিল।
Q: আল-বিৰুনী কোন আছিল আৰু ভাৰতৰ বিষয়ে তেওঁ কি লিখিছিল?
A: আল-বিৰুনী মাহমুদ ঘজনীৰ ৰাজসভাৰ মহান বিদ্বান আছিল। তেওঁ ভাৰতীয় বিজ্ঞান, ধৰ্ম, দৰ্শন আৰু সমাজ অধ্যয়ন কৰি কিতাব-উল-হিন্দ (তাহকিক-ই-হিন্দ) লিখিছিল, যি প্ৰাৰম্ভিক মধ্যযুগীয় ভাৰতৰ বিষয়ে এটা আটাইতকৈ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ বিদেশী বিৱৰণ।
Q: ভাৰতত তুৰ্কী আক্ৰমণৰ মূল পৰিণাম কি আছিল?
A: তুৰ্কী আক্ৰমণে দিল্লী চুলতানী প্ৰতিষ্ঠা, উত্তৰ ভাৰতত ৰাজপুত আধিপত্যৰ অন্ত, এটা প্ৰধান ধৰ্ম হিচাপে ইছলামৰ প্ৰৱেশ, আৰু এক মিশ্ৰিত ইণ্ডো-ইছলামিক সংস্কৃতি তথা নতুন স্থাপত্য শৈলীৰ জন্ম দিছিল। ইয়াৰ লগতে বৃহৎ পৰিমাণৰ ধ্বংস, লুণ্ঠন আৰু অৰ্থনৈতিক বিঘিনি ঘটিছিল।

### Vijayanagar & Bahmani Kingdoms — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/medieval-indian-history-sec/vijayanagar-bahmani/
Summary: Practice vijayanagar & bahmani kingdoms questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Who founded the Vijayanagar empire?
A: Harihara I and Bukka I, two brothers, in 1336 AD.
Q: Who was the mentor of Harihara and Bukka?
A: The famous saint Vidyaranya (Madhava) of the Sringeri math.
Q: Which dynasty did Harihara and Bukka found?
A: The Sangama dynasty, the first dynasty of Vijayanagar.
Q: Which dynasty founded by Narasimha Saluva ruled Vijayanagar?
A: The Saluva dynasty, the second dynasty of Vijayanagar.
Q: Which dynasty founded by Narasa Nayaka ruled Vijayanagar?
A: The Tuluva dynasty, the third dynasty of Vijayanagar.
Q: Who was the greatest ruler of the Vijayanagar empire?
A: Krishnadevaraya of the Tuluva dynasty (1509–1529 AD).
Q: Who was the mentor of Krishnadevaraya?
A: Tenali Ramakrishna, the witty court poet, and the sage Vyasatirtha.
Q: Which Telugu work did Krishnadevaraya write?
A: Amuktamalyada, a poetic work on the story of Andal.
Q: What were the eight poets of Krishnadevaraya's court called?
A: Ashtadiggajas.
Q: Which foreign travellers visited the Vijayanagar court?
A: Nicolo Conti, Abdur Razzak, Paes and Nuniz.
Q: Which traveller described Hampi as a city 'equal to Rome'?
A: Domingo Paes, the Portuguese traveller.
Q: Which traveller called the Vijayanagar empire the richest kingdom in the world?
A: Fernao Nuniz, the Portuguese traveller.
Q: What was the system of provincial administration in Vijayanagar called?
A: The Nayankara system, where the emperor appointed Nayakas as provincial governors.
Q: What was the local self-government unit in the Vijayanagar empire?
A: The village assembly, which managed local affairs through elders and temples.
Q: Who was the founder of the Bahmani kingdom?
A: Ala-ud-din Hasan Bahman Shah (Zafar Khan), in 1347 AD.
Q: What was the capital of the Bahmani kingdom?
A: Gulbarga (later Bidar).
Q: Who was the greatest ruler of the Bahmani kingdom?
A: Mahmud Gawan, the prime minister, though the title is usually given to rulers; the greatest ruler was Muhammad Shah III under Gawan's guidance.
Q: How many provinces (Taraf) was the Bahmani kingdom divided into?
A: Four provinces, each under a governor called Tarafdar.
Q: Which battle decided the fate of the Vijayanagar empire?
A: The battle of Talikota (1565 AD), in which Vijayanagar was defeated.
Q: Which rulers fought the battle of Talikota against Vijayanagar?
A: The combined forces of the Deccan Sultanates (Ahmadnagar, Bijapur, Golconda, Bidar and Berar).
Q: Which city was the capital of Vijayanagar?
A: Hampi (Vijayanagara) on the banks of the Tungabhadra river.
Q: Who built the famous Vitthalaswami temple at Hampi?
A: Krishnadevaraya.
Q: Which foreign traveller was an ambassador of the Timurid ruler at the Vijayanagar court?
A: Abdur Razzak, the Persian ambassador.
Q: What was the main reason for the rivalry between Vijayanagar and the Bahmani kingdom?
A: The struggle for the fertile Raichur doab between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers, and control over the coastal trade.
Q: What was the title of the Vijayanagar rulers?
A: Maharajadhiraja (Great King of Kings).
Q: Who was the founder of the fourth dynasty of Vijayanagar (Aravidu)?
A: Tirumala, brother of Rama Raya.
Q: Who was the regent who virtually ruled Vijayanagar before the battle of Talikota?
A: Rama Raya, the regent of the weak king Sadashiva.
Q: Which Mughal emperor is said to have invaded the Deccan and defeated the remnants of Vijayanagar?
A: Aurangzeb, who annexed the southern states in the late 17th century.
Q: Which Bahmani ruler shifted the capital to Bidar?
A: Ahmad Shah Wali I.
Q: Which Sultan of the Deccan built the famous Gol Gumbaz at Bijapur?
A: Muhammad Adil Shah of Bijapur.
Q: Which city was founded by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah?
A: Hyderabad (Bhaganagar).
Q: What was the famous horse trade route that brought horses to Vijayanagar?
A: The Arab and Portuguese horse trade through the western ports.
Q: What was the main source of revenue of the Vijayanagar empire?
A: Land revenue, which was generally one-sixth of the produce.
Q: What was the water tank built by Krishnadevaraya at Hampi called?
A: The Kamalapuram tank, part of the irrigation system.
Q: Which dynasty of Vijayanagar came from the Kolar region?
A: The Tuluva dynasty.
Q: What was the royal emblem of Vijayanagar?
A: The boar (Varaha).
Q: Who was the founder of the Adil Shahi dynasty of Bijapur?
A: Yusuf Adil Khan.
Q: Who was the founder of the Qutb Shahi dynasty of Golconda?
A: Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk (Sultan Quli).
Q: Which of the five Deccan Sultanates had its capital at Ahmadnagar?
A: The Nizam Shahi dynasty.
Q: Which Bahmani general, a Persian, became very powerful and later the kingdom broke up?
A: Mahmud Gawan, whose execution weakened the kingdom leading to its breakup.
Q: In which year was the Bahmani kingdom divided into five states?
A: Around 1490 AD, after the death of Mahmud Gawan.
Q: Which city was the capital of the Nizam Shahi dynasty?
A: Ahmadnagar.
Q: Who was the famous minister of Vijayanagar under whom trade and agriculture flourished?
A: Saluva Timma, minister of Krishnadevaraya.
Q: What did the Portuguese traveller Paes say about Krishnadevaraya's court?
A: He praised it as one of the most splendid courts in the world.
Q: Which Vijayanagar king was known as 'Amaruka'?
A: Krishnadevaraya, who was also called 'Andhra Bhoja'.
Q: Which temple at Hampi is dedicated to Lord Vitthala?
A: The Vitthalaswami temple, famous for its stone chariot.
Q: Who founded the city of Golconda?
A: The Qutb Shahi dynasty, with the fort built by Sultan Quli.
Q: What was the famous diamond of Golconda?
A: The Kohinoor diamond, which was mined in the Golconda region.
Q: Which Vijayanagar king built the city of Vijayanagara on the Tungabhadra?
A: Harihara I and Bukka I founded the city.
Q: Which Sultanate was annexed first by the Mughals?
A: Ahmadnagar, which fell to the Mughals in the early 17th century.
Q: Who founded the Vijayanagar Empire and who was its greatest ruler?
A: The Vijayanagar Empire was founded in 1336 AD by the brothers Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty, guided by the sage Vidyaranya. Its greatest ruler was Krishnadevaraya (1509-1529) of the Tuluva dynasty.
Q: Who founded the Bahmani Kingdom and what were its capitals?
A: The Bahmani Kingdom was founded in 1347 AD by Hasan Gangu (Alauddin Bahman Shah). Its first capital was Gulbarga, which was later shifted to Bidar.
Q: What was the Battle of Talikota and when did it take place?
A: The Battle of Talikota (also called Rakshasa-Tangadi) took place in 1565 AD. The combined forces of the Deccan Sultanates defeated the Vijayanagar army and killed the regent Ramaraya. The capital Vijayanagar was sacked and abandoned, leading to the decline of the empire.
Q: Who was Krishnadevaraya and what were his achievements?
A: Krishnadevaraya (1509-1529) of the Tuluva dynasty was the greatest Vijayanagar ruler. He conquered Raichur and Udayagiri, wrote the Telugu work Amuktamalyada, patronised the Ashtadiggajas (eight poets) and took titles such as Andhra Bhoja and Kannada Rajya Rama Ramana.
Q: What were the five Deccan Sultanates that arose from the Bahmani Kingdom?
A: After the decline of the Bahmani Kingdom, it broke up into five sultanates: Ahmadnagar, Bijapur, Berar, Bidar and Golconda. These sultanates later combined against Vijayanagar at the Battle of Talikota in 1565.
Q: Why did Vijayanagar and the Bahmani Kingdom fight each other?
A: The main causes were the desire to control the fertile Raichur Doab between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers, and the rich Krishna-Godavari delta. The two powers fought continuously for about two hundred years, usually without a decisive result.
Q: বিজয়নগৰ সাম্ৰাজ্য কোনে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল আৰু শ্ৰেষ্ঠ শাসক কোন আছিল?
A: বিজয়নগৰ সাম্ৰাজ্য খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দ ১৩৩৬ চনত সংগম ৰাজবংশৰ ভাতৃ হৰিহৰ আৰু বুক্কই, ঋষি বিদ্যাৰণ্যৰ পথপ্ৰদৰ্শনত প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল। ইয়াৰ শ্ৰেষ্ঠ শাসক আছিল তুলুৱ ৰাজবংশৰ কৃষ্ণদেৱৰায় (১৫০৯-১৫২৯)।
Q: বাহমনী ৰাজ্য কোনে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল আৰু ইয়াৰ ৰাজধানী কি আছিল?
A: বাহমনী ৰাজ্য খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দ ১৩৪৭ চনত হাছান গংগুৱে (আলাউদ্দিন বাহমন শ্বাহ) প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল। ইয়াৰ প্ৰথম ৰাজধানী আছিল গুলবৰ্গা, যি পিছত বিদাৰলৈ স্থানান্তৰিত হয়।
Q: তালিকোটা যুদ্ধ কি আছিল আৰু কেতিয়া হৈছিল?
A: তালিকোটা যুদ্ধ (ৰাক্ষস-তাংগাদিও বোলা হয়) খ্ৰীষ্টাব্দ ১৫৬৫ চনত হৈছিল। দাক্ষিণাত্য চুলতানীসমূহৰ যুটীয়া সেনাই বিজয়নগৰ সেনাক পৰাস্ত কৰি ৰাজপ্ৰতিনিধি ৰামৰায়ক নিহত কৰিছিল। ৰাজধানী বিজয়নগৰ লুণ্ঠিত আৰু পৰিত্যক্ত হৈছিল, যাৰ ফলত সাম্ৰাজ্যৰ অৱনতি ঘটিছিল।
Q: কৃষ্ণদেৱৰায় কোন আছিল আৰু তেওঁৰ কৃতিত্ব কি আছিল?
A: তুলুৱ ৰাজবংশৰ কৃষ্ণদেৱৰায় (১৫০৯-১৫২৯) শ্ৰেষ্ঠ বিজয়নগৰ শাসক আছিল। তেওঁ ৰায়চুৰ আৰু উদয়গিৰি জয় কৰিছিল, তেলেগু ৰচনা অমুক্তমাল্যদ লিখিছিল, অষ্টদিগ্গজ (আঠজন কবি)ক পৃষ্ঠপোষকতা কৰিছিল আৰু অন্ধ্ৰ ভোজ তথা কন্নড় ৰাজ্য ৰাম ৰমণৰ দৰে উপাধি গ্ৰহণ কৰিছিল।
Q: বাহমনী ৰাজ্যৰ পৰা উঠি অহা পাঁচটা দাক্ষিণাত্য চুলতানী কি কি?
A: বাহমনী ৰাজ্যৰ অৱনতিৰ পিছত ই পাঁচটা চুলতানীত বিভক্ত হৈছিল: আহমদনগৰ, বিজাপুৰ, বেৰাৰ, বিদাৰ আৰু গোলকোণ্ডা। এই চুলতানীসমূহে পিছত ১৫৬৫ চনত তালিকোটা যুদ্ধত বিজয়নগৰৰ বিৰুদ্ধে একগোট হৈছিল।
Q: বিজয়নগৰ আৰু বাহমনী ৰাজ্যই কিয় পৰস্পৰে যুদ্ধ কৰিছিল?
A: মূল কাৰণ আছিল কৃষ্ণা আৰু তুংগভদ্ৰা নদীৰ মাজৰ উৰ্বৰ ৰায়চুৰ দুআব তথা সমৃদ্ধ কৃষ্ণা-গোদাবৰী বদ্বীপ নিয়ন্ত্ৰণৰ ইচ্ছা। দুয়ো শক্তি প্ৰায় দুশ বছৰ ধৰি অবিৰত যুদ্ধ কৰিছিল, সাধাৰণতে কোনো নিষ্পত্তিমূলক ফল নোহোৱাকৈ।

### British Conquest & Consolidation (Plassey & Buxar)
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/modern-indian-history-sec/british-conquest-plassey-buxar/
Summary: Practice british conquest & consolidation (plassey & buxar) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free.
Q: In which year was the battle of Plassey fought?
A: 1757 AD.
Q: Who was the Nawab of Bengal at the time of the battle of Plassey?
A: Siraj-ud-daula.
Q: Who led the English forces at the battle of Plassey?
A: Robert Clive.
Q: Who betrayed Siraj-ud-daula in the battle of Plassey?
A: Mir Jafar, his commander-in-chief, along with Rai Durlabh and others.
Q: Who was made the Nawab of Bengal after the battle of Plassey?
A: Mir Jafar.
Q: What was the result of the battle of Plassey for the English?
A: The English gained political power and the control of the Bengal treasury.
Q: In which year was the battle of Buxar fought?
A: 1764 AD.
Q: Who fought against the English at the battle of Buxar?
A: The combined forces of Mir Qasim (Nawab of Bengal), Shuja-ud-daula (Nawab of Awadh) and Shah Alam II (Mughal emperor).
Q: Who was the Nawab of Bengal at the time of the battle of Buxar?
A: Mir Qasim.
Q: Who led the English forces at the battle of Buxar?
A: Major Hector Munro.
Q: What was the result of the battle of Buxar?
A: A decisive victory for the English, leading to the treaty of Allahabad.
Q: Which treaty was signed after the battle of Buxar in 1765?
A: The treaty of Allahabad.
Q: Who was granted the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa by the treaty of Allahabad?
A: The English East India Company.
Q: Who signed the treaty of Allahabad on behalf of the Mughal emperor?
A: Shah Alam II, who granted the Diwani to the Company.
Q: What was the Dual Government (Dual System) of Bengal?
A: A system in which the Company collected revenue (Diwani) while the Nawab remained responsible for administration (Nizamat).
Q: Who introduced the Dual Government in Bengal?
A: Robert Clive, in 1765 AD.
Q: When was the Dual Government abolished?
A: In 1772 AD, when Warren Hastings took over the administration of Bengal.
Q: Who was the first Governor General of Bengal?
A: Warren Hastings (1772–1785).
Q: Who was the Nawab of Bengal who tried to free himself from the Company's control?
A: Mir Qasim.
Q: What was the First Carnatic War?
A: A war between the English and the French in South India (1746–1748), part of the Austrian War of Succession.
Q: Which treaty ended the First Carnatic War?
A: The treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748 AD).
Q: Who captured Madras in the First Carnatic War?
A: The French under Dupleix.
Q: Which treaty ended the Second Carnatic War?
A: The treaty of Pondicherry (1754 AD).
Q: Who was the Nawab of Arcot in the Second Carnatic War?
A: Muhammad Ali (supported by the English) and Chanda Sahib (supported by the French).
Q: Which treaty ended the Third Carnatic War?
A: The treaty of Paris (1763 AD).
Q: Which battle decisively defeated the French in the Third Carnatic War?
A: The battle of Wandiwash (1760 AD), led by Sir Eyre Coote.
Q: Who was the founder of the Kingdom of Mysore's power under Haidar Ali?
A: Haidar Ali, a soldier who rose to the position of the de facto ruler of Mysore.
Q: Who won the First Anglo-Mysore War?
A: It was inconclusive; the war ended with the treaty of Madras (1769 AD).
Q: Who was the ruler of Mysore who died during the Second Anglo-Mysore War?
A: Haidar Ali (1782 AD), who was succeeded by his son Tipu Sultan.
Q: Which treaty ended the Second Anglo-Mysore War?
A: The treaty of Mangalore (1784 AD).
Q: Which Governor General fought the Third Anglo-Mysore War?
A: Lord Cornwallis.
Q: Which treaty ended the Third Anglo-Mysore War?
A: The treaty of Seringapatam (1792 AD).
Q: Who fought the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War?
A: The English under Lord Wellesley against Tipu Sultan.
Q: In which year was Tipu Sultan killed?
A: 1799 AD, during the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War at Seringapatam.
Q: What happened to Mysore after the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War?
A: Mysore was restored to the Wodeyar dynasty under the Company's subsidiary system.
Q: Who was the first Governor General of India (under the Charter Act of 1833)?
A: William Bentinck.
Q: Which Governor General introduced the Doctrine of Lapse?
A: Lord Dalhousie.
Q: Which states were annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse?
A: Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur and several others.
Q: Who was the last Peshwa who accepted the subsidiary alliance?
A: Baji Rao II.
Q: What was the Subsidiary Alliance system introduced by Lord Wellesley?
A: A system in which an Indian ruler accepted British troops in his territory and paid for them, losing external sovereignty.
Q: Which Nawab of Awadh accepted the subsidiary alliance?
A: Saadat Ali Khan.
Q: Who fought the First Anglo-Maratha War?
A: The English East India Company and the Maratha Confederacy.
Q: Which treaty ended the First Anglo-Maratha War?
A: The treaty of Salbai (1782 AD).
Q: Which treaty was signed between the British and the Peshwa Baji Rao II in 1802?
A: The treaty of Bassein.
Q: Who was the Maratha leader who was defeated at the battle of Assaye?
A: The Scindia forces were defeated by the English under Arthur Wellesley.
Q: Which battle in the Third Anglo-Maratha War ended the Peshwa's power?
A: The battle of Khadki (Kirkee) and Ashti (1818 AD).
Q: Which Governor General abolished the office of Peshwa?
A: Lord Hastings.
Q: Who fought the First Anglo-Sikh War?
A: The English and the Sikh kingdom of Lahore under the Dogra regents.
Q: Which treaty ended the First Anglo-Sikh War?
A: The treaty of Lahore (1846 AD).
Q: Which treaty ended the Second Anglo-Sikh War?
A: The treaty of Lahore (1849 AD), which annexed the Punjab.
Q: Who annexed the Punjab in 1849 AD?
A: Lord Dalhousie, after the Second Anglo-Sikh War.
Q: Which king of Burma (Myanmar) fought the three Anglo-Burmese Wars?
A: King Thibaw was the last, defeated in the Third Anglo-Burmese War (1885).
Q: Which Governor General annexed Awadh in 1856 AD?
A: Lord Dalhousie, on the grounds of misgovernment.
Q: Who was the ruler of Awadh annexed by the British in 1856?
A: Wajid Ali Shah.
Q: Which French settlement remained with France until 1954?
A: Pondicherry and its enclaves.
Q: Which treaty gave the English the revenue of the Bengal province in 1765?
A: The treaty of Allahabad.
Q: When was the Battle of Plassey fought?
A: On 23 June 1757.
Q: Who was the Nawab of Bengal at the time of the Battle of Plassey?
A: Siraj-ud-Daulah.
Q: Who led the British forces at the Battle of Plassey?
A: Robert Clive.
Q: Who was Mir Jafar?
A: The commander of Siraj-ud-Daulah who betrayed him at Plassey and became the Nawab of Bengal.
Q: What was the result of the Battle of Plassey?
A: The British gained control over Bengal and Siraj-ud-Daulah was killed.
Q: When was the Battle of Buxar fought?
A: On 22 October 1764.
Q: Who fought against the British in the Battle of Buxar?
A: Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II.
Q: Who was Mir Qasim?
A: The Nawab of Bengal who revolted against the British after being made Nawab in place of Mir Jafar.
Q: What was the result of the Battle of Buxar?
A: The British won and gained the right to collect revenue (Diwani) of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
Q: Who got the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa?
A: The East India Company, in 1765.
Q: What was the Treaty of Allahabad?
A: The treaty signed in 1765 by which Shah Alam II granted the Diwani to the Company and the Company paid an annual tribute.
Q: Who signed the Treaty of Allahabad?
A: Robert Clive on behalf of the Company, and Shah Alam II and Shuja-ud-Daulah.
Q: Who introduced the Dual Government system in Bengal?
A: Robert Clive, in 1765.
Q: What was the Dual Government system?
A: The system in which the Company collected revenue (Diwani) while the Nawab remained responsible for administration (Nizamat).
Q: Why is the Battle of Plassey important in Indian history?
A: The Battle of Plassey, fought on 23 June 1757, made the English East India Company the real power behind the throne of Bengal. After defeating Siraj-ud-Daulah with the help of Mir Jafar's treachery, the Company gained money, territory and trade privileges, and began its rise from trader to ruler.
Q: What were the main causes of the Battle of Plassey?
A: The main causes were the misuse of dastaks (free trade passes), the unauthorised fortification of Calcutta by the English, the refusal to obey the Nawab, and the clash between Siraj-ud-Daulah and the Company. The capture of Calcutta and the Black Hole episode led Clive to retaliate and plot the Nawab's overthrow.
Q: How was the Battle of Buxar different from the Battle of Plassey?
A: Plassey (1757) was a short battle won largely through conspiracy, while Buxar (1764) was a full and decisive battle. At Buxar the English under Hector Munro defeated the combined armies of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II, which firmly established British rule in Bengal.
Q: What was the Treaty of Allahabad and what did the Company gain from it?
A: The Treaty of Allahabad (1765) was concluded by Robert Clive after Buxar. Shuja-ud-Daulah got back Awadh, Shah Alam II got Kara and Allahabad, and most importantly the Mughal emperor granted the Company the Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa on 12 August 1765.
Q: What was the Dual Government and who abolished it?
A: The Dual Government (1765-1772) was a system in which the Company held the Diwani (revenue) while the Nawab held the Nizamat (police and criminal justice). It gave the Company power without responsibility and was abolished by Warren Hastings in 1772.
Q: Why is Buxar called more decisive than Plassey?
A: Buxar is called more decisive because the English there defeated not only a Nawab but a grand alliance of Bengal, Awadh and the Mughal emperor. The victory led directly to the grant of the Diwani in 1765, which gave the Company legal control over the revenues of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, making it the true ruler.
Q: ভাৰতীয় ইতিহাসত পলাশী যুদ্ধ কিয় গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: ২৩ জুন ১৭৫৭ চনত সংঘটিত পলাশী যুদ্ধই ইংৰাজ ইষ্ট ইণ্ডিয়া কোম্পানীক বংগৰ সিংহাসনৰ প্ৰকৃত শক্তি কৰি তুলিছিল। মিৰজাফৰ বিশ্বাসঘাতৰ সহায়ত ছিৰাজ-উদ-দৌলাহক পৰাস্ত কৰাৰ পিছত কোম্পানীয়ে ধন, ভূখণ্ড আৰু বাণিজ্যিক সুবিধা লাভ কৰিছিল আৰু বণিকৰ পৰা শাসকলৈ উত্থান আৰম্ভ কৰিছিল।
Q: পলাশী যুদ্ধৰ মূল কাৰণসমূহ কি কি আছিল?
A: মূল কাৰণসমূহ আছিল দস্তক (মুক্ত বাণিজ্য পথ) ৰ অপব্যৱহাৰ, ইংৰাজসকলে কৰা অনুমতিহীন কলিকতা দুৰ্গীকৰণ, নৱাবক মানিবলৈ অস্বীকৃতি, আৰু ছিৰাজ-উদ-দৌলাহ আৰু কোম্পানীৰ মাজৰ সংঘাত। কলিকতা দখল আৰু ব্লেক হ'ল পৰিঘটনাই ক্লাইভক প্ৰতিশোধ ল'বলৈ আৰু নৱাবক উৎখাত কৰিবলৈ ষড়যন্ত্ৰ কৰিবলৈ বাধ্য কৰিছিল।
Q: বক্সাৰ যুদ্ধ পলাশী যুদ্ধৰ পৰা কেনেকৈ বেলেগ আছিল?
A: পলাশী (১৭৫৭) এটা চুটি যুদ্ধ আছিল যি মূলতঃ ষড়যন্ত্ৰৰ জৰিয়তে জিকা হৈছিল, আনহাতে বক্সাৰ (১৭৬৪) এটা সম্পূৰ্ণ আৰু নিৰ্ণায়ক যুদ্ধ আছিল। বক্সাৰত হেক্টৰ মুনৰোৰ নেতৃত্বত ইংৰাজসকলে মিৰ কাচিম, শুজা-উদ-দৌলাহ আৰু শাহ আলম দ্বিতীয়ৰ সংযুক্ত সেনাক পৰাস্ত কৰিছিল, যিয়ে বংগত ব্ৰিটিছ শাসন দৃঢ়ভাৱে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল।
Q: এলাহাবাদ সন্ধি কি আছিল আৰু কোম্পানীয়ে ইয়াৰ পৰা কি লাভ কৰিছিল?
A: এলাহাবাদ সন্ধি (১৭৬৫) বক্সাৰৰ পিছত ৰবাৰ্ট ক্লাইভে সম্পন্ন কৰিছিল। শুজা-উদ-দৌলাহে অৱধ ঘূৰাই পাইছিল, শাহ আলম দ্বিতীয়ই কাৰা আৰু এলাহাবাদ পাইছিল, আৰু আটাইতকৈ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণভাৱে মোগল সম্ৰাটে ১২ আগষ্ট ১৭৬৫ চনত কোম্পানীক বংগ, বিহাৰ আৰু ওড়িশাৰ দেৱানী অধিকাৰ প্ৰদান কৰিছিল।
Q: দ্বৈত শাসন কি আছিল আৰু কোনে বিলুপ্ত কৰিছিল?
A: দ্বৈত শাসন (১৭৬৫-১৭৭২) এটা ব্যৱস্থা আছিল য'ত কোম্পানীয়ে দেৱানী (ৰাজহ) আৰু নৱাবে নিজামত (আৰক্ষী আৰু ফৌজদাৰী ন্যায়) ধাৰণ কৰিছিল। ই কোম্পানীক দায়িত্ব নোহোৱাকৈ ক্ষমতা দিছিল আৰু ৱাৰেন হেষ্টিংছে ১৭৭২ চনত ইয়াক বিলুপ্ত কৰিছিল।
Q: বক্সাৰক পলাশীতকৈ অধিক নিৰ্ণায়ক কিয় কোৱা হয়?
A: বক্সাৰক অধিক নিৰ্ণায়ক কোৱা হয় কাৰণ তাত ইংৰাজসকলে কেৱল এজন নৱাবক নহয়, বংগ, অৱধ আৰু মোগল সম্ৰাটৰ এটা মহা-মিত্ৰতাক পৰাস্ত কৰিছিল। এই বিজয়ে পোনপটীয়াকৈ ১৭৬৫ চনত দেৱানী প্ৰদানলৈ লৈ গৈছিল, যিয়ে কোম্পানীক বংগ, বিহাৰ আৰু ওড়িশাৰ ৰাজহৰ ওপৰত বৈধ নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ দিছিল, তেওঁলোকক প্ৰকৃত শাসক কৰি তুলিছিল।

### British Economic & Land Revenue Policies — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/modern-indian-history-sec/british-economic-land-policies/
Summary: Practice british economic & land revenue policies questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: What was the Permanent Settlement?
A: A land revenue system in which the revenue demand was fixed permanently, introduced in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
Q: Who introduced the Permanent Settlement?
A: Lord Cornwallis, in 1793 AD.
Q: Who were the owners of land under the Permanent Settlement?
A: The Zamindars, who were declared the owners of the land in return for paying fixed revenue.
Q: How much of the revenue did the Zamindar keep under the Permanent Settlement?
A: One-tenth of the revenue, while the remaining nine-tenths went to the government.
Q: Which was the main drawback of the Permanent Settlement?
A: The exploitation of the peasants by the zamindars, who were free to increase their share.
Q: Who introduced the Ryotwari system?
A: Alexander Read and Thomas Munro.
Q: Who was the Governor General who implemented the Ryotwari system in Madras?
A: Thomas Munro, under Lord Hastings.
Q: In which provinces was the Ryotwari system introduced?
A: Madras, Bombay and parts of Assam.
Q: Who was the owner of land under the Ryotwari system?
A: The individual cultivator (ryot), who paid revenue directly to the government.
Q: What was the rate of revenue in the Ryotwari system?
A: About 50 percent of the produce in some areas, later revised.
Q: Who introduced the Mahalwari system?
A: Holt Mackenzie.
Q: Who implemented the Mahalwari system in practice?
A: William Bentinck, with the help of James Thomson in the North-Western Provinces.
Q: In which areas was the Mahalwari system introduced?
A: The North-Western Provinces, Punjab, Central India and parts of the Gangetic valley.
Q: Who was considered the owner of the land in the Mahalwari system?
A: The village community (mahal) or its representatives, the village headmen.
Q: What was the term of revenue settlement in the Mahalwari system?
A: Usually 20 to 30 years.
Q: What was the 'Drain of Wealth' theory?
A: The continuous transfer of India's wealth to England without any equivalent return.
Q: Who propounded the 'Drain of Wealth' theory?
A: Dadabhai Naoroji, who presented it in his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.
Q: What did Dadabhai Naoroji estimate as the annual drain of wealth?
A: About £15 million annually in the 1860s.
Q: What was the 'Home Charges'?
A: The expenses of the Indian government paid in England, such as the salaries and pensions of British officials.
Q: Which system replaced the system of revenue farming before the Permanent Settlement?
A: The Company initially used revenue farming (ijaradari) and then settled directly with the zamindars.
Q: What was the economic condition of the Indian peasantry under the British land revenue systems?
A: They were impoverished by high revenue demands, indebtedness and frequent famines.
Q: What was the 'Commercialisation of Agriculture'?
A: The shift of Indian agriculture from food crops to cash crops (like indigo, cotton, opium) for the world market.
Q: Which crop cultivation was forced on the peasants of Bengal?
A: Indigo, through oppressive contracts.
Q: What was the 'Indigo Revolt'?
A: The uprising of indigo peasants in Bengal in 1859–60 against the oppressive planters.
Q: Which landlord class emerged in Bengal after the Permanent Settlement?
A: A new class of absentee zamindars and a rentier class of middlemen.
Q: What was the result of the revenue auctions in Bengal?
A: Many old zamindars lost their estates, and a new class of urban money-lenders became landlords.
Q: What was the main source of British profit from India?
A: Land revenue, trade monopoly, and the export of raw materials.
Q: Which policy of the British destroyed the Indian handicrafts?
A: The policy of free trade, which flooded India with cheap British machine-made goods.
Q: Which British act prohibited the Indian cotton manufacturers from exporting to England?
A: The Calico Acts and the duties on Indian textiles.
Q: What was the condition of Indian industry under British rule?
A: The traditional industries declined while modern industries developed very slowly, mainly under British ownership.
Q: Who was the first Indian to be elected to the British Parliament?
A: Dadabhai Naoroji, elected in 1892.
Q: What was the 'economic drain' according to R.C. Dutt?
A: The continuous export of India's wealth to Britain leading to India's poverty.
Q: Which book of R.C. Dutt analysed the British economic policies?
A: The Economic History of India.
Q: What was the 'Famine Policy' of the British?
A: A laissez-faire policy that failed to provide relief, leading to millions of deaths in famines like 1876–78 and 1899–1900.
Q: Which famine commission was set up after the 1876–78 famine?
A: The Famine Commission headed by Richard Strachey (1880).
Q: What was the 'Zamindari' system in the Assam valley?
A: It was not the same as Bengal; in Assam the revenue was settled with the ryots under the Ryotwari pattern.
Q: Who introduced the Ryotwari system in Assam?
A: David Scott, the first British Governor of Assam, in 1826–28.
Q: What was the 'Mozumi' (Mauzadari) system in Assam?
A: A revenue system in which the revenue was settled with the village headmen (Mauzadars).
Q: Who was the officer in charge of revenue collection in a 'Mauza' in Assam?
A: The Mauzadar.
Q: What was the 'Valuation' policy of the British in Assam?
A: The periodic revision of revenue rates, which often increased the burden on the peasants.
Q: What was the impact of the British revenue policies on the tea industry of Assam?
A: The tea gardens received cheap land grants, promoting the growth of the tea industry.
Q: Which system of land revenue was prevalent in the tea gardens of Assam?
A: Special low-rate leases (Nij and Chukaniti) granted to the tea planters.
Q: What was the 'Permanent Settlement' for the peasantry in the long run?
A: It made the peasants tenants-at-will and subject to the exactions of the zamindars.
Q: Which Governor General introduced the revenue settlement in the North-Western Provinces?
A: Lord Hastings and later William Bentinck.
Q: Who wrote the book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'?
A: Dadabhai Naoroji.
Q: What was the condition of the peasantry under the Ryotwari system?
A: They were burdened with high taxes and faced land alienation when they failed to pay.
Q: What was the 'Subordinate Land System' in Assam called?
A: It referred to the system of granting land to subordinate tenants and tea planters.
Q: What was the main effect of the British land revenue policy on the Indian economy?
A: It transformed the agrarian structure, impoverished the peasantry and facilitated the drain of wealth.
Q: Which was the first land revenue settlement made by the British in India?
A: The settlement with the zamindars of Bengal in 1793 (Permanent Settlement).
Q: What was the 'Tanka' system in Assam?
A: A system of paying land revenue partly in cash and partly in kind.
Q: What was the effect of the deindustrialisation on Indian craftsmen?
A: Millions of weavers and artisans lost their livelihood and were forced into agriculture.
Q: Who established the first modern cotton mill in India?
A: Cowasjee Nanabhoy Davar, who set up the first mill in Bombay in 1854.
Q: What was the 'First Jute Mill' location in India?
A: Rishra (near Calcutta), established in 1855.
Q: What was the condition of the Indian economy under the British after 1857?
A: India was transformed into a supplier of raw materials and a market for British goods.
Q: Who founded the Bengal Bonded Warehouse Association?
A: Dwarkanath Tagore, who also started the Union Bank of Calcutta.
Q: What was the 'Indigo Planters' role in the British economy?
A: They produced indigo for the European dye market, exploiting the peasants.
Q: Who led the Indigo Rebellion of 1859-60?
A: The revolt was led by the ryots of Nadia district, with Dinabandhu Mitra's 'Nil Darpan' highlighting it.
Q: What was the Permanent Settlement?
A: A revenue system introduced in 1793 fixing the land revenue permanently with the zamindars.
Q: Who introduced the Permanent Settlement?
A: Lord Cornwallis, in 1793.
Q: In which areas was the Permanent Settlement introduced?
A: In Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
Q: What was the Ryotwari System?
A: A revenue system in which the settlement was made directly with the ryots (peasants).
Q: Who introduced the Ryotwari System?
A: Alexander Read and Thomas Munro, in the Madras Presidency.
Q: What was the Mahalwari System?
A: A revenue system in which the settlement was made with the village community (mahal).
Q: Who introduced the Mahalwari System?
A: Holt Mackenzie, in the North-Western Provinces, in 1822.
Q: What was the drain of wealth theory?
A: The theory that British rule drained India's wealth to England, propounded by Dadabhai Naoroji.
Q: Who propounded the drain of wealth theory?
A: Dadabhai Naoroji.
Q: What was de-industrialisation in India?
A: The decline of Indian handicraft industries due to British policies and the import of cheap machine-made goods.
Q: What was the effect of the British revenue policies on the peasants?
A: The peasants were heavily taxed, leading to poverty, indebtedness and famines.
Q: What was the effect of the Permanent Settlement on the zamindars?
A: The zamindars became owners of land and the peasants were reduced to tenants-at-will.
Q: What was the Charter Act of 1833?
A: An act which abolished the Company's commercial functions and made it purely an administrative body.
Q: Who introduced the Permanent Settlement and when?
A: The Permanent Settlement was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793 in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. Under it, zamindars were recognised as landowners and had to pay a fixed annual revenue to the Company, which could never be increased.
Q: What is the difference between the Permanent, Ryotwari and Mahalwari systems?
A: In the Permanent Settlement the revenue was fixed with the zamindars; in the Ryotwari System it was settled directly with the individual cultivator (ryot); and in the Mahalwari System it was settled with the village or mahal community. They were introduced in Bengal (1793), Madras and Bombay, and the North-Western Provinces (1822) respectively.
Q: What was the Sunset Law?
A: Under the Permanent Settlement, the Sunset Law said that if a zamindar did not deposit the fixed revenue by sunset of the appointed day, his land would be auctioned. It made revenue collection strict but ruined many zamindars.
Q: What was the commercialisation of agriculture?
A: Commercialisation of agriculture means the shift from growing food crops to cash crops such as indigo, opium, cotton, jute and tea for sale in the market. The British encouraged it so that India would supply raw materials to British industries, but it increased peasant debt and contributed to famines.
Q: What is meant by de-industrialisation and drain of wealth?
A: De-industrialisation means the decline of Indian handicraft industries, especially textiles, due to the import of cheap British goods. Drain of wealth means the one-way transfer of Indian wealth to Britain through revenue, salaries, pensions and trade. Both were exposed by leaders like Dadabhai Naoroji and R. C. Dutt.
Q: Which system was introduced by Holt Mackenzie and where?
A: Holt Mackenzie introduced the Mahalwari System in 1822 in the North-Western Provinces and parts of Central India. In this system the unit of revenue was the mahal (village or group of villages), and the revenue was settled with the village community. It was revised in 1833 under Lord William Bentinck.
Q: স্থায়ী বন্দোবস্ত কোনে প্ৰৱৰ্তন কৰিছিল আৰু কেতিয়া?
A: স্থায়ী বন্দোবস্ত লৰ্ড কৰ্নৱালিছে ১৭৯৩ চনত বংগ, বিহাৰ আৰু ওড়িশাত প্ৰৱৰ্তন কৰিছিল। ইয়াৰ অধীনত জমিদাৰসকলক ভূমিৰ মালিক হিচাপে স্বীকৃতি দিয়া হৈছিল আৰু তেওঁলোকে কোম্পানীক এটা নিৰ্দিষ্ট বাৰ্ষিক ৰাজহ দিব লাগিছিল, যি কেতিয়াও বৃদ্ধি কৰিব নোৱাৰি।
Q: স্থায়ী, ৰায়ৎৱাৰী আৰু মহলৱাৰী ব্যৱস্থাৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: স্থায়ী বন্দোবস্তত ৰাজহ জমিদাৰসকলৰ সৈতে স্থিৰ কৰা হৈছিল; ৰায়ৎৱাৰী ব্যৱস্থাত ব্যক্তিগত কৃষক (ৰায়ৎ)ৰ সৈতে পোনপটীয়াকৈ; আৰু মহলৱাৰী ব্যৱস্থাত গাঁও বা মহল সম্প্ৰদায়ৰ সৈতে। ইয়াক ক্ৰমে বংগ (১৭৯৩), মাদ্ৰাজ আৰু বোম্বাই, আৰু উত্তৰ-পশ্চিম প্ৰদেশত (১৮২২) প্ৰৱৰ্তন কৰা হৈছিল।
Q: সূৰ্যঅস্ত আইন কি আছিল?
A: স্থায়ী বন্দোবস্তৰ অধীনত সূৰ্যঅস্ত আইনে কৈছিল যে নিৰ্ধাৰিত দিনৰ সূৰ্যঅস্তৰ ভিতৰত কোনো জমিদাৰে নিৰ্দিষ্ট ৰাজহ জমা নকৰিলে তেওঁৰ ভূমি নিলাম কৰা হ'ব। ই ৰাজহ সংগ্ৰহ কঠোৰ কৰিছিল কিন্তু বহু জমিদাৰক ধ্বংস কৰিছিল।
Q: কৃষিৰ বাণিজ্যিকীকৰণ কি?
A: কৃষিৰ বাণিজ্যিকীকৰণ মানে খাদ্য শস্যৰ পৰা বজাৰত বিক্ৰীৰ বাবে নীল, আফিং, কপাহ, পাট আৰু চাহৰ দৰে নগদ শস্যলৈ সলনি কৰা। ব্ৰিটিছসকলে ইয়াক উৎসাহিত কৰিছিল যাতে ভাৰত ব্ৰিটিছ উদ্যোগলৈ কেঁচা সামগ্ৰী যোগান ধৰে, কিন্তু ই কৃষকৰ ঋণ বৃদ্ধি কৰিছিল আৰু দুৰ্ভিক্ষত অৰিহণা যোগাইছিল।
Q: অ-শিল্পীকৰণ আৰু ধন সম্পদৰ নিষ্কাশন মানে কি?
A: অ-শিল্পীকৰণ মানে সস্তা ব্ৰিটিছ সামগ্ৰীৰ আমদানিৰ বাবে ভাৰতীয় হস্তশিল্প, বিশেষকৈ বস্ত্ৰ উদ্যোগৰ অৱনতি। ধন সম্পদৰ নিষ্কাশন মানে ৰাজহ, দৰমহা, পেঞ্চন আৰু বাণিজ্যৰ জৰিয়তে ভাৰতৰ ধন ব্ৰিটেইনলৈ একপক্ষীয় স্থানান্তৰ। দুয়োটাকে দাদাভাই নৌৰজী আৰু আৰ. চি. দত্তৰ দৰে নেতাসকলে উন্মোচন কৰিছিল।
Q: হল্ট মেকেঞ্জিয়ে কোন ব্যৱস্থা আৰু ক'ত প্ৰৱৰ্তন কৰিছিল?
A: হল্ট মেকেঞ্জিয়ে ১৮২২ চনত উত্তৰ-পশ্চিম প্ৰদেশ আৰু মধ্য ভাৰতৰ কিছু অংশত মহলৱাৰী ব্যৱস্থা প্ৰৱৰ্তন কৰিছিল। এই ব্যৱস্থাত ৰাজহৰ একক আছিল মহল (গাঁও বা গাঁৱৰ সমষ্টি), আৰু ৰাজহ গাঁও সম্প্ৰদায়ৰ সৈতে স্থিৰ কৰা হৈছিল। ই ১৮৩৩ চনত লৰ্ড উইলিয়াম বেণ্টিংকৰ অধীনত সংশোধিত হৈছিল।

### Constitutional Developments & Acts (1909, 1919, 1935)
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/modern-indian-history-sec/constitutional-developments-acts/
Summary: Practice constitutional developments & acts (1909, 1919, 1935) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free.
Q: When was the Morley-Minto Reforms introduced?
A: In 1909, through the Indian Councils Act.
Q: Who were the two persons after whom the 1909 Act is named?
A: Lord Morley (Secretary of State) and Lord Minto (Viceroy).
Q: What was the main feature of the Morley-Minto Reforms?
A: Introduction of separate electorates for the Muslims.
Q: What was the system of separate electorates?
A: A system by which Muslims voted only for Muslim candidates in separate constituencies.
Q: What was the first time separate electorates were introduced in India?
A: In the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.
Q: Who was the Secretary of State for India at the time of the 1909 Act?
A: Lord Morley.
Q: Who was the Viceroy at the time of the 1909 Act?
A: Lord Minto.
Q: What was the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms?
A: The reforms introduced by the Government of India Act of 1919.
Q: Who were the two persons after whom the 1919 Act is named?
A: Edwin Montagu (Secretary of State) and Lord Chelmsford (Viceroy).
Q: What was 'dyarchy'?
A: The system of divided government introduced by the 1919 Act, dividing provincial subjects into 'reserved' and 'transferred'.
Q: What was the system of dyarchy?
A: In the provinces, certain subjects were transferred to the elected ministers and certain reserved subjects remained with the Governor.
Q: When was the Government of India Act of 1919 passed?
A: In 1919, based on the Montagu-Chelmsford Report of 1918.
Q: What was the Simon Commission?
A: A commission sent to India in 1928 to review the working of the 1919 Act.
Q: Who was the head of the Simon Commission?
A: Sir John Simon.
Q: What was the main demand of the Indians against the Simon Commission?
A: The withdrawal of the all-white commission and Indian representation in any such commission.
Q: What was the All-Party Conference of 1928?
A: A conference of all Indian political parties convened to frame a constitution for India.
Q: Who was the chairman of the Nehru Committee?
A: Motilal Nehru.
Q: What was the 'Fourteen Points'?
A: The fourteen demands put forward by M.A. Jinnah in 1929, after the rejection of the Nehru Report.
Q: Who put forward the Fourteen Points?
A: M.A. Jinnah.
Q: When did the First Round Table Conference take place?
A: In November 1930, in London.
Q: Why did the Congress not attend the First Round Table Conference?
A: Because the Civil Disobedience Movement was going on and the Congress demanded release of its leaders.
Q: Who represented the Congress in the Second Round Table Conference?
A: Mahatma Gandhi.
Q: When was the Second Round Table Conference held?
A: In 1931 (September to December) in London.
Q: What was the outcome of the Second Round Table Conference?
A: The conference failed and Gandhiji resumed the Civil Disobedience Movement on his return.
Q: When was the Third Round Table Conference held?
A: In 1932, in London, without the Congress.
Q: When was the Government of India Act of 1935 passed?
A: In August 1935.
Q: What was the basis of the Government of India Act 1935?
