A: The recommendations of the Simon Commission and the Round Table Conferences.
Q: What were the main features of the Act of 1935?
A: Provincial autonomy, dyarchy at the centre, a federal structure and separate electorates.
Q: What was 'provincial autonomy'?
A: The grant of responsible government in the provinces under the Act of 1935.
Q: What was the federal structure proposed by the Act of 1935?
A: A federation of British Indian provinces and the princely states.
Q: Did the federal part of the Act of 1935 come into force?
A: No, the federation never came into operation because the princely states did not join.
Q: What was the All India Federation?
A: The proposed union of British Indian provinces and princely states under the Act of 1935.
Q: What were the elections under the Act of 1935?
A: Elections were held in 1937 in which the Congress won in most provinces.
Q: When were the first provincial elections under the 1935 Act held?
A: In February 1937.
Q: In how many provinces did the Congress form governments in 1937?
A: In seven provinces (out of eleven).
Q: Why did the Congress ministries resign in 1939?
A: In protest against India being made a party to World War II without consultation.
Q: When did the Congress ministries resign?
A: In October 1939.
Q: What was the August Offer of 1940?
A: An offer by Lord Linlithgow promising expansion of the Viceroy's Executive Council and a constituent assembly after the war.
Q: Who gave the August Offer?
A: Viceroy Lord Linlithgow, in August 1940.
Q: What was the Cripps Mission?
A: A mission headed by Stafford Cripps in 1942 offering dominion status and a constituent assembly after the war.
Q: What was the Wavell Plan?
A: A plan proposed by Viceroy Lord Wavell in 1945 for reconstituting the Viceroy's Executive Council.
Q: When was the Simla Conference held?
A: In June-July 1945, called by Viceroy Wavell.
Q: Why did the Simla Conference fail?
A: Because of the disagreement between the Congress and the Muslim League over the nomination of Muslim members.
Q: What was the Cabinet Mission of 1946?
A: A mission of three British cabinet ministers sent to India to discuss the transfer of power.
Q: What was the Cabinet Mission Plan?
A: A plan proposing a federal union of India with provincial groups and a constituent assembly.
Q: What was the 'group system' of the Cabinet Mission?
A: The proposal to group provinces into three sections (A, B and C) for forming their own constitutions.
Q: Who were the members of the Cabinet Mission?
A: Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander.
Q: What was the Constituent Assembly?
A: The body elected in 1946 to frame the Constitution of India.
Q: When was the Constituent Assembly first convened?
A: On 9 December 1946.
Q: Who was the temporary president of the Constituent Assembly?
A: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha.
Q: What was the Regulating Act of 1773?
A: An act which brought the East India Company's affairs under the control of the British government.
Q: What was the Pitts India Act of 1784?
A: An act establishing a Board of Control to supervise the Company's affairs.
Q: When was the Charter Act of 1833 passed?
A: In 1833.
Q: What did the Charter Act of 1833 do?
A: It abolished the Company's trade monopoly and made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India.
Q: What was the Indian Councils Act of 1861?
A: An act which allowed Indians to be nominated to the Viceroy's legislative council.
Q: Who were nominated to the legislative council under the Act of 1861?
A: Raja Banerji, Dinkar Rao and Maharaja of Patiala were among the first Indian members.
Q: What was the Indian Councils Act of 1892?
A: An act which increased the number of members in the councils and allowed some elected members.
Q: When was the Indian Councils Act of 1909 passed?
A: In 1909, also known as the Morley-Minto Reforms.
Q: What was the Montagu Declaration of 1917?
A: The British announcement that India would be given responsible government gradually.
Q: When was the Montagu Declaration made?
A: On 20 August 1917.
Q: What was the 'Montagu-Chelmsford Report'?
A: The report of 1918 on which the Government of India Act 1919 was based.
Q: What was the Government of India Act of 1919?
A: An act introducing dyarchy in the provinces and a bicameral legislature at the centre.
Q: What was the bicameral legislature under the 1919 Act?
A: The Council of State and the Legislative Assembly.
Q: What was the Simon Commission's recommendation?
A: It recommended the abolition of dyarchy and the formation of a federation.
Q: What were the Round Table Conferences?
A: Three conferences held in London between 1930-1932 to discuss constitutional reforms.
Q: What was the result of the Round Table Conferences?
A: They led to the Government of India Act of 1935.
Q: What was the federal scheme of the 1935 Act?
A: A proposed federation of British Indian provinces and princely states with a federal legislature.
Q: What was the 'Instrument of Instructions' in the 1935 Act?
A: Instructions to the Governors to guide the exercise of their discretionary powers.
Q: What was the 'August Offer' of 1940?
A: An offer promising expansion of the Viceroy's Council and a constitution-making body after the war.
Q: What was the 'Cripps Mission' of 1942?
A: A British mission offering dominion status after the war, which was rejected by the Congress.
Q: Why is the Regulating Act of 1773 important in Indian constitutional history?
A: The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first law by which the British Parliament tried to control the East India Company. It created the office of Governor-General of Bengal, with Warren Hastings as the first incumbent, set up an Executive Council, and provided for a Supreme Court at Calcutta. It marked the beginning of parliamentary supervision over Indian affairs.
Q: What is the difference between dyarchy under the Act of 1919 and provincial autonomy under the Act of 1935?
A: Under the Act of 1919, dyarchy divided provincial subjects into transferred subjects administered by Indian ministers and reserved subjects administered by the Governor and his executive council. Under the Act of 1935, provincial autonomy replaced dyarchy: the Governor was to act on the advice of the provincial ministry, the ministers were responsible to the provincial legislature, and the provinces received a greater measure of self-government.
Q: Why was the Simon Commission opposed by Indians?
A: The Simon Commission was opposed because it had no Indian member. It was an all-British body, so Indians argued that a commission deciding India's constitutional future without any Indian representation was an insult. The Congress and other parties boycotted it with the slogan "Simon Go Back", and the protests led to lathi charges in which Lala Lajpat Rai was fatally injured.
Q: What was the significance of the Government of India Act of 1935?
A: The Government of India Act of 1935 was important because it introduced provincial autonomy, provided for an All India Federation, established a Federal Court, and contained the Instrument of Instructions. It was the longest Act passed by the British Parliament and became the main source of many provisions of the Constitution of India.
Q: How did the Cabinet Mission plan propose to keep India united?
A: The Cabinet Mission of 1946 rejected the demand for a separate Pakistan and proposed a Union of India with a weak central government handling only foreign affairs, defence and communications. The provinces were grouped into three sections (A, B and C), and the Constitution was to be framed by a Constituent Assembly. The Muslim League eventually rejected the plan.
Q: When did the Constituent Assembly first meet and who presided over it?
A: The Constituent Assembly first met on 9 December 1946. Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was the temporary president for the first meeting, and Dr. Rajendra Prasad was later elected the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly.
Q: ভাৰতীয় সাংবিধানিক ইতিহাসত ১৭৭৩ চনৰ নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ আইন কিয় গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: ১৭৭৩ চনৰ নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ আইন আছিল ব্ৰিটিছ সংসদে ইষ্ট ইণ্ডিয়া কোম্পানীক নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ কৰিবলৈ প্ৰণয়ন কৰা প্ৰথম আইন। ই বংগৰ গৱৰ্ণৰ-জেনেৰেলৰ পদ সৃষ্টি কৰিছিল, যাৰ প্ৰথম অধিষ্ঠিত আছিল ৱাৰেন হেষ্টিংছ, এটা কাৰ্যবাহী পৰিষদ গঠন কৰিছিল আৰু কলিকতাত এখন উচ্চ ন্যায়ালয়ৰ ব্যৱস্থা কৰিছিল। ই ভাৰতীয় পৰিক্ৰমাৰ ওপৰত সংসদৰ নজৰদাৰীৰ আৰম্ভণি চিহ্নিত কৰিছিল।
Q: ১৯১৯ চনৰ আইনৰ দ্বৈতশাসন আৰু ১৯৩৫ চনৰ আইনৰ প্ৰাদেশিক স্বায়ত্তশাসনৰ পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: ১৯১৯ চনৰ আইনৰ অধীনত দ্বৈতশাসনে প্ৰাদেশিক বিষয়বোৰক ভাৰতীয় মন্ত্ৰীসকলে পৰিচালনা কৰা হস্তান্তৰিত বিষয় আৰু গৱৰ্ণৰ তথা তেওঁৰ কাৰ্যবাহী পৰিষদে পৰিচালনা কৰা সংৰক্ষিত বিষয়ত বিভক্ত কৰিছিল। ১৯৩৫ চনৰ আইনৰ অধীনত প্ৰাদেশিক স্বায়ত্তশাসনে দ্বৈতশাসনৰ ঠাই লৈছিল: গৱৰ্ণৰে প্ৰাদেশিক মন্ত্ৰীসভাৰ পৰামৰ্শমতে কাম কৰিব লাগিছিল, মন্ত্ৰীসকল প্ৰাদেশিক বিধানমণ্ডলৰ প্ৰতি দায়বদ্ধ আছিল, আৰু প্ৰদেশসমূহে অধিক স্ব-শাসন লাভ কৰিছিল।
Q: চাইমন আয়োগক ভাৰতীয়সকলে কিয় বিৰোধ কৰিছিল?
A: চাইমন আয়োগক বিৰোধ কৰিছিল কাৰণ ইয়াত কোনো ভাৰতীয় সদস্য নাছিল। ই এটা সম্পূৰ্ণ ব্ৰিটিছ সংস্থা আছিল, সেয়েহে ভাৰতীয়সকলে যুক্তি দিছিল যে কোনো ভাৰতীয় প্ৰতিনিধিত্ব নোহোৱাকৈ ভাৰতৰ সাংবিধানিক ভৱিষ্যত নিৰ্ণয় কৰা আয়োগ এটা অপমান। কংগ্ৰেছ আৰু অন্য দলসমূহে "চাইমন উভতি যাওক" শ্লোগানেৰে ইয়াক বৰ্জন কৰিছিল, আৰু প্ৰতিবাদত লাঠিচালনা হৈছিল, য'ত লালা লাজপত ৰায়ৰ মৃত্যু ঘটিছিল।
Q: ১৯৩৫ চনৰ ভাৰতীয় চৰকাৰ আইনৰ তাৎপর্য কি আছিল?
A: ১৯৩৫ চনৰ ভাৰতীয় চৰকাৰ আইন গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ আছিল কাৰণ ই প্ৰাদেশিক স্বায়ত্তশাসন প্ৰৱৰ্তন কৰিছিল, এটা সৰ্বভাৰতীয় ফেডাৰেচনৰ ব্যৱস্থা কৰিছিল, এটা ফেডাৰেল আদালত স্থাপন কৰিছিল আৰু নিৰ্দেশনা পত্ৰ অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত কৰিছিল। এইখন ব্ৰিটিছ সংসদে প্ৰণয়ন কৰা আটাইতকৈ দীঘল আইন আছিল আৰু ভাৰতৰ সংবিধানৰ বহু বিধানৰ মূল উৎস হৈ পৰিছিল।
Q: কেবিনেট মিছনৰ পৰিকল্পনাই ভাৰতক একতাৰে ৰাখিবলৈ কেনেকৈ প্ৰস্তাৱ দিছিল?
A: ১৯৪৬ চনৰ কেবিনেট মিছনে পৃথক পাকিস্তানৰ দাবী নাকচ কৰি এটা ভাৰতীয় সংঘৰ প্ৰস্তাৱ দিছিল, যাৰ দুৰ্বল কেন্দ্ৰীয় চৰকাৰে কেৱল বৈদেশিক পৰিক্ৰমা, প্ৰতিৰক্ষা আৰু যোগাযোগ চম্ভালিব। প্ৰদেশসমূহক তিনিটা ভাগত (A, B আৰু C) গোট কৰা হৈছিল, আৰু সংবিধান এখন গণপৰিষদে প্ৰণয়ন কৰিব লাগিছিল। মুছলিম লীগে শেষত এই পৰিকল্পনা নাকচ কৰিছিল।
Q: গণপৰিষদে প্ৰথমে কেতিয়া বৈঠক কৰিছিল আৰু ইয়াৰ সভাপতি কোন আছিল?
A: গণপৰিষদে প্ৰথমে ৯ ডিচেম্বৰ ১৯৪৬ চনত বৈঠক কৰিছিল। প্ৰথম বৈঠকৰ বাবে ডাঃ সচ্চিদানন্দ সিনহা অস্থায়ী সভাপতি আছিল, আৰু পিছত ডাঃ ৰাজেন্দ্ৰ প্ৰসাদক গণপৰিষদৰ স্থায়ী সভাপতি হিচাপে নিৰ্বাচিত কৰা হৈছিল।

### Indian Freedom Struggle Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/modern-indian-history-sec/freedom-struggle/
Summary: Indian freedom struggle questions with answers for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Covers the Indian National Congress and the Gandhian movements.
Q: When was the Indian National Congress founded and by whom?
A: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by Allan Octavian Hume, with W. C. Bonnerjee as its first president.
Q: What was the Dandi March?
A: The Dandi March of 1930 was led by Mahatma Gandhi to break the salt law and began the civil disobedience movement.
Q: When did India become independent?
A: India became independent on 15 August 1947 under the Indian Independence Act passed by the British Parliament.

### Gandhian Era & Major Mass Movements (Non-Cooperation, Civil
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/modern-indian-history-sec/gandhian-era-movements/
Summary: Practice gandhian era & major mass movements (non-cooperation, civil disobedience, quit india) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE.
Q: In which year did Gandhiji return to India from South Africa?
A: In 1915.
Q: Where was the first successful satyagraha by Gandhiji in India?
A: Champaran in Bihar, 1917 (against the indigo plantation system).
Q: What was the Champaran Satyagraha about?
A: Against the oppression of the indigo planters on the peasants (tinkathia system).
Q: In which year did Gandhiji launch the Kheda Satyagraha?
A: In 1918, in Gujarat, to support the peasants affected by famine and crop failure.
Q: What was the Ahmedabad Mill Strike of 1918 about?
A: Demand for an increase in wages of the mill workers (Gandhiji observed his first hunger strike).
Q: What was the Rowlatt Act of 1919?
A: An act which allowed the government to arrest and detain any person without trial (Black Act).
Q: When did Gandhiji observe a nationwide hartal against the Rowlatt Act?
A: On 6 April 1919.
Q: What was the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
A: The killing of hundreds of unarmed people by General Dyer's troops in Amritsar on 13 April 1919.
Q: Who was responsible for the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
A: General Reginald Dyer.
Q: Who resigned from the Viceroy's Council in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
A: Rabindranath Tagore returned his knighthood; C.F. Andrews protested.
Q: What was the Khilafat Movement?
A: A movement led by Indian Muslims to protest the treatment of the Ottoman Caliph (Khilafat) by the British after World War I.
Q: Who were the leaders of the Khilafat Movement?
A: The Ali brothers (Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali), Maulana Azad and Maulana Abul Kalam.
Q: When was the Non-Cooperation Movement launched?
A: In August 1920, after the Calcutta Session of the Congress.
Q: What was the main programme of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
A: Boycott of government schools, law courts, titles, foreign goods and the legislature.
Q: Why was the Non-Cooperation Movement withdrawn?
A: Because of the violent incident at Chauri Chaura on 5 February 1922.
Q: Who were the martyrs of the Chauri Chaura incident?
A: 22 policemen were burnt alive by an angry mob; no particular martyr is named.
Q: Who was the leader of the Non-Cooperation Movement in Assam?
A: Tariknath Das, Gopinath Bordoloi and other Congress leaders led it in Assam.
Q: What was the Swaraj Party?
A: A party founded by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru in 1923 to contest elections and enter the councils.
Q: Who founded the Swaraj Party?
A: Chittaranjan Das and Motilal Nehru.
Q: What was the Hindustan Republican Association?
A: A revolutionary organisation founded in 1924 by Ram Prasad Bismil and others.
Q: When was the Simon Commission sent to India?
A: In 1928, to enquire into the working of the 1919 Act.
Q: Why was the Simon Commission boycotted?
A: Because it had no Indian member (all white commission).
Q: Who was lathi-charged during the Simon Commission protest in Lahore?
A: Lala Lajpat Rai, who later died of his injuries.
Q: What was the Nehru Report of 1928?
A: A report by Motilal Nehru recommending dominion status for India, prepared by an All-Party Conference committee.
Q: Who was the chairman of the Nehru Report Committee?
A: Motilal Nehru.
Q: What was the 'Purna Swaraj' declaration?
A: The declaration of complete independence made at the Lahore Session of Congress in December 1929.
Q: Who presided over the Lahore Session of Congress in 1929?
A: Jawaharlal Nehru.
Q: When was the Independence Day observed?
A: On 26 January 1930.
Q: What was the Dandi March?
A: Gandhiji's 240-mile march from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi (12 March to 6 April 1930) to break the salt law.
Q: When was the Civil Disobedience Movement launched?
A: On 6 April 1930, with the breaking of the salt law at Dandi.
Q: What was the salt tax issue?
A: A heavy tax on salt which hit the common people, and the government's monopoly on salt production.
Q: Who was the leader of the Civil Disobedience Movement in the North-West Frontier Province?
A: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Frontier Gandhi).
Q: What was the Red Shirt movement?
A: The Khudai Khidmatgar movement led by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan.
Q: What was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
A: An agreement in March 1931 by which the government released the political prisoners and Gandhi agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement.
Q: When was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed?
A: On 5 March 1931.
Q: Who was the Viceroy at the time of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
A: Lord Irwin.
Q: What was the Poona Pact?
A: An agreement between Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in September 1932 on reserved seats for the depressed classes.
Q: Why did Gandhiji fast against the Communal Award?
A: Because the Award proposed separate electorates for the depressed classes.
Q: What was the Communal Award of 1932?
A: An announcement by the British Prime Minister granting separate electorates to various communities.
Q: When was the Quit India Movement launched?
A: On 8 August 1942, at the Bombay session of the Congress.
Q: Who gave the slogan 'Do or Die'?
A: Mahatma Gandhi, at the Quit India Movement.
Q: What was the main demand of the Quit India Movement?
A: Immediate end of British rule in India.
Q: Who was the Congress President during the Quit India Movement?
A: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.
Q: Who were the leaders arrested after the Quit India Resolution?
A: Gandhiji and all the top Congress leaders.
Q: What was the role of the parallel governments during the Quit India Movement?
A: Parallel governments were set up in some places like Ballia and Satara to administer the areas.
Q: What was the 'August Kranti'?
A: Another name for the Quit India Movement launched in August 1942.
Q: What was the Cripps Mission?
A: A mission sent by the British government in 1942 to gain Indian cooperation during World War II.
Q: Who headed the Cripps Mission?
A: Stafford Cripps.
Q: Why did the Congress reject the Cripps proposals?
A: Because it did not provide for immediate full independence and the formation of a national government.
Q: What was the Cabinet Mission of 1946?
A: A mission of three British ministers sent to India to discuss the transfer of power.
Q: Who were the members of the Cabinet Mission?
A: Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander.
Q: Who was the leader of the Civil Disobedience Movement?
A: Mahatma Gandhi.
Q: What was the salt tax?
A: A tax imposed on salt by the British, which was a burden on the common people.
Q: Who were the leaders of the Quit India Movement?
A: Gandhi, Nehru, Patel, Maulana Azad and other Congress leaders.
Q: What was the 'August Revolution'?
A: Another name for the Quit India Movement of 1942.
Q: What was the 'Individual Satyagraha' of 1940?
A: A limited satyagraha launched by Gandhi in which selected individuals offered civil disobedience.
Q: Who was the first individual satyagrahi?
A: Vinoba Bhave.
Q: What was the Chauri Chaura incident?
A: The burning of a police station by a mob in 1922, leading to the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement.
Q: What was the 'No Tax' campaign?
A: The refusal to pay taxes as part of the Civil Disobedience Movement.
Q: Who was the leader of the Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928?
A: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
Q: What was the 'Bardoli Satyagraha'?
A: A peasants' movement against the increased land revenue in Bardoli, Gujarat, in 1928.
Q: What was the 'Wardha Scheme'?
A: A scheme of basic education proposed by Gandhi in 1937.
Q: Who was the Viceroy of India during the Quit India Movement?
A: Lord Linlithgow.
Q: What was the response of the British to the Quit India Movement?
A: The leaders were arrested and the movement was brutally suppressed.
Q: What was the role of the underground movement during Quit India?
A: Young leaders like J.P. Narayan and Aruna Asaf Ali carried on secret revolutionary activities.
Q: Who was known as the 'Frontier Gandhi'?
A: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan.
Q: What was the Khudai Khidmatgar?
A: The servant of God movement (Red Shirts) led by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan.
Q: What was the Poona Pact of 1932?
A: An agreement between Gandhi and Ambedkar about reserved seats for the depressed classes.
Q: What was the Communal Award of 1932?
A: The British decision to give separate electorates to different communities, including the depressed classes.
Q: Who founded the Congress Socialist Party?
A: Jai Prakash Narayan, Acharya Narendra Dev and others, in 1934.
Q: What was the role of the peasants in the Gandhian movements?
A: The peasants were the backbone of movements like Champaran, Kheda and Bardoli.
Q: In which year did Gandhiji return to India and what was his first satyagraha??
A: Gandhiji returned to India from South Africa on 9 January 1915. His first satyagraha in India was the Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 in Bihar, where he supported indigo peasants against the exploitative tinkathia system and won a refund for them.
Q: What was the Rowlatt Act and why did Gandhiji protest against it?
A: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 allowed the government to arrest and detain people without trial. Gandhiji called it a "black act" and organised a nationwide hartal on 6 April 1919. The protest was followed by the Jallianwala Bagh massacre on 13 April 1919, which deeply shocked the nation.
Q: Why was the Non-Cooperation Movement withdrawn?
A: The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-1922) was withdrawn by Gandhiji after the Chauri Chaura incident of 5 February 1922, when a mob burnt a police station and killed policemen in Gorakhpur district. Gandhiji felt the movement had turned violent and that the people were not yet ready for non-violent discipline.
Q: Who led the Bardoli Satyagraha and how did Patel get the title "Sardar"?
A: The Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 was led by Vallabhbhai Patel against an increase in land revenue. The peasants refused to pay and the government finally agreed to a compromise. For his successful leadership the women of Bardoli gave him the title "Sardar".
Q: What was the Poona Pact of 1932?
A: The Poona Pact was an agreement signed on 24 September 1932 between Gandhiji and Dr B. R. Ambedkar. It replaced the separate electorates for the depressed classes, given by the British Communal Award, with reserved seats within a joint electorate, after Gandhiji's fast against the award.
Q: When was the Quit India Movement launched and what was its slogan?
A: The Quit India Movement was launched on 8 August 1942 at the Bombay session of the Congress. Gandhiji gave the slogan "Do or Die", and the movement is also called the August Kranti. It led to the arrest of top leaders and the setting up of parallel governments in some areas.
Q: গান্ধীজী কোন বছৰত ভাৰতলৈ উভতি আহিছিল আৰু তেওঁৰ প্ৰথম সত্যাগ্ৰহ কি আছিল?
A: গান্ধীজী ১৯১৫ চনৰ ৯ জানুৱাৰী তাৰিখে দক্ষিণ আফ্ৰিকাৰ পৰা ভাৰতলৈ উভতি আহিছিল। ভাৰতত তেওঁৰ প্ৰথম সত্যাগ্ৰহ আছিল ১৯১৭ চনৰ বিহাৰৰ চাম্পাৰণ সত্যাগ্ৰহ, য'ত তেওঁ নীল খেতিয়কসকলৰ বিৰুদ্ধে শোষণমূলক তিনকাঠিয়া ব্যৱস্থাৰ বিৰুদ্ধে কৃষকসকলক সমৰ্থন কৰিছিল আৰু তেওঁলোকক ধন ঘূৰাই দিয়াবলৈ বাধ্য কৰাইছিল।
Q: ৰাউলাট আইন কি আছিল আৰু গান্ধীয়ে কিয় ইয়াৰ বিৰুদ্ধে প্ৰতিবাদ কৰিছিল?
A: ১৯১৯ চনৰ ৰাউলাট আইনে বিচাৰ নোহোৱাকৈ মানুহক গ্ৰেপ্তাৰ আৰু আটক কৰাৰ অনুমতি দিছিল। গান্ধীয়ে ইয়াক "কাল কানুন" বুলি অভিহিত কৰিছিল আৰু ১৯১৯ চনৰ ৬ এপ্ৰিলত দেশজুৰি হৰতাল আয়োজন কৰিছিল। প্ৰতিবাদৰ পিছত ১৩ এপ্ৰিল ১৯১৯ত জাল্লিয়ানৱালা বাগ হত্যাকাণ্ড সংঘটিত হৈছিল, যিয়ে দেশক গভীৰভাৱে স্তব্ধ কৰি তুলিছিল।
Q: অসহযোগ আন্দোলন কিয় প্ৰত্যাহাৰ কৰা হৈছিল?
A: ১৯২২ চনৰ ৫ ফেব্ৰুৱাৰীত সংঘটিত চৌৰী চৌৰা ঘটনাৰ পিছত গান্ধীয়ে অসহযোগ আন্দোলন (১৯২০-১৯২২) প্ৰত্যাহাৰ কৰিছিল, য'ত গোৰখপুৰ জিলাত এটা ভীৰে আৰক্ষী চকী জ্বলাই আৰক্ষীসকলক হত্যা কৰিছিল। আন্দোলনটো হিংসাত্মক হৈ পৰিছে বুলি গান্ধীয়ে অনুভৱ কৰিছিল আৰু জনসাধাৰণ অহিংস অনুশাসনৰ বাবে এতিয়াও প্ৰস্তুত নহয় বুলি ভাবিছিল।
Q: বৰদোলি সত্যাগ্ৰহ কোনে নেতৃত্ব দিছিল আৰু পেটেলে "সৰ্দাৰ" উপাধি কেনেকৈ পাইছিল?
A: ১৯২৮ চনৰ বৰদোলি সত্যাগ্ৰহ বল্লভভাই পেটেলে ভূমি ৰাজহ বৃদ্ধিৰ বিৰুদ্ধে নেতৃত্ব দিছিল। কৃষকসকলে ৰাজহ দিবলৈ অস্বীকাৰ কৰিছিল আৰু চৰকাৰে শেষত এটা আপোচত মান্তি হৈছিল। তেওঁৰ সফল নেতৃত্বৰ বাবে বৰদোলিৰ মহিলাসকলে তেওঁক "সৰ্দাৰ" উপাধি দিছিল।
Q: ১৯৩২ চনৰ পুনা চুক্তি কি আছিল?
A: পুনা চুক্তি ২৪ ছেপ্তেম্বৰ ১৯৩২ তাৰিখে গান্ধীজী আৰু ড° বি. আৰ. আম্বেদকৰৰ মাজত স্বাক্ষৰিত এটা চুক্তি আছিল। ব্ৰিটিছ সাম্প্ৰদায়িক বঁটাই দলিত শ্ৰেণীক দিয়া পৃথক নিৰ্বাচনী এলাকাৰ সলনি যুটীয়া নিৰ্বাচনী এলাকাৰ ভিতৰত সংৰক্ষিত আসনৰ ব্যৱস্থা কৰিছিল, যি গান্ধীজীৰ অনশনৰ পিছত সম্ভৱ হৈছিল।
Q: ভাৰত ছাড়ো আন্দোলন কেতিয়া আৰম্ভ কৰা হৈছিল আৰু ইয়াৰ ধ্বনি কি আছিল?
A: ভাৰত ছাড়ো আন্দোলন ৮ আগষ্ট ১৯৪২ তাৰিখে কংগ্ৰেছৰ বম্বে অধিৱেশনত আৰম্ভ কৰা হৈছিল। গান্ধীজীয়ে "কৰ বা মৰ" ধ্বনি দিছিল, আৰু এই আন্দোলনক আগষ্ট ক্ৰান্তি বুলিও কোৱা হয়। ইয়াৰ ফলত শীৰ্ষ নেতাসকলৰ গ্ৰেপ্তাৰ আৰু কিছুমান অঞ্চলত সমান্তৰাল চৰকাৰ গঠন হৈছিল।

### Mountbatten Plan, Partition & Independence (1947) Questions
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/modern-indian-history-sec/mountbatten-partition-independence/
Summary: Practice mountbatten plan, partition & independence (1947) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free.
Q: Who was the last Viceroy of India?
A: Lord Mountbatten.
Q: When did Lord Mountbatten become the Viceroy of India?
A: In March 1947.
Q: What was the Mountbatten Plan?
A: A plan announced on 3 June 1947 for the partition of India into India and Pakistan.
Q: When was the Mountbatten Plan announced?
A: On 3 June 1947.
Q: What was the 'June 3rd Plan'?
A: Another name for the Mountbatten Plan.
Q: What was the basis of the partition of India?
A: The Muslim-majority areas were to form Pakistan and the rest was to remain as India.
Q: Who accepted the Mountbatten Plan on behalf of the Congress?
A: The Congress Working Committee accepted it after being convinced of the inevitability of partition.
Q: Who accepted the Mountbatten Plan on behalf of the Muslim League?
A: M.A. Jinnah and the Muslim League.
Q: When was the Indian Independence Act passed?
A: On 18 July 1947, by the British Parliament.
Q: What did the Indian Independence Act of 1947 provide?
A: The partition of India into two dominions - India and Pakistan - and the end of British rule on 15 August 1947.
Q: Who was appointed the first Governor-General of free India?
A: Lord Mountbatten.
Q: Who was the first Governor-General of Pakistan?
A: M.A. Jinnah.
Q: When did India attain independence?
A: On 15 August 1947.
Q: Who hoisted the national flag at the Red Fort on 15 August 1947?
A: Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of India.
Q: Who was the first Prime Minister of free India?
A: Jawaharlal Nehru.
Q: What was the famous speech of Nehru on the eve of independence?
A: The 'Tryst with Destiny' speech.
Q: When did Nehru deliver the 'Tryst with Destiny' speech?
A: On the midnight of 14-15 August 1947.
Q: Who was the chairman of the Boundary Commission?
A: Sir Cyril Radcliffe.
Q: What was the Radcliffe Line?
A: The boundary line between India and Pakistan drawn by the Radcliffe Commission.
Q: Who drew the boundary line between India and Pakistan?
A: Sir Cyril Radcliffe.
Q: What was the fate of the princely states after independence?
A: They were integrated into India or Pakistan by 1949.
Q: Who was the Minister of States responsible for the integration of princely states?
A: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
Q: Who was known as the 'Iron Man of India'?
A: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
Q: What was the role of Sardar Patel in the integration of states?
A: He persuaded the princely states to join the Indian Union.
Q: What was the 'Instrument of Accession'?
A: A legal document by which a princely state joined the Indian Union.
Q: Which princely state was merged with India in 1948 after a police action?
A: Hyderabad.
Q: Who was the Nizam of Hyderabad?
A: Mir Osman Ali Khan.
Q: What was the 'Operation Polo'?
A: The police action against Hyderabad in 1948 to integrate it with India.
Q: Which was the last princely state to join India?
A: Jammu and Kashmir (in October 1947, via the Instrument of Accession).
Q: Who signed the Instrument of Accession of Kashmir?
A: Maharaja Hari Singh.
Q: When was the Instrument of Accession of Kashmir signed?
A: On 26 October 1947.
Q: What was the impact of the partition?
A: Mass migration, communal violence and the loss of millions of lives.
Q: How many people migrated during the partition?
A: About 10-15 million people crossed the new borders.
Q: What was the effect of partition on Gandhi?
A: Gandhiji was deeply distressed and undertook a fast to stop the communal violence in Calcutta.
Q: When was Mahatma Gandhi assassinated?
A: On 30 January 1948.
Q: Who assassinated Mahatma Gandhi?
A: Nathuram Godse.
Q: Where was Mahatma Gandhi assassinated?
A: At Birla House in New Delhi.
Q: What was the slogan of the Muslim League for Pakistan?
A: 'Pakistan or Death' and the demand for a separate Muslim state.
Q: Who gave the 'Pakistan or Death' slogan?
A: M.A. Jinnah, in his Lahore speech of March 1940.
Q: What was the Lahore Resolution?
A: The resolution passed by the Muslim League in 1940 demanding separate states for the Muslims.
Q: When was the Lahore Resolution passed?
A: On 23 March 1940.
Q: Who moved the Lahore Resolution?
A: A.K. Fazlul Haq, the Chief Minister of Bengal.
Q: What was the 'Divide and Rule' policy?
A: The British policy of creating divisions among Indians to weaken the nationalist movement.
Q: Who was the author of the book 'Discovery of India'?
A: Jawaharlal Nehru.
Q: Who wrote 'The Discovery of India'?
A: Jawaharlal Nehru, during his imprisonment.
Q: What was the significance of 15 August 1947 for India?
A: India became a free and independent nation on that day.
Q: What was the state of India at the time of independence?
A: It was a poor country facing partition, refugees, communal violence and economic problems.
Q: Who was the President of the Constituent Assembly when the Constitution was adopted?
A: Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
Q: When was the Constitution of India adopted?
A: On 26 November 1949.
Q: When did the Constitution of India come into force?
A: On 26 January 1950.
Q: What was the 'Two Nation Theory'?
A: The theory that Hindus and Muslims are two separate nations, propounded by M.A. Jinnah.
Q: Who propounded the Two Nation Theory?
A: M.A. Jinnah (and earlier Sir Syed Ahmed Khan).
Q: What was the demand of the Lahore Resolution?
A: The creation of independent states in the Muslim-majority areas of India.
Q: Who was the President of the Constituent Assembly?
A: Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
Q: When was the Constituent Assembly formed?
A: In 1946, under the Cabinet Mission Plan.
Q: What was the 'Objective Resolution'?
A: A resolution moved by Nehru in the Constituent Assembly in 1946 defining the aims of the Constitution.
Q: Who moved the Objective Resolution?
A: Jawaharlal Nehru.
Q: When was the Objective Resolution passed?
A: On 22 January 1947.
Q: What was the 'Indian Independence Act' of 1947?
A: The act that partitioned India into two dominions and ended British rule.
Q: When did the Indian Independence Act take effect?
A: On 15 August 1947.
Q: Who was the last Governor-General of India?
A: C. Rajagopalachari.
Q: Who was the first Indian Governor-General of free India?
A: C. Rajagopalachari.
Q: When did India become a Republic?
A: On 26 January 1950.
Q: Who was the chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution?
A: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
Q: How many members were in the Constituent Assembly?
A: Originally 389 members, later reduced after partition.
Q: What was the role of the Mountbatten Plan in Kashmir?
A: The princely states were given the choice to join India or Pakistan; Kashmir later acceded to India.
Q: What was the 'Standstill Agreement'?
A: An agreement by which states continued their existing relations with India and Pakistan until fresh arrangements.
Q: What was the 'Partition Council'?
A: A body set up to supervise the partition of India and Pakistan, headed by Mountbatten.
Q: Who were the members of the Partition Council?
A: Mountbatten, Nehru, Patel, Jinnah and Liaquat Ali Khan.
Q: What was the 'Jubilee of Freedom'?
A: The 25th anniversary of India's independence was called the Silver Jubilee of freedom.
Q: What was the significance of 26 January 1950?
A: The Constitution of India came into force on that day, making India a sovereign republic.
Q: Who was the last Viceroy of India and what was the Mountbatten Plan?
A: Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy, taking office in March 1947. The Mountbatten Plan, announced on 3 June 1947, was the scheme for transferring power to two successor dominions, India and Pakistan, and it led to the Indian Independence Act of 1947.
Q: When was the Mountbatten Plan announced and who accepted it?
A: It was announced on 3 June 1947. The Congress accepted it through Jawaharlal Nehru and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, and the Muslim League accepted it through Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
Q: What did the Indian Independence Act of 1947 provide?
A: Passed on 18 July 1947, the Act ended British sovereignty over India with effect from 15 August 1947, created the two independent dominions of India and Pakistan, and provided for the office of Governor-General and for the Constituent Assemblies to frame constitutions.
Q: What was the Radcliffe Line and who drew it?
A: The Radcliffe Line was the boundary drawn between India and Pakistan through the Punjab and Bengal. It was prepared by the Boundary Commission under its chairman Sir Cyril Radcliffe and was published on 17 August 1947.
Q: How were the princely states integrated into India?
A: Sardar Patel, as Minister of States, persuaded the rulers to sign the Instrument of Accession. Junagadh was integrated by diplomacy and a plebiscite, Hyderabad by the police action called Operation Polo in 1948, and Kashmir signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October 1947.
Q: When did India become a Republic and what was the role of the Constitution?
A: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India on 26 November 1949 and it came into force on 26 January 1950, when India became a sovereign democratic Republic. The Objective Resolution, moved by Nehru, had laid down its guiding ideals.
Q: ভাৰতৰ শেষ ভাইচৰয় কোন আছিল আৰু মাউন্টব্যাটেন পৰিকল্পনা কি আছিল?
A: লৰ্ড মাউন্টব্যাটেন শেষ ভাইচৰয় আছিল, যিয়ে ১৯৪৭ চনৰ মাৰ্চত কাৰ্যভাৰ গ্ৰহণ কৰিছিল। ৩ জুন ১৯৪৭ চনত ঘোষিত মাউন্টব্যাটেন পৰিকল্পনা আছিল ভাৰত আৰু পাকিস্তান নামৰ দুটা উত্তৰাধিকাৰী ডমিনিয়নলৈ ক্ষমতা হস্তান্তৰৰ আঁচনি, যাৰ ফলত ১৯৪৭ চনৰ ভাৰতীয় স্বাধীনতা আইন আহিছিল।
Q: মাউন্টব্যাটেন পৰিকল্পনা কেতিয়া ঘোষণা কৰা হৈছিল আৰু কোনে গ্ৰহণ কৰিছিল?
A: ইয়াক ৩ জুন ১৯৪৭ চনত ঘোষণা কৰা হৈছিল। কংগ্ৰেছে জৱাহৰলাল নেহৰু আৰু সৰদাৰ বল্লভভাই পাটেলৰ জৰিয়তে আৰু মুছলিম লীগে মহম্মদ আলী জিন্নাহৰ জৰিয়তে ইয়াক গ্ৰহণ কৰিছিল।
Q: ১৯৪৭ চনৰ ভাৰতীয় স্বাধীনতা আইনে কি বিধান দিছিল?
A: ১৮ জুলাই ১৯৪৭ চনত গৃহীত এই আইনে ১৫ আগষ্ট ১৯৪৭ চনৰ পৰা ভাৰতৰ ওপৰত ব্ৰিটিছৰ সাৰ্বভৌমত্বৰ অন্ত পেলাইছিল, ভাৰত আৰু পাকিস্তান নামৰ দুটা স্বাধীন ডমিনিয়ন সৃষ্টি কৰিছিল, আৰু গৱৰ্নৰ জেনেৰেলৰ পদ আৰু সংবিধান ৰচনাৰ বাবে গণপৰিষদৰ ব্যৱস্থা কৰিছিল।
Q: ৰেডক্লিফ ৰেখা কি আছিল আৰু কোনে আঁকিছিল?
A: ৰেডক্লিফ ৰেখা আছিল পঞ্জাব আৰু বংগৰ মাজেৰে ভাৰত আৰু পাকিস্তানৰ মাজত অঁকা সীমা। ইয়াক মুৰব্বী ছাৰ চিৰিল ৰেডক্লিফৰ নেতৃত্বত সীমা আয়োগে প্ৰস্তুত কৰিছিল আৰু ১৭ আগষ্ট ১৯৪৭ চনত প্ৰকাশ কৰা হৈছিল।
Q: দেশীয় ৰাজ্যসমূহ ভাৰতত কেনেকৈ অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত কৰা হৈছিল?
A: ৰাজ্য মন্ত্ৰী সৰদাৰ পাটেলে শাসকসকলক যোগদানৰ দস্তাবেজত স্বাক্ষৰ কৰিবলৈ সৈমান কৰাইছিল। জুনাগড়ক কূটনীতি আৰু জনমত সংগ্ৰহৰ জৰিয়তে, হায়দৰাবাদক ১৯৪৮ চনত অ'পাৰেচন প'ল' নামৰ আৰক্ষী কাৰ্যৰ জৰিয়তে অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত কৰা হৈছিল আৰু কাশ্মীৰে ২৬ অক্টোবৰ ১৯৪৭ চনত যোগদানৰ দস্তাবেজত স্বাক্ষৰ কৰিছিল।
Q: ভাৰত কেতিয়া প্ৰজাতন্ত্ৰ হৈছিল আৰু সংবিধানৰ ভূমিকা কি আছিল?
A: গণপৰিষদে ২৬ নৱেম্বৰ ১৯৪৯ চনত ভাৰতৰ সংবিধান গৃহীত কৰিছিল আৰু ২৬ জানুৱাৰী ১৯৫০ চনত ই কাৰ্যকৰ হৈছিল, যেতিয়া ভাৰত সাৰ্বভৌম গণতান্ত্ৰিক প্ৰজাতন্ত্ৰ হৈছিল। নেহৰুৱে উত্থাপন কৰা উদ্দেশ্য প্ৰস্তাৱে ইয়াৰ আদৰ্শ নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰিছিল।

### Rise of Indian Nationalism & Formation of INC — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/modern-indian-history-sec/nationalism-inc-formation/
Summary: Practice rise of indian nationalism & formation of inc questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual.
Q: Who founded the Indian National Congress?
A: Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, with the help of Indian leaders.
Q: When and where was the first session of the INC held?
A: In 1885, at Bombay (Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College).
Q: Who was the first president of the INC?
A: Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee.
Q: How many delegates attended the first session of the INC?
A: 72 delegates.
Q: Who was the founder president of the INC who was a retired ICS officer?
A: Allan Octavian Hume (though he was the founder, not president; the first president was W.C. Bonnerjee).
Q: What was the main demand of the early Congress?
A: Greater participation of Indians in the administration and reforms in the legislative councils.
Q: What was the 'Drain Theory' associated with the Congress?
A: The criticism of the economic drain of India's wealth by the British, led by Dadabhai Naoroji.
Q: Who was the first Indian to preside over the INC from Bengal?
A: Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee (the first president himself).
Q: Who was the president of the INC at its second session in Calcutta?
A: Dadabhai Naoroji.
Q: Who was the first Muslim president of the INC?
A: Badruddin Tyabji, in 1887.
Q: Who was the first woman to preside over the INC?
A: Annie Besant, in 1917.
Q: Who was the president of the INC at the historic Surat session of 1907?
A: Rash Behari Ghosh.
Q: What happened at the Surat session of 1907?
A: The split between the Moderates and the Extremists of the Congress.
Q: Who were the Moderates (Naram Dal) in the Congress?
A: Leaders like Dadabhai Naoroji, G.K. Gokhale, Ferozeshah Mehta and S.N. Banerjee who believed in constitutional methods.
Q: Who were the Extremists (Garam Dal) in the Congress?
A: Leaders like Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal and Lala Lajpat Rai who advocated swaraj and more radical methods.
Q: Who was the leader known as 'Lokamanya'?
A: Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
Q: Who founded the Indian National Conference?
A: Surendranath Banerjee, in 1883.
Q: Who founded the Indian Association of Calcutta?
A: Surendranath Banerjee and Anand Mohan Bose, in 1876.
Q: Who was the founder of the East India Association?
A: Dadabhai Naoroji, in London in 1866.
Q: Who founded the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha?
A: Mahadev Govind Ranade and others, in 1870.
Q: Who was the founder of the Bombay Presidency Association?
A: Ferozeshah Mehta and Badruddin Tyabji, in 1885.
Q: Who was the leader who founded the 'Servants of India Society'?
A: Gopal Krishna Gokhale.
Q: Who was called the 'Father of the Indian National Congress'?
A: Allan Octavian Hume.
Q: What was the 'Indian National Congress' demand for the ICS examination?
A: To hold the ICS examination simultaneously in India and England.
Q: Who was the president of the INC when 'Purna Swaraj' was demanded in 1929?
A: Jawaharlal Nehru.
Q: What was the 'Anushilan Samiti'?
A: A revolutionary organisation founded in Bengal in 1902 to promote physical and political training.
Q: Who founded the Anushilan Samiti?
A: Promotha Mitra, later developed by Aurobindo Ghosh and Barindra Kumar Ghosh.
Q: Who was the leader of the 'Extremists' who was called 'Bal-Pal-Lal'?
A: Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal and Lala Lajpat Rai.
Q: What was the 'Swaraj' demand of the Extremists?
A: Self-rule or self-government as the goal of the Congress.
Q: Who founded the 'Lok Hitawadi' journal?
A: Gopal Hari Deshmukh (Lok Hitawadi).
Q: Who founded the 'Kesari' and 'Maratha' newspapers?
A: Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
Q: Who wrote the book 'Indian Unrest'?
A: Valentine Chirol, a British journalist, describing the Extremist movement.
Q: Who was the founder of the 'Vande Mataram' slogan?
A: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee wrote the song in Anandamath; it became a popular slogan in the national movement.
Q: Who was the first Indian woman president of the INC?
A: Sarojini Naidu, in 1925 (Annie Besant, though a woman, was not Indian; she was British).
Q: What was the main method of the Moderates?
A: Petitions, prayers, resolutions and constitutional agitation.
Q: What was the main method of the Extremists?
A: Boycott, Swadeshi, strikes and more assertive nationalism.
Q: Who presided over the INC session at Lucknow in 1916?
A: A.C. Majumdar.
Q: What was the Lucknow Pact of 1916?
A: An agreement between the Congress and the Muslim League to jointly demand political reforms.
Q: Who was the president of the INC at its session when the Lucknow Pact was signed?
A: A.C. Majumdar.
Q: Who founded the 'Home Rule League' in India?
A: Annie Besant, in 1916.
Q: Who founded the other Home Rule League at Poona?
A: Bal Gangadhar Tilak, in 1916.
Q: What was the 'August Declaration' of 1917?
A: The declaration by Secretary of State Montagu promising responsible government in India.
Q: Who was the founder of the 'Young India' journal?
A: Lala Lajpat Rai (the journal later edited by Gandhi).
Q: Who was the president of the INC at the session when the demand for 'Purna Swaraj' was made?
A: Jawaharlal Nehru, at the Lahore session of 1929.
Q: When was 'Purna Swaraj' declared as the goal of the Congress?
A: At the Lahore session of the INC in December 1929.
Q: Who was the founder of the 'Swaraj Party'?
A: C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru, in 1923.
Q: What was the main objective of the Swaraj Party?
A: To enter the legislative councils and obstruct the British administration from within.
Q: Who was the president of the INC at the Nagpur session of 1920?
A: C. Vijayaraghavachariar.
Q: What was the main change in the Congress programme after the Nagpur session of 1920?
A: The adoption of Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement.
Q: Who was the president of the INC when the Quit India resolution was passed?
A: Abul Kalam Azad, at the Bombay session of 1942.
Q: What was the 'Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms'?
A: The reforms based on the Montagu-Chelmsford Report of 1918, enacted as the Government of India Act 1919.
Q: Who founded the Indian National Congress?
A: Allan Octavian Hume, with the help of Indian leaders.
Q: When was the Indian National Congress founded?
A: On 28 December 1885.
Q: Who was the first president of the Indian National Congress?
A: Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee.
Q: Where was the first session of the Congress held?
A: In Bombay, at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College.
Q: Who were called the 'Moderates' in the Congress?
A: The early Congress leaders who believed in constitutional methods and prayers.
Q: Who were the prominent Moderate leaders?
A: Dadabhai Naoroji, Surendranath Banerjee, Gopal Krishna Gokhale and Ferozshah Mehta.
Q: Who were called the 'Extremists'?
A: The radical nationalists who demanded Swaraj and used more aggressive methods.
Q: Who were the leaders of the Extremists?
A: Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, Lala Lajpat Rai and Aurobindo Ghosh.
Q: Who gave the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'?
A: Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
Q: When did the Congress split into Moderates and Extremists?
A: At the Surat session in 1907.
Q: Who was the president of the Congress at the Surat split?
A: Rash Behari Ghosh.
Q: When did the Congress reunite?
A: At the Lucknow session in 1916.
Q: What was the Lucknow Pact?
A: An agreement between the Congress and the Muslim League in 1916.
Q: Who were known as 'Lal Bal Pal'?
A: Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal.
Q: Who founded the Home Rule League?
A: Bal Gangadhar Tilak (April 1916) and Annie Besant (September 1916) separately.
Q: Who was the president of the Congress at the 1916 Lucknow session?
A: A.C. Majumdar.
Q: What was the main demand of the Moderates?
A: Constitutional reforms and self-government within the British Empire.
Q: What was the partition of Bengal?
A: The division of Bengal by Lord Curzon in 1905, which was a major issue for the early nationalists.
Q: Who was the first woman president of the Indian National Congress?
A: Annie Besant, in 1917.
Q: Who was the president of the Congress at its Haripura session in 1938?
A: Subhas Chandra Bose.
Q: When and where was the Indian National Congress founded?
A: The Indian National Congress was founded on 28 December 1885 at the Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay. It had 72 delegates and its first president was W. C. Bonnerjee. The main organiser was A. O. Hume.
Q: Who founded the Indian National Congress and who suggested its name?
A: A. O. Hume, a retired British civil servant, was the key founder-organiser of the Congress and is called its father. The name "Indian National Congress" was suggested by Dadabhai Naoroji, who is known as the Grand Old Man of India.
Q: What were the main demands of the Moderates?
A: The Moderates demanded the Indianisation of the services, reduction of military expenditure, greater Indian representation in the legislative councils, freedom of the press and the holding of Indian Civil Service examinations in India. They used constitutional methods such as prayer, petition and protest.
Q: Who were the Extremists and what did they want?
A: The Extremists were Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai and Bipin Chandra Pal, together called Lal-Bal-Pal. They demanded Swaraj (self-rule) and used the methods of boycott, swadeshi and passive resistance. The partition of Bengal in 1905 gave a great push to their movement.
Q: What happened at the Surat session of 1907?
A: At the Surat session of 1907 the Congress split into two groups, the Moderates and the Extremists, over differences in goals and methods. The two groups were reunited at the Lucknow session of 1916, where the Lucknow Pact was concluded with the Muslim League.
Q: Name some pre-Congress political associations.
A: Important pre-Congress associations were the Landholders' Society (1838), British Indian Association (1851), Madras Native Association (1852), Bombay Association (1852), East India Association (1866), Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1867), Indian Association (1876), Madras Mahajan Sabha (1884) and Bombay Presidency Association (1885).
Q: ভাৰতীয় জাতীয় কংগ্ৰেছ কেতিয়া আৰু ক'ত প্ৰতিষ্ঠা হৈছিল?
A: ভাৰতীয় জাতীয় কংগ্ৰেছ ১৮৮৫ চনৰ ২৮ ডিচেম্বৰত বোম্বাইৰ গোকুলদাস তেজপাল সংস্কৃত মহাবিদ্যালয়ত প্ৰতিষ্ঠা হৈছিল। ইয়াত ৭২ জন প্ৰতিনিধি আছিল আৰু ইয়াৰ প্ৰথম সভাপতি আছিল ডব্লিউ. চি. বনাৰ্জী। মূল সংগঠক আছিল এ. অ'. হিউম।
Q: ভাৰতীয় জাতীয় কংগ্ৰেছ কোনে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল আৰু নামটো কোনে প্ৰস্তাৱ কৰিছিল?
A: এ. অ'. হিউম, এজন অৱসৰপ্ৰাপ্ত ব্ৰিটিছ অসামৰিক বিষয়া, কংগ্ৰেছৰ মূল প্ৰতিষ্ঠাপক-সংগঠক আছিল আৰু তেওঁক ইয়াৰ পিতৃ বুলি কোৱা হয়। "ইণ্ডিয়ান নেশ্যনেল কংগ্ৰেছ" নামটো দাদাভাই নৌৰজীয়ে প্ৰস্তাৱ কৰিছিল, যাক ভাৰতৰ গ্ৰেণ্ড ওল্ড মেন বুলি কোৱা হয়।
Q: মধ্যপন্থীসকলৰ মূল দাবীসমূহ কি আছিল?
A: মধ্যপন্থীসকলে সেৱাৰ ভাৰতীয়কৰণ, সামৰিক ব্যয় হ্ৰাস, বিধান পৰিষদত ভাৰতীয়ৰ বৃহত্তৰ প্ৰতিনিধিত্ব, সংবাদপত্ৰৰ স্বাধীনতা আৰু ভাৰতত ভাৰতীয় অসামৰিক সেৱাৰ পৰীক্ষা অনুষ্ঠিত কৰাৰ দাবী জনাইছিল। তেওঁলোকে প্ৰাৰ্থনা, আবেদন আৰু প্ৰতিবাদৰ দৰে সাংবিধানিক পদ্ধতি ব্যৱহাৰ কৰিছিল।
Q: চৰমপন্থীসকল কোন আছিল আৰু তেওঁলোকে কি বিচাৰিছিল?
A: চৰমপন্থীসকল আছিল বাল গংগাধৰ টিলক, লালা লাজপত ৰায় আৰু বিপিন চন্দ্ৰ পাল, যাক একেলগে লাল-বাল-পাল বুলি কোৱা হয়। তেওঁলোকে স্বৰাজ (স্বশাসন) দাবী কৰিছিল আৰু বৰ্জন, স্বদেশী আৰু নিষ্ক্ৰিয় প্ৰতিৰোধৰ পদ্ধতি ব্যৱহাৰ কৰিছিল। ১৯০৫ চনৰ বংগ বিভাজনে তেওঁলোকৰ আন্দোলনক এক মহান গতি দিছিল।
Q: ১৯০৭ চনৰ চুৰাট অধিৱেশনত কি হৈছিল?
A: ১৯০৭ চনৰ চুৰাট অধিৱেশনত কংগ্ৰেছ লক্ষ্য আৰু পদ্ধতিৰ মতভেদৰ বাবে মধ্যপন্থী আৰু চৰমপন্থী দুটা গোটত বিভক্ত হৈছিল। দুয়োটা গোট ১৯১৬ চনৰ লক্ষ্ণৌ অধিৱেশনত পুনৰ একত্ৰিত হৈছিল, য'ত মুছলিম লীগৰ সৈতে লক্ষ্ণৌ চুক্তি সম্পন্ন হৈছিল।
Q: কংগ্ৰেছৰ পূৰ্বৰ কিছুমান ৰাজনৈতিক সংস্থাৰ নাম লিখক।
A: গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ কংগ্ৰেছ-পূৰ্বৱৰ্তী সংস্থাসমূহ আছিল ভূস্বামী সভা (১৮৩৮), ব্ৰিটিছ ইণ্ডিয়ান অছ'চিয়েশ্যন (১৮৫১), মাদ্ৰাজ নেটিভ অছ'চিয়েশ্যন (১৮৫২), বোম্বাই অছ'চিয়েশ্যন (১৮৫২), ইষ্ট ইণ্ডিয়া অছ'চিয়েশ্যন (১৮৬৬), পুনা সাৰ্বজনিক সভা (১৮৬৭), ইণ্ডিয়ান অছ'চিয়েশ্যন (১৮৭৬), মাদ্ৰাজ মহাজন সভা (১৮৮৪) আৰু বোম্বাই প্ৰেচিডেন্সি অছ'চিয়েশ্যন (১৮৮৫)।

### Partition of Bengal & Swadeshi Movement — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/modern-indian-history-sec/partition-bengal-swadeshi/
Summary: Practice partition of bengal & swadeshi movement questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: When was Bengal partitioned?
A: On 16 October 1905.
Q: Who was the Viceroy who partitioned Bengal?
A: Lord Curzon.
Q: What was the official reason given for the partition of Bengal?
A: To improve administrative efficiency, as the province of Bengal was too large.
Q: What was the real motive behind the partition of Bengal?
A: To weaken the rising national movement in Bengal by dividing the province on communal lines.
Q: Which two provinces were created by the partition of Bengal?
A: West Bengal (with its capital at Calcutta) and East Bengal and Assam (with its capital at Dacca).
Q: Who wrote the famous patriotic song 'Vande Mataram'?
A: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, in his novel Anandamath.
Q: What was the Swadeshi Movement?
A: A movement to promote Indian-made goods and boycott British goods.
Q: Who launched the Swadeshi Movement?
A: The movement was launched by the nationalists of Bengal in response to the partition, led by leaders like Surendranath Banerjee and Aurobindo Ghosh.
Q: What was the slogan of the Swadeshi Movement?
A: 'Vande Mataram'.
Q: Who was the leader who wrote the famous 'Sare Jahan Se Achha'?
A: Muhammad Iqbal, the poet.
Q: Who founded the 'Swadeshi Bandhav Samiti'?
A: Ashwini Kumar Dutta, at Barisal.
Q: Who wrote the book 'Swadeshi Andolan'?
A: No single author; it is a general topic. The main propagator of the idea was Aurobindo Ghosh and Bipin Chandra Pal.
Q: What was the 'Boycott Movement'?
A: The boycott of British goods as part of the Swadeshi movement.
Q: What was the main aim of the Swadeshi movement's boycott?
A: To hurt British economic interests and promote Indian industry.
Q: Who was the leader who called the partition of Bengal a 'settled fact'?
A: Lord Morley, the Secretary of State.
Q: When was the partition of Bengal annulled?
A: In December 1911, during the Delhi Durbar of George V.
Q: Who announced the annulment of the partition of Bengal?
A: Lord Hardinge, the Viceroy, at the Delhi Durbar.
Q: What was the capital of India shifted to in 1911?
A: From Calcutta to Delhi.
Q: Which new province was created in 1912 after the annulment?
A: Bihar and Orissa was separated from Bengal.
Q: What was the 'Rakhi Bandhan' day observed on 16 October 1905?
A: A day of protest observed by the Bengalis tying rakhis as a symbol of unity.
Q: Who was the leader who gave the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright'?
A: Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
Q: What was the aim of the 'Anushilan Samiti' in the Swadeshi context?
A: To organise physical and revolutionary training for the youth.
Q: Who was the revolutionary who was the editor of 'Sandhya' and 'Yugantar'?
A: Braj Kishore Ghosh, and the Yugantar was edited by Bhupendranath Dutt and Barindra Kumar Ghosh.
Q: Who founded the 'Barisal Conference' of the Swadeshi movement?
A: Ashwini Kumar Dutta, which was held in 1906.
Q: What was the 'Lal-Bal-Pal' slogan referring to?
A: The trio of Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal.
Q: Who was the first president of the 'East Bengal and Assam' province?
A: The first Lieutenant Governor was J. Bamfylde Fuller.
Q: What was the attitude of the Assam valley towards the partition?
A: The Assam valley initially welcomed the partition as it was united with East Bengal, but later opposed it.
Q: Who was the leader of the anti-partition movement in Assam?
A: Leaders like Manik Chandra Baruah and others opposed the partition in Assam.
Q: What was the role of the press in the Swadeshi movement?
A: Newspapers like 'Kesari', 'Sandhya' and 'Yugantar' propagated the Swadeshi ideas.
Q: What was the 'Dacca Anushilan Samiti'?
A: A revolutionary organisation based in East Bengal, founded by Pulin Behari Das.
Q: Who was the famous leader who resigned from the 'Anushilan Samiti' to join the mainstream?
A: Aurobindo Ghosh moved towards spiritualism after the Alipore bomb case.
Q: What was the 'Alipore Bomb Case'?
A: The trial of the revolutionaries of the Anushilan Samiti after the attempt on the life of Kingsford in 1908.
Q: Who was the magistrate targeted by the revolutionaries in Muzaffarpur?
A: Kingsford, who was saved, but the bomb killed the two Barrister wives of Mrs. Kennedy.
Q: Who threw the bomb at Muzaffarpur?
A: Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki.
Q: Who was the revolutionary hanged in the Muzaffarpur case?
A: Khudiram Bose, who was only 18 years old.
Q: What was the 'Swadeshi' attitude towards the partition of Bengal by the Moderates?
A: The Moderates initially supported the protest but later differed on the boycott methods.
Q: Who was the Viceroy who succeeded Curzon?
A: Lord Minto.
Q: What was the 'Morley-Minto Reforms' of 1909?
A: The Indian Councils Act 1909, which introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
Q: What was the main drawback of the Morley-Minto Reforms?
A: The introduction of separate electorates for Muslims, which sowed the seeds of communalism.
Q: Who was the president of the INC at its Calcutta session of 1906?
A: Dadabhai Naoroji, the third time he presided.
Q: What was the main resolution passed at the Calcutta session of 1906?
A: The resolution supporting Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education.
Q: Who was the leader who founded the 'National Council of Education'?
A: The National Council of Education was founded in 1906 by the nationalists of Bengal, leading to the Jadavpur University.
Q: What was the 'Benaras session' of 1905 known for?
A: It was the session where G.K. Gokhale presided and the Congress condemned the partition.
Q: Who was the leader of the 'Swadeshi' movement who wrote 'Anandamath'?
A: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, though he wrote it before the movement, it inspired it.
Q: What was the role of Rabindranath Tagore in the Swadeshi movement?
A: He wrote patriotic songs and actively supported the movement, but later withdrew from it.
Q: Who was the leader who established the 'Bangabhanga' protest at the 'Hindu Mela'?
A: The Hindu Mela was founded earlier by Nabagopal Mitra; the protest against Bangabhanga was led by the nationalists.
Q: What was the result of the partition of Bengal on the national movement?
A: It gave a powerful impetus to the national movement and the rise of extremism.
Q: Who was the 'Bengal partition' annulled by which announcement?
A: The Royal Announcement by George V at the Delhi Durbar in December 1911.
Q: Which two leaders of the INC met Lord Minto in 1906?
A: Aga Khan and Gokhale discussed the Muslim demands, leading to separate electorates.
Q: What was the 'Swadeshi' movement's impact on the economy?
A: It promoted indigenous industries like textiles and banks, and reduced the demand for British goods.
Q: Who was the leader who started the 'Arya Samaj' in Assam during the Swadeshi period?
A: No major Arya Samaj was founded then; the social reform was led by figures like Gunabhiram Barua.
Q: What was the impact of the partition on the Assamese people?
A: The Assam valley was separated from the Brahmaputra valley's unity with Bengal, creating both benefits and grievances.
Q: Who was the leader who advocated the 'Boycott' of foreign goods as a political weapon?
A: Aurobindo Ghosh and Bipin Chandra Pal.
Q: What was the 'Jugantar Patrika'?
A: A revolutionary newspaper edited by Barindra Kumar Ghosh and Bhupendranath Dutt.
Q: Who was the leader who organised the 'Swadeshi mela'?
A: The first Swadeshi Mela was organised in 1901 by the Indian National Congress supporters in Bengal.
Q: When was Bengal partitioned?
A: On 16 October 1905, by Lord Curzon.
Q: Who partitioned Bengal?
A: Lord Curzon.
Q: What was the official reason given for the partition of Bengal?
A: Administrative efficiency, as Bengal was too large to be governed as one province.
Q: What was the real reason for the partition of Bengal?
A: To weaken the growing nationalism in Bengal by dividing the Bengalis.
Q: What was the Swadeshi Movement?
A: A movement to use Indian goods and boycott British goods, launched during the anti-partition agitation.
Q: What was the Boycott Movement?
A: The refusal to use British goods as part of the Swadeshi movement.
Q: Who were the leaders of the Swadeshi Movement?
A: Aurobindo Ghosh, Bipin Chandra Pal, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Lala Lajpat Rai.
Q: What was the national education movement?
A: The establishment of national schools and colleges as an alternative to government institutions during the Swadeshi period.
Q: Who founded the National Council of Education?
A: It was founded in 1906 in Bengal to promote national education.
Q: What was the 'Raksha Bandhan' protest during the anti-partition movement?
A: The tying of rakhis as a symbol of unity against the partition.
Q: When was the partition of Bengal annulled?
A: In December 1911, at the Delhi Durbar of King George V.
Q: Who announced the annulment of the partition of Bengal?
A: Viceroy Lord Hardinge, on behalf of King George V.
Q: When was the capital of British India shifted from Calcutta to Delhi?
A: In 1911.
Q: What was the impact of the Swadeshi movement on Indian industry?
A: It encouraged the growth of indigenous industries like cotton mills, soap, match and steel.
Q: What was the 'Vande Mataram'?
A: The patriotic song written by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, which became the anthem of the Swadeshi movement.
Q: Who partitioned Bengal and why?
A: The Viceroy Lord Curzon announced the partition of Bengal on 19 July 1905. The official reason was administrative convenience, but the real aim was to weaken the nationalist movement and to divide Hindus and Muslims by creating a Muslim-majority province.
Q: When did the Partition of Bengal come into effect?
A: The partition came into effect on 16 October 1905. That day was observed by the people as a day of mourning with fasts, processions and the tying of rakhi between Hindus and Muslims as a symbol of unity.
Q: What was the Swadeshi Movement?
A: The Swadeshi Movement was the movement to boycott British goods and use indigenous (swadeshi) goods. It was formally launched at the Town Hall, Calcutta, on 7 August 1905 and used methods such as boycott, swadeshi, hartal, picketing and national education. Its slogan was Bande Mataram.
Q: Who were the main leaders of the anti-partition movement?
A: The main leaders were Surendranath Banerjee, Ananda Mohan Bose, Bipin Chandra Pal, Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Aurobindo Ghosh. Ashwini Kumar Dutt of Barisal was a leading organiser, and Rabindranath Tagore composed songs for the movement.
Q: What was the National Council of Education?
A: The National Council of Education was set up in 1906 during the Swadeshi Movement to promote national education. The Bengal National College was founded with Aurobindo Ghosh as its first principal. It reflected the movement's emphasis on self-reliance.
Q: When and by whom was the Partition of Bengal annulled?
A: The partition was annulled in 1911 by Lord Hardinge. In the same year the capital of British India was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi. The annulment was a major victory of the Swadeshi and anti-partition movement.
Q: বংগ কোনে বিভাজন কৰিছিল আৰু কিয়?
A: ভাইচৰয় লৰ্ড কাৰ্জনে ১৯০৫ চনৰ ১৯ জুলাইত বংগ বিভাজন ঘোষণা কৰিছিল। চৰকাৰী কাৰণ আছিল প্ৰশাসনিক সুবিধা, কিন্তু প্ৰকৃত উদ্দেশ্য আছিল জাতীয়তাবাদী আন্দোলন দুৰ্বল কৰা আৰু মুছলমান-সংখ্যাগৰিষ্ঠ এখন প্ৰদেশ সৃষ্টি কৰি হিন্দু-মুছলমানক ভাগ কৰা।
Q: বংগ বিভাজন কেতিয়া কাৰ্যকৰী হৈছিল?
A: বিভাজন ১৯০৫ চনৰ ১৬ অক্টোবৰত কাৰ্যকৰী হৈছিল। সেই দিনটো জনসাধাৰণে উপবাস, শোভাযাত্ৰা আৰু ঐক্যৰ প্ৰতীক হিচাপে হিন্দু-মুছলমানৰ মাজত ৰাখী বন্ধাৰ জৰিয়তে শোক দিৱস হিচাপে পালন কৰিছিল।
Q: স্বদেশী আন্দোলন কি আছিল?
A: স্বদেশী আন্দোলন আছিল ব্ৰিটিছ সামগ্ৰী বৰ্জন কৰি দেশীয় (স্বদেশী) সামগ্ৰী ব্যৱহাৰ কৰাৰ আন্দোলন। ই ১৯০৫ চনৰ ৭ আগষ্টত কলিকতাৰ টাউন হলত আনুষ্ঠানিকভাৱে আৰম্ভ হৈছিল আৰু বৰ্জন, স্বদেশী, হৰতাল, পিকেটিং আৰু জাতীয় শিক্ষাৰ দৰে পদ্ধতি ব্যৱহাৰ কৰিছিল। ইয়াৰ শ্ল'গান আছিল বন্দে মাতৰম।
Q: বিভাজন বিৰোধী আন্দোলনৰ মূল নেতাসকল কোন আছিল?
A: মূল নেতাসকল আছিল সুৰেন্দ্ৰনাথ বেনাৰ্জী, আনন্দমোহন বসু, বিপিন চন্দ্ৰ পাল, লালা লাজপত ৰায়, বাল গংগাধৰ টিলক আৰু অৰবিন্দ ঘোষ। বৰিশালৰ অশ্বিনী কুমাৰ দত্ত এজন অগ্ৰণী সংগঠক আছিল, আৰু ৰবীন্দ্ৰনাথ ঠাকুৰে আন্দোলনৰ বাবে গীত ৰচনা কৰিছিল।
Q: জাতীয় শিক্ষা পৰিষদ কি আছিল?
A: স্বদেশী আন্দোলনৰ সময়ত জাতীয় শিক্ষাক প্ৰচাৰ কৰিবলৈ ১৯০৬ চনত জাতীয় শিক্ষা পৰিষদ গঠন কৰা হৈছিল। অৰবিন্দ ঘোষক প্ৰথম অধ্যক্ষ হিচাপে বংগ জাতীয় মহাবিদ্যালয় প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰা হৈছিল। ই আন্দোলনৰ আত্মনিৰ্ভৰশীলতাৰ ওপৰত গুৰুত্ব প্ৰতিফলিত কৰিছিল।
Q: বংগ বিভাজন কেতিয়া আৰু কাৰ দ্বাৰা বাতিল হৈছিল?
A: বিভাজন ১৯১১ চনত লৰ্ড হাৰ্ডিঙে বাতিল কৰিছিল। একে বছৰতে ব্ৰিটিছ ভাৰতৰ ৰাজধানী কলিকতাৰ পৰা দিল্লীলৈ স্থানান্তৰ কৰা হৈছিল। বাতিল স্বদেশী আৰু বিভাজন বিৰোধী আন্দোলনৰ এটা ডাঙৰ বিজয় আছিল।

### Revolt of 1857 Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/modern-indian-history-sec/revolt-of-1857/
Summary: Practice revolt of 1857 questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: When did the Revolt of 1857 break out?
A: On 10 May 1857, at Meerut.
Q: Where did the Revolt of 1857 first break out?
A: Meerut.
Q: Who was the immediate cause of the Revolt of 1857?
A: The introduction of greased cartridges (rumoured to be greased with cow and pig fat) which offended both Hindu and Muslim sepoys.
Q: Who was the first martyr of the Revolt of 1857?
A: Mangal Pandey, a sepoy of the 34th Native Infantry, who revolted at Barrackpore.
Q: Who proclaimed himself the leader of the Revolt of 1857 at Delhi?
A: Bahadur Shah II (Zafar), the last Mughal emperor.
Q: Who was the leader of the Revolt of 1857 in Kanpur?
A: Nana Saheb (Dhondu Pant), the adopted son of the last Peshwa Baji Rao II.
Q: Who was the leader of the Revolt of 1857 at Jhansi?
A: Rani Lakshmibai.
Q: Who was the leader of the Revolt of 1857 in Lucknow?
A: Begum Hazrat Mahal, the wife of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah.
Q: Who was the leader of the Revolt in Bihar (Arrah)?
A: Kunwar Singh, a zamindar of Jagdispur.
Q: Who was the leader of the Revolt of 1857 in Gwalior?
A: Tantia Tope, the general of Nana Saheb.
Q: Who was the ruler of Gwalior who supported the British during the Revolt?
A: Maharaja Scindia (Jayaji Rao Scindia).
Q: Which ruler of the Punjab helped the British in suppressing the Revolt?
A: The Sikhs under Maharaja Ranjit Singh's successors and the Punjab chiefs remained loyal to the British.
Q: Who was the Governor General of India at the time of the Revolt of 1857?
A: Lord Canning.
Q: Who was the commander-in-chief who suppressed the Revolt?
A: Sir Colin Campbell, and in Delhi, John Nicholson.
Q: Where was Bahadur Shah II exiled after the Revolt?
A: Rangoon (Yangon) in Burma.
Q: Who was the Nana Saheb in the Revolt of 1857?
A: Dhondu Pant, the adopted son of Baji Rao II, the last Peshwa.
Q: What was the main reason for the discontent of the sepoys?
A: The greased cartridges, poor pay and conditions, and the General Service Enlistment Act.
Q: What was the political cause of the Revolt of 1857?
A: The Doctrine of Lapse, the annexation of Awadh, and the abolition of pensions of rulers like the Peshwa.
Q: What was the social cause of the Revolt of 1857?
A: The fear of forced conversion to Christianity and the interference in social customs.
Q: What was the economic cause of the Revolt?
A: The heavy land revenue, the drain of wealth, and the destruction of Indian industries.
Q: Who was the leader of the Revolt in Bareilly?
A: Khan Bahadur Khan.
Q: Who was the leader of the Revolt in Allahabad?
A: Liaqat Ali.
Q: Who led the revolt in the Gorakhpur and Azamgarh regions?
A: Kunwar Singh and his brother Amar Singh.
Q: Who was the leader of the Revolt in Faizabad?
A: Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah, known as 'Danka Shah'.
Q: Who was the Mughal prince who fought against the British during the Revolt?
A: Mirza Mughal, son of Bahadur Shah II.
Q: What was the result of the Revolt of 1857?
A: The rule of the East India Company ended and India came under the direct rule of the British Crown.
Q: Which act transferred the government of India from the Company to the Crown?
A: The Government of India Act, 1858.
Q: Who was the first Viceroy of India?
A: Lord Canning.
Q: What was the 'Queen's Proclamation' of 1858?
A: The declaration by Queen Victoria promising no further annexation and religious tolerance.
Q: What happened to the Mughal dynasty after the Revolt?
A: The Mughal dynasty was abolished, and Bahadur Shah II was exiled to Rangoon.
Q: Which group of sepoys started the Revolt at Meerut?
A: The sepoys of the 3rd Cavalry, who were imprisoned and then released by their comrades.
Q: Why did the Revolt fail?
A: Lack of unity, no common programme, localised leadership, and the support of many Indian rulers and the modern educated class for the British.
Q: Which Indian states remained loyal to the British during the Revolt?
A: Hyderabad, Mysore, Gwalior (Scindia), the Punjab and the Rajput states.
Q: Who was the commander who recaptured Delhi?
A: The British forces under John Nicholson and General Wilson recaptured Delhi in September 1857.
Q: Who fought in the battle at Kotah ki Serai where Tantia Tope was defeated?
A: Tantia Tope was defeated by the British under Sir Hugh Rose.
Q: Who captured Jhansi from Rani Lakshmibai?
A: The British under Sir Hugh Rose, in April 1858.
Q: Where was Rani Lakshmibai killed?
A: At Gwalior, on 17 June 1858.
Q: Who was Tantia Tope's real name?
A: Ramachandra Pandurang Tope (also written as Tatya Tope).
Q: What was the result of the annexation of Awadh on the Revolt?
A: The annexation of Awadh alienated the taluqdars and led to a strong revolt in Awadh.
Q: Who was the leader of the Revolt in the 'Gorakhpur' region who was a zamindar?
A: Kunwar Singh.
Q: Which of the following was NOT a leader of the Revolt of 1857?
A: Bal Gangadhar Tilak, who was born much later (1856) and was not part of the Revolt.
Q: What was the British policy of 'Divide and Rule' after 1857?
A: The policy of creating divisions among Indians based on religion, caste and region to weaken the national movement.
Q: Which of the following was a result of the Revolt of 1857?
A: The end of the Company's rule, the abolition of the Doctrine of Lapse, and the reorganization of the army.
Q: What was the position of the princely states after 1858?
A: They were recognised as independent and were to remain loyal to the Crown.
Q: Who was the Secretary of State for India after 1858?
A: A member of the British cabinet who headed the India Office and was aided by the Council of India.
Q: What happened to the East India Company's army after 1857?
A: It was reorganised into the Indian Army under the British Crown.
Q: What was the immediate effect of the Revolt on the British attitude?
A: The British became suspicious of Indians and adopted a policy of racial discrimination.
Q: Who was the ruler of Delhi who was captured by the British?
A: Bahadur Shah II.
Q: What was the role of the Muslims in the Revolt?
A: Both Hindus and Muslims fought together against the British.
Q: Who was the leader of the revolt at 'Satara'?
A: The revolt at Satara was led by the followers of Nana Saheb and the deposed rulers.
Q: What was the condition of the peasants during the Revolt?
A: The peasants joined the Revolt due to the heavy revenue demands and the fear of losing their lands.
Q: Who was the British officer who killed Mangal Pandey?
A: Mangal Pandey was executed by the British after being captured; he was shot at Barrackpore.
Q: When did the Revolt of 1857 begin?
A: On 10 May 1857, at Meerut.
Q: Who was the leader of the revolt in Delhi?
A: Bahadur Shah Zafar (the last Mughal emperor).
Q: Who was the leader of the revolt in Kanpur?
A: Nana Saheb.
Q: Who was the leader of the revolt in Lucknow?
A: Begum Hazrat Mahal.
Q: Who was the leader of the revolt in Jhansi?
A: Rani Lakshmibai.
Q: Who was the leader of the revolt in Bareilly?
A: Khan Bahadur Khan.
Q: Who was the leader of the revolt in Bihar (Arrah)?
A: Kunwar Singh.
Q: What was the immediate cause of the Revolt of 1857?
A: The greased cartridges of the new Enfield rifles, which were rumoured to contain cow and pig fat.
Q: Who was the sepoy who refused to use the greased cartridges and was hanged?
A: Mangal Pandey, at Barrackpore in March 1857.
Q: Who was the Governor-General of India during the Revolt of 1857?
A: Lord Canning.
Q: Where did Rani Lakshmibai die?
A: In the battle of Gwalior, in June 1858.
Q: What was the Doctrine of Lapse?
A: A policy of annexing states whose rulers died without a natural heir, introduced by Lord Dalhousie.
Q: Which states were annexed by the Doctrine of Lapse?
A: Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur, Sambalpur and Udaipur.
Q: What was the result of the Revolt of 1857?
A: The rule of the East India Company ended and India came under the direct rule of the British Crown.
Q: When was the Government of India Act 1858 passed?
A: In August 1858.
Q: Who became the first Viceroy of India?
A: Lord Canning.
Q: What happened to Bahadur Shah Zafar after the revolt?
A: He was exiled to Rangoon, where he died in 1862.
Q: What was the main cause of the failure of the Revolt of 1857?
A: Lack of unity, no common programme, and no support from many sections like the educated class and most princely states.
Q: When and where did the Revolt of 1857 begin?
A: The Revolt of 1857 began on 10 May 1857 at Meerut, when Indian sepoys rose against their British officers. They then marched to Delhi and proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar as their leader.
Q: What was the immediate cause of the Revolt of 1857?
A: The immediate cause was the introduction of the new Enfield rifle, whose cartridges were greased with cow and pig fat. Since soldiers had to bite the cartridge, it offended both Hindu and Muslim religious feelings. Mangal Pandey's action at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857 was the first spark.
Q: Who were the main leaders of the Revolt of 1857?
A: The main leaders were Bahadur Shah Zafar and Bakht Khan at Delhi, Nana Saheb and Tantia Tope at Kanpur, Begum Hazrat Mahal at Lucknow, Rani Lakshmibai at Jhansi, Kunwar Singh in Bihar, Khan Bahadur Khan at Bareilly and Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah at Faizabad.
Q: Why did the Revolt of 1857 fail?
A: The revolt failed due to the lack of a central leader and a common plan, its localised spread, and the help that many Indian rulers such as the Sikhs, Gurkhas, Scindia, the Nizam and the Rajputs gave to the British. The British also had better arms, money, discipline and the telegraph.
Q: What were the results of the Revolt of 1857?
A: The main result was the end of the East India Company's rule. The Government of India Act of 1858 abolished the Company and transferred power to the British Crown. Queen Victoria issued a Proclamation on 1 November 1858 and Lord Canning became the first Viceroy. The army was reorganised and the policy of divide and rule was followed.
Q: What is meant by the Doctrine of Lapse?
A: The Doctrine of Lapse was a policy of Lord Dalhousie under which a state was annexed if its ruler died without a natural heir, and adopted heirs were not recognised. It was used to annex states such as Satara, Jhansi and Nagpur, and it created great resentment that contributed to the Revolt of 1857.
Q: ১৮৫৭ চনৰ বিদ্ৰোহ কেতিয়া আৰু ক'ত আৰম্ভ হৈছিল?
A: ১৮৫৭ চনৰ বিদ্ৰোহ ১৮৫৭ চনৰ ১০ মে' তাৰিখে মিৰাটত আৰম্ভ হৈছিল, যেতিয়া ভাৰতীয় চিপাহীসকলে তেওঁলোকৰ ব্ৰিটিছ বিষয়াসকলৰ বিৰুদ্ধে উঠিছিল। তাৰ পিছত তেওঁলোকে দিল্লীলৈ গৈ বাহাদুৰ শাহ জাফৰক তেওঁলোকৰ নেতা হিচাপে ঘোষণা কৰিছিল।
Q: ১৮৫৭ চনৰ বিদ্ৰোহৰ তাৎক্ষণিক কাৰণ কি আছিল?
A: তাৎক্ষণিক কাৰণ আছিল নতুন এনফিল্ড ৰাইফলৰ প্ৰৱৰ্তন, যাৰ কাৰ্ট্ৰিজ গাই আৰু গাহৰিৰ চৰ্বিৰে লিপ্ত আছিল। সৈন্যবিলাকে কাৰ্ট্ৰিজ কামোৰাৰ দৰে কৰিবলগীয়া হৈছিল বাবে ই হিন্দু আৰু মুছলমান উভয়ৰে ধৰ্মীয় অনুভূতিত আঘাত কৰিছিল। ২৯ মাৰ্চ ১৮৫৭ চনত বাৰাকপুৰত মঙ্গল পাণ্ডেৰ কাৰ্য্যই প্ৰথম ষ্ট্ৰ'ক আছিল।
Q: ১৮৫৭ চনৰ বিদ্ৰোহৰ প্ৰধান নেতাসকল কোন আছিল?
A: প্ৰধান নেতাসকল আছিল দিল্লীত বাহাদুৰ শাহ জাফৰ আৰু বখত খান, কানপুৰত নানা চাহেব আৰু তাতিয়া টোপে, লক্ষ্ণৌত বেগম হজৰত মহল, ঝাঁসীত ৰাণী লক্ষ্মীবাঈ, বিহাৰত কুনৱৰ সিং, বেৰেলীত খান বাহাদুৰ খান আৰু ফৈজাবাদত মৌলৱী আহমদুল্লাহ শাহ।
Q: ১৮৫৭ চনৰ বিদ্ৰোহ কিয় বিফল হৈছিল?
A: বিদ্ৰোহ বিফল হৈছিল কেন্দ্ৰীয় নেতা আৰু সাধাৰণ পৰিকল্পনাৰ অভাৱ, ইয়াৰ স্থানীয় বিস্তাৰ, আৰু শিখ, গুৰখা, সিন্ধিয়া, নিজাম আৰু ৰাজপুতৰ দৰে বহু ভাৰতীয় শাসকে ব্ৰিটিছসকলক দিয়া সহায়ৰ বাবে। ব্ৰিটিছসকলৰ উন্নত অস্ত্ৰ, ধন, শৃংখলা আৰু টেলিগ্ৰাফো আছিল।
Q: ১৮৫৭ চনৰ বিদ্ৰোহৰ ফলাফল কি আছিল?
A: মূল ফলাফল আছিল ইষ্ট ইণ্ডিয়া কোম্পানীৰ শাসনৰ অন্ত। ১৮৫৮ চনৰ ভাৰত শাসন আইনে কোম্পানী বিলুপ্ত কৰি ক্ষমতা ব্ৰিটিছ ৰাজমুকুটলৈ হস্তান্তৰ কৰিছিল। ৰাণী ভিক্টোৰিয়াই ১৮৫৮ চনৰ ১ নৱেম্বৰত ঘোষণাপত্ৰ জাৰি কৰিছিল আৰু লৰ্ড ক্যানিং প্ৰথম ভাইচৰয় হৈছিল। সেনা পুনৰ সংগঠিত কৰা হৈছিল আৰু ভাগ কৰি শাসন কৰাৰ নীতি অনুসৰণ কৰা হৈছিল।
Q: অপ্ৰাপ্তি নীতি মানে কি?
A: অপ্ৰাপ্তি নীতি লৰ্ড ডালহাউজীৰ এটা নীতি আছিল, যাৰ অধীনত কোনো শাসকৰ প্ৰাকৃতিক উত্তৰাধিকাৰী নোহোৱাকৈ মৃত্যু হ'লে ৰাজ্য সংযুক্ত কৰা হৈছিল আৰু গ্ৰহণ কৰা উত্তৰাধিকাৰীক স্বীকৃতি দিয়া নহৈছিল। ইয়াৰ দ্বাৰা সাতাৰা, ঝাঁসী আৰু নাগপুৰৰ দৰে ৰাজ্য সংযুক্ত কৰা হৈছিল, আৰু ই ১৮৫৭ চনৰ বিদ্ৰোহত অৰিহণা যোগোৱা তীব্ৰ অসন্তোষ সৃষ্টি কৰিছিল।

### Revolutionary Freedom Movements — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/modern-indian-history-sec/revolutionary-movements/
Summary: Practice revolutionary freedom movements questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Who founded the Abhinav Bharat Society?
A: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and his brother Ganesh Savarkar.
Q: Who founded the Ghadar Party?
A: Lala Har Dayal, in 1913 in San Francisco, USA.
Q: What was the newspaper of the Ghadar Party?
A: 'The Ghadar' (Gadar).
Q: Who founded the 'India House' in London?
A: Shyamji Krishna Varma.
Q: Who was the revolutionary who assassinated Curzon Wyllie?
A: Madan Lal Dhingra, in London in 1909.
Q: Who founded the 'Mitra Mela' which later became Abhinav Bharat?
A: The Savarkar brothers founded it in Nashik.
Q: Who was the leader of the 'Anushilan Samiti' in Calcutta?
A: Aurobindo Ghosh and Barindra Kumar Ghosh.
Q: Who was the founder of the 'Dacca Anushilan Samiti'?
A: Pulin Behari Das.
Q: Who founded the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)?
A: Chandrasekhar Azad and Bhagat Singh, after the Kakori case.
Q: Who was the founder of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA)?
A: Ram Prasad Bismil, Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee and Sachindra Nath Sanyal.
Q: What was the Kakori Conspiracy Case?
A: The robbery of a government train at Kakori (near Lucknow) in 1925 by the HRA to raise funds.
Q: Who was hanged in the Kakori Conspiracy Case?
A: Ram Prasad Bismil, Roshan Singh, Ashfaqullah Khan and Rajendra Lahiri.
Q: Who was the revolutionary who threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly?
A: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt, in 1929.
Q: Who was the British police officer killed by Bhagat Singh and his associates?
A: J.P. Saunders, in Lahore in 1928 (killed mistakenly for Scott).
Q: Why did Bhagat Singh and his comrades kill Saunders?
A: To avenge the death of Lala Lajpat Rai, who was injured in a lathi charge during the Simon Commission protest.
Q: Who was the leader who gave the slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad'?
A: Bhagat Singh popularised it, originally coined by Muhammad Iqbal.
Q: Who was the founder of the 'Naujawan Bharat Sabha'?
A: Bhagat Singh, in 1926 in Lahore.
Q: When were Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru hanged?
A: On 23 March 1931, at Lahore jail.
Q: Who was the revolutionary leader who escaped from the British and was known as 'Azad'?
A: Chandrasekhar Azad.
Q: Where did Chandrasekhar Azad die?
A: At Alfred Park in Allahabad, in 1931.
Q: Who led the Chittagong Armoury Raid?
A: Surya Sen (Masterda), in 1930.
Q: Who was the female revolutionary of the Chittagong raid?
A: Pritilata Waddedar, who led a raid on the European Club.
Q: Who was the revolutionary leader known as 'Masterda'?
A: Surya Sen.
Q: What was the 'Chittagong Armoury Raid'?
A: A raid on the armoury of Chittagong by revolutionaries led by Surya Sen in 1930 to seize arms.
Q: Who founded the 'India Independence League'?
A: Rash Behari Bose, in Japan.
Q: Who was the revolutionary who attempted to assassinate Lord Hardinge?
A: Rash Behari Bose, who threw a bomb at his procession in Delhi in 1912.
Q: Who was the revolutionary who planned the Delhi Conspiracy Case?
A: Rash Behari Bose and Sachin Sanyal.
Q: Who founded the 'Swadesh Bandhav Samiti'?
A: Ashwini Kumar Dutta.
Q: Who was the leader of the revolutionaries in the 'Sanyasi revolt'?
A: The Sannyasi revolt was a peasant uprising in Bengal; no single famous leader is recorded.
Q: Who was the revolutionary hanged in the 'Barisal conspiracy case'?
A: This was a trial of many revolutionaries; the prominent one was Trailokya Nath Chakravarty.
Q: Who was the leader of the 'Jugantar' group?
A: Barindra Kumar Ghosh and Aurobindo Ghosh.
Q: Who was the founder of the 'Anushilan' group in Mymensingh?
A: Hemendra Prasad Ghosh.
Q: What was the role of the revolutionaries in the Ghadar movement?
A: They tried to organise an armed rebellion in India with the help of the Indian soldiers abroad.
Q: What was the 'Komagata Maru' incident?
A: The ship carrying Indian immigrants that was prevented from landing in Canada in 1914, leading to violence.
Q: Who was the leader of the Komagata Maru?
A: Gurdit Singh.
Q: Who was the revolutionary who was a poet and wrote 'Sarfaroshi ki Tamanna'?
A: Ram Prasad Bismil.
Q: Who founded the 'Berlin Committee' during World War I?
A: Virendranath Chattopadhyay (Chatto), in 1914.
Q: Who was the founder of the 'Revolutionary Socialist Party'?
A: Ajoy Kumar Mukherjee, in 1940.
Q: Who was the revolutionary leader of the Punjab known as 'Master Tara Singh'?
A: Tara Singh was a Sikh leader, not a revolutionary of the armed kind; the Punjab revolutionary leader was Sohan Singh Josh (communist).
Q: Who was the founder of the 'Azad Hind Fauj' (INA) initially?
A: Mohammad Mohan Singh and later Subhas Chandra Bose took over its leadership.
Q: Who was the revolutionary woman who was a member of the 'Anushilan Samiti'?
A: Kalyani Das and later Bina Das, who shot at the Bengal Governor.
Q: Who shot at the Governor of Bengal in 1932?
A: Bina Das.
Q: Who was the leader of the revolutionaries in the 'Andaman Cellular Jail'?
A: Many revolutionaries like Barindra Ghosh, Sachin Sanyal and V.D. Savarkar were imprisoned there.
Q: Who was the revolutionary who wrote 'The Indian War of Independence'?
A: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar.
Q: What was the main objective of the revolutionary movements?
A: To achieve independence through armed struggle and to remove the British by force.
Q: Who was the revolutionary leader who was the editor of 'Pratap' newspaper?
A: Ganesh Shankar Vidyarthi.
Q: Who founded the 'Hindustan Seva Dal'?
A: N.S. Hardikar, in 1923.
Q: Who was the revolutionary leader who died in the 'Lahore Conspiracy Case' trial?
A: The main martyrs were Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru.
Q: Who was the revolutionary who attempted to assassinate Sir John Simon?
A: The revolutionaries like Bhagat Singh's group; no direct attempt on Simon succeeded.
Q: Who was the leader of the 'All India Revolutionary Party'?
A: This is not a distinct well-known party; the main organisations were the HRA, HSRA, Ghadar and Anushilan.
Q: Who was the founder of the 'Anushilan Samiti'?
A: Pramathanath Mitra, in 1902 in Calcutta.
Q: Who was the leader of the 'Jugantar' party?
A: Barindra Kumar Ghosh.
Q: Who was the editor of the 'Jugantar' newspaper?
A: Bhupendranath Dutta.
Q: What was the Bengal Conspiracy Case?
A: The trial of the Alipore bomb case revolutionaries in 1908.
Q: Who was the defence lawyer in the Alipore Bomb Case?
A: Chittaranjan Das.
Q: Who was the revolutionary who escaped from the Alipore Jail?
A: Aurobindo Ghosh's brother Barindra Ghosh was imprisoned; the famous escape was of the revolutionary Upen Banerjee.
Q: Who was the founder of the 'Bharat Mata Society'?
A: Shyamji Krishna Varma.
Q: What was the 'India House'?
A: A hostel for Indian students in London that was a centre of revolutionary activity.
Q: Who founded the 'Free India Society'?
A: V.D. Savarkar, in London in 1907.
Q: Who was the founder of the 'Abhinav Bharat'? (English name)
A: It was called the 'Young India Society' in English.
Q: Who was the leader of the revolutionaries in the 1912 Delhi conspiracy?
A: Rash Behari Bose and Sachin Sanyal.
Q: Who was the founder of the 'Hindustan Ghadar' newspaper?
A: It was published by the Ghadar Party, led by Lala Har Dayal.
Q: What was the 'Mutiny of the Ghadar'?
A: The planned armed revolt in February 1915 by the Ghadar party with the help of Indian soldiers.
Q: Who was the leader of the Ghadar revolt of 1915?
A: Rash Behari Bose was the chief organiser.
