Q: What was the 'Lahore Conspiracy Case' of 1915?
A: The trial of the Ghadar revolutionaries after the failed revolt of February 1915.
Q: Who was the revolutionary who killed a British officer in Poona in 1909?
A: Anant Lakshman Kanhere, who killed Collector Jackson.
Q: Who was the leader of the 'Anushilan Samiti' in Dacca?
A: Pulin Behari Das.
Q: Who was the founder of the 'Kirti' group in Punjab?
A: Bhagat Singh and Sukhdev, who started the 'Kirti Kisan' newspaper.
Q: Who was the leader of the 'Tarak Nath Das' group of revolutionaries?
A: Tarak Nath Das was a revolutionary who worked for the Ghadar movement from abroad.
Q: What was the significance of the revolutionary movement?
A: It inspired the youth and created a spirit of sacrifice, though it did not achieve immediate success.
Q: What were the revolutionary movements in India?
A: The revolutionary movements were armed and secret attempts by young Indians to overthrow British rule, mainly after the partition of Bengal in 1905. They used bombs, pistols and secret societies, and had two phases: the early phase (1905-1917) and the later phase (1920s-1930s).
Q: Who founded the Ghadar Party and where?
A: The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 at San Francisco by Lala Har Dayal and other Indian immigrants in North America. The Ghadar movement tried to spread revolution among Indian soldiers and workers abroad and was strengthened by the Komagata Maru episode of 1914.
Q: What was the Kakori Conspiracy Case?
A: On 9 August 1925 the Hindustan Republican Association carried out the Kakori train robbery to raise funds. Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri were tried in the Kakori Conspiracy Case and hanged.
Q: What was the difference between the HRA and the HSRA?
A: The Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) was founded in 1924 by Sachindranath Sanyal and Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee. In 1928 it was reorganised at Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi, as the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA), adding socialism to its aims. Chandrashekhar Azad and Bhagat Singh were its leading members.
Q: Why were Bhagat Singh and his comrades hanged?
A: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev shot the police officer Saunders on 17 December 1928 to avenge the death of Lala Lajpat Rai, and Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April 1929. In the Lahore Conspiracy Case, Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were hanged on 23 March 1931.
Q: What was the Chittagong Armoury Raid?
A: The Chittagong Armoury Raid was led by Surya Sen (Masterda) on 18 April 1930. The revolutionaries captured the armoury and hoisted the national flag. Surya Sen was arrested and hanged on 12 January 1934. Women such as Pritilata Waddedar and Kalpana Dutt also took part in the revolutionary activities.
Q: ভাৰতত বিপ্লবী আন্দোলন কি আছিল?
A: বিপ্লবী আন্দোলনসমূহ আছিল যুৱ ভাৰতীয়সকলে ব্ৰিটিছ শাসন উৎখাত কৰিবলৈ কৰা সশস্ত্ৰ আৰু গোপন প্ৰচেষ্টা, মূলতঃ ১৯০৫ চনৰ বংগ বিভাজনৰ পিছত। তেওঁলোকে বোমা, পিষ্টল আৰু গোপন সমিতি ব্যৱহাৰ কৰিছিল, আৰু ইয়াৰ দুটা পৰ্যায় আছিল: প্ৰাৰম্ভিক পৰ্যায় (১৯০৫-১৯১৭) আৰু পিছৰ পৰ্যায় (১৯২০ৰ পৰা ১৯৩০ৰ দশক)।
Q: ঘদৰ পাৰ্টি কোনে আৰু ক'ত প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল?
A: ঘদৰ পাৰ্টি ১৯১৩ চনত ছান ফ্ৰান্সিস্কোত লালা হৰ দয়াল আৰু উত্তৰ আমেৰিকাৰ আন ভাৰতীয় প্ৰবাসীসকলে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল। ঘদৰ আন্দোলনে বিদেশত ভাৰতীয় সৈনিক আৰু শ্ৰমিকসকলৰ মাজত বিপ্লৱ বিস্তাৰ কৰিবলৈ চেষ্টা কৰিছিল আৰু ১৯১৪ চনৰ কোমাগাতা মাৰু ঘটনাই ইয়াক সবল কৰিছিল।
Q: কাকৰী ষড়যন্ত্ৰ মামলা কি আছিল?
A: ১৯২৫ চনৰ ৯ আগষ্টত হিন্দুস্তান ৰিপাব্লিকান এছ'চিয়েশ্যনে ধন সংগ্ৰহৰ বাবে কাকৰী ৰেল ডকাইতি কৰিছিল। ৰাম প্ৰসাদ বিসমিল, আশফাকুল্লাহ খান, ৰোশন সিং আৰু ৰাজেন্দ্ৰ লাহিড়ীক কাকৰী ষড়যন্ত্ৰ মামলাত বিচাৰ কৰি ফাঁচি দিয়া হৈছিল।
Q: HRA আৰু HSRA ৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি আছিল?
A: হিন্দুস্তান ৰিপাব্লিকান এছ'চিয়েশ্যন (HRA) ১৯২৪ চনত সচিন্দ্ৰনাথ সান্যাল আৰু জগেশ চন্দ্ৰ চেটাৰ্জীয়ে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল। ১৯২৮ চনত ইয়াক দিল্লীৰ ফিৰোজ শাহ কোটলাত হিন্দুস্তান চ'চিয়েলিষ্ট ৰিপাব্লিকান এছ'চিয়েশ্যন (HSRA) হিচাপে পুনৰ সংগঠিত কৰা হৈছিল, যাৰ লক্ষ্যত সমাজবাদ যোগ কৰা হৈছিল। চন্দ্ৰশেখৰ আজাদ আৰু ভগত সিং ইয়াৰ আগশাৰীৰ সদস্য আছিল।
Q: ভগত সিং আৰু তেওঁৰ সংগীসকলক কিয় ফাঁচি দিয়া হৈছিল?
A: ভগত সিং, ৰাজগুৰু আৰু সুখদেৱে লালা লাজপত ৰায়ৰ মৃত্যুৰ প্ৰতিশোধ ল'বলৈ ১৯২৮ চনৰ ১৭ ডিচেম্বৰত আৰক্ষী বিষয়া ছ'ণ্ডাৰ্ছক গুলীয়াইছিল, আৰু ভগত সিং আৰু বটুকেশ্বৰ দত্তই ১৯২৯ চনৰ ৮ এপ্ৰিলত কেন্দ্ৰীয় বিধান সভাত বোমা নিক্ষেপ কৰিছিল। লাহোৰ ষড়যন্ত্ৰ মামলাত ভগত সিং, সুখদেৱ আৰু ৰাজগুৰুক ১৯৩১ চনৰ ২৩ মাৰ্চত ফাঁচি দিয়া হৈছিল।
Q: চট্টগ্ৰাম কাৰখানা লুণ্ঠন কি আছিল?
A: চট্টগ্ৰাম কাৰখানা লুণ্ঠন ১৯৩০ চনৰ ১৮ এপ্ৰিলত সূৰ্য সেনে (মাষ্টৰদা) নেতৃত্ব দিছিল। বিপ্লৱীসকলে কাৰখানা দখল কৰি ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় পতাকা উত্তোলন কৰিছিল। সূৰ্য সেনক গ্ৰেপ্তাৰ কৰি ১৯৩৪ চনৰ ১২ জানুৱাৰীত ফাঁচি দিয়া হৈছিল। প্ৰীতিলতা ৱাদ্দেদাৰ আৰু কল্পনা দত্তৰ দৰে মহিলাও বিপ্লৱী কাৰ্যকলাপত অংশ লৈছিল।

### Socio-Religious Reform Movements — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/modern-indian-history-sec/socio-religious-reforms/
Summary: Practice socio-religious reform movements questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Who is regarded as the 'Father of Indian Renaissance'?
A: Raja Rammohan Roy.
Q: Who founded the Brahmo Samaj?
A: Raja Rammohan Roy, in 1828 AD.
Q: What was the main belief of the Brahmo Samaj?
A: Belief in one formless God and the rejection of idol worship, superstition and caste discrimination.
Q: Which reform was championed by Raja Rammohan Roy against Sati?
A: The abolition of Sati, which was legalised by Lord William Bentinck in 1829.
Q: Who was the Governor General who abolished Sati?
A: Lord William Bentinck, in 1829 AD.
Q: Who was the supporter of Rammohan Roy in the abolition of Sati?
A: His disciple William Carey and the support of Governor Bentinck.
Q: Who founded the Tattwabodhini Sabha?
A: Debendranath Tagore, in 1839 AD.
Q: Who was the leader of the Brahmo Samaj after Rammohan Roy?
A: Debendranath Tagore and later Keshab Chandra Sen.
Q: Who founded the breakaway 'Brahmo Samaj of India'?
A: Keshab Chandra Sen, in 1866 AD.
Q: Who was the founder of the Arya Samaj?
A: Swami Dayananda Saraswati, in 1875 AD.
Q: What was the motto of the Arya Samaj?
A: 'Back to the Vedas' and 'India for Indians'.
Q: Who founded the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (DAV) schools?
A: The Arya Samaj after the death of Dayananda, following his vision of education.
Q: What was the Shuddhi movement of the Arya Samaj?
A: A movement to reconvert Hindus who had converted to other religions.
Q: Who wrote the book 'Satyarth Prakash'?
A: Swami Dayananda Saraswati.
Q: Who was the founder of the Ramakrishna Mission?
A: Swami Vivekananda, in 1897 AD.
Q: Who was the spiritual guru of Swami Vivekananda?
A: Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa.
Q: Where did Vivekananda deliver his famous speech on Hinduism?
A: At the Parliament of World Religions in Chicago in 1893 AD.
Q: Who founded the Theosophical Society in India?
A: Madam H.P. Blavatsky and Colonel H.S. Olcott, with headquarters at Adyar (Madras).
Q: Who was the president of the Theosophical Society who became a leading Indian nationalist?
A: Annie Besant.
Q: Who founded the Prarthana Samaj in Bombay?
A: Mahadev Govind Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar.
Q: Who founded the Satya Shodhak Samaj?
A: Jyotirao Phule, in 1873 AD.
Q: What was the main aim of the Satya Shodhak Samaj?
A: To fight against caste oppression and the domination of the Brahmins.
Q: Who wrote 'Gulamgiri' (Slavery)?
A: Jyotirao Phule.
Q: Who was the wife of Jyotirao Phule who worked for women's education?
A: Savitribai Phule.
Q: Who founded the Widow Remarriage Association?
A: Vishnushastri Pandit, a reformer from Bombay.
Q: Who founded the Young Bengal movement?
A: Henry Louis Vivian Derozio, a teacher at Hindu College, Calcutta.
Q: What was the aim of the Young Bengal movement?
A: To promote rationalism, free thinking and social reform among the educated youth.
Q: Who was the founder of the Hindu College of Calcutta?
A: Raja Rammohan Roy, David Hare and others in 1817.
Q: Who was the great reformer of Bengal who fought for widow remarriage?
A: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.
Q: Which act legalised widow remarriage in 1856?
A: The Hindu Widow Remarriage Act, passed during the Governor Generalship of Lord Dalhousie.
Q: Who was the famous scholar who popularised the term 'Bande Mataram'?
A: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, in his novel Anandamath.
Q: Who founded the Aligarh Movement?
A: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan.
Q: What was the main aim of the Aligarh Movement?
A: To modernise the Muslim community through western education and social reform.
Q: Who founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College?
A: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan, in 1875 AD (later became Aligarh Muslim University).
Q: Who wrote the book 'Causes of Indian Revolt'?
A: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan.
Q: Who founded the Deoband movement?
A: Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi, with the Dar-ul-Uloom at Deoband in 1867.
Q: Who founded the Ramakrishna Mission's educational work?
A: Swami Vivekananda, who stressed on education for all, especially the poor.
Q: Who founded the Brahmo Samaj in Assam?
A: Gunabhiram Barua and Hemchandra Barua were associated with the reform movement in Assam.
Q: Who was the first Assamese to write about widow remarriage?
A: Gunabhiram Barua, who wrote the drama 'Ramnabami' supporting widow remarriage.
Q: Who was the founder of the Seva Sadan?
A: Behramji Malabari, a Parsi social reformer.
Q: Who founded the Servants of India Society?
A: Gopal Krishna Gokhale, in 1905 AD.
Q: Who founded the 'Bharat Stri Mahamandal'?
A: Sarala Devi Chaudhurani.
Q: Who founded the 'Arya Mahila Samaj'?
A: Pandita Ramabai.
Q: Who founded the 'Sharada Sadan' for widows?
A: Pandita Ramabai.
Q: Who was the great Tamil reformer who fought for the Self-Respect Movement?
A: E.V. Ramasamy (Periyar).
Q: Who founded the Self-Respect Movement?
A: E.V. Ramasamy Naicker, in 1925 AD.
Q: Who founded the 'Derozian' movement of rationalism?
A: Henry Louis Vivian Derozio.
Q: Who was the famous Assamese reformer who fought against child marriage?
A: Hemchandra Barua, and also the Anushilan movement's associates.
Q: Who founded the 'Barak Valley' reform organisation?
A: This is not a standard question; the region saw the spread of Brahmo Samaj ideals.
Q: Who was the founder of the 'Radhasoami' movement?
A: Tulsi Sahib, popularised by Shiv Dayal Singh (Soami Ji Maharaj).
Q: Who founded the 'Society for the Promotion of Female Education'?
A: John Elliot Drinkwater Bethune, who founded the Bethune School for girls.
Q: Who founded the first girls' school in India?
A: Savitribai Phule, who established a school for girls in Pune in 1848.
Q: Who was the founder of the 'Hindu Mela'?
A: Nabagopal Mitra, a Bengali nationalist.
Q: Who was the first Indian woman to preside over the Indian National Congress?
A: Sarojini Naidu (1925, at the Kanpur session).
Q: Who was the first woman president of the Indian National Congress?
A: Annie Besant (1917, at the Calcutta session).
Q: Who founded the Brahmo Samaj?
A: Raja Ram Mohan Roy, in 1828.
Q: Who was known as the 'Father of Modern India'?
A: Raja Ram Mohan Roy.
Q: What was the main aim of the Brahmo Samaj?
A: To reform Hindu society, promote monotheism and oppose idol worship and social evils.
Q: Who founded the Arya Samaj?
A: Swami Dayanand Saraswati, in 1875.
Q: What was the motto of the Arya Samaj?
A: 'Back to the Vedas'.
Q: Who wrote the 'Satyarth Prakash'?
A: Swami Dayanand Saraswati.
Q: Who founded the Prarthana Samaj?
A: Atmaram Pandurang, in Bombay in 1867.
Q: Who founded the Ramakrishna Mission?
A: Swami Vivekananda, in 1897.
Q: Who was the guru of Swami Vivekananda?
A: Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa.
Q: Who founded the Theosophical Society?
A: Madame H.P. Blavatsky and Colonel H.S. Olcott, in 1875 in New York.
Q: Who popularised the Theosophical Society in India?
A: Annie Besant.
Q: Who founded the Aligarh Movement?
A: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan.
Q: Who founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College?
A: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan, in 1875 at Aligarh.
Q: Who is known as the pioneer of women's education in India?
A: Jyotirao Phule and his wife Savitribai Phule.
Q: Who founded the Satyashodhak Samaj?
A: Jyotirao Phule, in 1873.
Q: Who founded the Servants of India Society?
A: Gopal Krishna Gokhale, in 1905.
Q: Who was known as the 'Mahatma of Maharashtra'?
A: Jyotirao Phule.
Q: Who founded the Veda Samaj in Madras?
A: Keshub Chunder Sen's followers, inspired by the Brahmo Samaj.
Q: Who founded the Brahmo Samaj and why is it important?
A: The Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828 (as the Brahmo Sabha). It opposed idolatry, caste rigidity and sati, and promoted rational worship, women's rights and modern education. Ram Mohan Roy is called the Father of the Indian Renaissance.
Q: When and by whose efforts was sati abolished?
A: Sati was abolished in 1829 by the Governor-General Lord William Bentinck (Regulation XVII). The campaign against sati was led mainly by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, who argued that the practice had no sanction in the scriptures.
Q: What were the main teachings of the Arya Samaj?
A: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875 with the slogan "Back to the Vedas". He rejected idolatry and caste by birth, wrote Satyarth Prakash, started the Shuddhi (reconversion) movement and set up DAV schools and colleges for education.
Q: Who founded the Ramakrishna Mission and what was its aim?
A: Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 with headquarters at Belur Math. Its aim was to combine spiritual teaching with social service, following the message of his guru Ramkrishna Paramhansa that all religions lead to the same goal.
Q: What was the Aligarh Movement?
A: The Aligarh Movement was led by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan for the modern education and social reform of Muslims. He founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in 1875, which became the Aligarh Muslim University in 1920, and published the journal Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq.
Q: Name some important socio-religious reform organisations of the nineteenth century.
A: Important organisations included the Brahmo Samaj (1828), Prarthana Samaj (1867), Arya Samaj (1875), Ramakrishna Mission (1897), Theosophical Society (1875), Aligarh Movement, Deoband Movement (1866), Singh Sabha (1875) and the Rehnumai Mazdayasan Sabha (1851).
Q: ব্ৰাহ্ম সমাজ কোনে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল আৰু ই কিয় গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: ব্ৰাহ্ম সমাজ ৰাজা ৰামমোহন ৰায়ে ১৮২৮ চনত (ব্ৰাহ্ম সভা হিচাপে) প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল। ই মূৰ্তিপূজা, জাতিভেদ আৰু সতীৰ বিৰোধিতা কৰিছিল আৰু যুক্তিবাদী উপাসনা, মহিলাৰ অধিকাৰ আৰু আধুনিক শিক্ষা প্ৰচাৰ কৰিছিল। ৰামমোহন ৰায়ক ভাৰতীয় নৱজাগৰণৰ পিতৃ বুলি কোৱা হয়।
Q: সতী কেতিয়া আৰু কাৰ প্ৰচেষ্টাত বিলুপ্ত হৈছিল?
A: সতী ১৮২৯ চনত গৱৰ্ণৰ-জেনেৰেল লৰ্ড উইলিয়াম বেণ্টিংকে বিলুপ্ত কৰিছিল (ৰেগুলেচন XVII)। সতীৰ বিৰুদ্ধে অভিযান মূলতঃ ৰাজা ৰামমোহন ৰায়ে চলাইছিল, যিয়ে যুক্তি দিছিল যে এই প্ৰথাৰ শাস্ত্ৰত কোনো অনুমোদন নাই।
Q: আৰ্য সমাজৰ মূল শিক্ষা কি আছিল?
A: স্বামী দয়ানন্দ সৰস্বতীয়ে ১৮৭৫ চনত "বেদলৈ উভতি যাওক" স্ল'গানৰ সৈতে আৰ্য সমাজ প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল। তেওঁ মূৰ্তিপূজা আৰু জন্মগত জাতিভেদ নাকচ কৰিছিল, সত্যাৰ্থ প্ৰকাশ লিখিছিল, শুদ্ধি (পুনৰ ধৰ্মান্তৰ) আন্দোলন আৰম্ভ কৰিছিল আৰু শিক্ষাৰ বাবে DAV বিদ্যালয় আৰু মহাবিদ্যালয় স্থাপন কৰিছিল।
Q: ৰামকৃষ্ণ মিছন কোনে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল আৰু ইয়াৰ উদ্দেশ্য কি আছিল?
A: স্বামী বিবেকানন্দই বেলুৰ মঠত মুখ্য কাৰ্যালয়ৰ সৈতে ১৮৯৭ চনত ৰামকৃষ্ণ মিছন প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল। ইয়াৰ উদ্দেশ্য আছিল তেওঁৰ গুৰু ৰামকৃষ্ণ পৰমহংসৰ বাৰ্তা যে সকলো ধৰ্ম একে লক্ষ্যলৈ লৈ যায়, অনুসৰণ কৰি আধ্যাত্মিক শিক্ষাৰ লগতে সমাজসেৱা একত্ৰিত কৰা।
Q: আলিগড় আন্দোলন কি আছিল?
A: আলিগড় আন্দোলন মুছলমানসকলৰ আধুনিক শিক্ষা আৰু সামাজিক সংস্কাৰৰ বাবে ছাৰ ছৈয়দ আহমদ খানে নেতৃত্ব দিছিল। তেওঁ ১৮৭৫ চনত মুহাম্মদান এংলো-ওৰিয়েণ্টেল কলেজ প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল, যি ১৯২০ চনত আলিগড় মুছলিম বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় হৈছিল, আৰু তাহজিব-উল-আখলাক পত্ৰিকা প্ৰকাশ কৰিছিল।
Q: ঊনবিংশ শতিকাৰ কিছুমান গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ সামাজিক-ধৰ্মীয় সংস্কাৰ সংস্থাৰ নাম লিখক।
A: গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ সংস্থাসমূহৰ ভিতৰত ব্ৰাহ্ম সমাজ (১৮২৮), প্ৰাৰ্থনা সমাজ (১৮৬৭), আৰ্য সমাজ (১৮৭৫), ৰামকৃষ্ণ মিছন (১৮৯৭), থিঅ'চফিকেল ছ'চাইটি (১৮৭৫), আলিগড় আন্দোলন, দেওবন্দ আন্দোলন (১৮৬৬), সিং সভা (১৮৭৫) আৰু ৰেহনুমাই মাজদেয়াসন সভা (১৮৫১) অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত।

### Subhas Chandra Bose & Azad Hind Fauj (INA) — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/indian-history/modern-indian-history-sec/subhas-bose-ina/
Summary: Practice subhas chandra bose & azad hind fauj (ina) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: When and where was Subhas Chandra Bose born?
A: On 23 January 1897, in Cuttack, Odisha.
Q: What was the famous slogan of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose?
A: 'Delhi Chalo' (March to Delhi) and 'Jai Hind'.
Q: Who gave the slogan 'Jai Hind'?
A: Subhas Chandra Bose.
Q: What was the book written by Subhas Chandra Bose?
A: 'The Indian Struggle'.
Q: When was the first session of the Congress where Bose was elected as President?
A: In 1938, at the Haripura session.
Q: Who was Subhas Chandra Bose's rival in the 1939 Congress presidential election?
A: Pattabhi Sitaramayya (the Gandhian candidate).
Q: When did Subhas Chandra Bose escape from India?
A: In January 1941, from his house arrest in Calcutta.
Q: Who established the Free India Centre in Berlin?
A: Subhas Chandra Bose, in 1941.
Q: When was the Indian National Army (INA) formed?
A: In 1942, under the leadership of Mohan Singh in Singapore.
Q: Who was the founder of the Indian National Army?
A: Mohan Singh (with the support of Captain Fujiwara of Japan).
Q: Who took over the leadership of the INA from Mohan Singh?
A: Subhas Chandra Bose, in 1943.
Q: When did Subhas Chandra Bose arrive in Singapore?
A: In July 1943, by submarine.
Q: What was the name of the INA regiment of women?
A: The Rani of Jhansi Regiment, led by Lakshmi Swaminathan.
Q: Who was the leader of the Rani of Jhansi Regiment?
A: Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan (Lakshmi Sahgal).
Q: When was the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind Government) formed?
A: On 21 October 1943, in Singapore.
Q: Where was the Azad Hind Government formed?
A: In Singapore.
Q: Who was the head of the Azad Hind Government?
A: Subhas Chandra Bose.
Q: Which country recognized the Azad Hind Government?
A: Japan, Germany, Italy and other Axis powers.
Q: What was the battle cry of the INA?
A: 'Delhi Chalo' (On to Delhi).
Q: Which islands were renamed by Subhas Chandra Bose?
A: Andaman and Nicobar islands were renamed 'Shahid' and 'Swaraj' islands.
Q: Who was the leader of the INA during the battle of Imphal and Kohima?
A: Subhas Chandra Bose led the INA in the invasion of India through Burma.
Q: What was the main aim of the INA?
A: To drive the British out of India with the help of the Axis powers.
Q: What was the strength of the INA under Bose?
A: About 60,000 soldiers, including many Indian prisoners of war.
Q: Where did the INA plant the national flag?
A: At Moirang in Manipur, on 14 April 1944.
Q: What was the INA war memorial called?
A: The 'Amar Jawan Jyoti' of the INA was the INA Martyrs' Memorial in Singapore.
Q: Where did Subhas Chandra Bose reportedly die?
A: In a plane crash at Taihoku (Taipei) on 18 August 1945.
Q: When did the INA trials begin?
A: In November 1945, at the Red Fort in Delhi.
Q: Who were the three officers tried first in the INA trials?
A: Prem Kumar Sehgal, Shah Nawaz Khan and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon.
Q: Who led the defence in the INA trials?
A: Bhulabhai Desai, with Tej Bahadur Sapru and Jawaharlal Nehru.
Q: What was the impact of the INA trials on India?
A: It created nationwide sympathy for the INA and hastened the British decision to leave India.
Q: What was the effect of the INA on the Royal Indian Navy Mutiny?
A: The INA trials inspired the naval ratings to mutiny in February 1946.
Q: What was the Royal Indian Navy Mutiny of 1946?
A: The revolt of naval ratings of the Royal Indian Navy in Bombay in February 1946.
Q: Which two slogans did the RIN mutiny raise?
A: 'Jai Hind' and 'Inquilab Zindabad'.
Q: Who was known as 'Netaji'?
A: Subhas Chandra Bose.
Q: What was the Indian Legion (Azad Hind Legion)?
A: The Indian soldiers recruited in Germany by Bose during World War II.
Q: What was the 'Azad Hind Radio'?
A: A radio station set up by Subhas Chandra Bose to broadcast his message to India.
Q: What did Bose say in his famous speech in Singapore in 1943?
A: He said 'Give me blood and I will give you freedom'.
Q: What was the Rani Jhansi Regiment?
A: The women's regiment of the INA formed in July 1943.
Q: Which fort was the site of the INA trials?
A: The Red Fort in Delhi.
Q: Who was the finance minister of the Azad Hind Government?
A: The prominent members included Subhas Chandra Bose as head and others like S.A. Ayer as publicity officer; the finance portfolio was held by Bose's close associates.
Q: What was the currency issued by the Azad Hind Government?
A: The Azad Hind Government issued its own currency notes.
Q: What was the battle for Imphal and Kohima?
A: The Japanese and INA offensive against the British in Manipur and Nagaland in 1944.
Q: Why did the INA fail in its march to Delhi?
A: Because of the failure of the Japanese supplies, monsoon floods and superior British forces.
Q: What happened to the INA soldiers after the war?
A: Many were captured, tried, and some were released after the INA trials.
Q: What was the contribution of the INA to India's freedom?
A: It exposed the loyalty of the Indian soldiers to the British and strengthened the demand for freedom.
Q: Who was Mohan Singh?
A: An Indian officer who founded the INA in 1942 in Malaya.
Q: What was the Bose's political philosophy called?
A: He advocated a synthesis of socialism and spiritualism, and radical revolution.
Q: When was Subhas Chandra Bose elected President of the Congress for the second time?
A: In 1939, at the Tripuri session, defeating Pattabhi Sitaramayya.
Q: What was the Forward Bloc?
A: A political party founded by Subhas Chandra Bose in 1939 after his resignation from the Congress.
Q: What was Netaji's famous war cry during the Azad Hind movement?
A: 'Chalo Delhi' (Onward to Delhi) and 'Tum mujhe khoon do, main tumhe azaadi dunga'.
Q: Where was Subhas Chandra Bose's father from?
A: His father Janakinath Bose was from Cuttack, Odisha.
Q: What was the name of Subhas Chandra Bose's wife?
A: Emilie Schenkl.
Q: What was Subhas Chandra Bose's daughter's name?
A: Anita Bose Pfaff.
Q: What did Subhas Chandra Bose call himself as the head of the Azad Hind Government?
A: The Head of State and Prime Minister of the Provisional Government of Free India.
Q: Which party did Subhas Chandra Bose form after leaving the Congress?
A: The Forward Bloc, in 1939.
Q: What was the 'Kadam Katar' slogan?
A: It is a phrase meaning 'I have decided to march forward'; it was a revolutionary slogan of the Azad Hind movement.
Q: Who was the commander of the INA at the time of the Moirang flag hoisting?
A: Shah Nawaz Khan's regiment planted the flag at Moirang.
Q: What was the 'Delhi Chalo' movement?
A: The INA's march towards Delhi to liberate India.
Q: Who was the propaganda officer of the Azad Hind Government?
A: S.A. Ayer.
Q: What was the 'Azad Hind Bank'?
A: A bank set up by the Azad Hind Government to manage its funds.
Q: What was the role of Japan in the INA?
A: Japan provided weapons, money and military support to the INA.
Q: Who was the leader of the INA's 'Rani of Jhansi' regiment?
A: Lakshmi Swaminathan (Lakshmi Sahgal).
Q: What was the outcome of the Imphal-Kohima campaign?
A: The INA and Japanese forces were defeated and forced to retreat.
Q: What happened to the INA after the surrender of Japan?
A: The INA was disbanded and many soldiers were captured and tried by the British.
Q: Who were the three INA officers tried in the first Red Fort trial?
A: Prem Kumar Sahgal, Shah Nawaz Khan and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon.
Q: What was the effect of the INA trials on the Indian public?
A: It created a wave of nationalist sentiment and protests across India.
Q: Who defended the INA officers in the Red Fort trial?
A: Bhulabhai Desai, assisted by Jawaharlal Nehru and Tej Bahadur Sapru.
Q: What was the impact of the INA on the British decision to leave India?
A: The INA trials and the naval mutiny convinced the British that they could no longer rely on Indian soldiers.
Q: What was the 'Azad Hind Radio' slogan?
A: 'Azad Hind' broadcast the message of freedom struggle to the Indian masses.
Q: What is the significance of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose in Indian history?
A: He was a great freedom fighter who built the INA and symbolised armed resistance to British rule.
Q: When and where was Subhas Chandra Bose born?
A: Subhas Chandra Bose was born on 23 January 1897 at Cuttack in Orissa (now Odisha). His father was Janakinath Bose, a lawyer, and his mother was Prabhavati Devi.
Q: Why did Bose resign from the ICS?
A: Bose passed the Indian Civil Service examination in 1920, but he did not wish to serve the British government. He resigned from the ICS in 1921 and returned to India to join the freedom struggle.
Q: What was the Forward Bloc?
A: The Forward Bloc was a political party formed by Subhas Chandra Bose in 1939, after he resigned from the Congress presidency, to unite the radical nationalists and carry on the struggle for complete freedom.
Q: Who founded the first INA and when did Bose take it over?
A: The first Indian National Army was founded by Mohan Singh in 1942 among Indian prisoners of war in Malaya and Singapore. Subhas Chandra Bose arrived in Singapore in July 1943 and took over the leadership of the INA.
Q: What was the Rani of Jhansi Regiment?
A: The Rani of Jhansi Regiment was the women's regiment of the Azad Hind Fauj, led by Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan (Lakshmi Sahgal). It was one of the few all-women combat units raised during the freedom struggle.
Q: What was the impact of the INA trials and the Royal Indian Navy Mutiny?
A: The Red Fort trials of INA officers in 1945-46 created huge public sympathy and turned the accused into national heroes. The Royal Indian Navy Mutiny of February 1946 showed that the British could no longer rely on Indian soldiers, and together these events contributed to Britain's decision to leave India.
Q: সুভাষ চন্দ্ৰ বসুৰ জন্ম কেতিয়া আৰু ক'ত হৈছিল?
A: সুভাষ চন্দ্ৰ বসুৰ জন্ম ১৮৯৭ চনৰ ২৩ জানুৱাৰীত উৰিষ্যাৰ (বৰ্তমান ওড়িশা) কটকত হৈছিল। তেওঁৰ পিতৃ আছিল জনকীনাথ বসু, এজন উকীল, আৰু মাতৃ আছিল প্ৰভাৱতী দেৱী।
Q: বসুৱে ICS ৰ পৰা কিয় পদত্যাগ কৰিছিল?
A: বসুৱে ১৯২০ চনত ভাৰতীয় অসামৰিক সেৱাৰ পৰীক্ষাত উত্তীৰ্ণ হৈছিল, কিন্তু তেওঁ ব্ৰিটিছ চৰকাৰৰ অধীনত সেৱা কৰিবলৈ বিচৰা নাছিল। তেওঁ ১৯২১ চনত ICS ৰ পৰা পদত্যাগ কৰি স্বাধীনতা সংগ্ৰামত যোগদান কৰিবলৈ ভাৰতলৈ ঘূৰি আহিছিল।
Q: ফৰৱাৰ্ড ব্লক কি আছিল?
A: ফৰৱাৰ্ড ব্লক হৈছে ১৯৩৯ চনত সুভাষ চন্দ্ৰ বসুৱে কংগ্ৰেছৰ সভাপতিত্বৰ পৰা পদত্যাগ কৰাৰ পিছত গঠন কৰা এটা ৰাজনৈতিক দল, যি ৰাডিকেল জাতীয়তাবাদীসকলক একত্ৰিত কৰি সম্পূৰ্ণ স্বাধীনতাৰ সংগ্ৰাম অব্যাহত ৰাখিছিল।
Q: প্ৰথম INA কোনে প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল আৰু বসুৱে কেতিয়া ইয়াৰ নেতৃত্ব লৈছিল?
A: প্ৰথম ভাৰতীয় জাতীয় সেনা ১৯৪২ চনত মোহন সিঙে মালয়া আৰু চিংগাপুৰত ভাৰতীয় যুদ্ধবন্দীসকলৰ মাজত প্ৰতিষ্ঠা কৰিছিল। সুভাষ চন্দ্ৰ বসু ১৯৪৩ চনৰ জুলাইত চিংগাপুৰত উপস্থিত হৈ INA ৰ নেতৃত্ব গ্ৰহণ কৰিছিল।
Q: ৰাণী ঝাঁসী ৰেজিমেণ্ট কি আছিল?
A: ৰাণী ঝাঁসী ৰেজিমেণ্ট আছিল আজাদ হিন্দ ফৌজৰ মহিলা ৰেজিমেণ্ট, যাৰ নেতৃত্বত আছিল কেপ্তেইন লক্ষ্মী স্বামীনাথন (লক্ষ্মী চাহগাল)। স্বাধীনতা সংগ্ৰামৰ সময়ত গঠিত অতি কম সংখ্যক মহিলা যুঁজাৰু বাহিনীৰ ভিতৰত ই অন্যতম।
Q: INA ৰ বিচাৰ আৰু ৰয়েল ইণ্ডিয়ান নেভি বিদ্ৰোহৰ প্ৰভাৱ কি আছিল?
A: ১৯৪৫-৪৬ চনত লাল কিল্লাত INA বিষয়াসকলৰ বিচাৰে বিপুল জনসমৰ্থন সৃষ্টি কৰিছিল আৰু অভিযুক্তসকলক জাতীয় বীৰ কৰি তুলিছিল। ১৯৪৬ চনৰ ফেব্ৰুৱাৰীত ৰয়েল ইণ্ডিয়ান নেভিৰ বিদ্ৰোহে দেখুৱাইছিল যে ব্ৰিটিছে ভাৰতীয় সৈন্যসকলৰ ওপৰত আৰু নিৰ্ভৰ কৰিব নোৱাৰে, আৰু এই দুয়ো ঘটনাই ভাৰত এৰাৰ ব্ৰিটিছ সিদ্ধান্তত অৰিহণা যোগাইছিল।

### Article 371B & Assam Accord — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/polity/assam-local-admin-sec/article-371b-assam-accord/
Summary: Practice article 371b & assam accord questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution contains special provisions for Assam?
A: Article 371B.
Q: What does Article 371B of the Constitution provide for?
A: It provides for the constitution and functions of a committee of the Assam Legislative Assembly consisting of members elected from the tribal areas of the state.
Q: Who is empowered to make provisions under Article 371B for Assam?
A: The President of India.
Q: The committee under Article 371B consists of members elected from which areas of Assam?
A: The tribal areas of the state (the Sixth Schedule areas).
Q: What is the main purpose of Article 371B?
A: To protect the interests of the tribal areas within the Assam legislature.
Q: Which state's special provision is contained in Article 371A?
A: Nagaland.
Q: Which Article contains the special provision for Sikkim?
A: Article 371F.
Q: When was the Assam Accord signed?
A: On 15 August 1985.
Q: Where was the Assam Accord signed?
A: At Raj Bhavan, Guwahati.
Q: Between which parties was the Assam Accord signed?
A: Between the Government of India and the leaders of the Assam Agitation (AASU and AAGSP).
Q: Who represented the Government of India when the Assam Accord was signed?
A: Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi.
Q: Which organisations led the Assam Agitation?
A: The All Assam Students' Union (AASU) and the All Assam Gana Sangram Parishad (AAGSP).
Q: When was the Assam Agitation launched and how long did it last?
A: It was launched in 1979 and lasted until 1985 (1979-1985).
Q: Against what was the Assam Agitation launched?
A: Against illegal foreign (Bangladeshi) immigration into Assam.
Q: What is the cut-off date for the detection and deportation of foreigners under the Assam Accord?
A: 25 March 1971.
Q: Under the Accord, what was the status of those who entered India before 1966?
A: They were to be regularized.
Q: Under the Accord, what was to happen to those who entered India between 1966 and 25 March 1971?
A: Their names were to be deleted from the electoral rolls for 10 years and then restored.
Q: Under the Accord, what was to happen to those who entered India after 25 March 1971?
A: They were to be detected and deported.
Q: Which clause of the Assam Accord promises constitutional, legislative and administrative safeguards to protect the culture, language and identity of the Assamese people?
A: Clause 6.
Q: Which party came to power in Assam after the post-Accord elections?
A: The Asom Gana Parishad (AGP).
Q: When were the post-Accord elections held and who became Chief Minister?
A: In December 1985; Prafulla Kumar Mahanta.
Q: Who founded the Asom Gana Parishad (AGP)?
A: The leaders of the Assam Agitation (AASU).
Q: Under whose supervision was the National Register of Citizens (NRC) for Assam updated?
A: Under the supervision of the Supreme Court of India.
Q: When was the final NRC for Assam published?
A: In 2019.
Q: Was the Assam Accord signed during the Prime Ministership of Indira Gandhi?
A: No; it was signed on 15 August 1985 under Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi.

A: Article 371B & Assam Accord (Bilingual English & Assamese) is completely free. You can read all 25 questions and their explanations on axomexam.in with no registration or charge, which makes it easy to revise the same set more than once.
Q: Are the Article 371B & Assam Accord (Bilingual English & Assamese) questions available in Assamese and English?
A: Yes. Article 371B & Assam Accord (Bilingual English & Assamese) is bilingual: the question, every option and the full explanation are given in both Assamese and English, so you can read the problem in one language and the solution in the other.
Q: How many questions does Article 371B & Assam Accord (Bilingual English & Assamese) include?
A: Article 371B & Assam Accord (Bilingual English & Assamese) currently contains 25 practice questions, each with a worked explanation. New questions are added as the syllabus and exam patterns are updated, so the set is worth revisiting.
Q: When was the Assam Accord signed and between whom?
A: The Assam Accord was signed on 15 August 1985 at New Delhi between the All Assam Students' Union (AASU) and the All Assam Gana Sangram Parishad (AAGSP) on one side and the Government of India and the Government of Assam on the other. It ended the Assam Movement and laid down a settlement on the foreigners issue, economic development, cultural safeguards and constitutional measures.
Q: What is the cut-off date fixed by the Assam Accord?
A: The Assam Accord fixed 25 March 1971 as the cut-off date for the detection and deportation of foreigners in Assam. Persons who entered before that date were to be dealt with according to the terms of the Accord, while those who entered on or after that date were to be detected and deported. The 1966 electoral roll was accepted as the base for identifying earlier entrants.
Q: What does Article 371B provide for Assam?
A: Article 371B, inserted in 1969, empowers the President to provide by order for the constitution and functions of a committee of the Assam Legislative Assembly consisting of members elected from the tribal areas of Assam. The committee gives the tribal areas a special voice and does not create a separate legislature or autonomous state.
Q: How has the Assam Accord been implemented?
A: Implementation has taken place through several measures: the Illegal Migrants (Determination by Tribunals) Act of 1983, which was struck down by the Supreme Court in 2005; the use of the Foreigners Act, 1946; the update of the National Register of Citizens under Supreme Court supervision; and constitutional and administrative steps such as Article 371B and the Bodo Accord of 2020 that created the Bodoland Territorial Region.
Q: Why is the Assam Accord important for exams?
A: The Assam Accord is important because it links modern Assamese history with constitutional provisions and citizenship law. ADRE, APSC and Assam Police papers frequently ask its date, its signatories, the cut-off date of 25 March 1971 and its implementation through the NRC and the autonomous councils. It is therefore a high-value topic for both general studies and Assam-specific papers.
Q: অসম চুক্তি কেতিয়া আৰু কাৰ মাজত স্বাক্ষৰিত হৈছিল?
A: অসম চুক্তি ১৯৮৫ চনৰ ১৫ আগষ্টত নতুন দিল্লীত সৰ্ব অসম ছাত্ৰ সন্থা (AASU) আৰু সৰ্ব অসম গণ সংগ্ৰাম পৰিষদ (AAGSP)ৰ এফালে আৰু ভাৰত চৰকাৰ তথা অসম চৰকাৰৰ আনফালে স্বাক্ষৰিত হৈছিল। ই অসম আন্দোলনৰ অন্ত পেলাইছিল আৰু বিদেশী প্ৰশ্ন, অৰ্থনৈতিক বিকাশ, সাংস্কৃতিক সুৰক্ষা আৰু সাংবিধানিক ব্যৱস্থাৰ ওপৰত এক নিষ্পত্তি নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰিছিল।
Q: অসম চুক্তিয়ে নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰা শেষ তাৰিখ কি?
A: অসম চুক্তিয়ে অসমত বিদেশী চিনাক্ত আৰু বহিষ্কাৰৰ বাবে ২৫ মাৰ্চ ১৯৭১ক শেষ তাৰিখ হিচাপে নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰিছিল। সেই তাৰিখৰ আগতে প্ৰৱেশ কৰা ব্যক্তিসকলক চুক্তিৰ চৰ্ত অনুসৰি ব্যৱহাৰ কৰিব লাগিছিল, আনহাতে সেই তাৰিখ বা তাত পিছত প্ৰৱেশ কৰাসকলক চিনাক্ত কৰি বহিষ্কাৰ কৰিব লাগিছিল। পূৰ্বৰ প্ৰৱেশকাৰী চিনাক্তৰ বাবে ১৯৬৬ চনৰ নিৰ্বাচনী তালিকা ভিত্তি হিচাপে গ্ৰহণ কৰা হৈছিল।
Q: অনুচ্ছেদ ৩৭১B-য়ে অসমৰ বাবে কি বিধান দিয়ে?
A: ১৯৬৯ চনত সন্নিৱিষ্ট অনুচ্ছেদ ৩৭১B-য়ে ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতিক আদেশৰ জৰিয়তে অসমৰ জনজাতীয় অঞ্চলসমূহৰ পৰা নিৰ্বাচিত সদস্যসকলৰ সমন্বয়ে গঠিত অসম বিধানসভাৰ এটা সমিতিৰ গঠন আৰু কাৰ্য্যৰ ব্যৱস্থা কৰাৰ ক্ষমতা দিয়ে। সমিতিখনে জনজাতীয় অঞ্চলসমূহক বিশেষ কণ্ঠস্বৰ দিয়ে আৰু পৃথক আইনসভা বা স্বায়ত্ত ৰাজ্য সৃষ্টি নকৰে।
Q: অসম চুক্তি কেনেকৈ ৰূপায়ণ কৰা হৈছে?
A: ৰূপায়ণ কেইবাটাও ব্যৱস্থাৰ জৰিয়তে হৈছে: ১৯৮৩ চনৰ অবৈধ অনুপ্ৰৱেশকাৰী (ট্ৰাইবিউনেলৰ দ্বাৰা নিৰ্ধাৰণ) আইন, যি উচ্চতম ন্যায়ালয়ে ২০০৫ চনত বাতিল কৰিছিল; ১৯৪৬ চনৰ বিদেশী আইনৰ ব্যৱহাৰ; উচ্চতম ন্যায়ালয়ৰ অধীক্ষণত ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় নাগৰিক পঞ্জীৰ অধিকালন; আৰু অনুচ্ছেদ ৩৭১B তথা ২০২০ চনৰ বড়ো চুক্তিৰ দৰে সাংবিধানিক আৰু প্ৰশাসনিক পদক্ষেপ, যিয়ে বড়োলেণ্ড টেৰিটৰিয়েল ৰিজিয়ন সৃষ্টি কৰিছিল।
Q: পৰীক্ষাৰ বাবে অসম চুক্তি কিয় গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: অসম চুক্তি গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ কাৰণ ই আধুনিক অসমীয়া ইতিহাসক সাংবিধানিক বিধান আৰু নাগৰিকত্ব আইনৰ সৈতে সংযোগ কৰে। ADRE, APSC আৰু অসম আৰক্ষীৰ প্ৰশ্নপত্ৰই ইয়াৰ তাৰিখ, স্বাক্ষৰকাৰী, ২৫ মাৰ্চ ১৯৭১ৰ শেষ তাৰিখ আৰু NRC তথা স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদৰ জৰিয়তে ইয়াৰ ৰূপায়ণ সোধে। সেয়ে ই সাধাৰণ অধ্যয়ন আৰু অসম-নিৰ্দিষ্ট প্ৰশ্নপত্ৰ দুয়োটাৰ বাবে উচ্চ মূল্যৰ বিষয়।

### Panchayati Raj & Municipalities — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/polity/assam-local-admin-sec/panchayati-raj-municipalities/
Summary: Practice panchayati raj & municipalities questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Which constitutional amendment act gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions?
A: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 (Part IX, Articles 243 to 243O).
Q: On which date did the 73rd Constitutional Amendment come into force, and which day is celebrated as National Panchayati Raj Day?
A: On 24 April 1993.
Q: Which committee recommended the three-tier Panchayati Raj system in 1957?
A: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee.
Q: In which state and district was Panchayati Raj first introduced on 2 October 1959?
A: In Rajasthan, at Nagaur.
Q: Which committee recommended a two-tier Panchayati Raj system in 1977?
A: The Ashok Mehta Committee.
Q: What is a Gram Sabha?
A: It is the assembly of all voters of a village.
Q: What is the fixed term of a Panchayat?
A: Five years.
Q: Who conducts elections to the Panchayats?
A: The State Election Commission.
Q: What is the minimum proportion of seats reserved for women in Panchayats?
A: At least one-third of the seats.
Q: How many subjects are listed in the 11th Schedule for Panchayats?
A: 29 subjects.
Q: Which Act of 1996 extended Panchayati Raj to the Scheduled Areas?
A: The PESA Act (Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act), 1996.
Q: Which Act provides for the three-tier Panchayati Raj system in Assam?
A: The Assam Panchayat Act, 1994.
Q: What are the three tiers of Panchayati Raj in Assam?
A: Gaon Panchayat (village), Anchalik Panchayat (block) and Zila Parishad (district).
Q: Which constitutional amendment act gave constitutional status to urban local bodies?
A: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 (Part IXA, Articles 243P to 243ZG).
Q: What are the three types of urban local bodies under the 74th Amendment?
A: Nagar Panchayat (transitional area), Municipal Council (smaller urban area) and Municipal Corporation (larger urban area).
Q: Which type of urban local body is established for a transitional area?
A: Nagar Panchayat.
Q: How many subjects are listed in the 12th Schedule for municipalities?
A: 18 subjects.
Q: Which committees are provided in municipalities for each ward?
A: Wards Committees.
Q: Which is the only Municipal Corporation of Assam, constituted in 1971?
A: The Guwahati Municipal Corporation (GMC).
Q: The Guwahati Municipal Corporation is the municipal body of which city?
A: Guwahati, the capital city of Assam.
Q: Under which Part of the Constitution are the Panchayati Raj provisions (Articles 243 to 243O) found?
A: Part IX.
Q: Under which Part of the Constitution are the municipal provisions (Articles 243P to 243ZG) found?
A: Part IXA.
Q: Which amendment is related to urban local bodies (municipalities) and not to Panchayati Raj?
A: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.
Q: Which tier of Panchayati Raj in Assam is at the block (intermediate) level?
A: Anchalik Panchayat.
Q: What is the fixed term of a municipality under the 74th Amendment?
A: Five years.

Q: Are the Panchayati Raj & Municipalities (Bilingual English & Assamese) questions available in Assamese and English?
A: Every item in Panchayati Raj & Municipalities (Bilingual English & Assamese) appears in Assamese and English. That covers all 25 questions, including the options and explanations, so the same idea is reinforced in whichever language you find easier.
Q: How many questions does Panchayati Raj & Municipalities (Bilingual English & Assamese) include?
A: Panchayati Raj & Municipalities (Bilingual English & Assamese) currently contains 25 practice questions, each with a worked explanation. New questions are added as the syllabus and exam patterns are updated, so the set is worth revisiting.
Q: Which amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions?
A: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions. It inserted Part IX (Articles 243 to 243O) and added the Eleventh Schedule with 29 subjects. It came into force on 24 April 1993, which is observed as National Panchayati Raj Day.
Q: What is the difference between the 73rd and 74th Amendments?
A: The 73rd Amendment deals with rural local self-government, that is panchayats, through Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule. The 74th Amendment deals with urban local self-government, that is municipalities, through Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule. The 73rd came into force on 24 April 1993 and the 74th on 1 June 1993.
Q: What is a Gram Sabha under the Constitution?
A: A Gram Sabha is defined under Article 243A as the body consisting of all persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village comprised within the area of a panchayat at the village level. It is the foundation of the panchayat system and exercises the powers and functions provided by the state legislature.
Q: What is the structure of Panchayati Raj in Assam?
A: Assam follows a three-tier structure under the Assam Panchayat Act, 1994: the Gaon Panchayat at the village level, the Anchalik Panchayat at the block level and the Zilla Parishad at the district level. The Assam State Election Commission conducts elections to these bodies. Urban areas have Municipal Corporations, Municipal Boards and Town Committees.
Q: Do the panchayat provisions apply to the Sixth Schedule areas of Assam?
A: No. The panchayat provisions of the 73rd Amendment generally do not apply to the Sixth Schedule areas, which are the Bodoland Territorial Region, the Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council and the Dima Hasao Autonomous District Council. These areas are administered through autonomous councils under the Sixth Schedule, not through the ordinary panchayat system.
Q: কোন সংশোধনীয়ে পঞ্চায়তী ৰাজ অনুষ্ঠানসমূহক সাংবিধানিক মৰ্যাদা দিছিল?
A: ১৯৯২ চনৰ ৭৩ সংখ্যক সাংবিধানিক সংশোধনী আইনে পঞ্চায়তী ৰাজ অনুষ্ঠানসমূহক সাংবিধানিক মৰ্যাদা দিছিল। ই নৱম ভাগ (অনুচ্ছেদ ২৪৩ৰ পৰা ২৪৩O) সন্নিৱিষ্ট কৰিছিল আৰু ২৯টা বিষয়সহ একাদশ অনুসূচী যোগ কৰিছিল। ই ১৯৯৩ চনৰ ২৪ এপ্ৰিলত বলৱৎ হয়, যি দিন ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় পঞ্চায়তী ৰাজ দিৱস হিচাপে পালন কৰা হয়।
Q: ৭৩ সংখ্যক আৰু ৭৪ সংখ্যক সংশোধনীৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: ৭৩ সংখ্যক সংশোধনী গ্ৰাম্য স্থানীয় স্ব-শাসন, অৰ্থাৎ পঞ্চায়তৰ সৈতে, নৱম ভাগ আৰু একাদশ অনুসূচীৰ জৰিয়তে জড়িত। ৭৪ সংখ্যক সংশোধনী চহৰীয়া স্থানীয় স্ব-শাসন, অৰ্থাৎ পৌৰসভাৰ সৈতে, নৱম-ক ভাগ আৰু দ্বাদশ অনুসূচীৰ জৰিয়তে জড়িত। ৭৩ সংখ্যক ১৯৯৩ চনৰ ২৪ এপ্ৰিলত আৰু ৭৪ সংখ্যক ১৯৯৩ চনৰ ১ জুনত বলৱৎ হয়।
Q: সংবিধান অনুসৰি গাঁও সভা কি?
A: গাঁও সভাক অনুচ্ছেদ ২৪৩Aৰ অধীনত গাঁও স্তৰৰ পঞ্চায়তৰ এলেকাৰ ভিতৰত থকা এখন গাঁৱৰ সৈতে সম্পৰ্কিত নিৰ্বাচনী তালিকাত পঞ্জীয়নভুক্ত সকলো ব্যক্তিৰ সমন্বয়ে গঠিত শৰীৰ হিচাপে সংজ্ঞায়িত কৰা হৈছে। ই পঞ্চায়ত ব্যৱস্থাৰ ভেটি আৰু ৰাজ্যিক বিধানসভাই প্ৰদান কৰা ক্ষমতা তথা কাৰ্য্য পালন কৰে।
Q: অসমত পঞ্চায়তী ৰাজৰ গঠন কি?
A: অসমে ১৯৯৪ চনৰ অসম পঞ্চায়ত আইনৰ অধীনত তিনিস্তৰীয় গঠন অনুসৰণ কৰে: গাঁও স্তৰত গাঁও পঞ্চায়ত, খণ্ড স্তৰত আঞ্চলিক পঞ্চায়ত আৰু জিলা স্তৰত জিলা পৰিষদ। অসম ৰাজ্যিক নিৰ্বাচন আয়োগে এই অনুষ্ঠানসমূহৰ নিৰ্বাচন অনুষ্ঠিত কৰে। চহৰীয়া অঞ্চলত পৌৰ নিগম, পৌৰ পৰিষদ আৰু নগৰ সমিতি আছে।
Q: পঞ্চায়ত বিধানসমূহ অসমৰ ষষ্ঠ অনুসূচীৰ অঞ্চলসমূহত প্ৰযোজ্য নেকি?
A: নহয়। ৭৩ সংখ্যক সংশোধনীৰ পঞ্চায়ত বিধানসমূহ সাধাৰণতে ষষ্ঠ অনুসূচীৰ অঞ্চলসমূহত প্ৰযোজ্য নহয়, যিবোৰ হ'ল বড়োলেণ্ড টেৰিটৰিয়েল ৰিজিয়ন, কাৰ্বি আংলং স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদ আৰু ডিমা হাছাও স্বায়ত্তশাসিত জিলা পৰিষদ। এই অঞ্চলসমূহ সাধাৰণ পঞ্চায়ত ব্যৱস্থাৰ পৰিৱৰ্তে ষষ্ঠ অনুসূচীৰ অধীনত স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদৰ জৰিয়তে পৰিচালিত হয়।

### Sixth Schedule & Autonomous Councils — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/polity/assam-local-admin-sec/sixth-schedule-autonomous-councils/
Summary: Practice sixth schedule & autonomous councils questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What is the Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
A: It provides for the administration of certain tribal areas.
Q: Which Articles of the Constitution relate to the Sixth Schedule?
A: Articles 244(2) and 275(1).
Q: In how many states does the Sixth Schedule apply?
A: Four states.
Q: Name the four states to which the Sixth Schedule applies.
A: Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
Q: What is the purpose of the Sixth Schedule?
A: To protect the interests of tribal people through the ADCs and ARCs.
Q: What do ADC and ARC stand for?
A: Autonomous District Council and Autonomous Regional Council.
Q: Which three types of powers do the ADCs possess?
A: Legislative, executive and judicial powers.
Q: Name any four subjects under the jurisdiction of the ADCs.
A: Land, forests, shifting cultivation and marriage (also village administration, inheritance and appointment of village chiefs).
Q: Do ADCs have jurisdiction over reserved forests?
A: No, reserved forests are excluded from their jurisdiction.
Q: Which three areas of Assam are covered under the Sixth Schedule?
A: Karbi Anglong, Dima Hasao and the Bodoland Territorial Area Districts (BTAD).
Q: Name the three autonomous councils of Assam under the Sixth Schedule.
A: Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council (KAAC), Dima Hasao Autonomous Council (DHAC) and Bodoland Territorial Council (BTC).
Q: What is the full form of KAAC?
A: Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council.
Q: What is the full form of DHAC?
A: Dima Hasao Autonomous Council.
Q: What was Dima Hasao district earlier known as?
A: North Cachar Hills district.
Q: In which year was the Bodoland Territorial Council established?
A: 2003.
Q: Under which Accord was the Bodoland Territorial Council created?
A: The Bodo Accord of 2003.
Q: Which organisation led the Bodoland movement?
A: The All Bodo Students' Union (ABSU).
Q: Who was the prominent leader of the Bodoland movement?
A: Upendra Nath Brahma.
Q: Under which legislation are councils like Deori, Mising and Tiwa constituted?
A: State (Assam) legislation, not the Sixth Schedule.
Q: Is the Rabha Hasong Autonomous Council under the Sixth Schedule?
A: No, it is constituted under an Assam state act.
Q: The Sixth Schedule does NOT apply to which of these states: Nagaland, Assam or Mizoram?
A: Nagaland.
Q: What is the full form of BTAD?
A: Bodoland Territorial Area Districts.
Q: What do the Sixth Schedule councils protect for the Scheduled Tribes?
A: Their interests and culture.
Q: Which is the most recently established among the three Sixth Schedule councils of Assam?
A: The Bodoland Territorial Council (BTC), established in 2003.
Q: Which body administers the tribal areas under the Sixth Schedule?
A: The Autonomous District Councils (ADCs).
Q: Is Sixth Schedule & Autonomous Councils in Assam (Bilingual English & Assamese) free to use on axomexam?
A: There is no payment involved in Sixth Schedule & Autonomous Councils in Assam (Bilingual English & Assamese). The complete set of 25 questions and its step-by-step explanations are open to every visitor, so you can practise without creating an account or paying a fee.
Q: Are the Sixth Schedule & Autonomous Councils in Assam (Bilingual English & Assamese) questions available in Assamese and English?
A: Yes — the content is fully bilingual. You can switch between Assamese and English at any point while working through Sixth Schedule & Autonomous Councils in Assam (Bilingual English & Assamese), which helps when a term is clearer in one language than the other.
Q: How many questions does Sixth Schedule & Autonomous Councils in Assam (Bilingual English & Assamese) include?
A: The Sixth Schedule & Autonomous Councils in Assam (Bilingual English & Assamese) set is expanded over time, so the number of questions keeps growing. At the moment you can work through about 25 questions here with full answers.
Q: What is the Sixth Schedule and which articles contain it?
A: The Sixth Schedule provides for the administration of certain tribal areas through Autonomous District Councils and Regional Councils. It is contained in Article 244(2) and Article 275(1) of the Constitution and applies to the tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
Q: How many Sixth Schedule areas are there in Assam and what are they?
A: Assam has three Sixth Schedule areas: the Bodoland Territorial Region with its headquarters at Kokrajhar, the Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council at Diphu, and the Dima Hasao Autonomous District Council at Haflong. Together these cover the hill districts and the Bodo region of the state.
Q: What is the composition and term of an Autonomous District Council?
A: An Autonomous District Council can have a maximum of 30 members, of whom 26 are elected on the basis of adult franchise and up to 4 are nominated by the Governor. The term of the council is five years, and the Governor has special responsibilities for the administration of Sixth Schedule areas.
Q: How did the Bodoland Autonomous Council become the Bodoland Territorial Region?
A: The Bodoland Autonomous Council was created by the Bodo Accord of 1993. The Bodo Accord of 2003 replaced it with the Bodoland Territorial Council under the Sixth Schedule, and the Bodo Accord of 2020 renamed it the Bodoland Territorial Region and expanded its territory, powers and development package. Its headquarters is Kokrajhar.
Q: Are all autonomous councils in Assam under the Sixth Schedule?
A: No. Only the Bodoland Territorial Region, the Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council and the Dima Hasao Autonomous District Council are under the Sixth Schedule. Councils such as the Deori, Mising, Rabha Hasong, Tiwa, Sonowal Kachari, Thengal Kachari, Moran, Motok, Chutia and Koch-Rajbongshi councils are created under state laws and have more limited powers.
Q: ষষ্ঠ অনুসূচী কি আৰু কোন অনুচ্ছেদত আছে?
A: ষষ্ঠ অনুসূচীয়ে স্বায়ত্তশাসিত জিলা পৰিষদ আৰু আঞ্চলিক পৰিষদৰ জৰিয়তে কিছুমান জনজাতীয় অঞ্চল পৰিচালনাৰ ব্যৱস্থা কৰে। ই সংবিধানৰ অনুচ্ছেদ ২৪৪(২) আৰু অনুচ্ছেদ ২৭৫(১)ত আছে আৰু অসম, মেঘালয়, ত্ৰিপুৰা তথা মিজোৰামৰ জনজাতীয় অঞ্চলসমূহত প্ৰযোজ্য।
Q: অসমত কিমানখন ষষ্ঠ অনুসূচী অঞ্চল আছে আৰু সেইবোৰ কি কি?
A: অসমত তিনি খন ষষ্ঠ অনুসূচী অঞ্চল আছে: কোকৰাঝাৰ মুখ্য কাৰ্যালয়ৰ সৈতে বড়োলেণ্ড টেৰিটৰিয়েল ৰিজিয়ন, ডিফুত কাৰ্বি আংলং স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদ, আৰু হাফলঙত ডিমা হাছাও স্বায়ত্তশাসিত জিলা পৰিষদ। এইবোৰে ৰাজ্যৰ পাহাৰীয়া জিলা আৰু বড়ো অঞ্চল সামৰি লয়।
Q: স্বায়ত্তশাসিত জিলা পৰিষদৰ গঠন আৰু কাৰ্যকাল কি?
A: এখন স্বায়ত্তশাসিত জিলা পৰিষদত সৰ্বাধিক ৩০ জন সদস্য থাকিব পাৰে, যাৰ ২৬ জন প্ৰাপ্তবয়স্ক ভোটাধিকাৰৰ ভিত্তিত নিৰ্বাচিত আৰু সৰ্বাধিক ৪ জন ৰাজ্যপালে মনোনীত কৰে। পৰিষদৰ কাৰ্যকাল পাঁচ বছৰ, আৰু ষষ্ঠ অনুসূচীৰ অঞ্চলসমূহৰ প্ৰশাসনত ৰাজ্যপালৰ বিশেষ দায়িত্ব থাকে।
Q: বড়োলেণ্ড স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদ কেনেকৈ বড়োলেণ্ড টেৰিটৰিয়েল ৰিজিয়ন হ'ল?
A: ১৯৯৩ চনৰ বড়ো চুক্তিৰ জৰিয়তে বড়োলেণ্ড স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদ গঠিত হৈছিল। ২০০৩ চনৰ বড়ো চুক্তিয়ে ইয়াৰ ঠাইত ষষ্ঠ অনুসূচীৰ অধীনত বড়োলেণ্ড টেৰিটৰিয়েল কাউন্সিল গঠন কৰিছিল, আৰু ২০২০ চনৰ বড়ো চুক্তিয়ে ইয়াৰ নাম বড়োলেণ্ড টেৰিটৰিয়েল ৰিজিয়ন ৰাখি অঞ্চল, ক্ষমতা আৰু উন্নয়ন পেকেজ সম্প্ৰসাৰণ কৰিছিল। ইয়াৰ মুখ্য কাৰ্যালয় কোকৰাঝাৰ।
Q: অসমৰ সকলো স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদ ষষ্ঠ অনুসূচীৰ অধীনত নেকি?
A: নহয়। কেৱল বড়োলেণ্ড টেৰিটৰিয়েল ৰিজিয়ন, কাৰ্বি আংলং স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদ আৰু ডিমা হাছাও স্বায়ত্তশাসিত জিলা পৰিষদ ষষ্ঠ অনুসূচীৰ অধীনত। ডেউৰী, মিচিং, ৰাভা হাচং, তিওয়া, চোনোৱাল কছাৰী, থেংগাল কছাৰী, মৰাণ, মটক, চুটীয়া আৰু কোচ-ৰাজবংশীৰ দৰে পৰিষদসমূহ ৰাজ্যিক আইনৰ অধীনত গঠিত আৰু অধিক সীমিত ক্ষমতাৰ।

### State Administrative & Border Setup — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/polity/assam-local-admin-sec/state-administrative-border-setup/
Summary: Practice state administrative & border setup questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: What is the capital of Assam?
A: Dispur (a locality of Guwahati).
Q: In which year was the capital of Assam shifted from Shillong to Dispur?
A: 1972.
Q: How many administrative divisions does Assam have?
A: Five.
Q: Name the five administrative divisions of Assam.
A: Lower Assam, North Assam, Central Assam, Upper Assam, and Hills & Barak Valley.
Q: How many districts does Assam have after the recent administrative reorganization?
A: 35 districts.
Q: Districts of Assam are further divided into which administrative units?
A: Subdivisions, revenue circles, blocks and gaon panchayats.
Q: Who is the executive head of the state of Assam?
A: The Governor.
Q: Who is the real executive head of the state of Assam?
A: The Chief Minister.
Q: Who is the administrative head of the state government of Assam?
A: The Chief Secretary.
Q: Which country shares an international border with Assam to the north?
A: Bhutan.
Q: Which country shares an international border with Assam to the west/south-west?
A: Bangladesh.
Q: Which Indian state shares a border with Assam to the north-east?
A: Arunachal Pradesh.
Q: Which Indian state shares a border with Assam to the east?
A: Nagaland.
Q: Which Indian state shares a border with Assam to the south-east?
A: Manipur.
Q: Which Indian state shares a border with Assam to the south?
A: Mizoram.
Q: Which Indian state shares a border with Assam to the south-west?
A: Meghalaya.
Q: Which Indian state shares a border with Assam to the west?
A: West Bengal.
Q: How many Indian states share a border with Assam?
A: Six Indian states - Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Meghalaya and West Bengal.
Q: Which river flows through the middle of Assam dividing the valley?
A: The Brahmaputra.
Q: With which states does Assam have long-standing border disputes?
A: Nagaland, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram.
Q: How many areas of disagreement are there in the Assam-Meghalaya border dispute, and how many were settled through the 2022 Memorandum of Understanding?
A: 12 areas of disagreement; 6 areas were settled through the 2022 Memorandum of Understanding.
Q: Which 2021 incident is associated with the Assam-Mizoram border dispute?
A: The Lailapur incident.
Q: Which areas are associated with the Assam-Nagaland border dispute?
A: Several areas such as Merapani, as well as the Rengma reserved forest areas.
Q: What is the largest city of Assam?
A: Guwahati.
Q: Does Assam have a bicameral or unicameral legislature?
A: Bicameral - it has a Legislative Assembly and a Legislative Council.
