A: State Administrative & Border Setup of Assam (Bilingual English & Assamese) currently contains 25 practice questions, each with a worked explanation. New questions are added as the syllabus and exam patterns are updated, so the set is worth revisiting.
Q: What is the capital of Assam and when was it shifted from Shillong?
A: The capital of Assam is Dispur, which is a locality within Guwahati. The capital was shifted from Shillong to Dispur in 1972, after Meghalaya became a separate state on 21 January 1972 and retained Shillong as its own capital.
Q: How many administrative divisions and districts does Assam have?
A: Assam has five administrative divisions: Lower Assam, North Assam, Central Assam, Upper Assam, and Hills and Barak Valley. After the recent administrative reorganisation the state has 35 districts, which are further divided into subdivisions, revenue circles, blocks, gaon panchayats and villages.
Q: Which countries and states share a border with Assam?
A: Assam shares international borders with Bhutan to the north and Bangladesh to the west and south-west. It shares inter-state boundaries with six major states: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Meghalaya and West Bengal, and it also has a short boundary with Tripura near Karimganj.
Q: With which states does Assam have border disputes?
A: Assam has long-standing border disputes with Nagaland, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram. The Nagaland dispute involves areas such as Merapani and the Rengma reserved forest, the Meghalaya dispute had 12 areas of which 6 were settled by a Memorandum of Understanding in 2022, and the Mizoram dispute is associated with the 2021 Lailapur incident.
Q: Why is Assam called the gateway of the North-East?
A: Assam is called the gateway of the North-East because of its central location. The narrow Siliguri corridor connects it with the rest of India, and all the other north-eastern states lie beyond it. Its strategic position, its international borders with Bhutan and Bangladesh, and its Brahmaputra river system make it the natural entry point for the whole region.
Q: অসমৰ ৰাজধানী কি আৰু শ্বিলঙৰ পৰা কেতিয়া স্থানান্তৰিত হৈছিল?
A: অসমৰ ৰাজধানী দিছপুৰ, যি গুৱাহাটীৰ এটা অঞ্চল। ২১ জানুৱাৰী ১৯৭২ত মেঘালয় পৃথক ৰাজ্য হোৱাৰ পিছত আৰু শ্বিলঙক নিজৰ ৰাজধানী হিচাপে ৰাখি অসমে ১৯৭২ চনত ৰাজধানী শ্বিলঙৰ পৰা দিছপুৰলৈ স্থানান্তৰ কৰিছিল।
Q: অসমত কিমানখন প্ৰশাসনিক খণ্ড আৰু জিলা আছে?
A: অসমত পাঁচখন প্ৰশাসনিক খণ্ড আছে: নিম্ন অসম, উত্তৰ অসম, মধ্য অসম, উচ্চ অসম, আৰু পাহাৰ আৰু বৰাক উপত্যকা। শেহতীয়া প্ৰশাসনিক পুনৰ্গঠনৰ পিছত ৰাজ্যত ৩৫খন জিলা আছে, যিবোৰ উপবিভাগ, ৰাজহ চক্ৰ, ব্লক, গাঁও পঞ্চায়ত আৰু গাঁৱত বিভক্ত।
Q: কোন দেশ আৰু ৰাজ্যই অসমৰ সৈতে সীমা ভাগ কৰে?
A: অসমে উত্তৰে ভূটান আৰু পশ্চিম তথা দক্ষিণ-পশ্চিমে বাংলাদেশৰ সৈতে আন্তৰ্জাতিক সীমা ভাগ কৰে। ই ছখন প্ৰধান ৰাজ্যৰ সৈতে আন্তঃৰাজ্যিক সীমা ভাগ কৰে: অৰুণাচল প্ৰদেশ, নাগালেণ্ড, মণিপুৰ, মিজোৰাম, মেঘালয় আৰু পশ্চিমবংগ, লগতে কৰিমগঞ্জৰ ওচৰত ত্ৰিপুৰাৰ সৈতে এটা চুটি সীমা আছে।
Q: অসমৰ সৈতে কোন কোন ৰাজ্যৰ সীমান্ত বিতৰ্ক আছে?
A: অসমৰ নাগালেণ্ড, মেঘালয়, অৰুণাচল প্ৰদেশ আৰু মিজোৰামৰ সৈতে দীৰ্ঘদিনীয়া সীমান্ত বিতৰ্ক আছে। নাগালেণ্ড বিতৰ্কত মেৰাপানী আৰু ৰেংমা সংৰক্ষিত বনৰ দৰে অঞ্চল, মেঘালয় বিতৰ্কত ১২টা অঞ্চল যাৰ ৬টা ২০২২ চনত বুজাবুজি memorandum ৰ জৰিয়তে নিষ্পত্তি হৈছিল, আৰু মিজোৰাম বিতৰ্ক ২০২১ চনৰ লাইলাপুৰ ঘটনাৰ সৈতে জড়িত।
Q: অসমক উত্তৰ-পূৱাঞ্চলৰ প্ৰৱেশদ্বাৰ কিয় কোৱা হয়?
A: কেন্দ্ৰীয় অৱস্থানৰ বাবে অসমক উত্তৰ-পূৱাঞ্চলৰ প্ৰৱেশদ্বাৰ কোৱা হয়। সংকীৰ্ণ শিলিগুৰি কৰিডৰে ইয়াক ভাৰতৰ বাকী অংশৰ সৈতে সংযোগ কৰে, আৰু বাকী উত্তৰ-পূৱাঞ্চলীয় ৰাজ্যসমূহ ইয়াৰ পিছফালে অৱস্থিত। ইয়াৰ কৌশলগত অৱস্থান, ভূটান তথা বাংলাদেশৰ সৈতে আন্তৰ্জাতিক সীমা, আৰু ব্ৰহ্মপুত্ৰ নদী ব্যৱস্থাই ইয়াক সমগ্ৰ অঞ্চলৰ স্বাভাৱিক প্ৰৱেশদ্বাৰ কৰি তোলে।

### Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/polity/bodies-provisions-sec/cag/
Summary: Practice comptroller and auditor general (cag) questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: Under which Article of the Constitution is the Comptroller and Auditor General of India established?
A: Article 148.
Q: Who appoints the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
A: The President of India.
Q: What is the main function of the CAG?
A: To audit the accounts of the Union Government, State Governments and public corporations.
Q: For how long does the CAG hold office?
A: Six years or till the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
Q: How can the CAG be removed?
A: In the same manner as a judge of the Supreme Court, i.e., by impeachment.
Q: Who administers the oath of office to the CAG?
A: The President of India.
Q: To whom does the CAG submit his report?
A: The President of India in respect of the Union, and the Governors in respect of the states.
Q: Which Committee of the Parliament examines the CAG report on the Union accounts?
A: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC).
Q: Who is the guardian of the public purse in India?
A: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
Q: What is the salary of the CAG?
A: It is equal to the salary of a judge of the Supreme Court.
Q: Who was the first Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
A: V. Narahari Rao.
Q: Is the CAG eligible for further government employment after his term?
A: No, he is not eligible for any further office under the Government of India or a state.
Q: Who audits the accounts of the State Governments?
A: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
Q: What is the constitutional status of the CAG?
A: It is an independent constitutional authority established under Article 148.
Q: What is the term of office of the CAG?
A: Six years from the date of assuming office, or till the age of 65, whichever is earlier.
Q: Can the CAG audit the accounts of local bodies?
A: Yes, he can audit the accounts of local bodies as well.
Q: Who presents the CAG report on state accounts in the State Legislature?
A: The Governor of the state.
Q: Which committee examines the CAG report in the State Legislature?
A: The Public Accounts Committee of the state.
Q: What are the three types of audit conducted by the CAG?
A: Financial audit, compliance audit and performance audit.
Q: Is the CAG a member of the Parliament?
A: No, the CAG is not a member of the Parliament.
Q: What is the role of the CAG in relation to the government companies?
A: He audits the accounts of government companies and corporations.
Q: Who is known as the 'Watchdog of the Public Purse'?
A: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
Q: What happens to the CAG report after it is submitted to the President?
A: It is laid before the Parliament for examination.
Q: Does the CAG require the consent of any authority to audit the government accounts?
A: No, the CAG can audit the accounts of the government on his own authority.
Q: Which Article empowers the CAG to audit the accounts of the states?
A: Article 149.
Q: Which article establishes the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General?
A: Article 148 of the Constitution establishes the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India. It provides that the President shall appoint the CAG, and lays down the conditions of service. Articles 149, 150 and 151 deal with duties, the form of accounts and the submission of reports respectively.
Q: What is the tenure of the CAG and how can the CAG be removed?
A: The CAG holds office for six years or until attaining the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. The CAG can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court, that is, for proved misbehaviour or incapacity, by a special majority of both Houses of Parliament and an address to the President.
Q: Why is the CAG called a comptroller in name only in India?
A: The CAG is called a comptroller in name only because, unlike the Comptroller and Auditor General in Britain, the CAG in India does not control the issue of money from the Consolidated Fund. In India the CAG audits the accounts after the money has been spent, and the real function of the office is audit rather than control.
Q: What is the role of the CAG's reports in Parliament?
A: Under Article 151 the CAG's reports on Union accounts are submitted to the President and those on state accounts to the Governor, and they are then laid before Parliament or the state legislature. The reports are examined by the Public Accounts Committee and other financial committees, and they form the basis of legislative scrutiny of government spending. The reports are advisory in nature but carry great weight.
Q: Which law lays down the duties and powers of the CAG?
A: Article 149 provides that the duties and powers of the CAG shall be prescribed by Parliament. Parliament enacted the Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service Act, 1971, commonly called the DPC Act, to lay down the detailed duties, powers and conditions of service, including the audit of government companies, corporations and autonomous bodies.
Q: কোন অনুচ্ছেদে নিয়ন্ত্ৰক আৰু মহাহিসাব-পৰীক্ষকৰ কাৰ্যালয় স্থাপন কৰে?
A: সংবিধানৰ অনুচ্ছেদ ১৪৮-এ ভাৰতৰ নিয়ন্ত্ৰক আৰু মহাহিসাব-পৰীক্ষকৰ কাৰ্যালয় স্থাপন কৰে। ই ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতিয়ে CAG-ক নিয়োগ কৰিব বুলি আৰু সেৱাৰ চৰ্তাৱলী নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰে। অনুচ্ছেদ ১৪৯, ১৫০ আৰু ১৫১য়ে ক্ৰমে কৰ্তব্য, হিচাপৰ ৰূপ আৰু প্ৰতিবেদন দাখিলৰ সৈতে জড়িত।
Q: CAG-ৰ কাৰ্যকাল কিমান আৰু CAG-ক কেনেকৈ অপসাৰণ কৰিব পাৰি?
A: CAG ছবছৰ বা ৬৫ বছৰ বয়স পোৱালৈকে, যিটো আগতে হয়, কাৰ্যকালত থাকে। CAG-ক কেৱল উচ্চতম ন্যায়ালয়ৰ ন্যায়াধীশৰ দৰে একেই ধৰণে আৰু একেই কাৰণত, অৰ্থাৎ প্ৰমাণিত অসদাচৰণ বা অক্ষমতাৰ বাবে, সংসদৰ দুয়ো সদনৰ বিশেষ সংখ্যাগৰিষ্ঠতা আৰু ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতিক সম্বোধনৰ জৰিয়তে অপসাৰণ কৰিব পাৰি।
Q: ভাৰতত CAG-ক কিয় কেৱল নামত নিয়ন্ত্ৰক কোৱা হয়?
A: CAG-ক কেৱল নামত নিয়ন্ত্ৰক কোৱা হয় কাৰণ বৃটেইনৰ নিয়ন্ত্ৰক আৰু মহাহিসাব-পৰীক্ষকৰ দৰে ভাৰতৰ CAG-য়ে সংহত নিধিৰ পৰা ধন ওলোৱাৰ নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ নকৰে। ভাৰতত CAG-য়ে ধন ব্যয় হোৱাৰ পিছত হিচাপ পৰীক্ষা কৰে, আৰু কাৰ্যালয়ৰ প্ৰকৃত কৰ্তব্য নিয়ন্ত্ৰণৰ পৰিৱৰ্তে হিচাব-পৰীক্ষা।
Q: সংসদত CAG-ৰ প্ৰতিবেদনৰ ভূমিকা কি?
A: অনুচ্ছেদ ১৫১ৰ অধীনত সংঘৰ হিচাপৰ ওপৰত CAG-ৰ প্ৰতিবেদন ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতিক আৰু ৰাজ্যৰ হিচাপৰ প্ৰতিবেদন ৰাজ্যপালক দাখিল কৰা হয়, আৰু তাৰ পিছত সংসদ বা ৰাজ্যিক বিধানমণ্ডলৰ সন্মুখত ৰখা হয়। প্ৰতিবেদনসমূহ ৰাজহুৱা হিচাপ সমিতি আৰু অন্য আৰ্থিক সমিতিয়ে পৰীক্ষা কৰে আৰু সেইবোৰে চৰকাৰী ব্যয়ৰ আইনসভিক পৰীক্ষাৰ ভিত্তি গঢ়ে। প্ৰতিবেদনসমূহ উপদেশমূলক যদিও মহান গুৰুত্ব বহন কৰে।
Q: CAG-ৰ কৰ্তব্য আৰু ক্ষমতা কোনটো আইনে নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰে?
A: অনুচ্ছেদ ১৪৯-এ বিধান দিয়ে যে CAG-ৰ কৰ্তব্য আৰু ক্ষমতা সংসদে নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰিব। সংসদে সবিস্তাৰ কৰ্তব্য, ক্ষমতা আৰু সেৱাৰ চৰ্তাৱলী নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰিবলৈ ১৯৭১ চনৰ কৰ্তব্য, ক্ষমতা আৰু সেৱাৰ চৰ্তাৱলী আইন, অৰ্থাৎ DPC আইন, প্ৰণয়ন কৰিছিল, যাৰ ভিতৰত চৰকাৰী কোম্পানী, নিগম আৰু স্বায়ত্তশাসিত অনুষ্ঠানসমূহৰ হিচাব-পৰীক্ষাও সন্নিৱিষ্ট।

### ECI & State EC Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/polity/bodies-provisions-sec/eci-state-ec/
Summary: Practice eci & state ec questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Under which Article of the Constitution is the Election Commission of India established?
A: Article 324.
Q: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner of India?
A: The President of India.
Q: What is the composition of the Election Commission of India?
A: The Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners.
Q: For how long does the Chief Election Commissioner hold office?
A: Six years or till the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
Q: How can the Chief Election Commissioner be removed?
A: Only by impeachment in the same manner as a judge of the Supreme Court.
Q: Who conducts elections to the office of the President and the Vice-President of India?
A: The Election Commission of India.
Q: Who conducts elections to the Parliament and the State Legislatures?
A: The Election Commission of India.
Q: Who is the first Chief Election Commissioner of India?
A: Sukumar Sen.
Q: When was the Election Commission of India established?
A: On 25 January 1950.
Q: Which day is celebrated as National Voters' Day in India?
A: 25 January, to mark the establishment of the Election Commission.
Q: Under which Article is the State Election Commission established?
A: Article 243K.
Q: Who appoints the State Election Commissioner?
A: The Governor of the state.
Q: What are the elections conducted by the State Election Commission?
A: Elections to the Panchayats and Municipalities.
Q: What is the Model Code of Conduct?
A: Guidelines issued by the Election Commission to ensure free and fair elections.
Q: When was the Electronic Voting Machine (EVM) first used in India?
A: First used experimentally in 1982, and used on a large scale from 1999.
Q: What is VVPAT?
A: Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail, which allows voters to verify their vote.
Q: What is the minimum age of voting in India?
A: 18 years.
Q: Which Amendment lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years?
A: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988.
Q: What is the Election Symbol?
A: A symbol allotted to a political party or candidate for identification in elections.
Q: Who allots election symbols to political parties?
A: The Election Commission of India.
Q: What is the tenure of the Election Commission members?
A: The CEC serves six years or till 65 years; the term of the Election Commissioners is determined by the President.
Q: Can the Election Commissioners be removed on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner?
A: Yes, they can be removed by the President on the recommendation of the CEC.
Q: Who is responsible for the preparation of electoral rolls in India?
A: The Election Commission of India.
Q: What is the function of the Election Commission regarding political parties?
A: It registers political parties and grants recognition to them.
Q: Who is the Chief Election Commissioner who introduced the use of EVMs on a large scale?
A: M.S. Gill.
Q: Under which article is the Election Commission of India established?
A: The Election Commission of India is established under Article 324 of the Constitution. This article vests in the Commission the superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of elections to Parliament, the State Legislatures and the offices of the President and the Vice-President.
Q: What is the composition of the Election Commission and when did it become multi-member?
A: The Election Commission originally consisted only of the Chief Election Commissioner. It became a multi-member body on 1 October 1993 and now consists of the Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners. The CEC and the Election Commissioners are appointed by the President and hold office for six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
Q: What is the State Election Commission and under which article is it created?
A: The State Election Commission is a constitutional body created by the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts. Article 243K provides for a State Election Commission for panchayats and Article 243ZA for municipalities. The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and conducts elections only to local bodies.
Q: What is the difference between the ECI and the State Election Commission?
A: The ECI, under Article 324, conducts elections to Parliament, the State Legislatures and the offices of the President and the Vice-President. The State Election Commission, under Articles 243K and 243ZA, conducts elections to panchayats and municipalities. The CEC is appointed by the President and removed like a Supreme Court judge, while the State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and removed like a High Court judge.
Q: Which amendment lowered the voting age to 18 years?
A: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 lowered the voting age from 21 years to 18 years. It amended Article 326 of the Constitution, and the change came into force in 1989. The Election Commission uses the updated electoral rolls prepared on the basis of this provision.
Q: ভাৰতৰ নিৰ্বাচন আয়োগ কোন অনুচ্ছেদৰ অধীনত স্থাপিত?
A: ভাৰতৰ নিৰ্বাচন আয়োগ সংবিধানৰ অনুচ্ছেদ ৩২৪ৰ অধীনত স্থাপিত। এই অনুচ্ছেদে আয়োগৰ ওপৰত নিৰ্বাচনী তালিকা প্ৰস্তুত কৰাৰ তথা সংসদ, ৰাজ্যিক বিধানমণ্ডল আৰু ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতি তথা উপ-ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতিৰ কাৰ্যালয়লৈ নিৰ্বাচন অনুষ্ঠিত কৰাৰ তত্ত্বাৱধান, পৰিচালনা আৰু নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ অৰ্পণ কৰে।
Q: নিৰ্বাচন আয়োগৰ গঠন কি আৰু ই কেতিয়া বহু-সদস্যীয় হৈছিল?
A: নিৰ্বাচন আয়োগ মূলতঃ কেৱল মুখ্য নিৰ্বাচন আয়ুক্তৰে গঠিত আছিল। ই ১৯৯৩ চনৰ ১ অক্টোবৰত বহু-সদস্যীয় শৰীৰ হৈ পৰে আৰু এতিয়া মুখ্য নিৰ্বাচন আয়ুক্ত আৰু দুজন নিৰ্বাচন আয়ুক্তৰ সমন্বয়ে গঠিত। CEC আৰু নিৰ্বাচন আয়ুক্তসকলক ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতিয়ে নিয়োগ কৰে আৰু তেওঁলোক ছবছৰ বা ৬৫ বছৰ বয়স পোৱালৈকে, যিটো আগতে হয়, কাৰ্যকালত থাকে।
Q: ৰাজ্যিক নিৰ্বাচন আয়োগ কি আৰু কোন অনুচ্ছেদত সৃষ্টি কৰা হৈছে?
A: ৰাজ্যিক নিৰ্বাচন আয়োগ ৭৩ সংখ্যক আৰু ৭৪ সংখ্যক সাংবিধানিক সংশোধনী আইনৰ জৰিয়তে সৃষ্টি কৰা এক সাংবিধানিক অনুষ্ঠান। অনুচ্ছেদ ২৪৩K-এ পঞ্চায়তৰ বাবে আৰু অনুচ্ছেদ ২৪৩ZA-ই পৌৰসভাৰ বাবে ৰাজ্যিক নিৰ্বাচন আয়োগৰ ব্যৱস্থা কৰে। ৰাজ্যিক নিৰ্বাচন আয়ুক্তক ৰাজ্যপালে নিয়োগ কৰে আৰু ই কেৱল স্থানীয় অনুষ্ঠানলৈ নিৰ্বাচন অনুষ্ঠিত কৰে।
Q: ECI আৰু ৰাজ্যিক নিৰ্বাচন আয়োগৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: ECI, অনুচ্ছেদ ৩২৪ৰ অধীনত, সংসদ, ৰাজ্যিক বিধানমণ্ডল আৰু ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতি তথা উপ-ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতিৰ কাৰ্যালয়লৈ নিৰ্বাচন অনুষ্ঠিত কৰে। ৰাজ্যিক নিৰ্বাচন আয়োগ, অনুচ্ছেদ ২৪৩K আৰু ২৪৩ZAৰ অধীনত, পঞ্চায়ত আৰু পৌৰসভালৈ নিৰ্বাচন অনুষ্ঠিত কৰে। CEC-ক ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতিয়ে নিয়োগ কৰি উচ্চতম ন্যায়ালয়ৰ ন্যায়াধীশৰ দৰে অপসাৰণ কৰা হয়, আনহাতে ৰাজ্যিক নিৰ্বাচন আয়ুক্তক ৰাজ্যপালে নিয়োগ কৰি উচ্চ ন্যায়ালয়ৰ ন্যায়াধীশৰ দৰে অপসাৰণ কৰা হয়।
Q: কোন সংশোধনীয়ে ভোটদানৰ বয়স ১৮ বছৰলৈ হ্ৰাস কৰিছিল?
A: ১৯৮৮ চনৰ ৬১ সংখ্যক সাংবিধানিক সংশোধনী আইনে ভোটদানৰ বয়স ২১ বছৰৰ পৰা ১৮ বছৰলৈ হ্ৰাস কৰিছিল। ই সংবিধানৰ অনুচ্ছেদ ৩২৬ সংশোধন কৰিছিল আৰু এই পৰিৱৰ্তন ১৯৮৯ চনত বলৱৎ হয়। নিৰ্বাচন আয়োগে এই বিধানৰ আধাৰত প্ৰস্তুত কৰা অধিকালিক নিৰ্বাচনী তালিকা ব্যৱহাৰ কৰে।

### Emergency Provisions Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/polity/bodies-provisions-sec/emergency-provisions/
Summary: Practice emergency provisions questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Under which Article can the National Emergency be declared?
A: Article 352.
Q: Who declares the National Emergency?
A: The President of India.
Q: On what grounds can the National Emergency be proclaimed?
A: War, external aggression or armed rebellion.
Q: Who must approve the proclamation of National Emergency?
A: Both Houses of Parliament, within one month of the proclamation.
Q: What is the maximum period for which the National Emergency can continue?
A: There is no maximum limit, but it must be approved by Parliament every six months.
Q: Which Fundamental Right is automatically suspended during the National Emergency?
A: The right to freedom of speech and expression (Article 19).
Q: Under which Article can the President impose President's Rule in a state?
A: Article 356.
Q: On what ground is President's Rule imposed in a state?
A: Failure of the constitutional machinery of the state.
Q: What is the maximum period for which President's Rule can be imposed in a state?
A: A maximum of three years, with parliamentary approval every six months.
Q: Who approves the proclamation of President's Rule?
A: Both Houses of Parliament.
Q: Under which Article can the Financial Emergency be proclaimed?
A: Article 360.
Q: On what ground can the Financial Emergency be proclaimed?
A: If the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.
Q: Who proclaims the Financial Emergency?
A: The President of India.
Q: How many times has the National Emergency been declared in India so far?
A: Three times - 1962, 1971 and 1975.
Q: What was the ground for the National Emergency of 1975?
A: Internal disturbance (later changed to armed rebellion by the 44th Amendment).
Q: Which Amendment restricted the ground of National Emergency from 'internal disturbance' to 'armed rebellion'?
A: The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978.
Q: What is the effect of the National Emergency on Fundamental Rights?
A: Article 19 is suspended automatically, and other rights can be suspended by order.
Q: What happens to the State Government when President's Rule is imposed?
A: The state government is dismissed and the state is governed by the Governor on behalf of the President.
Q: Who approves the National Emergency when the Lok Sabha is dissolved?
A: The Rajya Sabha, within the specified period, and later the new Lok Sabha.
Q: What is the difference between the National Emergency and President's Rule?
A: National Emergency is declared for the whole country due to war or aggression, while President's Rule is imposed in a state due to constitutional failure.
Q: Who can revoke a proclamation of National Emergency?
A: The President, or the Lok Sabha by a resolution.
Q: What is the special majority required to approve a proclamation of emergency?
A: A majority of the total membership of each house and a two-thirds majority of members present and voting.
Q: What happens to the life of the Lok Sabha during the National Emergency?
A: The term of the Lok Sabha can be extended beyond five years by Parliament, for one year at a time.
Q: Under which Article is the power to suspend Fundamental Rights during the National Emergency given?
A: Article 359.
Q: Which authority has the power to declare that a state is under President's Rule?
A: The President of India, on the report of the Governor or otherwise.
Q: What are the three types of emergency in the Indian Constitution?
A: The Constitution provides for three types of emergency: the National Emergency under Article 352, declared on grounds of war, external aggression or armed rebellion; President's Rule under Article 356, imposed on the failure of the constitutional machinery of a state; and the Financial Emergency under Article 360, proclaimed when the financial stability or credit of India is threatened.
Q: How many times has a National Emergency been declared in India?
A: A National Emergency has been declared three times: in 1962 during the Chinese aggression, in 1971 during the war with Pakistan, and in 1975 on the ground of internal disturbance. The 1975 emergency was the most controversial and led to the 44th Amendment Act of 1978, which replaced internal disturbance with armed rebellion.
Q: What is the effect of a National Emergency on Fundamental Rights?
A: During a National Emergency caused by war or external aggression, Article 19 is automatically suspended. Other Fundamental Rights can be suspended by an order under Article 359, but Articles 20 and 21, which protect against arbitrary conviction and protect life and personal liberty, cannot be suspended. After the 44th Amendment, Article 19 can be suspended only in an emergency caused by war or external aggression.
Q: What is President's Rule and how long can it continue?
A: President's Rule under Article 356 is imposed when the constitutional machinery of a state fails. It must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within two months and can continue for six months at a time up to a maximum of three years. Extension beyond one year requires a National Emergency to be in operation and a certification by the Election Commission that elections cannot be held.
Q: What did the S.R. Bommai case decide about President's Rule?
A: In S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) the Supreme Court held that a proclamation under Article 356 is subject to judicial review and that the power is not absolute. The Court also held that the majority of a government should be tested on the floor of the House and that a government cannot be dismissed merely on the Governor's subjective satisfaction. The judgment strengthened the safeguards against the misuse of President's Rule.
Q: ভাৰতীয় সংবিধানত কিমান ধৰণৰ আপৎকাল আছে?
A: সংবিধানত তিনি ধৰণৰ আপৎকালৰ ব্যৱস্থা আছে: অনুচ্ছেদ ৩৫২ৰ অধীনত ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় আপৎকাল, যি যুদ্ধ, বাহ্যিক আক্ৰমণ বা সশস্ত্ৰ বিদ্ৰোহৰ কাৰণে ঘোষণা কৰা হয়; অনুচ্ছেদ ৩৫৬ৰ অধীনত ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতি শাসন, যি ৰাজ্য এখনৰ সাংবিধানিক ব্যৱস্থা বিফল হ'লে জাপি দিয়া হয়; আৰু অনুচ্ছেদ ৩৬০ৰ অধীনত আৰ্থিক আপৎকাল, যি ভাৰতৰ আৰ্থিক স্থিতি বা ঋণনিৰ্ভৰতা বিপদাপন্ন হ'লে ঘোষণা কৰা হয়।
Q: ভাৰতত ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় আপৎকাল কিমানবাৰ ঘোষণা কৰা হৈছে?
A: ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় আপৎকাল তিনিবাৰ ঘোষণা কৰা হৈছে: ১৯৬২ চনত চীনৰ আক্ৰমণৰ সময়ত, ১৯৭১ চনত পাকিস্তানৰ সৈতে যুদ্ধৰ সময়ত, আৰু ১৯৭৫ চনত আভ্যন্তৰীণ বিশৃংখলাৰ কাৰণে। ১৯৭৫ চনৰ আপৎকাল আটাইতকৈ বিতৰ্কিত আছিল আৰু ইয়াৰ ফলত ১৯৭৮ চনৰ ৪৪ সংখ্যক সংশোধনী আইন আহিছিল, যিয়ে আভ্যন্তৰীণ বিশৃংখলাক সশস্ত্ৰ বিদ্ৰোহলৈ সলনি কৰিছিল।
Q: ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় আপৎকালৰ মৌলিক অধিকাৰৰ ওপৰত প্ৰভাৱ কি?
A: যুদ্ধ বা বাহ্যিক আক্ৰমণৰ বাবে হোৱা ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় আপৎকালত অনুচ্ছেদ ১৯ স্বয়ংক্ৰিয়ভাৱে স্থগিত হয়। অনুচ্ছেদ ৩৫৯ৰ অধীনত আদেশৰ জৰিয়তে অন্য মৌলিক অধিকাৰ স্থগিত কৰিব পাৰি, কিন্তু অনুচ্ছেদ ২০ আৰু ২১, যিবোৰে স্বেচ্ছাচাৰী দণ্ড আৰু জীৱন তথা ব্যক্তিগত স্বাধীনতাৰ সুৰক্ষা দিয়ে, স্থগিত কৰিব নোৱাৰি। ৪৪ সংখ্যক সংশোধনীৰ পিছত অনুচ্ছেদ ১৯ কেৱল যুদ্ধ বা বাহ্যিক আক্ৰমণৰ আপৎকালত স্থগিত কৰিব পাৰি।
Q: ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতি শাসন কি আৰু কিমান দিন চলিব পাৰে?
A: অনুচ্ছেদ ৩৫৬ৰ অধীনত ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতি শাসন ৰাজ্য এখনৰ সাংবিধানিক ব্যৱস্থা বিফল হ'লে জাপি দিয়া হয়। ই দুমাহৰ ভিতৰত সংসদৰ দুয়ো সদনে অনুমোদন কৰিব লাগে আৰু একেষেৰে ছমাহ, সৰ্বাধিক তিনি বছৰলৈকে চলিব পাৰে। এক বছৰৰ ওপৰত সম্প্ৰসাৰণৰ বাবে ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় আপৎকাল চলি থকা আৰু নিৰ্বাচন আয়োগে নিৰ্বাচন অনুষ্ঠিত কৰিব নোৱাৰি বুলি প্ৰমাণপত্ৰ দিয়া প্ৰয়োজন।
Q: S.R. বোম্মাই গোচৰে ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতি শাসনৰ বিষয়ে কি সিদ্ধান্ত লৈছিল?
A: S.R. বোম্মাই বনাম ভাৰত সংঘ (১৯৯৪) গোচৰত উচ্চতম ন্যায়ালয়ে ৰায় দিছিল যে অনুচ্ছেদ ৩৫৬ৰ ঘোষণাপত্ৰ ন্যায়িক পুনৰ্বিচাৰৰ অধীন আৰু ক্ষমতাখন নিখুঁত নহয়। ন্যায়ালয়ে এইয়াও ৰায় দিছিল যে চৰকাৰৰ সংখ্যাগৰিষ্ঠতা সদনত পৰীক্ষা কৰা উচিত আৰু কেৱল ৰাজ্যপালৰ ব্যক্তিনিষ্ঠ সন্তুষ্টিৰ ভিত্তিত চৰকাৰক বৰ্খাস্ত কৰিব নোৱাৰি। এই ৰায়দানে ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতি শাসনৰ অপব্যৱহাৰৰ বিৰুদ্ধে সুৰক্ষা সবল কৰিছিল।

### Finance Commission & State FC — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/polity/bodies-provisions-sec/finance-commission-state-fc/
Summary: Practice finance commission & state fc questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Under which Article of the Constitution is the Finance Commission established?
A: Article 280.
Q: Who appoints the Finance Commission of India?
A: The President of India.
Q: After how many years is the Finance Commission constituted?
A: Every five years.
Q: What is the main function of the Finance Commission?
A: To recommend the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the states.
Q: Who is the chairman of the Finance Commission?
A: A person appointed by the President, having experience in public affairs.
Q: What is the composition of the Finance Commission?
A: A Chairman and four other members.
Q: When was the first Finance Commission constituted?
A: In 1951.
Q: Who was the chairman of the first Finance Commission?
A: K.C. Neogy.
Q: Who was the chairman of the 15th Finance Commission?
A: N.K. Singh.
Q: What are the recommendations of the Finance Commission based on?
A: The population, income and fiscal needs of the states.
Q: Under which Article is the State Finance Commission established?
A: Article 243-I.
Q: Who appoints the State Finance Commission?
A: The Governor of the state.
Q: What is the main function of the State Finance Commission?
A: To recommend the distribution of financial resources between the state and the Panchayats and Municipalities.
Q: Who constitutes the State Finance Commission?
A: The Governor of the state.
Q: What is the composition of the State Finance Commission?
A: A Chairman and four other members, appointed by the Governor.
Q: How often is the State Finance Commission constituted?
A: Every five years.
Q: What are grants-in-aid?
A: Financial assistance given by the Union to the states, recommended by the Finance Commission.
Q: Which tax is divided between the Union and the states on the recommendation of the Finance Commission?
A: The shareable central taxes like income tax and excise duties (now GST).
Q: What is the devolution of taxes?
A: The transfer of a share of central taxes to the states as recommended by the Finance Commission.
Q: Who presents the recommendations of the Finance Commission to the Parliament?
A: The President of India, along with a memorandum explaining the action taken.
Q: What is the GST compensation fund?
A: A fund recommended to compensate states for any loss of revenue due to the implementation of GST.
Q: What is the period for which the Finance Commission makes its recommendations?
A: For a period of five years.
Q: Who has to implement the recommendations of the State Finance Commission?
A: The State Government, by presenting the recommendations to the State Legislature.
Q: What is the difference between the Finance Commission and the State Finance Commission?
A: The Finance Commission distributes taxes between the Union and the states, while the State Finance Commission distributes resources between the state and the local bodies.
Q: Which was the latest Finance Commission constituted for the period 2021-26?
A: The 15th Finance Commission.
Q: Under which article is the Finance Commission of India established?
A: The Finance Commission of India is established under Article 280 of the Constitution. The President constitutes a Finance Commission every fifth year or earlier, and it consists of a Chairman and four other members. It recommends the distribution of taxes between the Union and the states and the principles governing grants-in-aid to the states.
Q: What is the composition and tenure of the Finance Commission?
A: The Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and four other members appointed by the President. The Chairman is a person with experience in public affairs, and the other members are drawn from persons with qualifications in finance, administration, economics and government accounts. The Commission is constituted every five years or earlier, and its recommendations cover a period of five years.
Q: What is the State Finance Commission and what does it do?
A: The State Finance Commission is created under Article 243-I for panchayats and Article 243-Y for municipalities. It is constituted by the Governor every five years. It reviews the financial position of panchayats and municipalities and recommends the distribution of taxes between the state and local bodies, the assignment of taxes, grants-in-aid from the state's Consolidated Fund and measures to improve local finances.
Q: What is the difference between the Finance Commission and the State Finance Commission?
A: The Finance Commission under Article 280 is constituted by the President and distributes tax revenue between the Union and the states. The State Finance Commission under Articles 243-I and 243-Y is constituted by the Governor and distributes resources between the state and its panchayats and municipalities. The Union Finance Commission has a Chairman and four members, while the composition of the State Finance Commission is decided by the state legislature.
Q: Which was the latest Finance Commission and what period did it cover?
A: The 15th Finance Commission, chaired by N.K. Singh, made recommendations for the period 2021-26. It fixed the states' share of the divisible pool at 41 per cent after the reorganisation of Jammu and Kashmir. The 14th Finance Commission had earlier recommended a 42 per cent share for the states.
Q: ভাৰতৰ অৰ্থ আয়োগ কোন অনুচ্ছেদৰ অধীনত স্থাপিত?
A: ভাৰতৰ অৰ্থ আয়োগ সংবিধানৰ অনুচ্ছেদ ২৮০ৰ অধীনত স্থাপিত। ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতিয়ে প্ৰতি পাঁচ বছৰৰ মূৰে মূৰে বা আগতেও এখন অৰ্থ আয়োগ গঠন কৰে, য'ত এজন অধ্যক্ষ আৰু চাৰিজন সদস্য থাকে। ই সংঘ আৰু ৰাজ্যসমূহৰ মাজত কৰ বিতৰণ আৰু ৰাজ্যসমূহক সহায়ক অনুদানৰ নিয়ন্ত্ৰণকাৰী নীতিৰ পৰামৰ্শ দিয়ে।
Q: অৰ্থ আয়োগৰ গঠন আৰু কাৰ্যকাল কি?
A: অৰ্থ আয়োগত ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতিয়ে নিয়োগ কৰা এজন অধ্যক্ষ আৰু চাৰিজন সদস্য থাকে। অধ্যক্ষ ৰাজহুৱা বিষয়ত অভিজ্ঞতা থকা ব্যক্তি আৰু অন্য সদস্যসকলক বিত্ত, প্ৰশাসন, অৰ্থনীতি আৰু চৰকাৰী হিচাপৰ যোগ্যতা থকা ব্যক্তিসকলৰ পৰা বাছনি কৰা হয়। আয়োগ প্ৰতি পাঁচ বছৰৰ মূৰে মূৰে বা আগতেও গঠিত হয় আৰু ইয়াৰ পৰামৰ্শই পাঁচ বছৰৰ এক সময় সামৰি লয়।
Q: ৰাজ্যিক অৰ্থ আয়োগ কি আৰু ই কি কৰে?
A: ৰাজ্যিক অৰ্থ আয়োগ পঞ্চায়তৰ বাবে অনুচ্ছেদ ২৪৩-I আৰু পৌৰসভাৰ বাবে অনুচ্ছেদ ২৪৩-Yৰ অধীনত সৃষ্টি কৰা হয়। ই ৰাজ্যপালৰ দ্বাৰা প্ৰতি পাঁচ বছৰে গঠিত হয়। ই পঞ্চায়ত আৰু পৌৰসভাৰ আৰ্থিক স্থিতি পৰ্যালোচনা কৰি ৰাজ্য আৰু স্থানীয় অনুষ্ঠানসমূহৰ মাজত কৰ বিতৰণ, কৰৰ অৰ্পণ, ৰাজ্যৰ সংহত নিধিৰ পৰা সহায়ক অনুদান আৰু স্থানীয় বিত্ত উন্নত কৰাৰ উপায়ৰ পৰামৰ্শ দিয়ে।
Q: অৰ্থ আয়োগ আৰু ৰাজ্যিক অৰ্থ আয়োগৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: অনুচ্ছেদ ২৮০ৰ অধীনত অৰ্থ আয়োগ ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতিয়ে গঠন কৰে আৰু সংঘ আৰু ৰাজ্যসমূহৰ মাজত কৰ ৰাজহ বিতৰণ কৰে। অনুচ্ছেদ ২৪৩-I আৰু ২৪৩-Yৰ অধীনত ৰাজ্যিক অৰ্থ আয়োগ ৰাজ্যপালে গঠন কৰে আৰু ৰাজ্য তথা ইয়াৰ পঞ্চায়ত-পৌৰসভাৰ মাজত সম্পদ বিতৰণ কৰে। সংঘৰ অৰ্থ আয়োগত এজন অধ্যক্ষ আৰু চাৰিজন সদস্য, আনহাতে ৰাজ্যিক অৰ্থ আয়োগৰ গঠন ৰাজ্যিক বিধানমণ্ডলে নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰে।
Q: শেহতীয়া অৰ্থ আয়োগ কোনখন আৰু ই কোন সময় সামৰি লৈছিল?
A: ১৫ সংখ্যক অৰ্থ আয়োগ, যাৰ অধ্যক্ষ এন.কে. সিং, ২০২১-২৬ সময়ৰ বাবে পৰামৰ্শ দিছিল। জম্মু-কাশ্মীৰৰ পুনৰ্গঠনৰ পিছত ই ৰাজ্যসমূহৰ বিভাজ্য পুলৰ ভাগ ৪১ শতাংশ নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰিছিল। ইয়াৰ আগতে ১৪ সংখ্যক অৰ্থ আয়োগে ৰাজ্যসমূহৰ বাবে ৪২ শতাংশ ভাগৰ পৰামৰ্শ দিছিল।

### UPSC & APSC Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/polity/bodies-provisions-sec/upsc-apsc/
Summary: Practice upsc & apsc questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: Under which Article is the Union Public Service Commission established?
A: Article 315.
Q: Who appoints the members of the Union Public Service Commission?
A: The President of India.
Q: For how long does the Chairman of the UPSC hold office?
A: Six years or till the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
Q: What is the main function of the UPSC?
A: To conduct examinations for recruitment to the Central Civil Services and to advise the Government on service matters.
Q: Which examination is conducted by the UPSC for recruitment to the IAS, IPS and IFS?
A: The Civil Services Examination (CSE).
Q: Who appoints the Chairman and members of the Assam Public Service Commission (APSC)?
A: The Governor of Assam.
Q: For how long does the Chairman of the APSC hold office?
A: Six years or till the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier.
Q: What is the main function of the APSC?
A: To conduct examinations for recruitment to the Assam Civil Services and to advise the State Government on service matters.
Q: Which examination is conducted by the APSC for recruitment to the Assam Civil Services?
A: The APSC Combined Competitive Examination (CCE).
Q: Under which Article is the State Public Service Commission established?
A: Article 315 (which provides for a PSC for each state).
Q: How can the Chairman or members of the UPSC be removed?
A: By the President, only on the ground of misbehaviour, after an enquiry by the Supreme Court.
Q: Who presents the annual report of the UPSC to the Parliament?
A: The President of India (through the concerned minister).
Q: What is the qualification required for appointment as a member of the UPSC?
A: At least half of the members must have held office under the Government for at least ten years.
Q: When was the Assam Public Service Commission (APSC) established?
A: On 1 April 1937.
Q: What is the eligibility age limit for the UPSC Civil Services Examination?
A: 21 to 32 years (with relaxations for reserved categories).
Q: What is the upper age limit for the APSC Combined Competitive Examination?
A: Generally 21 to 38 years for unreserved candidates, with relaxations.
Q: Can the UPSC members be appointed to another post after retirement?
A: No, they are not eligible for further employment under the Government of India or a state.
Q: Who determines the conditions of service of the UPSC members?
A: The President of India.
Q: What is the composition of the UPSC?
A: A Chairman and other members, the number of which is determined by the President.
Q: What is the difference between the UPSC and the APSC?
A: The UPSC is a central constitutional body for central services, while the APSC is a state-level constitutional body for Assam state services.
Q: Which of the following services is filled through the APSC CCE in Assam?
A: Assam Civil Service (ACS), Assam Police Service (APS) and allied services.
Q: Who acts as the chief adviser to the Government of Assam on service matters?
A: The Assam Public Service Commission (APSC).
Q: What is the constitutional status of the UPSC?
A: It is an independent constitutional body established under Article 315.
Q: Who can remove the Chairman of the APSC?
A: The President of India, on the ground of misbehaviour, after an enquiry by the Supreme Court.
Q: What is the service tenure of a member of the UPSC?
A: Six years or till the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
Q: Under which article are the Public Service Commissions established?
A: Public Service Commissions are established under Article 315 of the Constitution, which provides for a Union Public Service Commission and a State Public Service Commission for each state. It also allows two or more states to have a Joint State Public Service Commission created by an Act of Parliament.
Q: What is the tenure and age limit of UPSC and state commission members?
A: The Chairman and members of the UPSC hold office for six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. For a State Public Service Commission such as the APSC, the term is six years or until the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier. Members are appointed by the President for the UPSC and by the Governor for a state commission.
Q: How can the Chairman or a member of a Public Service Commission be removed?
A: The Chairman or a member of a Public Service Commission can be removed only on the ground of misbehaviour, and only after the matter has been referred to the Supreme Court and the Court has, on inquiry, found the member guilty. The President removes members of the UPSC and the Governor removes members of a state commission. Removal is also possible on grounds such as insolvency or infirmity.
Q: What is the difference between the UPSC and the APSC?
A: The UPSC is the Union Public Service Commission, a central constitutional body under Article 315, whose members are appointed by the President and who hold office up to the age of 65. It recruits for central and all-India services such as the IAS, IPS and IFS. The APSC is the Assam Public Service Commission, whose members are appointed by the Governor of Assam and who hold office up to the age of 62. It recruits for Assam state services such as the ACS and APS.
Q: When was the Assam Public Service Commission established?
A: The Assam Public Service Commission was established on 1 April 1937 and has its headquarters at Guwahati. It conducts the Combined Competitive Examination for recruitment to the Assam Civil Service, the Assam Police Service and allied services, and advises the Government of Assam on recruitment, promotion and disciplinary matters.
Q: লোকসেৱা আয়োগসমূহ কোন অনুচ্ছেদৰ অধীনত স্থাপিত?
A: লোকসেৱা আয়োগসমূহ সংবিধানৰ অনুচ্ছেদ ৩১৫ৰ অধীনত স্থাপিত, যি সংঘৰ বাবে এটা সংঘ লোকসেৱা আয়োগ আৰু প্ৰতিখন ৰাজ্যৰ বাবে এটা ৰাজ্যিক লোকসেৱা আয়োগৰ ব্যৱস্থা কৰে। ই দুই বা তাতোধিক ৰাজ্যক সংসদৰ আইনৰ জৰিয়তে সৃষ্টি কৰা সংযুক্ত ৰাজ্যিক লোকসেৱা আয়োগ ৰখাৰ অনুমতিও দিয়ে।
Q: UPSC আৰু ৰাজ্যিক আয়োগ সদস্যৰ কাৰ্যকাল তথা বয়সসীমা কিমান?
A: UPSC-ৰ অধ্যক্ষ আৰু সদস্যসকলে ছবছৰ বা ৬৫ বছৰ বয়স পোৱালৈকে, যিটো আগতে হয়, কাৰ্যকালত থাকে। APSC ৰ দৰে ৰাজ্যিক লোকসেৱা আয়োগৰ ক্ষেত্ৰত কাৰ্যকাল ছবছৰ বা ৬২ বছৰ বয়স পোৱালৈকে, যিটো আগতে হয়। UPSC-ৰ সদস্যসকলক ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতিয়ে আৰু ৰাজ্যিক আয়োগৰ সদস্যসকলক ৰাজ্যপালে নিয়োগ কৰে।
Q: লোকসেৱা আয়োগৰ অধ্যক্ষ বা সদস্য এজনক কেনেকৈ অপসাৰণ কৰিব পাৰি?
A: লোকসেৱা আয়োগৰ অধ্যক্ষ বা সদস্য এজনক কেৱল অপকৰ্মৰ কাৰণতহে অপসাৰণ কৰিব পাৰি, আৰু তাও বিষয়টো উচ্চতম ন্যায়ালয়লৈ প্ৰসংগ কৰাৰ পিছত ন্যায়ালয়ে তদন্ত কৰি সদস্যজনক দোষী পোৱাৰ পিছতহে। ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতিয়ে UPSC-ৰ সদস্যসকলক আৰু ৰাজ্যপালে ৰাজ্যিক আয়োগৰ সদস্যসকলক অপসাৰণ কৰে। দেউলীয়া অৱস্থা বা দৌৰ্বল্যৰ দৰে কাৰণতো অপসাৰণ সম্ভৱ।
Q: UPSC আৰু APSC ৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: UPSC হৈছে সংঘ লোকসেৱা আয়োগ, অনুচ্ছেদ ৩১৫ৰ অধীনত এটা কেন্দ্ৰীয় সাংবিধানিক অনুষ্ঠান, যাৰ সদস্যসকলক ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতিয়ে নিয়োগ কৰে আৰু তেওঁলোক ৬৫ বছৰ বয়সলৈকে কাৰ্যকালত থাকে। ই IAS, IPS আৰু IFSৰ দৰে কেন্দ্ৰীয় তথা সৰ্বভাৰতীয় সেৱাৰ বাবে নিযুক্তি কৰে। APSC হৈছে অসম লোকসেৱা আয়োগ, যাৰ সদস্যসকলক অসমৰ ৰাজ্যপালে নিয়োগ কৰে আৰু তেওঁলোক ৬২ বছৰ বয়সলৈকে কাৰ্যকালত থাকে। ই ACS আৰু APSৰ দৰে অসম ৰাজ্যিক সেৱাৰ বাবে নিযুক্তি কৰে।
Q: অসম লোকসেৱা আয়োগ কেতিয়া স্থাপিত হৈছিল?
A: অসম লোকসেৱা আয়োগ ১৯৩৭ চনৰ ১ এপ্ৰিলত স্থাপিত হৈছিল আৰু ইয়াৰ মুখ্য কাৰ্যালয় গুৱাহাটীত। ই অসম অসামৰিক সেৱা, অসম আৰক্ষী সেৱা আৰু সংযুক্ত সেৱালৈ নিয়োগৰ বাবে সংযুক্ত প্ৰতিযোগিতামূলক পৰীক্ষা অনুষ্ঠিত কৰে আৰু নিযুক্তি, পদোন্নতি তথা শৃংখলামূলক বিষয়ত অসম চৰকাৰক পৰামৰ্শ দিয়ে।

### Citizenship Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/polity/constitution-rights-sec/citizenship/
Summary: Practice citizenship questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: In which Part of the Indian Constitution are the provisions relating to citizenship found?
A: Part II (Articles 5 to 11).
Q: Which Articles of the Constitution deal with citizenship?
A: Articles 5 to 11.
Q: From which country's constitution did India adopt the idea of single citizenship?
A: Britain (British Constitution).
Q: What kind of citizenship does India provide?
A: Single citizenship.
Q: Which Article deals with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution (26 January 1950)?
A: Article 5.
Q: Which Articles deal with the citizenship of migrants to India from Pakistan?
A: Articles 6 and 7.
Q: Which Article deals with the citizenship of persons of Indian origin residing outside India?
A: Article 8.
Q: Which Article says that a person who voluntarily acquires the citizenship of a foreign state shall not be a citizen of India?
A: Article 9.
Q: Which Article deals with the continuance of the rights of citizenship?
A: Article 10.
Q: Which Article gives Parliament the power to regulate the right of citizenship by law?
A: Article 11.
Q: Which Act governs the acquisition and termination of citizenship in India?
A: The Citizenship Act, 1955.
Q: What are the five ways of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act, 1955?
A: By birth, by descent, by registration, by naturalisation, and by incorporation of territory.
Q: What are the three ways of losing citizenship under the Citizenship Act, 1955?
A: Renunciation, termination, and deprivation.
Q: When was the Citizenship Act first amended to restrict citizenship by birth?
A: In 1986.
Q: What condition did the 1986 amendment impose for citizenship by birth?
A: For those born on or after 1 July 1987, at least one parent must be an Indian citizen.
Q: What condition did the 2003 amendment impose for citizenship by birth?
A: For those born on or after 3 December 2004, both parents must be citizens, or one parent must be a citizen and the other not an illegal migrant.
Q: In which year was the Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) scheme introduced?
A: In 2005.
Q: Is OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) full citizenship of India?
A: No. OCIs cannot vote and cannot hold constitutional offices.
Q: Can an OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) holder vote in Indian elections?
A: No, OCI holders cannot vote.
Q: To which people does the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 grant citizenship?
A: Persecuted religious minorities - Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis and Christians - from Pakistan, Bangladesh and Afghanistan.
Q: What is the cut-off date fixed under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019?
A: 31 December 2014.
Q: How many religious communities are covered by the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019?
A: Six - Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis and Christians.
Q: From how many countries does the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 cover migrants?
A: Three - Pakistan, Bangladesh and Afghanistan.
Q: What cut-off date was fixed by the Assam Accord (1985) for the detection and deportation of foreigners?
A: 25 March 1971.
Q: Who supervised the updating of the National Register of Citizens (NRC) in Assam?
A: The Supreme Court of India.
Q: Is Citizenship - Indian Constitution (Bilingual English & Assamese) free to use on axomexam?
A: There is no payment involved in Citizenship - Indian Constitution (Bilingual English & Assamese). The complete set of 25 questions and its step-by-step explanations are open to every visitor, so you can practise without creating an account or paying a fee.
Q: Are the Citizenship - Indian Constitution (Bilingual English & Assamese) questions available in Assamese and English?
A: Yes — the content is fully bilingual. You can switch between Assamese and English at any point while working through Citizenship - Indian Constitution (Bilingual English & Assamese), which helps when a term is clearer in one language than the other.
Q: How many questions does Citizenship - Indian Constitution (Bilingual English & Assamese) include?
A: The Citizenship - Indian Constitution (Bilingual English & Assamese) set is expanded over time, so the number of questions keeps growing. At the moment you can work through about 25 questions here with full answers.
Q: What is meant by single citizenship in India?
A: Single citizenship means that a person is only a citizen of India and not separately a citizen of any state. This principle was borrowed from the British Constitution. Because of single citizenship, every Indian citizen enjoys the same fundamental rights and the same protection throughout the country, though some special provisions exist for certain states and regions under Articles 371 and 371A to 371J and the Sixth Schedule.
Q: What are the ways of acquiring Indian citizenship?
A: Under the Citizenship Act of 1955, citizenship can be acquired in five ways: by birth, by descent, by registration, by naturalisation and by incorporation of territory. Birth and descent depend on parentage, registration is available to persons of Indian origin and to spouses of citizens, naturalisation is granted to foreigners who fulfil residence and other conditions, and incorporation of territory applies when a new territory becomes part of India.
Q: Is an Overseas Citizen of India a citizen of India?
A: No. An Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card holder is not a citizen of India. The OCI scheme, introduced in 2005, gives persons of Indian origin who hold foreign citizenship a long-term visa and certain rights, but OCIs cannot vote, cannot contest elections and cannot hold constitutional posts such as that of the President, Vice-President, a judge of the Supreme Court or High Court, or a member of Parliament or a state legislature.
Q: Who is covered by the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019?
A: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 covers persecuted religious minorities belonging to six communities, namely Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis and Christians, who migrated to India on or before 31 December 2014 from Pakistan, Bangladesh and Afghanistan. It provides them with eligibility for citizenship subject to the conditions laid down in the Act and the rules framed under it.
Q: What is the importance of 25 March 1971 in Assam?
A: The Assam Accord of 1985 fixed 25 March 1971 as the cut-off date for the detection and deportation of foreigners in Assam. Persons who came to Assam before that date were to be treated in accordance with the Accord, while those who came after it were to be detected and deported. The National Register of Citizens in Assam was later updated under the supervision of the Supreme Court of India to give effect to this cut-off date.
Q: ভাৰতত একক নাগৰিকত্ব মানে কি?
A: একক নাগৰিকত্বৰ অৰ্থ হ'ল এজন ব্যক্তি কেৱল ভাৰতৰ নাগৰিক, কোনো ৰাজ্যৰ পৃথক নাগৰিক নহয়। এই নীতি ব্ৰিটিছ সংবিধানৰ পৰা লোৱা হৈছিল। একক নাগৰিকত্বৰ বাবে প্ৰতিজন ভাৰতীয় নাগৰিকে দেশজুৰি একেই মৌলিক অধিকাৰ আৰু একেই সুৰক্ষা ভোগ কৰে, যদিও অনুচ্ছেদ ৩৭১ তথা ৩৭১এ ৰ পৰা ৩৭১জে আৰু ষষ্ঠ অনুসূচীৰ অধীনত কিছুমান ৰাজ্য আৰু অঞ্চলৰ বাবে বিশেষ ব্যৱস্থা আছে।
Q: ভাৰতীয় নাগৰিকত্ব লাভৰ পদ্ধতিসমূহ কি কি?
A: ১৯৫৫ চনৰ নাগৰিকত্ব আইনৰ অধীনত পাঁচটা পদ্ধতিত নাগৰিকত্ব লাভ কৰিব পাৰি: জন্মৰ দ্বাৰা, বংশগতিৰ দ্বাৰা, পঞ্জীয়নৰ দ্বাৰা, স্বাভাৱিকীকৰণৰ দ্বাৰা আৰু ভূখণ্ড অন্তৰ্ভুক্তিৰ দ্বাৰা। জন্ম আৰু বংশগতি পিতৃ-মাতৃৰ ওপৰত নিৰ্ভৰ কৰে, পঞ্জীয়ন ভাৰতীয় মূলৰ ব্যক্তি আৰু নাগৰিকসকলৰ জীৱনসংগীৰ বাবে উপলব্ধ, স্বাভাৱিকীকৰণ বিদেশীসকলক বাসস্থান আদি চৰ্ত পূৰণ কৰিলে প্ৰদান কৰা হয়, আৰু কোনো নতুন ভূখণ্ড ভাৰতৰ অংশ হ'লে ভূখণ্ড অন্তৰ্ভুক্তি প্ৰযোজ্য হয়।
Q: বিদেশী ভাৰতীয় নাগৰিক (OCI) ভাৰতৰ নাগৰিক নেকি?
A: নহয়। এজন বিদেশী ভাৰতীয় নাগৰিক (OCI) কাৰ্ডধাৰী ভাৰতৰ নাগৰিক নহয়। ২০০৫ চনত প্ৰৱৰ্তিত OCI আঁচনিয়ে বিদেশী নাগৰিকত্ব থকা ভাৰতীয় মূলৰ ব্যক্তিসকলক দীৰ্ঘম্যাদী ভিছা আৰু কিছুমান অধিকাৰ দিয়ে, কিন্তু OCI সকলে ভোট দিব নোৱাৰে, নিৰ্বাচনত প্ৰতিদ্বন্দ্বিতা কৰিব নোৱাৰে, আৰু ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতি, উপ-ৰাষ্ট্ৰপতি, উচ্চতম ন্যায়ালয় বা উচ্চ ন্যায়ালয়ৰ ন্যায়াধীশ, বা সংসদ বা ৰাজ্যিক বিধানমণ্ডলৰ সদস্যৰ দৰে সাংবিধানিক পদত অধিষ্ঠিত হ'ব নোৱাৰে।
Q: ২০১৯ চনৰ নাগৰিকত্ব (সংশোধনী) আইনৰ দ্বাৰা কোনসকল সামৰি লোৱা হৈছে?
A: ২০১৯ চনৰ নাগৰিকত্ব (সংশোধনী) আইনে ছটা সম্প্ৰদায়ৰ নিপীড়িত ধৰ্মীয় সংখ্যালঘুসকলক, অৰ্থাৎ হিন্দু, শিখ, বৌদ্ধ, জৈন, পাৰ্চী আৰু খ্ৰীষ্টানসকলক সামৰি লৈছে, যিসকলে ৩১ ডিচেম্বৰ ২০১৪ বা তাত আগতে পাকিস্তান, বাংলাদেশ আৰু আফগানিস্তানৰ পৰা ভাৰতলৈ প্ৰব্ৰজন কৰিছে। আইনখনত আৰু ইয়াৰ অধীনত প্ৰণীত নিয়মাৱলীত নিৰ্ধাৰিত চৰ্ত পূৰণ কৰিলে ই তেওঁলোকক নাগৰিকত্বৰ অৰ্হতা প্ৰদান কৰে।
Q: অসমত ২৫ মাৰ্চ ১৯৭১ ৰ গুৰুত্ব কি?
A: ১৯৮৫ চনৰ অসম চুক্তিয়ে অসমত বিদেশী চিনাক্ত আৰু বহিষ্কাৰৰ বাবে ২৫ মাৰ্চ ১৯৭১ক শেষ তাৰিখ হিচাপে নিৰ্ধাৰণ কৰিছিল। সেই তাৰিখৰ আগতে অসমলৈ অহা ব্যক্তিসকলক চুক্তি অনুসৰি ব্যৱহাৰ কৰিব লাগিছিল, আনহাতে তাৰ পিছত অহাসকলক চিনাক্ত কৰি বহিষ্কাৰ কৰিব লাগিছিল। পিছত এই শেষ তাৰিখ কাৰ্যকৰী কৰিবলৈ অসমৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় নাগৰিক পঞ্জী ভাৰতৰ উচ্চতম ন্যায়ালয়ৰ অধীক্ষণত অধিকালিক কৰা হৈছিল।

### Directive Principles & Fundamental Duties — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/polity/constitution-rights-sec/directive-principles-fundamental-duties/
Summary: Practice directive principles & fundamental duties questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: In which Part of the Constitution are the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) contained?
A: Part IV, Articles 36 to 51.
Q: From the Constitution of which country were the DPSP borrowed?
A: Ireland.
Q: Are the DPSP enforceable in a court of law?
A: No, they are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts).
Q: Under Article 37, what is said about the DPSP?
A: They are 'fundamental in the governance of the country' and the State shall apply them while making laws.
Q: By what name are the DPSP often called?
A: 'Instrument of instructions' or 'a cheque on a bank payable at the convenience of the bank'.
Q: How are the DPSP classified?
A: Into Socialist Principles, Gandhian Principles, and Liberal-Intellectual Principles.
Q: Which Article deals with the welfare state and a just social order?
A: Article 38.
Q: Which Article provides for 'equal pay for equal work' for both men and women?
A: Article 39.
Q: Which Article provides for free legal aid to the poor?
A: Article 39A.
Q: Which Article provides for the organisation of village panchayats?
A: Article 40 (a Gandhian principle).
Q: Which Article deals with securing a living wage for workers?
A: Article 43.
Q: Which Article provides for the participation of workers in the management of industries?
A: Article 43A.
Q: Which Article deals with the Uniform Civil Code?
A: Article 44.
Q: Which Article provides for early childhood care and education of children below the age of 6 years?
A: Article 45 (as amended by the 86th Amendment).
Q: Which Article promotes the educational and economic interests of the SCs, STs and weaker sections?
A: Article 46.
Q: Which Article provides for the prohibition of intoxicating drinks?
A: Article 47.
Q: Which Article provides for the prohibition of the slaughter of cows and improvement of animal husbandry?
A: Article 48.
Q: Which Article deals with the protection and improvement of the environment?
A: Article 48A (added by the 42nd Amendment).
Q: Which Article provides for the separation of the judiciary from the executive?
A: Article 50.
Q: Which Article promotes international peace and security?
A: Article 51.
Q: What did the Supreme Court hold in the Minerva Mills case regarding the DPSP and Fundamental Rights?
A: Both are equally important and must be balanced; both form part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
Q: By which Constitutional Amendment Act were the Fundamental Duties added?
A: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.
Q: On whose recommendation were the Fundamental Duties added to the Constitution?
A: The Swaran Singh Committee.
Q: In which Part and Article are the Fundamental Duties contained?
A: Part IVA, Article 51A.
Q: Which Amendment added the 11th Fundamental Duty, and what is that duty?
A: The 86th Amendment (2002) - the duty of a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between 6 and 14 years.
Q: Is Directive Principles & Fundamental Duties (Bilingual English & Assamese) free to use on axomexam?
A: Directive Principles & Fundamental Duties (Bilingual English & Assamese) is completely free. You can read all 25 questions and their explanations on axomexam.in with no registration or charge, which makes it easy to revise the same set more than once.
Q: Are the Directive Principles & Fundamental Duties (Bilingual English & Assamese) questions available in Assamese and English?
A: Yes. Directive Principles & Fundamental Duties (Bilingual English & Assamese) is bilingual: the question, every option and the full explanation are given in both Assamese and English, so you can read the problem in one language and the solution in the other.
Q: How many questions does Directive Principles & Fundamental Duties (Bilingual English & Assamese) include?
A: At present Directive Principles & Fundamental Duties (Bilingual English & Assamese) has 25 questions. They are arranged for practice and revision — attempt them once, study the explanations, then re-attempt after a few days to check what you remember.
Q: Why are the Directive Principles not enforceable in a court of law?
A: The Directive Principles are not enforceable because they depend on the financial and administrative capacity of the State and are meant to be implemented gradually. Article 37 makes it clear that they are not enforceable by any court, yet declares that they are fundamental in the governance of the country and that the State shall apply them while making laws. They guide policy and legislation rather than create directly enforceable rights.
Q: What is the difference between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles?
A: Fundamental Rights are justiciable and can be enforced in the courts; they are mainly negative in character, restraining the State from interfering with individual freedom. Directive Principles are non-justiciable; they are positive in character, directing the State to take steps to promote social and economic welfare. Fundamental Rights are contained in Part III, while Directive Principles are in Part IV. In the Minerva Mills case the Supreme Court held that both are equally important and must be balanced.
Q: Which amendment and committee are connected with Fundamental Duties?
A: Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. They are contained in Part IVA, Article 51A. The 86th Amendment of 2002 added the eleventh duty relating to the education of children between six and fourteen years. The duties are not directly enforceable, but courts may consider them while interpreting laws.
Q: What is the importance of Article 39A?
A: Article 39A, inserted by the 42nd Amendment, directs the State to secure equal justice and free legal aid. It asks the State to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen because of economic or other disabilities, and to provide free legal aid so that the poor can approach the courts. This principle led to the establishment of legal services authorities and Lok Adalats.
Q: What did the Supreme Court decide in the Minerva Mills case?
A: In the Minerva Mills case (1980) the Supreme Court held that the Fundamental Rights and the Directive Principles of State Policy are equally important and that a balance between them is a part of the basic structure of the Constitution. The Court struck down provisions of the 42nd Amendment that gave the Directive Principles primacy over Fundamental Rights, holding that the harmony between the two must not be destroyed.
Q: নিৰ্দেশাত্মক সূত্ৰসমূহ ন্যায়ালয়ত বলবৎযোগ্য নহয় কিয়?
A: নিৰ্দেশাত্মক সূত্ৰসমূহ বলবৎযোগ্য নহয় কাৰণ এইবোৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰৰ আৰ্থিক আৰু প্ৰশাসনিক সামৰ্থ্যৰ ওপৰত নিৰ্ভৰশীল আৰু ক্ৰমে কাৰ্যকৰী কৰাৰ উদ্দেশ্যে ৰখা হৈছে। অনুচ্ছেদ ৩৭য়ে স্পষ্ট কৰি দিয়ে যে এইবোৰ কোনো ন্যায়ালয়ে বলবৎ কৰিব নোৱাৰে, তথাপি ঘোষণা কৰে যে এইবোৰ দেশৰ শাসনত মৌলিক আৰু ৰাষ্ট্ৰই আইন প্ৰণয়নৰ সময়ত এইবোৰ প্ৰয়োগ কৰিব। এইবোৰে প্ৰত্যক্ষভাৱে বলবৎযোগ্য অধিকাৰ সৃষ্টি নকৰি নীতি আৰু আইন প্ৰণয়নক পথ দেখুৱায়।
Q: মৌলিক অধিকাৰ আৰু নিৰ্দেশাত্মক সূত্ৰৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: মৌলিক অধিকাৰ ন্যায়যোগ্য আৰু ন্যায়ালয়ত বলবৎ কৰিব পাৰি; ই মূলতঃ নেতিবাচক প্ৰকৃতিৰ, যি ৰাষ্ট্ৰক ব্যক্তিৰ স্বাধীনতাত হস্তক্ষেপ কৰাৰ পৰা বিৰত ৰাখে। নিৰ্দেশাত্মক সূত্ৰ অন্যায়যোগ্য; ই ধনাত্মক প্ৰকৃতিৰ, যি ৰাষ্ট্ৰক সামাজিক তথা অৰ্থনৈতিক কল্যাণ প্ৰসাৰৰ পদক্ষেপ লবলৈ নিৰ্দেশ দিয়ে। মৌলিক অধিকাৰ তৃতীয় অংশত আৰু নিৰ্দেশাত্মক সূত্ৰ চতুৰ্থ অংশত আছে। মিনাৰ্ভা মিলছ গোচৰত উচ্চতম ন্যায়ালয়ে কৈছিল যে দুয়োটা সমানভাৱে গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ আৰু ভাৰসাম্য ৰক্ষা কৰিব লাগিব।
Q: মৌলিক কৰ্তব্যৰ সৈতে কোন সংশোধনী আৰু সমিতি জড়িত?
A: স্বৰণ সিং সমিতিৰ পৰামৰ্শত ১৯৭৬ চনৰ ৪২ সংখ্যক সাংবিধানিক সংশোধনী আইনে মৌলিক কৰ্তব্য যোগ কৰিছিল। এইবোৰ চতুৰ্থ-ক অংশ, অনুচ্ছেদ ৫১এত সন্নিবিষ্ট। ২০০২ চনৰ ৮৬ সংখ্যক সংশোধনীয়ে ছয়ৰ পৰা চৈধ্য বছৰৰ শিশুৰ শিক্ষাৰ সৈতে জড়িত এঘাৰ সংখ্যক কৰ্তব্য যোগ কৰিছিল। কৰ্তব্যসমূহ প্ৰত্যক্ষভাৱে বলবৎযোগ্য নহয়, কিন্তু ন্যায়ালয়ে আইনৰ ব্যাখ্যাৰ সময়ত ইয়াক বিবেচনাত লব পাৰে।
Q: অনুচ্ছেদ ৩৯এ ৰ গুৰুত্ব কি?
A: ৪২ সংখ্যক সংশোধনীয়ে সন্নিবিষ্ট অনুচ্ছেদ ৩৯এয়ে ৰাষ্ট্ৰক সমান ন্যায় আৰু বিনামূলীয়া আইনী সহায় নিশ্চিত কৰিবলৈ নিৰ্দেশ দিয়ে। ই ৰাষ্ট্ৰক নিৰ্দেশ দিয়ে যে অৰ্থনৈতিক বা অন্য অক্ষমতাৰ বাবে কোনো নাগৰিকক ন্যায় লাভৰ সুযোগৰ পৰা বঞ্চিত কৰা নহ'ব, আৰু দৰিদ্ৰসকলে ন্যায়ালয়ত যাব পৰাকৈ বিনামূলীয়া আইনী সহায় প্ৰদান কৰিব। এই নীতিয়ে আইনী সেৱা কৰ্তৃপক্ষ আৰু লোক আদালতসমূহৰ প্ৰতিষ্ঠালৈ লৈ গৈছিল।
Q: মিনাৰ্ভা মিলছ গোচৰত উচ্চতম ন্যায়ালয়ে কি সিদ্ধান্ত লৈছিল?
A: মিনাৰ্ভা মিলছ গোচৰ (১৯৮০)ত উচ্চতম ন্যায়ালয়ে কৈছিল যে মৌলিক অধিকাৰ আৰু ৰাষ্ট্ৰৰ নীতি নিৰ্দেশাত্মক সূত্ৰ সমানভাৱে গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ আৰু ইয়াৰ মাজত ভাৰসাম্য সংবিধানৰ মৌলিক গাঁথনিৰ এটা অংশ। ন্যায়ালয়ে ৪২ সংখ্যক সংশোধনীৰ সেইবোৰ বিধান বাতিল কৰিছিল যিয়ে নিৰ্দেশাত্মক সূত্ৰসমূহক মৌলিক অধিকাৰতকৈ শ্ৰেষ্ঠত্ব দিছিল, আৰু কৈছিল যে দুয়োটাৰ মাজৰ সমন্বয় নষ্ট কৰিব নালাগে।

### Fundamental Rights Questions with Answers — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/polity/constitution-rights-sec/fundamental-rights/
Summary: Practice fundamental rights questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no sign-up.
Q: In which part of the Indian Constitution are the Fundamental Rights contained?
A: Part III (Articles 12 to 35).
Q: Which Article defines the 'State' for the purpose of Fundamental Rights?
A: Article 12.
Q: According to Article 13, what happens to any law inconsistent with Fundamental Rights?
A: It is void (judicial review).
Q: How many Fundamental Rights are there in the Indian Constitution?
A: Six.
Q: Which Articles deal with the Right to Equality?
A: Articles 14 to 18.
Q: Which Article guarantees equality before law and equal protection of laws?
A: Article 14.
Q: Which Article prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth?
A: Article 15.
Q: Which Article provides equality of opportunity in matters of public employment?
A: Article 16.
Q: Which Article abolishes untouchability?
A: Article 17.
Q: Which Article abolishes titles, except military and academic distinctions?
A: Article 18.
Q: Which Article guarantees the six freedoms of speech, assembly, association, movement, residence and profession?
A: Article 19.
Q: Which Articles deal with the Right to Freedom?
A: Articles 19 to 22.
Q: Which Article provides protection of life and personal liberty?
A: Article 21.
Q: Which Article provides the right to elementary education to children?
A: Article 21A.
Q: Which Article provides protection against arrest and detention in certain cases?
A: Article 22.
Q: Which Articles deal with the Right against Exploitation?
A: Articles 23 and 24.
Q: Which Article prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour?
A: Article 23.
Q: Up to what age does Article 24 prohibit employment of children in hazardous industries?
A: Children below 14 years of age.
Q: Which Articles deal with the Right to Freedom of Religion?
A: Articles 25 to 28.
Q: Which Articles deal with Cultural and Educational Rights?
A: Articles 29 and 30.
Q: Which Article provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies?
A: Article 32.
Q: Who called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
A: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
Q: Which writ is issued to produce a person unlawfully detained before the court?
A: Habeas Corpus.
Q: Which Amendment removed the Right to Property as a Fundamental Right, and under which Article is it now a legal right?
A: The 44th Amendment (1978); now under Article 300A.
Q: During a National Emergency, which two Fundamental Rights are never suspended?
A: Articles 20 and 21.
Q: Is Fundamental Rights - Indian Constitution (Bilingual English & Assamese) free to use on axomexam?
A: Yes. Fundamental Rights - Indian Constitution (Bilingual English & Assamese) is free to use on axomexam.in — there is no login, subscription or hidden charge. All 25 questions come with worked explanations, and you can re-attempt the set as often as you like.
Q: Are the Fundamental Rights - Indian Constitution (Bilingual English & Assamese) questions available in Assamese and English?
A: Every item in Fundamental Rights - Indian Constitution (Bilingual English & Assamese) appears in Assamese and English. That covers all 25 questions, including the options and explanations, so the same idea is reinforced in whichever language you find easier.
Q: How many questions does Fundamental Rights - Indian Constitution (Bilingual English & Assamese) include?
A: At present Fundamental Rights - Indian Constitution (Bilingual English & Assamese) has 25 questions. They are arranged for practice and revision — attempt them once, study the explanations, then re-attempt after a few days to check what you remember.
Q: What is the importance of Article 32?
A: Article 32 gives a person the right to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar called it the heart and soul of the Constitution because without a remedy a right has little value. Under Article 32 the Supreme Court can issue writs such as habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and quo warranto. A similar power is given to the High Courts under Article 226.
Q: Why was the Right to Property removed from the Fundamental Rights?
A: The Right to Property created difficulties for land reform and social welfare legislation, because laws meant to redistribute land were frequently challenged as violations of the right. To remove this obstacle, the 44th Amendment Act of 1978 removed the Right to Property from Part III. It was retained as a legal right under Article 300A, so a person can still not be deprived of property except by authority of law, but the right can be regulated by ordinary legislation.
Q: Which Fundamental Rights cannot be suspended during an emergency?
A: The rights guaranteed by Article 20 (protection in respect of conviction for offences) and Article 21 (protection of life and personal liberty) can never be suspended, even during a National Emergency. This protection was strengthened after the 44th Amendment. Other Fundamental Rights may be affected during an emergency, and the right to move the courts may be suspended under Article 359, but Articles 20 and 21 always remain in force.
Q: What is the difference between Article 14 and Article 15?
A: Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and the equal protection of the laws to all persons within the territory of India. Article 15 is more specific: it prohibits discrimination by the State on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth. Article 15 also permits special provisions for women, children, and socially and educationally backward classes, including the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Q: What does Article 12 mean by the State?
A: For the purpose of Part III, the State includes the Government and Parliament of India, the Government and legislature of each state, all local authorities such as municipalities and panchayats, and other authorities within the territory of India or under the control of the Government of India. The courts have interpreted other authorities to include statutory bodies and, in many cases, bodies performing public functions. Fundamental Rights can generally be claimed against the State as defined in Article 12.
Q: অনুচ্ছেদ ৩২ ৰ গুৰুত্ব কি?
A: অনুচ্ছেদ ৩২য়ে ব্যক্তিক মৌলিক অধিকাৰ বলবৎ কৰিবলৈ উচ্চতম ন্যায়ালয়ত পোনপটীয়াকৈ আবেদন কৰাৰ অধিকাৰ দিয়ে। ডাঃ বি. আৰ. আম্বেদকৰে ইয়াক সংবিধানৰ হৃদয় আৰু আত্মা বুলি কৈছিল কাৰণ প্ৰতিকাৰ নহ'লে অধিকাৰৰ মূল্য কম। অনুচ্ছেদ ৩২ ৰ অধীনত উচ্চতম ন্যায়ালয়ে হেবিয়াছ কৰ্পাছ, মেণ্ডামাছ, প্ৰহিবিচন, ছাৰ্ছিঅৰাৰি আৰু কু ৱাৰেণ্টোৰ দৰে ৰিট জাৰি কৰিব পাৰে। অনুচ্ছেদ ২২৬ ৰ অধীনত উচ্চ ন্যায়ালয়সমূহকো একেধৰণৰ ক্ষমতা দিয়া হৈছে।
Q: সম্পত্তিৰ অধিকাৰ মৌলিক অধিকাৰৰ পৰা কিয় আঁতৰোৱা হৈছিল?
A: সম্পত্তিৰ অধিকাৰে ভূমি সংস্কাৰ আৰু সমাজকল্যাণমূলক আইনত অসুবিধা সৃষ্টি কৰিছিল, কাৰণ ভূমি পুনৰ্বিতৰণৰ আইনসমূহক এই অধিকাৰৰ উলংঘা বুলি বাৰে বাৰে প্ৰত্যাহ্বান জনোৱা হৈছিল। এই বাধা আঁতৰাবলৈ ১৯৭৮ চনৰ ৪৪ সংখ্যক সংশোধনী আইনে সম্পত্তিৰ অধিকাৰ তৃতীয় অংশৰ পৰা আঁতৰাইছিল। ইয়াক অনুচ্ছেদ ৩০০এৰ অধীনত এটা আইনগত অধিকাৰ হিচাপে ৰখা হৈছিল, সেয়ে আইনৰ কৰ্তৃত্বৰ বাহিৰে কোনো ব্যক্তিক সম্পত্তিৰ পৰা বঞ্চিত কৰিব নোৱাৰি, কিন্তু ইয়াক সাধাৰণ আইনৰ দ্বাৰা নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ কৰিব পাৰি।
Q: কোনবোৰ মৌলিক অধিকাৰ জৰুৰীকালীন অৱস্থাত স্থগিত কৰিব নোৱাৰি?
A: অনুচ্ছেদ ২০ (অপৰাধৰ সিদ্ধান্তৰ সন্দৰ্ভত সুৰক্ষা) আৰু অনুচ্ছেদ ২১ (জীৱন আৰু ব্যক্তিগত স্বাধীনতাৰ সুৰক্ষা)ৰ অধীনৰ অধিকাৰসমূহ ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় জৰুৰীকালীন অৱস্থাতো কেতিয়াও স্থগিত কৰিব নোৱাৰি। ৪৪ সংখ্যক সংশোধনীৰ পিছত এই সুৰক্ষা আৰু সবল হৈছিল। অন্য মৌলিক অধিকাৰ জৰুৰীকালীন অৱস্থাত প্ৰভাৱিত হ'ব পাৰে, আৰু অনুচ্ছেদ ৩৫৯ ৰ অধীনত ন্যায়ালয়ত যোৱাৰ অধিকাৰ স্থগিত কৰিব পাৰি, কিন্তু অনুচ্ছেদ ২০ আৰু ২১ সদায় বলবৎ থাকে।
Q: অনুচ্ছেদ ১৪ আৰু অনুচ্ছেদ ১৫ ৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি?
A: অনুচ্ছেদ ১৪য়ে ভাৰতৰ ভূখণ্ডত থকা সকলো ব্যক্তিক আইনৰ আগত সমতা আৰু আইনৰ সমান সুৰক্ষা নিশ্চিত কৰে। অনুচ্ছেদ ১৫ অধিক নিৰ্দিষ্ট: ই ৰাষ্ট্ৰক ধৰ্ম, বৰ্ণ, জাতি, লিংগ বা জন্মস্থানৰ ভিত্তিত বৈষম্য কৰিবলৈ নিষেধ কৰে। অনুচ্ছেদ ১৫য়ে মহিলা, শিশু আৰু সামাজিক তথা শিক্ষামূলকভাৱে পিছপৰা শ্ৰেণী, যেনে অনুসূচিত জাতি আৰু অনুসূচিত জনজাতিৰ বাবে বিশেষ ব্যৱস্থাৰ অনুমতি দিয়ে।
Q: অনুচ্ছেদ ১২ ৰ ৰাষ্ট্ৰ মানে কি?
A: তৃতীয় অংশৰ উদ্দেশ্যে ৰাষ্ট্ৰৰ অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত: ভাৰতৰ চৰকাৰ আৰু সংসদ, প্ৰতিখন ৰাজ্যৰ চৰকাৰ আৰু বিধানমণ্ডল, পৌৰসভা আৰু পঞ্চায়তৰ দৰে সকলো স্থানীয় কৰ্তৃপক্ষ, আৰু ভাৰতৰ ভূখণ্ডত থকা বা ভাৰত চৰকাৰৰ নিয়ন্ত্ৰণত থকা অন্য কৰ্তৃপক্ষ। ন্যায়ালয়সমূহে অন্য কৰ্তৃপক্ষৰ ভিতৰত বিধিবদ্ধ সংস্থা আৰু বহু ক্ষেত্ৰত ৰাজহুৱা কাৰ্য সম্পাদন কৰা সংস্থাসমূহক অন্তৰ্ভুক্ত কৰি ব্যাখ্যা কৰিছে। মৌলিক অধিকাৰ সাধাৰণতে অনুচ্ছেদ ১২ ত সংজ্ঞায়িত ৰাষ্ট্ৰৰ বিৰুদ্ধে দাবী কৰিব পাৰি।
Q: অনুচ্ছেদ ১৭ আৰু ১৮ ৰ বিষয় কি?
A: অনুচ্ছেদ ১৭য়ে অস্পৃশ্যতা বিলোপ কৰে আৰু ইয়াৰ যিকোনো ৰূপৰ প্ৰচলন নিষিদ্ধ কৰে; ইয়াক বলবৎ কৰিবলৈ সংসদে অস্পৃশ্যতা (অপৰাধ) আইন, ১৯৫৫ গ্ৰহণ কৰিছিল। অনুচ্ছেদ ১৮য়ে সামৰিক তথা শিক্ষামূলক উপাধিৰ বাহিৰে আন উপাধি বিলোপ কৰে, যাতে সামাজিক মৰ্যাদাৰ ভিত্তিত বৈষম্য সৃষ্টি নহয়। দুয়োটা অনুচ্ছেদ সমতাৰ অধিকাৰৰ অংশ।

### Historical Background, Making & Sources — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/polity/constitution-rights-sec/historical-background-making-sources/
Summary: Practice historical background, making & sources questions with step-by-step answers and explanations for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police. Free, bilingual, no.
Q: Under which plan was the Constituent Assembly of India formed?
A: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan, 1946.
Q: When was the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly held?
A: On 9 December 1946.
Q: Who first put forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India?
A: M.N. Roy, in 1934.
Q: Who was the President of the Constituent Assembly?
A: Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
Q: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
A: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
Q: How many members were there in the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
A: 7 members.
Q: Who moved the Objective Resolution in the Constituent Assembly and on which date?
A: Jawaharlal Nehru, on 13 December 1946.
Q: How much time did the Constituent Assembly take to frame the Indian Constitution?
A: 2 years, 11 months and 18 days.
Q: On which date was the Indian Constitution adopted?
A: On 26 November 1949.
Q: From which date did the Indian Constitution come into force?
A: From 26 January 1950.
Q: True or false: The Indian Constitution came into force on 26 November 1949.
A: False. It was adopted on 26 November 1949, but came into force on 26 January 1950.
Q: When was the draft Constitution submitted to the Constituent Assembly?
A: On 4 November 1948.
Q: Who was the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly?
A: B.N. Rau.
Q: Why is the Indian Constitution called the longest written constitution and a 'bag of borrowings'?
A: Because it is the lengthiest written constitution in the world and has borrowed features from many constitutions of different countries.
Q: Which Act is the biggest source of the Indian Constitution?
A: The Government of India Act, 1935.
Q: Which features have been borrowed from the British Constitution?
A: Parliamentary system, rule of law, single citizenship, cabinet system, writs and legislative procedure.
Q: Which features have been borrowed from the US Constitution?
A: Fundamental Rights, independent judiciary, judicial review, impeachment of the President, removal of judges and the post of Vice-President.
Q: Which features have been borrowed from the Irish Constitution?
A: Directive Principles of State Policy, method of election of the President and nomination of members of the Rajya Sabha.
Q: Which features have been borrowed from the Canadian Constitution?
A: A strong centre in the federation, residuary powers with the Centre, appointment of state governors and advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
Q: Which features have been borrowed from the Australian Constitution?
A: The Concurrent List, freedom of trade and commerce and joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament.
Q: From which constitution has the suspension of Fundamental Rights during emergency been borrowed?
A: From the German (Weimar) Constitution.
Q: From which constitution have the Fundamental Duties been borrowed?
A: From the Soviet (USSR) Constitution.
Q: From which constitution have the ideals of liberty, equality and fraternity been borrowed?
A: From the French Constitution.
Q: From which constitution has the procedure of amendment been borrowed?
A: From the South African Constitution.
Q: How is India described in the Preamble of the Constitution?
A: As a 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic'.
