Q: Pen is to Ink as Car is to?
A: Fuel — A pen runs on ink and a car runs on fuel, so the answer is Fuel.
Q: Find the odd one out: 6, 12, 18, 25, 30
A: 25 — 6, 12, 18 and 30 are multiples of 6, while 25 is not, so 25 is the odd one.
Q: Find the next number: 7, 14, 28, 56, ?
A: 112 — Each term is double the previous term, so the next term is 56 x 2 = 112.
Q: If A=1, B=2, ..., Z=26, what is the value of CAB?
A: 6 — C=3, A=1 and B=2, so CAB = 3 + 1 + 2 = 6.
Q: My father's wife is my?
A: Mother — The wife of one's father is one's mother, so the answer is Mother.
Q: A man facing south turns right twice. Which direction is he facing now?
A: North — Facing south, the first right turn makes him face west and the second right turn makes him face north.
Q: In a row of 25 students, B is 9th from the right. What is his position from the left?
A: 17th — Position from the left = total - position from the right + 1 = 25 - 9 + 1 = 17th.
Q: Some doctors are teachers. All teachers are graduates. Which conclusion follows?
A: Some doctors are graduates — The doctors who are teachers are also graduates, so some doctors are graduates.
Q: If 15th August 2024 was Thursday, what day was 15th September 2024?
A: Sunday — August has 31 days and 31 divided by 7 leaves 3, so the day moves three days ahead of Thursday, which is Sunday.
Q: Sailor is to Ship as Pilot is to?
A: Aeroplane — A sailor operates a ship and a pilot operates an aeroplane, so the answer is Aeroplane.
Q: Find the odd one: Circle, Triangle, Square, Sphere
A: Sphere — Circle, triangle and square are two-dimensional figures, while a sphere is a three-dimensional solid, so Sphere is the odd one.
Q: Complete the series: AB, CD, EF, ?
A: GH — Each pair uses consecutive letters and the next pair starts after the previous pair, so after EF comes GH.
Q: A is 24 years old and B is 6 years old. In how many years will A be twice as old as B?
A: 12 years — Let x be the number of years: 24 + x = 2(6 + x), which gives x = 12 years.
Q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 9:00?
A: 90 degrees — At 9:00 the hour hand is on 9 and the minute hand is on 12, so the angle is 3 x 30 = 90 degrees.
Q: Find the odd one: 15, 21, 27, 32
A: 32 — 15, 21 and 27 are divisible by 3, while 32 is not, so 32 is the odd one.
Q: A man walks 8 km east and then 6 km north. How far is he from the starting point?
A: 10 km — The path forms a right-angled triangle with sides 8 and 6, so the distance is the square root of (64 + 36) = 10 km.
Q: How many meaningful English words can be formed with the letters S, U, N using each letter once?
A: One — Using S, U and N once each, only the word SUN can be formed, so the answer is One.
Q: Bird is to Wings as Fish is to?
A: Fins — A bird uses wings to move and a fish uses fins to move, so the answer is Fins.
Q: Find the next number: 1, 4, 9, 16, ?
A: 25 — The terms are the squares of 1, 2, 3 and 4, so the next term is 5 squared = 25.
Q: My brother's wife is my?
A: Sister-in-law — The wife of one's brother is one's sister-in-law, so the answer is Sister-in-law.
Q: Find the odd one: Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Nepal
A: Nepal — Delhi, Mumbai and Kolkata are cities in India, while Nepal is a country, so Nepal is the odd one.
Q: All mangoes are sweet. Which conclusion definitely follows?
A: Some sweet things are mangoes — Since all mangoes are sweet, mangoes form a part of sweet things, so some sweet things are mangoes.
Q: In a row of 15 students, C is 5th from the left. What is his position from the right?
A: 11th — Position from the right = total - position from the left + 1 = 15 - 5 + 1 = 11th.
Q: If East is called North, North is called West, West is called South and South is called East, what is the direction opposite to the actual East called?
A: South — The direction opposite to the actual east is west, and in this naming scheme west is called south, so the answer is South.

A: 160 — Each term is double the previous term, so the next term is 80 x 2 = 160.

A: Grandfather — The father of one's mother is one's maternal grandfather, so the answer is Grandfather.

A: East — Facing west, the first left turn makes him face south and the second left turn makes him face east.

A: 31st — Rank from the bottom = total - rank from the top + 1 = 50 - 20 + 1 = 31st.

A: None of these — The wild animals may or may not include cats, so none of the given conclusions definitely follows.

A: Monday — From 1 January to 1 April 2024 there are 31 + 29 + 31 = 91 days, and 91 is divisible by 7, so 1 April was also a Monday.

A: Date — A watch shows time and a calendar shows dates, so the answer is Date.

A: R — Each letter moves two steps backward in the alphabet (Z, X, V, T), so the next letter is R.
Q: The sum of the ages of a father and his son is 50 years, and the father is 4 times as old as the son. What is the son's age?
A: 10 years — Let the son's age be x; then x + 4x = 50, so 5x = 50 and x = 10 years.
Q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 12:00?
A: 0 degrees — At 12:00 both hands point to 12, so they overlap and the angle between them is 0 degrees.
Q: Find the odd one: 5, 10, 15, 22
A: 22 — 5, 10 and 15 are multiples of 5, while 22 is not, so 22 is the odd one.
Q: A man walks 4 km north, then 3 km west, then 4 km south. Where is he from the starting point?
A: 3 km west — The 4 km north and 4 km south cancel out, leaving only the 3 km westward movement, so he is 3 km west of the start.
Q: How many meaningful English words can be formed with the letters T, O, N using each letter once?
A: Two — Using T, O and N once each, the words NOT and TON can be formed, i.e. two words.

A: Hammer — A stethoscope is the tool of a doctor and a hammer is the tool of a carpenter, so the answer is Hammer.

A: All pencils are useful — All pencils are instruments and all instruments are useful, so all pencils are useful.

A: 17th — Position from the left = total - position from the right + 1 = 30 - 14 + 1 = 17th.
Q: A man walks 2 km east, turns left and walks 2 km, then turns left again and walks 2 km. Where is he from the starting point?
A: 2 km north — He goes 2 km east, then 2 km north, then 2 km west; the east and west movements cancel, leaving him 2 km north of the start.

### Physics Mock Test Set 1 — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/mock-test/science/physics/set-1/
Summary: Take free timed physics mock test set 1 with 25 bilingual questions, instant scoring and answers. Practice for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police.
Q: What is the SI unit of force?
A: Newton — The SI unit of force is the newton (N). From Newton's second law, F = ma, so 1 N = 1 kg·m/s².
Q: The SI unit of work is?
A: Joule — Work is the product of force and displacement (W = F·d), and its SI unit is the joule (J), where 1 J = 1 N·m.
Q: Speed of light in vacuum is approximately?
A: 3 × 10^8 m/s — Light travels in vacuum at approximately 3 × 10^8 m/s, a fundamental constant denoted by c.
Q: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
A: Mass — Mass is a scalar quantity because it has only magnitude and no direction. Force, velocity and acceleration are vectors.
Q: Newton's first law of motion is also known as?
A: Law of inertia — Newton's first law states that a body remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by a net external force; this property is inertia, so it is called the law of inertia.
Q: The acceleration due to gravity on Earth is approximately?
A: 9.8 m/s² — The acceleration due to gravity near the Earth's surface is approximately 9.8 m/s².
Q: Which instrument is used to measure atmospheric pressure?
A: Barometer — A barometer measures atmospheric pressure by balancing it against a column of mercury.
Q: Sound cannot travel through?
A: Vacuum — Sound is a mechanical wave and needs a material medium to propagate; therefore it cannot travel through a vacuum.
Q: The SI unit of electric current is?
A: Ampere — The SI unit of electric current is the ampere (A), defined as the flow of one coulomb of charge per second.
Q: Ohm's law is?
A: V = IR — Ohm's law states that the current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across it, V = IR, where R is resistance.
Q: The device used to measure electric current is?
A: Ammeter — An ammeter measures electric current and is connected in series in a circuit.
Q: Which mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
A: Convex mirror — A convex mirror is used as a rear-view mirror because it always forms an erect, diminished image and gives a wider field of view.
Q: The phenomenon of splitting of white light into seven colours is called?
A: Dispersion — The splitting of white light into its seven constituent colours when passing through a prism is called dispersion.
Q: The primary colours of light are?
A: Red, green, blue — The primary additive colours of light are red, green and blue; their combination produces white light.
Q: Heat is a form of?
A: Energy — Heat is a form of energy, specifically the energy transferred between bodies due to a temperature difference.
Q: The boiling point of water at standard pressure is?
A: 100°C — At standard atmospheric pressure (1 atm), pure water boils at 100°C.
Q: The SI unit of power is?
A: Watt — Power is the rate of doing work, P = W/t, and its SI unit is the watt (W); 1 W = 1 J/s.
Q: A freely falling body has which acceleration?
A: g (acceleration due to gravity) — Ignoring air resistance, a freely falling body is acted upon only by gravity, so its acceleration is g, the acceleration due to gravity.
Q: Frequency of a sound wave is measured in?
A: Hertz — Frequency is the number of vibrations per second, measured in hertz (Hz); 1 Hz = 1 cycle per second.
Q: Which of the following is a good conductor of electricity?
A: Copper — Copper is a good conductor of electricity because it has free electrons; rubber, glass and wood are insulators.
Q: The nucleus of an atom contains?
A: Protons and neutrons — The nucleus of an atom contains protons and neutrons (together called nucleons), while electrons revolve around it.
Q: X-rays were discovered by?
A: W. C. Roentgen — X-rays were discovered by Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen in 1895, for which he received the first Nobel Prize in Physics.
Q: The escape velocity from the Earth's surface is about?
A: 11.2 km/s — The escape velocity from the Earth's surface is about 11.2 km/s, the minimum speed needed to escape Earth's gravitational field.
Q: A transformer is used to?
A: Step up or step down AC voltage — A transformer works on the principle of mutual induction and changes AC voltage from one level to another (step up or step down) without changing its frequency.
Q: The SI unit of pressure is?
A: Pascal — Pressure is force per unit area (P = F/A), and its SI unit is the pascal (Pa); 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

### Physics Mock Test Set 2 — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/mock-test/science/physics/set-2/
Summary: Take free timed physics mock test set 2 with 25 bilingual questions, instant scoring and answers. Practice for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police.
Q: Newton's second law of motion is expressed as?
A: F = ma — Newton's second law states that the net force on a body equals the rate of change of its momentum, giving F = ma for constant mass. Hence the correct expression is F = ma.
Q: The product of mass and velocity is called?
A: Momentum — Momentum is defined as the product of mass and velocity (p = mv), and it is a vector quantity. Therefore the product of mass and velocity is called momentum.
Q: Kinetic energy of a body is given by?
A: ½ mv² — The kinetic energy of a moving body is given by KE = ½ mv², where m is mass and v is velocity. Thus ½ mv² is the correct formula.
Q: Potential energy of a body at height h is?
A: mgh — Gravitational potential energy of a body raised to height h is PE = mgh, where g is acceleration due to gravity. Hence mgh is correct.
Q: The SI unit of frequency is?
A: Hertz — Frequency is the number of oscillations per second, and its SI unit is the hertz (Hz). One hertz equals one cycle per second.
Q: Which colour of light has the longest wavelength?
A: Red — In the visible spectrum, red light has the longest wavelength (about 700 nm) and the lowest frequency. Therefore red has the greatest wavelength.
Q: Which colour of visible light has the highest frequency?
A: Violet — Violet light lies at the short-wavelength end of the visible spectrum (about 400 nm), giving it the highest frequency among visible colours.
Q: A concave lens is also known as?
A: Diverging lens — A concave lens is thinner at the centre and diverges parallel rays of light, so it is called a diverging lens. A convex lens, by contrast, is converging.
Q: The image formed by a plane mirror is?
A: Virtual and erect — A plane mirror always forms a virtual, erect image of the same size as the object, located as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.
Q: The SI unit of electric charge is?
A: Coulomb — Electric charge is measured in coulombs (C); one coulomb is the charge transported by a current of one ampere in one second. Hence the SI unit is coulomb.
Q: The SI unit of resistance is?
A: Ohm — Resistance is the opposition to the flow of current and its SI unit is the ohm (Ω), defined by Ohm's law R = V/I. Thus the correct unit is ohm.
Q: A fuse wire is used in an electric circuit to?
A: Protect from excess current — A fuse wire has low melting point and high resistance; it melts and breaks the circuit when current exceeds a safe limit, protecting appliances from excess current.
Q: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
A: Solar energy — Solar energy is renewable because it is continuously replenished by the Sun, whereas coal, petroleum and natural gas are finite fossil fuels. Hence solar energy is renewable.
Q: The process by which a liquid changes into vapour at any temperature is?
A: Evaporation — Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour at any temperature from its surface, without reaching the boiling point. Hence the correct process is evaporation.
Q: Absolute zero temperature is?
A: –273.15°C — Absolute zero is the lowest possible temperature, 0 K = –273.15°C, at which molecular motion is minimum. Therefore the correct value is –273.15°C.
Q: The thermometer used to measure high temperature of furnaces is?
A: Pyrometer — A pyrometer is used to measure very high temperatures such as those of furnaces by detecting the radiation emitted. Clinical thermometers cannot measure such high temperatures.
Q: Which law states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed?
A: Law of conservation of energy — The law of conservation of energy states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only converted from one form to another. Hence this is the correct law.
Q: Newton's third law of motion states that?
A: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction — Newton's third law states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction, acting on two different bodies simultaneously.
Q: The weight of a body is maximum at?
A: The poles — Weight W = mg, and g is maximum at the poles because Earth is flattened at the poles and the polar radius is least. Thus weight is maximum at the poles.
Q: The value of g is zero at?
A: Centre of the Earth — At the centre of the Earth the mass of the outer shell exerts no net gravitational force, so the effective value of g is zero there. Hence g is zero at the centre.
Q: Which particle has no charge?
A: Neutron — A neutron is electrically neutral, having no charge, while protons are positive and electrons are negative. Hence the neutron is the chargeless particle.
Q: The number of electrons in a neutral atom is equal to?
A: Number of protons — A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons, so the total positive and negative charges balance. Thus electrons equal the number of protons.
Q: Radioactivity was discovered by?
A: Henri Becquerel — Radioactivity was discovered by Henri Becquerel in 1896 through his experiments on uranium salts. Hence he is credited with the discovery.
Q: The unit of radioactivity is?
A: Becquerel — The SI unit of radioactivity is the becquerel (Bq), which equals one nuclear decay per second. Therefore the correct unit is becquerel.
Q: Which of the following is used in a nuclear reactor as a moderator?
A: Heavy water — In a nuclear reactor heavy water (D2O) is used as a moderator to slow down fast neutrons without absorbing them, sustaining the chain reaction. Hence heavy water is correct.

A: Physics Mock Test Set 2 is completely free. You can read all 25 questions and their explanations on axomexam.in with no registration or charge.

A: Yes. Every question, option and explanation in Physics Mock Test Set 2 is given in both Assamese and English.

### Physics Mock Test Set 3 — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/mock-test/science/physics/set-3/
Summary: Take free timed physics mock test set 3 with 25 bilingual questions, instant scoring and answers. Practice for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police.
Q: The SI unit of energy is?
A: Joule — Energy is the capacity to do work and its SI unit is the joule (J), where 1 J = 1 N·m = 1 kg·m²/s². Newton is the unit of force, pascal of pressure and ampere of current.
Q: Work done is zero when the angle between force and displacement is?
A: 90° — Work done W = F·s·cosθ. When the force is perpendicular to the displacement (θ = 90°), cos90° = 0 and hence the work done is zero.
Q: Power is defined as?
A: Rate of doing work — Power is the rate of doing work, P = W/t, and its SI unit is the watt (1 W = 1 J/s). Work × time and force × distance do not define power.
Q: 1 horsepower is equal to?
A: 746 W — One horsepower (1 hp) is equal to exactly 746 watts in the metric (SI) convention, a unit originally defined for comparing engines.
Q: The density of water is maximum at?
A: 4°C — Water shows anomalous expansion: between 0°C and 4°C its volume decreases on heating, so its density is maximum at 4°C.
Q: Archimedes' principle is related to?
A: Buoyancy — Archimedes' principle states that a body immersed in a fluid experiences an upthrust equal to the weight of the fluid displaced, which is the basis of buoyancy.
Q: A body floats in a liquid when?
A: Weight is equal to upthrust — A floating body is in equilibrium when the upthrust (buoyant force) exactly balances its weight, i.e. weight = upthrust.
Q: The instrument used to measure relative density of a liquid is?
A: Hydrometer — A hydrometer works on Archimedes' principle and is used to measure the relative density (specific gravity) of a liquid by its depth of floatation.
Q: Pascal's law is used in?
A: Hydraulic lift — Pascal's law states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally in all directions; this principle is used in the hydraulic lift (and hydraulic brakes).
Q: The speed of sound is maximum in?
A: Solids — The speed of sound depends on the elasticity and density of the medium. It is maximum in solids, less in liquids and least in gases; sound cannot travel in vacuum.
Q: Echo is due to?
A: Reflection of sound — Echo is produced when sound waves are reflected back from a distant hard surface; the reflected sound is heard separately if the delay is at least about 0.1 s.
Q: The loudness of sound is measured in?
A: Decibel — Loudness (intensity level) of sound is measured in decibels (dB), while hertz measures frequency, newton force and watt power.
Q: Ultrasound has frequency?
A: More than 20,000 Hz — Ultrasound is sound of frequency greater than 20,000 Hz (20 kHz), which is above the upper limit of human hearing, used in sonography and SONAR.
Q: The human audible range is approximately?
A: 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz — The normal human audible range is approximately 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz (20 kHz); below this is infrasound and above is ultrasound.
Q: A rainbow is formed due to?
A: Dispersion, refraction and reflection of light — A rainbow is formed when sunlight undergoes refraction and dispersion inside water droplets and then total internal reflection, followed by refraction on exit; thus dispersion, refraction and reflection all occur.
Q: Myopia (short-sightedness) is corrected by using?
A: Concave lens — In myopia (short-sightedness) the image forms in front of the retina, so the eye cannot see distant objects clearly; it is corrected using a concave (diverging) lens.
Q: Hypermetropia (long-sightedness) is corrected by?
A: Convex lens — In hypermetropia (long-sightedness) the image forms behind the retina; it is corrected by a convex (converging) lens that brings the image forward onto the retina.
Q: The power of a lens is measured in?
A: Dioptre — The power of a lens is the reciprocal of its focal length in metres, P = 1/f, and its SI unit is the dioptre (D).
Q: The SI unit of magnetic field is?
A: Tesla — The SI unit of magnetic field (magnetic flux density) is the tesla (T), where 1 T = 1 N/(A·m). Newton, joule and ohm are units of force, energy and resistance.
Q: A magnetic field is produced around a conductor when?
A: Electric current flows through it — A current-carrying conductor produces a magnetic field around it (Oersted's discovery, basis of Ampere's law); heating, painting or breaking it does not create a magnetic field.
Q: The device that converts electrical energy into mechanical energy is?
A: Electric motor — An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy, using the force on a current-carrying coil placed in a magnetic field.
Q: A dynamo (generator) converts?
A: Mechanical energy into electrical energy — A dynamo (generator) works on electromagnetic induction and converts mechanical energy into electrical energy; a motor does the reverse.
Q: Which of the following is used to detect charge?
A: Gold leaf electroscope — A gold leaf electroscope detects the presence and nature of electric charge; the divergence of its gold leaves indicates that the body is charged.
Q: The specific heat of water is?
A: 1 cal/g°C — The specific heat of water is 1 cal/g°C (or 4.18 J/g°C), which is unusually high and is why water is used as a coolant.
Q: Which metal is the best conductor of heat?
A: Silver — Among metals, silver has the highest thermal conductivity, followed by copper; hence silver is the best conductor of heat.

A: Physics Mock Test Set 3 is completely free. You can read all 25 questions and their explanations on axomexam.in with no registration or charge.
Q: Are the Physics Mock Test Set 3 questions available in Assamese and English?
A: Yes. Every question, option and explanation in Physics Mock Test Set 3 is given in both Assamese and English.

### Physics Mock Test Set 4 — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/mock-test/science/physics/set-4/
Summary: Take free timed physics mock test set 4 with 25 bilingual questions, instant scoring and answers. Practice for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police.
Q: The gravitational force between two bodies is given by?
A: F = G m1 m2 / r² — Newton's universal law of gravitation states that every particle attracts every other particle with a force F = G m1 m2 / r², where G is the gravitational constant and r is the distance between the two masses.
Q: Who gave the universal law of gravitation?
A: Isaac Newton — The universal law of gravitation was given by Sir Isaac Newton, published in 1687 in his work Principia.
Q: The time period of a simple pendulum depends on?
A: Length and g — The time period of a simple pendulum is T = 2π√(L/g), so it depends only on the length L and the acceleration due to gravity g; the mass of the bob and (for small oscillations) the amplitude do not affect it.
Q: If the length of a simple pendulum is increased, its time period?
A: Increases — Since T = 2π√(L/g), the time period is directly proportional to the square root of the length (T ∝ √L). Increasing the length therefore increases the time period.
Q: The SI unit of wavelength is?
A: Metre — Wavelength is the distance between two consecutive crests or troughs of a wave, so its SI unit is the metre (m).
Q: Relation between wave speed v, frequency f and wavelength λ is?
A: v = f λ — The speed of a wave equals its frequency multiplied by its wavelength: v = f λ.
Q: Light year is a unit of?
A: Distance — A light year is the distance travelled by light in vacuum in one year, about 9.46 × 10^15 metres, so it is a unit of distance.
Q: The nearest star to the Earth after the Sun is?
A: Proxima Centauri — Proxima Centauri, about 4.24 light years away, is the nearest star to Earth after the Sun.
Q: The ozone layer protects us from?
A: Harmful ultraviolet rays — The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet rays of the Sun, protecting living organisms from UV damage.
Q: Which radiation has the highest penetrating power?
A: Gamma rays — Gamma rays are electromagnetic radiation with very short wavelength and no charge, giving them the highest penetrating power among alpha, beta and gamma radiations.
Q: Alpha particles are?
A: Helium nuclei — An alpha particle is a helium nucleus containing two protons and two neutrons, i.e. He²⁺.
Q: Beta particles are?
A: Fast moving electrons — Beta particles are fast-moving electrons emitted from the nucleus during beta decay.
Q: The half-life of a radioactive substance is?
A: Time in which half of the nuclei decay — Half-life is the time in which half of the nuclei of a radioactive sample decay.
Q: Nuclear fission is?
A: Splitting of a heavy nucleus — Nuclear fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus (such as uranium-235) into lighter nuclei, releasing a large amount of energy.
Q: The energy of the Sun is produced mainly by?
A: Nuclear fusion — The Sun's energy is produced mainly by nuclear fusion, in which hydrogen nuclei combine to form helium and release enormous energy.
Q: Which of the following is used in solar cells?
A: Silicon — Solar cells are made of the semiconductor silicon, which converts light energy into electrical energy through the photovoltaic effect.
Q: The refractive index of a medium is?
A: Speed of light in vacuum / speed of light in medium — The refractive index of a medium is the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to its speed in the medium: n = c / v.
Q: Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from?
A: Denser to rarer medium beyond critical angle — Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from a denser medium to a rarer medium and the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle.
Q: Optical fibre works on the principle of?
A: Total internal reflection — Optical fibres transmit light signals by repeated total internal reflection along the length of the fibre.
Q: The sky appears blue due to?
A: Scattering of sunlight by atmosphere — The atmosphere scatters blue light (shorter wavelength) much more strongly than red, so scattered blue light reaches our eyes and the sky appears blue (Rayleigh scattering).
Q: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
A: Velocity — Velocity is a vector quantity because it has both magnitude and direction. Speed, distance and time are scalar quantities.
Q: Distance and displacement are equal when motion is?
A: Along a straight line in one direction — For motion along a straight line in one direction, distance and displacement have the same magnitude, so they are equal.
Q: The slope of a distance-time graph gives?
A: Speed — The slope of a distance-time graph gives speed, because slope = distance / time.
Q: The slope of a velocity-time graph gives?
A: Acceleration — The slope of a velocity-time graph gives acceleration, because slope = change in velocity / time.
Q: The area under a velocity-time graph represents?
A: Displacement — The area under a velocity-time graph equals velocity × time, which represents displacement.

### Physics Mock Test Set 5 — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/mock-test/science/physics/set-5/
Summary: Take free timed physics mock test set 5 with 25 bilingual questions, instant scoring and answers. Practice for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police.
Q: The SI unit of potential difference is?
A: Volt — Potential difference is the work done per unit charge in moving a charge between two points, and its SI unit is the volt (1 V = 1 J/C). Hence 'Volt' is correct.
Q: In a series combination of resistors, the current is?
A: Same through each resistor — In a series circuit there is only one path for the current, so the same current flows through every resistor while the voltage divides across them. Hence 'Same through each resistor' is correct.
Q: In a parallel combination of resistors, the voltage is?
A: Same across each resistor — In a parallel combination all resistors are connected across the same two nodes, so the potential difference (voltage) across each resistor is the same while the current divides. Hence 'Same across each resistor' is correct.
Q: The commercial unit of electrical energy is?
A: Kilowatt-hour — Electrical energy is sold commercially in kilowatt-hour (kWh), the energy consumed by a 1 kW appliance in 1 hour. Hence 'Kilowatt-hour' is correct.
Q: 1 kWh is equal to?
A: 3.6 × 10^6 J — 1 kWh = 1000 W × 3600 s = 3.6 × 10^6 J. Hence '3.6 × 10^6 J' is correct.
Q: The heating effect of current is given by?
A: H = I²Rt — Joule's law of heating states H = I²Rt, the heat produced in a resistor of resistance R carrying current I for time t. Hence 'H = I²Rt' is correct.
Q: Which of the following is used in electric heater coils?
A: Nichrome — Nichrome has high resistivity, a high melting point and does not oxidise easily, so it is used in electric heater coils. Hence 'Nichrome' is correct.
Q: The earth wire in household wiring is usually?
A: Green or green-yellow — The earth wire provides a low-resistance path to the ground and is usually green or green-yellow in colour. Hence 'Green or green-yellow' is correct.
Q: AC used in Indian household supply has frequency?
A: 50 Hz — The alternating current supplied for domestic use in India has a frequency of 50 Hz, i.e. it reverses direction 100 times per second. Hence '50 Hz' is correct.
Q: The voltage of household AC supply in India is about?
A: 220 V — The domestic AC supply voltage in India is about 220 V with a frequency of 50 Hz. Hence '220 V' is correct.
Q: Which of the following is a semiconductor?
A: Germanium — Germanium (like silicon) is a semiconductor whose resistivity lies between that of conductors and insulators, whereas copper, silver and gold are conductors. Hence 'Germanium' is correct.
Q: LED stands for?
A: Light Emitting Diode — LED stands for Light Emitting Diode, a semiconductor diode that emits light when forward biased. Hence 'Light Emitting Diode' is correct.
Q: The first Indian satellite was?
A: Aryabhata — Aryabhata, launched on 19 April 1975, was India's first satellite. Hence 'Aryabhata' is correct.
Q: ISRO was established in which year?
A: 1969 — ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation) was established on 15 August 1969. Hence '1969' is correct.
Q: Geostationary satellites have a time period of about?
A: 24 hours — A geostationary satellite revolves around the Earth once in 24 hours in the equatorial plane, so it appears stationary over one point. Hence '24 hours' is correct.
Q: Which force is responsible for falling of objects towards Earth?
A: Gravitational force — The gravitational force of the Earth attracts objects towards its centre, which causes them to fall. Hence 'Gravitational force' is correct.
Q: Friction can be reduced by?
A: Using lubricants — Lubricants form a thin layer between surfaces, reducing interlocking of irregularities and hence friction. Hence 'Using lubricants' is correct.
Q: Inertia of a body depends on its?
A: Mass — Inertia is the inability of a body to change by itself its state of rest or uniform motion, and it is directly proportional to the mass of the body. Hence 'Mass' is correct.
Q: The momentum of a body at rest is?
A: Zero — Momentum p = mv; for a body at rest the velocity v = 0, so its momentum is zero. Hence 'Zero' is correct.
Q: Which of the following is not a unit of energy?
A: Newton — Newton is the SI unit of force, not of energy; joule, calorie and kilowatt-hour are all units of energy. Hence 'Newton' is correct.
Q: The instrument used to measure humidity is?
A: Hygrometer — A hygrometer measures the humidity (moisture content) of air, while a barometer measures atmospheric pressure. Hence 'Hygrometer' is correct.
Q: Manometer is used to measure?
A: Pressure of a gas or liquid — A manometer measures the pressure of a gas or liquid from the difference in liquid levels in its two limbs. Hence 'Pressure of a gas or liquid' is correct.
Q: The first law of thermodynamics is based on?
A: Conservation of energy — The first law of thermodynamics is the law of conservation of energy applied to heat processes, written as ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW. Hence 'Conservation of energy' is correct.
Q: Which of the following has the highest specific heat?
A: Water — Among the given substances water has the highest specific heat capacity (about 4186 J/kg·°C), so it heats up and cools down slowly. Hence 'Water' is correct.
Q: A clinical thermometer is used to measure?
A: Human body temperature — A clinical thermometer is designed with a small range (about 35–42 °C) to measure human body temperature accurately. Hence 'Human body temperature' is correct.

### Physics Mock Test Set 6 — ADRE, APSC

Q: What is the SI base unit of length?
A: Metre — The metre (m) is the SI base unit of length.
Q: The number of fundamental (base) SI units is?
A: 7 — There are seven fundamental SI units: metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela.
Q: Which instrument is used to measure the diameter of a thin wire accurately?
A: Screw gauge — A screw gauge (micrometer) accurately measures small lengths such as the diameter of a thin wire.
Q: The SI unit of time is?
A: Second — The second (s) is the SI base unit of time.
Q: Which of the following is a fundamental physical quantity?
A: Mass — Mass is a fundamental quantity, while speed, force and pressure are derived quantities.
Q: The rate of change of displacement is called?
A: Velocity — Velocity is the rate of change of displacement.
Q: The rate of change of velocity is called?
A: Acceleration — Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.
Q: The SI unit of acceleration is?
A: m/s² — Acceleration = change in velocity / time, so its SI unit is m/s².
Q: A body moving with uniform velocity has an acceleration of?
A: Zero — As velocity is constant, its rate of change (acceleration) is zero.
Q: A physical quantity having both magnitude and direction is called?
A: Vector — A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction.
Q: The CGS unit of force is?
A: Dyne — In the CGS system, force is measured in dyne.
Q: Which of the following is the first equation of motion?
A: v = u + at — The first equation of motion is v = u + at.
Q: The initial velocity of a body starting from rest is?

Q: The area under a speed-time graph gives?
A: Distance travelled — The area under a speed-time graph represents the distance travelled.
Q: 1 kilometre is equal to?
A: 1000 m — 1 kilometre = 1000 metres.
Q: The least count of an ordinary metre scale is?
A: 1 mm — A metre scale is graduated in millimetres, so its least count is 1 mm.
Q: The device used to measure the speed of a running vehicle is?
A: Speedometer — A speedometer shows the instantaneous speed of a vehicle.
Q: A body dropped freely from a height falls with?
A: Uniform acceleration — A freely falling body moves with uniform acceleration equal to g.
Q: The motion of the pendulum of a wall clock is an example of?
A: Periodic motion — The pendulum repeats its motion at regular intervals, so it is periodic motion.
Q: The total distance travelled by a vehicle is recorded by an?
A: Odometer — An odometer records the total distance travelled by a vehicle.
Q: The SI unit of mass is the?
A: Kilogram — The kilogram (kg) is the SI base unit of mass.
Q: The dimensional formula of force is?
A: [M L T⁻²] — Force = mass × acceleration, so its dimensional formula is [M L T⁻²].
Q: A body moving along a circular path with constant speed has?
A: Changing velocity — The direction changes continuously, so the velocity changes even though the speed is constant.
Q: A body is said to be in uniform motion when it covers?
A: Equal distances in equal intervals of time — In uniform motion, a body covers equal distances in equal intervals of time.
Q: A person walks 3 m towards the north and then 4 m towards the east. The magnitude of his displacement is?
A: 5 m — The two displacements are perpendicular, so the resultant = √(3² + 4²) = 5 m.

### Physics Mock Test Set 7 — ADRE, APSC
URL: https://axomexam.in/mock-test/science/physics/set-7/
Summary: Take free timed physics mock test set 7 with 25 bilingual questions, instant scoring and answers. Practice for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police.
Q: The force that opposes the relative motion between two surfaces in contact is called?
A: Friction — Friction is the force that opposes relative motion between two surfaces in contact.
Q: The force that keeps the planets revolving around the Sun is the?
A: Gravitational force — The gravitational force of the Sun keeps the planets in their orbits.
Q: The acceleration due to gravity on the Moon is about?
A: One-sixth of that on the Earth — The acceleration due to gravity on the Moon is about one-sixth of that on the Earth.
Q: The value of acceleration due to gravity (g) is maximum at the?
A: Poles — The value of g is maximum at the poles and minimum at the equator.
Q: The weight of a body is measured with a?
A: Spring balance — A spring balance measures the weight of a body.
Q: The universal gravitational constant G has the SI unit?
A: N·m²/kg² — G = Fd²/(m₁m₂), so its SI unit is N·m²/kg².
Q: Which of the following is a contact force?
A: Friction — Friction acts only when two surfaces are in contact, so it is a contact force.
Q: Pressure is defined as?
A: Force per unit area — Pressure = force / area, i.e. force per unit area.
Q: The pressure exerted by a liquid at a point increases with?
A: Depth — Liquid pressure increases with depth.
Q: The upward force exerted by a fluid on a body immersed in it is called?
A: Buoyant force — The upward force exerted by a fluid on an immersed body is called buoyant force or upthrust.
Q: A body sinks in water if its density is?
A: Greater than that of water — A body sinks if its density is greater than that of water.
Q: The relative density of a substance is the ratio of its density to the density of?
A: Water — Relative density is the ratio of the density of a substance to the density of water.
Q: When the weight of a body is equal to the upthrust acting on it, the body?
A: Floats — When weight equals upthrust, the body floats in equilibrium.
Q: A hydrometer works on the principle of?
A: Archimedes' principle — A hydrometer works on Archimedes' principle to measure the density of a liquid.
Q: Hydraulic brakes used in vehicles work on?
A: Pascal's law — Hydraulic brakes work on Pascal's law.
Q: Ball bearings are used in machines to?
A: Reduce friction — Ball bearings convert sliding friction into rolling friction and so reduce friction.
Q: The instrument used to measure the volume of a liquid accurately is a?
A: Measuring cylinder — A measuring cylinder is used to measure the volume of a liquid.
Q: When a body is taken from the Earth to the Moon, its mass?
A: Remains the same — Mass is the quantity of matter and does not change with place.
Q: When a body is taken from the Earth to the Moon, its weight?
A: Decreases — Weight depends on gravity; as the Moon's gravity is weaker, the weight decreases.
Q: The pressure exerted by a given force can be increased by?
A: Decreasing the area of contact — Since pressure = force / area, decreasing the area increases the pressure.
Q: An astronaut feels weightless inside an orbiting spacecraft because?
A: The spacecraft and astronaut are in free fall — The astronaut and spacecraft fall freely together, so there is no normal reaction and hence weightlessness.
Q: Thrust is a force acting?
A: Perpendicular to a surface — Thrust is the force acting perpendicular to a surface.
Q: The atmospheric pressure at sea level is about?
A: 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa — Standard atmospheric pressure at sea level is about 1.01 × 10⁵ pascal.
Q: The force of friction always acts?
A: Opposite to the direction of relative motion — Friction always opposes the relative motion between the surfaces.
Q: The centre of gravity of a uniform metre scale lies at?
A: Its midpoint — A uniform rod's centre of gravity is at its midpoint.

### Physics Mock Test Set 8 — ADRE, APSC

Summary: Take free timed physics mock test set 8 with 25 bilingual questions, instant scoring and answers. Practice for ADRE, APSC and Assam Police.
Q: The product of force and displacement in the direction of the force is called?
A: Work — Work done = force × displacement in the direction of the force.
Q: The work done by a coolie carrying a load on his head and walking on a horizontal road is?
A: Zero — The force is vertical while displacement is horizontal, so the work done is zero.
Q: The energy possessed by a body due to its motion is called?
A: Kinetic energy — Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body because of its motion.
Q: The energy possessed by a body due to its position is called?
A: Potential energy — Potential energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its position.
Q: The energy stored in a stretched rubber band is?
A: Potential energy — A stretched rubber band stores elastic potential energy.
Q: When a body falls freely, its potential energy is converted into?
A: Kinetic energy — During free fall, potential energy is converted into kinetic energy.
Q: A body of mass 1 kg moving with a velocity of 1 m/s has kinetic energy equal to?
A: 0.5 J — KE = ½mv² = ½ × 1 × 1² = 0.5 J.
Q: Heat flows from a body at?
A: Higher temperature to a body at lower temperature — Heat always flows from a body at higher temperature to one at lower temperature.
Q: The average kinetic energy of the molecules of a substance determines its?
A: Temperature — Temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy of the molecules.
Q: The amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1°C is called its?
A: Specific heat capacity — Specific heat capacity is the heat needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1°C.
Q: The transfer of heat through a solid without the movement of its particles is called?
A: Conduction — Conduction is the transfer of heat through a solid without the movement of particles.
Q: The transfer of heat in liquids and gases by the actual movement of particles is called?
A: Convection — Convection is the transfer of heat by the actual movement of heated particles.
Q: The transfer of heat that does not require any medium is called?
A: Radiation — Radiation is heat transfer that needs no medium.
Q: The heat of the Sun reaches the Earth by?
A: Radiation — The Sun's heat reaches the Earth through the vacuum of space by radiation.
Q: The change of state from solid to liquid is called?
A: Melting — Melting is the change of state from solid to liquid.
Q: The heat energy required to change 1 kg of a solid into liquid at its melting point is called?
A: Latent heat of fusion — The heat required to change 1 kg of solid to liquid at its melting point is the latent heat of fusion.
Q: Sea breeze and land breeze are caused by?
A: Convection — Sea and land breezes are caused by convection currents in air.
Q: The temperature at which the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales show the same reading is?
A: -40° — The Celsius and Fahrenheit scales read the same value, -40°, at that temperature.
Q: A bimetallic strip bends on heating because the two metals have different?
A: Coefficients of thermal expansion — The two metals expand by different amounts, so the bimetallic strip bends.
Q: The CGS unit of heat is the?
A: Calorie — In the CGS system, heat is measured in calorie.
Q: Water is a poor conductor of heat. This helps aquatic animals to survive in winter because?
A: Ice forms on the surface and insulates the water below — Ice formed on the surface does not allow heat to escape, so the water below stays warm.
Q: The heat energy released when 1 kg of a fuel is burnt completely is called its?
A: Calorific value — The heat released on complete burning of 1 kg of fuel is its calorific value.
Q: The device used to measure the quantity of heat exchanged is a?
A: Calorimeter — A calorimeter measures the quantity of heat exchanged in a process.
Q: Two bodies are said to be in thermal equilibrium when they have the same?
A: Temperature — Two bodies are in thermal equilibrium when their temperatures are equal.
Q: The temperature at which a liquid starts boiling at standard atmospheric pressure is its?
A: Boiling point — The temperature at which a liquid boils at standard pressure is its boiling point.

## as

### চৰ্যাপদ আৰু লোক-গীত — ADRE, APSC, অসম আৰক্ষী প্ৰশ্নোত্তৰ
URL: https://axomexam.in/as/topic/gk/assam-literature/ancient-pre-vaishnavite-sec/charyapada-folk-songs/
Summary: চৰ্যাপদ আৰু অসমীয়া লোক-গীতৰ গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ প্ৰশ্ন আৰু উত্তৰ — ADRE, APSC আৰু অসম আৰক্ষী পৰীক্ষাৰ বাবে।
Q: What is Charyapada?
A: Charyapada is a collection of mystical Buddhist songs composed between the 8th and 12th centuries, considered the earliest specimen of Assamese (and related eastern Indo-Aryan) literature.
Q: Who discovered the Charyapada manuscript?
A: Haraprasad Shastri discovered the Charyapada manuscript in 1907 from the royal library of Nepal.
Q: In which script was the Charyapada written?
A: The Charyapada was written in the Gaudi script, an old Bengali-Assamese script.
Q: Who were the composers of the Charyapada?
A: The Charyapada was composed by Buddhist Siddhacharyas such as Luipa, Sarahapa, Kambalabar, Sabaripa, and others.
Q: How many Charyapadas are extant?
A: A total of 47 Charyapadas are extant, but some scholars believe the original number was around 50.
Q: Who is considered the first Charyapada poet?
A: Luipa (Luipada) is considered the first Charyapada poet.
Q: What is the language of Charyapada?
A: The language of Charyapada is 'Sandhya Bhasya' or twilight language, an early form related to Old Assamese and Old Bengali.
Q: Which Buddhist sect's philosophy is reflected in the Charyapada?
A: The philosophy of Vajrayana Buddhism is reflected in the Charyapada songs.
Q: Who wrote the commentary 'Charyagitikosh-vritti' on Charyapada?
A: The commentary 'Charyagitikosh-vritti' was written by Munidatta.
Q: Which is the earliest manuscript of Charyapada?
A: The earliest manuscript of Charyapada is dated 1538 AD and was found in Nepal.
Q: What did Banikanta Kakati say about Charyapada?
A: Banikanta Kakati in his 'Bara Mahanata' and related works argued that the Charyapada language is old Assamese.
Q: What is a 'Bihu geet'?
A: A Bihu geet is an Assamese folk song associated with the Bihu festival, reflecting rural life, love, and nature.
Q: What is a 'Lali geet' or 'Nisaoni lali'?
A: A Lali geet is a lullaby sung by mothers to put babies to sleep in Assamese folk tradition.
Q: What is 'Ainam'?
A: Ainam is a lamentation or mourning song sung at funerals and death rituals in Assamese folk tradition.
Q: What is a 'Tokari geet'?
A: A Tokari geet is a folk song sung to the accompaniment of the Tokari, a stringed instrument, often devotional in nature.
Q: What is 'Deh Bichar' or 'Deh-Bixar Geet'?
A: Deh Bichar geet are philosophical folk songs dealing with the body and soul, popular among the saints.
Q: What is a 'Baramahi geet'?
A: A Baramahi geet is a folk song that describes the feelings of a woman separated from her husband through the twelve months of the year.
Q: What is a 'Biya geet' or 'Biyanam'?
A: Biya geet or Biyanam are wedding songs sung during Assamese marriage ceremonies.
Q: What is 'Jikir'?
A: Jikir is a devotional folk song of the Assamese Muslim community, generally attributed to Azan Fakir (Shah Miran).
Q: Who composed the famous 'Jikir' songs?
A: Azan Fakir (Shah Miran), a 17th-century Sufi saint of Assam, composed the famous Jikir and Zari songs.
Q: What is 'Zari'?
A: Zari is a type of devotional folk song of the Assamese Muslims, usually sung in chorus, dealing with the tragedy of Karbala.
Q: What is 'Kushan geet'?
A: Kushan geet is a category of Assamese folk songs sung by women while performing household tasks like grinding paddy.
Q: What is 'Dhaina geet'?
A: Dhaina geet are folk songs sung during agricultural work, especially in paddy fields.
Q: What is 'Nao geet' or 'Bhatial'?
A: Nao geet are boatmen's songs, while Bhatial is a type of folk song sung by boatmen in the rivers of Assam.
Q: Who is associated with the 'Bhatima' tradition?
A: Bhatima is associated with Madhavdev, who composed devotional songs in this genre praising saints and God.
Q: What is 'Ojapali'?
A: Ojapali is a traditional performing art of Assam that combines narrative songs, dance, and dramatic presentation, sung in folk style.
Q: What is 'Khol' or 'Mridanga' in folk music?
A: Khol (Mridanga) is a traditional clay drum used as the main percussion instrument in Assamese devotional and folk music.
Q: What is 'Gopinath Bordoloi' connection to folk song collection?
A: Gopinath Bordoloi's association is not with folk songs; he was a political leader. Folk song collections were made by scholars like Laxminath Bezbaroa, Birinchi Kumar Barua, and Prafulladatta Goswami.
Q: Who is known as the collector of 'Buranjis' as folk literature?
A: Buranjis are historical chronicles, not folk literature. Surya Kumar Bhuyan is the main scholar who edited and published many Buranjis.
Q: What is 'Nisukoni geet' or 'Ajai geet'?
A: Nisukoni (Ajai) geet are lullabies or songs sung while spinning cotton (Ajai), soothing babies to sleep.
Q: What is 'Phukoni geet'?
A: Phukoni geet are songs sung by women while blowing the fire (phukoni) in the kitchen or hearth in Assamese folk life.
Q: What is 'Gorokhiya geet'?
A: Gorokhiya geet are folk songs sung by cowherds while grazing cattle.
Q: What is 'Huchori'?
A: Huchori is a folk song-and-dance performance by young people during Bihu, especially in the Rongali season, going door to door.
Q: What is 'Kamar geet'?
A: Kamar geet are folk songs sung by blacksmiths (kamar) while working in their furnaces.
Q: Who wrote the book 'Folk-Literature of Assam'?
A: Birinchi Kumar Barua wrote 'Folk-Literature of Assam'.
Q: Which of these is the 'Saptakanda Ramayana' of Madhava Kandali?
A: The Saptakanda Ramayana is not folk literature; it is the Assamese translation of the Ramayana by Madhava Kandali in the 14th century.
Q: What is the folk song 'Bihoo geet' related to?
A: Bihu geet is related to the Bihu festival and agricultural life of Assam.
Q: What is Charyapada?
A: Charyapada is the oldest surviving collection of mystical songs in the Eastern Indo-Aryan languages. It was composed by Buddhist Siddhacharyas between the 8th and 12th centuries CE and is regarded as the earliest specimen of Assamese and related eastern Indo-Aryan literature.
Q: Who discovered the Charyapada manuscript and when?
A: The manuscript was discovered by Haraprasad Shastri in 1907 in the royal library of Nepal. He published the collection in 1916. The only surviving manuscript is dated 1538 CE.
Q: In which language and script was the Charyapada written?
A: Charyapada was written in Sandhya Bhasha, the twilight language, and in the Gaudi script, an old Bengali-Assamese script. A Sanskrit commentary on it, the Charyagitikosh-vritti, was written by Munidatta.
Q: How many Charyapada songs are extant and who were the poets?
A: A total of 47 songs are extant, though some scholars believe the original number was about 50. The chief poets include Luipa, Sarahapa, Kambalapada, Sabaripa, Kanhapa and Bhusukupada, with Luipa traditionally regarded as the first poet.
Q: Why is Charyapada important for Assam competitive exams?
A: It is the starting point of Assamese literary history and a regular part of the Assam Literature section in ADRE, APSC, Assam Police and other recruitment examinations. The questions are factual and repeat often, so the topic is easy to score.
Q: চৰ্যাপদ কি?
A: চৰ্যাপদ হৈছে পূৱ ভাৰতীয় আৰ্য ভাষাৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি সংৰক্ষিত ৰহস্যমূলক গীতৰ সংকলন। ই বৌদ্ধ সিদ্ধাচাৰ্যসকলে খ্ৰীষ্টীয় অষ্টমৰ পৰা দ্বাদশ শতিকাৰ ভিতৰত ৰচনা কৰিছিল আৰু অসমীয়া তথা সংশ্লিষ্ট পূৱ ভাৰতীয় আৰ্য সাহিত্যৰ আটাইতকৈ পুৰণি নিদৰ্শন বুলি গণ্য কৰা হয়।
Q: চৰ্যাপদ পুথিখন কোনে কেতিয়া আৱিষ্কাৰ কৰিছিল?
A: পুথিখন হৰপ্ৰসাদ শাস্ত্ৰীয়ে ১৯০৭ চনত নেপালৰ ৰাজকীয় পুথিভঁৰালত আৱিষ্কাৰ কৰিছিল। তেওঁ ১৯১৬ চনত সংকলনটো প্ৰকাশ কৰিছিল। একমাত্ৰ জীৱিত পুথিখনৰ তাৰিখ খ্ৰীষ্টীয় ১৫৩৮ চন।
Q: চৰ্যাপদ কোন ভাষা আৰু আখৰত লিখা হৈছিল?
A: চৰ্যাপদ সন্ধ্যা ভাষা (গোধূলি ভাষা) আৰু গৌড়ী আখৰত লিখা হৈছিল, যিটো পুৰণি বঙলা-অসমীয়া আখৰ। ইয়াৰ ওপৰত মুনিদত্তই লিখা সংস্কৃত টীকা হৈছে চৰ্যাগীতিকোষ-বৃত্তি।
Q: চৰ্যাপদত কিমানখন গীত আছে আৰু কবিসকল কোন আছিল?
A: মুঠ ৪৭ খন গীত বৰ্তমান আছে, যদিও কিছুমান পণ্ডিতৰ মতে মূল সংখ্যা আছিল প্ৰায় ৫০। প্ৰধান কবিসকলৰ ভিতৰত লুইপা, সৰহাপা, কম্বলপাদ, শৱৰীপা, কান্ধাপা আৰু ভুসুকুপাদ আদি; লুইপাক পৰম্পৰাগতভাৱে প্ৰথম কবি বুলি গণ্য কৰা হয়।
Q: অসমৰ প্ৰতিযোগিতামূলক পৰীক্ষাত চৰ্যাপদ কিয় গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ?
A: ই অসমীয়া সাহিত্য ইতিহাসৰ আৰম্ভণি আৰু ADRE, APSC, অসম আৰক্ষী আদি পৰীক্ষাৰ অসম সাহিত্য অংশত নিয়মীয়াকৈ আহে। প্ৰশ্নবোৰ তথ্যভিত্তিক আৰু বাৰে বাৰে পুনৰাবৃত্ত হয়, গতিকে এই বিষয়টো সহজে নম্বৰ পোৱা বিষয়।
